questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem:
Mr Cheung bought restaurant premises 2 years ago for $5 000 000 and sells 'two-dish-rice' meal boxes at the premises. Recently, his monthly profit has decreased from $30 000 to $10 000 due to the opening of new restaurants nearby. A businessman offers to rent Mr Cheung's restaurant premises for a monthly rental of $15 000.

Which of the following would be included in Mr Cheung's opportunity cost of continuing to operate his 'two-dish-rice' business at the premises?

choices.text: the $5 000 000 purchase price of the restaurant premises

questions.explanation: The purchase price is a sunk cost. Continuing the business means giving up the rental income from the premises, so the monthly rental is part of opportunity cost.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Jacky, a Secondary 6 student in Hong Kong, is going to travel to Korea for his graduation trip. Which of the following will decrease his cost of having the graduation trip to Korea?

choices.text: Hong Kong dollar appreciates against South Korean Won.
The return flight from Korea to Hong Kong is delayed.
The number of confirmed cases of COVID-19 in Korea has increased drastically.
The services of the hotel in Korea are better than his expectation.

questions.explanation: When the Hong Kong dollar appreciates against the South Korean Won, Korean goods and services cost fewer Hong Kong dollars, lowering the money cost of the trip.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meaning of private property rights and its importance in a market economy
questions.stem:
A band in Hong Kong adopted a real-name registration system for the sale of its concert tickets. These tickets were not transferrable so that the chance of ticket scalping was reduced.

Which of the following statements about the above real-name registration system is/are correct?

(1) It is a mechanism to tackle the problem of 'what to produce'.
(2) The private property rights over the tickets would be weakened under the system.
(3) Non-price competition would not be involved in the allocation of the tickets under the system.
questions.explanation: Making tickets non-transferable weakens the right to transfer them. The system concerns allocation rather than what to produce, and non-price competition can still exist when demand exceeds supply.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Which of the following is a normative statement / are normative statements?

(1) Launching consumption voucher schemes will lead to inflation.
(2) Promoting tourism is the most appropriate way to stimulate economic growth.
(3) The government should continue to attract Mainland enterprises to invest in Hong Kong.
questions.explanation: Statements about what is most appropriate or what the government should do involve value judgements, so (2) and (3) are normative.

questions.keyPoint: Distinguishing between free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the classification of goods is correct?

choices.text: Musical instruments used by street performers are public goods because the music performed with these instruments can be enjoyed concurrently by many people.
Textbooks are private goods because the marginal cost of producing an additional unit of textbooks is positive.
Artworks exhibited in the Hong Kong Palace Museum are consumer goods because costs are involved in their production.
Popular free online videos for learning English are economic goods because their quantities are not enough to satisfy human wants.

questions.explanation: A good can be an economic good even if users do not pay a money price. If the quantity available is insufficient to satisfy wants, scarcity and opportunity cost exist.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following would raise both the labour supply and average labour productivity of an economy?

choices.text: The government raises the amount of unemployment benefits.
Free education is extended to university programmes.
More firms install advanced production equipment.
The quota of an immigration scheme of highly skilled individuals is increased.

questions.explanation: Admitting more highly skilled immigrants raises the labour supply and can raise the average productivity of workers in the economy.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: The occupational mobility of labour of an economy will decrease if _____.

choices.text: transport subsidies are provided to workers who live in remote districts.
the statutory retirement age is raised from 65 to 70.
more job retraining courses are provided by the government free of charge.

questions.explanation: When more jobs require specialised skills, workers find it harder to switch occupations, so occupational mobility decreases.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about Firm A and Firm B in Hong Kong.

choices.text: Firm B raises more capital than Firm A.
owners of both firms are required to obtain consent from other owners when transferring their ownership.
Firm A may enjoy a lower profits tax rate than Firm B.
Firm B is an independent legal entity while Firm A is not.

questions.explanation: Firm A's features are consistent with an unincorporated business, while Firm B's features are consistent with a public limited company. An unincorporated business may enjoy a lower profits tax rate.

visuals.caption: Firm A and Firm B in Hong Kong
rows: Disclosure of financial information to the public

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, we can conclude that _____.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The following table shows the data of a price-taking garment factory. The fixed cost of the factory is $10.
questions.explanation: After the changes, maximum profit is $70 at 8 or 9 units. Compared with the old profit-maximising output of 7 or 8 units, the output can increase by 1 unit and profit becomes $70.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the market price of garments rises from $17 to $19, and the fixed cost of the factory rises by $2. As a result, the profit-maximising output of the factory would _____ while its profit would _____.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which of the following is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

choices.text: When a theme park reduces its ticket price, visitors stay in the theme park for longer hours on average.
Both the price and quantity transacted of private housing units decrease when people expect an increase in mortgage interest rates.
Compared with customers living close to supermarkets, customers living far away from supermarkets tend to buy more items in each visit to supermarkets.
If the Hong Kong Government shortens the quarantine period for incoming arrivals, the number of tourists visiting Hong Kong would increase.

questions.explanation: The law of demand concerns the quantity demanded of a good when its own price changes. Visitors staying longer is not a direct increase in the quantity demanded of theme park tickets.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem:
When Good X and Good Y are in _____, a decrease in the price of Good X will lead to _____.

(1) competitive demand ...... a decrease in the price of Good Y
(2) joint demand ...... a decrease in the producer surplus in the market of Good Y
(3) competitive supply ...... an increase in the consumer surplus in the market of Good Y
(4) joint supply ...... a decrease in consumers' total expenditure on Good Y
questions.explanation: For substitutes in demand, a fall in the price of X reduces demand for Y and lowers Y's price. For goods in competitive supply, a fall in X's price can shift resources to Y, raising supply and consumer surplus in Y's market.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the supply and demand curves of electric vehicles. The original equilibrium point is E0.
questions.explanation: Higher production cost decreases supply, shifting supply left to S2. Higher consumer confidence increases demand, shifting demand right to D1. The new equilibrium is E2.

visuals.alt: Supply and demand diagram of electric vehicles with S2, S0, S1 and D2, D0, D1.
visuals.caption: Electric vehicles

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose there is an increase in the cost of producing electric vehicles. At the same time, the decreasing number of car accidents involving electric vehicles increases consumers' confidence in electric vehicles. As a result, the new equilibrium point will be at _____.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
questions.stem:
Semiconductor chips are key components for producing smartphones.

Due to a global shortage of semiconductor chips, the quantity of smartphones sold has changed by 10% whereas the price of smartphones has increased by 20%. Which of the following best explains the above changes in the price and quantity sold of smartphones?

choices.text: Smartphone manufacturers have excess capacity in production.
Consumers' expenditure on smartphones takes up a large proportion of their total expenditure.
The workers for producing smartphones cannot be easily recruited.

questions.explanation: A supply shortage causing price to change proportionately more than quantity is consistent with inelastic demand. A lack of close substitutes helps explain inelastic demand.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem: Suppose the demand curve of face masks is a downward-sloping straight line. When the price of face masks falls from $5 to $4, consumers' total expenditure on face masks remains unchanged. If the price of face masks falls further from $4 to $3, consumers' total expenditure on face masks _____.

choices.text: may increase, decrease or remain unchanged.

questions.explanation: Along a straight-line demand curve, demand becomes less elastic as price falls. Below the unit-elastic point, a further price fall lowers total expenditure.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the tax burden
questions.stem:
The initial equilibrium price of pineapples is $5. Suppose the government imposes a per unit tax of $4 on pineapples. If the elasticity of demand for pineapples is _____ than their elasticity of supply, the new equilibrium price can be _____.

(1) higher ...... $6
(2) higher ...... $8
(3) lower ...... $7
(4) lower ...... $8
questions.explanation: If demand is more elastic than supply, consumers bear a smaller part of the $4 tax and price may rise to $6. If demand is less elastic than supply, consumers bear a larger part and price may rise to $8.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following market demand and supply schedules of Good X.

choices.text: If a price ceiling is set at $10, the quantity transacted of Good X will be 140 units.
If a production quota is set at 40 units, the price and quantity transacted of Good X will remain unchanged.
If a per-unit subsidy of $5 is provided, the equilibrium price of Good X will decrease to $20.
If a per-unit tax of $5 is imposed, the net-of-tax revenue of Good X will decrease to $1 600.

questions.explanation: The original transaction quantity is 80 at a consumer price of $25. With a $5 unit tax and perfectly inelastic supply at 80 units, producers' net-of-tax revenue becomes ($25 - $5) x 80 = $1 600.

visuals.caption: Market demand and supply schedules of Good X

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the market of Good X is correct?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the supply and demand curves of a good.
questions.explanation: Both P1 and P2 are below the equilibrium price, so the price floor is not effective in either case. The market price and quantity transacted remain unchanged.

visuals.alt: Supply and demand diagram with price floor levels P1 and P2 below the market equilibrium.
visuals.caption: Price floor

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the government changes the price floor from P1 to P2. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) The marginal benefit of the last unit of the good will decrease.
(2) There will be an increase in the excess demand for the good.
(3) Consumers' total expenditure on the good will decrease.
(4) The quantity transacted of the good will remain unchanged.

questions.keyPoint: Identify the type of market structure
questions.stem: The table below shows the distribution of market share of Mandatory Provident Fund trustees in Hong Kong in 2021.

choices.text: oligopoly ...... sellers are interdependent in their marketing strategies
oligopoly ...... there are a few dominant sellers in the market
monopolistic competition ...... there are many sellers in the market
monopolistic competition ...... services provided by different sellers are heterogeneous

questions.explanation: The data show a few trustees with large market shares, so the market can be identified as an oligopoly on the basis of a few dominant sellers.

visuals.caption: Market share of Mandatory Provident Fund trustees in Hong Kong in 2021

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, we can conclude that the above market is an example of _____ because _____.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram about the market of local vegetables in an economy.

choices.text: can be caused by an increase in the price of local vegetables
will raise the marginal cost of the last unit of local vegetables
can be caused by a decrease in the sales tax on imported vegetables

questions.explanation: Imported vegetables are substitutes for local vegetables. A lower sales tax on imported vegetables lowers their price and can reduce the demand for local vegetables.

visuals.alt: Demand for local vegetables shifts left from D0 to D1.
visuals.caption: Local vegetables market

questions.postVisualStem: The shift of the demand curve from D0 to D1 _____.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: The provision of a per-unit production subsidy on a good will lead to _____.

choices.text: a fall in the producer surplus of the good
a rise in consumers' total expenditure on the good
a rise in the total social surplus of the good
a rise in the total revenue including the subsidy of the good

questions.explanation: A per-unit production subsidy raises the amount received by producers per unit including the subsidy, so total revenue including the subsidy rises.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the supply and demand curves of Good Z.
questions.explanation: With the price ceiling, quantity supplied at P1 is below the efficient quantity after demand increases. This is under-production, and the deadweight loss is area abc.

visuals.alt: Supply and demand diagram of Good Z with price ceiling P1 and demand shifting from D1 to D2.
visuals.caption: Price ceiling and deadweight loss

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose a price ceiling is set at P1. When the demand for Good Z increases from D1 to D2, there is _____ and the deadweight loss is _____.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem:
Plastic straws are a major source of plastic waste. Most plastic straws would break into smaller particles, releasing chemicals which threaten the environment.

Based on the above information, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: The use of plastic straws results in negative externality, and the quantity of plastic straws used is below the efficient level.
To maximise total social surplus, governments around the world should completely ban the use of plastic straws.
Charging a lump-sum tax on the businesses that provide plastic straws to customers must restore efficiency in the market of plastic straws.
Granting a per-unit subsidy to the producers of environmentally-friendly paper straws tends to reduce the deadweight loss in the market of plastic straws.

questions.explanation: Plastic straws create negative external costs, so their market quantity tends to exceed the efficient level. Subsidising a substitute such as paper straws can reduce plastic straw use and the related deadweight loss.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem: Study the following data about an economy.
questions.explanation: The Gini coefficient increased. A shift from progressive to regressive taxation and wider salaries tax bands can raise post-tax income inequality, while more transfers to low-income households would tend to lower it.

visuals.caption: Gini coefficient based on post-tax post-social transfer household income
rows: Gini coefficient based on post-tax post-social transfer household income

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following are possible explanations for the above change from 2016 to 2021?

(1) The progressive tax system changed to a regressive one.
(2) The tax bands of the progressive salaries tax are widened.
(3) The transfer payments provided to the low-income households increased.

questions.topicGroup: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.keyPoint: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.stem: Which of the following would be included in the calculation of Hong Kong's gross domestic product (GDP)?

choices.text: the value of a second-hand bicycle purchased by a student
the commission earned by a broker from transactions of shares for his clients
the capital gain earned by a household from reselling a residential property
the allowance under the Comprehensive Social Security Assistance Scheme received by the needy

questions.explanation: GDP includes the value of currently produced final goods and services. The broker's commission is a current service, while second-hand goods, capital gains and transfer payments are excluded.

questions.keyPoint: Production/value added approach
questions.stem: The following diagram shows a production chain of smartphones in an economy.
questions.explanation: Value added at factor cost is local materials $60 plus manufacturers' value added $(100 + 460 - 60) plus retailers' value added $(640 - 40 - 460 - X). Thus 700 - X = 560, so X = 140.

visuals.alt: Production chain of smartphones with local materials, manufacturers, retailers, consumers and imported smartphones.
visuals.caption: Smartphone production chain

questions.postVisualStem: If the contribution of the above production chain to the economy's GDP at factor cost is $560, the value of X is _____.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: The following table shows some data of an economy in a certain year.
questions.explanation: Net factor income from abroad is negative, so GDP exceeds GNI. GDP at factor cost equals GDP at market price minus indirect taxes plus subsidies, so it is higher here. A GDP deflator above 100 means nominal GDP is higher than real GDP.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the economy are correct?

(1) The GDP is higher than the gross national income (GNI).
(2) The GDP at factor cost is higher than the GDP at market price.
(3) The nominal GDP is higher than the real GDP.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: Study the following data of a country.

choices.text: More employed persons emigrate to other countries.
The government raises the effective minimum wage rate.
The government raises the amount of unemployment benefits.

questions.explanation: The unemployed population fell but the unemployment rate rose, which is consistent with a fall in the labour force caused by employed persons emigrating.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following best explains the above changes of the country from 2020 to 2021?

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Suppose there is a fall in the national income of a country's major trading partner. Which of the following would offset its effect on the aggregate output of the country?

choices.text: The government increases the amount of tax rebate on salaries tax.
The government imposes stricter quarantine requirements for inbound travellers.
Firms become pessimistic about the economic prospect of the country.
Landlords raise the rent of their office and retail premises.

questions.explanation: A fall in a trading partner's income reduces exports and aggregate demand. A larger salaries tax rebate raises disposable income and consumption, offsetting the fall in aggregate demand.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: Suppose the stock market becomes more volatile. Which of the following diagrams best illustrates the effect of the above change on the money market?
questions.explanation: A more volatile stock market raises the desire to hold money as a safer asset, so asset demand for money shifts to the right.

visuals.alt: Four money market diagrams showing possible changes in asset demand and transaction demand for money.
visuals.caption: Money market

questions.postVisualStem:
Ma = asset demand for money
Mt = transaction demand for money

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand (AD) curves, the short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curves and the long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve of an economy. The economy initially operates at point E.

choices.text: The government offers more retraining programmes to workers.

questions.explanation: A higher desire to save reduces consumption and aggregate demand. In the long run, factor prices adjust downward and SRAS increases, moving the economy to F at a lower price level.

visuals.alt: AD-SRAS-LRAS diagram with long-run equilibrium moving from E to F on the LRAS curve.

questions.keyPoint: How central bank functions are carried out in
questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority?

choices.text: providing loans to licensed banks and the public

questions.explanation: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority manages Hong Kong's Exchange Fund and foreign currency reserves. It does not determine market interest rates or collect taxes.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem: Which of the following will lead to an increase in monetary base?

choices.text: The central bank raises the discount rate.
The central bank reduces the required reserve ratio.
The central bank buys government bonds from the public.
The central bank replaces some of the paper banknotes in circulation with polymer banknotes.

questions.explanation: When the central bank buys government bonds from the public, it injects base money into the economy, increasing the monetary base.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem:
Carmen withdraws HK$600 000 from her savings deposits with a licensed bank in Hong Kong. She puts one-third of the amount into her current account and remits the remaining amount overseas.

What will be the immediate effects of the above actions on the Hong Kong dollar money supply?

(1) M1 increases by HK$200 000.
(2) M2 decreases by HK$600 000.
(3) M3 decreases by HK$400 000.
questions.explanation: Moving HK$200 000 into a current account raises M1 by that amount. The HK$400 000 remitted overseas leaves Hong Kong dollar deposits, so M3 falls by HK$400 000; M2 does not fall by HK$600 000 because HK$200 000 remains in a current deposit.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Refer to the following balance sheet of a banking system which has excess reserves of $125 million.

choices.text: If the banking system loans out all the excess reserves, the amount of reserves will decrease after the deposit creation process is completed.
If the banking system loans out all the excess reserves, the maximum possible increase in loans will be $500 million.
If the public withdraws $125 million from the banking system and holds it as cash, the amount of excess reserves will decrease to zero immediately.

questions.explanation: Required reserves are $375 million, so the required reserve ratio is 25%. Lending out $125 million of excess reserves can support a maximum deposit and loan expansion of $125 million / 25% = $500 million.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the above banking system is correct?

questions.keyPoint: Taxation in
questions.stem:
Bobby lives in his newly bought property in Wan Chai. He gains $100 000 from trading shares in the stock market of Hong Kong.

Based on the above information, Bobby needs to pay _____ to the Hong Kong Government.

(1) capital gains tax
(2) property tax
(3) rates
(4) stamp duty
questions.explanation: Hong Kong does not charge capital gains tax, and owner-occupied property is not subject to property tax on rental income. A property owner pays rates, and share transactions involve stamp duty.

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: Which of the following diagrams describe a progressive tax?
questions.explanation: A progressive tax has an average tax rate that rises with taxable income. Diagrams (2) and (4) show a rising average tax rate.

visuals.alt: Four diagrams showing tax payment or average tax rate against taxable income.
visuals.caption: Progressive tax

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: According to the classical quantity theory of money, if the money supply of an economy increases by 8%, _____.

choices.text: the government's income tax revenue will increase by 8%
the nominal output will increase by 8%
the real output will increase by 8%
the price level may increase by less than 8%

questions.explanation: With velocity assumed constant, the quantity theory implies that the same percentage increase in money supply leads to the same percentage increase in nominal output.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: The table below shows the Composite Consumer Price Index of Hong Kong.

choices.text: a lender who provided a one-year loan to an enterprise at a fixed interest rate in 2020
an employee whose salary in 2021 was adjusted according to the inflation rate
a student who paid a fixed tuition fee in both 2020 and 2021
an elderly who held time deposits in a bank from 2020 to 2021

questions.explanation: The price level rose unexpectedly. A person paying a fixed nominal fee gains because the real value of that payment falls.

visuals.caption: Composite Consumer Price Index of Hong Kong

questions.keyPoint: Effects of inflation and deflation on different aspects
questions.stem: The following chart shows the changes in the GDP deflator of a country.
questions.explanation: The GDP deflator was falling, so the purchasing power of money increased and nominal GDP growth was lower than real GDP growth. The cost of living did not increase.

Based on the above chart, which of the following statements about the country during the above period are correct?

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Which of the following would result in a rise in the price level of an economy and a fall in its employment level at the same time?

choices.text: The government reduces the profits tax rate.
The economy's currency appreciates against the currencies of its trading partners.
The government increases its spending on research and development.
The prices of imported raw materials increase.

questions.explanation: Higher imported raw material prices raise production costs and reduce short-run aggregate supply, causing a higher price level and lower employment.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem:
Which of the following are examples of an expansionary fiscal policy?

(1) increasing the child allowance of salaries tax
(2) launching a consumption voucher scheme
(3) lowering required reserve ratio
questions.explanation: Increasing tax allowances and launching consumption vouchers are expansionary fiscal policies. Lowering the required reserve ratio is monetary policy.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: The following table shows the amount of apples or peaches that Country A and Country B can produce with one unit of resources.
questions.explanation: Country A's opportunity cost of 1 apple is 80/100 = 0.8 peaches. Country B can produce more apples, so it has an absolute advantage. Country B's opportunity cost of 1 apple is 0.5 peaches, so 0.7 peaches is a mutually beneficial terms of trade.

visuals.caption: Amount produced with one unit of resources

questions.postVisualStem:
According to the above table, which of the following statements are correct?

(1) The opportunity cost of producing 1 unit of apples is 0.8 units of peaches in Country A.
(2) Country B has an absolute advantage in producing apples.
(3) A mutually beneficial terms of trade can be 1 unit of apples = 0.7 units of peaches.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the market of Good X in a small open economy. The economy has imposed a per unit tariff on Good X.

choices.text: the tariff revenue of Good X will remain unchanged
the domestic price of Good X will increase
the quantity of Good X consumed domestically will remain unchanged
the quantity of Good X produced domestically will decrease

questions.explanation: With a fixed tariff, a fall in the world price lowers the domestic price facing consumers and producers. Domestic production therefore decreases.

visuals.alt: Tariff diagram for Good X in a small open economy with Pw and Pw + t.
visuals.caption: Per-unit tariff

questions.postVisualStem: If the world price of Good X decreases, _____.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: Which of the following is included in the calculation of the balance of Hong Kong's current account?

choices.text: A Mainland billionaire spends HK$20 billion building a shopping mall in Hong Kong.
A Japanese resident buys an air ticket to Hong Kong from an airline company in Japan.
A Hong Kong resident receives interest from US Government bonds.
A Hong Kong investor buys shares issued by a German listed company.

questions.explanation: Interest received by a Hong Kong resident from foreign bonds is investment income, which is part of the current account.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of trade surplus and deficit
questions.stem: The figure below shows the values of a country's exports and imports of goods from 2018 to 2022.
questions.explanation: From 2020 to 2021, imports rose and exports rose by more, so the visible trade surplus increased at the same time.

visuals.caption: Exports and imports of goods

questions.postVisualStem: From year _____ to year _____, the country had an increase in the value of imports of goods and an increase in visible trade surplus at the same time.

questions.keyPoint: 識別及計算選擇一個選項時涉及的成本（顯性成本及隱含成本）
questions.stem:
張先生兩年前以 $5 000 000 購入一個餐廳鋪位，並於該鋪位出售「兩餸飯」。由於他的店鋪附近最近開了一些新餐廳，導致他每月的利潤由 $30 000 下降至 $10 000。一名商人提出以每月 $15 000 租金租用張先生的鋪位。

下列哪項屬張先生繼續於該鋪位經營「兩餸飯」生意的機會成本？

choices.text: 每月減少了的 $20 000 利潤

questions.explanation: 購入價是沉沒成本。繼續經營即放棄出租鋪位可得的租金，所以每月租金屬機會成本。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 志傑是一名香港中六學生，他打算到韓國畢業旅行。以下哪項會令他到韓國畢業旅行的成本下降？

choices.text: 由韓國飛往香港的回程航班延誤。
韓國的新冠肺炎確診宗數大幅上升。
韓國的酒店服務比他預期的好。

questions.explanation: 港元兌南韓圜升值，代表以港元計算在韓國消費較便宜，會降低旅程的金錢成本。

questions.chapterTitle: 三個基本經濟問題與私有產權
questions.keyPoint: 私有產權的意思和在市場經濟中的重要性
questions.stem:
一支香港樂隊採用了實名登記制發售其演唱會門票。這些門票不可轉讓，所以炒賣的機會減少。

以下哪項／哪些有關上述實名登記制的陳述是正確的？

(1) 這是解決「生產什麼」的問題的一個機制。
(2) 在該機制下，門票的私有產權會被削弱。
(3) 在該機制下，門票的分配並不涉及非價格競爭。
questions.explanation: 門票不可轉讓削弱了轉讓權，所以私有產權被削弱。制度處理的是門票分配，不是「生產什麼」，而且若需求大於供應，仍可能涉及非價格競爭。

questions.topicGroup: 區分實證性陳述和規範性陳述
questions.keyPoint: 區分實證性陳述和規範性陳述
questions.stem:
以下哪項／哪些是規範性陳述？

(1) 推行消費券計劃會導致通脹。
(2) 宣傳旅遊業是刺激經濟增長的最適切的途徑。
(3) 政府應繼續吸引內地企業來港投資。
questions.explanation: 「最適切」和「應」涉及價值判斷，屬規範性陳述；(1) 是可驗證的因果陳述。

questions.keyPoint: 區分免費物品及經濟物品
questions.stem: 下列哪項有關物品分類的陳述是正確的？

choices.text: 街頭藝人所用的樂器是共用品，因為用這些樂器演奏的音樂可被多人同時享用。
課本是私用品，因為生產多一個單位的課本的邊際成本是正數。
香港故宮文化博物館展出的藝術品是消費者物品，因為它們的生產涉及成本。
受歡迎的免費網上英語學習影片是經濟物品，因為它們的數量不足夠滿足人們的慾望。

questions.explanation: 即使使用者不用付價格，只要數量不足以滿足慾望，便有稀少性和機會成本，屬經濟物品。

questions.keyPoint: 勞力供應
questions.stem: 下列哪項會同時提高某經濟的勞力供應和平均勞工生產力？

choices.text: 政府提高失業救濟金額。
免費教育延伸至大學課程。
更多廠商安裝先進的生產設備。
一項為高技術人才而設的入境計劃的配額增加。

questions.explanation: 增加高技術人才入境配額會增加勞力供應，亦可提高整體工人的平均生產力。

questions.keyPoint: 勞力的流動性
questions.stem: 若 _____，該經濟中勞工的職業流動性會下降。

choices.text: 居於偏遠地區的工人獲發交通津貼
更多工作需要專門化的技能
法定退休年齡由 65 歲提高至 70 歲
政府提供更多免費的再培訓課程

questions.explanation: 更多工作要求專門化技能，工人較難轉換職業，職業流動性會下降。

兩家廠商的東主在轉讓其擁有權時，均需獲得其他東主同意。
甲廠商可能比乙廠商享有較低的利得稅稅率。
乙廠商是獨立法人而甲廠商不是。

questions.explanation: 甲廠商特徵較接近非有限公司，乙廠商特徵較接近公眾有限公司。非有限公司可能享有較低的利得稅稅率。

questions.topicGroup: 貨幣價格（名義價格）和相對價格
questions.keyPoint: 將相對價格或全價格應用於需求定律，以解釋特定現象
questions.stem: 下列哪項與需求定律並不相符？

choices.text: 當某主題公園降低其門票價格，平均而言，遊客於該主題公園逗留更長時間。
當人們預期按揭利率上升，私人住宅單位的價格與交易量同時下降。
相比居於超市附近的顧客，居所遠離超市的顧客每次到超市時傾向購買較多物品。
若香港政府縮短入境人士的隔離檢疫期，訪港旅客人數會上升。

questions.explanation: 需求定律關於物品本身價格改變對需求量的影響；逗留時間增加並不等同主題公園門票需求量增加。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋相關物品價格、收入、價格預期、天氣、市場消費者人數等因素如何影響個別需求及市場需求
questions.stem:
當物品 X 和 Y 是 _____，物品 X 的價格下降會導致 _____。

(1) 競爭性需求 ...... 物品 Y 的價格下降
(2) 聯合需求 ...... 物品 Y 市場上的生產者盈餘下降
(3) 競爭性供應 ...... 物品 Y 市場上的消費者盈餘上升
(4) 聯合供應 ...... 消費者對物品 Y 的總支出下降
questions.explanation: 競爭性需求即替代品需求，X 價格下降會減少 Y 的需求並令 Y 價格下降。競爭性供應下，X 價格下降可令資源轉往生產 Y，Y 的供應上升，消費者盈餘增加。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋需求改變和供應改變如何影響均衡價格和數量
questions.stem: 下圖顯示電動車的供需曲線。原初的均衡點是 E0。
questions.explanation: 生產成本上升令供應減少，供應曲線左移至 S2；信心提高令需求增加，需求曲線右移至 D1。新均衡點是 E2。

questions.chapterTitle: 需求和供應的價格彈性
questions.keyPoint: 影響需求價格彈性的因素
questions.stem:
半導體晶片是生產智能電話的關鍵組件。

由於全球半導體晶片短缺，智能電話的銷售量有 10% 的變動，而智能電話的價格則上升了 20%。下列哪項最能解釋上述智能電話價格與銷售量的轉變？

choices.text: 智能電話沒有接近的替代品。
智能電話生產商有剩餘的產能。
消費者在智能電話的開支佔其總開支的比例高。
生產智能電話的工人不容易招聘。

questions.explanation: 供應減少時價格變動比例大於數量變動，反映需求較缺乏彈性；沒有接近替代品可解釋需求彈性較低。

questions.chapterTitle: 需求和供應的價格彈性
questions.keyPoint: 需求價格彈性和總收入之間的關係
questions.stem: 假設口罩的需求曲線是一條向下傾斜的直線。當口罩價格由 $5 下降至 $4 時，消費者對口罩的總支出維持不變。若口罩價格再由 $4 下降至 $3，消費者對口罩的總支出 _____。

choices.text: 可能上升、下降或維持不變。

questions.explanation: 沿一條直線需求曲線向下移動時，需求會愈來愈缺乏彈性。在單一彈性點以下再降價，總支出會下降。

questions.topicGroup: 物品及服務的稅項（銷售稅）
questions.keyPoint: 了解需求及供應價格彈性如何影響稅項負擔分配
questions.stem:
菠蘿原初的均衡價格為 $5。假設政府對菠蘿開徵 $4 的從量稅。若菠蘿的需求彈性 _____ 其供應彈性，新的均衡價格可以是 _____。

(1) 高於 ...... $6
(2) 高於 ...... $8
(3) 低於 ...... $7
(4) 低於 ...... $8
questions.explanation: 若需求彈性高於供應彈性，消費者承擔較少稅項，價格可升至 $6；若需求彈性低於供應彈性，消費者承擔較多稅項，價格可升至 $8。

questions.topicGroup: 物品及服務的稅項（銷售稅）
questions.keyPoint: 分析從量稅對價格、交易量及總收入等的影響，並說明生產者和消費者的稅項負擔分配
questions.stem: 參閱以下物品 X 的市場供需表。

choices.text: 若價格上限設於 $10，物品 X 的交易量會是 140 單位。
若生產配額設於 40 單位，物品 X 的價格及交易量會維持不變。
若提供 $5 的從量補貼，物品 X 的均衡價格會下降至 $20。
若徵收 $5 的從量稅，物品 X 的除稅後總收入會下降至 $1 600。

questions.explanation: 原本交易量為 80，消費者價格為 $25。徵收 $5 從量稅而供應量固定為 80 時，生產者除稅後總收入為 ($25 - $5) x 80 = $1 600。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 負面界外效應與經濟無效率；把外部成本內在化
questions.stem:
塑膠飲管是塑膠廢料的主要源頭。大部分塑膠飲管會分解成較細小的粒子，釋出危害環境的化學物質。

根據以上資料，下列哪項陳述是正確的？

choices.text: 塑膠飲管的使用引致負面界外影響，而塑膠飲管的使用量低於效率水平。
為達至總社會盈餘極大化，各地政府應全面禁止使用塑膠飲管。
對提供塑膠飲管予顧客的業務徵收一項定額稅，必然可以回復塑膠飲管市場的效率。
向環保紙飲管生產者提供從量補貼，傾向降低塑膠飲管市場的效率損失。

questions.explanation: 塑膠飲管帶來外部成本，市場使用量傾向高於效率水平。補貼替代品環保紙飲管可減少塑膠飲管使用量，降低相關效率損失。

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Mr Chan lives in his own apartment which is worth $8 000 000. He can sell the apartment and deposit the $8 000 000 in a bank at an interest rate of 5% per year. He can also rent out the apartment at $25 000 a month.

Based on the above information, which of the following statements are correct?

(1) When the market value of his apartment increases, the opportunity cost for Mr Chan to live in his own apartment will not be affected.
(2) When the deposit interest rate increases, the opportunity cost for Mr Chan to live in his own apartment will increase.
(3) When the rental value of his apartment increases, the opportunity cost for Mr Chan to live in his own apartment may increase.
questions.explanation: The opportunity cost is the best alternative forgone. It may be affected by the forgone bank interest and forgone rent, but not necessarily by market value alone unless it changes the best alternative return.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem:
Which of the following situations imply the existence of scarcity?

(1) People need to choose between two options.
(2) People can obtain what they want by paying the market price.
(3) People cannot obtain what they want even after queuing up for hours.
questions.explanation: Scarcity exists when wants exceed available resources, so choices, a positive market price and non-price competition such as queuing can all imply scarcity.

Seawater is a free good as people can obtain seawater free of charge.
Seawater is an inferior good as no one drinks seawater.

questions.explanation: When seawater is used by fishermen in production to keep catches alive, it is a producer good or capital good in that use.

to utilise its resources more efficiently
to ensure a steady supply of raw materials

questions.explanation: Taking over a grocery chain in Hong Kong is not mainly for securing raw materials, so that is the least likely motive.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem:
The Hong Kong Government has implemented the 'Top Talent Pass Scheme' ('高端人才通行證計劃') to attract foreign talents to work in Hong Kong. Successful applicants will be issued a two-year pass for exploring job opportunities in Hong Kong.

As a result of the implementation of the above scheme, _____.

(1) Hong Kong's labour supply will increase
(2) geographical mobility of foreign talents will increase
(3) average labour productivity of workers in Hong Kong will increase
questions.explanation: The scheme attracts talents to Hong Kong, increasing labour supply and geographical mobility. Since the scheme targets high-skilled talents, average labour productivity may also increase.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about a toy-making firm.
questions.explanation: Average labour productivity per worker-hour falls from 9 000/(250 x 8)=4.5 to 10 800/(300 x 9)=4. A lack of training and poorer management can explain the fall.

visuals.caption: Toy-making firm information
rows: Number of working hours per worker per day (hours)

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following are possible reasons for the above change in the average labour productivity of the toy-making firm?

(1) The wage payment method of the firm is changed from time rate to piece rate.
(2) The firm does not provide adequate training for new workers in Year 2.
(3) The working environment of the firm is improved in Year 2.
(4) The management of the firm becomes poorer in Year 2.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Calculate producer surplus
questions.stem: The table below shows the production costs of a price-taking firm.
questions.explanation: Total cost at 2 units is $50, so variable cost is $45 after deducting fixed cost. Total revenue is $60 and producer surplus is $60 - $45 = $15, which is the maximum.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the fixed cost of the firm is $5 and the product price is $30. The firm's maximum producer surplus is _____.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem:
Suppose a campaign successfully attracted many pilots in Mainland cities to work in Hong Kong. Meanwhile, more and more Hong Kong people travel abroad for leisure.

Which of the following diagrams best illustrates the effects of the above events?
questions.explanation: More Mainland pilots working in Hong Kong increase the supply of pilots. More Hong Kong people travelling abroad increase demand for pilots working in Hong Kong. Diagram A shows both effects in the pilot labour market.

visuals.alt: Four demand-supply diagrams for pilots working in Hong Kong and flight services in Hong Kong.
visuals.caption: Pilots and flight services

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem:
As part of the 'Happy Hong Kong' campaign, the 'Hong Kong Cinema Day' was held in April 2023, with tickets priced at HK$30 across all participating cinemas. It was reported that many people failed to buy any discounted film ticket even after queuing up for hours.

From the information above, we can infer that the quantity transacted of the discounted film tickets is _____.

choices.text: equal to the quantity supplied and smaller than the quantity demanded
equal to the quantity supplied and larger than the quantity demanded
equal to the quantity demanded and smaller than the quantity supplied
equal to the quantity demanded and larger than the quantity supplied

questions.explanation: Queuing and failure to buy tickets imply excess demand. Quantity transacted equals the smaller side, the quantity supplied, and is below quantity demanded.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Suppose the government of an economy subsidises the manufacturing of air purifiers. As a result, the price of air purifiers decreases from $1 200 to $1 000 and the quantity transacted increases from 5 000 to 8 000 units. This indicates that within the price range, the price elasticity (in absolute value) of _____ is _____.
questions.explanation: A subsidy shifts supply and causes a movement along demand. Price falls by about 16.7% while quantity demanded rises by 60%, so demand is elastic.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: When the per-unit sales tax on Good X is halved, the government's tax revenue from Good X is also halved. One possible explanation is that _____.

choices.text: the supply of Good X is perfectly elastic
the supply of Good X is perfectly inelastic
the demand for Good X is perfectly elastic
the demand for Good X is unitarily elastic

questions.explanation: If supply is perfectly inelastic, the quantity transacted is unchanged when the per-unit tax is halved. Tax revenue therefore halves.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: Suppose the government of an economy imposes an effective catch limit (quota) on Pacific bluefin tuna. If the catch limit is lowered, the marginal benefit of the last unit of Pacific bluefin tuna will _____ and consumers' total expenditure on Pacific bluefin tuna _____.
questions.explanation: A lower effective quota reduces quantity, so marginal benefit at the last unit rises. Total expenditure may rise or fall depending on elasticity over the range.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following market demand schedule of a good. The equilibrium price is $20.

choices.text: the consumers will not have any tax burden.
producers' total revenue net of tax will be $1 600.
the deadweight loss caused by the imposition of the sales tax will disappear due to the decrease in the production cost.
the government's tax revenue from the good will be $800.

questions.explanation: At the unchanged consumer price of $20, quantity demanded is 80. Tax revenue is $10 x 80 = $800.
questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the government imposes a per-unit sales tax of $10 on the good. At the same time, there is a decrease in the production cost of the good. As a result, the equilibrium price remains at $20.

Based on the above information, we can conclude that _____.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the supply curve of taxi services.

choices.text: The government lowers the taxi fares.
The government provides subsidies for citizens to use railway services.
The government reduces the quota on taxi licences.
The government amends the law to punish providers of ride-sharing services such as Uber drivers.

questions.explanation: A subsidy to railway services lowers demand for taxi services, moving the equilibrium down along the taxi supply curve from X to Y.

visuals.alt: Supply curve of taxi services with points X and Y.
visuals.caption: Taxi services supply

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following best explains the change in the equilibrium position from point X to point Y?

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about perfect competition is INCORRECT?

choices.text: The market price tends to be stable as no firm can affect the market price.
Price is the only competitive criterion in determining the distribution of goods.
The marginal cost of the last unit of all firms is equal when the firms maximise their profits.

questions.explanation: In perfect competition each firm is a price taker, but this does not imply the market price tends to be stable. The market price can still change with market demand or supply.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Maximisation of total social surplus: marginal benefit equals marginal cost
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about overproduction is/are correct?

(1) Overproduction of a good occurs when there is an excess supply of the good.
(2) Overproduction does not occur whenever the market is at equilibrium.
(3) When overproduction occurs, the marginal social cost is greater than the marginal social benefit at the last unit.
questions.explanation: Overproduction in efficiency terms means output exceeds the efficient level, where marginal social cost is greater than marginal social benefit. It can occur even at market equilibrium if external costs exist.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the supply and demand curves of a good.

choices.text: The new total social surplus is area aib.
The new total social surplus is area acdb.
The increase in deadweight loss is area ehif.
The increase in deadweight loss is area cid.

questions.explanation: Increasing the subsidy from $5 to $10 expands the inefficient quantity further. The additional deadweight loss is the area between marginal cost and marginal benefit over the extra units, ehif.

visuals.alt: Demand and supply diagram with supply curves without subsidy, with $5 subsidy and with $10 subsidy.
visuals.caption: Per-unit subsidy

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government increases the per-unit subsidy from $5 to $10. Which of the following statements is correct?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem: The following is the demand-supply diagram of Good X. Initially the price of Good X is P0.
questions.explanation: Effective price ceilings and price floors create deadweight loss and may reduce consumer surplus. A demand decrease alone does not create deadweight loss in a competitive market.

visuals.alt: Demand and supply diagram of Good X with initial equilibrium at P0 and Q0.
visuals.caption: Price controls

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following situations may reduce the consumer surplus and create a deadweight loss in the market of Good X at the same time?

(1) a decrease in the demand for Good X
(2) the imposition of an effective price ceiling on Good X
(3) the imposition of an effective price floor on Good X

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem:
In recent years, more and more people play videos loudly with their smartphones on public transport, disturbing other passengers.

Based on the above information, which of the following statements are correct?

(1) Total social surplus may decrease if playing videos loudly with smartphones on public transport is banned by the government.
(2) Economic efficiency may improve if suppliers of public transportation services designate quiet zones in their vehicles where passengers are not allowed to play videos loudly with their smartphones.
(3) The divergence between private and social costs may decrease if people playing videos loudly with their smartphones on public transport are fined.
questions.explanation: A total ban may reduce total surplus if some mutually beneficial use is prevented. Quiet zones and fines can internalise part of the external cost and improve efficiency.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem: The table below shows the Gini coefficients by industry of an economy.
questions.explanation: A lower average salary does not by itself explain within-industry inequality. More homogeneous human capital can lower inequality, while basic salary plus commission can widen income differences.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following are possible explanations for the above difference in the Gini coefficient?

(1) The salaries of workers in the accommodation and food services industry are lower than that of professionals in the finance and insurance industry.
(2) Compared to professionals in the finance and insurance industry, the levels of human capital tend to be more homogeneous among workers in the accommodation and food services industry.
(3) The wage payment method for professionals in the finance and insurance industry is mostly basic salary plus commission while that for workers in the accommodation and food services industry is mostly time rate.

questions.keyPoint: Expenditure approach
questions.stem: Refer to the following data of an economy.
questions.explanation: GDP at market price by expenditure is C + gross domestic capital formation + G + net exports of goods and services = 100 + (20 + 11 - 5) + 30 + 60 + (40 - 80) = 176.
questions.postVisualStem: The gross domestic product (GDP) at market price is $_____ million.

questions.keyPoint: Growth rate of GDP
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the nominal GDP growth rates and the inflation rates of an economy.
questions.explanation: Inflation is positive in every year, so the price level rises. Nominal GDP growth is higher than real GDP growth by the inflation rate, but real GDP growth is negative in 2020 because nominal growth is lower than inflation.

visuals.alt: Line chart showing nominal GDP growth rates and inflation rates from 2017 to 2022.
visuals.caption: Nominal GDP growth and inflation

questions.postVisualStem:
Based on the above information, we can conclude that from 2017 to 2022, _____ in the economy.

(1) the real GDP increased in all consecutive years
(2) the price level increased in all consecutive years
(3) the nominal GDP growth rate was always higher than the real GDP growth rate

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem:
Suppose the unemployment rate of an economy is 5%. Which of the following situations would lead to a decrease in the unemployment rate of the economy?

(1) Foreign workers are imported to fill the vacancies in various industries.
(2) 96% of the new university graduates who enter the labour market are employed.
(3) Some underemployed workers work for more hours.
questions.explanation: Filling vacancies with workers and having a 96% employment rate among new labour-market entrants can lower the unemployment rate. More hours for underemployed workers do not directly reduce the number unemployed.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: If there is an increase in the tax allowance of salaries tax, transactions demand for money will _____ and the equilibrium nominal interest rate will _____.
questions.explanation: A higher tax allowance raises disposable income, increasing transactions demand for money. With money supply unchanged, the nominal interest rate rises.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Suppose the central bank of Country A lowers the discount rate. Which of the following situations would weaken the effect of the above policy on the aggregate output of Country A in the short run?

choices.text: The use of digital money becomes more popular in Country A.
Some major trading partners of Country A experience an economic recession.
The government of Country A relaxes the restrictions on the importation of foreign workers.
The government of Country A increases its investment on local infrastructure.

questions.explanation: Lowering the discount rate is expansionary. Recession among trading partners reduces exports and aggregate demand, weakening the short-run output effect.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.stem: Suppose a large number of highly skilled foreign talents have been admitted to live and work in Hong Kong. Which of the following diagrams best illustrates the effects on Hong Kong's economy?
questions.explanation: Highly skilled foreign talents increase productive capacity, shifting LRAS right. Their settlement can also increase aggregate demand. Diagram B shows both effects.

visuals.alt: Four AD-AS diagrams showing possible shifts in AD, SRAS or LRAS.
visuals.caption: Foreign talents and the macroeconomy

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curves of a country.

choices.text: The government of the country provides subsidies to the core technology industries.
The currency of the country appreciates against that of its trading partners.
A large-scale hill fire occurs in the country and leads to massive destruction of production facilities.
The central bank of the country raises the money supply.

questions.explanation: A large-scale fire destroying production facilities reduces short-run aggregate supply and shifts SRAS left.

visuals.alt: SRAS curve shifts left from SRAS0 to SRAS1.
visuals.caption: SRAS shift

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following is a possible reason for the above shift of the SRAS curve from SRAS0 to SRAS1?

questions.keyPoint: Qualities of good money
questions.stem:
9999 gold is better than diamond in performing the _____ function of money because the former has a higher _____.

(1) medium of exchange ...... divisibility
(2) unit of account ...... homogeneity
(3) store of value ...... portability
questions.explanation: Gold is generally more divisible than diamonds, helping it act as a medium of exchange, and is more homogeneous, helping it act as a unit of account.

questions.keyPoint: How central bank functions are carried out in
questions.stem:
Which of the following are functions of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority?

(1) acting as the lender of last resort for commercial banks
(2) setting the prime rate (最優惠利率) of bank loans
(3) issuing Hong Kong dollar coins
questions.explanation: The HKMA acts as lender of last resort and issues Hong Kong dollar coins on behalf of the government. Prime rates are set by banks, not the HKMA.

questions.keyPoint: Definitions of M1, M2 and M3 in
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the relationship between money supply M1 and M2 in Hong Kong.

choices.text: all types of deposits with licensed banks, restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies
time deposits with restricted licence banks and negotiable certificates of deposit issued by restricted licence banks held by non-bank public
savings deposits and time deposits with licensed banks and negotiable certificates of deposits issued by licensed banks held by non-bank public
reserves of licensed banks, restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies

questions.explanation: K is the part of M2 not included in M1. It includes savings deposits and time deposits with licensed banks and negotiable certificates of deposit issued by licensed banks held by the non-bank public.

visuals.alt: Diagram showing M1 as currency in public circulation plus demand deposits inside M2, with K outside M1.
visuals.caption: M1 and M2

questions.postVisualStem: In the above diagram, M2 = M1 + K. Which of the following are components of K?

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The table below shows the balance sheet of a banking system. Suppose there are excess reserves of $20 million in the banking system and the public always holds a fixed amount of cash.

choices.text: The reserves of the banking system become $20 million.
The excess reserves of the banking system become $16 million.
The banking system has a reserve shortage of $8 million.
The amount of deposits in the banking system becomes $200 million.

questions.explanation: Required reserves are $20 million, so the required reserve ratio is 20%. A $20 million loan increase creates $20 million deposits. Required reserves become $24 million, leaving $16 million excess reserves.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose some banks lend out their excess reserves. After deposit creation, the loans in the banking system increase by $20 million. Which of the following statements about the banking system is correct?

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The table below shows the monetary data of a country. The public always holds a fixed amount of cash.
questions.explanation: Deposits are $80 million and reserves are 25% x $80 million = $20 million, so the monetary base is $35 million. Required reserves are $16 million after deducting excess reserves, giving a 20% required reserve ratio and a multiplier of 5. Full lending raises deposits by $20 million and money supply to $115 million.
questions.postVisualStem:
Based on the above information, which of the following statements are correct?

(1) The monetary base is $35 million.
(2) The maximum banking multiplier is 5.
(3) When all banks are fully loaned up, the maximum amount of money supply is $115 million.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Nominal interest rate as the (opportunity) cost of holding money
questions.explanation: The nominal interest rate on bonds is the opportunity cost of holding money. Holding money has a nominal return of 0%, so its expected real return is 0% - 4% = -4%.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, the _____ of holding money is 6%, and the expected real rate of return of holding _____ is -4%.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: Which of the following about the quantity theory of money is correct?

choices.text: An increase in money supply will not affect the nominal output in the long run.
If the money supply growth rate is constant, the price level will also be constant in the long run.
If the price level is constant, a decrease in real output will lead to a decrease in money supply.
If the real output growth rate is zero, the price level growth rate will be equal to the money supply growth rate.

questions.explanation: With velocity constant, money supply growth equals price level growth plus real output growth. If real output growth is zero, price level growth equals money supply growth.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: Which of the following tax systems tend to raise the post-tax Gini coefficient of an economy?
questions.explanation: Regressive tax systems tend to raise post-tax inequality. Diagram (1) is regressive and diagram (3) is a lump-sum tax, which also tends to be regressive in effect.

visuals.alt: Four tax system diagrams relating average tax rate or tax payment to taxable income.
visuals.caption: Tax systems

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem:
A contractionary monetary policy is adopted in China when

(1) the People's Bank of China (中國人民銀行) increases the required reserve ratio of commercial banks.
(2) the People's Bank of China cuts the interest rate on its loans to commercial banks.
(3) the Chinese Government raised the tax rates of the individual income tax.
questions.explanation: Increasing the required reserve ratio is contractionary monetary policy. Cutting the lending rate is expansionary, and raising income tax is fiscal policy.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem:
Which of the following measures may increase the aggregate output and reduce the balance of payments deficits at the same time?

(1) to set up night markets to attract foreign tourists
(2) to construct infrastructure by importing raw materials from foreign countries
(3) to launch a promotion campaign to attract more investment from foreign countries
questions.explanation: Attracting foreign tourists raises exports of services and AD. Attracting foreign investment improves the capital and financial account and may raise AD. Importing raw materials worsens the balance of payments deficit initially.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: In an open economy, if the government raises the income tax rate, the income tax revenue _____ and the total import value _____.

choices.text: will increase ...... may increase or decrease
will decrease ...... may increase or decrease
may increase or decrease ...... will increase
may increase or decrease ...... will decrease

questions.explanation: A higher income tax rate may raise or lower tax revenue depending on the tax base response. It reduces disposable income and tends to reduce imports.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: The following table shows the outputs of books and smartphones of Country Y.
questions.explanation: Producing 120 extra smartphones costs 60 books, so the opportunity cost of one smartphone is 0.5 books. With a gain of 0.2 books per smartphone, the terms of trade are 0.7 books per smartphone.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose for each unit of smartphones traded, the gain to Country Y is 0.2 units of books. The terms of trade for 1 unit of smartphones is _____ units of books.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the market of Good X in a small open economy. A per-unit tariff is imposed on Good X in the economy.

choices.text: the domestic price of Good X will remain unchanged
the import value net of tariff of Good X will increase
the quantity of Good X produced domestically will increase
the tariff revenue of Good X may increase

questions.explanation: With a tariff, a rise in world price raises the domestic price and encourages more domestic production.

visuals.alt: Tariff diagram for Good X in a small open economy with Pw and Pw plus t.
visuals.caption: Per-unit tariff

questions.postVisualStem: If the world price of Good X increases, _____.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of trade surplus and deficit
questions.stem: Refer to the following balance of payments data of an economy.

choices.text: the total value of exports of goods in 2021 was larger than that in 2020
there was a current account surplus in 2020
there was a balance of payments surplus in 2021
the value of exports of services was larger than the value of imports of services in both 2020 and 2021

questions.explanation: A positive balance on services means exports of services exceed imports of services. This is true in both 2020 and 2021.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above data, we can conclude that _____.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: The following table shows the change in the exchange rate of Hong Kong dollar (HKD) against Renminbi (RMB).

choices.text: an appreciation of US dollar against Renminbi
an increase in the total value of imports from the Mainland to Hong Kong in terms of Hong Kong dollar
an increase in the competitiveness of the Mainland's goods exported to Hong Kong
an increase in the production cost of construction companies in Hong Kong which import construction materials from the Mainland

questions.explanation: HKD appreciates against RMB, so Mainland goods become cheaper in HKD and more competitive in Hong Kong.
questions.postVisualStem: The above change in the exchange rate would lead to _____.

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem:
陳先生居住在自己擁有的住宅單位，該單位價值 $8 000 000。他可以出售該單位，並將所得的 $8 000 000 存入銀行，以年利率 5% 來收取利息。他亦可以將該單位出租，每月收取租金 $25 000。

根據上述資料，下列哪些陳述是正確的？

(1) 當陳先生的住宅單位的市值上升時，他居住在自己擁有的住宅單位的機會成本不會受影響。
(2) 當存款利率上升時，陳先生居住在自己擁有的住宅單位的機會成本會上升。
(3) 當陳先生的住宅單位的租值上升時，他居住在自己擁有的住宅單位的機會成本可能上升。
questions.explanation: 機會成本是被放棄的最佳選擇。銀行利息和租金上升都可能令機會成本上升，但單位市值上升本身未必影響最佳被放棄選擇的收益。

questions.keyPoint: 稀少性的意思
questions.stem:
下列哪些情況意味著稀少性的存在？

(1) 人們須從兩個選項中擇其一。
(2) 人們可支付市價以獲得想要的東西。
(3) 人們即使排隊輪候數小時仍未能獲得想要的東西。
questions.explanation: 稀少性表示資源不足以滿足所有慾望；需要取捨、要付市價，以及要排隊競爭都反映稀少性存在。

questions.keyPoint: 生產者物品及消費品
questions.stem: 下列哪項關於海水的陳述是正確的？

choices.text: 當漁民用海水保持漁獲鮮活時，海水是資本物品。
因為政府提供海水予公眾作沖廁之用，所以海水是共用品。
因為人們可以免費獲得海水，所以海水是免費物品。
因為沒有人飲用海水，所以海水是劣等物品。

questions.explanation: 漁民用海水保持漁獲鮮活時，海水被用於生產過程，是生產者物品或資本物品。

questions.chapterTitle: 三個基本經濟問題與私有產權
questions.keyPoint: 私有產權的意思和在市場經濟中的重要性
questions.stem:
當私有產權被削弱時，_____。

(1) 資源被分配到其最高價值的用途的可能性較低
(2) 從資產所衍生的收入很可能減少
(3) 非價格競爭較有可能出現
questions.explanation: 私有產權削弱會降低有效使用和保養資產的誘因，亦令非價格競爭較可能出現，所以三項均正確。

questions.keyPoint: 私人廠商的分類：獨資、合夥、私人有限公司及公眾有限公司
questions.stem:

questions.keyPoint: 勞力供應
questions.stem:
香港政府推出「高端人才通行證計劃」，以吸引境外人才來港工作。成功申請者會獲發為期兩年的許可證，讓他們在香港探索工作機遇。

推出上述計劃的結果是 _____。

(1) 香港的勞力供應會上升
(2) 境外人才的地域流動性會上升
(3) 在香港的工人的平均勞工生產力會上升
questions.explanation: 計劃吸引境外人才來港，會增加勞力供應和地域流動性；由於對象是高端人才，亦可令平均勞工生產力上升。

(2) 該廠商在第二年沒有為新工人提供足夠的培訓。
(3) 該廠商的工作環境在第二年有改善。
(4) 該廠商的管理在第二年變差了。

questions.stem:
作為「開心香港」活動的一部分，「全港戲院日」在 2023 年 4 月舉行，參與活動的戲院的電影票價一律為 $30。有報道指，很多人即使排隊輪候數小時，仍未能購得優惠戲票。

從以上資料可以推斷，該些優惠戲票的交易量 _____。

questions.chapterTitle: 需求和供應的價格彈性
questions.keyPoint: 需求價格彈性的類型
questions.stem: 假設某經濟的政府補貼空氣清新機的製造。因此，空氣清新機的價格由 $1 200 下降至 $1 000，而交易量則由 5 000 單位上升至 8 000 單位。這顯示了在該價格範圍內，_____ 價格彈性（以絕對值計算）的數值 _____。
questions.explanation: 補貼令供應增加，價格和數量的變化反映沿需求曲線移動。價格跌約 16.7%，需求量升 60%，所以需求具彈性。

questions.stem: 當物品 X 的從量銷售稅減半時，政府來自物品 X 的稅項收入亦減半。一個可能的解釋是 _____。

choices.text: 物品 X 的供應屬完全彈性供應
物品 X 的供應屬完全無彈性供應
物品 X 的需求屬完全彈性需求
物品 X 的需求屬單一彈性需求

questions.explanation: 若供應完全無彈性，稅率減半時交易量不變，稅項收入亦會減半。

questions.stem: 假設某經濟的政府對太平洋藍鰭金槍魚實施一項有效的捕撈限制（配額）。如果捕撈限制降低，最後一單位太平洋藍鰭金槍魚的邊際利益會 _____，而消費者在太平洋藍鰭金槍魚上的總開支 _____。

choices.text: 上升 ...... 可能下降或上升
下降 ...... 可能下降或上升

questions.explanation: 有效配額降低令交易量下降，最後一單位的邊際利益上升。總開支則視乎相關範圍的彈性而定，可能升或跌。

questions.stem: 下列哪項關於完全競爭的陳述是不正確的？

choices.text: 市場價格傾向穩定，因為沒有廠商能夠影響市場價格。

當廠商利潤極大化時，所有廠商的最後一單位的邊際成本相等。

questions.explanation: 完全競爭下個別廠商不能影響市場價格，但市場價格仍會因市場需求或供應改變而改變，所以不一定傾向穩定。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 總社會盈餘達致最大：邊際利益等於邊際成本
questions.stem:
下列哪項／些關於過度生產的陳述是正確的？

(1) 當某物品有超額供應時，該物品會出現過度生產。
(2) 每當市場處於均衡狀態時，便不會出現過度生產。
(3) 當過度生產出現時，最後一單位的邊際社會成本大於邊際社會利益。
questions.explanation: 效率分析中的過度生產是產量高於有效率水平，最後一單位邊際社會成本大於邊際社會利益；有界外成本時即使市場均衡亦可能過度生產。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 負面界外效應與經濟無效率；把外部成本內在化
questions.stem:
近年，越來越多人在公共交通工具上用智能電話大聲地播放影片，對其他乘客造成滋擾。

根據上述資料，下列哪些陳述是正確的？

(1) 假如政府禁止在公共交通工具上用智能電話大聲地播放影片，總社會盈餘可能會下降。
(2) 假如公共交通服務的供應者在其交通工具上設立靜音區，不准乘客在該區內用智能電話大聲地播放影片，經濟效率可能會有所改善。
(3) 假如在公共交通工具上用智能電話大聲地播放影片會被罰款，私人成本與社會成本的分歧可能會下降。
questions.explanation: 全面禁止可能阻止部分有淨利益的活動而令總社會盈餘下降；靜音區和罰款可令部分外部成本內在化，改善效率。

(2) 與金融及保險業專才相比，住宿及膳食服務業工人之間的人力資本水平傾向較同質。
(3) 金融及保險業專才的付酬方式多為底薪加佣金，而住宿及膳食服務業工人的付酬方式多為以時計薪。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.keyPoint: 計算失業率及辨識勞動人口
questions.stem:
假設某經濟的失業率是 5%。下列哪些情況會令該經濟的失業率下降？

(1) 輸入外勞以填補不同行業的職位空缺。
(2) 加入勞動市場的應屆大學畢業生中，96% 成功獲得聘用。
(3) 一些就業不足的工人的工時增加。
questions.explanation: 外勞填補職位及新入職畢業生就業率高於 95% 均可降低失業率；就業不足工時增加不直接減少失業人數。

questions.keyPoint: 分析貨幣需求、貨幣供應和名義利率的改變
questions.stem: 假如薪俸稅的免稅額提高，交易性貨幣需求會 _____，而均衡名義利率會 _____。
questions.explanation: 免稅額提高令可支配收入上升，交易性貨幣需求增加；貨幣供應不變時，均衡名義利率上升。

questions.topicGroup: 總需求及/或總供應改變導致均衡產出水平和物價水平的改變

questions.stem: 假設甲國的中央銀行調低貼現率。下列哪項情況會削弱上述政策在短期對甲國總產出的影響？

choices.text: 數碼貨幣的使用在甲國漸趨流行。

甲國政府放寬輸入外勞的限制。
甲國政府增加對本地基建的投資。

questions.explanation: 調低貼現率屬擴張性貨幣政策。主要貿易伙伴衰退會減少出口和總需求，削弱短期產出增加的效果。
