questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem:
Susan planned to watch a concert and bought a ticket of the concert for $1 500. Soon after Susan bought the ticket, a company offered to pay her $3 000 for a part-time job. However, the work hours of the part-time job clashed with the time of the concert. At the same time, as all tickets were sold out, her friend offered to buy her concert ticket for $1 800.

Based on the above information, at the time when Susan was deciding whether to sell the concert ticket to her friend, her opportunity cost of choosing to watch the concert would be _____.
questions.explanation: The $1 500 ticket price is a sunk cost at the time of the decision. Watching the concert gives up the $3 000 part-time job and the $1 800 resale value, so the opportunity cost is $4 800.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem:
Compared to a planned economy, _____.

(1) individuals in a market economy tend to have higher freedom when deciding the allocation of resources
(2) interest rate in a market economy tends to be higher
(3) resource allocation in a market economy tends to rely less on non-price competition
questions.explanation: A market economy gives individuals more freedom in resource allocation and relies mainly on the price mechanism, not non-price competition, to allocate resources. There is no general conclusion that its interest rate must be higher.

questions.keyPoint: Distinguishing between free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: Trees in a natural rainforest are _____.

choices.text: economic goods if people are willing to spend money to preserve the trees
free goods because they are natural resources which involve no production costs
land in Economics because they are geographically immobile
public goods if the rainforest is managed by the government

questions.explanation: If people are willing to spend resources to preserve the trees, the trees are scarce and involve opportunity cost. They are therefore economic goods.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
In response to a rise in the demand for electric vehicles, a manufacturer decided to produce more electric vehicles and sell them at a higher price.

The above decision of the manufacturer is related to the question(s) in Economics because it is related to _____.

(1) 'what to produce' ...... the choice on the quantity of outputs
(2) 'how to produce' ...... the choice on factor inputs
(3) 'for whom to produce' ...... the distribution of outputs
questions.explanation: Producing more electric vehicles concerns the quantity of output, so it is related to 'what to produce'. Selling at a higher price affects the distribution of outputs among buyers, so it is also related to 'for whom to produce'.

questions.keyPoint: Recognise the contribution of each type of production to the economy
questions.stem:
The table below shows the distribution of total production value in an economy. The total production value in this economy was higher in 2024 than that in 2014.

Based on the above information, we can conclude that from 2014 to 2024, the _____.

choices.text: proportion of workers engaged in primary production decreased
labour productivity of primary production decreased
total production value of secondary production remained unchanged
total production value of tertiary production must have increased

questions.explanation: Tertiary production's share rose from 62.5% to 72.7%, while total production value also rose. Therefore the total production value of tertiary production must have increased.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, we can conclude that from 2014 to 2024, the _____.

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem:
The table below shows the input-output relationship of a firm. The only input required for the firm's production is labour. The wage rate per unit of labour is $50.

Based on the above information, we can conclude that _____.

choices.text: the law of diminishing marginal returns applies to the firm because when the 4th unit of labour is employed, marginal product starts to diminish
when output increases from 90 units to 100 units, the firm suffers from diseconomies of scale
when output increases from 100 units to 105 units, the firm suffers a loss

questions.explanation: Labour is the only input, so increasing labour from 3 to 4 units means increasing all inputs. Input rises by 33.3%, but output rises only from 90 to 100 units, so output increases less than proportionately and diseconomies of scale occur.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, we can conclude that _____.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem:
The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a firm in a perfectly competitive market. The fixed cost of the firm is $6 and the market price is $20.

Suppose the fixed cost decreases by $4 and the marginal cost for each unit of output increases by $4. As a result, the firm's profits will _____.
questions.explanation: Originally, maximum profit is $34 at 4 or 5 units. After fixed cost falls to $2 and each marginal cost rises by $4, the new total variable costs are $8, $20, $36, $56, $80, $108 and $140, giving maximum profit $22. Profit decreases by $12.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the fixed cost decreases by $4 and the marginal cost for each unit of output increases by $4. As a result, the firm's profits will _____.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem:
Suppose the wage payment system of the salespersons in a health product company changes as follows.

Which of the following statements about the above change in the wage payment system is/are correct?

(1) The company's total cost of employing salespersons will decrease.
(2) The working incentive of the salespersons will decrease.
(3) Part of the business risk is shifted to the salespersons.
questions.explanation: The firm's total wage cost may rise or fall depending on sales revenue, and commission raises rather than lowers salespersons' working incentive. A lower fixed salary plus commission shifts part of business risk to the salespersons.

questions.keyPoint: Types of division of labour
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about division of labour are correct?

(1) When a barter economy starts using money to facilitate exchange, division of labour tends to be practised to a greater extent.
(2) When a closed economy opens up to free trade, division of labour tends to be practised to a greater extent.
(3) When a small clinic expands into a large hospital, division of labour tends to be practised to a greater extent.
questions.explanation: Money, free trade and a larger scale of operation all facilitate specialisation and division of labour. Hence all three statements are correct.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of buying shares and bonds from small investors’ point of view
questions.stem: Mr Wong decides to invest in the bonds of a listed company instead of the shares of that company. Which of the following is the LEAST likely reason behind Mr Wong's investment decision above?

choices.text: Mr Wong is optimistic about the business prospects of the company.
Mr Wong prefers a more stable return from investment.
Mr Wong wants to have a lower risk of suffering from a loss.
Mr Wong wants to have a higher priority in getting back his investment in case the company liquidates.

questions.explanation: Being optimistic about the company's business prospects is more likely to support buying shares, which can benefit from higher profits and capital gains. The other options are typical reasons for preferring bonds.

questions.keyPoint: External economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem:
Miss Chan plans to open a flower shop. She is considering whether to open a flower shop at Flower Market Road, a district famous for having lots of flower shops, or to open at another location with no flower shops nearby.

Based on the above information, an advantage for Miss Chan to open a flower shop at Flower Market Road is that she may be able to _____.

(1) enjoy internal economies of scale in terms of lower transportation costs
(2) enjoy external economies of scale in terms of lower marketing costs
(3) sell flowers at a higher price due to keener competition among sellers
questions.explanation: Being located in a well-known flower district may reduce marketing cost through external economies of scale. It is not internal economies of scale, and keener competition does not imply a higher selling price.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem:
ABC Company is a food delivery service provider. It offers the following two payment options to customers.

Option 1: to pay a delivery fee of $30 per order
Option 2: to pay a lump-sum membership fee of $200 per month and do not need to pay any delivery fee per order

Based on the above information, after a customer paying the lump-sum membership fee, _____.

(1) he/she tends to use the food delivery services of ABC Company more frequently
(2) he/she tends to order higher-priced food when using the food delivery services of ABC Company
(3) the marginal benefit of the last unit of food delivery services of ABC Company consumed by him/her tends to become lower
questions.explanation: After paying the lump-sum fee, the marginal money cost of an extra delivery is zero, so the customer tends to use the service more frequently. With more use, the marginal benefit of the last delivery tends to be lower. The price of the food itself is not changed by the delivery membership.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem:
The supply curve of Good X is vertical and its demand curve is downward-sloping.

Suppose the supply of Good X decreases while the demand for Good X increases. As a result, the equilibrium price of Good X _____ and its equilibrium quantity _____.

choices.text: will increase ...... may increase, decrease or remain unchanged
will decrease ...... may increase, decrease or remain unchanged

questions.explanation: With a vertical supply curve, a decrease in supply directly lowers equilibrium quantity. A simultaneous increase in demand and decrease in supply both put upward pressure on price, so price will rise.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem:
Good X and Good Y are substitutes. If the cost of production of Good X increases, _____.

(1) the quantity demanded for Good Y decreases
(2) the quantity supplied of Good Y increases
(3) the supply of Good Y increases
(4) the total revenue of Good Y increases
questions.explanation: A rise in the production cost of Good X reduces its supply and raises its price. Since X and Y are substitutes, demand for Good Y increases, raising Good Y's price and quantity supplied. Its total revenue rises, while its supply curve does not shift.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Which of the following will lower Hong Kong households' price elasticity of demand for foreign domestic helpers?

choices.text: More Hong Kong people are trained to work as part-time domestic helpers.
Fewer child care centres are provided in Hong Kong for parents who both work.
The Hong Kong Government reduces the quota of foreign domestic helpers.
The wage rate of foreign domestic helpers in Hong Kong increases.

questions.explanation: Child care centres are substitutes for foreign domestic helpers for some households. Fewer substitutes make demand less price elastic.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, cost of production, technology, price expectations, weather, number of sellers in the market, etc. affect individual supply and market supply
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram.

choices.text: Cost of production of wine in China decreases.
The income of Australian residents increases.
The Chinese Government abolishes the import tariffs on Australian wine.

questions.explanation: Abolishing China's import tariff on Australian wine lowers the cost of supplying Australian wine in China, shifting the supply curve to the right.

questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules of Good X.

choices.text: If the government increases the quota, the total revenue of Good X may decrease.
If the government increases the quota, the deadweight loss may increase.
Instead of imposing the quota, the imposition of a per-unit tax of $6 would have equivalent effect on the price.
Instead of imposing the quota, the imposition of a per-unit tax of $12 would have equivalent effect on the quantity transacted.

questions.explanation: A quota of 100 units gives a demand price of $18 and a supply price of $6, so the equivalent per-unit tax wedge for the same quantity is $12.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in supply
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in supply
questions.stem:
Due to poor harvests of oranges, many juice producers use other fruits such as mandarins as an alternative ingredient to produce juice.

Based on the above information, which of the following is correct?

choices.text: There is a deadweight loss in the market of oranges.
The total revenue of orange sellers may increase.
The total social surplus in the market of mandarins decreases.
The total exchange value of mandarins may decrease.

questions.explanation: Poor orange harvests reduce the supply of oranges and raise their price. Depending on price elasticity of demand, the total revenue of orange sellers may increase.

questions.keyPoint: Identify the type of market structure
questions.stem:
The table below shows the market shares of top four subscription video-on-demand (SVoD) service providers worldwide in March 2024.

Based on the above information, we can conclude that the market structure of the worldwide SVoD market in March 2024 could be regarded as _____ because _____.

choices.text: monopolistic competition ...... market information was imperfect
monopolistic competition ...... services provided by different service providers were heterogeneous
oligopoly ...... there were several dominant service providers in the market
oligopoly ...... the governments in different countries controlled the entry of service providers into their markets

questions.explanation: The table shows a few service providers with sizable market shares. This is consistent with oligopoly, where several dominant firms exist in the market.

questions.stem: The diagram below shows the market of Good X. A per-unit subsidy of $30 is provided to the producers of Good X.

choices.text: The subsidy benefit enjoyed by consumers is $1 400.
The total revenue inclusive of the subsidy is $11 700.
Within the range of the original and the new equilibrium prices, the price elasticity of demand is higher than the price elasticity of supply.
Within the range of the original and the new equilibrium prices, the price elasticity of demand is smaller than one.

questions.explanation: After the subsidy, consumers pay $100 and quantity is 90. Producers receive $100 + $30 = $130 per unit, so total revenue inclusive of the subsidy is $130 x 90 = $11 700.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Maximisation of total social surplus: marginal benefit equals marginal cost
questions.stem:
A developer plans to construct a tall building. The building will block the sea view enjoyed by some households living in another building.

In the above situation, efficiency may be attained if _____.

(1) the government restricts the height of the new building
(2) the developer pays a compensation to each affected household for blocking the sea view
(3) the affected households pay the developer to request it to reduce the height of the new building
questions.explanation: Efficiency may be attained by government restriction or by private negotiation/compensation if the benefits and costs are properly reflected. Both directions of compensation can lead to an efficient outcome depending on the assignment of rights.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem:
The following diagram shows the supply and demand curves of a good. Suppose the government imposes a per-unit tax on the production of the good.

Which of the following statements about the imposition of the per-unit tax are correct?

(1) The consumers bear no tax burden.
(2) The decrease in total social surplus is area Oabc.
(3) There is deadweight loss after the imposition of the tax.
questions.explanation: The demand curve is horizontal, so the market price paid by consumers is unchanged and consumers bear no tax burden. The tax reduces quantity and creates deadweight loss, but the loss in total social surplus is not the whole area Oabc.

visuals.alt: Per-unit tax shifts supply upward while demand is horizontal.
visuals.caption: Per-unit tax

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the imposition of the per-unit tax are correct?

(1) The consumers bear no tax burden.
(2) The decrease in total social surplus is area Oabc.
(3) There is deadweight loss after the imposition of the tax.

questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Lorenz curve
questions.stem:
Study the Lorenz curves of Country A and Country B below.

Suppose the total incomes in the two countries are equal. Based on the above information, we can conclude that _____.

(1) Country A has a lower Gini coefficient than Country B
(2) the bottom 20% households in Country A earn a higher total income than the bottom 20% households in Country B
(3) the top 20% households in Country A earn a smaller proportion of the country's total income than that in Country B
questions.explanation: Country A's Lorenz curve is closer to the line of equality, so it has a lower Gini coefficient. Its bottom 20% receive more income, and its top 20% receive a smaller income share than in Country B.

visuals.alt: Lorenz curves of Country A and Country B.
visuals.caption: Lorenz curves

questions.preVisualStem: Study the Lorenz curves of Country A and Country B below.

Suppose the total incomes in the two countries are equal. Based on the above information, we can conclude that _____.

(1) Country A has a lower Gini coefficient than Country B

(3) the top 20% households in Country A earn a smaller proportion of the country's total income than that in Country B

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT included in the gross national income of Hong Kong?

choices.text: the dividend received by a Japanese resident from a company in Hong Kong
the salary received by a British consultant working in Hong Kong for 18 months
the interest received by a Hong Kong resident holding silver bonds which is issued by the Hong Kong Government
the rental income earned by a Hong Kong resident for investing in properties in Mainland

questions.explanation: Hong Kong's gross national income includes income earned by Hong Kong residents, including from abroad, and income of resident producing units. A dividend received by a Japanese resident is income to a non-resident and is not included.

questions.keyPoint: Uses and limitations of national income statistics
questions.stem:
When the per capita real gross domestic product (GDP) of a country decreases, the general living standard of the country may still improve if _____.

(1) there are more non-marketed goods in the country
(2) the working hours of the country's residents increases
(3) the general price level of the country decreases
questions.explanation: More non-marketed goods can raise living standards even if measured real GDP per capita falls. Longer working hours do not necessarily improve living standards, and real GDP has already adjusted for price-level changes.

questions.keyPoint: Production/value added approach
questions.stem:
The following diagram shows a production chain of coffee grinders in an economy.

What is the contribution of the above production chain to the economy's GDP at factor cost?
questions.explanation: Using the value-added approach at factor cost: local materials add $70, local manufacturers add $140 + $80 - $70 = $150, and local retailers add ($440 - $60 sales tax) - $90 - $140 = $150. Total contribution is $370.

visuals.alt: Production chain of coffee grinders in an economy.
visuals.caption: Production chain

questions.postVisualStem: What is the contribution of the above production chain to the economy's GDP at factor cost?

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely to cause an increase in the short run aggregate output of an economy?

choices.text: an increase in the rate of savings and an increase in the labour productivity in the economy
an increase in the income tax rate in the economy and a faster economic growth in its trading partners
a decrease in the discount rate in the economy and a decrease in the world oil price
a decrease in the tariff imposed on imported consumer goods and an increase in the quota for the immigration of skilled workers in the economy

questions.explanation: A lower discount rate raises aggregate demand, while a lower world oil price lowers production costs and raises short-run aggregate supply. Both changes tend to increase short-run aggregate output.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem:
The diagram below shows the long run aggregate supply curve of a country.

Which of the following would result in a change in the long run equilibrium point from E1 to E2?

choices.text: The production of the country is disrupted by extreme weather.
The infrastructure of the country is improved by a government construction project.
There is a persistent increase in the price level.

questions.explanation: Moving from E1 to E2 means a higher price level at the same full-employment output. A decrease in households' desire to save raises consumption and aggregate demand, producing this upward movement along LRAS in long-run equilibrium.

visuals.alt: Long run aggregate supply curve with points E1 and E2 on the same LRAS.
visuals.caption: LRAS

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following would result in a change in the long run equilibrium point from E1 to E2?

questions.topicGroup: Reasons for a vertical long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve
questions.keyPoint: Reasons for a vertical long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve
questions.stem:
Which of the following can explain why a long run aggregate supply curve is vertical?

(1) Input prices can be perfectly adjusted in the long run.
(2) Firms are unable to adjust their output levels in the long run.
(3) Technological level is not constant in the long run.
questions.explanation: In the long run, input prices can fully adjust, so the price level does not affect the full-employment level of output. Firms can adjust output, and changes in technology would shift LRAS rather than explain its vertical shape.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Inflationary gap
questions.stem: When the short run aggregate output exceeds the full-employment output level, _____.

choices.text: an increase in the required reserve ratio by the central bank may help bring the aggregate output back to the full-employment output level
the aggregate output would fall back to the full-employment output level due to a decrease in aggregate demand through the market adjustment mechanism
there would be an excess supply in the factor market
the full-employment output level would increase until it is equal to the short run aggregate output

questions.explanation: Output above the full-employment level is an inflationary gap. Raising the required reserve ratio is contractionary monetary policy and may reduce aggregate demand, helping output return to the full-employment level.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem:
Refer to the following hypothetical case.

Country P experiences a long period of hyperinflation. When workers receive wages in P dollar (the legal tender of Country P), they would quickly use the P dollar to buy gold or convert it into US dollar. Some workers even only accept jobs with wages denominated in US dollar. Lenders generally do not accept repayment of loans in P dollar when lending money.

Based on the above information, which functions of money of the P dollar were weakened?

(1) medium of exchange
(2) store of value
(3) standard of deferred payment
questions.explanation: Hyperinflation makes people unwilling to hold P dollars, weakening its store of value function. Some workers do not accept P dollars for wages, weakening its medium of exchange function, and lenders do not accept repayment in P dollars, weakening its standard of deferred payment function.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem:
Miss Ho uses HK$500 000 cash to buy from Mr Lai a negotiable certificate of deposit issued by a deposit-taking company. Mr Lai then deposits HK$200 000 cash to his Hong Kong dollar savings account and remits the remaining amount to his parents in Australia.

What will be the immediate effect of the above actions on the Hong Kong dollar money supply?

choices.text: M1 will increase while M3 will remain unchanged.
M1 will remain unchanged while M3 will decrease.
Both M1 and M3 will decrease.
Both M1 and M3 will remain unchanged.

questions.explanation: Cash held by the public falls by HK$500 000. Only HK$200 000 is deposited back into a Hong Kong dollar savings account, while the remaining HK$300 000 is remitted overseas. Therefore M1 and M3 both decrease immediately.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem:
The diagram below shows the money demand and money supply curves of an economy. The original equilibrium point is at E.

Suppose more and more people in the economy like to make payments for daily expenses using e-wallets. At the same time, the central bank of the economy performs an open market purchase of government bonds. The new equilibrium point in the above diagram will be at point _____.
questions.explanation: Using e-wallets lowers the demand for money, shifting money demand from Md0 to Md1. An open market purchase increases money supply from Ms0 to Ms2. The new equilibrium is point B.

visuals.alt: Money demand curves Md1, Md0, Md2 and money supply curves Ms1, Ms0, Ms2.
visuals.caption: Money demand and money supply

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem:
Study the following balance sheet of a banking system.

Initially, the banking system has an excess reserve of $50. Suppose the public decides to reduce cash holdings by depositing $100 cash into the banking system. When the maximum deposit of the banking system is reached, which of the following will be its new balance sheet?
questions.explanation: Required reserves are $250 - $50 = $200, so the required reserve ratio is $200 / $1 000 = 20%. After a $100 cash deposit, reserves become $350. Maximum deposits are $350 / 0.2 = $1 750, and loans are $1 750 - $350 = $1 400.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate
questions.stem:
Suppose the nominal interest rate remains constant. When the actual inflation rate is lower than the expected inflation rate, the actual real interest rate will be higher than the _____.

(1) expected real interest rate
(2) nominal interest rate
(3) actual inflation rate
questions.explanation: With a given nominal interest rate, actual real interest rate equals nominal interest rate minus actual inflation, while expected real interest rate equals nominal interest rate minus expected inflation. If actual inflation is lower than expected inflation, the actual real interest rate is higher than the expected real interest rate.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: In an economy, a large number of workers migrate overseas together with their family members. In the short run, the price level of the economy _____ and its real output _____.

choices.text: will fall ...... may rise or fall
may rise or fall ...... will fall
may rise or fall ...... may rise or fall

questions.explanation: Emigration of workers reduces aggregate supply, while emigration of workers and their families also reduces aggregate demand. Both effects lower real output, but their effects on the price level are opposite, so the price level may rise or fall.

questions.keyPoint: Surplus budget, deficit budget and balanced budget
questions.stem:
Suppose both a fiscal deficit and a trade deficit exist in an economy. Which of the following may eliminate both the fiscal deficit and the trade deficit at the same time?

(1) The government imposes tariffs on a wide range of imported goods.
(2) The government raises the rate of the salaries tax.
(3) The government devaluates its currency against that of its major trading partners.
questions.explanation: Tariffs may raise government revenue and reduce imports. A higher salaries tax may raise government revenue and reduce import spending through lower disposable income. Currency devaluation may improve the trade balance and raise income-related tax revenue. Hence each may help eliminate both deficits.

questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem:
Study the following diagram.

Based on the above information, which of the following is an implication of the quantity theory of money?
questions.explanation: Under the quantity theory of money with velocity constant, money supply growth equals inflation plus real output growth. Since money supply grows faster than real output, the implied inflation rate is positive.

questions.keyPoint: Taxation in
questions.stem:
Mr Cheung earned huge profits as a sole proprietor in Hong Kong. He purchased a second-hand car and a second-hand apartment in Hong Kong for his own use.

Based on the above information, which types of indirect tax does Mr Cheung need to pay to the Hong Kong Government?

(1) profits tax
(2) stamp duty
(3) rates
(4) motor vehicle first registration tax
questions.explanation: Profits tax is a direct tax, and a second-hand car does not involve motor vehicle first registration tax. Stamp duty and rates are indirect taxes that apply to the second-hand apartment.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: Suppose Country X and Country Y both allocate half of their resources in producing clothing and half in producing toys. Their total output is shown below.
questions.explanation: The countries may have different total resources, so absolute advantage cannot be concluded from total output when each uses half of its own resources. Country Y's opportunity cost of clothing is 0.5 units of toys, lower than Country X's 5 units of toys. Even with a transport cost of 4 units of toys, importing clothing from Y costs 4.5 units of toys, still below X's domestic opportunity cost.
questions.postVisualStem:
Based on the above information, which of the following is/are correct?

(1) Country Y enjoys an absolute advantage in producing clothing.
(2) Country Y enjoys a comparative advantage in producing clothing.
(3) If the transportation cost for importing each unit of clothing is 4 units of toys, mutually beneficial trade is still possible between the two countries.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of a quota on domestic price, domestic consumption, domestic production and import quantity for a small open economy
questions.stem: A small open economy has imposed an effective quota on imported red wine. If the world price of red wine decreases, _____.

choices.text: the volume of red wine imported by the economy will increase
the quantity of red wine domestically produced in the economy will increase
the quantity of red wine consumed in the economy will remain unchanged
the price of red wine sold in the economy will decrease

questions.explanation: With an effective import quota, the import volume is fixed by the quota. A fall in the world price changes the quota rent but does not change domestic consumption or production as long as the quota remains effective, so domestic consumption remains unchanged.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT included in the calculation of Hong Kong's current account balance?

choices.text: a bank transfer received by a Hong Kong resident from her son residing in London
the revenue earned by a Hong Kong retailer from selling souvenirs to Mainland tourists
the sum of money received by a Hong Kong landlord from selling his restaurant premises to an investor in Paris
the rental income received by a Hong Kong resident from renting his apartment to a Mainland professor who stayed in Hong Kong for four months

questions.explanation: Selling restaurant premises is a transaction in a non-financial asset/asset ownership, not a current-account transaction. The other items relate to current transfers, services or income.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem:
The diagram below shows the exchange rate between Japanese Yen (JPY) and Hong Kong Dollar (HKD) from 27 September to 23 October 2024.

During the above period, if Japan's demand for imports from Hong Kong is _____, the total value of Japan's imports from Hong Kong (in terms of JPY) would _____.
questions.explanation: The HKD value of 100 JPY falls, so the JPY depreciates against the HKD and Hong Kong imports become more expensive to Japanese buyers in JPY terms. If demand is elastic, Japan's total import value from Hong Kong in JPY decreases.

questions.keyPoint: 識別及計算選擇一個選項時涉及的成本（顯性成本及隱含成本）
questions.stem:
珊珊計劃觀看一場演唱會，並以 $1 500 購買了一張該場演唱會的門票。珊珊剛購買門票後，一間公司給予她一份薪酬 $3 000 的兼職工作。然而，該兼職的工作時間與該場演唱會的時間相撞。與此同時，由於所有門票經已售罄，她的朋友提出以 $1 800 購買她那張演唱會門票。

根據以上資料，在珊珊決定是否將演唱會門票出售予她的朋友時，她選擇觀看該場演唱會的機會成本是 ____。
questions.explanation: 在作出決定時，已付出的 $1 500 門票費用屬沉沒成本。觀看演唱會會放棄 $3 000 兼職收入和 $1 800 轉售收入，所以機會成本為 $4 800。

questions.chapterTitle: 三個基本經濟問題與私有產權
questions.keyPoint: 不同社會解決基本經濟問題的方法
questions.stem:
與計劃經濟相比，____。

(1) 個人在市場經濟中決定資源分配時傾向有較高自由度
(2) 利率在市場經濟中傾向較高
(3) 資源分配在市場經濟中傾向較少依賴非價格競爭
questions.explanation: 市場經濟中個人有較大自由度，資源分配主要依靠價格機制，較少依賴非價格競爭。市場經濟的利率不一定較高。

questions.keyPoint: 區分免費物品及經濟物品
questions.stem: 天然雨林裏的樹木是 ____。

choices.text: 經濟物品，假如人們願意花費金錢保育該些樹木
免費物品，因為它們是不涉及生產成本的天然資源
經濟學中的土地，因為它們沒有地域流動性
共用品，假如該雨林是由政府管理

questions.explanation: 假如人們願意運用資源保育樹木，保育樹木便涉及機會成本，因此樹木是經濟物品。

questions.chapterTitle: 三個基本經濟問題與私有產權
questions.keyPoint: 三個基本經濟問題的意思及相關例子
questions.stem:
面對電動車需求上升，一間製造商決定生產更多電動車，並提高電動車的售價。

上述製造商的決定與經濟學中的 ____ 問題相關，因為該決定與 ____ 相關。

(1) 「生產什麼」...... 產量的選擇
(2) 「怎樣生產」...... 要素投入的選擇
(3) 「為誰生產」...... 產出的分配
questions.explanation: 生產更多電動車涉及產量選擇，即「生產什麼」；提高售價影響哪些人可取得產出，即「為誰生產」。

questions.keyPoint: 認識每一生產種類對香港經濟的貢獻
questions.stem: 下表顯示某經濟生產總值的分佈。該經濟 2024 年的生產總值高於 2014 年。

choices.text: 從事初級生產的工人的比例下跌了
初級生產的勞工生產力下跌了
次級生產的生產總值維持不變
三級生產的生產總值必然上升了

questions.explanation: 三級生產比例由 62.5% 升至 72.7%，而整體生產總值亦上升，所以三級生產的生產總值必然上升。
questions.postVisualStem: 根據以上資料，可得出的結論是：由 2014 年至 2024 年，____。

questions.topicGroup: 內部規模經濟/規模負經濟
questions.keyPoint: 內部規模經濟/規模負經濟
questions.stem: 下表顯示某廠商的投入與產出的關係。該廠商生產所需的投入只有勞力。每單位勞力的工資率是 $50。

choices.text: 邊際回報遞減定律適用於該廠商，因為當僱用第 4 個勞力單位時，邊際產量開始遞減
當產量由 90 單位增加至 100 單位時，該廠商會承受規模不經濟
當產量由 100 單位增加至 105 單位時，該廠商會承受虧損
利潤極大化的產量是 90 單位

questions.explanation: 勞力是唯一投入，因此增加勞力即增加全部投入。由 3 單位勞力增至 4 單位時，投入增加 33.3%，但產出只由 90 增至 100，增幅較少，故出現規模不經濟。
questions.postVisualStem: 根據以上資料，可得出的結論是：____。

questions.topicGroup: 廠商的基本目標：利潤極大化
questions.keyPoint: 競爭性廠商如何選擇利潤極大化產出水平
questions.stem: 下表顯示某完全競爭市場中一間廠商的成本與產出的關係。該廠商的固定成本是 $6，而市場價格是 $20。
questions.explanation: 原來最高利潤為 $34。固定成本降至 $2 後，各單位邊際成本上升 $4，新的最高利潤為 $22，因此利潤下降 $12。
questions.postVisualStem: 假設固定成本下降 $4，而每單位產出的邊際成本上升 $4。結果，該廠商的利潤會 ____。

questions.keyPoint: 不同的付酬方式
questions.stem: 假設某健康產品公司的售貨員的付酬方式有以下改變：
questions.explanation: 總成本視乎營業額而定，不一定下降；佣金會提高而非降低工作意欲。固定薪金降低並加入佣金，會把部分經營風險轉嫁到售貨員。

visuals.alt: 售貨員薪金由每月固定薪金改為較低薪金加佣金。
visuals.caption: 付酬方式

questions.postVisualStem:
下列哪項／些關於上述付酬方式改變的陳述是正確的？

(1) 該公司僱用售貨員的總成本會下降。
(2) 售貨員的工作意欲會下降。
(3) 部分經營風險被轉嫁到售貨員。

questions.keyPoint: 分工的種類
questions.stem:
下列哪些關於分工的陳述是正確的？

(1) 當一個以物易物經濟開始使用貨幣促進交易時，實施分工的程度傾向變得更大。
(2) 當一個封閉經濟開放自由貿易時，實施分工的程度傾向變得更大。
(3) 當一間小型診所擴張成一間大型醫院時，實施分工的程度傾向變得更大。
questions.explanation: 使用貨幣、開放自由貿易和擴大機構規模都可促進專門化和分工，因此三項皆正確。

questions.topicGroup: 股票及債券作為資金來源
questions.keyPoint: 從小投資者的角度出發，購買股票及債券的優點和缺點
questions.stem: 王先生決定投資某上市公司的債券，而非投資該公司的股票。下列哪項最不可能是王先生作上述投資決定背後的原因？

choices.text: 王先生對該公司的經營前景感到樂觀。
王先生偏好較穩定的投資回報。
王先生想有較低的蒙受損失的風險。
王先生想在該公司一旦清盤時，可較優先取回他的投資。

questions.explanation: 若對公司前景樂觀，較可能選擇股票以分享盈利和資本增值；其餘均是偏好債券的常見原因。

questions.topicGroup: 外部規模經濟/規模負經濟
questions.keyPoint: 外部規模經濟/規模負經濟
questions.stem:
陳小姐計劃開設一間花店。她正考慮將花店開設在花墟道（一個以花店眾多而聞名的地區）還是開設在一個附近沒有花店的地點。

根據上述資料，陳小姐將花店開設在花墟道的一個優點是，她可能可以 ____。

(1) 在降低運輸成本方面享有內部規模經濟
(2) 在降低營銷成本方面享有外部規模經濟
(3) 以更高價格出售花卉，因為賣家之間的競爭更激烈
questions.explanation: 位於知名花店集中地可帶來外部規模經濟，例如降低營銷成本；這不是內部規模經濟，而較激烈競爭亦不代表可提高售價。

questions.topicGroup: 貨幣價格（名義價格）和相對價格
questions.keyPoint: 將相對價格或全價格應用於需求定律，以解釋特定現象
questions.stem:
ABC 公司是一間提供送餐服務的公司。它予顧客以下兩種付費選項。

選項 1：每次點餐支付 $30 送餐費用
選項 2：每月支付 $200 定額會員費，每次點餐無須支付任何送餐費用

根據上述資料，當一名顧客支付定額會員費後，____。

(1) 他／她傾向更頻密地使用 ABC 公司的送餐服務
(2) 他／她使用 ABC 公司送餐服務時傾向點選較高價的食品
(3) 他／她消費的最後一單位的 ABC 公司送餐服務的邊際利益傾向變得較低
questions.explanation: 支付定額費後，額外一次送餐的邊際金錢成本為零，所以顧客傾向更頻密使用服務；使用量增加時，最後一單位送餐服務的邊際利益傾向較低。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋需求改變和供應改變如何影響均衡價格和數量
questions.stem:
物品 X 的供應曲線是垂直的，而其需求曲線是向下傾斜的。

假設物品 X 的供應下降，同時物品 X 的需求上升。結果，物品 X 的均衡價格 ____，而其均衡數量 ____。

choices.text: 會上升 ...... 可能上升、下降或維持不變
會下降 ...... 可能上升、下降或維持不變

questions.explanation: 供應曲線垂直時，供應下降會令均衡數量下降；需求上升和供應下降同時推高價格，所以均衡價格會上升。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋相關物品價格、收入、價格預期、天氣、市場消費者人數等因素如何影響個別需求及市場需求
questions.stem:
物品 X 和物品 Y 是代替品。假如物品 X 的生產成本上升，____。

(1) 物品 Y 的需求量下降
(2) 物品 Y 的供應量上升
(3) 物品 Y 的供應上升
(4) 物品 Y 的總收入上升
questions.explanation: 物品 X 成本上升令其供應下降、價格上升；X 和 Y 為代替品，Y 的需求上升，令 Y 的價格和供應量上升，總收入亦上升，但 Y 的供應曲線沒有移動。

questions.chapterTitle: 需求和供應的價格彈性
questions.keyPoint: 影響需求價格彈性的因素
questions.stem: 下列哪項會令香港家庭對外籍家庭傭工的需求價格彈性下降？

choices.text: 更多香港人接受培訓成為兼職家庭傭工。
為雙職家長提供的托兒中心減少。
香港政府減少外籍家庭傭工的配額。
在香港的外籍家庭傭工的工資率上升。

questions.explanation: 托兒中心是外籍家庭傭工的代替服務之一。代替品減少會令需求價格彈性下降。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋相關物品價格、生產成本、科技、價格預期、天氣、市場生產者人數等因素如何影響個別供應及市場供應
questions.stem: 參考下圖。

choices.text: 中國生產葡萄酒的成本下降。
中國政府取消澳洲葡萄酒的進口關稅。

questions.explanation: 取消進口關稅會降低澳洲葡萄酒在中國市場的供應成本，令供應曲線右移。

visuals.alt: 在中國出售的澳洲葡萄酒供應由 S1 右移至 S2。
visuals.caption: 在中國出售的澳洲葡萄酒

questions.postVisualStem: 下列哪項最能解釋為什麼供應曲線從 S1 移至 S2？

questions.keyPoint: 分析（有效）配額對價格、交易量、總收入及產品質素等的影響
questions.stem: 參考下列物品 X 的供需表。

choices.text: 若政府增加配額，物品 X 的總收入可能下降。
若政府增加配額，效率損失可能上升。
若政府以徵收 $6 從量稅取代配額，兩項措施對價格的影響是相等的。
若政府以徵收 $12 從量稅取代配額，兩項措施對交易量的影響是相等的。

questions.explanation: 配額為 100 單位時，需求價格為 $18，供應價格為 $6，造成相同交易量的從量稅稅楔為 $12。
questions.postVisualStem: 假設政府對物品 X 實施 100 單位的配額。下列哪項陳述是正確的？

questions.keyPoint: 供應改變的影響
questions.stem:
由於橙的收成欠佳，很多果汁生產商改以柑橘等其他水果作為生產果汁的材料。

根據上述資料，下列哪項是正確的？

choices.text: 橙的市場上出現效率損失。
橙的賣家的總收入可能上升。
柑橘市場上的總社會盈餘下降。
柑橘的總交易價值可能下降。

questions.explanation: 橙收成欠佳令橙的供應下降、價格上升；若需求缺乏彈性，橙的賣家的總收入可能上升。

questions.keyPoint: 辨識市場結構種類
questions.stem: 下表顯示全球四大訂閱制隨選影片服務供應商於 2024 年 3 月的市場佔有率。

choices.text: 壟斷性競爭 ...... 市場資訊是不完全的
壟斷性競爭 ...... 不同服務供應商提供的服務是異質的
寡頭壟斷 ...... 市場上有數個具支配力的服務供應商
寡頭壟斷 ...... 不同國家的政府對服務供應商進入其市場有管控

questions.explanation: 市場上有數間具相當市場佔有率的主要服務供應商，符合寡頭壟斷有數個具支配力廠商的特徵。

columns: 訂閱制隨選影片服務供應商

questions.postVisualStem: 根據以上資料，可得出的結論是：全球訂閱制隨選影片服務供應商市場於 2024 年 3 月的市場結構可被視為 ____，因為 ____。

questions.topicGroup: 物品及服務的 津貼
questions.keyPoint: 分析從量津貼對價格、交易量及總收入等的影響，並說明生產者和消費者如何分配津貼得益
questions.stem: 下圖顯示物品 X 的市場。物品 X 的生產者有 $30 從量補貼。

choices.text: 消費者享有的補貼得益是 $1 400。
包含補貼在內的總收入是 $11 700。
在介乎原初的均衡價格和新的均衡價格之間的範圍內，需求價格彈性高於供應價格彈性。
在介乎原初的均衡價格和新的均衡價格之間的範圍內，需求價格彈性小於一。

questions.explanation: 補貼後消費者支付 $100，交易量為 90；生產者每單位收到 $100 + $30 = $130。因此包含補貼在內的總收入為 $130 x 90 = $11 700。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 總社會盈餘達致最大：邊際利益等於邊際成本
questions.stem:
某發展商計劃興建一座高聳的建築物。該建築物將會擋閉另一座建築物部分住戶享有的海景。

在上述情況中，若 ____，則可能達至有效率。

(1) 政府限制該幢新建築物的高度
(2) 該發展商向每一個受影響住戶就阻擋海景支付賠償
(3) 受影響住戶向該發展商付費，要求它降低該幢新建築物的高度
questions.explanation: 政府規管或私下補償／協商均可能令相關成本和利益反映於決策之中。無論由發展商補償住戶，或由住戶付費要求降低高度，在合適條件下均可能達至效率。

questions.topicGroup: 物品及服務的稅項（銷售稅）
questions.keyPoint: 分析從量稅對價格、交易量及總收入等的影響，並說明生產者和消費者的稅項負擔分配
questions.stem: 下圖顯示某物品的供需曲線。假設政府對該物品的生產徵收一項從量稅。
questions.explanation: 需求曲線水平，消費者支付的價格不變，所以沒有稅項負擔。徵稅令交易量下降並出現效率損失，但總社會盈餘的下降不是整個 Oabc 面積。

visuals.alt: 需求曲線水平，從量稅令供應曲線上移。
visuals.caption: 從量稅

questions.postVisualStem:
下列哪些關於徵收上述從量稅的陳述是正確的？

(1) 消費者沒有任何稅項負擔。
(2) 總社會盈餘的下降是面積 Oabc。
(3) 徵收該稅項後出現效率損失。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(II)
questions.keyPoint: 詮釋洛倫茨曲線提供的資料
questions.stem: 細閱甲國和乙國的洛倫茨曲線。
questions.explanation: 甲國的洛倫茨曲線較接近完全平均線，所以堅尼系數較低；最低端 20% 收入較高，最高端 20% 所佔收入比例亦較乙國小。

visuals.alt: 甲國和乙國的洛倫茨曲線。
visuals.caption: 洛倫茨曲線

questions.postVisualStem:
假設兩國的總收入相等。根據上述資料，可得出的結論是：____。

(1) 甲國的堅尼系數較乙國的低
(2) 甲國最低端 20% 的住戶的總收入高於乙國最低端 20% 的住戶的總收入
(3) 甲國最高端 20% 的住戶的收入佔其國家總收入的比例較乙國的小

questions.keyPoint: 本地居民總收入（本地居民生產總值）
questions.stem: 下列哪項不包括在香港的本地居民總收入中？

choices.text: 一位日本居民從香港公司收取的股息
一位英國顧問在香港工作 18 個月收取的薪酬
一位香港居民從其持有的由香港政府發行的銀色債券收取的利息
一位香港居民從投資內地物業收取的租金收入

questions.explanation: 本地居民總收入包括本地居民所得的收入及居民生產單位的收入。日本居民從香港公司收取股息屬非本地居民收入，不包括在香港的本地居民總收入內。

questions.keyPoint: 國民收入統計數字的運用和限制
questions.stem:
當某國的人均實質本地生產總值下降時，若 ____，該國的一般生活水平仍可能提高。

(1) 該國有更多非市場物品
(2) 該國居民的工作時間增加
(3) 該國的一般物價水平下降
questions.explanation: 非市場物品增加可改善生活水平但未必反映於 GDP；工作時間增加不一定改善生活水平，而實質 GDP 已剔除一般物價變動的影響。

questions.keyPoint: 生產面/增加價值面
questions.stem: 下圖顯示某經濟中咖啡豆研磨機的生產鏈。
questions.explanation: 以增加價值計算並扣除 $60 銷售稅：本地材料增加價值 $70；本地生產商增加價值 $140 + $80 - $70 = $150；本地零售商增加價值 ($440 - $60) - $90 - $140 = $150。合共 $370。

questions.postVisualStem: 以上生產鏈對該經濟本地生產總值（以要素成本計算）的貢獻是多少？

questions.topicGroup: 總需求及/或總供應改變導致均衡產出水平和物價水平的改變
questions.keyPoint: 透過明確說明受影響的總需求組成部分及/ 或影響短期總供應及/或長期總供應的因素，解釋某情況會如何導致總需求、短期總供應及/ 或長期總供應轉變，因而令總需求曲線、短期總供應曲線及/或長期總供應曲線移動
questions.stem: 下列哪項最可能令某經濟在短期的總產出上升？

choices.text: 該經濟的儲蓄比率上升以及勞工生產力上升
該經濟的入息稅稅率上升以及其貿易伙伴的經濟增長加快
該經濟的貼現率下降和國際油價下降
該經濟降低對進口消費品徵收的關稅稅率和增加高技術工人入境的配額

questions.explanation: 貼現率下降會增加總需求；國際油價下降會降低生產成本並增加短期總供應。兩者均傾向令短期總產出上升。

questions.topicGroup: 總需求及/或總供應改變導致均衡產出水平和物價水平的改變
questions.keyPoint: 由短期均衡達至長期均衡的機制
questions.stem: 下圖顯示某國的長期總供應曲線。

choices.text: 該國的生產受極端天氣阻礙。
該國的基礎建設因一項政府工程項目而改善。

questions.explanation: 由 E1 移至 E2 表示在相同充分就業產出下物價水平上升。住戶儲蓄意欲下降會增加消費和總需求，令長期均衡沿 LRAS 上移。

visuals.alt: 長期總供應曲線上 E1 移至 E2。
visuals.caption: 長期總供應曲線

questions.postVisualStem: 下列哪項會令在長期的均衡點由 E1 移至 E2？

questions.topicGroup: 長期總供應曲線垂直的原因
questions.keyPoint: 長期總供應曲線垂直的原因
questions.stem:
下列哪項／些能夠解釋為什麼長期總供應曲線是垂直的？

(1) 投入的價格在長期可被完全調整。
(2) 廠商在長期無法調整其產出水平。
(3) 科技水平在長期不是固定的。
questions.explanation: 長期投入價格可完全調整，因此物價水平不影響充分就業產出。廠商在長期可調整產出，而科技改變會令 LRAS 移動，不是其垂直的原因。

questions.topicGroup: 短期均衡偏離長期均衡
questions.keyPoint: 通脹差距
questions.stem: 當短期的總產出超過充分就業產出水平時，____。

choices.text: 中央銀行上調法定儲備比率可能有助總產出回復至充分就業產出水平
透過市場調節機制，總產出會因總需求下跌而降回充分就業產出水平
要素市場會出現超額供應
充分就業產出水平會上升，直至與短期的總產出相等

questions.explanation: 短期總產出高於充分就業產出屬通脹缺口。上調法定儲備比率屬緊縮性貨幣政策，可減少總需求，幫助產出回復至充分就業水平。

questions.keyPoint: 貨幣的功能
questions.stem:
參考以下假設個案。

P 國經歷長時間的惡性通脹。當工人收到以 P 元（P 國的法定貨幣）支付的薪金時，他們會趕快地以之購買黃金，或將之兌換成美元。一些工人更只接受以美元計算薪金的工作。放貸者貸款時一般不接受以 P 元歸還欠款。

根據上述資料，P 元的哪些貨幣功能被削弱了？

(1) 交易媒介
(2) 價值儲藏
(3) 延期支付的標準
questions.explanation: 惡性通脹令 P 元難以保存價值；部分工人不接受以 P 元支薪，削弱其交易媒介功能；放貸者不接受以 P 元還款，削弱其延期支付標準功能。

questions.keyPoint: 資產轉移對貨幣供應的影響
questions.stem:
何小姐以港幣 $500 000 現金向黎先生購買某接受存款公司發行的可轉讓存款證。其後，黎先生將港幣 $200 000 現金存入其港元儲蓄戶口，並將餘款匯出予居於澳洲的父母。

上述行動對港元貨幣供應會有什麼即時的影響？

choices.text: 貨幣供應 M1 會上升，而貨幣供應 M3 會維持不變。
貨幣供應 M1 會維持不變，而貨幣供應 M3 會下降。
貨幣供應 M1 和 M3 皆會下降。
貨幣供應 M1 和 M3 皆會維持不變。

questions.explanation: 公眾持有現金減少 $500 000，只有 $200 000 存回港元儲蓄戶口，其餘匯往海外。因此 M1 和 M3 均即時下降。

questions.keyPoint: 分析貨幣需求、貨幣供應和名義利率的改變
questions.stem: 下圖顯示某經濟的貨幣需求曲線和貨幣供應曲線。原初的均衡點是 E。
questions.explanation: 使用電子錢包會減少貨幣需求，貨幣需求由 Md0 移至 Md1。中央銀行購買政府債券會增加貨幣供應，由 Ms0 移至 Ms2。新均衡點為 B。

visuals.alt: 貨幣需求曲線 Md1、Md0、Md2 和貨幣供應曲線 Ms1、Ms0、Ms2。
visuals.caption: 貨幣需求和貨幣供應

questions.keyPoint: 了解及計算存款、放款、貨幣供應等在存款創造/ 收縮過程後的最大及實際改變
questions.stem: 細閱下列某銀行系統的資產負債表。
questions.postVisualStem: 原初，該銀行系統有 $50 的超額儲備。假設公眾決定將 $100 現金存入該銀行系統以減持現金。當該銀行系統達至最大存款時，下列哪項是其新的資產負債表？

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 名義利率及實質利率的關係
questions.keyPoint: 了解方程式：名義利率 = 實質利率 + 預期通脹率
questions.stem:
假設名義利率維持不變。當實際通脹率低於預期通脹率時，實際實質利率會高於 ____。

(1) 預期實質利率
(2) 名義利率
(3) 實際通脹率
questions.explanation: 名義利率不變時，實際實質利率等於名義利率減實際通脹率；預期實質利率等於名義利率減預期通脹率。實際通脹率低於預期通脹率，所以實際實質利率高於預期實質利率。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.keyPoint: 經濟周期四個階段的特點
questions.stem: 細閱下圖。
questions.explanation: A 點顯示經濟低迷或負增長，商舖空置率和未能償還貸款的頻率較可能上升；進口開支則較可能下降。

visuals.alt: 實質本地生產總值改變百分率圖，A 點低於零增長。
visuals.caption: 經濟周期

questions.postVisualStem:
下列哪些是當一個經濟在 A 點運作時很可能出現的經濟現象？

(1) 商舖舖位的空置率正在上升。
(2) 未能償還銀行貸款的頻率正在上升。
(3) 對進口物品的開支正在上升。

questions.topicGroup: 總需求及/或總供應改變導致均衡產出水平和物價水平的改變
questions.keyPoint: 透過明確說明受影響的總需求組成部分及/ 或影響短期總供應及/或長期總供應的因素，解釋某情況會如何導致總需求、短期總供應及/ 或長期總供應轉變，因而令總需求曲線、短期總供應曲線及/或長期總供應曲線移動
questions.stem: 在某經濟中，大量工人攜同他們的家人移民海外。在短期，該經濟的物價水平 ____，而該經濟的實質產出 ____。

choices.text: 會下降 ...... 可能上升或下降
可能上升或下降 ...... 會下降
可能上升或下降 ...... 可能上升或下降

questions.explanation: 工人移民令總供應下降；工人及家人離開亦令總需求下降。兩者均使實質產出下降，但對物價水平的影響相反，因此物價水平可能上升或下降。

questions.keyPoint: 盈餘預算、赤字預算和平衡預算
questions.stem:
假設某經濟中出現財政赤字和貿易赤字。下列哪些可能同時消除其財政赤字和貿易赤字？

(1) 政府對廣泛的進口物品徵收關稅。
(2) 政府提高薪俸稅稅率。
(3) 政府令其貨幣兌主要貿易伙伴的貨幣官方貶值。
questions.explanation: 關稅可增加政府收入並減少進口；提高薪俸稅可增加稅收並透過降低可支配收入減少進口；官方貶值可改善貿易差額並可能提高收入和稅收。因此三者均可能同時改善兩項赤字。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹與貨幣數量論
questions.keyPoint: 貨幣數量論的意思
questions.stem: 細閱下圖。

choices.text: 通脹率為正並大致維持不變。
名義產出增長率維持在 0%。

questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹和通貨緊縮的影響
questions.keyPoint: 解釋為何出現非預期通貨膨脹（緊縮）時，債務人會得益（受損），而債權人會受損（得益）
questions.stem: 細閱下圖。

一位收取固定月租的業主
一位支付固定薪金的僱主
一位以浮動利率償還貸款的欠債人

questions.explanation: 名義本地生產總值不變而實質本地生產總值上升，意味一般物價水平非預期地下跌。固定薪金的實質成本上升，僱主會受損。

questions.keyPoint: 香港的徵稅
questions.stem:
張先生以獨資經營者的身分在香港賺得巨額利潤。他在香港購買了一輛二手車和一所二手住宅自用。

根據上述資料，張先生須向香港政府支付哪些類別的間接稅？

(1) 利得稅
(2) 印花稅
(3) 差餉
(4) 汽車首次登記稅
questions.explanation: 利得稅是直接稅；購買二手車不涉及汽車首次登記稅。二手住宅涉及印花稅和差餉，兩者屬間接稅。

questions.keyPoint: 根據個案資料，解釋哪個國家在生產某物品上擁有比較優勢
questions.stem: 假設 X 國和 Y 國都是分配一半資源生產成衣，而另一半資源則生產玩具。他們的產出總量如下：
questions.explanation: 兩國總資源可能不同，不能單從各自一半資源的總產量判斷絕對優勢。Y 國生產成衣的機會成本為 0.5 單位玩具，低於 X 國的 5 單位玩具；加上 4 單位玩具運輸成本後仍為 4.5，低於 X 國成本，故仍可能互利貿易。
questions.postVisualStem:
根據以上資料，下列哪項／些是正確的？

(1) Y 國在生產成衣方面享有絕對優勢。
(2) Y 國在生產成衣方面享有比較優勢。
(3) 若進口每單位成衣的運輸成本是 4 單位玩具，兩國之間仍可能出現互利貿易。

questions.keyPoint: 分析配額對小型開放經濟的本地價格、本地消費、本地生產和進口數量的影響
questions.stem: 某小型開放經濟一直對進口紅酒實施有效配額。若紅酒的國際價格下降，____。

choices.text: 該經濟的紅酒進口量會上升
該經濟的本地紅酒生產量會上升
該經濟的紅酒消費量會維持不變
該經濟中銷售的紅酒的價格會下降

questions.explanation: 有效進口配額固定進口量。若配額仍然有效，國際價格下降只會改變配額租，國內價格、消費量和本地生產量不變。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 經常帳（主要組成部分：貨物、服務、收益及經常轉移）

questions.stem: 下列哪項不包括在香港經常帳差額的計算之內？

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
Refer to the following information of the COVID-19 vaccination programme.

- All residents are eligible for joining the programme free-of-charge.
- The government has set up vaccination centres in some government buildings and deployed civil servants to work in these centres.

The above information is related to the ______ question(s) in Economics.

(1) 'what to produce'
(2) 'how to produce'
(3) 'for whom to produce'
questions.explanation: Free participation concerns distribution, so it relates to 'for whom to produce'. Setting up centres and deploying staff concerns input choice, so it relates to 'how to produce'.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Tommy is planning for his future after his S.6 graduation. He has several options and his order of preference is as follows.

First option: Being a barista in a café
Second option: Being a trainee in digital marketing
Third option: Being a junior fireman

Which of the following factors would LEAST likely affect the cost-benefit analysis for Tommy's career choice?

choices.text: More companies expand their digital marketing departments.
The remuneration of junior firemen worsens.
Safety measures of fire-fighting are improved drastically.

questions.explanation: Tommy's opportunity cost is the best foregone option, the trainee job. Changes to the least preferred option are least likely to affect the choice.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem: The Government purchased the broadcasting rights of the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games. This enabled all Hong Kong people to watch the events for free. The Olympic Games broadcast is a ______ because ______.

choices.text: public good ...... the Government paid for the broadcasting rights
private good ...... one individual's consumption reduces its amount available to others
free good ...... more is not preferred
consumer good ...... it can directly satisfy human wants

questions.explanation: A broadcast directly satisfies human wants, so it is a consumer good in this question.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible reason for turning a firm from a sole proprietorship to a partnership?

choices.text: The firm can get more profit.
The firm can enjoy a wider scope of specialisation.
The firm will become an independent legal entity.
Business risk will be reduced as all partners have unlimited liability.

questions.explanation: A partnership allows more owners and a wider scope of specialisation.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of internal expansion
questions.stem:
The Walt Disney Company expanded its business to provide video streaming service, Disney+.

Which of the following are most likely the motives behind the expansion?

(1) to spread risk by service diversification
(2) to extend its brand name to other products
(3) to enjoy economies of scale
questions.explanation: The expansion can diversify risk, extend the brand and create economies of scale.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Total product, average product and marginal product
questions.stem: The following table shows the input, output and cost relationships of a firm. The only inputs required for production are labour and capital.

choices.text: the firm enjoys economies of scale.
the optimal scale of production is 70 units.
the average product of labour is at the highest when the quantity of labour is 2 units.
the law of diminishing marginal returns does not apply to the firm.

questions.explanation: Average product of labour is 20, 25, about 23.3 and 20, so it is highest at 2 units of labour.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above table, we can conclude that

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: The ______ of labour in Hong Kong will increase if ______.

choices.text: occupational mobility ...... a professional labour union tightens the requirements for entering the industry
occupational mobility ...... the Government waives the examination for foreign-trained doctors to work in Hong Kong
geographical mobility ...... Tuen Ma Line connecting Tuen Mun and Ma On Shan is open
geographical mobility ...... the Government reduces the travel subsidy to the low-income group

questions.explanation: Opening a new rail link improves workers' geographical mobility.

questions.keyPoint: Types of division of labour
questions.stem:
In the Outline Development Plan for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, Hong Kong is an international financial and transportation centre; Macao is a leisure and tourism centre; Guangzhou is an international commercial centre.

This is an example of ______ division of labour because ______.

choices.text: simple ...... each city has its own comparative advantage
simple ...... each city engages in different production stages
regional ...... multiple cities cooperate to build the Greater Bay Area
regional ...... each city has its own specialty of production

questions.explanation: Different cities specialise in different activities, so this is regional division of labour.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Rationing function
questions.stem: In 2021, Trial & Error, a Hong Kong YouTube channel, held its first live show. The following was the pricing arrangement of its tickets.

choices.text: allocative ...... more resources can be allocated to the production of the show
allocative ...... the arrangement can guarantee a sell-out of the tickets
rationing ...... the tickets are sold to the highest-valued buyers
rationing ...... the tickets are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis

questions.explanation: The varying price allocates tickets to the buyers who value them most.
questions.postVisualStem:
Ticket price adjusts daily at 10 am.

10 August $10 000
11 August $5 000
31 August $20
1 September onwards $10

The above case illustrates the ______ function of price because ______.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: Winnie operates a café in Sham Shui Po. To maximise her profit, Winnie will produce more output if

choices.text: water charges for commercial use fall.
the monthly rental payment of the café rises.
the wage rate of part-time waiters increases.

questions.explanation: A fall in water charges lowers variable cost and encourages more output.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem: The following table shows the total expenditure of Mary and Peter on soft drinks.

choices.text: between zero and one ...... equal to zero
between zero and one ...... equal to one
equal to zero ...... equal to zero
equal to zero ...... equal to one

questions.explanation: Mary's total expenditure rises with price, so demand is inelastic. Peter's total expenditure is unchanged, so demand is unit elastic.
questions.postVisualStem: Mary's elasticity of demand for soft drinks is ______ while Peter's elasticity of demand for soft drinks is ______ (without regard to the negative sign).

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity

The total expenditure on high-quality red wine will drop by the same percentage as that on low-quality red wine.
The proportion of low-quality red wine sold in the market will decrease.
The average quality of red wine sold in the market will decrease.

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem:
Clothing retail market can be classified as monopolistic competition. Which of the following statements about clothing retail market are correct?

(1) The retailers engage in both price and non-price competitions.
(2) There are a few dominant sellers in the market.
(3) There is imperfect information about the quality of clothing in the market.
(4) The entry and exit of retailers are restricted.
questions.explanation: Monopolistic competition features price and non-price competition plus product differentiation, not a few dominant sellers or restricted entry.

The business of restaurants near the stations of MTR Tuen Ma Line rises.

questions.explanation: Some unemployed workers move into jobs, so the unemployment rate falls.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: Which of the following would be deducted from the GDP of Hong Kong to calculate the gross national income (GNI) of Hong Kong?

the dividend earned by a Filipino billionaire from his holding of shares of a Hong Kong company
the salary received by an Indonesian domestic worker who worked for a Hong Kong family for two years
the rental income earned from a residential property in the United Kingdom owned by a Hong Kong resident

questions.explanation: Income earned in Hong Kong by a non-resident is deducted from GDP when converting to GNI.

questions.stem: Which of the following will result in a leftward shift of the short run aggregate supply curve?

choices.text: The stock market becomes more volatile.
There is a decrease in birth rate.
The transportation cost of raw materials rises.

questions.explanation: Higher transportation cost raises production cost and shifts SRAS left.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem:
A country relaxed its immigration requirements to attract foreigners to work, live and study there. It is estimated that 200 000 foreigners will be settling there this year. Which of the following statements about the relaxation of immigration requirements is correct?

(1) The aggregate demand of the country will rise.
(2) The labour productivity of the country will rise.
(3) The short run aggregate supply of the country will rise.
questions.explanation: More people increase AD, and an inflow of workers can raise SRAS and productivity if they are skilled enough.

questions.explanation: If all deposits are kept as reserves, the banking multiplier is 1, not 0.

questions.stem: Which of the following will widen the deflationary (output) gap of a country?

choices.text: Its trading partners experience an economic recovery.
Credit cards are more widely used.
There is a decrease in transfer payment.
The central bank prints more money.

questions.explanation: Lower transfer payments reduce aggregate demand and widen the output gap.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem:
Which of the following may lead to a rise in aggregate output and an improvement in equity in Hong Kong at the same time?

(1) a charity fund donating HK$10 billion to set up non-governmental organisations in order to provide services for the underprivileged
(2) a cash payout of HK$10 000 to each permanent resident aged 18 or above by the Government
(3) a 1% reduction in the standard tax rate of salaries tax
questions.explanation: A targeted charity fund and a broad cash payout both raise AD and can improve equity; the tax cut is less clearly equity-improving.

choices.text: The public can sell their Hong Kong dollars to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in exchange for US dollars at the market exchange rate.
The public can sell their Hong Kong dollars to the three note-issuing banks in exchange for US dollars at the linked exchange rate.
An appreciation of Hong Kong dollar against Japanese yen would lead to an appreciation of US dollar against Japanese yen.
An appreciation of US dollar against Japanese yen would lead to an appreciation of Hong Kong dollar against Japanese yen.

questions.explanation: Because HKD is linked to USD, an appreciation of USD against JPY implies HKD also appreciates against JPY.

questions.chapterTitle: 三個基本經濟問題與私有產權
questions.keyPoint: 三個基本經濟問題的意思及相關例子
questions.stem:
參考以下有關新冠肺炎疫苗接種計劃的資料。

- 所有居民可以免費參加該計劃。
- 政府在一些政府大樓設立了疫苗接種中心，並調派公務員往中心工作。

上述資料與經濟學中的 ______ 問題有關。

(1) 「生產什麼」
(2) 「怎樣生產」
(3) 「為誰生產」
questions.explanation: 免費參加涉及分配，所以關乎「為誰生產」；設立中心和調派人手涉及投入選擇，所以關乎「怎樣生產」。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem:
湯美中六畢業，正計劃將來。他有數個選項，其優先次序如下。

第一選項：在咖啡店當一名咖啡師
第二選項：當一名數碼市場推廣業的實習生
第三選項：當一名初級消防員

在湯美的就業選擇中，下列哪項因素最不可能影響他的成本效益分析？

choices.text: 更多公司擴張其數碼市場推廣部。
初級消防員的薪金下降。
救火的安全措施大幅改善。

questions.explanation: 他的機會成本是最佳被放棄選項，即第二選項，所以與第三選項相關的改變最不可能影響分析。

questions.keyPoint: 生產者物品及消費品

私用品 ...... 某一個人的消費會令其他人可享用的數量減少

消費者物品 ...... 它能直接滿足人們的慾望

questions.explanation: 轉播能直接滿足人們的慾望，所以是消費者物品。

由於所有合夥人均負無限責任，業務風險會減少。

公眾能以聯繫匯率向三家發鈔銀行賣出港元以兌換美元。
港元兌日圓升值會令美元兌日圓升值。
美元兌日圓升值會令港元兌日圓升值。

questions.explanation: 由於港元與美元掛鈎，美元兌日圓升值會令港元兌日圓同樣升值。

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem:
If a command economy turns into a market-oriented economy,

(1) the income distribution of the economy will be more uneven.
(2) more resources will be allocated by price mechanism.
(3) people will have private property rights over all resources.
questions.explanation: A market-oriented economy relies more on the price mechanism. A market system does not necessarily make income distribution more uneven or give private rights over every resource.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: In Lunar New Year, tourists reserve tables in waterfront restaurants to enjoy firework display. The firework display is a ______ because ______.

choices.text: public good ...... the government pays for the firework display
public good ...... one individual's consumption will not reduce its availability to others
private good ...... private firms have to use resources to produce the firework display
private good ...... the seats in waterfront restaurants are excludable in consumption

questions.explanation: A firework display is non-rival in consumption: one viewer does not reduce the display available to another viewer.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of interest
questions.stem:
Which of the following may exist in a barter economy?

(1) specialisation
(2) inflation
(3) interest
questions.explanation: Specialisation can exist with barter, and interest can be the price of earlier access to resources. Inflation requires a monetary price level.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of buying shares and bonds from small investors’ point of view
questions.stem: Some small investors prefer debentures to shares. Which of the following is a possible reason for that?

choices.text: The return of debentures is generally higher than that of shares.
The price of shares may rise while that of debentures is fixed.
Shareholders need to spend time managing the company but debenture holders do not.
Companies have obligation to redeem debentures but they have no such obligation for shares.

questions.explanation: A debenture is debt that a company must repay at maturity, unlike a share. This can make it more attractive to a risk-averse small investor.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: If a public limited company in Hong Kong gets listed on the stock exchange,

choices.text: it will face a higher profits tax rate.
it can no longer keep its accounting information confidential.
its shareholders will enjoy higher liquidity of their assets.
it will enjoy economies of scale.

questions.explanation: Listing makes a company's shares easier to buy and sell, increasing shareholders' liquidity.

questions.keyPoint: Natural resources: land
questions.stem: Refer to the following dialogue.

visuals.alt: Dialogue about a lake owner and a fishing-boat captain organising tours.
visuals.caption: Lake tour arrangement

choices.text: wage and interest ...... rent and profit

questions.explanation: Captain Cook supplies labour and capital, earning wage and interest. Landlord Li supplies land and entrepreneurship, earning rent and profit.
questions.postVisualStem:
Landlord Li: 'I own a lake with great natural views. How can I earn income from it, Captain Cook?'

Captain Cook: 'I have a fishing boat! I can be the captain of some boat trips in the lake!'

Landlord Li: 'Let's organise fishing tours and charge the tourists a large sum! I will pay you a daily rate, Captain Cook. And I will pocket the remaining income. We will earn a lot of money together!'

Given the return of land is rent, the return of labour is wage, the return of capital is interest while the return of entrepreneur is profit. The income earned by Captain Cook consists of ______ while the remaining income earned by Landlord Li consists of ______.

questions.keyPoint: External economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem:
Tai On Building (太安樓) in eastern Hong Kong Island is well-known as a 'foodie paradise'. A variety of street snacks such as cart noodles, egg waffles, dumplings and mango mochi are sold by numerous small vendors. Customers from different districts fill their stomachs at Tai On Building.

Based on the above information, street snack vendors at Tai On Building can ______.
questions.explanation: The concentration of many snack vendors creates a shared reputation and attracts customers, an external economy of scale.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The following table shows the production plan of a firm which employs two factors only, namely labour and machinery.
questions.explanation: Total products are 20, 42 and 66. The marginal products are 20, 22 and 24, so the next marginal product must be below 24; average product can still be 23.
questions.postVisualStem: If the above data illustrate the law of diminishing marginal returns, the value of X ______.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: Refer to the following table about the cost-output relationship of a profit-maximising firm.

choices.text: the minimum cost of production is $18.
the profit maximising output is 3 units.
the marginal cost of every unit of output will remain unchanged.

questions.explanation: After every average cost falls by $1, total costs are $4, $10, $18, $28 and $40. At price $8, profit is maximised at 3 units with profit $6, so only the minimum total cost statement is correct.
questions.postVisualStem: If the average cost of every unit of output decreases by $1 and the market price is $8,

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem:
Alfred booked a room in a resort hotel. Later he found that Betty had booked a room in the same hotel at a lower price. Which of the following are possible reasons for such a price difference?

(1) Alfred's booking was non-refundable while Betty's booking was with free cancellation.
(2) Alfred booked the room in a weekend while Betty booked the room in a weekday.
(3) Alfred booked the room with sea view while Betty booked the room with street view.
questions.explanation: Weekend demand and a sea view can raise a room price. A non-refundable booking normally costs less, not more, than one with free cancellation.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Measuring price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: When the price of Australia's red wine decreases from $70 to $50, the quantity demanded increases from 100 units to 122 units. What is the arc elasticity of demand for Australia's red wine within the above price range?
questions.explanation: Arc elasticity = (22 / 111) divided by (20 / 60) = about 0.59.

questions.keyPoint: Concepts of demand
questions.stem:
When the market supply curve of a good is derived, which of the following is/are assumed to be constant?

(1) the market price of the good
(2) the prices of factors of production of the good
(3) the expected future price of the good
questions.explanation: A supply curve relates quantity supplied to the good's own price, so factor prices and expected future prices must be held constant.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Allocative function
questions.stem:
In recent years, the rise in demand for private cars in China has attracted Volkswagen, a German car manufacturer, to set up car manufacturing factories in China.

The above case illustrates the ______ function of price because ______.

choices.text: rationing ...... private cars are sold to the highest-valued users in China
rationing ...... fewer buyers are willing to buy private cars in Germany
allocative ...... the supply of private cars falls in Germany
allocative ...... more resources are allocated to the production of private cars in China

questions.explanation: Higher demand and expected prices signal firms to direct resources to car production in China, showing the allocative function of price.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings of complements, substitutes, normal and inferior goods
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram for Good Y.

visuals.alt: Supply and demand curves S0-S2 and D0-D2 with equilibrium points A-E.
visuals.caption: Inferior good

questions.explanation: A fall in income raises demand for an inferior good, shifting demand from D0 to D1 and moving equilibrium from E to A.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose Good Y is an inferior good and the initial market equilibrium point is E. If there is a fall in the average income level of consumers, the new market equilibrium point will be ______.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: The following table shows the demand and supply schedules of a good.
questions.explanation: With the subsidy, buyers pay $22 and producers receive $28, so 60 units are traded. The subsidy is $360 and the consumers' and producers' shares are $2 and $4 per unit respectively, a 1:2 ratio.
questions.postVisualStem: If the government provides a $6 per-unit subsidy for the producers of the good, the total subsidy provided by the government will be ______ and the ratio of consumers' share to producers' share of the subsidy will be ______.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram for the exported Chinese rare earth minerals.

visuals.alt: Supply-demand diagram with an effective quota for exported Chinese rare earth minerals.
visuals.caption: Rare earth export quota

questions.explanation: Removing an effective quota increases quantity and lowers price. With demand elastic over the relevant range, the total exchange value rises rather than falls.
questions.postVisualStem:
If China abolished the quota on the export of rare earth minerals,

(1) the export price of the rare earth minerals would drop.
(2) the export quantity of the rare earth minerals would rise.
(3) the total exchange value of the exported rare earth minerals would drop.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: A non-profit organisation supports the increase in cigarette tax. The organisation reveals that every 10% increase in cigarette prices reduces the total cigarette quantity transacted by 4%. Which of the following statements about cigarette tax is INCORRECT?

choices.text: Law of demand is illustrated in the above case.
The total expenditure on cigarette will increase after the increase of the cigarette tax.
The increase in cigarette tax may lead to a greater income inequality.
The cigarette tax could help reduce the problem of under-production of cigarette.

questions.explanation: Cigarettes create a negative externality and are over-produced, not under-produced. A corrective tax can reduce that over-production.

questions.stem: ABC Diamond Cutting Factories expand its business as follows.

visuals.alt: ABC Diamond Cutting Factories expanding to jewellery shops and a hotel.
visuals.caption: Business expansion

questions.explanation: Opening jewellery shops moves forward along the production chain, while entering the hotel business is conglomerate diversification.
questions.postVisualStem: To ABC Diamond Cutting Factories, the types of expansion shown by X and Y are ______ expansion and ______ expansion respectively.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem:
Study the following news extract.

In the last decade, the rent of residential units in Berlin was doubled due to continuous increase in demand. To deal with the problem, the Berlin government imposed a 'Rent Frozen Bill' under which the rent of residential units was not allowed to increase for at least 5 years.

Suppose a similar bill is implemented in Hong Kong. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: The property tax revenue of the government will increase.
There will be a deadweight loss if the demand for residential units keeps on increasing.
The property owners will have higher incentives to renovate their flats.

questions.explanation: A binding rent ceiling creates a shortage and a deadweight loss when demand keeps rising.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price floor
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram for Good X.

visuals.alt: Supply-demand diagram with price floors P1 and P2.
visuals.caption: Price floor

choices.text: quantity transacted of Good X will remain at Q1.
excess demand of Good X will change to excess supply.

questions.explanation: Raising an effective price floor increases the shortage/excess supply distortion and the deadweight loss.
questions.postVisualStem: If the price floor of Good X changes from P1 to P2,

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem:
Refer to the following cafe post.

**SCREAMING CHILD TAX**
For the benefit of both staff and customers alike, we have taken the decision to impose a tax on children who scream. If we notice that your child is screaming, an automatic 15% surcharge will be applied to your bill. For every further screaming child you have in your group, an additional 10% will be added.

With reference to the above information, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: Children screaming in the cafe results in negative externality and all cafes should introduce similar policy to restore efficiency.
The extra charge on screaming children increases the marginal private cost of the groups with screaming children.
The 'screaming child tax' is a government solution to the divergence between private and social costs.
The 'screaming child tax' is a kind of discrimination and should not be imposed.

questions.explanation: The cafe's surcharge makes a group pay more for an additional screaming child, increasing that group's marginal private cost. It is not a government tax.

questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Lorenz curve
questions.stem: Study the following two Lorenz curves.

visuals.alt: Lorenz curves for Country A and Country B.
visuals.caption: Lorenz curves

choices.text: the Gini coefficient of Country A is larger.
Country A has a higher standard of living.
the top 20% of households in Country A have less total income.
Country A has a more even income distribution.

questions.explanation: Country A's Lorenz curve lies closer to the line of equality, showing a more even income distribution.
