questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem: The following table shows the data of average annual income earned by women and men according to their age in 2018.
questions.explanation: Career interruption, discrimination and accumulated human capital can all explain the observed income differences.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following may explain the phenomena shown by the above data?

(1) Women tend to leave the job market earlier than men for taking care of the family, leading to fewer women to take up senior positions in companies.
(2) Sex discrimination in labour market exists in the older generations.
(3) Accumulation of human capital contributes to the difference in income between different age groups.

questions.postVisualStem: According to the above data, the underemployment rate is ______.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: Which of the following should be deducted from the gross domestic product of Hong Kong to calculate the gross national income of Hong Kong?

choices.text: the fee paid by a Hong Kong football club to a Japanese football team for an exhibition match in Hong Kong
the rent earned by a Hong Kong property developer from its residential property in Japan
the capital gain earned by a Japanese insurance corporation from its financial investment in Hong Kong
the dividend paid by a listed company in Japan to a Hong Kong resident

questions.explanation: Income paid from Hong Kong to a foreign football team is a factor income outflow and is deducted when moving from GDP to GNI.

questions.keyPoint: Growth rate of GDP
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the gross domestic product (GDP) of Country A.

visuals.alt: Nominal and real GDP curves from 2015 to 2019.

The actual inflation rate was equal to the expected inflation rate in 2017.
The nominal GDP has been increasing since 2016.

questions.explanation: From 2016 to 2018, nominal GDP rises faster than real GDP, so the price level rises. The other statements cannot be concluded from the graph.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about Country A is correct?

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason for a leftward shift of the short run aggregate supply curve in a country?

choices.text: There is a continuous increase in price level.
The largest market of the country's exports suffers from an economic recession.
More citizens emigrate to foreign countries.
The wages of labour slowly adjust downward due to institutional factors.

questions.explanation: When wages are sticky downward after an adverse change, production costs remain high and SRAS shifts left.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the asset demand for money of an economy.

visuals.alt: Asset demand for money shifts left from MA0 to MA1.
visuals.caption: Asset demand for money

choices.text: There is a contraction of monetary base.
The use of electronic wallets such as Alipay (支付寶) becomes more popular.
The expected rate of return of holding bonds increases.

questions.explanation: A higher expected return on bonds increases the opportunity cost of holding money and shifts asset demand for money left.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following will cause the above change in asset demand for money?

questions.keyPoint: Definitions of M1, M2 and M3 in
questions.stem:
The legal tender in Hong Kong held by licensed banks is included in ______.

(1) monetary base
(2) money supply M2
(3) money supply M3
questions.explanation: Legal tender held by licensed banks is part of the monetary base, not money held by the public in M2 or M3.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about an economy. Suppose all banks do not hold any excess reserves.

choices.text: the actual banking multiplier will be 4.
the maximum amount of loans will be $120 million.
the maximum amount of deposits will be $140 million.
the new money supply will be $160 million.

questions.explanation: The initial reserves are $20 million and deposits $100 million, implying a 20% reserve ratio. Depositing the $10 million cash raises reserves to $30 million, so maximum deposits are $150 million and loans $120 million.
questions.postVisualStem: If the public deposits all the cash into the banking system,

visuals.caption: Money market

choices.text: will increase ...... may increase or decrease
may increase or decrease ...... will decrease

questions.explanation: Higher income raises money demand and selling bonds lowers money supply. Both changes raise the interest rate, while money supply falls so equilibrium money quantity falls.
questions.postVisualStem: If the income of the public increases and the central bank sells government bonds to the public, the interest rate ______ and the quantity of money ______.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Which of the following is a contractionary monetary policy?

choices.text: an increase in the discount rate
an increase in the salaries tax rate
a decrease in the required reserve ratio
a decrease in the quota for migration

questions.explanation: A higher discount rate discourages banks from borrowing from the central bank and contracts money supply.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual banking multipliers
questions.stem: Which of the following will increase the actual banking multiplier?

choices.text: The public tends to hold more cash.
The use of credit card becomes more popular.
The central bank increases the required reserve ratio.
The interest rate of bank deposit decreases.

questions.explanation: More credit-card use reduces the public's need to hold cash and leaves more funds in banks, raising the actual banking multiplier.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: When there is unexpected inflation, which of the following persons will gain?

choices.text: a landlord who adjusts his rental according to the price index
a creditor who has loaned out a sum of money at a floating interest rate
an employer who signs a fixed nominal wage contract with his employees
a retired civil servant who receives a fixed monthly pension

questions.explanation: With a fixed nominal wage, unexpected inflation lowers the employer's real wage cost, so the employer gains.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem:
Which of the following policies would offset the effect of an increase in the willingness to invest on the price level?

(1) an increase in profits tax rate
(2) an increase in transfer payment
(3) a decrease in tax allowance
questions.explanation: Higher profits tax reduces investment, while a lower tax allowance reduces consumption. Both offset the inflationary effect; higher transfer payments would reinforce it.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)

visuals.alt: AD, SRAS and LRAS diagram with initial short-run equilibrium E0.
visuals.caption: Aggregate demand and supply

questions.explanation: Lower transfer payments reduce aggregate demand, widening the output gap. Lower income reduces imports, creating a trade surplus from the initially balanced position.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: An economist said, 'The continuous fall in stock prices in our country has already affected the consumption expenditure as well as the money demand. We should implement a policy to relieve the effects on the output level and the interest rate.' Which of the following policies can stabilise the output level and the interest rate in the country at the same time in the short run? (Assume the interest rate is mainly affected by the asset demand for money in this case.)

choices.text: The government increases cash subsidy to the poor.
The government gives tariff exemption to the imports of goods.
The central bank instructs the commercial banks to tighten the requirement of personal loans.
The central bank buys government bonds from the public.

questions.explanation: A stock-price fall lowers consumption and asset demand for money. An open-market purchase raises money supply, offsetting the fall in output while stabilising the interest rate.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem:
In 2019, the Japanese government increases the general sales tax rate on most of the goods and services from 8% to 10%. As a result,

(1) income inequality will be higher.
(2) the fiscal deficit will be eliminated.
(3) the invisible trade deficit will decrease.
questions.explanation: A general sales tax is regressive, so it may widen income inequality. It does not necessarily eliminate a fiscal deficit or change the invisible trade balance in the stated way.

questions.keyPoint: Four basic principles of taxation
questions.stem:
The following is an extract of the mission of the Inland Revenue Department.

Our Mission
We are committed to
- collecting revenue efficiently and cost-effectively
- enabling staff to acquire the necessary knowledge, skills and attitude so that they can contribute their best to the achievement of our vision

The above mission is in line with the ______ principle of taxation put forward by Adam Smith.
questions.explanation: Collecting tax efficiently and cost-effectively expresses Adam Smith's principle of economy.

questions.keyPoint: Taxation in

According to the above information, which type(s) of tax does he need to pay to the Hong Kong government?

(1) Property tax
(2) Stamp duty
(3) Profits tax
(4) First registration tax
questions.explanation: Buying the flat incurs stamp duty. The overseas factory profit, an owner-occupied flat and a second-hand car do not create the other listed Hong Kong tax liabilities.

the volume of goods exported from Europe to the US.
the total value of US exports to Europe (in terms of Euro).

questions.stem: Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: The money supply M1 of Hong Kong has to be fully backed up by the US dollar.
Hong Kong's export volume will increase when the US dollar depreciates against other currencies.

questions.chapterTitle: 三個基本經濟問題與私有產權
questions.keyPoint: 不同社會解決基本經濟問題的方法
questions.stem:
若一計劃經濟轉變為市場主導經濟，

(1) 該經濟的收入分佈會更不均。
(2) 更多的資源會以價格機制分配。
(3) 人們擁有全部資源的私有產權。

questions.explanation: 固定名義薪酬在通脹下實質成本下降，僱主得益。

questions.stem:

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements

questions.stem:
Refer to the following statements made by Peter and Mary.

Mary: Hong Kong's Gini coefficient is the highest in Asia.

questions.stem:
After graduating from secondary school, Paul considers whether to become a full-time Key Opinion Leader (KOL) in social media channels or to become an e-sports player.

Which of the following will lower Paul's cost of being a full-time KOL after his graduation?

(1) Paul receives sponsored video equipment for KOL.
(2) The e-sports team offers a lower basic salary to Paul.
(3) The risk of social media channels being attacked by hackers increases.
questions.explanation: The sponsored equipment and a lower e-sports salary both lower the cost of choosing KOL work.

questions.stem:
Because of COVID-19, normal schooling was disrupted. Most schools used video communication software, such as Zoom and Google Meet, to conduct online lessons. Suppose the school campus was re-opened and face-to-face lessons were allowed.

Which of the following would be the LEAST important factor for teachers to choose between online lessons and face-to-face lessons?

choices.text: The risk of contracting COVID-19 for teachers is lower when they conduct online lessons.
Teachers have no idea what their students are doing during online lessons because students may turn off their cameras.
Teachers have already spent a lot of time learning how to use the video communication software to conduct online lessons.
The eyesight of teachers may be worsened by the intensive use of the video communication software in conducting online lessons.

questions.explanation: The time already spent learning video software is a sunk cost and is least relevant to the current choice.

questions.explanation: Nominal GDP is unchanged while real GDP falls, so the price level rises; per-capita nominal GDP falls, so population rises.
questions.postVisualStem: Compared to the previous year, the general price level has ______ and population has ______ in the economy in the current year.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem:
Suppose the unemployment rate of an economy is 8%. Which of the following would increase the unemployment rate?

(1) 15% of the new graduates could not find jobs successfully.
(2) Some employers closed down their local businesses and migrated to other countries.
(3) Some of the part-time workers lost their job due to automation of production.
questions.explanation: All three events increase unemployment or reduce employment among people in the labour force.

questions.keyPoint: Uses and limitations of national income statistics
questions.stem: The per-capita real GDP of a country would understate the general living standard because

choices.text: it includes the value of non-consumption goods.
it does not consider the size of population.
it does not reflect the increasing crime rate in society.
it does not include all non-marketed goods.

questions.explanation: Non-marketed goods are omitted from GDP, so living standards can be understated.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply

choices.text: The cost of production increases due to an increase in global demand for oil.
The profitability of firms increases with the rise in price level, since the difference between output prices and input prices increases.
An increase in interest rate leads to an increase in cost of investment.
The operation of labour market resumes to normal after a massive labour strike.

questions.explanation: A recovery after a massive labour strike shifts SRAS right.

visuals.alt: Short run aggregate supply curve shifting right from SRAS0 to SRAS1.
visuals.caption: Rightward shift of SRAS

questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: Study the following diagram.

choices.text: There is an increase in oil prices.
There is a decrease in production subsidy.
The public tends to save less.
The government increases the salaries tax rate.

questions.explanation: Saving less raises aggregate demand, moving the economy to a higher long-run equilibrium point on LRAS.

visuals.alt: AD-AS diagram with initial equilibrium E and new long-run point C.
visuals.caption: AD-AS long-run equilibrium

questions.postVisualStem: The initial equilibrium point of an oil importing country is at E. If the new long run equilibrium point is at C, which of the following is a possible reason for the change in the equilibrium point?

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem:
The outbreak of COVID-19 results in a significant decline in employment level and the volume of exports of a country.

Which of the following policies can most likely relieve the above two problems?

choices.text: The central bank reduces the discount rate.
The government distributes cash to citizens aged 18 years old or above.
The government imposes 'employment support scheme' to industries that are adversely affected.
The country devalues its currency against the currencies of its major trading partners.

questions.explanation: Currency devaluation can raise exports and employment together.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem:
Study the following news extract about Bitcoin (比特幣).

In 2018, Kentucky Fried Chicken Canada launched 'Bitcoin Bucket'. The company set up a Facebook live feed, displaying the number of bitcoins needed to pay for the meal as in the picture below. The 'Bitcoin Bucket' could only be purchased online and would be delivered to the buyers' home later.
questions.explanation: Bitcoin is used for online payment and pricing in the case, but not deferred payment.

visuals.alt: Bitcoin Bucket news extract with bitcoin price shown on a food bucket.
visuals.caption: Bitcoin Bucket

questions.postVisualStem:
In the above case, Bitcoin performed as a ______.

(1) medium of exchange
(2) unit of account
(3) standard of deferred payment

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(1) Monetary base is $100 million.
(2) Actual reserves are $40 million.

questions.topicGroup: Licensed banks, restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies in
questions.keyPoint: Features of the three types of deposit-taking institutions
questions.stem:
Jack wants to deposit $400 000 for 5 months. Which of the following financial institutions in Hong Kong can accept his deposit?

(1) a restricted licence bank
(2) a virtual bank which is classified as a licensed bank
(3) a deposit-taking company
questions.explanation: A virtual bank classified as a licensed bank can accept the deposit, and a deposit-taking company can accept a fixed deposit of $100000 or above for at least 3 months; a restricted licence bank cannot accept this $400000 deposit.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money demand and money supply curves of an economy. The original equilibrium point is at E.
questions.explanation: A more volatile stock market raises money demand; bond redemption increases money supply, leading to point B.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Nominal interest rate as the (opportunity) cost of holding money
questions.stem:
Suppose the actual inflation rate and the nominal interest rate are -1% and 3% respectively. Which of the following statements are correct?

(1) The cost of holding cash is 3%.
(2) The expected real interest rate is higher than the nominal interest rate.
(3) The actual real rate of return on holding cash is 1%.
questions.explanation: Holding cash forgoes the nominal interest rate and gains purchasing power under deflation.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem: Which of the following would offset the effect on aggregate output of an expansionary fiscal policy?

choices.text: The use of electronic wallets became more popular.
The government increased quota on the importation of foreign domestic helpers.

questions.explanation: A rise in cash holding reduces the expansionary effect on aggregate output.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem:
Due to the COVID-19 outbreak, most of the flights were cancelled, leading to a significant drop in the number of tourists visiting Hong Kong. At the same time, many employees in Hong Kong were forced to take no pay leave.

Which of the following diagrams can best describe the consequence of the above incidents?
questions.explanation: Fewer tourists and no-pay leave reduce aggregate demand, matching diagram B.

visuals.alt: Four AD-AS diagram options labelled A, B, C and D.
visuals.caption: AD-AS diagram options

questions.keyPoint: Surplus budget, deficit budget and balanced budget
questions.stem: Which of the following policies may narrow a deflationary (output) gap and reduce the budget deficit at the same time?

choices.text: an open market purchase of government bonds
an increase in income tax allowance
an increase in required reserve ratio

questions.explanation: Open-market purchase is expansionary monetary policy and does not widen the budget deficit.

questions.stem: Suppose a government finances its expenditure by collecting tax from the households and the amount of expenditure equals the amount of tax collected. The effect on aggregate demand will be ______.
questions.explanation: Under the balanced-budget multiplier, equal increases in tax and expenditure can still raise aggregate demand.

questions.keyPoint: Taxation in
questions.stem:
Mr Li is a major shareholder of a Hong Kong listed company which makes huge profits. He has sold some of his residential properties, and received rental income from some leased commercial buildings.

According to the above information, which types of tax does Mr Li need to pay to the Hong Kong government?

(1) profits tax
(2) stamp duty
(3) property tax
questions.explanation: Stamp duty and property tax apply, but profits tax is paid by the company, not Mr Li as shareholder.

choices.text: Hong Kong had an invisible trade deficit in 2020 second quarter.
Hong Kong's net exports in 2020 second quarter was lower than that in 2019 second quarter.
Hong Kong's exports of goods in 2020 second quarter was lower than that in 2020 first quarter.
Hong Kong's total imports of goods and services in 2020 second quarter was lower than that in 2019 second quarter.

questions.explanation: Imports of both goods and services fell year-on-year in 2020 Q2.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: Both Country A and Country B produce only toys and computers. The table below shows the amount of inputs required by Country A and Country B in the production of toys and computers.

choices.text: Country A has an absolute advantage in the production of computers over Country B.
Country B has no comparative advantage in producing any goods as its opportunity cost of producing toys equals that of producing computers.
If a transportation cost of 1 unit of computers is required to trade 1 unit of toys, it is impossible to have mutually beneficial trade.
It is impossible to have mutually beneficial trade as the two countries have equal productivity in producing toys.

questions.explanation: The extra transport cost removes the possible gains from trade in toys.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, which of the following statements is correct?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: Suppose the world price of soybeans is $20. A small open economy imposes a per unit tariff of $5 on imported soybeans. The diagram below shows the economy's supply and demand curves of soybeans.

choices.text: The total revenue of domestic producers is $400 after the imposition of tariff.
The total import value inclusive of tariff is $500.
If the tariff is raised to $15, this economy will become an exporter of soybeans.
If the tariff is abolished, the total import value will be $400.

questions.explanation: With the $5 tariff, the domestic price is $25 and imports are 20 units, so import value inclusive of tariff is $500.

questions.topicGroup: 區分實證性陳述和規範性陳述
questions.keyPoint: 區分實證性陳述和規範性陳述
questions.stem:
參閱下列彼得和瑪莉所作的陳述。

彼得：香港作為一已發展經濟體，它的堅尼系數太高了。
瑪莉：香港的堅尼系數是全亞洲最高的。

______ 的陳述是 ______，因為 ______。

choices.text: 彼得 ... 實證性 ... 大部分人認同該陳述
彼得 ... 規範性 ... 該陳述和現實世界的數據並不相符
瑪莉 ... 實證性 ... 該陳述可以被事實推翻
瑪莉 ... 規範性 ... 該陳述涉及價值判斷

questions.explanation: 瑪莉的陳述可用事實核對，所以屬實證性陳述。

questions.chapterTitle: 三個基本經濟問題與私有產權
questions.keyPoint: 不同社會解決基本經濟問題的方法
questions.stem: 為應對口罩市場短缺，政府向全港市民免費派發可重用的 CuMask。這是以 ______ 去解決 ______ 問題的一個例子。
questions.explanation: 政府把免費口罩分配給市民，是以政府指令解決「為誰生產」的問題。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem:
中學畢業後，保羅考慮成為全職的社交媒體頻道關鍵意見領袖（KOL），或成為電競選手。下列哪些會減低保羅畢業後成為全職 KOL 的成本？

(1) 保羅獲得錄製 KOL 影片器材的贊助。
(2) 電競隊給予保羅較低的基本薪金。
(3) 社交媒體頻道被駭客攻擊的風險增加。
questions.explanation: 獲贊助器材及電競薪金下降，均會降低成為全職 KOL 的成本。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋為何已付出且無法取回的支出並非成本
questions.stem: 由於新冠肺炎，正常上課受到干擾。大部分學校使用視像通訊軟件，例如 Zoom 和 Google Meet，進行網上授課。假設校園重新開放，並准許面對面授課。下列哪項是教師選擇網上授課還是面對面授課時最不重要的因素？

choices.text: 網上授課可令教師感染新冠肺炎的風險較低。
教師不知道學生在網上授課時正在做甚麼，因為學生可能關掉鏡頭。
教師已經花費很多時間學習使用視像通訊軟件進行網上授課。
頻密使用視像通訊軟件進行網上授課可導致教師的視力受損。

questions.explanation: 已花在學習軟件上的時間是沉沒成本，對現時選擇最不相關。

questions.explanation: 件薪可提高產量誘因，但可能降低質素；時薪與產量的直接關係較弱。

choices.text: 該公司能享有較低利得稅稅率。

questions.explanation: 私有化後公司仍可為有限公司，亦仍可發行股份籌集資金。

Refer to the following suggestion for tackling the housing problem.

The government should build a new type of housing, called Easy Living, for which the owners can lease their flats at a controlled rent. If the owners want to sell their flats, they can only sell them back to the government.

Compared with owning a private housing unit, ______ will be weakened for those owning an Easy Living housing unit.

(1) the right to use
(2) the right to receive income
(3) the right to transfer
questions.explanation: A controlled rent restricts the income right and sale-back restriction limits the transfer right; the owner still has the right to use the flat.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are related to the problem of 'for whom to produce'?

(1) Only the elderly and eligible persons with disabilities can enjoy a concessionary fare of $2 per trip under the Public Transport Fare Concession Scheme.
(2) Public rental housing (PRH) households whose family income exceeds 5 times the PRH income limits should vacate their PRH flats.
(3) The e-Sports & Music Festival moved from Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre to Hong Kong Coliseum to house more fans from all over the world.
questions.explanation: The first two policies determine who receives subsidised transport and housing. The venue change is about how much to produce.

questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem: Mr Lo spent $60 000 on buying a second hand car three years ago. Suppose he can resell the car at $2 000. Alternatively, he needs to spend $5 000 on repairing the car before he can continue to use it. What is his cost of continuing to use the car?
questions.explanation: The relevant cost is the $5 000 repair bill plus the $2 000 forgone resale value, totalling $7 000. The original purchase is sunk cost.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: If the fixed cost of a price-taking firm decreases by $200 and the marginal cost of each unit of output increases by $10, the profit-maximising output will ______ and the profit ______.
questions.explanation: A higher marginal cost lowers the price-taking firm's profit-maximising output. The lower fixed cost and higher variable costs have opposing effects on profit.

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: The following table shows the production data of a firm. The only inputs required are capital and labour.

choices.text: the law of diminishing returns applies to the firm.
the firm enjoys economies of scale.

questions.explanation: Average cost falls from $10 to $7 as output rises, so the firm is enjoying economies of scale.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above table, we can conclude that

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem:
In the 2018-19 Budget, the Hong Kong Government raised the subsidy ceiling of the Continuing Education Fund from $10 000 to $20 000 per applicant to encourage members of the public to pursue further education.

This policy will lead to a rise in ______ and ______ in the future.
questions.explanation: Further education raises human capital and workers' productivity, and it makes changing occupations easier rather than directly changing location.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
New World China Land Limited (Stock Code: 0917) announced privatisation of the company and cancelled its listing status at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

Which of the following are the possible advantages of the above change?

(1) The company can choose not to disclose its financial accounts to the public.
(2) The company can reduce the risk of being taken over.
(3) The company can enjoy a lower profits tax rate.
questions.explanation: A private company has fewer public disclosure requirements and is less exposed to takeovers. Delisting does not change the profits tax rate.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital
questions.stem:
Which of the following are capital of a cafe?

(1) coffee machines
(2) coffee beans
(3) video game consoles brought by its customers for party
(4) comic books which can be borrowed by its customers free of charge
questions.explanation: Coffee machines and comic books are man-made resources used in supplying the cafe's service. Coffee beans are raw materials and customers' consoles are not the cafe's resources.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of internal expansion
questions.stem:
A Hong Kong travel company offers package tours to Japan. It invested in building a hotel, which provides accommodation services to its tour members visiting Japan.

Which of the following is most likely the motive behind the expansion?

choices.text: to secure the supply of factor inputs
to ensure a market outlet of its services

questions.explanation: Owning accommodation lets the firm secure a market outlet for its package-tour customers, a forward integration motive.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The following table shows the cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm.
questions.explanation: Total costs at 5, 6 and 7 units are $100, $150 and $210, so marginal costs are $50 and $60. A competitive firm's price at 6 units is $50.
questions.postVisualStem: If the profit-maximising output is 6 units, the market price will be ______.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of supply
questions.stem:
Study the following news abstract.

A Dengue fever (登革熱) scare has hit Hong Kong after 19 people in the past week were confirmed to have contracted the virus locally. Dengue fever is transmitted to humans by Aedes albopictus (白紋伊蚊), a type of mosquito commonly found in Hong Kong.

Suppose the price and the quantity of mosquito repellents sold in Hong Kong changed by 5% and 120% respectively shortly after the release of the above news. This indicates that during that period and within the price range, there was an ______ the mosquito repellents in Hong Kong.
questions.explanation: The news shifts demand. Quantity changes much more than price, showing elastic supply in the relevant range.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: The table below shows the quantities of high-quality and average-quality Japanese fruits sold in Japan and Hong Kong. Assume the consumers' preferences on Japanese fruits are similar in both economies.
questions.explanation: With the same preferences and transport cost, high-quality fruit must have a higher price and therefore a lower proportional quantity in Hong Kong. Only case (2) fits the law of demand.

visuals.caption: Japanese fruits sold
columns: Quantity of high-quality Japanese fruits sold (units)
Quantity of average-quality Japanese fruits sold (units)

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the cost of transporting both types of fruits from Japan to Hong Kong are the same. Which of the following figures is/are consistent with the law of demand?

(1) Q1 = 30; Q2 = 140
(2) Q1 = 40; Q2 = 150
(3) Q1 = 45; Q2 = 180

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is the supply-demand diagram of e-sports equipment. The initial equilibrium point is E0.
questions.explanation: The equipment subsidy shifts supply right and training support raises demand, moving equilibrium to E2.

visuals.alt: Supply-demand diagram for e-sports equipment with S0-S2, D0-D2 and E0-E4.
visuals.caption: E-sports equipment market

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government promotes e-sports by subsidising e-sports equipment manufacturers as well as the e-sports training programmes. The new equilibrium point will be ______.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following market demand for imported soybeans in Country A.
questions.explanation: At $13, 400 units are demanded and importers receive $10 net of tariff, so revenue is $4 000. The $2 buyer-price rise from a $3 tariff means supply is less elastic than demand; the demand elasticity is below one.
questions.postVisualStem:
When the government of Country A imposes a per-unit tariff of $3 on imported soybeans, the equilibrium price of the imported soybeans increases from $11 to $13. Which of the following statements are correct?

(1) The total sales revenue (net-of-tariff) of the imported soybeans is $4 000.
(2) The supply of the imported soybeans is more elastic than the demand for them.
(3) Within the range of the original and the new equilibrium prices, the elasticity of demand of the imported soybeans is smaller than one.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings of joint supply and competitive supply
questions.stem:
A new private hospital, Gleneagles Hong Kong Hospital (GHK), opened in Wong Chuk Hang in early 2017. GHK offered a 50% salary rise to attract experienced nurses from public hospitals.

Based on the above information, which of the following statements is correct after the opening of GHK?

choices.text: The wage rates of experienced nurses in public hospitals would increase by more than 50% if the demand for nurses is elastic.
The supply of experienced nurses in public hospitals would decrease.
The elasticity of demand of public medical services would decrease.
The waiting time for public medical services would remain unchanged.

questions.explanation: Experienced nurses moving to the new private hospital reduce labour supply available to public hospitals.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules of Good X.
questions.explanation: An effective quota of 200 sets price at $14; a quota of 350 sets price at $8. The market price falls by $6.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules of Good X

questions.postVisualStem: If the government increases the quota for Good X from 200 units to 350 units, the market price will ______.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: SS is the supply curve of electric vehicles. Which of the following reasons can best explain the change of the equilibrium position in the electric vehicle market from A to B?

choices.text: All electric vehicle dealers provided a longer warranty period.
The government removed the subsidies on buying electric vehicles.
The gasoline suppliers greatly raised the price of gasoline.
The cost of building charging stations drastically decreased.

questions.explanation: A move down along an unchanged supply curve comes from a fall in demand. Removing a buyer subsidy lowers demand for electric vehicles.

visuals.alt: Electric-vehicle supply curve SS with equilibrium moving from A to B.
visuals.caption: Electric vehicle market

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about a perfectly competitive market are correct?

(1) Firms cannot survive if they ask a price higher than the market price.
(2) There is no entry barrier to the market.
(3) The profit-maximising condition of the firms is that price equals marginal cost.
questions.explanation: Perfect competitors are price takers with free entry and choose output where price equals marginal cost; charging above market price leaves no sales.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.

choices.text: increasing the progressivity of the salaries tax
raising the air passenger departure tax

questions.explanation: The new Lorenz curve is closer to the equality line. A more progressive salaries tax reduces post-tax income inequality.

visuals.alt: Old and new Lorenz curves for post-tax income distribution.
visuals.caption: Change in Lorenz curve

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following policies would result in the above change in the Lorenz curve in Hong Kong?

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.stem:
Starting from the academic year 2017-18, the Hong Kong Government provides a subsidy of $30 000 annually for students pursuing full-time, self-financed undergraduate programmes (自資學士學位課程) offered by local private educational institutions.

Which of the following are the possible effects of this subsidy scheme?

(1) The unemployment rate will drop as labour force will increase.
(2) The scheme helps equalise opportunities because students from low-income households will have a better chance to receive higher education.
(3) The full employment output level will increase in the future because the average productivity increases after people receiving better education and training.
questions.explanation: The subsidy can widen access to education and raise future productivity and LRAS. Full-time study does not increase the labour force immediately.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram of Good X.
questions.explanation: A binding quota decreases total social surplus and consumer surplus. Producer surplus rises and total expenditure need not decrease.

visuals.alt: Demand and supply diagram of Good X with a quota at Q1.
visuals.caption: Quota on Good X

questions.postVisualStem:
If the government sets a quota at Q1, then ______ will decrease.

(1) total social surplus
(2) total expenditure on Good X
(3) consumer surplus
(4) producer surplus

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between marginal benefit and demand
questions.stem: Suppose there is a bad harvest of flowers due to global warming. The marginal benefit of flowers will ______ and the total exchange value ______.
questions.explanation: A supply decrease raises equilibrium price, so the marginal benefit of the final unit rises. The effect on total exchange value depends on demand elasticity.

questions.keyPoint: Growth rate of GDP
questions.stem: The following table shows the gross domestic product (GDP) data of an economy in a certain year.
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP fell less than real GDP, so the price level increased. Nominal GDP fell less than population, so per-capita nominal GDP increased.
questions.postVisualStem: According to the information above, we can conclude that in that year, the price level ______ and the per capita nominal GDP ______.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: The following table shows the data of an economy.
questions.explanation: The labour force is 6 500 000 x 60% = 3 900 000. Unemployed people equal 120 000, so the unemployment rate is 120 000 / 3 900 000 = 3.08%.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above data, the unemployment rate of the economy is ______.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: To calculate the gross national income of Hong Kong, which of the following should be added to the GDP of Hong Kong?

choices.text: the income earned by a Japanese chef who has worked in a Hong Kong restaurant for two months
the rental received by a Hong Kong resident from leasing his house in Japan to a Japanese
the salary earned by a Hong Kong resident from working as a secretary at the Hong Kong branch office of an Australian company
the money received from selling an apartment in Australia by a Hong Kong resident

questions.explanation: GNI adds factor income received by Hong Kong residents from abroad. The rental from property in Japan is such income; sale proceeds are not income.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: Refer to the following production chain in Country A and answer the question.
questions.explanation: GDP at factor cost includes domestic final consumption, exports and the subsidy, but excludes imported fruit and intermediate sales: 500 + 1 000 + 1 300 + 300 - 800 = $2 300.

visuals.alt: Production chain from imported fruit to domestic and foreign jam consumers.
visuals.caption: Production chain in Country A

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the above production chain has included a subsidy of $300 that is given to the jam manufacturers. What is the contribution of the above production chain to Country A's GDP at factor cost?

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.stem: Country A is an oil-importing country. Which of the following will result in a rightward shift of its short-run aggregate supply curve?

choices.text: All oil-exporting countries decide to increase the daily production of oil.
Extreme cold weather sharply raises the consumption of oil for heating in Country A.
The government of Country A provides tax relief for research in new energy aiming to lessen the reliance on oil.
An earthquake destroys an oil refinery factory in Country A.

questions.explanation: Greater oil supply lowers imported energy costs and shifts short-run aggregate supply right.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The following table shows the balance sheet of Country A's banking system. The money supply in Country A is $2 800 and all banks do not hold excess reserves.

choices.text: The money supply would increase by $1 000.
The monetary base would increase by $200.

questions.explanation: Required reserves are 20% of deposits. The $200 cash deposit creates $1 000 deposits and $800 loans; money supply rises by $800 because currency held by the public falls by $200.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the public deposits $200 cash into the banking system. Which of the following statements about the banking system is correct after the deposit creation process is completed?

questions.keyPoint: How central bank functions are carried out in
questions.stem:
Which of the following is/are the function(s) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority?

(1) Managing the Exchange Fund
(2) Supervising the implementation of fiscal policy
(3) Determining Hong Kong's market interest rate
questions.explanation: The HKMA manages the Exchange Fund. Fiscal policy is not its mandate and market interest rates are not directly determined by it.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem:
Refer to the following hypothetical case.

The currency of Country T, T-Dollar, has depreciated by 40 percent from the beginning of 2018 after the US announced a series of trade sanctions against Country T. As a result, some shops in Country T quoted prices in US Dollar instead of T-Dollar. Shops in black markets refused to accept T-Dollar. Some citizens bought foreign currencies to safeguard their assets.

Which functions of money of the T-Dollar were weakened?

(1) medium of exchange
(2) unit of account
(3) store of value
questions.explanation: Refusal to accept T-Dollar weakens its exchange function, prices quoted in US dollars weaken its unit-of-account role, and flight to foreign currency weakens its store-of-value role.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem:
When a Hong Kong citizen transfers $500 000 from her time deposit account with a restricted licence bank to her savings account with a licensed bank,

(1) money supply (M1) will increase.
(2) money supply (M2) will increase.
(3) money supply (M3) will increase.
questions.explanation: A savings deposit at a licensed bank is included in M2, while a restricted-licence-bank time deposit is included only in M3. M2 rises but M3 is unchanged.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate
questions.stem:
In times of inflation, suppose the nominal interest rate of a bond is higher than the expected inflation rate. If the actual inflation rate turns out to be higher than the expected inflation rate,

(1) the actual inflation rate will be higher than the nominal interest rate of the bond.
(2) the expected real rate of return of the bond will be greater than the actual real rate of return.
(3) the actual real rate of return of the bond may be negative.
(4) the real rate of return of holding cash will be higher than zero.
questions.explanation: Higher-than-expected inflation lowers the actual real return below its expected value and may make it negative; holding cash has a negative real return in inflation.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money supply and money demand curves of an economy. The original equilibrium point is at E.
questions.explanation: Electronic payments lower money demand and a higher reserve ratio lowers money supply. The resulting equilibrium is at D.

visuals.alt: Money supply and money demand curves with equilibrium points A to E.
visuals.caption: Money market

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose electronic payments become more common, and the central bank increases the legal reserve ratio of the commercial banks. The new equilibrium point will be at ______.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: Both the wage rate and general price level increase by 8% in a certain year. If the government increases the salaries tax allowance by 5%,

choices.text: more people will fall into the tax net.
income distribution will become more even.
people's real income after tax will increase.

questions.explanation: Wages and prices rise at the same rate, while a higher tax allowance reduces tax payable. Real income after tax therefore rises.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about quantity theory of money are correct?

(1) If money supply is growing too fast relative to the supply of goods in the economy, inflation will occur.
(2) If money supply increases, nominal output will increase by the same percentage.
(3) If inflation rate is constant, real output will grow at the same percentage as money supply.
questions.explanation: With constant velocity, excessive money growth relative to output causes inflation and money growth changes nominal output proportionally. Constant inflation alone does not determine real output growth.

questions.keyPoint: Four basic principles of taxation
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the relationship between taxable income and tax payment in a tax system.

choices.text: The lower income group pays a smaller percentage of their taxable income as tax payment.
It violates the tax principle of equity put forward by Adam Smith.
It leads to a more even income distribution.

questions.explanation: A fixed tax payment is regressive: lower-income people pay a larger proportion of income, violating the equity principle.

visuals.alt: Tax payment is fixed as taxable income rises.
visuals.caption: Tax payment and taxable income

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the above tax system is correct?

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem:
Under unexpected deflation, which of the following persons will lose?

(1) Ms Mok holds a time deposit of one million dollars in a deposit taking company.
(2) Mr Lo receives interest from Silver Bond of which the rate of return is linked to the inflation, subject to a minimum return of 3%.
(3) Mr Chan signs a two-year contract with an online TV company to subscribe to its service by a fixed monthly payment.
questions.explanation: A fixed monthly payment becomes more valuable under deflation, so Mr Chan loses as the payer. Fixed nominal deposit holders gain; the Silver Bond's minimum return protects Mr Lo.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: The government carried out the following two policies: reduce the profits tax rate for corporations with profit less than two million dollars; inject fifty billion dollars to develop innovation and technology.
questions.explanation: The tax cut raises aggregate demand and innovation investment raises long-run productive capacity, matching Diagram C.

visuals.caption: Government policies
rows: Reduce the profits tax rate for corporations with profit less than two million dollars.
Inject fifty billion dollars to develop innovation and technology.

visuals.alt: Four AD-AS diagram options A to D.
visuals.caption: Effects of the two policies

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following AD-AS diagrams could most likely show the effect on aggregate output caused by the above two policies?

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: Which of the following results can be a negative number?
questions.explanation: Gross investment exceeds net investment by depreciation, total exports include re-exports and M3 includes M2. Employment can be lower than unemployment in an economy.

questions.keyPoint: Surplus budget, deficit budget and balanced budget
questions.stem: Suppose an inflationary (output) gap and a fiscal surplus exist in an economy. Which of the following measures would help narrow the inflationary (output) gap and attain a balanced fiscal condition at the same time?

choices.text: adopting a universal retirement protection scheme for all elderly aged 65 or above

questions.explanation: Raising income tax lowers aggregate demand and increases tax revenue, narrowing the output gap while reducing the fiscal surplus.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem: Study the following table.

choices.text: Policy I and Policy III only

questions.explanation: Policy II combines an open-market purchase and higher tax allowance, both expansionary. The other bundles contain offsetting measures.

visuals.caption: Policy bundles
rows:
an open market purchase of government bonds
a rise in the discount rate

an open market purchase of government bonds
a rise in the salaries tax allowance

a rise in the salaries tax allowance
a rise in the discount rate

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the policies in the above table is/are expansionary?

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: The following table shows the amount of goods that can be produced with 1 unit of resources in Country A and Country B respectively.

choices.text: 1 unit of Good X = 1.3 units of Good Y
1 unit of Good X = 1.7 units of Good Y
1 unit of Good X = 1.8 units of Good Y
1 unit of Good X = 2.0 units of Good Y

questions.explanation: Country A's opportunity cost of X is 1.5Y; Country B's is 2Y. Including the 0.2Y transport cost, 1.8Y lies inside both countries' beneficial range.

visuals.caption: Output with one unit of resources

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the transportation cost for 1 unit of Good X is 0.2 units of Good Y and it is borne by the exporting country. Which of the following is a mutually beneficial terms of trade between Country A and Country B?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of a quota on domestic price, domestic consumption, domestic production and import quantity for a small open economy
questions.stem: The following is the supply-demand diagram of Good X in a small open economy. Initially the economy imports Good X at the world price (Pw) and the government imposes an import quota of (Q2 - Q1) units. Suppose the world price of Good X drops. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: The domestic price of Good X will remain at Pw.
The domestic price of Good X will fall.
The domestic supply curve will shift to the right.
The quantity of domestically produced Good X will increase.

questions.explanation: With a binding quota the domestic price is determined by domestic demand and supply at the fixed import quantity, so a fall in world price does not change it.

visuals.alt: Small open economy supply-demand diagram with world price Pw and fixed import quota Q2-Q1.
visuals.caption: Import quota

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem:
A Hong Kong billionaire travelled to Russia to watch matches in the World Cup. Which of the following would be included in the calculation of Hong Kong's balance of payments?

(1) He bought a travel insurance for his Russia trip from a Hong Kong agency.
(2) He bought a jersey of the Russia national team in Moscow as a souvenir.
(3) He invested in a Russian football club and became the major owner.
questions.explanation: The overseas jersey is an import of goods and buying the foreign club is a financial outflow. Buying insurance from a Hong Kong agency is a domestic transaction.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: Study the prices of iPhone X in Hong Kong in terms of Hong Kong dollar (HKD) and in the Mainland in terms of Renminbi (RMB).

choices.text: Travellers tend to buy an iPhone X in the Mainland instead of in Hong Kong.
RMB is under-valued as the price of an iPhone X in the Mainland is lower than that in Hong Kong.
If the transportation cost is HKD 950, buying an iPhone X in Hong Kong and re-selling it in the Mainland will no longer gain.
The potential gain from 'buy low, sell high' will disappear when the price of iPhone X in Hong Kong is higher than HKD 9 504.

questions.explanation: The Mainland price is RMB 8 316 / 0.875 = HKD 9 504. Buying in Hong Kong yields a HKD 916 gross gain, so a HKD 950 transport cost eliminates it.
questions.postVisualStem: Given the exchange rate of HKD 1 = RMB 0.875, which of the following statements is correct?

questions.chapterTitle: 三個基本經濟問題與私有產權
questions.keyPoint: 私有產權的意思和在市場經濟中的重要性
questions.stem:
參考以下解決房屋問題的建議：

政府應該興建一種新類型的房屋「居住易」，其業主能以一受管制的租金出租其單位。若業主想出售其物業，他們只能將單位售回政府。

與擁有一個私人樓宇單位相比，擁有一個「居住易」單位的業主的 ______ 會被削弱了。

(1) 使用權
(2) 獲取收入權
(3) 轉讓權
questions.explanation: 受管制租金限制獲取收入權，而只能售回政府限制轉讓權；業主仍然有使用權。

questions.chapterTitle: 三個基本經濟問題與私有產權
questions.keyPoint: 三個基本經濟問題的意思及相關例子
questions.stem:
下列哪些陳述與「為誰生產」的問題有關？

(1) 只有長者和合資格的傷殘人士才可以享有「公共交通票價優惠計劃」的每程 $2 票價優惠。
(2) 若公共租住房屋（公屋）的住戶其家庭入息超過公屋入息限額五倍，便須遷出其公屋單位。
(3) 電競音樂節由香港會議展覽中心轉移到香港體育館舉行，以容納更多來自世界各地的電競迷。
questions.explanation: 首兩項決定誰可獲得受資助的交通和房屋；場地轉換關於生產多少。

questions.explanation: 相關成本是 $5 000 維修費加上放棄的 $2 000 轉售價值，即 $7 000；原先的買入價是沉沒成本。

questions.stem:
在 2018-19 年度財政預算案，香港政府將持續進修基金的資助上限由每位申請人 $10 000 提高至 $20 000，以鼓勵市民繼續進修。

questions.keyPoint: 比較不同所有權形式的特徵及利弊
questions.stem:
新世界中國地產有限公司（股票編號：0917）宣布把公司私有化，並取消其在香港交易所的上市地位。

下列哪些是上述改變的可能好處？

(1) 該公司可以選擇不向公眾披露其財務帳目。
(2) 該公司可以減低被收購的風險。
(3) 該公司可享有較低的利得稅率。
questions.explanation: 私有公司可以減少公開披露要求，亦較少面對被收購的風險；取消上市不會改變利得稅率。

(4) 可供顧客免費借閱的漫畫書

(2) 進入市場並沒有限制。
(3) 廠商利潤極大化的條件為價格等於邊際成本。

由 2017-18 學年起，香港政府向修讀本地私立教育機構所開辦的全日制自資學士學位課程的學生提供每年 $30 000 的資助。

下列哪些是這資助計劃的可能影響？

(1) 失業率會下降，因為勞動人口會增加。
(2) 該計劃有助於機會均等化，因為來自低收入住戶的學生有更大機會接受高等教育。
(3) 全民就業產出水平將來會上升，因為人們接受較佳的教育和培訓後平均生產力會上升。
questions.explanation: 資助可令低收入家庭較容易取得高等教育，並提高日後生產力及全民就業產出；全日制進修不會即時增加勞動人口。

questions.keyPoint: 貨幣的功能
questions.stem:
參考以下的假設個案：

自 2018 年初美國公佈一系列針對 T 國的貿易制裁措施後，T 國的貨幣「T 元」貶值了 40%。結果，T 國的一些店舖以美元而非 T 元訂價。黑市的店舖拒絕接受 T 元。一些市民購買外幣以保障他們的資產。

T 元的哪些貨幣功能被削弱了？

(1) 交易媒介
(2) 記帳單位
(3) 價值儲藏
questions.explanation: 店舖拒收 T 元削弱其交易媒介功能；以美元訂價削弱記帳單位功能；市民轉持外幣則削弱其價值儲藏功能。

questions.keyPoint: 資產轉移對貨幣供應的影響
questions.stem:
當一名香港市民把 $500 000 由他在某有限制牌照銀行的定期存款戶口轉至在某持牌銀行的儲蓄戶口，

(1) 貨幣供應定義一會上升。
(2) 貨幣供應定義二會上升。
(3) 貨幣供應定義三會上升。
questions.explanation: 持牌銀行的儲蓄存款計入 M2；有限制牌照銀行的定期存款只計入 M3。因此 M2 上升，而 M3 不變。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 名義利率及實質利率的關係
questions.keyPoint: 了解方程式：名義利率 = 實質利率 + 預期通脹率
questions.stem:
在通脹的時期，假設某債券的名義利率高於預期通脹率。若實際通脹率高於預期通脹率，

(1) 實際通脹率會高於該債券的名義利率。
(2) 該債券的預期實質回報率會高於實際實質回報率。
(3) 該債券的實際實質回報率可能是負數。
(4) 持有現金的實質回報率會大於零。
questions.explanation: 高於預期的通脹令實際實質回報低於預期實質回報，亦可能令它變成負數；通脹下持有現金的實質回報是負數。

questions.keyPoint: 徵稅的影響
questions.stem: 某年的工資率和一般物價水平均上升 8%。若政府增加薪俸稅免稅額 5%，

choices.text: 收入分佈會變得更平均。
人們的稅後實質收入會增加。

questions.explanation: 工資和物價以相同幅度上升，而增加免稅額會減少應繳稅款，故稅後實質收入上升。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹與貨幣數量論
questions.keyPoint: 貨幣數量論的意思
questions.stem:
下列哪些有關貨幣數量理論的陳述是正確的？

(1) 若某經濟的貨幣供應相對於物品供應增長得太快，通脹便會出現。
(2) 若貨幣供應增加，名義產出便會以相同的百分率增加。
(3) 若通脹率是固定的，實質產出和貨幣供應會以相同的百分率增長。
questions.explanation: 在貨幣流通速度不變下，貨幣供應相對物品供應增長過快會帶來通脹，貨幣供應改變會使名義產出同百分率改變；固定通脹率本身不能決定實質產出增長率。

questions.keyPoint: 四個基本的徵稅原則

choices.text: 低收入組別以其應課稅收入中較小的百分比支付該稅款。
它違反了亞當史密夫所提出的公平賦稅原則。

questions.explanation: 固定稅款是累退稅，低收入人士繳付的收入比例較高，違反公平賦稅原則。

questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹和通貨緊縮的影響
questions.keyPoint: 解釋為何出現非預期通貨膨脹（緊縮）時，債務人會得益（受損），而債權人會受損（得益）
questions.stem:
在非預期通縮下，下列哪（幾）位人士會有所損失？

(2) 盧先生持有銀色債券收取利息，債券的回報率和通脹掛鈎，最低回報為 3%。

questions.topicGroup: 經常帳（主要組成部分：貨物、服務、收益及經常轉移）
questions.keyPoint: 一宗交易會否及如何影響經常帳
questions.stem:
一名本港億萬富翁到俄羅斯旅遊，欣賞世界盃賽事。下列哪些會包括在本港國際收支平衡的計算之內？

(1) 他向一家本港代理為他的俄國之旅購買旅遊保險。
(2) 他在莫斯科購買一件俄羅斯國家隊球衣做紀念品。
(3) 他投資於俄羅斯一家球會，成為大股東。
questions.explanation: 在莫斯科購買球衣是貨物進口，投資俄羅斯球會是金融流出；向本港代理購買保險是本地交易。

questions.stem: 細閱 iPhone X 在香港的價格（以港元計算）與在內地的價格（以人民幣計算）。

choices.text: 遊客傾向於在內地而非在香港購買 iPhone X。

若運費是 950 港元，在香港購買一部 iPhone X 並在內地轉售便再不能獲利。
當本港 iPhone X 的價格高於 9 504 港元，「低買高賣」的潛在利益便會消失。

questions.explanation: 內地價格為 8 316 / 0.875 = 9 504 港元；香港購入後轉售的毛利為 916 港元，因此運費為 950 港元時不能獲利。

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about a planned economy is correct?

choices.text: The quantity of public goods in the economy is greater than that in a market-oriented economy.
Most production activities are carried out by government officials.
All resources are allocated by government commands.
Competitions still exist in the economy.

questions.explanation: A planned economy can still contain competition. Its defining feature is that the government directs most resource allocation, not necessarily all of it.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: The Chief Executive proposed to raise the recurrent education spending by $5 billion. One of her proposals was to provide a $30 000 subsidy to eligible secondary school graduates studying self-financing programmes. The above proposal is related to the ______ question(s) in Economics.

choices.text: 'what to produce' and 'for whom to produce'

questions.explanation: The government chooses to provide education subsidies and determines which eligible graduates receive them, relating to what and for whom to produce.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
John, a Secondary 6 graduate, is considering studying a programme either in Hong Kong or the Mainland. Which of the following situations would lower his opportunity cost of studying the programme in Hong Kong?

(1) His tuition fee of the first year will be waived if he studies the programme in Hong Kong.
(2) The graduates of the Mainland programme have better job prospects.
(3) The qualification of the Mainland programme may not be recognised in Hong Kong.
questions.explanation: A waived Hong Kong tuition fee lowers its cost, and a less-recognised Mainland qualification makes the next-best Mainland option less valuable. Better Mainland job prospects do the opposite.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
The following statements are adapted from the 2017-18 Budget Speech by the Financial Secretary of Hong Kong.

Statement (1): The global economy in 2016 recorded the slowest growth since the global financial crisis.

Statement (2): For 2016 as a whole, there was a growth of 1.9%, consistent with the 1% to 2% economic growth as forecast in last year's Budget.

Statement (3): While recognising the effect of market forces, the Government should play an active role as a facilitator by taking forward appropriate policies with good use of public resources.

Which of the above is a normative statement / are normative statements?
questions.explanation: Statements (1) and (2) can be checked against data. Statement (3) contains a value judgement about what the Government should do.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the exhibits in the Louvre Museum is correct?

choices.text: They are public goods because the Louvre Museum is open to the public.
They are capital because they are man-made resources used in production.
They are consumer goods because more of them are preferred.
They are economic goods because they satisfy human wants.

questions.explanation: Museum exhibits are man-made resources used in the production of museum services, so they are capital goods.

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem:
A professor has decided to change the way of marking the exam papers of his subject. Instead of asking his teaching assistants to mark the whole paper for their own classes, he assigns each teaching assistant to mark one question of the paper for the entire candidature. Which of the following situations would likely occur?

(1) The marking will be more accurate since practice makes perfect.
(2) Training time will be reduced as each assistant only needs to know part of the marking schemes.
(3) The tools required for marking will be reduced such as fewer red pens are needed.
questions.explanation: Division of labour brings learning by doing and reduces training needs. It does not reduce the total marking tools required.

questions.explanation: Economies of scale can give large firms a cost advantage which is a barrier to entry and source of monopoly power.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)

questions.stem:
The government imposes a per unit tax on a good. The price of the good will remain unchanged if

(1) the demand is perfectly elastic.
(2) the demand is perfectly inelastic.
(3) the supply is perfectly elastic.
(4) the supply is perfectly inelastic.
questions.explanation: With perfectly elastic demand, producers bear the tax and buyer price is unchanged. With perfectly inelastic supply, sellers absorb the tax and the market price is unchanged.

a rise in the income limit of applying for public housing
a relaxation of rules regulating the change of land use

questions.explanation: Raising the income limit makes more households eligible for public housing and increases long-run demand, lengthening the waiting time.

As a result, more people bought Sausage McMuffin with Egg during the promotion period. Which of the following statements about this situation is correct?

choices.text: McDonald's was not maximising profit during the promotion period.

The total expenditure of consumers on Sausage McMuffin with Egg would increase if the demand was elastic.

The total revenue received by taxi drivers will increase.
The fixed cost of operating taxi service will increase.

questions.explanation: The fixed starting fare rises while the per-distance charge is unchanged. Short trips become relatively more expensive, so the ratio of short to long trips decreases.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: The following table shows the number of new Tesla electric vehicle registered in Hong Kong. The Government announced in mid-February 2017 that the full exemption from first registration tax on electric vehicles would end on March 31, 2017.

choices.text: The supply of electric vehicles increased because new technology reduced the production cost of battery used in electric vehicles.
The supply of electric vehicles increased because of the exemption of first registration tax by the Government.
The demand for electric vehicles increased because the Government built more charging stations in the city.
The demand for electric vehicles increased because the buyers expected the cost of buying electric vehicles to go up in the future.

questions.explanation: An expected future rise in the cost of buying electric vehicles leads buyers to bring purchases forward, increasing current demand.

visuals.caption: New Tesla electric vehicles registered in Hong Kong
columns: Number of new Tesla electric vehicle registered in Hong Kong

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following best explains the above data?

questions.keyPoint: Identify the type of market structure
questions.stem:
Sony's PS4 was responsible for $17.8 billion of sales value, or 51% share of the global console hardware market, compared with Microsoft's Xbox One at $9.1 billion of sales value or a 26% market share. Nintendo's 3DS platform (and its variants, such as the 2DS) was a distant third on the list with $2.6 billion of sales value or 8% share of the market.

The market structure of the above global console hardware market is oligopoly. This statement is

choices.text: correct because the companies sell heterogeneous goods in the market.
correct because there are a few dominating companies in the market.
incorrect because the PS4 was only responsible for 51% of the market.
incorrect because there are a lot of sellers in the global market.

questions.explanation: An oligopoly is a market dominated by a few firms. The data show that Sony, Microsoft and Nintendo have major shares.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of deadweight loss
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the demand and supply curves of Good X.

choices.text: The deadweight loss will increase by area bcgh.
The deadweight loss will decrease by area abh.
The new deadweight loss is area bcf.
The new deadweight loss is area aci.

questions.explanation: Increasing the tax reduces output further. The added deadweight loss is the area bcgh.

questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: Recently, unmanned aircraft systems have become very popular but using those aircrafts in urban areas has caused noise and safety concerns. The Civil Aviation Department is considering regulating the manufacture, import and sale of unmanned aircraft systems.
questions.explanation: Noise and safety concerns are external costs, so private and social costs diverge. Government regulation is the proposed solution.

questions.topicGroup: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP

Which of the following are included in the calculation of the gross domestic product of Hong Kong?

(1) the estimated rental value of an owner-occupied property in Hong Kong
(2) the commission received by a real estate agent from selling second-hand property
(3) the scholarship received by a university student
questions.explanation: Imputed rent of owner-occupied housing and the service commission are current production. A scholarship is a transfer payment and is excluded.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: The following table shows the gross domestic product (GDP) data of an economy in a particular year.
questions.explanation: Positive net factor income from abroad means GNI exceeds GDP. Indirect taxes exceed subsidies, so GDP at market price exceeds factor cost. Positive capital consumption allowance means depreciation is positive.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the economy are correct?

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.stem: The short run aggregate supply curve will shift to the right if

choices.text: the government relaxes the immigration quota of foreign workers.
the government increases the profits tax rate.
the central bank sells government bonds to the public.
there is an increase in the price level.

questions.explanation: Relaxing the quota increases available labour and productive capacity, shifting SRAS right.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS

questions.stem: Which of the following will lead to an increase in both price level and aggregate output in the short run?

choices.text: There is an improvement in production technology.
There is an increase in the oil price.
There is a decrease in money supply.
There is a decrease in the desire to save.

questions.explanation: A reduced desire to save raises consumption and aggregate demand, increasing both output and the price level in the short run.

choices.text: The central bank issues larger denomination banknotes for circulation.
The risk of investing in stock market decreases.
Security problems have been found in the major electronic payment system.

questions.explanation: The money demand curve shifts left. A lower risk of stock investment makes financial assets more attractive than money and reduces money demand.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem: Which of the following will lead to a reduction in monetary base?

choices.text: The central bank increases the required reserve ratio.
The central bank purchases government bonds from the public.
The central bank raises the discount rate.
The commercial banks hold more excess reserves.

questions.explanation: A higher discount rate discourages commercial banks from borrowing from the central bank and can reduce the monetary base.

questions.topicGroup: Licensed banks, restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies in
questions.keyPoint: Features of the three types of deposit-taking institutions
questions.stem: Brian wants to deposit $80 000 for two months in an authorised institution in Hong Kong in the form of a negotiable certificate of deposit. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: As the term of maturity is longer than one month, a deposit-taking company can accept his deposit.
As the term of maturity is shorter than three months, a restricted licence bank can accept his deposit.
As the amount of deposit is less than $500 000, a restricted licence bank cannot accept his deposit.
As negotiable certificates of deposit are not available in a licensed bank, a licensed bank cannot accept his deposit.

questions.explanation: A restricted licence bank must take deposits of at least $500 000, so it cannot accept this $80 000 deposit.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about an economy.

the monetary base of the economy will be $16 600.
the maximum possible amount of loans will be $23 000.
the maximum banking multiplier will be 4.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority?
questions.explanation: The HKMA supervises banks, manages the Exchange Fund and authorises note issue. It does not stabilise mortgage rates.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Nominal interest rate as the (opportunity) cost of holding money
questions.stem: Assume that the real interest rate is 6% and the expected inflation rate is 3%. If the actual inflation rate is 5%, the cost of holding money will be ______.
questions.explanation: The cost of holding money is the nominal interest rate. Nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation = 6% + 3% = 9%.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: Suppose the salaries tax system in Hong Kong has the following changes.

choices.text: Fewer people will fall into the tax net.
Fewer people will have to pay at the standard tax rate.

questions.explanation: The progressive brackets are widened while the standard rate stays at 15%. Fewer taxpayers will reach the standard rate.
questions.postVisualStem: If the basic tax allowance remains unchanged, which of the following is most likely to be a result of the above changes in the tax system?

questions.keyPoint: Surplus budget, deficit budget and balanced budget
questions.stem: Suppose a deflationary (output) gap and a fiscal deficit exist in a country. Which of the following would narrow the deflationary (output) gap and reduce the fiscal deficit at the same time?

choices.text: increasing the tax rebate on salaries tax
allowing more tourists to travel to the country visa-free

questions.explanation: Visa-free entry increases tourism exports and tax revenue, raising aggregate demand while reducing the fiscal deficit.

choices.text: The growth rate of real output is increasing.

The growth rate of nominal income is constant.

questions.explanation: The money-supply growth rate rises while price-level growth is constant. Under the quantity theory, real-output growth is therefore increasing.
