questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the subsidy
questions.stem:
The government provides a per-unit subsidy of $10 on producing green products. The market price drops by $6 as a result. Which of the following statements about the green product market is/are correct?

(1) The supply of green products is more elastic than their demand.
(2) Consumers enjoy more subsidy benefit than producers.
(3) The demand for green products increases.
questions.explanation: Consumers receive $6 of the $10 subsidy while producers receive $4, so demand is less elastic than supply. The subsidy changes quantity demanded, not the demand curve.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem: Many people queued up for days for the tickets to watch the show of Tsz-Wah, a famous artist performing stand-up comedy. Some people complained that they were unable to buy tickets even though they were willing to pay the ticket price set by the organiser. The above situation implies that

choices.text: price was the only criterion for allocating the tickets.
the producer was not maximising its profit.
a black market for the tickets will emerge.
there was an effective price ceiling in the ticket market.

questions.explanation: A shortage at the organiser's ticket price creates an incentive for resale at a higher price in a black market.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings of complements, substitutes, normal and inferior goods
questions.stem: Holding other factors constant, a rise in the price of Good X will lead to a fall in the total revenue of Good Y if

choices.text: Good X and Good Y are complements.
Good X and Good Y are substitutes.
Good X and Good Y are in joint supply.
Good X and Good Y are in competitive supply.

questions.explanation: A higher price of a complement lowers demand for Good Y, reducing its equilibrium price and quantity and hence its total revenue.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: SS is the supply curve for smartphones. Which of the following reasons can best explain the change of the equilibrium position in the smartphone market from A to B?

choices.text: The retailers offer more free gifts for buying smartphones.
The cost of computer production functions is reduced.
There are more smartphone producers in the market.
The major network service providers increase the service charge at the same time.

questions.explanation: More free gifts lower the full price paid by buyers, shifting demand right and moving equilibrium up along the unchanged supply curve.

visuals.alt: Smartphone supply curve with equilibrium moving from A to B along it.
visuals.caption: Smartphone market

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following table for the supply and demand schedules for a good. The government imposes a $2 per unit tax on the good. Which of the following statements about the good is correct?

choices.text: Sellers' revenue net of tax is $70.
The above information is insufficient to determine the tax burden on sellers.

questions.explanation: Supply is perfectly inelastic at 14 units. The quantity remains 14 and tax revenue is $2 x 14 = $28.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of the divergence between private and social benefits?

choices.text: A security guard watches live concerts when he is working in a concert hall.
A tourist enjoys the music performed by a singer on the street and he does not pay for that.
A resident living next to a karaoke lounge cannot fall asleep because of the noise.
After the removal of the airport, the market value of the residential flats in that region increases.

questions.explanation: The street performance provides an external benefit to the tourist, who receives enjoyment without paying the singer.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which of the following is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

choices.text: More high-quality Japanese grapes are imported to Hong Kong during Mid-Autumn Festival.
An increase of the per unit tax on beer results in a fall in the quantity of small-bottle beer sold in the market.
After the introduction of the airport departure tax which is a fixed amount for any traveller, the average length of airplane journeys decreases.
The birth rate increases when the income tax allowance for children increases.

questions.explanation: A fixed departure tax raises the full price of short journeys proportionately more, so it should increase rather than decrease the average journey length.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram. If the government lowers the price ceiling from Pa to Pb,
questions.explanation: A lower binding ceiling reduces the quantity supplied and the price received by sellers, so producer surplus decreases.

visuals.alt: Supply-demand diagram with price ceilings Pa and Pb.
visuals.caption: Price ceiling

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the theme park industry in Hong Kong is correct?

choices.text: Hong Kong Disneyland is a monopolist because its average cost of production drops when there are more tourists.
Hong Kong Disneyland guarantees a profit because it is protected by the government.
Hong Kong Disneyland and Ocean Park Hong Kong have no competition with each other as tourists may go to both theme parks.
Hong Kong Disneyland and Ocean Park Hong Kong are interdependent in their marketing strategies.

questions.explanation: The two large theme parks are rivals in an oligopolistic market, so each firm's marketing decisions affect the other.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem: Suppose the post-tax Gini coefficient of an economy is larger than its pre-tax Gini coefficient. This implies that

choices.text: the government has increased the amount of transfer payment to the poor.
the tax system of the economy is likely to be regressive.
the problem of income inequality is worse than that in the previous year.
the government should reform the tax system.

questions.explanation: A tax system that raises the Gini coefficient makes after-tax income more unequal, which is characteristic of a regressive tax system.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: Illustrate total social surplus with a diagram
questions.keyPoint: Adding up consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram. The maximum total social surplus is equal to ________.
questions.explanation: Total social surplus is consumer surplus plus producer surplus. These are Z and X+Y respectively.

visuals.alt: Demand and vertical supply diagram with regions W, X, Y and Z.
visuals.caption: Total social surplus

questions.keyPoint: Recognise the contribution of each type of production to the economy
questions.stem: The following table shows the employment distribution in an economy.

choices.text: the number of workers engaged in the primary sector remained constant.
the overall employment rate was the same.
the contribution of the tertiary sector to gross domestic product (GDP) increased.
the relative importance of the secondary sector in terms of employment decreased.

questions.explanation: The secondary sector's employment share fell from 23.6% to 18.5%, showing a fall in its relative importance in employment.
questions.postVisualStem: From the above table, we can conclude that from 2010 to 2014,

questions.topicGroup: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.keyPoint: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.stem: Which of the following would be included in the calculation of Hong Kong's GDP for 2014?

choices.text: the old age allowance paid by the government in 2014
the market value of a flat built in 2013 but sold in 2014
the salary of a salesperson working in a shop selling second-hand handbags in 2014
the rental income from a property in Canada owned by a Hong Kong resident producing unit in 2014

questions.explanation: The salesperson provides a current production service in Hong Kong. Transfer payments, the resale of an old flat and overseas production are excluded from Hong Kong GDP.

questions.keyPoint: Growth rate of GDP
questions.stem: Refer to the following table about an economy. Which of the following statements about the economy is correct?

choices.text: The per capita nominal GDP in year 2 is the same as that in year 1.
The real output increased in year 2.
The general price level decreased in year 2.
The per capita real GDP decreased in year 2.

questions.explanation: In year 2 nominal GDP is unchanged while the price level and population rise. Real GDP therefore falls, and per-capita real GDP falls further.

visuals.caption: Growth rate relative to previous year (%)

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: Which of the following will result in a rightward shift of the aggregate demand curve of a country?

choices.text: The central bank reduces the discount rate.
The minimum wage rate is increased.
Its trading partners suffer from an economic recession.

questions.explanation: A lower discount rate is expansionary monetary policy. It raises money supply and investment, shifting aggregate demand right.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: The government provides cash subsidies for new-born children from their birth to age 10. Which of the following diagrams best illustrates the effect of the subsidies on the economy after twenty years?
questions.explanation: The subsidies raise current aggregate demand and, after twenty years, the larger cohort raises labour supply and LRAS. Diagram D shows both AD and LRAS shifting right.

visuals.alt: Four AD-AS diagrams labelled A to D for child subsidies after twenty years.
visuals.caption: Long-run effect of child subsidies

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram. The curve of asset demand for money will shift from Ma1 to Ma2 when

choices.text: the risk of investing in the stock market increases.
the government reduces the income tax rate.

questions.explanation: A higher risk of holding stocks makes money relatively more attractive as an asset, shifting asset demand for money right.

visuals.alt: Asset-demand-for-money curve shifting right from Ma1 to Ma2.
visuals.caption: Asset demand for money

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Study the following balance sheet of a banking system. The required reserve ratio is 20%. If the central bank issues newly printed banknotes worth $200 million, the cash held by the non-bank public will increase by $100 million and the money supply will increase by $500 million. The total amount of excess reserves in the banking system will then be ________.
questions.explanation: The new deposits are $1 400 million, requiring $280 million reserves. Bank reserves become $400 million, leaving $120 million excess reserves.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem: Which of the following transactions would increase the money supply (M2) of Hong Kong?

choices.text: Ms Chan transfers $500 000 from her time deposit account in a restricted licence bank to her time deposit account in a licensed bank.
Mr Lee transfers $200 000 from his current account to his savings account in a licensed bank.
Mr Man deposits $100 000 cash into his savings account in a licensed bank.
Ms Chung deposits $600 000 cash into her time deposit account in a deposit-taking company.

questions.explanation: Time deposits in licensed banks count in M2, while a restricted licence bank's deposits do not. The transfer therefore raises M2.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate
questions.stem: If the nominal interest rate is 5% and the expected inflation rate is 3%, the cost of holding money is ________, the nominal return of holding money is ________ and the expected real interest rate is ________.
questions.explanation: The nominal interest rate is the opportunity cost of holding money; money's nominal return is zero; and the expected real interest rate is 5% - 3% = 2%.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem: The monetary base increases when

choices.text: the commercial banks hold less excess reserves.
the commercial banks buy government bonds from the public.
the central bank buys government bonds from the public.
the central bank increases the discount rate.

questions.explanation: When the central bank buys bonds, it pays with newly created base money and increases the monetary base.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: The quantity theory of money implies that

choices.text: an increase in money supply will lead to a rise in price level when real output is falling.
the economy is always at the full employment output level.
an increase in money supply will lead to a decrease in the velocity of circulation of money when real output is kept constant.
an increase in money supply will lead to a same-proportional increase in real output.

questions.explanation: With velocity given, more money increases nominal spending. If real output falls, the price level must rise by even more to accommodate it.

questions.keyPoint: Taxation in
questions.stem:
Which of the following are indirect taxes in Hong Kong?

(1) property tax
(2) rates on property
(3) stamp duty on transfer of stock
(4) general sales tax
questions.explanation: Rates on property and stamp duty are indirect taxes. Property tax is direct and Hong Kong does not levy a general sales tax.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem: Refer to the following news extract. Yu'e Bao is a better ________ as compared with bank deposits because ________.

choices.text: unit of account ...... it provides a homogeneous means of payment
unit of account ...... it can facilitate people's buying and selling of goods and services
store of value ...... it allows customers to have higher purchasing power in the future
store of value ...... the customers can keep their unused funds in Yu'e Bao

questions.explanation: Its higher return helps funds preserve and increase purchasing power, which is the store-of-value function of money.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: When unanticipated deflation occurs, which of the following people will lose?

choices.text: people paying a fixed amount of rental payment
people receiving interest from their savings deposits
people repaying a mortgage loan at a floating interest rate
people working under a fixed nominal wage contract

questions.explanation: Deflation increases the real burden of a fixed nominal payment, so a tenant paying fixed rent loses.

questions.topicGroup: Reasons for a vertical long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve
questions.keyPoint: Reasons for a vertical long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve
questions.stem:
Refer to the following aggregate supply diagram. When the economy moves from point A to point B, which of the following will NOT change?

(1) real output
(2) nominal output
(3) potential output
questions.explanation: Moving vertically along LRAS changes only the price level. Real output and potential output remain unchanged, while nominal output rises.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Initially an economy operates at the long-run equilibrium. Which of the following will lead to a deflationary (output) gap in the economy?

choices.text: The government increases the salaries tax rate.
The government reduces the profits tax rate.
The government invests in the construction of a cross-border express rail link.
The central bank reduces the required reserve ratio.

questions.explanation: A higher salaries tax reduces disposable income and aggregate demand, moving output below potential output.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: In an economy with severe inflation and income inequality, the government can lower the price level and reduce the income gap by

choices.text: increasing the environmental tax on handling household sewage.
increasing the salaries tax and its progressivity.
reducing its spending on social welfare.
reducing the personal allowance of the salaries tax.

questions.explanation: A more progressive and higher salaries tax reduces aggregate demand and redistributes disposable income, lowering inflation and inequality.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: Assume the labour input requirements for the production of computers and toys in Japan and Hong Kong are as follows. Suppose there is no transportation cost. Which of the following can be the terms of trade so that trade is mutually beneficial to Japan and Hong Kong?

choices.text: 1 unit of computers exchanges for 0.4 units of toys
1 unit of computers exchanges for 0.5 units of toys
1 unit of computers exchanges for 1 unit of toys
1 unit of computers exchanges for 2.5 units of toys

questions.explanation: Japan's opportunity cost of a computer is one third of a toy and Hong Kong's is one half. A rate of 0.4 toy lies between them.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning of absolute advantage
questions.stem: A country has an absolute advantage in producing good X. Which of the following statements about the country is correct?

choices.text: The country can produce a greater amount of good X than another good with the same amount of resources.
The country has a comparative advantage in producing good X.
The country has an absolute disadvantage in producing another good.
The country may import good X from the international market.

questions.explanation: Absolute advantage alone does not determine comparative advantage or trade direction. The country may still import good X.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.keyPoint: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.stem: Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: The money supply (M1) of Hong Kong has to be fully backed up by the US dollar.
The market exchange rate of the HK dollar to the US dollar is fixed at 1 USD to 7.8 HKD by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.
Hong Kong's import volume will increase when the US dollar appreciates against other currencies.
A current account deficit in the US will lead to a current account deficit in Hong Kong.

questions.explanation: When the US dollar appreciates, the linked Hong Kong dollar appreciates too. Imports become cheaper in Hong Kong-dollar terms, tending to increase import volume.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem:
A lecturer from the US has been working in Hong Kong for 10 years. Which of the following would be included in the calculation of Hong Kong's current account balance?

(1) the money he gives to his wife in Hong Kong
(2) the money he uses to buy shares listed in the US stock market
(3) the money he donates to a charity organization in Africa
(4) the money he spends on visiting his parents in the US
questions.explanation: A donation to a foreign charity is a current transfer outflow and spending on travel in the US is an import of services. Share purchases are financial-account transactions.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Balance of payments and balance of the BOP account
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of balance of payment surplus and deficit
questions.stem: The following table shows some information about the balance of payments of Country A.
questions.explanation: The current account is -1 200 + 700 + 200 - 100 = -400. Positive net factor income means GNP exceeds GDP, and reserve assets rising by $180 million indicate a BOP surplus of $180 million.

visuals.caption: Balance of payments of Country A

questions.postVisualStem:
According to the above data, which of the following statements are correct?

(1) The current account deficit is $400 million.
(2) Country A's GDP is smaller than its gross national product.
(3) The balance of payments surplus is $180 million.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison between tariff and quota
questions.stem: The supply curve of a certain good is upward-sloping in a small open economy. What is the main difference between imposing an effective import quota and a tariff on the good?

choices.text: Imposing an effective import quota will lower the volume of import while imposing a tariff will not.
Imposing an effective import quota will result in a rise in consumer surplus of the good while imposing a tariff may not.
Imposing a tariff will raise the world price of the good while imposing an effective import quota will not.
Imposing a tariff will result in an increase in the government revenue while imposing an effective import quota may not.

questions.explanation: A tariff raises government revenue. Quota rents may instead go to importers or foreign exporters, so an effective quota may not raise government revenue.

questions.topicGroup: 區分實證性陳述和規範性陳述
questions.keyPoint: 區分實證性陳述和規範性陳述
questions.stem:
下列哪些是實證性陳述？

(1) 從內地輸入勞工會增加本港的職位空缺。
(2) 從廣東省輸入勞工會較佳，因為他們能操粵語。
(3) 來自中國的勞工的生產力比來自其他東南亞國家的勞工高。
(4) 從內地輸入 30 000 名勞工會令本港的失業率上升 1%。
questions.explanation: (1)、(3)和(4)均可由數據驗證；(2)含有「較佳」的價值判斷。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 大衛可選擇乘搭港鐵列車或巴士往元朗。假設上述兩種選擇所需的交通時間和車費在正常情況下均相同。下列哪項會引致乘搭港鐵列車往元朗的機會成本上升？

choices.text: 巴士的空調設備發生故障。
交通阻塞令巴士車程延長了 15 分鐘。
訊號問題令港鐵列車車程增加了 15 分鐘。
大衛對港鐵列車車廂內的新聞廣播感到煩擾。

questions.explanation: 港鐵本身所需的時間增加，令選擇港鐵的成本上升。

questions.chapterTitle: 三個基本經濟問題與私有產權
questions.keyPoint: 不同社會解決基本經濟問題的方法
questions.stem: 下列哪項是市場經濟的一個特點？

choices.text: 該經濟的收入分配不平均。
政府在調控該經濟內的商業活動中沒有角色。
該經濟的生產要素大多是私人擁有的。
該經濟內只有價格競爭。

questions.explanation: 生產要素大多由私人擁有是市場經濟的特徵。

questions.keyPoint: 勞力的流動性

choices.text: 政府在所有火車站推行「城市單車租賃計劃」……地域
數家大公司在其辦公室設立幼兒託管中心……地域
政府所提供的交通津貼因財政赤字而減少……職業
政府在更多的行業規定從業員須具備執業牌照……職業

questions.explanation: 更多職業須具備牌照會提高入行門檻，降低職業流動性。

questions.topicGroup: 廠商的基本目標：利潤極大化
questions.keyPoint: 競爭性廠商如何選擇利潤極大化產出水平
questions.stem: 下表顯示在完全競爭市場內某廠商的邊際成本。
questions.explanation: 邊際成本下降令利潤極大化產量上升；固定成本上升和邊際成本下降對利潤有相反影響。
questions.postVisualStem: 假設租用機器的租金（屬固定成本）上升了 $2，而每單位產出的邊際成本減少了 $0.5。該廠商利潤極大化的產量因此 ________，而利潤 ________。

questions.keyPoint: 勞工生產力
questions.stem: 細閱下表。下列哪項是工廠甲和工廠乙在勞工生產力上有差異的一個可能原因？

choices.text: 工廠甲以時薪支付工資，工廠乙則以件工計算。
工廠甲向工人提供較多的訓練。
工廠乙聘請的兼職工人有較高技術。
工廠乙運用較多資本物品。

questions.explanation: 工廠甲每勞工小時產出 60 單位，工廠乙為 50 單位；工廠甲提供較多訓練可解釋較高生產力。

visuals.caption: 工廠資料
rows: 全職工人的平均工作時數
兼職工人的平均工作時數

questions.keyPoint: 私人廠商的分類：獨資、合夥、私人有限公司及公眾有限公司
questions.stem:
某廠商有獨立的法人地位，但擁有人不得未經其他擁有人同意而轉讓其擁有權。當擁有人想擴展廠商的業務，他們可以 ________。

(1) 運用廠商的保留利潤
(2) 向公眾發售股票以籌集資金
(3) 向朋友借貸以籌集資金
questions.explanation: 這是私人有限公司。它可運用保留利潤和借貸，但不可向公眾發售股票。

questions.keyPoint: 列出各類內部擴張的可能動機
questions.stem: 759 阿信屋是本地一家售賣進口零食的零售商。它將業務擴展至售賣化妝品和護膚產品。下列哪項最不可能是該擴張背後的動機？

choices.text: 將品牌推廣至其他產品
以業務多元化分散風險

questions.explanation: 業務多元化可分散風險、推廣品牌及可能帶來規模經濟，卻不會因而減少競爭。

questions.topicGroup: 短期投入與產出的關係
questions.keyPoint: 邊際回報遞減定律
questions.stem: 下表顯示甲廠商的總產出，該廠商生產時只運用資本和勞力。下列哪項有關甲廠商的陳述是正確的？

choices.text: 若上述資料說明邊際回報遞減定律，X 的值可以等於 180。
若上述資料說明邊際回報遞減定律，X 的值可以等於 190。
若上述資料說明邊際回報遞減定律，X 的值可以大於 200。
邊際回報遞減定律並不適用於甲廠商，因為資本不是固定生產要素。

questions.explanation: 勞力固定於 12，資本的邊際產出先後是 20 和 30；下一個邊際產出為 20 仍可符合遞減回報，故 X 可為 180。

questions.topicGroup: 物品及服務的 津貼
questions.keyPoint: 分析從量津貼對價格、交易量及總收入等的影響，並說明生產者和消費者如何分配津貼得益
questions.stem: 下列哪項會引致活雞農場的總收入上升？

choices.text: 政府調低對活雞農場的利得稅率。
出售活雞的有效配額有所提高。
政府減少對豬肉生產商的補貼。

questions.explanation: 豬肉與活雞是代替品。減少豬肉補貼會令豬肉供應下降，從而增加對活雞的需求。

questions.chapterTitle: 需求和供應的價格彈性
questions.keyPoint: 需求價格彈性的類型
questions.stem: 下表顯示雪糕的價格和顧客對雪糕的總支出的關係。
questions.explanation: 價格上升時總支出上升，表示需求缺乏彈性，彈性介乎零和一。
questions.postVisualStem: 我們可從上表得出結論：雪糕的需求彈性是 ________（不理會其負號）。

questions.topicGroup: 物品及服務的 津貼
questions.keyPoint: 了解需求及供應價格彈性如何影響津貼分配
questions.stem:
政府對生產綠色產品提供 $10 的從量補貼，市場價格因而下降了 $6。下列哪項/些有關綠色產品市場的陳述是正確的？

(1) 綠色產品的供應較其需求更具彈性。
(2) 消費者所獲得的補貼得益比生產者多。
(3) 綠色產品的需求上升。
questions.explanation: 消費者取得 $6 補貼得益、生產者取得 $4，故需求較供應缺乏彈性。補貼改變需求量，不會令需求曲線上升。

choices.text: 香港的貨幣供應定義一（M1）必須全部由美元支持。
港元兌美元的市場匯率由香港金融管理局固定在 1 美元兌 7.8 港元。
當美元兌其他貨幣升值，香港的進口量會上升。
美國經常帳赤字會導致香港經常帳出現赤字。

questions.explanation: 港元與美元聯繫；美元升值時港元亦升值，進口貨物變得較便宜，進口量傾向上升。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 經常帳（主要組成部分：貨物、服務、收益及經常轉移）
questions.keyPoint: 一宗交易會否及如何影響經常帳
questions.stem:
一位來自美國的講師在香港已工作了 10 年。下列哪些會包括在香港經常帳差額計算之內？

(1) 他給予在香港的太太的款項
(2) 他用來購買在美國股市上市的股票的款項
(3) 他捐給非洲慈善機構的款項
(4) 他到美國探望父母所花的款項
questions.explanation: 捐予外地慈善機構屬經常轉移流出；在美國探親的支出屬服務入口。購買股票屬金融帳。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 國際收支差額和國際收支平衡表差額
questions.keyPoint: 國際收支盈餘和國際收支赤字的意思
questions.stem: 下表顯示甲國有關國際收支平衡的一些資料。
questions.explanation: 經常帳為 -1 200 + 700 + 200 - 100 = -400；海外要素收入淨值為正，故本地居民生產總值較大；儲備資產上升 180 表示國際收支盈餘 180。
questions.postVisualStem:
根據以上資料，下列哪些陳述是正確的？

(1) 經常帳的赤字是 400 百萬元。
(2) 甲國的本地生產總值小於其本地居民生產總值。
(3) 國際收支平衡的盈餘是 180 百萬元。

questions.keyPoint: 比較關稅和配額
questions.stem: 在一個小型開放經濟內某物品的供應曲線是向右上斜的。對該物品實施有效進口配額和徵收關稅的主要分別是什麼？

choices.text: 實施有效進口配額會降低進口量，而徵收關稅則不會。
實施有效進口配額會令該物品的消費者盈餘上升，而徵收關稅則可能不會。
徵收關稅會提高該物品的國際價格，而實施有效進口配額則不會。
徵收關稅會令政府收入增加，而實施有效進口配額可能不會。

questions.explanation: 關稅帶來政府收入；配額租可由進口商或外國出口商取得，未必增加政府收入。

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: A famous football team, Manchester United, visited Hong Kong for a friendly match. The day before the match, the team found the pitch in the Hong Kong Stadium had been damaged by prolonged rain and it considered cancelling the match. The opportunity cost for Manchester United to continue playing in such a poor pitch would ________ because ________.

choices.text: increase ...... there was a higher chance for the players to get injured
increase ...... the team was likely to have poor performance
remain unchanged ...... the expense on the visit to Hong Kong had already been paid
remain unchanged ...... the players spent the same amount of time in Hong Kong

questions.explanation: A damaged pitch increases the risk of player injury, raising the opportunity cost of playing.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Definitions of inflation and deflation
questions.stem:
Which of the following do(es) NOT exist in a barter economy?

(1) inflation
(2) interest
(3) comparative advantage
questions.explanation: Inflation requires money; interest and comparative advantage can exist without money.

questions.keyPoint: Definition of free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: An economic good

choices.text: is a good with its demand greater than its supply.
brings us more satisfaction than a free good.
is a good whose quantity available cannot satisfy human wants at zero price.
cannot be found free of charge in any economy.

questions.explanation: Economic goods are scarce relative to wants at a zero price.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: Mei Ho House (美荷樓), a public housing block built in the 1950s, was recently graded as a historic building in Hong Kong. The building was then turned into a hostel which provides double rooms, family rooms and disabled rooms. The above case is related to the ________ question(s) in Economics.

choices.text: ‘what to produce’ and ‘for whom to produce’

questions.explanation: Turning the building into different types of hostel rooms concerns what services to produce and for whom.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The following table shows a production plan of a firm which employs two factors only, namely labour and machinery. The marginal product of labour will start to diminish when the ________ unit of labour is put to work.
questions.explanation: Marginal products are 20, 30, 20 and -5. They first decline when the fourth worker is employed.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The following table shows the cost-output relationship of a price taker. Given that the profit maximizing output of the firm is 3 units. If the fixed cost increases by $5, the price of the good and the output will be ________ and ________ respectively.
questions.explanation: At three units marginal cost is $30. A fixed-cost change does not alter marginal cost or the profit-maximising output.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of issuing shares and bonds to raise capital
questions.stem: A public limited company plans to issue new bonds for expansion. For the existing shareholders, which of the following is an advantage of issuing bonds instead of shares?

choices.text: The accounts of the company need not be disclosed to the public.
They have priority in getting back their capital if the company liquidates.
The interest paid to the bondholders is lower than the dividend paid to the shareholders.
Their power of control over the company will not be diluted.

questions.explanation: New bonds do not create new voting shareholders, so existing shareholders retain their control.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about partnership and sole proprietorship is correct?

choices.text: Partnership has better continuity than sole proprietorship.
Partnership has less flexibility in decision making than sole proprietorship.
Partnership has more capital than sole proprietorship.
Partnership enjoys more economies of scale than sole proprietorship.

questions.explanation: Partners must agree on key decisions, so a partnership is less flexible in decision making.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following will increase the labour supply of an economy?

choices.text: More firms allow male employees to take paternity leave.
More companies offer free transport to employees working overtime.
Universities provide more full-time associate degree programmes for secondary school graduates.
The government adopts maximum working hours for the civil servants.

questions.explanation: Free transport for overtime makes supplying additional work more attractive, increasing labour supply.

questions.keyPoint: Describe the inter-relationship between the three types of production
questions.stem: The following graph shows the relationship of the three stages of production. What do E and F stand for respectively?
questions.explanation: The diagram labels E as producer goods supplied by secondary production and F as raw materials supplied by primary production.

visuals.alt: Flow diagram linking primary, secondary and tertiary production.
visuals.caption: Three stages of production

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following would most likely increase the occupational mobility of labour in an economy?

choices.text: The labour unions have stronger bargaining power for the welfare of their members.
The labour department provides tuition fee rebates for participants of retraining programmes.
The transport network is improved by the extension of highways.
The government stops granting funding for an online data system about job vacancies.

questions.explanation: Retraining makes workers' skills transferable to other occupations.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: In which of the following pairs does the demand for the first good create a derived demand for the second one?

choices.text: West Rail Line train service and Light Rail train service
Blu-ray discs and Blu-ray disc players
Hong Kong Disneyland and Ocean Park Hong Kong

questions.explanation: Pilots are factors of production demanded because aviation services are demanded.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Which of the following would reduce the elasticity of demand for the transport service of the Airport Express?

choices.text: There are more airport bus routes to different districts.
Vans are not allowed to pick up passengers at the airport.
The fare of the Airport Express is raised.
The maintenance cost of the Airport Express trains increases.

questions.explanation: Banning airport pick-up vans removes a close substitute and makes demand less elastic.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: Suppose the equilibrium point of the cosmetic surgery market in Hong Kong is originally at E0. If people become open-minded to cosmetic surgery while more regulations are imposed on the cosmetic surgery industry, the new equilibrium point will be at ________.
questions.explanation: More open-minded consumers raise demand and regulations reduce supply, so the new equilibrium is E3.

visuals.alt: Cosmetic-surgery supply-demand diagram with equilibrium points E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Cosmetic surgery market

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram for the Cross-Harbour Tunnel. The government proposed to raise the toll for the Cross-Harbour Tunnel so as to lessen the traffic congestion during rush hours. Suppose the maximum vehicular volume of the tunnel is fixed. Which of the following statements are correct?
questions.explanation: With capacity fixed, raising the toll does not shift demand. It raises revenue and reduces congestion-related inefficiency.

visuals.alt: Tunnel toll demand diagram with fixed vertical supply.
visuals.caption: Cross-Harbour Tunnel

questions.postVisualStem:
(1) The demand for the service of the Cross-Harbour Tunnel will decrease.
(2) The total revenue of the Cross-Harbour Tunnel will increase.
(3) The deadweight loss caused by traffic congestion will decrease.
(4) The opportunity cost of the drivers using the tunnel will increase.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand and supply schedules of a good.

choices.text: the total sales revenue would be $200 when the price is $2.
there would be a shortage of 25 units when the government imposes a price floor at $4.
when a per unit subsidy of $2 was granted to the seller, the total revenue (including the subsidy) would increase by $160.
when a per unit subsidy of $2 was granted to the seller, the equilibrium price would drop to $1.

questions.explanation: A $2 subsidy moves the buyer price to $2 and seller price to $4, with 100 units transacted. Seller revenue including the subsidy rises from $240 to $400, an increase of $160.
questions.postVisualStem: According to the above information, we can conclude that

questions.keyPoint: Identify the type of market structure
questions.stem: The table below shows the distribution of market share of supermarkets in Hong Kong in 2012.

choices.text: oligopoly ...... sellers are interdependent in their marketing strategies
oligopoly ...... a few major sellers are in control of the total sales of the market
monopolistic competition ...... sellers can affect the market price as their products are heterogeneous from the consumers’ viewpoint
monopolistic competition ...... there are many sellers adopting non-price competition in the market

questions.explanation: A few large sellers account for most market sales, which is evidence of oligopoly.
questions.postVisualStem: From the above table, we can conclude that the market of supermarkets in Hong Kong is an example of ________ because ________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem:
Korean pop singers are becoming more popular in Hong Kong. To these singers, which of the following are their private benefits?

(1) the rise in royalties from the sales of their albums
(2) the rise in sales revenue of Korea-designed fashion
(3) the rise in the number of tourists visiting Korea
(4) the rise in revenue shared from their concerts held in Hong Kong
questions.explanation: Royalties and their share of concert revenue accrue directly to the singers.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem:
Which of the following are ways to lessen the problem of divergence between private and social costs in Hong Kong?

(1) to collect a sewage charge
(2) to collect a university tuition fee
(3) to collect a charge on electricity
(4) to collect a levy on plastic bags
questions.explanation: A sewage charge and plastic-bag levy internalise external costs.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: Which of the following policies can reduce the Gini coefficient based on post-tax post-social transfer monthly household income in Hong Kong?

choices.text: to raise the standard tax rate on salaries tax
to reduce the marginal tax rate on salaries tax
to reduce the amount of Comprehensive Social Security Assistance Schemes (綜合社會保障援助計劃)
to grant an equal sum of money to the Mandatory Provident Fund accounts of every employee

questions.explanation: Raising the standard salaries-tax rate reduces post-tax income inequality more for higher-income households.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem:
Which of the following are results of the government lowering an effective price ceiling on a good?

(1) a reduction in the producer surplus
(2) an increase in excess demand
(3) an increase in the total sales revenue if the demand is elastic
questions.explanation: A lower effective ceiling lowers producer surplus and increases excess demand. With elastic demand, lower price raises total sales revenue.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: The imposition of a per-unit sales tax on cosmetics will

choices.text: reduce the total expenditure on cosmetics.
increase the total social surplus in the cosmetics market.
increase the producer surplus in the cosmetics market.

questions.explanation: A tax creates a wedge, lowers the seller's net price and quantity, and therefore reduces net-of-tax sales revenue.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: Suppose the supply curves of cars and petrol are upward-sloping. If the government imposes an effective quota on the production of cars,

choices.text: the total social surplus in the car market will increase.
the producer surplus in the car market will increase.
the total social surplus in the petrol market will decrease.
the consumer surplus in the petrol market will increase.

questions.explanation: Cars and petrol are complements. Lower car output reduces petrol demand and total social surplus in the petrol market.

questions.keyPoint: Production/value added approach
questions.stem: The following diagram shows a production chain of a good in Economy X. What is the contribution of the production chain to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at market price of Economy X?
questions.explanation: Domestic value added is $230 by the factory, $70 by the wholesaler and $90 by the retailer, plus $60 sales tax, giving $450.

visuals.alt: Production chain using imported raw materials, domestic factory, wholesaler and retailer.
visuals.caption: Production chain and GDP

questions.keyPoint: Growth rate of GDP
questions.stem: The following table gives year-on-year percentage changes in nominal GDP and nominal government spending.
questions.explanation: Government spending grew faster than GDP in 2012, so the public-sector share rose. Positive nominal growth can coexist with falls in real GDP and real public spending under sufficient inflation.
questions.postVisualStem:
Based on the above information, which of the following statements are correct?

(1) The size of the public sector in the economy increased in 2012.
(2) Both the nominal GDP and the nominal government spending dropped in 2012.
(3) A drop in both the real GDP and the real government spending was possible in 2012.

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of nominal GDP and real GDP
questions.stem: Suppose a closed economy produces food and clothing only. The output of Year 1 and Year 2 are as follows. Which of the following statements about the economy are correct?
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP is higher in Year 1. Using either year as base prices, Year 1 has higher real output; the given relative-price changes imply a higher cost of living in Year 1.
questions.postVisualStem:
(1) The nominal GDP in Year 1 is higher than that in Year 2.
(2) The real GDP in Year 1 is higher than that in Year 2.
(3) The cost of living in Year 1 is higher than that in Year 2.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply

choices.text: to relax the quota for foreign domestic helpers
to reduce the subsidy in research and development
to increase the profits tax rate
to increase the number of places in tertiary education

questions.explanation: Relaxing the quota increases labour supply and lowers short-run production cost, shifting SRAS right.

visuals.alt: SRAS shifting right from SRAS0 to SRAS1.
visuals.caption: Short-run aggregate supply

questions.postVisualStem: Refer to the above diagram. Which of the following would most likely lead to the shift of the short run aggregate supply curve from SRAS0 to SRAS1?

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: The Old Age Living Allowance (長者生活津貼) introduced by the Hong Kong government increases the ________ in GDP and results in a ________ shift of the aggregate demand curve.
questions.explanation: A transfer payment raises elderly households' consumption, so private consumption expenditure and aggregate demand rise.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: If there is a decrease in national income of a major trading partner of an economy, the employment of the economy will ________ and the price level will ________ in the short run.
questions.explanation: Lower foreign income reduces exports and aggregate demand, lowering employment and the price level.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Refer to the following balance sheet of a banking system. Suppose the required reserve ratio is 25%.

choices.text: The amount of reserves held by the banks will decrease.
The maximum banking multiplier will increase.
The money supply will remain unchanged.
The maximum possible increase in loans will be the same as the maximum possible increase in deposits.

questions.explanation: With $100 million excess reserves, deposit creation raises loans and deposits by the same cumulative amount; reserves and the required ratio remain unchanged.
questions.postVisualStem: If all banks loan out their excess reserves, which of the following statements about the above banking system is correct?

questions.topicGroup: Licensed banks, restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies in
questions.keyPoint: Features of the three types of deposit-taking institutions
questions.stem:
Maggie plans to deposit $500 000 in a financial institution in Hong Kong for two months. Which of the following institutions can accept this deposit?

(1) licensed banks
(2) restricted licence banks
(3) deposit-taking companies
questions.explanation: Licensed and restricted licence banks can accept this size and term of deposit; deposit-taking companies require larger and longer deposits.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate
questions.stem: The nominal interest rate of a one-year bond and the expected inflation rate are 8% and 3% respectively. If the actual inflation rate is 6%, then the actual real interest rate is ________ and the actual rate of return of holding cash is ________.
questions.explanation: Actual real interest is 8% - 6% = 2%; cash has zero nominal return, so its real return is -6%.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Study the following information about an economy. If all the banks are fully loaned up, the amount of deposits will be ________.
questions.explanation: Bank reserves are monetary base less public cash: $500 - $300 = $200 billion. At a 20% reserve ratio, deposits are $200 / 0.2 = $1 000 billion.

visuals.caption: Monetary information
rows: The coins and notes circulated in the public

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Deflationary gap
questions.stem: Deflationary (output) gap

choices.text: will be widened when there is a depreciation of the domestic currency.
will be eliminated by a rightward shift of the aggregate demand curve when the market adjusts from short run equilibrium to long run equilibrium.
will result in a downward pressure on the prices of inputs.
will exist if the aggregate demand falls short of the short run aggregate supply.

questions.explanation: A deflationary gap lowers demand for inputs, placing downward pressure on their prices.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem: Which of the following policies can the government introduce to reduce the price and unemployment levels at the same time?

choices.text: to raise the subsidies to small and medium-sized enterprises
to raise the salaries tax rate
to raise the expenditure on social welfare

questions.explanation: Higher production subsidies shift SRAS right, reducing prices and increasing employment.

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: The government plans to impose a new tax under which the tax payment drops when taxable income drops. Which of the following statements about the new tax is correct?

choices.text: The tax is regressive as the tax rate increases when the taxable income drops.
The tax is proportional as the taxable income and the tax payment are positively related.
The tax cannot be progressive as the tax rate increases when the tax payment drops.
The tax can be progressive, proportional or regressive.

questions.explanation: Tax payment increasing with income is consistent with all three tax structures; the tax-rate pattern is not given.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: Suppose the velocity of circulation of money remains constant. If a central bank reduces money supply by 10%,

choices.text: the price level will decrease by 10%.
nominal output may decrease by less than 10%.
real output may decrease by less than 10%.

questions.explanation: The quantity equation fixes nominal spending's response under additional assumptions, but real output may fall by less than 10% as prices adjust.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.stem:
Which of the following government policies will lead to an increase in the aggregate output of a country in the long run?

(1) to tighten regulations on environmental protection
(2) to grant an amnesty (特赦) of illegal immigrants
(3) to ban the importation of foreign domestic helpers
(4) to build more international schools for attracting expatriates to work in the country
questions.explanation: An amnesty increases the legal labour force and international schools attract expatriate workers, both raising long-run aggregate output.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Features of the four phases of a business cycle
questions.stem: In the diagram below, A is situated in a certain phase of the business cycle. At Point A, there will be an increase in ________ in the economy.
questions.explanation: At A growth is above the average rate in an expansion: employment, prices and firm sales rise, whereas transfer payments do not.

visuals.alt: Business-cycle graph with point A above average real-GDP growth.
visuals.caption: Business cycle

questions.postVisualStem:
(1) the labour employment level
(2) the general price level
(3) the sales of firms
(4) transfer payments

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Effects of inflation and deflation on different aspects
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about inflation is/are correct?

(1) Inflation occurs when the government handouts a large sum of cash to every citizen in a certain year.
(2) Inflation redistributes wealth from lenders to debtors if it is anticipated.
(3) People prefer holding real assets to cash under expected inflation.
questions.explanation: A cash handout does not necessarily cause inflation, and anticipated inflation is built into contracts. Expected inflation makes real assets preferable to cash.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: The following table shows the number of man-hours required by Country A and Country B in the production of Good X and Good Y. Trade is mutually beneficial between Country A and Country B when the terms of trade is ________.
questions.explanation: The opportunity cost of X is 0.4Y in A and one third Y in B. A terms of trade of 0.35Y lies between them.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem:
Suppose South Korean Won depreciates against the US Dollar. Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, which of the following would be results of the above change in the exchange rate?

(1) The volume of imported goods from South Korea to Hong Kong would increase.
(2) The price of exported goods from Hong Kong to South Korea in terms of US dollar would increase.
(3) The number of tourists from South Korea to Hong Kong would decrease.
questions.explanation: A weaker won makes Korean imports cheaper and Hong Kong travel dearer to Koreans, so (1) and (3) follow. Hong Kong export prices in US dollars do not change because the Hong Kong dollar is linked to the US dollar.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: Which of the following is included in the calculation of the balance of Hong Kong’s current account?

choices.text: A mainland investor purchases a house in Hong Kong.
A Hong Kong investor buys shares issued by a mainland listed company.
A mainland resident buys an air ticket to Hong Kong from a mainland airline.
A Hong Kong resident buys a life insurance policy from a mainland insurance company.

questions.explanation: A life-insurance policy bought from a non-resident insurer is an import of financial services in the current account.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: The following table shows the data about Country A. Which of the following statements about Country A is correct?

choices.text: Country A has both absolute advantage and comparative advantage in producing rubber.
The gain from trade of exporting 1 unit of rubber is 1 unit of petroleum.
The opportunity cost of producing 1 unit of rubber (R) is 2/3 units of petroleum (P) and the terms of trade is 1R=3/4P.
Country A can benefit from trading with Country B, whose opportunity cost of producing 1 unit of rubber is 2 units of petroleum.

questions.explanation: Country A's opportunity cost of rubber is below 1 petroleum, while Country B's is 2 petroleum. A trade rate implied by the data can benefit both countries.

visuals.caption: Country A production and trade
rows: Total output with no international trade
Total output with specialization and international trade

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the imposition of an import tariff on a good in a small open economy. After the imposition of the tariff, which of the following statements about the good in this economy is INCORRECT?

choices.text: The volume of imports is (Q3 - Q2) units.
The domestic consumption is Q3 units.

在任何經濟中找不到免費的經濟物品。

questions.explanation: 經濟物品相對稀少，在零價格時供應量不足以滿足需要。

questions.explanation: 改建和提供不同房型同時涉及生產什麼和為誰生產。

questions.explanation: 邊際產量依次為 20、30、20、-5，第四個勞工加入時開始下降。

付予債券持有人的利息比付予股東的股息低。

(1) 持牌銀行
(2) 有限制牌照銀行
(3) 接受存款公司
questions.explanation: 持牌銀行及有限制牌照銀行均可接受這存款；接受存款公司的最低金額和期限要求較高。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 名義利率及實質利率的關係
questions.keyPoint: 了解方程式：名義利率 = 實質利率 + 預期通脹率
questions.stem: 一年期債券的名義利率和預期通脹率分別是 8% 和 3%。若實際通脹率是 6%，則實際實質利率是 ________ 而持有現金的實際回報率是 ________。
questions.explanation: 實際實質利率為 8% - 6% = 2%；現金的名義回報為零，實質回報為 -6%。

questions.keyPoint: 了解及計算存款、放款、貨幣供應等在存款創造/ 收縮過程後的最大及實際改變
questions.stem: 細閱下列有關某經濟的資料。若所有銀行將可貸款項全數借出，存款的金額會是 ________。
questions.explanation: 銀行儲備為貨幣基礎 $500 減公眾現金 $300，即 $200 十億元；以 20% 比率可創造 $1 000 十億元存款。

visuals.caption: 貨幣資料
rows: 公眾流通的硬幣和紙幣

questions.topicGroup: 短期均衡偏離長期均衡
questions.keyPoint: 通貨緊縮差距
questions.stem: 下列哪項有關通縮（產出）差距的陳述是正確的？

choices.text: 當本國的貨幣貶值，通縮（產出）差距會被擴闊。
當市場由短期均衡調整至長期均衡，總需求曲線的向右移動會消除通縮（產出）差距。
通縮（產出）差距會引致投入的價格有下調壓力。
若總需求小於短期總供應，通縮（產出）差距便會存在。

questions.explanation: 通縮差距令對投入的需求下降，投入價格有下調壓力。

questions.topicGroup: 財政政策對 物價及產出 水平的影響
questions.keyPoint: 擴張性財政政策的影響
questions.stem: 政府可以採用下列哪項政策同時調低物價和失業水平？

choices.text: 增加對中小型企業的補貼

questions.explanation: 增加生產補貼使短期總供應右移，物價和失業同時下降。

questions.keyPoint: 累進稅、比例稅和累退稅
questions.stem: 政府計劃開徵一項新稅：當應課稅收入下降，它的稅款亦下降。下列哪項有關該項新稅的陳述是正確的？

choices.text: 該稅屬累退稅，因為隨著應課稅收入下降，稅率會上升。
該稅屬比例稅，因為應課稅收入和稅款金額有正向的關係。
該稅不會是累進稅，因為隨著稅款金額下降，稅率會上升。
該稅可能是累進稅、比例稅或累退稅。

questions.explanation: 稅款隨收入變動不能確定平均稅率的走勢，三種稅制皆有可能。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹與貨幣數量論
questions.keyPoint: 貨幣數量論的意思
questions.stem: 假設貨幣流通速率維持不變。若中央銀行減少貨幣供應 10%，

choices.text: 名義產出可能下跌少於 10%。
實質產出可能下跌少於 10%。

questions.explanation: 在物價可調整下，實質產出可能下跌少於 10%。

questions.topicGroup: 影響長期總供應的因素
questions.keyPoint: 影響長期總供應的因素
questions.stem:
長期而言，下列哪些政府政策會增加某國的總產出？

(1) 收緊環境保護的法例
(2) 特赦非法入境者
(3) 禁止輸入外籍家庭傭工
(4) 興建更多國際學校以吸引外國人到該國工作
questions.explanation: 特赦增加合法勞動人口，國際學校吸引外籍勞工，均增加長期產出。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.keyPoint: 經濟周期四個階段的特點
questions.stem: 下圖中，A 標示經濟周期中的某一時期。在 A 點，該經濟的 ________ 會上升。
questions.explanation: A 位於高於平均增長率的擴張期，就業、物價及公司銷售額上升，轉移支付不會上升。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹和通貨緊縮的影響
questions.keyPoint: 通貨膨脹和通貨緊縮在不同方面的影響
questions.stem:
下列哪（幾）項有關通脹的陳述是正確的？

(1) 當政府在某一年向每位市民派發一大筆現金，通脹便會出現。
(2) 若通脹是預期的，通脹會令財富再分配，由貸款人轉至債務人。
(3) 在預期通脹的情況下，人們偏好持有實質資產而非現金。
questions.explanation: 派錢未必引起通脹，預期通脹已反映於合約；預期通脹下實質資產較現金吸引。

questions.topicGroup: 了解貿易實現互惠互利的先決條件
questions.keyPoint: 了解貿易實現互惠互利的先決條件
questions.stem: 下表顯示甲、乙兩國生產物品 X、Y 時所需的工作時數。當貿易比率是 ________，甲、乙兩國之間的貿易是互惠互利的。
questions.explanation: 甲生產 X 的機會成本為 0.4Y，乙為三分之一 Y；0.35Y 介乎兩者之間。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 匯率改變對進口及出口的影響
questions.keyPoint: 匯率改變對進出口價格（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）、進出口數量及進出口價值（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）的影響
questions.stem:
假設南韓圜兌美元貶值。在香港聯繫匯率制度下，下列哪些會是上述匯率改變的結果？

(1) 從南韓進口至香港的物品數量會增加。
(2) 從香港出口至南韓的物品價格（以港元計算）會上升。
(3) 到訪香港的南韓遊客人數會下跌。
questions.explanation: 韓圜貶值令韓國入口貨更便宜，訪港對韓國人更昂貴；港元與美元聯繫，港元計的出口價格不變。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 經常帳（主要組成部分：貨物、服務、收益及經常轉移）
questions.keyPoint: 一宗交易會否及如何影響經常帳
questions.stem: 下列哪項包括在香港經常帳差額的計算之內？

choices.text: 一位內地投資者在香港購買一間房屋。
一位香港投資者購買一家內地上市公司發行的股票。
一位內地居民從一家內地航空公司購買前往香港的機票。
一位香港居民從一家內地保險公司購買人壽保險。

questions.explanation: 香港居民向非居民保險公司購買保險屬服務入口，計入經常帳。

questions.topicGroup: 了解貿易實現互惠互利的先決條件
questions.keyPoint: 了解貿易實現互惠互利的先決條件
questions.stem: 下表顯示有關甲國的資料。下列哪項有關甲國的陳述是正確的？

choices.text: 甲國生產橡膠有絕對優勢亦有比較優勢。
出口 1 單位橡膠的貿易得益是 1 單位石油。
生產 1 單位橡膠（R）的機會成本是 2/3 單位石油（P），而貿易比率是 1R=3/4P。
若乙國生產 1 單位橡膠的機會成本是 2 單位石油，甲國可從與乙國貿易獲益。

questions.explanation: 甲國橡膠的機會成本低於一單位石油，乙國為兩單位石油，符合互惠貿易條件。

questions.keyPoint: 分析自由貿易和關稅對小型開放經濟的價格、本地產出、進口、消費量及關稅收入造成的影響
questions.stem: 下圖顯示一小型開放經濟對某物品開徵進口關稅。在這經濟開徵進口關稅後，下列哪項有關該物品的陳述是不正確的？

choices.text: 進口物品的數量為 (Q3 - Q2) 單位。
本地消費量為 Q3 單位。
本地生產商生產者盈餘的增加為面積 a。
關稅總額為面積 b、c、d 之和。

questions.explanation: 關稅收入是入口量乘從量關稅的矩形面積，不是 b、c、d 的總和。
