questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
The Hong Kong government proposes to build new towns with residential flats and shopping malls in the North District. However, there are concerns about the ratio of public housing to private housing. Some people are also worried about the size of shopping malls, which may mainly serve mainland tourists.

The above case is related to the ________ question(s) in Economics.

choices.text: 'what to produce' and 'for whom to produce'
'how to produce' and 'for whom to produce'

questions.explanation: The case concerns the kinds of housing and retail services to provide and the groups that will receive them.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Jeremy is going to watch a tennis match in which Li Na, a Grand Slam winner, will play. Which of the following will increase the cost to Jeremy of watching the tennis match?

choices.text: He is 30 minutes late for the match due to traffic congestion.
His view is blocked by the spectators in front of him.
Due to a rainstorm, the match is extended by an hour.
Li Na is injured and does not show up for the match.

questions.explanation: The longer match uses an additional hour that Jeremy could have used for other activities, so its opportunity cost rises.

questions.keyPoint: Total cost, average cost and marginal cost
questions.stem: The following table shows the cost-output relationship of a firm.

choices.text: the firm enjoys the benefits of economies of scale.
the firm's optimal scale of production is 5 units of outputs.
the average variable cost is increasing.

questions.explanation: At zero output total cost is $10, so that amount is fixed cost.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above table, we can conclude that

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The following table shows a ________ situation in which ________.

choices.text: short run ... the law of diminishing returns does not apply
short run ... the law of diminishing returns applies
long run ... economies of scale exists
long run ... diseconomies of scale exists

questions.explanation: Machinery is fixed while labour varies, so this is a short-run production situation. Marginal product eventually falls, so diminishing returns applies.

questions.keyPoint: External economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: In order to increase the number of nurses for expanding medical services, the government has allocated more resources to expand the nursing programme in universities. In this case, private hospitals will
questions.explanation: Training more nurses improves the environment and input availability for the hospital industry, producing an external economy.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem: The television broadcast of European football matches is

choices.text: a public good if citizens can enjoy the broadcast of matches in public areas like restaurants and Karaoke lounges.
a private good if a local television broadcasting company has purchased the exclusive right to broadcast in Hong Kong.
a free good because there is no cost in serving an additional viewer.
a producer good if the broadcast is used to teach the children in a football training school.

questions.explanation: When used in a training school, the broadcast is an input in producing training services, making it a producer good.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: Teachers in secondary schools are usually paid by time rate because

choices.text: this can improve their work incentive.
it is costly to measure their outputs.

questions.explanation: A teacher's output is difficult and costly to measure precisely, so time-rate payment is used.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem: A firm can ensure a steady supply of raw materials by engaging in ________ while it can increase its market share by engaging in ________.
questions.explanation: Backward integration secures inputs from suppliers; horizontal integration combines with firms at the same production stage to expand market share.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
If a partnership is turned into a private limited company,

(1) the company will become an independent legal entity.
(2) the company will be at a higher risk of being taken over.
(3) the company will pay a higher profits tax rate.
(4) the number of owners will increase.
questions.explanation: A private limited company is a separate legal entity. Under the tax treatment tested in the paper, the applicable profits-tax rate is higher than the partnership's rate.

questions.keyPoint: Concepts of demand
questions.stem:
Which of the following is assumed to be constant when the market demand curve of a good is derived?

(1) the income of the consumers
(2) the price of the good
(3) prices of related goods
(4) preference of the consumers
questions.explanation: A market demand curve varies the good's own price while holding income, related-goods prices and consumer preferences constant.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram showing the market of luxury watches in Hong Kong. The initial equilibrium point is E0. Suppose the rental of shopping premises in Hong Kong rises sharply and the economy in the mainland experiences a recession. The new equilibrium point will be ________.
questions.explanation: Higher shop rents decrease supply and a mainland recession decreases demand. The diagram's joint leftward shifts lead to E2.

visuals.alt: Luxury-watch demand and supply curves with equilibria E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Luxury-watch market

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings of complements, substitutes, normal and inferior goods
questions.stem:
A drop in the price for good X will lead to a drop in the price of good Y if

(1) good X and good Y are substitutes.
(2) good X and good Y are complements.
(3) good X and good Y are in competitive supply.
(4) good X and good Y are in joint supply.
questions.explanation: A lower price of X reduces demand for substitute Y. In competitive supply, a lower return from X shifts resources toward Y, increasing Y supply and lowering its price.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: The following table shows the demand and supply schedule of good X. Suppose the government imposes a $2 per-unit sales tax on each unit of good X sold. The total sales revenue net of tax is ________.
questions.explanation: The tax creates a $2 gap. At buyer price $6 and seller price $4, 70 units are traded, so net sales revenue is $4 x 70 = $280.

visuals.caption: Demand and supply schedule of good X

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram. If the government raises the price floor from P2 to P1, the total revenue received by the sellers

choices.text: may rise or fall, depending on the price elasticity of demand.

questions.explanation: P2 is below the equilibrium price P1, so raising a price floor from P2 to P1 does not change the equilibrium transaction and total revenue.

visuals.alt: Demand and supply diagram with price levels P1 and P2 and quantities Q1 and Q2.
visuals.caption: Price floor

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem:
Suppose the government introduces an effective rent control which sets a maximum rental per square feet the landlords can charge to any tenants. Which of the following statements is correct?

(1) There will be a shortage of rental units.
(2) The landlords will have less incentive to rent out their flats.
(3) The landlords will spend less on maintenance of the rental flats.
questions.explanation: An effective rent ceiling creates excess demand, weakens landlords' incentive to supply flats and reduces incentives to maintain them.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which of the following is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

choices.text: When a higher per-unit import tariff is imposed, the quantity of garment imports worsens.
When a government reduces the unemployment benefit, the number of unemployed people drops.
When political unrest in a country causes riots in its major cities, the number of tourists visiting the country drops.
When people expect the price of the shares of a listed company to rise, the price of those shares rises.

questions.explanation: The statement in A does not describe the inverse relationship between a good's own price and quantity demanded required by the law of demand.

questions.keyPoint: Identify the type of market structure
questions.stem: The market structure of the electric power industry in Hong Kong is

choices.text: an oligopoly because there are two dominating companies in the market.
an oligopoly because the pricing strategies of the companies are interdependent.
a monopoly because the companies can increase the price without losing customers.
a monopoly because there is only one electric company providing electricity in any district.

questions.explanation: Each geographic electricity market is served by a single provider, so it is a monopoly in that district.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Maximisation of total social surplus: marginal benefit equals marginal cost
questions.stem: Suppose the market equilibrium output level is greater than the efficient output level. It implies that

choices.text: total social surplus will increase if output is reduced towards the efficient output level.
at the equilibrium output level, marginal benefit is greater than marginal cost.
the sum of consumer surplus and producer surplus is maximized as the market output level satisfies the equilibrium condition.
government intervention is necessary to reduce output as there is over-production.

questions.explanation: Output above the efficient level means marginal social cost exceeds marginal social benefit. Reducing output toward the efficient level raises total social surplus.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram of a good with the government setting a quota at Q1. Which of the following will be the result of a reduction in quota on the good?
questions.explanation: A tighter binding quota raises price and lowers quantity. Consumer surplus falls, while total expenditure can move either way depending on demand elasticity. Total social surplus falls rather than varying either way.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram with a binding quota at Q1.
visuals.caption: Quota

questions.postVisualStem:
(1) The total expenditure on the good may increase or decrease.
(2) The consumer surplus will decrease.
(3) The total social surplus may increase or decrease.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: A beekeeper keeps the bees for their honey. The bee-keeping benefits the farmers in the orchard nearby because the bees help pollinate the fruits in the orchard. Which of the following statements about this case is correct?

choices.text: There will be a divergence between private and social benefits and the honey is over-produced.
The beekeeper should be subsidized by the government to improve economic efficiency.
If the value of honey is higher than the value of fruits, there is no need for the government to intervene to correct the externality.
There will be no divergence between private and social benefits if the orchard nearby is owned by the beekeeper.

questions.explanation: When the beekeeper owns the orchard, the pollination benefit is internalised, so private and social benefits no longer diverge.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: Which of the following items is NOT included in the calculation of Hong Kong's net factor income from abroad for the current year?

choices.text: the income received by a Japanese teacher who worked in a language school in Hong Kong for one year
rental income earned from real estate holdings in Canada owned by a Hong Kong resident
salary received by an Indian consultant who worked for the Hong Kong Airport Authority for three months
dividends earned from shares in Hong Kong held by a US resident

questions.explanation: A person who has worked in Hong Kong for one year is treated as a Hong Kong resident for this purpose; the income is domestic factor income rather than a net factor flow from abroad.

questions.keyPoint: Expenditure approach
questions.stem: Consider the following Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data about a country. The government consumption expenditure for that year is $________ million.
questions.explanation: GDP = C + I + G + (X - M). Net exports are $10 million and investment is $50 million, so G = 200 - 120 - 50 - 10 = $20 million.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: The aggregate demand curve will shift to the right if

choices.text: there is a fall in the price level.
there is an improvement in technology.
the government reduces the import tariff.
the government reduces the salaries tax rate.

questions.explanation: A salaries-tax cut raises households' disposable income and consumption expenditure, shifting aggregate demand right.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Inflationary gap
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand (AD) curve, the short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve and the long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve of an economy. Suppose initially the economy operates at E0. There is a/an ________ and ________ can help restore the long run equilibrium.

choices.text: inflationary (output) gap ... a rise in transfer payments to the poor
inflationary (output) gap ... a rise in the discount rate
deflationary (output) gap ... a rise in transfer payments to the poor
deflationary (output) gap ... a rise in the discount rate

questions.explanation: E0 lies to the right of LRAS, so there is an inflationary gap. Raising the discount rate contracts money supply and aggregate demand, helping return output to LRAS.

visuals.alt: AD, SRAS and LRAS diagram with short-run equilibrium E0 above full-employment output.
visuals.caption: Inflationary gap

questions.keyPoint: Definitions of M1, M2 and M3 in
questions.stem:
Which of the following is included in the money supply M2?

(1) legal tender held by licensed banks
(2) demand deposits with licensed banks
(3) time deposits with restricted licence banks
(4) negotiable certificates of deposit issued by licensed banks held by the non-bank public
questions.explanation: M2 includes public bank deposits and negotiable certificates of deposit held by the non-bank public, but not legal tender held by licensed banks.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Initially, a banking system has an excess reserve of $160 million and the public holds $200 million cash. The balance sheet of the banking system is as follows. Suppose $100 million is withdrawn from the banking system and held as cash by the public. What will the money supply be if the banks lend out all excess reserves?
questions.explanation: Initially required reserves are $240 million, so the reserve ratio is 20%. After the withdrawal, $80 million remains excess and can support $400 million deposits. Final deposits are $1,500 million and public cash is $300 million, giving $1,800 million.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram. Which of the following will cause the money demand curve to shift from D1 to D2?

choices.text: a fall in the nominal interest rate
more widespread use of electronic money
an open market purchase of bonds by the central bank

questions.explanation: Higher national income increases transactions demand for money, shifting the money-demand curve right.

visuals.alt: Money demand curve shifting right from D1 to D2.
visuals.caption: Money demand

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem:
An expansionary monetary policy is adopted in China when

(1) the Ministry of Finance provides cash subsidies to agricultural workers.
(2) the People's Bank of China reduces the required reserve ratio of all commercial banks.
(3) the Bank of China lowers its lending rate to small and medium-sized enterprises.
questions.explanation: Reducing the required reserve ratio is a central-bank action that directly enables commercial banks to create more deposits. The other actions are not expansionary monetary policy by the central bank.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.stem: Suppose the government greatly increases the tax allowance on continuing education. Which of the following can best explain the effect of the above change on the price and output levels?
questions.explanation: A larger education allowance increases current aggregate demand through lower tax and raises human capital and long-run aggregate supply. Diagram A shows the required rightward shifts.

visuals.alt: Four AD-AS diagrams labelled A to D for an education tax allowance.
visuals.caption: Education tax allowance

questions.keyPoint: One unit increase in disposable income will induce a less-than-one-unit increase in consumption expenditure
questions.stem: If there is a decrease in the desire to consume, the net exports of an economy will ________ and the amount of money held for transaction purposes will ________.
questions.explanation: Lower consumption reduces imports, raising net exports. It also lowers transaction demand for money.

questions.keyPoint: Surplus budget, deficit budget and balanced budget
questions.stem: Initially an economy operates at the full-employment equilibrium and the government expenditure equals its tax revenue. Which of the following will result in a coexistence of deflationary (output) gap and budget deficit?

choices.text: a reduction in desire to import

questions.explanation: A reduction in money supply lowers aggregate demand and output. The resulting lower tax revenue can create a budget deficit from an initially balanced budget.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem:
The real output of an economy grows at a lower rate than the money supply. According to the quantity theory of money, we can conclude that

(1) the price level is increasing.
(2) the unemployment rate is decreasing.
(3) the velocity of circulation of money is decreasing.
(4) the nominal output is increasing.
questions.explanation: With the quantity-theory assumption of constant velocity, faster money-supply growth than real-output growth raises the price level and nominal output.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Features of the four phases of a business cycle
questions.stem:
The following phenomena are observed in an economy:

(1) The unemployment rate is increasing.
(2) The inflation rate is no longer rising but falling instead.
(3) The inventories of producers are accumulating.
(4) The forecast of economic growth is revised downward.

The economy is in the ________ phase of a business cycle.
questions.explanation: Rising unemployment, falling inflation, unwanted inventories and weaker growth forecasts are features of recession.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: Which of the following people will benefit from unanticipated inflation?

choices.text: A loan shark who lends out a sum of money at a floating interest rate
A manager who receives a fixed salary with the period of a two-year contract
A flat-owner who repays a fixed-rate mortgage loan
A retired teacher who receives dividends from various listed companies

questions.explanation: Unexpected inflation reduces the real value of fixed nominal debt repayments, benefiting a borrower with a fixed-rate mortgage.

questions.keyPoint: Four basic principles of taxation
questions.stem:
In July 2009, the government introduced an environmental levy of 50 cents on each plastic shopping bag at the retail level, with the first phase covering chain or large supermarkets, convenience stores and personal health and beauty product stores. Small shops are exempted in the first phase. Customers can pay the levy, with the original amount of purchase of goods, by credit card, Easy Pay System (EPS) or cash.

The collection of the above environmental levy is LEAST in line with the ________ principle of taxation put forward by Adam Smith.
questions.explanation: Exempting small shops makes otherwise similar consumers and retailers face different tax treatment, which is least consistent with equality.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the change in the salaries tax structure of an economy. Compared to the old salaries tax structure, the new tax structure

choices.text: has a lower standard tax rate.
will narrow the income gap between the rich and the poor.

questions.explanation: The diagram shows a higher income threshold before tax and a higher standard rate for higher earners, making the structure more progressive and narrowing the income gap.

visuals.alt: Old and new salaries-tax structures by income and tax rate.
visuals.caption: Salaries tax structure

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: A country's currency appreciates against its trading partners' currencies. If the country's demand for imports is ________, the appreciation of its currency will lead to ________ in the total import value (in terms of domestic currency).
questions.explanation: Currency appreciation lowers import prices in domestic currency. With inelastic import demand, the percentage rise in quantity is smaller than the price fall, so total import value falls.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: Before trade, the output of Thailand and Japan with all their resources evenly allocated between the production of rice and computers is shown below.
questions.explanation: Japan has a lower opportunity cost of computers, so it has comparative advantage in computers. The given outputs alone do not establish absolute advantage, and specialization need not increase the total output of each good.

visuals.caption: Output before trade with resources evenly allocated

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the above case is correct?

(1) Japan has a comparative advantage in producing computers.
(2) Japan has an absolute advantage in producing computers.
(3) With complete specialization in the two countries, the total output of both rice and computers will increase.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: Suppose the terms of trade is 1 unit of computers = 2.4 units of rice and the computer-exporting country has to pay a transportation cost of 0.1 units of rice for each unit of export. To export 5 units of computers, the net gain of the country is ________ units of rice.
questions.explanation: The computer exporter gives up 2 units of rice per computer, receives 2.4, and pays 0.1 in transport. Its gain is (2.4 - 2 - 0.1) x 5 = 1.5 units of rice.

visuals.caption: Output before trade with resources evenly allocated

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.keyPoint: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong is correct?

(1) Hong Kong dollar banknotes are fully backed by Renminbi and the US dollar.
(2) The Hong Kong Monetary Authority holds a considerable amount of foreign exchange reserves.
(3) All note-issuing banks can exchange for US dollars at the linked rate with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.
(4) The exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar to the US dollar in the foreign exchange market is fixed.
questions.explanation: The linked system is backed by foreign-exchange reserves, and note-issuing banks may exchange Hong Kong dollars for US dollars with the Monetary Authority at the linked rate. The market rate is constrained within a convertibility zone rather than literally fixed.

questions.chapterTitle: 三個基本經濟問題與私有產權
questions.keyPoint: 三個基本經濟問題的意思及相關例子
questions.stem:
香港政府建議在北區興建有住宅樓宇和商場的新市鎮。其中公共房屋與私人房屋的比例引起不少人關注。另外，亦有人憂慮商場的規模，指這些商場可能主要為內地遊客服務。

上述個案和經濟學中的 ________ 問題有關。
questions.explanation: 個案涉及生產甚麼住宅和服務，以及為哪些人提供。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 書豪將觀看大滿貫得主李娜參與的一場網球比賽。下列哪項會令書豪觀看該場網球比賽的成本上升？

choices.text: 由於交通擠塞，他遲到了30分鐘。
他的視線被前面的觀眾阻擋。
由於暴雨關係，比賽時間延長了一小時。
李娜受傷，沒有出場比賽。

questions.explanation: 比賽多用一小時，書豪放棄其他活動的機會成本上升。

questions.keyPoint: 總成本、平均成本及邊際成本
questions.stem: 下表顯示某廠商的成本與產出的關係。

choices.text: 該廠商享有規模經濟的好處。
該廠商的最佳生產規模是5單位的產出。

questions.explanation: 零產出時的總成本為$10，故總固定成本是$10。
questions.postVisualStem: 根據上表，我們可得出結論如下：

questions.topicGroup: 短期投入與產出的關係
questions.keyPoint: 邊際回報遞減定律

choices.text: 短期 … 邊際回報遞減定律並不適用
短期 … 邊際回報遞減定律適用
長期 … 出現規模經濟
長期 … 出現規模負經濟

questions.explanation: 機器固定、勞力可變，屬短期；邊際產出最終下降，故邊際回報遞減定律適用。

questions.topicGroup: 外部規模經濟/規模負經濟
questions.keyPoint: 外部規模經濟/規模負經濟
questions.stem: 為求增加護士的數目以擴展醫療服務，政府投放了更多資源予大學開辦更多護士課程。在這情況下，私家醫院會
questions.explanation: 更多護士供應改善整個醫療業的外在生產環境，屬外部規模經濟。

questions.keyPoint: 生產者物品及消費品
questions.stem: 下列哪項有關歐洲足球賽事的電視廣播的陳述是正確的？

choices.text: 若市民可在公眾場所如餐廳和卡拉OK欣賞賽事廣播，這些賽事的電視廣播便是公共用品。
若某本地電視台購買了在本港的獨家播映權，這些賽事的電視廣播便是私用品。
這些賽事的電視廣播是免費物品，因為服務額外一位觀眾是沒有成本的。
若足球訓練學校播放這些比賽作教導兒童之用，這些賽事的電視廣播便是生產者物品。

questions.explanation: 用作訓練學校提供教學服務的投入品，是生產者物品。

questions.keyPoint: 不同的付酬方式
questions.stem: 中學教師一般按工時支薪，因為

choices.text: 這可改善他們的工作意欲。
大部分教師都是勤力的。
量度他們產出的成本很高。

questions.explanation: 教師的產出難以準確量度，按工時支薪的量度成本較低。

questions.keyPoint: 列出各類結合的可能動機
questions.stem: 某廠商可透過進行 ________ 確保原料供應穩定，而它可以透過進行 ________ 增加市場佔有率。

choices.text: 後向合併 … 橫向合併
後向合併 … 側向合併
前向合併 … 橫向合併
前向合併 … 側向合併

questions.explanation: 後向合併確保投入品；橫向合併擴大同一生產階段的市場佔有率。

questions.keyPoint: 比較不同所有權形式的特徵及利弊
questions.stem:
若一家合夥變成了一家私人有限公司，

(1) 該公司會成為一獨立法人。
(2) 該公司被收購的風險會較高。
(3) 該公司須付較高的利得稅率。
(4) 東主的數目會上升。
questions.explanation: 私人有限公司為獨立法人；按本題所用的稅制資料，利得稅率較高。

questions.keyPoint: 需求的概念
questions.stem:
當導出某物品的市場需求曲線時，下列哪項是假設不變的？

(1) 消費者的收入
(2) 該物品的價格
(3) 相關物品的價格
(4) 消費者的偏好
questions.explanation: 導出需求曲線時改變本身價格，其他因素如收入、相關物品價格和偏好保持不變。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋需求改變和供應改變如何影響均衡價格和數量
questions.stem: 參閱以下有關本港名貴手錶市場的供需圖。原初的均衡點是E0。假設本港商舖的租金大幅上升，而內地的經濟出現衰退。新的均衡點會是 ________。
questions.explanation: 租金上升令供應減少，內地衰退令需求減少，圖中的新均衡點為E2。

visuals.alt: 名貴手錶市場的供需圖，標示E0至E4。
visuals.caption: 名貴手錶市場

questions.keyPoint: 了解輔助品、代替品、正常物品及劣等物品的含義
questions.stem:
在下列哪種情況下，物品X的價格下跌會令物品Y的價格下跌？

(1) 物品X及物品Y是替代品。
(2) 物品X及物品Y是輔助品。
(3) 物品X及物品Y屬競爭性供應。
(4) 物品X及物品Y屬聯合供應。
questions.explanation: X變平使替代品Y的需求減少；競爭性供應下資源轉往Y，增加Y的供應。兩者均令Y價格下跌。

questions.topicGroup: 物品及服務的稅項（銷售稅）
questions.keyPoint: 分析從量稅對價格、交易量及總收入等的影響，並說明生產者和消費者的稅項負擔分配
questions.stem: 以下是物品X的供需表。假設政府就每售賣一單位物品X收取$2從量銷售稅。除稅後的總銷售收益是 ________。
questions.explanation: 買方價格為$6、賣方價格為$4時交易70單位，除稅後收益為4 x 70 = $280。

questions.keyPoint: 分析（有效）價格下限對（貨幣）價格、交易量及總收入等的影響
questions.stem: 參閱以下供需圖。若政府將價格下限由P2提高至P1，賣方收取的總收益

choices.text: 可能上升或下降，視乎需求的價格彈性。

questions.explanation: P2低於均衡價格P1，提高下限至P1不改變均衡交易，總收益不變。

visuals.alt: 標示P1、P2、Q1和Q2的供需圖。
visuals.caption: 價格下限

questions.keyPoint: 分析（有效）價格上限對（貨幣）價格、交易量及總收入等的影響
questions.stem:
假設政府實施有效租金管制，即為業主可向租客收取的每平方呎租金設定上限。下列哪項陳述是正確的？

(1) 出租單位會有短缺。
(2) 業主出租他們單位的意欲會較低。
(3) 業主會花費較少的金錢維修出租單位。
questions.explanation: 有效租金上限造成超額需求，並減低業主出租和維修單位的意欲。

questions.topicGroup: 貨幣價格（名義價格）和相對價格
questions.keyPoint: 將相對價格或全價格應用於需求定律，以解釋特定現象
questions.stem: 下列哪項與需求定律並不相符？

choices.text: 當實施更高的從量進口關稅，進口成衣的質素下降。
當政府削減失業救濟金，失業人數下跌。
當某國政局不穩引致它的主要城市發生暴亂，到該國遊覽的旅客人數下跌。
當人們預期某上市公司股票的價格上升，該股票的價格上升。

questions.explanation: A不是由本身價格改變引起需求量反向變化的關係，故不符合需求定律。

questions.keyPoint: 辨識市場結構種類
questions.stem: 香港電力行業的市場結構屬

choices.text: 寡頭壟斷，因為市場上有兩間具支配力的公司。
寡頭壟斷，因為各公司的訂價策略互相影響。
壟斷，因為各公司可提高價格而不會流失顧客。
壟斷，因為在任何地區只有一間電力公司提供電力。

questions.explanation: 每個供電地區只有一間供應商，屬壟斷。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 總社會盈餘達致最大：邊際利益等於邊際成本
questions.stem: 假設市場均衡產出水平高於效率產出水平。這意味着

choices.text: 若減少產出令其更接近效率產出水平，總社會盈餘會上升。
在均衡產出水平，邊際得益大於邊際成本。
消費者盈餘和生產者盈餘之和達到最大，因為市場產出水平滿足均衡條件。
政府有需要作出干預以令產出下降，因為出現過度生產。

questions.explanation: 產出高於效率水平時，減產可增加總社會盈餘。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.topicGroup: 以供需圖輔助，分析市場干預對消費者盈餘、生產者盈餘和效率的影響
questions.keyPoint: 配額
questions.stem: 參閱以下某物品的供需圖，政府為該物品設立配額Q1。下列哪項是減少該物品配額的結果？
questions.explanation: 收緊有效配額令消費者盈餘下降；總支出視乎需求彈性，總社會盈餘則下降。

visuals.alt: 配額Q1的供需圖。
visuals.caption: 配額

questions.postVisualStem:
(1) 對該物品的總支出可能上升或下降。
(2) 消費者盈餘會下降。
(3) 總社會盈餘可能上升或下降。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 正面界外效應與經濟無效率；矯正界外效應
questions.stem: 養蜂者養蜂是為了獲取蜂蜜。養蜂對附近果園的農民有利，因為蜜蜂幫助果園的果樹傳播花粉。下列哪項有關上述個案的陳述是正確的？

choices.text: 私人和社會得益分歧會出現，而蜂蜜會過度生產。
養蜂者應獲政府補貼以改善經濟效率。
若蜂蜜的價值高於水果的價值，政府毋須介入改正界外效應。
若附近果園屬該養蜂者所擁有，私人和社會得益分歧不會出現。

questions.explanation: 養蜂者同時擁有果園時，授粉得益被內在化，私人和社會得益不再分歧。

questions.keyPoint: 本地居民總收入（本地居民生產總值）
questions.stem: 下列哪項並不包括在香港該年度的海外要素淨收入的計算之中？

choices.text: 一位日本教師在香港某語文學校工作一年所得的收入
一位香港居民在加拿大擁有地產物業所賺取的租金收入
一位印度顧問為香港機場管理局工作三個月所得的薪金
一位美國居民持有香港股票所賺取的股息

questions.explanation: 在香港工作一年的教師按居住地準則視作香港居民，其收入不是海外要素淨收入。

questions.keyPoint: 支出面
questions.stem: 參閱下列某國本地生產總值的資料。該年的政府消費支出是 ________ 百萬元。

visuals.caption: 本地生產總值資料
rows: 以市價計算的本地生產總值
本地固定資本形成總額

questions.keyPoint: 導致總需求曲線移動的因素
questions.stem: 在下列哪種情況下，總需求曲線會向右移？
questions.explanation: 減低薪俸稅提高可支配收入和消費，令總需求向右移。

questions.topicGroup: 短期均衡偏離長期均衡
questions.keyPoint: 通脹差距
questions.stem: 下圖顯示某經濟的總需求（AD）曲線、短期總供應（SRAS）曲線及長期總供應（LRAS）曲線。假設原初該經濟在E0運作，這出現了 ________ 而 ________ 可幫助這經濟回復至長期均衡。

choices.text: 通脹（產出）差距 … 增加對貧窮人士的轉移支付
通脹（產出）差距 … 增加貼現率
通縮（產出）差距 … 增加對貧窮人士的轉移支付
通縮（產出）差距 … 增加貼現率

questions.explanation: E0在LRAS右方，出現通脹差距。提高貼現率可收緊貨幣供應和總需求。

visuals.alt: AD、SRAS和LRAS圖，標示E0。
visuals.caption: 通脹差距

questions.keyPoint: 香港M1、M2、M3的定義
questions.stem:
下列哪項是包括在貨幣供應定義二之內？

(1) 持牌銀行持有的法定貨幣
(2) 存於持牌銀行的活期存款
(3) 存於有限制牌照銀行的定期存款
(4) 持牌銀行發出而由非銀行的公眾人士持有的可轉讓存款證
questions.explanation: M2包括公眾的存款和公眾持有的可轉讓存款證，但不包括銀行持有的法定貨幣。

questions.keyPoint: 了解及計算存款、放款、貨幣供應等在存款創造/ 收縮過程後的最大及實際改變
questions.stem: 某銀行系統原初的超額儲備是160百萬元，而公眾持有200百萬元的現金。該銀行系統的資產負債表如下。假設公眾從該銀行系統提取100百萬元並以現金方式持有。若銀行借出全部超額儲備，貨幣供應會是多少？
questions.explanation: 法定儲備比率為20%。提取後尚有80超額儲備，創造400存款；最終存款1500加現金300，共1800百萬元。

questions.keyPoint: 分析貨幣需求、貨幣供應和名義利率的改變
questions.stem: 參閱下圖。下列哪項會令貨幣需求曲線由D1移至D2？

choices.text: 人們更廣泛使用電子貨幣
中央銀行在公開市場購買債券

questions.explanation: 國民收入上升增加交易用途的貨幣需求，令曲線右移。

visuals.alt: 貨幣需求曲線由D1右移至D2。
visuals.caption: 貨幣需求

questions.keyPoint: 擴張性及緊縮性貨幣政策，包括改變法定儲備比率及貼現率
questions.stem:
在下列哪種情況下，中國正採取擴張性貨幣政策？

(1) 財政部向農民提供現金補貼
(2) 中國人民銀行調低所有商業銀行的存款準備金率（即法定儲備比率）
(3) 中國銀行減低對中小企業的借貸利率
questions.explanation: 人民銀行調低法定儲備比率直接增加銀行創造存款的能力，屬擴張性貨幣政策。

questions.topicGroup: 影響長期總供應的因素
questions.keyPoint: 影響長期總供應的因素
questions.stem: 假設政府大幅增加持續教育的免稅額。下列哪幅圖最能解釋上述改變對物價水平和產出水平的影響？
questions.explanation: 免稅額增加會提高當期總需求，並透過人力資本提高長期總供應；圖A同時顯示兩者右移。

visuals.alt: 四幅標示A至D的總需求總供應圖。
visuals.caption: 持續教育免稅額

questions.keyPoint: 可支配收入增加一單位時，消費支出的增加會少於一單位。
questions.stem: 假設某經濟的消費意欲下降，其淨出口會 ________，而持有作交易用途的貨幣金額會 ________。
questions.explanation: 消費減少會減少進口，淨出口上升；交易用途的貨幣需求下降。

questions.keyPoint: 盈餘預算、赤字預算和平衡預算
questions.stem: 原初某經濟在全民充分就業均衡運作，而政府支出相等於其稅項收入。下列哪項會導致通縮（產出）差距和赤字預算同時出現？
questions.explanation: 減少貨幣供應會減少總需求和產出，稅收下降可令原先平衡預算轉為赤字。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹與貨幣數量論
questions.keyPoint: 貨幣數量論的意思
questions.stem:
某經濟的實質產出有所增長，其增長率較貨幣供應的增長率為低。根據貨幣數量理論，我們可得出結論如下：

(1) 物價水平正上升。
(2) 失業率正下降。
(3) 貨幣流通速度正下降。
(4) 名義產出正上升。
questions.explanation: 在貨幣流通速度不變的貨幣數量論下，貨幣增長快於實質產出會推高物價和名義產出。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.keyPoint: 經濟周期四個階段的特點
questions.stem:
某經濟出現下列現象：

(1) 失業率正上升。
(2) 通脹率不再上升而是下降。
(3) 生產商的存貨正增加。
(4) 經濟增長的預測被調低了。

該經濟正處於經濟週期的 ________ 階段。
questions.explanation: 失業上升、通脹下降、存貨累積和增長預測下調均為衰退特徵。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹和通貨緊縮的影響
questions.keyPoint: 解釋為何出現非預期通貨膨脹（緊縮）時，債務人會得益（受損），而債權人會受損（得益）
questions.stem: 下列哪位人士會受惠於非預期通脹？

choices.text: 一位放高利貸者，以浮動利率借出一筆金錢
一位經理，在兩年合約內收取固定薪金
一位物業業主，償還固定息率按揭貸款
一位退休教師，收取多間上市公司的股息

questions.explanation: 非預期通脹降低固定名義還款的實質值，固定利率按揭借款人受惠。

questions.keyPoint: 四個基本的徵稅原則
questions.stem:
在二零零九年七月，政府在零售層面開徵每個塑膠購物袋5角的環保費，首階段範圍包括連鎖或大型超市、便利店及個人護理和美容產品店。在首階段小商戶獲得豁免。顧客可使用信用卡、易辦事（EPS）或現金一併支付原初購物金額和環保費。

徵收上述的環保費最不符合亞當史密所提出的 ________ 賦稅原則。
questions.explanation: 首階段豁免小商戶令相近情況的納稅人受到不同待遇，最不符合公平原則。

questions.keyPoint: 徵稅的影響
questions.stem: 下圖顯示某經濟薪俸稅制的轉變。與舊薪俸稅制相比，新稅制

choices.text: 會收窄貧富之間的收入差距。

questions.explanation: 圖中新制度有較高的免稅門檻及較高的高收入稅率，較進步並收窄收入差距。

visuals.alt: 舊、新薪俸稅制的稅率收入圖。
visuals.caption: 薪俸稅制

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 匯率改變對進口及出口的影響
questions.keyPoint: 匯率改變對進出口價格（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）、進出口數量及進出口價值（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）的影響
questions.stem: 相對於其貿易伙伴的貨幣，某國的貨幣升值。若該國對進口的需求屬 ________，貨幣升值會令進口總值（以本國貨幣計算）________。
questions.explanation: 本幣升值使進口本幣價格下降；需求低彈性時數量增幅較小，進口總值下跌。

questions.keyPoint: 根據個案資料，解釋哪個國家在生產某物品上擁有比較優勢
questions.stem: 貿易前，泰國和日本將他們所有的資源平均分配在生產白米和電腦上，其產量如下。
questions.explanation: 日本生產電腦的機會成本較低，故有比較優勢；資料不足以判定絕對優勢，完全專門化亦未必令兩種物品總產量均增加。

visuals.caption: 貿易前平均分配資源時的產量

questions.postVisualStem:
下列哪項有關以上個案的陳述是正確的？

(1) 日本生產電腦有比較優勢。
(2) 日本生產電腦有絕對優勢。
(3) 當兩國完全專門化生產，白米和電腦的總產量均會增加。

questions.keyPoint: 計算貿易得益
questions.stem: 假設貿易比率是1單位電腦 = 2.4單位白米，而出口電腦的國家每單位出口須支付0.1單位白米的運輸成本。當該國出口5單位的電腦，該國的淨得益是 ________ 單位白米。
questions.explanation: 電腦出口國每單位放棄2白米、獲2.4白米並支付0.1白米運輸，得益為(2.4 - 2 - 0.1) x 5 = 1.5。

visuals.caption: 貿易前平均分配資源時的產量

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 簡介香港的聯繫匯率制度
questions.keyPoint: 簡介香港的聯繫匯率制度
questions.stem:
下列哪項有關香港聯繫匯率制度的陳述是正確的？

(1) 港元鈔票由人民幣和美元十足支持。
(2) 香港金融管理局持有相當數量的外匯儲備。
(3) 所有發鈔銀行可按聯繫匯率與香港金融管理局兌換美元。
(4) 港元兌美元在外匯市場的兌換率是固定的。
questions.explanation: 金管局持有外匯儲備，發鈔銀行可按聯繫匯率與金管局兌換美元；市場匯率在兌換保證範圍內浮動，非固定不變。

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are positive statements?

(1) More workers will be employed on a part-time basis after the imposition of a minimum wage.
(2) Less low skilled workers will be unemployed after the imposition of a minimum wage.
(3) Meal times should be counted as working time in the calculation of a minimum wage.
(4) The imposition of a minimum wage widens the income gap between the rich and the poor.
questions.explanation: Statements (1), (2) and (4) can be tested against evidence. Statement (3) is a value judgement.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Mr Kwok plans to purchase a new racing car from a German automobile manufacturer and drive the car in Hong Kong. In which of the following situations will the cost of purchasing the racing car increase?

choices.text: The Euro depreciates against the Hong Kong dollar.

questions.explanation: A higher first registration fee directly raises the purchase cost of the car.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of interest
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about interest is correct?

choices.text: People will reduce current consumption when the interest rate drops.
The interest rate will be zero if there is no inflation.
Interest does not exist in a planned economy.

questions.explanation: Interest is the reward for waiting and can exist in a barter economy without money.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: A parking lot in the government headquarters is reserved for government officials. The parking lot is ________ because ________.

choices.text: a private good ... it is for private use only
a private good ... concurrent consumption is not possible
a public good ... the government owns it
a public good ... no one has an exclusive right to use

questions.explanation: Only one vehicle can occupy a parking space at a time, so consumption is rival and the lot is a private good.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: The occupational mobility of labour in an economy will increase when

choices.text: the cross-border railway network is improved.
licences are required for more types of job in the labour market.
tax allowances are provided for continuing education.
there is a greater degree of specialisation in production.

questions.explanation: Continuing education raises transferable skills and occupational mobility.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following policies will result in an increase in the labour force of Hong Kong?

choices.text: extension of free education from 9 years to 12 years
an increase in the minimum capital requirement of the Capital Investment Entrant Scheme
an increase in the immigration scheme quota for talented persons from the mainland

questions.explanation: A larger quota for talented immigrants increases Hong Kong's labour force.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem:
Some property agencies pay their employees a basic salary plus commission because

(1) it can increase the working incentive of the employees.
(2) it can transfer part of the business risk to the employees.
(3) the cost of calculating wages is lower.
questions.explanation: Commission links pay to sales and transfers some revenue risk to employees, but it does not lower wage-calculation cost.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership

choices.text: Firm A is at a greater risk of being taken over by another firm than Firm B.
Firm A is a legal entity while Firm B is not.
Both firms are subject to the same profits tax rate.
Firm A is required to disclose its financial status to the public while Firm B is not.

questions.explanation: Firm A has continuity despite an owner's bankruptcy and two owners, indicating a private limited company and thus a legal entity; Firm B is a partnership.

visuals.caption: Firm A and Firm B
rows: Needs the consent of other owners
Needs the consent of other owners
Continues to exist when one of the owners goes bankrupt
Will be dissolved when one of the owners goes bankrupt

questions.postVisualStem: According to the above table, which of the following descriptions of Firm A and Firm B is correct?

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: Refer to the following table showing the production costs of a price-taking firm. If the product price is $6,

choices.text: the firm will produce 5 units of output to maximize its profit.
the maximum profit the firm can make is $5.
the average variable cost is $5 when the firm maximizes its profit.
the minimum total cost of the firm is $13.

questions.explanation: The firm produces 3 units where price equals marginal cost. Revenue is $18 and total cost is $13, so maximum profit is $5.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: Refer to the table below. Which of the following is a possible reason for the difference between the labour productivity of Factory A and Factory B?

choices.text: Factory B provides more training for its workers.
More machines are used in Factory B.
The working environment in Factory A is poorer.
Factory A pays its workers at piece rate while Factory B pays at time rate.

questions.explanation: Factory A produces 6 units per hour while B produces 4. Piece-rate pay in A can produce stronger work incentives, explaining the difference.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem: Michelle is a jewelry lover and she says, 'I will spend all my monthly salary on jewelry no matter what the price is.' From this we can conclude that her demand for jewelry is
questions.explanation: Her total expenditure on jewellery is constant, which means price elasticity of demand is unitary.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem:
Owing to continuous bad weather, the quantity transacted of local vegetables falls by 40% while the price rises by 13%. Which of the following statements are correct?

(1) The quantity demanded of local vegetables falls.
(2) The total expenditure on local vegetables rises.
(3) The demand for imported vegetables rises.
(4) The total expenditure on imported vegetables may rise or fall depending on the elasticity of demand.
questions.explanation: Bad weather reduces local-vegetable supply, raising its price and lowering quantity demanded. Imported vegetables are substitutes, so their demand rises.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: A train accident seriously affects the confidence of travellers using a high-speed electric train service. At the same time, the airlines are facing the problem of rising fuel prices. Which of the following diagrams could represent a result of the above events?
questions.explanation: The accident shifts demand for high-speed train service left. Diagram D shows that relevant shift.

visuals.alt: Four supply-demand diagrams labelled A to D for air travel and high-speed electric train services.
visuals.caption: Train accident and travel services

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on consumer surplus
questions.stem:
On 10th July 2011, the urban taxi fare for the first 2 km was raised from $18 to $20. Which of the following statements about the urban taxi service are correct?

(1) The demand for taxi service dropped.
(2) The price of long-distance taxi trips relative to short-distance taxi trips dropped.
(3) The consumer surplus for the taxi service dropped.
questions.explanation: The fare rise is a movement along, not a shift of, the demand curve. It lowers the relative price of long trips and lowers consumer surplus.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is the demand-supply diagram of a property market. E0 is the original equilibrium point. If the government increases the stamp duties levied on property buyers and tightens the controls on dumping of construction waste, the new equilibrium point in the property market will be ________.
questions.explanation: Higher stamp duty reduces demand and tighter waste controls raise construction cost, reducing supply. The diagram shows E2 for these joint shifts.

visuals.alt: Property-market supply-demand diagram with equilibrium points E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Property market

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply schedule of good X. If the government imposes a per unit tax of $4 on good X,

choices.text: the total tax revenue will be $2 000.
the total sales revenue will drop by $1 800.
the demand for good X is elastic.
the total sales revenue of the substitutes of good X will drop.

questions.explanation: Total sales revenue is $6 000 before the tax ($12 x 500) and $4 200 after the tax ($14 x 300), so it falls by $1 800.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the tax burden
questions.explanation: The buyer price rises from $12 to $14 and the seller price falls from $12 to $10. Consumers and producers each bear $2 of the $4 tax.
questions.postVisualStem: With reference to the above question, the ratio of the consumers' tax burden to the producers' tax burden is ________.

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: If a firm is a monopolist in a market,

choices.text: its monopoly power may come from the government.

questions.explanation: Government licensing or legal protection can be a source of monopoly power. A monopolist need not earn profit and can face potential competition and risk.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem:
The increase of an effective quota on a good will result in

(1) an increase in the quantity transacted of the good.
(2) a further improvement in the quality of the good.
(3) a smaller deadweight loss.
questions.explanation: A less restrictive effective quota increases quantity traded and reduces the deadweight loss; quality does not necessarily improve.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Understand the relationship between the size of the Gini coefficient and the shape of the Lorenz curve
questions.stem: The following diagrams show the Lorenz curves of Country A and Country B.

choices.text: Country B has a higher national income than Country A.
the low income group of Country B has a higher income than that of Country A.
Country A has a more even distribution of income than Country B.
Country A has a larger Gini coefficient than Country B.

questions.explanation: Country A's Lorenz curve is farther from the line of equality, so it has greater income inequality and a larger Gini coefficient.

visuals.alt: Lorenz curves for Country A and Country B.
visuals.caption: Income distribution

questions.postVisualStem: According to the above two diagrams,

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem:
Which of the following are possible causes of income inequality among individuals?

(1) difference in race
(2) difference in capital ownership
(3) difference in health
questions.explanation: Discrimination, unequal capital ownership and differences in health can all lead to income inequality.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: Refer to the following table. If the GDP at factor cost is $264 million, the value of X is ________.
questions.explanation: GDP at market price is $294 million after adding indirect taxes and subtracting subsidies. Gross investment is $80 million after adding depreciation to net fixed capital formation, so X = -20.

questions.keyPoint: Growth rate of GDP
questions.stem: Country A's general price level increases by 10% and its aggregate output and population drop by 2% and 10% respectively. As a result, Country A's nominal GDP will ________ and the per-capita real GDP will ________.
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP rises because the price increase exceeds the output decrease. Real GDP per person rises because population falls more than real output.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: Many Hong Kong construction workers stay in Macau to work for several years. If they are attracted by the job opportunities offered by new infrastructure projects in Hong Kong and return to seek jobs, what will be the effect on the unemployment rate in Hong Kong?

choices.text: The unemployment rate will remain unchanged.
The effect on the unemployment rate cannot be determined.

questions.explanation: Returning workers raise labour supply, but the number of jobs they obtain is not given, so the unemployment-rate effect cannot be determined.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: Which of the following will lead to a decrease in aggregate demand?

choices.text: a fall in the progressivity of income tax

questions.explanation: Higher private saving lowers consumption expenditure and aggregate demand.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand (AD) curves, the short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curves and the long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve of a country. Point E is the initial equilibrium point. When there is an economic recovery in the country's major trading partner, ________ in the short run and ________ in the long run.

choices.text: AD1 will shift to AD2 ... SRAS1 will shift to SRAS2
AD1 will shift to AD2 ... AD2 will shift back to AD1
SRAS1 will shift to SRAS2 ... AD1 will shift to AD2
SRAS1 will shift to SRAS2 ... SRAS2 will shift back to SRAS1

questions.explanation: A recovery abroad raises exports and shifts AD right in the short run. The higher price level then raises input costs, shifting SRAS left in the long run as shown.

visuals.alt: AD, SRAS and LRAS diagram with initial point E.
visuals.caption: Trading-partner recovery

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The table below shows the balance sheet of a banking system. Suppose the required reserve ratio for the banking system is 25%. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: The excess reserves of the banking system are $200 million.
The actual banking multiplier of the banking system is 4.
The banking system can expand its total deposits to $1 600 million.
The maximum amount of loans the banking system can make is $1 000 million.

questions.explanation: With reserves of $400 million and a 25% reserve ratio, maximum deposits are $1,600 million. Current deposits are $1,000 million.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem: Winnie withdraws HK$500 000 from her time deposit with a deposit-taking company. Then she deposits HK$200 000 as a time deposit and HK$100 000 as a demand deposit with a licensed bank. She keeps $50 000 in a safe at home and remits the remainder overseas. What will be the immediate effect of the above actions on the Hong Kong dollar money supply?

choices.text: M1 will increase by HK$50 000 and M2 will increase by HK$350 000.
M1 will increase by HK$150 000 and M3 will decrease by HK$150 000.
M2 will increase by HK$150 000 and M3 will decrease by HK$150 000.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem:
On-line shopping has become more popular, and hence people hold less cash for transaction purposes. Which of the following measures can be adopted by a central bank to reduce the effect of the above situation on the interest rate?

(1) an increase in discount rate
(2) an increase in required reserve ratio
(3) an open market purchase of government bonds
questions.explanation: Lower transaction demand for money tends to lower interest rates. Higher discount and required-reserve rates contract money supply and offset that effect; buying bonds would reinforce it.

questions.keyPoint: Surplus budget, deficit budget and balanced budget

choices.text: a budget deficit ... a trade deficit
a budget deficit ... a trade surplus
a budget surplus ... a trade deficit
a budget surplus ... a trade surplus

questions.explanation: Higher private consumption raises tax revenue from the initially balanced budget and raises imports, yielding a budget surplus and trade deficit.

countries holding a large amount of US government bonds, like China and Japan

questions.explanation: Unexpected inflation erodes the real value of fixed nominal government debt, benefiting the debtor, the US government.

(4) a budget deficit in the years of construction.
questions.explanation: The project raises short-run demand and employment and expands productive capacity in the long run. It is funded from reserves, so it need not create a budget deficit.

In Hong Kong, there are many yoga studios providing yoga classes.

Give TWO reasons to explain why the market of yoga classes in Hong Kong is NOT perfectly competitive.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
Miss Chan and her friends jointly operate a yoga studio in the form of a private limited company in Hong Kong.

Define 'limited liability'. Give TWO possible reasons why they chose to set up a private limited company instead of a public limited company.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: Define 'limited liability'.
parts.modelAnswer: Limited liability means that when a firm is liquidated, the liability of an owner is confined to the amount of his or her investment in the firm.
markingPoints: Owner's liability is limited to the amount invested.
The owner does not have to pay the firm's debts beyond that amount.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
Miss Chan and her friends jointly operate a yoga studio in the form of a private limited company in Hong Kong.

Define 'limited liability'. Give TWO possible reasons why they chose to set up a private limited company instead of a public limited company.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: Give TWO possible reasons why they chose to set up a private limited company instead of a public limited company.
parts.modelAnswer: Possible reasons include lower risk of takeover because the transfer of ownership requires consent of other owners, and no need to disclose financial accounts to the public.
markingPoints: Lower risk of takeover because the transfer of ownership requires consent of other owners.
No need to disclose financial accounts to the public.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem:
A tutorial teacher shares his short teaching videos on social media to the public free of charge. Many people benefit from his videos without paying him anything.

Explain why externality is NOT necessarily involved in the above situation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain why externality is NOT necessarily involved in the above situation.
parts.modelAnswer: The teacher may gain from extra income through advertising or from more people joining his classes because the videos become more popular. If the increase in his income equals the benefit enjoyed by viewers at the margin, there is no externality.
markingPoints: The teacher may benefit from higher income from advertising or his classes.
If private benefit matches marginal social benefit, there is no externality.

questions.keyPoint: Qualities of good money
questions.stem:
In a small village, all villagers accept rice in settling payments for exchanges.

Give TWO reasons to explain why rice is NOT a good form of money compared to banknotes even if rice is generally acceptable.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Give TWO reasons to explain why rice is NOT a good form of money compared to banknotes even if rice is generally acceptable.
parts.modelAnswer: Rice is not durable because it may decay within years and cannot be stored for a long time. It is also not homogeneous or portable, so it is inconvenient for transactions.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources

questions.stem:

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: In the 2024-25 Budget, the Financial Secretary proposed to adjust the rate of the hotel accommodation tax (HAT) from 0% to 3% with effect from 1 January 2025. Hotels and guesthouses would be required to pay the HAT at the rate of 3% on accommodation charges.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the proposed HAT is a progressive tax, a proportional tax or a regressive tax.
parts.modelAnswer: It is a regressive tax. The same amount of tax is paid for a hotel room of the same price regardless of income, so the average tax rate decreases as income increases.
markingPoints: Explains that the same room price leads to the same tax amount regardless of income.
Average tax rate falls when income rises.

questions.keyPoint: Direct tax and indirect tax
questions.stem: In the 2024-25 Budget, the Financial Secretary proposed to adjust the rate of the hotel accommodation tax (HAT) from 0% to 3% with effect from 1 January 2025. Hotels and guesthouses would be required to pay the HAT at the rate of 3% on accommodation charges.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: An economist comments, 'Both the indirect tax revenue and the direct tax revenue of the Government may be affected by the above proposed HAT.' Justify the economist's comment.
parts.modelAnswer: The proposed HAT is an indirect tax, so raising its rate from 0% to 3% increases indirect tax revenue from zero to a positive amount. It may also marginally reduce hotels’ and guesthouses’ profits, reducing direct tax revenue from profits tax.
markingPoints: Indirect tax revenue from HAT increases.
The tax may reduce hotel and guesthouse profits.
Profits tax revenue, a direct tax revenue, may fall.

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem: In the 2024-25 Budget, the Financial Secretary proposed to adjust the rate of the hotel accommodation tax (HAT) from 0% to 3% with effect from 1 January 2025. Hotels and guesthouses would be required to pay the HAT at the rate of 3% on accommodation charges.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: There are receptionists, bell boys, room attendants and managers working in hotels. What economic principle is illustrated by the above phenomenon? List THREE reasons why applying this principle can increase labour productivity.
parts.modelAnswer: The phenomenon illustrates complex division of labour. Productivity may increase because practice makes perfect, the most suitable person can be assigned to each task, training time can be saved, job rotation time can be saved, and mechanisation may be stimulated.
markingPoints: The most suitable person can be assigned to each task.
Training time or job-rotation time can be saved.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: In the 2024-25 Budget, the Financial Secretary proposed to adjust the rate of the hotel accommodation tax (HAT) from 0% to 3% with effect from 1 January 2025. Hotels and guesthouses would be required to pay the HAT at the rate of 3% on accommodation charges.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: A room attendant job advertisement states that the major duty is tidying hotel rooms, working hours are 10am-2pm, and salary is $85 per hour. From the viewpoint of hotel owners, give ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of this wage payment method over piece rate.
parts.modelAnswer: An advantage is that it is easier to maintain a stable team of staff because income is more stable, or the cost of measuring output is lower. A disadvantage is that monitoring against shirking is more costly, or labour productivity may be lower due to weaker working incentives.
markingPoints: Advantage: more stable income helps retain staff, or output measurement cost is lower.
Disadvantage: higher monitoring cost against shirking, or lower productivity due to weaker incentives.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: In the 2024-25 Budget, the Financial Secretary proposed to adjust the rate of the hotel accommodation tax (HAT) from 0% to 3% with effect from 1 January 2025. Hotels and guesthouses would be required to pay the HAT at the rate of 3% on accommodation charges.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Many hotels in Hong Kong charge a higher room rate during public holidays than on other days. Explain whether the opportunity cost of staying in those hotels in Hong Kong is necessarily higher during public holidays than on other days.
parts.modelAnswer: No. Some people may have a lower time cost during public holidays. If the saving in time cost is greater than the additional money cost from the higher room rate, the opportunity cost of staying in a Hong Kong hotel would be lower.
markingPoints: Opportunity cost includes money cost and time cost.
Time cost may be lower during public holidays.
The saving in time cost may exceed the extra money cost, so opportunity cost is not necessarily higher.

questions.keyPoint: 累進稅、比例稅和累退稅
questions.stem: 在 2024-25 年度財政預算案中，財政司司長建議由 2025 年 1 月 1 日起，把酒店房租稅（HAT）的稅率由 0% 調整至 3%。酒店和賓館須按房租的 3% 繳交酒店房租稅。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 解釋上述建議的酒店房租稅是累進稅、比例稅，還是累退稅。
parts.modelAnswer: 這是累退稅。收入高低不論，只要入住相同價格的酒店房間便需支付相同稅額；因此收入上升時，平均稅率下降。
markingPoints: 入住相同價格房間需支付相同稅額。
收入上升時平均稅率下降。

questions.keyPoint: 直接稅與間接稅
questions.stem: 在 2024-25 年度財政預算案中，財政司司長建議由 2025 年 1 月 1 日起，把酒店房租稅（HAT）的稅率由 0% 調整至 3%。酒店和賓館須按房租的 3% 繳交酒店房租稅。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 一名經濟學家評論：「政府的間接稅稅收和直接稅稅收均可能受上述建議的酒店房租稅影響。」論證該經濟學家的評論。
parts.modelAnswer: 酒店房租稅是間接稅。稅率由 0% 調整至 3% 後，酒店房租稅的間接稅收入會由零變為正數。重新徵收此稅亦可能在邊際上降低酒店和賓館的利潤，從而降低來自利得稅的直接稅收入。
markingPoints: 稅率上升令間接稅收入增加。
稅項可能降低酒店和賓館利潤。
利得稅收入作為直接稅收入可能下降。

questions.keyPoint: 分工的好處及壞處
questions.stem: 在 2024-25 年度財政預算案中，財政司司長建議由 2025 年 1 月 1 日起，把酒店房租稅（HAT）的稅率由 0% 調整至 3%。酒店和賓館須按房租的 3% 繳交酒店房租稅。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 酒店的工作人員包括接待員、行李服務員、房務員和經理。上述現象說明了什麼經濟原理？列出三個理由，解釋應用該原理如何能提高勞工生產力。
parts.modelAnswer: 上述現象說明複雜分工。分工能透過熟能生巧、挑選最合適的人負責每項工作、節省訓練時間、節省轉換工作崗位時間，以及促進機械化，提高勞工生產力。
markingPoints: 挑選最合適的人做每項工作。
節省訓練或轉換崗位時間。

questions.keyPoint: 不同的付酬方式
questions.stem: 在 2024-25 年度財政預算案中，財政司司長建議由 2025 年 1 月 1 日起，把酒店房租稅（HAT）的稅率由 0% 調整至 3%。酒店和賓館須按房租的 3% 繳交酒店房租稅。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 某酒店招聘房務員的廣告列明：主要職責為清理酒店房間；工作時間為上午 10 時至下午 2 時；薪金為每小時 $85。從酒店東主的角度，舉出上述支薪方法相對於以件計薪的一項優點和一項缺點。
parts.modelAnswer: 優點可以是收入較穩定，較容易維持穩定員工團隊；或量度產出的成本較低。缺點可以是監管員工偷懶的成本較高；或因工作誘因較低而令勞工生產力較低。
markingPoints: 優點：收入較穩定有助留住員工，或量度產出成本較低。
缺點：監管偷懶成本較高，或工作誘因較低令生產力較低。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 在 2024-25 年度財政預算案中，財政司司長建議由 2025 年 1 月 1 日起，把酒店房租稅（HAT）的稅率由 0% 調整至 3%。酒店和賓館須按房租的 3% 繳交酒店房租稅。

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: 香港很多酒店在公眾假期期間收取較其他日子高的房租。解釋在公眾假期期間入住該些香港酒店的機會成本是否一定較其他日子高。
parts.modelAnswer: 否。有些人在公眾假期期間的時間成本可能較其他日子低。若節省的時間成本大於因較高房租而增加的金錢成本，入住香港酒店的機會成本便會較低。
markingPoints: 機會成本包括金錢成本和時間成本。
公眾假期期間的時間成本可能較低。
若節省的時間成本大於額外金錢成本，機會成本不一定較高。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: Based on the above data, what was the real output growth rate in the US from May 2022 to May 2023 as implied by the quantity theory of money? Explain your answer.
parts.modelAnswer: Using MV = PY, where M is money supply, V is velocity of circulation, P is the general price level and Y is real output. Assuming V is constant, growth of Y = growth of M - growth of P = -3.94% - 3.6% = -7.54%.

parts.prompt: Suppose the Government has two objectives: reduce the waiting time for PRH units and reduce income inequality. Strategy X is increasing the penalty for PRH tenants whose incomes substantially exceed the limit. Strategy Y is allocating more land for PRH units instead of private residential units. Discuss how EACH strategy may help achieve EACH objective, and, except for the effects on PRH tenants, discuss ONE possible undesirable economic effect of Strategy X on one group of stakeholders and ONE possible undesirable economic effect of Strategy Y on another group of stakeholders.
parts.modelAnswer: Strategy X raises the cost of staying in PRH units for households whose incomes exceed the limit, reducing demand and excess demand, so waiting time may fall. It can also allow more lower-income households to move into PRH units, increasing their real income and reducing income inequality. Strategy Y increases PRH supply, which may reduce excess demand and waiting time if the supply increase is larger than any induced increase in demand. It can also let more lower-income households live in PRH and may reduce private residential rental by shifting some tenants away from private housing, reducing income inequality. Undesirable effects may include lower property-agent income if private housing transactions fall, or higher private housing prices if less land is available for private residential units.
markingPoints: Strategy X reduces PRH demand from households above the income limit and may shorten waiting time.
Strategy X can shift PRH units to lower-income households and reduce income inequality.
Strategy Y increases PRH supply and may reduce excess demand and waiting time.
Strategy Y can help lower-income households and may lower private residential rent, reducing income inequality.
Discusses a possible undesirable effect of Strategy X on a non-PRH-tenant stakeholder.
Discusses a possible undesirable effect of Strategy Y on another non-PRH-tenant stakeholder.
Uses sources and economic reasoning in an organised essay answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 假設政府有兩項政策目標：縮短公屋單位輪候時間及減低收入不均。策略 X 是提高對收入遠高於限額的公屋租戶的懲罰；策略 Y 是分配更多土地興建公屋單位而非私人住宅單位。討論兩項策略分別如何可能有助達成每項政策目標，並在撇除對公屋租戶的影響下，討論策略 X 對一組持份者及策略 Y 對另一組持份者可能造成的一項負面經濟影響。
parts.modelAnswer: 策略 X 令收入高於限額的家庭租住公屋的成本上升，公屋需求下降，超額需求減少，輪候時間可能縮短。它亦可讓更多低收入家庭入住公屋，提高其實質收入，減低收入不均。策略 Y 增加公屋供應；若供應增加幅度大於需求增加幅度，超額需求及輪候時間會下降。它亦可讓更多低收入家庭入住公屋，並可能減少私人住宅需求及租金，從而減低收入不均。負面影響可包括：私人住宅成交或出租量下降令地產經紀收入下跌，或私人住宅土地供應下降令私人住宅價格上升，令準買家更難置業。
markingPoints: 策略 X 減少高收入家庭對公屋需求，可能縮短輪候時間。
策略 X 讓更多低收入家庭入住公屋，可能減低收入不均。
策略 Y 增加公屋供應，可能減少超額需求和輪候時間。
策略 Y 可幫助低收入家庭，並可能降低私人住宅租金，減低收入不均。
討論策略 X 對非公屋租戶持份者的一項負面經濟影響。
討論策略 Y 對另一非公屋租戶持份者的一項負面經濟影響。
答案能運用資料及經濟理論，有組織地論述。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Due to an increase in oil price, the efficient output level of Airline A drops to Q0 as in (a)(i). 'Airline A will produce at the efficient output level after the change.' Do you agree? Explain your answer with the aid of Figure 2.
parts.modelAnswer: No. When marginal cost rises, both the efficient output and the monopolist’s profit-maximising output fall. However, the new profit-maximising output is still below the efficient output because marginal benefit remains greater than the new marginal cost at the firm’s output.
markingPoints: Marginal cost rises after the oil-price increase.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: Many industrial activities emit carbon dioxide, intensifying global warming and potentially bringing hazards to all human beings. A system of carbon credits is introduced by the governments in some countries. Carbon credits are permits for emitting carbon dioxide. Producers must purchase carbon credits from the government in order to engage in production activities that emit carbon dioxide.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: In terms of externality, explain why the emission of carbon dioxide by industrial activities may result in economic inefficiency.
parts.modelAnswer: Negative externality may be involved when producers emitting carbon dioxide do not have to compensate others for the harm caused. The market equilibrium output, where marginal private benefit equals marginal private cost, would be higher than the socially efficient level where marginal social benefit equals marginal social cost. The divergence between marginal private cost and marginal social cost leads to over-production and inefficient resource allocation.
markingPoints: Negative externality may be involved when producers do not compensate others for harm.
Market output is higher than the socially efficient output.
Marginal private cost is lower than marginal social cost.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: Many industrial activities emit carbon dioxide, intensifying global warming and potentially bringing hazards to all human beings. A system of carbon credits is introduced by the governments in some countries. Carbon credits are permits for emitting carbon dioxide. Producers must purchase carbon credits from the government in order to engage in production activities that emit carbon dioxide.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain how the introduction of the system of carbon credits may improve economic efficiency.
parts.modelAnswer: Paying for carbon credits raises producers' marginal private cost and lowers equilibrium output towards the efficient level. At the lower output, the gap between marginal private cost and marginal social cost is reduced and economic efficiency improves.
markingPoints: Carbon credits raise marginal private cost.
Output falls towards the efficient level and the external cost gap is reduced.

questions.stem: Since the 2010s, the government of Saudi Arabia has been actively promoting football development. Some football clubs in Saudi Arabia have established their own football academies to train young players.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Suppose some unemployed youngsters stopped seeking jobs and enrolled in the full-time training programmes of these football academies. Explain how the unemployment rate in Saudi Arabia would be affected.
parts.modelAnswer: Unemployment rate = unemployed population / labour force x 100%. parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Ahmed is considering whether to stop seeking jobs and enrol in a full-time training programme. His first option is Football Academy A, second option Football Academy B, and third option continuing to seek jobs. Suppose Football Academy B offers a scholarship to Ahmed. Explain whether the opportunity cost for Ahmed to continue seeking jobs would necessarily remain unchanged.
parts.modelAnswer: No. The scholarship makes the second option more attractive or raises its value. If it raises the value of Football Academy B above that of Football Academy A, the opportunity cost of continuing to seek jobs changes from the value of Academy A to the value of Academy B.
markingPoints: States that opportunity cost need not remain unchanged.
Scholarship raises the value of the second option.
If the second option becomes the highest-valued option forgone, opportunity cost changes.

parts.modelAnswer: Suggestion I may increase labour supply and lower equilibrium wages in catering, reducing production cost and increasing supply. Equilibrium quantity rises and total revenue may increase if demand rises enough, if price is unchanged, or if quantity rises by a larger percentage than any price fall. Its effect may be limited by HKD appreciation against RMB and lower Mainland inflation, which reduce Mainland visitors' spending in Hong Kong and encourage Hong Kong residents to spend in the Mainland. Suggestion II may raise investment in innovation and technology, improve production technology and make production more capital-intensive, raising labour productivity. It can increase LRAS, potential output and productive capacity. Its effect may be limited by high Hong Kong interest rates, which raise borrowing costs, and by HKD appreciation, which raises the cost of investing in Hong Kong for Mainland investors or encourages Hong Kong investors to invest in the Mainland.
markingPoints: Explains how imported workers raise labour supply and reduce catering production cost.
Explains how night-time events raise demand for catering services and may raise total revenue.
Explains possible limits from exchange-rate changes or relative inflation.
Explains how tax deductions may raise innovation and technology investment.
Links technology investment to higher labour productivity, LRAS and potential output.
Explains possible limits from higher interest rates or exchange-rate changes.

questions.keyPoint: 負面界外效應與經濟無效率；把外部成本內在化
questions.stem: 很多工業活動排放二氧化碳，加劇全球暖化，並可能對全人類帶來危害。一些國家的政府推行碳信用制度。碳信用是排放二氧化碳的許可證。生產者必須向政府買入碳信用，才可進行會排放二氧化碳的生產活動。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 以界外效應為依據，解釋為什麼工業活動的二氧化碳排放可能會導致經濟缺乏效率。
parts.modelAnswer: 若排放二氧化碳的生產者沒有為其對其他人造成的損害作出補償，則可能出現負面界外效應。由邊際私人利益等於邊際私人成本決定的均衡數量，會高於邊際社會利益等於邊際社會成本的有效率產出水平。邊際私人成本與邊際社會成本分離而導致過度生產，意味資源分配無效率。
markingPoints: 生產者沒有補償他人損害，可能有負面界外效應。
市場產出高於有效率產出。
邊際私人成本低於邊際社會成本。
過度生產導致經濟無效率。

questions.stem: 自 2010 年代起，沙特阿拉伯政府積極推動足球發展。一些沙特阿拉伯足球會成立自己的足球學院訓練年輕球員。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 假設一些失業青年停止尋找工作，並參加足球學院的全日制訓練課程。解釋沙特阿拉伯的失業率會如何受影響。
parts.modelAnswer: 失業率 = 失業人口 / 勞動人口 x 100%。失業青年參加全日制訓練後，失業人口和勞動人口以相同人數下降；失業人口下降百分比大於勞動人口下降百分比，所以失業率下降。
markingPoints: 失業人口和勞動人口同時以相同人數下降。
失業人口下降百分比較大。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 自 2010 年代起，沙特阿拉伯政府積極推動足球發展。一些沙特阿拉伯足球會成立自己的足球學院訓練年輕球員。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 艾德考慮是否停止求職並參加足球學院全日制訓練。他的第一選項為足球學院 A，第二選項為足球學院 B，第三選項為繼續求職。假設足球學院 B 向艾德提供獎學金，解釋他繼續求職的機會成本是否必然維持不變。
parts.modelAnswer: 否。獎學金令第二選項更具吸引力或提高其價值。若第二選項價值高於第一選項，繼續求職的機會成本會由參加足球學院 A 的價值改變為參加足球學院 B 的價值。
markingPoints: 獎學金提高第二選項價值。
若第二選項成為最高價值放棄選項，機會成本改變。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋需求改變和供應改變如何影響均衡價格和數量
questions.stem: 新冠疫情令香港經歷經濟下行。疫情過後，香港在復常路上仍面對種種挑戰。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 假設有兩項建議刺激香港經濟復蘇及增長：I. 輸入大量低技術工人給餐飲業，並舉辦更多夜間活動吸引市民和遊客夜間外出消閒；II. 為公司創新及科技項目開支提供稅務扣減，以吸引本地和海外投資者投資香港創新科技產業。參考以上資料及你的經濟學知識，討論每項建議如何達成其目標，以及可能限制兩項建議達成相應目標的一些因素。
parts.modelAnswer: 建議 I 可增加餐飲業勞力供應，令均衡工資下降，生產成本下降，供應上升；夜間活動亦會提高餐飲需求。均衡數量上升，若需求上升足夠、價格不變，或數量上升百分比大於價格下跌百分比，總收入會上升。其成效可能受港元兌人民幣升值及內地通脹較低限制，因這些因素會減少內地旅客在港消費或鼓勵香港居民到內地消費。建議 II 可增加創新及科技投資，提升生產技術，令生產模式更資本密集，提高勞工生產力，並增加長期總供應、潛在產出及生產能力。其成效可能受香港利率上升限制，因借貸成本上升；港元升值亦會提高內地投資者投資香港的成本，或鼓勵香港投資者到內地投資。
markingPoints: 說明輸入工人增加勞力供應並降低餐飲生產成本。
說明夜間活動增加餐飲需求及可能提高總收入。
說明匯率或相對通脹可能限制成效。
說明稅務扣減可增加創科投資。
連繫創科投資與勞工生產力、LRAS 及潛在產出。
說明利率或匯率可能限制成效。
有組織地運用資料及經濟理論。

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms

questions.stem: An electric car manufacturer took over a social media company.

parts.label: (a)

parts.modelAnswer: It was conglomerate integration because electric car manufacturing and social media operation are totally unrelated businesses.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Why did the electric car manufacturer choose to take over a social media company instead of taking over another electric car manufacturer? List TWO possible reasons.
parts.modelAnswer: Possible motives include spreading risk through product diversification and making use of its brand name in other products or services.
markingPoints: Making use of its brand name in other products/services.
Any other relevant point. Mark the first two points only.

questions.keyPoint: Distinguishing between free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: An electric car manufacturer took over a social media company.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Some economists share their economic analyses on social media free of charge. Explain whether these economic analyses are free goods to society.
parts.modelAnswer: No. The resources involved in writing these analyses have alternative uses, and more of these analyses are preferred by some people.
markingPoints: Resources used have alternative uses or more analyses are preferred by some people.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital

Study the following news extract.

A postal company has decided to introduce its first digital employee, a smart chatbot. The chatbot can answer commonly asked questions from customers, freeing up the customer services team to solve more complex queries.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings and give examples of variable and fixed factors
questions.stem: The table below shows the production data of a firm.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the law of diminishing marginal returns is illustrated by the above data.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. Given a fixed quantity of machinery at 12 units, labour is the variable factor. Total output rises from 180 to 221 units when labour increases from 12 to 13, so marginal product is 41 units, after previously rising. The marginal product then falls compared with 48 units when labour rose from 11 to 12, so diminishing marginal returns is illustrated.
markingPoints: Machinery is fixed at 12 units while labour is variable.
