questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: Smartphones of the same model are sold in different shops at different prices.

parts.label: Q4
parts.prompt: Explain with TWO reasons why some customers buy the smartphones from shops selling at higher prices.
parts.modelAnswer: Some customers may have imperfect market information and do not know about shops selling at lower prices, possibly because search costs are high. Also, shops may offer heterogeneous services, such as better after-sales service, longer warranty periods or better product descriptions by salespersons, so customers are willing to pay a premium.
markingPoints: Imperfect market information or high search costs.
Heterogeneous products/services such as better after-sales service, warranty or sales explanation.
Any other reasonable answer. Mark the first two points only.

questions.stem:

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: The amount of resources in Country A is twice of that in Country B. Suppose both Country A and Country B use ALL their resources in production. Their maximum output is shown in the table below.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain whether Country A has an absolute advantage in producing computers.
parts.modelAnswer: No. With the same amount of resources, Country A can only produce the same number of computers as Country B.
markingPoints: After adjusting for resources, Country A and Country B can produce the same number of computers.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has an absolute advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: The amount of resources in Country A is twice of that in Country B. Suppose both Country A and Country B use ALL their resources in production. Their maximum output is shown in the table below.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain whether Country A has a comparative advantage in producing computers.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. Opportunity cost of producing 1 computer is 500/800 = 0.625 units of rice in Country A and 300/400 = 0.75 units of rice in Country B. Country A has a lower opportunity cost, so it has a comparative advantage in computers.
markingPoints: Opportunity cost in Country A = 0.625 units of rice.
Opportunity cost in Country B = 0.75 units of rice.
Country A has a lower opportunity cost and hence comparative advantage.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: The amount of resources in Country A is twice of that in Country B. Suppose both Country A and Country B use ALL their resources in production. Their maximum output is shown in the table below.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Suppose the computer-importing country has to pay a transportation cost of 0.05 units of rice for each unit of computers imported. Find the range of terms of trade (for 1 unit of computers) that is mutually beneficial for both countries.
parts.modelAnswer: 0.625 units of rice < 1 unit of computers < 0.7 units of rice.
markingPoints: Lower bound is Country A's opportunity cost, 0.625 rice.
Upper bound for the importing country is 0.75 - 0.05 = 0.7 rice.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of buying shares and bonds from small investors’ point of view
questions.stem: In 2022, the Hong Kong Financial Secretary announced the issuance of Silver Bonds for citizens aged 60 or above to subscribe. The nominal interest rate of the Silver Bonds is equal to the actual inflation rate in Hong Kong, subject to a minimum of 4%.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: From the viewpoint of senior citizens, explain ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of holding Silver Bonds over holding cash.
parts.modelAnswer: An advantage is that purchasing power can be better preserved in times of inflation because the nominal return on Silver Bonds rises with inflation, while cash has zero nominal return. A disadvantage is lower liquidity because it takes days for Silver Bonds to be redeemed and converted into cash.
markingPoints: Advantage: purchasing power is better preserved during inflation.
Disadvantage: liquidity is lower than cash.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate
questions.stem: In 2022, the Hong Kong Financial Secretary announced the issuance of Silver Bonds for citizens aged 60 or above to subscribe. The nominal interest rate of the Silver Bonds is equal to the actual inflation rate in Hong Kong, subject to a minimum of 4%.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: Suppose the expected inflation rate is 4.5% and there turns out to be an actual deflation of 1%. Calculate the expected and the actual real rates of return on the Silver Bonds.
parts.modelAnswer: Expected real rate of return = 4.5% - 4.5% = 0%. Actual real rate of return = 4% - (-1%) = 5%.

questions.stem: Inflation is a concern in the US. Different causes of inflation have been suggested, including rising crude oil prices, expansionary monetary policy, and high import tariffs.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Apart from adjusting the discount rate, two other strategies have been suggested to address the problem of inflation in the US. With reference to Sources A to E and your own knowledge in Economics, discuss the effects of EACH strategy on the US economy in terms of price level, equity, and trade balance.
parts.modelAnswer:
Strategy 1, raising the salaries tax rate for the high-income group, reduces their disposable income, consumption and aggregate demand, so the price level may fall. It may also weaken work incentives, reduce labour supply and SRAS/LRAS, pushing the price level up. It improves equity because after-tax income of high-income earners falls while low-income earners are not directly affected. The trade balance may improve because lower disposable income reduces imports, and lower domestic prices can raise exports and lower imports.

Strategy 2, cancelling tariffs on Chinese imports, lowers imported input prices and production costs, increasing SRAS and lowering the price level. It also lowers imported consumer-goods prices, increases imports, reduces net exports and aggregate demand, lowering the price level. It improves equity because the fall in prices of imported goods represents a larger share of income for low-income households. Its trade-balance effect is ambiguous: imports from China may rise and worsen the trade balance, but lower input costs may reduce US product prices, raise exports and reduce imports, improving the trade balance. Award effective communication for well-supported, coherent use of sources and economic theory.
markingPoints: Strategy 1: lower disposable income reduces consumption, AD and price level.
Strategy 1: possible disincentive effect lowers labour supply and SRAS/LRAS, raising price level.
Strategy 1: may improve trade balance through lower imports and/or more competitive exports.
Strategy 2: lower imported input prices reduce production cost, increase SRAS and lower price level.
Strategy 2: lower imported consumer-goods prices may increase imports, reduce net exports and AD, lowering price level.
Strategy 2: may improve equity because imported goods prices fall by a larger proportion of low-income households' income.
Strategy 2: trade balance may worsen through higher imports or improve through lower US production cost and stronger exports.
Effective communication: uses sources and theories with logical presentation.

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(II)
questions.keyPoint: 收入均等化
questions.stem: 通脹是美國的關注事項。人們對通脹成因有不同見解，包括原油價格上升、擴張性貨幣政策，以及高額進口關稅。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 除調整貼現率外，有人建議另外兩項美國應付通脹的策略。參考資料 A 至資料 E，並就你對經濟學的認識，分別討論上述兩項策略對美國經濟在物價水平、公平及貿易差額方面的影響。
parts.modelAnswer:
策略 1 提高高收入人士的薪俸稅稅率，會令其可支配收入下降，消費及總需求下降，物價水平可能下跌。它亦可能削弱工作誘因，令勞力供應下降，SRAS/LRAS 下降，推高物價水平。公平方面，高收入人士稅後收入下降而低收入人士未直接受影響，有助收入均等化。貿易差額方面，可支配收入下降令進口減少，或國內價格下跌令出口增加及進口減少，故貿易差額可能改善。

策略 2 取消中國進口關稅，會降低進口原料價格及生產成本，增加 SRAS，令物價水平下降。進口消費品價格下降亦會增加進口，減少淨出口及總需求，令物價水平下降。公平方面，進口貨價格下降佔低收入住戶收入較大比例，故有助實質收入均等化。貿易差額方面，從中國進口量上升或令貿易差額惡化；但生產成本下降令美國產品相對便宜，出口增加及進口減少，亦可能改善貿易差額。有效傳意分數取決於能否有組織地運用資料及經濟理論。
markingPoints: 策略 1：可支配收入下降，消費、AD 及物價下降。
策略 1：可能削弱工作誘因，勞力供應及 SRAS/LRAS 下降，物價上升。
策略 1：有助稅後收入均等化。
策略 1：可能因進口減少或出口較具競爭力而改善貿易差額。
策略 2：進口原料價格下降，成本下降，SRAS 上升，物價下降。
策略 2：進口消費品價格下降可令進口增加、淨出口及 AD 下降，物價下降。
策略 2：進口貨價格下降對低收入住戶比例較大，有助公平。
策略 2：貿易差額可因進口增加而惡化，或因成本下降及出口增加而改善。
有效傳意：有邏輯地運用資料及經濟理論。

questions.stem: Mary was the major shareholder of a private limited company which operated a restaurant chain. She planned to change the form of business ownership to a listed company.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: After opening some new restaurants, Mary found that the average cost of production of her company had increased. Explain the change in average cost with ONE reason.
parts.modelAnswer: Average cost may have increased because the firm became too large in scale, causing managerial efficiency to decline. Alternatively, the market may have become saturated and raised marketing costs, or the firm may have large outstanding loans so marginal borrowing cost rises.
markingPoints: The firm may have become too large, so managerial efficiency declines.
Market saturation may raise marketing cost.
Outstanding loans may raise the marginal cost of further borrowing.

questions.keyPoint: Concepts of demand
questions.stem: There are two kinds of food deliverers: 'riders' delivering food by self-provided motorbikes and 'walkers' delivering food on foot.

parts.label: Q2
parts.prompt: Why do riders usually have a higher income per order than walkers? Suggest ONE demand-side factor and ONE supply-side factor to explain your answer.
parts.modelAnswer: Demand for riders may be larger because riders can serve a larger area or deliver food in a shorter time. Supply of riders may be smaller because riding a motorbike requires a licence or involves higher production costs such as gasoline and depreciation. Higher demand and lower supply explain the higher income per order.
markingPoints: Demand-side: riders can serve a larger area or deliver in a shorter time.
Supply-side: supply of riders is smaller due to licence requirements or higher costs.
Links larger demand and/or smaller supply to higher income per order.

questions.stem: Country B and Country C are two large open economies. Facing a huge visible trade deficit, Country B imposes a per-unit tariff on goods imported from Country C. Suppose Country B's demand for goods imported from Country C is elastic.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: With the aid of Figure 1, explain how the tariff would affect the total expenditure of Country B on goods imported from Country C.
parts.modelAnswer: The tariff decreases the supply of imported goods and raises their price. Since import demand is elastic, the percentage decrease in quantity demanded is greater than the percentage increase in price, so total expenditure on imports falls. The diagram should show a leftward shift of supply and Area(+) smaller than Area(-).
markingPoints: Tariff decreases the supply of imported goods.
Demand for imported goods is elastic.
Percentage decrease in quantity is larger than percentage increase in price.
Diagram shows a leftward supply shift.

questions.stem: Country B and Country C are two large open economies. Facing a huge visible trade deficit, Country B imposes a per-unit tariff on goods imported from Country C. Suppose Country B's demand for goods imported from Country C is elastic.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 'Devaluation of a country's currency against its trading partners may have the same effect on imports as tariff.' Use Country B as an example to justify this statement.
parts.modelAnswer: If Country B's currency is devalued against Country C's currency, the price of imports from Country C in terms of Country B's currency rises. This reduces import volume. Since import demand is elastic, total import expenditure falls, like the tariff case in part (a).
markingPoints: Devaluation raises import prices in terms of Country B's currency.

questions.stem: Country B and Country C are two large open economies. Facing a huge visible trade deficit, Country B imposes a per-unit tariff on goods imported from Country C. Suppose Country B's demand for goods imported from Country C is elastic.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Apart from the effect on the country's visible trade balance, explain ONE other effect of devaluation on its balance of payments.
parts.modelAnswer: Export of services may rise because devaluation makes local goods and services cheaper in terms of foreign currency, attracting more tourists to visit and spend. questions.keyPoint: Four basic principles of taxation
questions.stem: Country D introduced a short-term capital gains tax (STCGT) on property market. STCGT is a tax on capital gains from the sale of a property held for less than 1 year. A spokesman of the tax department said that a new computer system had been developed for STCGT. Although the system cost more than 1 billion dollars, it allowed taxpayers to check and pay the amount of STCGT online easily.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Evaluate the new tax in terms of TWO principles of taxation put forward by Adam Smith.
parts.modelAnswer: Convenience is consistent because online payment can be made easily. Equality is inconsistent because people with higher capital gains are subject to higher tax rates. Certainty is consistent because, once the transaction price and holding period are recorded, the amount of STCGT can be calculated with certainty. Economy is inconsistent because developing the new computer system was costly.
markingPoints: Convenience: consistent, online payment can be made easily.
Equality: inconsistent, higher capital gains face higher tax rates.
Certainty: consistent, amount can be calculated with certainty once price and holding period are known.
Economy: inconsistent, development cost was huge.
Mark the first two principles only.

questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 'Deflation will occur if the amount of goods and services produced is growing faster than money supply.' Explain this statement in terms of the quantity theory of money.
parts.modelAnswer: Quantity Theory of Money: MV = PY, where M is money supply, V is velocity of circulation, P is the price level and Y is real output. Assuming V is constant, if the percentage increase in Y is larger than the percentage increase in M, P falls. Therefore deflation occurs.
markingPoints: Defines M, V, P and Y.
If output grows faster than money supply, price level falls and deflation occurs.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 'If deflation is expected, the real interest rate will be higher than the nominal interest rate.' Why?
parts.modelAnswer: Nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate. Rearranging gives real interest rate = nominal interest rate - expected inflation rate. Expected deflation means expected inflation is negative, so the real interest rate is higher than the nominal interest rate.
markingPoints: Uses nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate.
Expected deflation means expected inflation is negative, making real interest rate higher than nominal interest rate.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: In a two-country-two-good model, the outputs per unit of resources of both countries are as follows.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Assume the terms of trade are that 1 unit of rice can be exchanged for 2.2 units of toys. Calculate the gains from trade of EACH country when trading 1 unit of rice. Show your workings.
parts.modelAnswer: Opportunity cost of producing 1 unit of rice is 2 toys in Country E and 3 toys in Country F. Country E exports rice and Country F imports rice. Country E gains 2.2 - 2 = 0.2 toys; Country F gains 3 - 2.2 = 0.8 toys.
markingPoints: OC of 1 rice in Country E = 2 toys.
OC of 1 rice in Country F = 3 toys.

questions.stem: In a two-country-two-good model, the outputs per unit of resources of both countries are as follows.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: With reference to your answer in part (a), defend the following statement: 'There is still a basis for trade even if a country has no absolute advantage in producing any goods.'
parts.modelAnswer: Country F has no absolute advantage in producing either good, but it has a comparative advantage in toys. As shown in part (a), Country F can still gain 0.8 toys per unit of rice traded by exporting toys in exchange for rice from Country E.
markingPoints: Country F has no absolute advantage but has comparative advantage in toys.
Country F can still enjoy gains from trade.

parts.modelAnswer: Original money supply = deposits + cash = 4 000 + 1 000 = $5 000 million. New deposits = (1 000 + 600) x 1 / 25% = $6 400 million. New money supply = 6 400 + 400 = $6 800 million. Change in money supply = 6 800 - 5 000 = $1 800 million.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning and examples of the three types of production; identify the type of production
questions.stem: The Mainland government introduced the Targeted Poverty Alleviation Campaign in 2014. After analysing the situations of people living in poverty, the government officials came up with tailor-made measures. Example 1: A village in Yunnan province has beautiful natural landscape. The government of Yunnan province promoted the village to attract more travellers. Apart from farming, the villagers also set up hostels to serve travellers in order to earn more income. Example 2: The government provided funding and invited private firms to develop hydroelectric power plants in six provinces such as Hubei and Jiangxi. Such development would help improve transportation, irrigation and flood prevention in the rural villages in these provinces.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: Refer to Example 1. In which types of production did the villagers engage after the introduction of the campaign? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: They engaged in primary production as farmers because they directly extract resources from nature. They also engaged in tertiary production as hostel owners because they provide catering and accommodation services to visitors.
markingPoints: Primary production: as farmers, they directly extract resources from nature.
Tertiary production: as hostel owners, they provide catering and accommodation services to visitors.

questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: The Olympic Games attract billions of international television viewers to watch the competitions among thousands of top athletes. Athletes compete in the Olympic Games with their support teams consisting of sport psychologists, physical therapists, nutritionists, etc. Some professional athletes receive a monthly salary and share a proportion of the prize money whenever they win in competitions. Whenever an athlete wins a gold medal in a certain sport, more people will start learning the sport. As a result, there will soon be long queues registering for courses in the sport. Professional athletes usually start their full-time training before graduating from secondary school and have to give up their studies.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Some restaurants in shopping malls find their businesses increase sharply when the malls broadcast Olympic events. Explain how the broadcast of Olympic events may result in a divergence between private and social benefits.
parts.modelAnswer: The broadcast attracts more customers and brings more business to restaurants. If restaurants do not compensate the shopping malls for the benefit, a positive externality exists. Marginal social benefit from the broadcast exceeds marginal private benefit.
markingPoints: Broadcast attracts customers and benefits restaurants.
Restaurants do not compensate the shopping malls.

parts.label: (b)

parts.modelAnswer: A market solution may involve restaurants paying the malls to broadcast more Olympic events, increasing the number of broadcasts towards the efficient level.

Broadcast quantity moves towards the efficient level.

questions.keyPoint: Classification of public expenditure
questions.stem: The Government launched the Consumption Voucher Scheme in 2021 to relieve the impact of COVID-19 on the Hong Kong economy.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Suppose the Government plans to spend another sum of money to cope with the pandemic. Scheme C distributes the sum using the same mechanism as the existing Consumption Voucher Scheme. Scheme H spends the sum on building new hospitals and hiring additional medical staff. With reference to the sources and your own knowledge in Economics, discuss which scheme the Government will prefer for EACH policy objective: (1) to relieve unemployment in an industry severely affected by the pandemic; (2) to increase average labour productivity; (3) to increase aggregate output in the short run and/or long run.
parts.modelAnswer:
For relieving unemployment in a severely affected industry, Scheme C is likely preferred because it directly stimulates spending in retail, accommodation and food services, where unemployment rose more seriously. Scheme H relieves unemployment mainly in construction and medical services.

For average labour productivity, Scheme C may improve workflow through wider use of stored value facilities, but it may also only boost consumption with little direct supply-side effect. Scheme H may raise future productivity by improving public health and workers' health. The preferred scheme depends on whether immediate workflow gains or longer-run health-related productivity is emphasised.

For aggregate output, Scheme C raises private consumption and AD in the short run, especially if promotions induce spending beyond $5 000. Scheme H raises government consumption and/or investment and AD in the short run, and may also increase LRAS in the long run through better infrastructure and health. Either scheme can be preferred if the comparison is consistent with the stated objective and supported by sources and economic theory.
markingPoints: Scheme C helps retail, accommodation and food services unemployment; Scheme H helps construction and medical sectors.

questions.stem: D 國對物業市場開徵一項短期資產增值稅（STCGT）。STCGT 是對出售持有少於一年的物業所得的資產增值徵稅。稅務部發言人表示他們為 STCGT 開發了新的電腦系統。雖然該系統耗資超過十億元，但可讓納稅人在網上輕鬆查閱稅款金額並繳付稅款。

questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹與貨幣數量論
questions.keyPoint: 貨幣數量論的意思

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 「若物品和服務的生產數量增長比貨幣供應快，便會出現通縮。」依據貨幣數量理論解釋這陳述。
parts.modelAnswer: 貨幣數量理論為 MV = PY，M 是貨幣供應，V 是貨幣流通速度，P 是物價水平，Y 是實質產出。假設 V 維持不變，若 Y 的增長率大於 M 的增長率，P 便會下跌，即通縮出現。
markingPoints: 產出增長快於貨幣供應時，物價水平下跌而出現通縮。

questions.topicGroup: 名義利率及實質利率的關係
questions.keyPoint: 了解方程式：名義利率 = 實質利率 + 預期通脹率

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 「若人們預期通縮出現，實質利率會高於名義利率。」為什麼？
parts.modelAnswer: 名義利率 = 實質利率 + 預期通脹率，所以實質利率 = 名義利率 - 預期通脹率。預期通縮代表預期通脹率為負值，因此實質利率會高於名義利率。
markingPoints: 運用名義利率 = 實質利率 + 預期通脹率。
預期通縮令預期通脹率為負值，所以實質利率高於名義利率。

parts.modelAnswer: 村民作為農夫，直接從自然界獲取資源，涉及初級生產。他們作為旅館東主，向遊客提供膳食和住宿服務，涉及三級生產。
markingPoints: 初級生產：作為農夫，直接從自然界獲取資源。
三級生產：作為旅館東主，向遊客提供膳食和住宿服務。

questions.keyPoint: 勞力的流動性
questions.stem: 在 2014 年，內地政府推行精準扶貧政策。在分析貧窮人士的情況後，政府官員會提出度身訂造的措施。例子一：雲南省的某村莊擁有優美的自然地貌。雲南省政府宣傳該村莊以吸引更多遊客。村民除了耕作外，也開設旅館招待遊客以賺取更高收入。例子二：政府在六個省份（如湖北及江西）提供資金並邀請私人廠商發展水力發電廠。該發展會幫助這些省份的鄉郊村落改善交通、灌溉和防洪。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 解釋村民的勞工流動性會如何受到影響。
parts.modelAnswer: 村民的職業流動性會增加，因為他們從事新的職業，成為旅館東主。
markingPoints: 村民從事新職業，成為旅館東主。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 參考例子二。以圖輔助，解釋該六個省份的總產出在長期會如何受到影響。
parts.modelAnswer: 較佳基建會令產能及潛在產出上升，因此長期總供應上升。更多基建投資亦令總需求上升。AD 及 LRAS 均向右移，長期總產出上升。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 正面界外效應與經濟無效率；矯正界外效應
questions.stem: 奧運會吸引數以十億計的國際電視觀眾觀看數以千計頂尖運動員的競賽。運動員出戰奧運會時，他們的支援隊伍包括運動心理學家、物理治療師、營養師等。一些專業運動員收取月薪，並可獲分發贏取比賽所得獎金的一部分。每當有運動員在某項運動獲得金牌，更多人會開始學習該項運動，相關課程很快出現報名人龍。專業運動員通常在中學畢業前便須放棄學業，投入全職訓練。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 當購物商場播放奧運賽事，商場裏一些餐廳的生意大幅增長。解釋播放奧運賽事如何可能引致私人得益與社會得益出現分歧。
parts.modelAnswer: 播放奧運賽事吸引顧客，令餐廳生意增加。若餐廳沒有向商場作出補償，便存在正面外部性，播放賽事的邊際社會得益大於邊際私人得益。
markingPoints: 播放賽事吸引顧客並令餐廳受益。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 假設 (a) 部的分歧確實存在。市場機制如何可以有助減低該分歧？
parts.modelAnswer: 餐廳可付款予商場，要求商場播放更多奧運賽事，使播放數量增加並接近效率水平。
markingPoints: 餐廳付款予商場播放更多賽事。
播放數量接近效率水平。

parts.modelAnswer: 課程需求上升。若價格未能足夠快地調整，價格會低於新的市場清銷價格，因此出現超額需求或短缺，即人龍。圖中應顯示需求曲線向右移及短缺。

parts.label: (f)
parts.prompt: 若專業運動員的平均收入上升，投身專業運動員的機會成本會受影響嗎？試加解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 不會。平均收入上升會提高成為全職專業運動員這個選項的價值，但機會成本是放棄選項中最高價值者，並不因此受影響。
markingPoints: 收入上升提高所選選項價值，但機會成本是放棄選項中最高價值者。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業

questions.stem: 政府在 2021 年推行消費券計劃以舒緩新冠肺炎對本港經濟的衝擊。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: 參考資料 A。本港經濟最有可能在經濟周期的哪個階段？除了失業率的改變，列出該階段的另一個經濟現象。
parts.modelAnswer: 最有可能處於衰退階段。其他經濟現象包括實質 GDP 增長下跌甚至負增長、低或下跌的通脹率甚至通縮、商業信心及投資下降，或消費水平下降。

markingPoints: 在家工作及感染風險令零售和餐飲勞工需求下降。

questions.keyPoint: 公共支出的分類
questions.stem: 政府在 2021 年推行消費券計劃以舒緩新冠肺炎對本港經濟的衝擊。

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: 假設政府計劃花費另一筆錢去應對疫情。計劃 C 使用與現行消費券計劃相同的機制發放該筆錢；計劃 H 把該筆錢用於興建新醫院及聘請額外醫療人員。參考以上資料並就你對經濟學的認識，分別討論政府為求達成以下每項政策目標時會偏好哪個計劃：目標 1 舒緩一個受疫情嚴重影響的行業的失業情況；目標 2 提高平均勞工生產力；目標 3 增加總產出（短期及 / 或長期）。
parts.modelAnswer:
就舒緩受疫情嚴重影響行業的失業而言，政府可能偏好計劃 C，因它直接刺激零售、款待及膳食服務業的消費，而該行業失業率上升較嚴重。計劃 H 則主要舒緩建造業及醫療界失業。

就提高平均勞工生產力而言，計劃 C 可能因廣泛使用儲值支付工具而改善工作流程，但亦可能只刺激消費，沒有直接供應面影響。計劃 H 可透過改善公共醫療及工人健康，在將來提高勞工生產力。偏好哪一個取決於重視即時流程改善還是長遠健康效益。

就增加總產出而言，計劃 C 會增加私人消費及總需求，尤其資料 E 顯示推廣可誘使消費者花費多於 $5 000。計劃 H 會增加政府消費及 / 或投資支出，短期提高總需求，亦可透過更佳基建及健康改善在長期提高 LRAS。只要比較能切合政策目標，並有資料及經濟理論支持，兩者皆可被偏好。
markingPoints: 計劃 C 可舒緩零售、款待及膳食服務業失業；計劃 H 可舒緩建造業及醫療界失業。
比較哪個計劃較切合目標 1。
計劃 C 可能透過儲值支付工具提高工作流程，或可能沒有直接供應面效應。
計劃 H 可透過改善健康 / 醫療服務提高生產力。
計劃 C 短期提高私人消費及 AD。
計劃 H 短期提高政府支出 / 投資及 AD。
計劃 H 可透過基建或健康在長期提高 LRAS。
有效傳意：運用資料、經濟理論，內容相關並有邏輯。

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The following is the advertisement of an online food delivery firm for recruiting riders.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: After employing more riders, the firm found that its system was overloaded and the marginal product of riders dropped. State the law that explains this phenomenon and briefly explain why such law can be applied in this case.
parts.modelAnswer: This is explained by the law of diminishing marginal returns. Holding technology constant, when more units of a variable factor are continuously added to a given amount of fixed factor, the marginal product of the variable factor eventually diminishes. In this case, riders are the variable factor and the firm's operating system is the fixed factor.
markingPoints: Identifies the law of diminishing marginal returns.
States that more variable factor is added to a fixed factor.
Marginal product eventually diminishes, holding technology constant.
The firm's operating system is the fixed factor.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Refer to the following taxi fare arrangement.

parts.label: Q2
parts.prompt: Suppose a late-night surcharge of $20 will be added to the original fare on any taxi trips from 1:00 am to 5:59 am. How will this surcharge affect the average travel distance of taxi passengers during late-night? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: The average travel distance would increase. Since the same $20 surcharge is added to both short-distance and long-distance trips, the price of long-distance trips relative to short-distance trips falls. The proportion of passengers taking long-distance trips would rise, so the average travel distance of late-night taxi passengers would increase.
markingPoints: The same surcharge is applied to short and long trips.
Long-distance trips become cheaper relative to short-distance trips.
The proportion of long-distance trips rises.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem: In 1992, Cathay Pacific Airways acquired an air-catering company which was renamed as Cathay Pacific Catering Services (H.K.) Limited (CPCS). CPCS provided around thirty million meals for various airlines in 2019.

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt: From the viewpoint of Cathay Pacific Airways, name the type of the above integration and give TWO motives for this type of integration.
parts.modelAnswer: It is vertical backward integration. Possible motives include ensuring a steady supply of inputs, diversifying sources of income and spreading risks, and making use of its brand name in other products.
markingPoints: Motive: ensure a steady supply of raw materials/inputs.
Motive: diversify sources of income and spread risks.
Motive: make use of the brand name in other products.
Mark the first two motives only.

questions.keyPoint: Identify perfect competition and imperfect competition

parts.label: Q4
parts.prompt: Give TWO reasons to explain why the smartphone market is NOT perfectly competitive.
parts.modelAnswer: The smartphone market is not perfectly competitive because sellers provide heterogeneous products, such as phones with different specifications. There is also non-price competition, such as advertising, and market information about performance is imperfect.
markingPoints: Imperfect market information, e.g. performance information.
Mark the first two reasons only.

questions.stem: Mr Chan, a Hong Kong retired footballer, was employed as a consultant by a football club in the United Kingdom in January 2020. Seven months later, he quitted his position and returned to Hong Kong.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the salary received by Mr Chan from the football club in the United Kingdom would be included in the calculation of gross domestic product (GDP) in Hong Kong.
parts.modelAnswer: No. The salary was derived from production by a non-resident producing unit, the UK football club, outside Hong Kong.
markingPoints: The production was by a non-resident producing unit outside Hong Kong.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: Mr Chan, a Hong Kong retired footballer, was employed as a consultant by a football club in the United Kingdom in January 2020. Seven months later, he quitted his position and returned to Hong Kong.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the salary would be included in the calculation of gross national income (GNI) in Hong Kong.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. Mr Chan is a Hong Kong resident, so the salary received would be counted as factor income from abroad in Hong Kong's GNI.
markingPoints: Mr Chan is a Hong Kong resident.

questions.topicGroup: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.keyPoint: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.stem: Mr Chan, a Hong Kong retired footballer, was employed as a consultant by a football club in the United Kingdom in January 2020. Seven months later, he quitted his position and returned to Hong Kong.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If Mr Chan could choose to receive his salary in either British Pound (GBP) or US Dollar (USD), which currency would you recommend him to choose? Explain your answer.
parts.modelAnswer: USD can be recommended because the USD/HKD exchange rate, and hence the purchasing power of USD in Hong Kong, is more stable under the linked exchange rate system. This gives Mr Chan lower exchange-rate risk. GBP is also acceptable if the reason is that GBP is legal tender in the UK and can be used directly during his stay there.
markingPoints: USD: lower exchange-rate risk under the linked exchange rate system.
Or GBP: legal tender in the UK and directly usable there.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the required reserve ratio.
parts.modelAnswer: Required reserve ratio = (600 - 300) / 1 500 = 20%.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The following table shows the balance sheet of a banking system. Initially the banks hold excess reserves of $300 million and the public always holds $100 million cash.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Suppose the required reserve ratio is reduced by 5% and banks lend out all excess reserves. Calculate the new money supply after the credit creation/contraction. Show your workings.
parts.modelAnswer: Taking the reduction as a 5 percentage point cut, the new required reserve ratio is 20% - 5% = 15%. New deposits = 1 500 + (600 - 0.15 x 1 500) / 0.15 = $4 000 million. New money supply = 4 000 + 100 = $4 100 million. If the 5% reduction is treated as a relative reduction, the accepted alternative is RRR = 19%, deposits = $3 157.89 million and money supply = $3 257.89 million.
markingPoints: New required reserve ratio = 15% under a percentage point cut.
Accept the consistent alternative with RRR = 19% and money supply = $3 257.89 million.

questions.keyPoint: Qualities of good money
questions.stem: In a country, most of the prisoners in a correctional institution use cigarettes as a medium of exchange, but citizens in society refuse to settle payment by using cigarettes.

parts.label: Q7
parts.prompt: Apart from not being generally acceptable, explain with TWO reasons why cigarettes are NOT a good form of money in society.
parts.modelAnswer: Cigarettes are not durable because they can be easily damaged and cannot be stored for a long time. They are not homogeneous because different cigarettes do not have uniform physical characteristics. They are also not portable for high-value transactions and not divisible without reducing total value.
markingPoints: Not divisible without losing total value.
Mark the first two reasons only.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: Suppose the outputs per unit of resources of Country A and Country B are as follows.

parts.label: Q8
parts.prompt: Find the range of terms of trade over which exchange between these two countries is mutually beneficial. Show your workings.
parts.modelAnswer: Country A's opportunity cost of producing 1 unit of wheat is 10 / 4 = 2.5 units of rice. Country B's opportunity cost of producing 1 unit of wheat is 6 / 3 = 2 units of rice. Therefore mutually beneficial trade requires 2R < 1W < 2.5R. Equivalently, 0.4W < 1R < 0.5W.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Wearing surgical mask can reduce the chance of contracting diseases for an individual and can prevent spreading diseases to others as well. In terms of externality, explain how the subsidy could improve economic efficiency.
parts.modelAnswer: Wearing masks creates external benefits because it protects others from infection, but the mask wearer is not compensated by those who benefit. Therefore masks are under-consumed relative to the efficient level. A subsidy lowers the marginal private cost of wearing masks, increases consumption towards the efficient level, and narrows the gap between marginal social benefit and marginal social cost.
markingPoints: Marginal social benefit exceeds marginal private benefit / under-consumption occurs.

parts.prompt: Define deflationary (output) gap and show the gap in Figure 2.
parts.modelAnswer: A deflationary output gap is the difference between aggregate output Y and full-employment output Yf when Y is below Yf. The diagram should mark the horizontal gap between short-run equilibrium output and Yf.
markingPoints: Defines deflationary gap as Yf - Y when Y < Yf.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A natural disaster has struck Country F. A large number of factories have closed down temporarily. Many people have lost their jobs and become pessimistic about their future. With the aid of Figure 2, explain why the natural disaster would lead to a wider deflationary (output) gap in Country F.
parts.modelAnswer: The temporary closure of factories reduces short-run aggregate supply. Loss of jobs and pessimism lower consumption and possibly investment expenditure, so aggregate demand decreases. With SRAS and AD both shifting left, aggregate output falls. Assuming LRAS and full-employment output remain unchanged, the fall in output widens the deflationary output gap.
markingPoints: Loss of jobs/pessimism reduce consumption and possibly investment.
Assuming LRAS/Yf unchanged, the deflationary gap widens.
Diagram shows leftward AD shift and wider gap.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: There exists a deflationary (output) gap in Country F.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Without using a diagram, explain how the central bank of Country F could use an open market operation to narrow the deflationary (output) gap.
parts.modelAnswer: The central bank could conduct an open-market purchase by buying government bonds from the public. This increases money supply and lowers the interest rate, inducing firms to invest more. Aggregate demand and short-run aggregate output rise while long-run output is unchanged, so the deflationary output gap narrows.
markingPoints: Money supply increases and interest rate falls.
Short-run output rises while long-run output is unchanged, narrowing the gap.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.stem: The declining labour force would be one of the problems of Hong Kong in the future.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Suppose the Government has two strategies to address the problem of declining labour force. Strategy I: Providing extra childcare service and cash to parents in order to increase the birth rate. Strategy II: Expanding the existing schemes in order to import more workers. With reference to Sources A-D and your own knowledge in Economics, discuss the effects of each strategy on aggregate output, government expenditure and average labour productivity in order to evaluate the two strategies.
parts.modelAnswer:
For aggregate output, Strategy I has uncertain short-run effects: cash may lead some parents to work less or quit to care for children, reducing labour force and SRAS, while childcare services may help other parents re-enter work, increasing labour force and SRAS. In the long run, children grow up and join the labour force, increasing LRAS and aggregate output. Strategy II raises labour supply immediately, increasing both SRAS and LRAS, so aggregate output rises in the short and long run.

For government expenditure, Strategy I increases government consumption expenditure on childcare and transfer payments to parents in the short run. In the long run, a larger population may raise demand for education and public medical services, although adult children may reduce future elderly welfare needs. Strategy II may require extra administrative expenditure to process applications, but this is likely small.

For average labour productivity, Strategy I has little short-run effect because newborns are not in the labour force. In the long run, productivity depends on education and training of the new generation. If family resources per child fall, productivity may fall unless the government invests more in education. Strategy II's effect depends on the skill mix of imported workers. Source D shows a much larger number of higher-skilled imported professionals than lower-skilled workers under SLS, so average labour productivity may rise if the proportion of high-skilled imported workers is high.

Overall, Strategy II is better for raising output quickly and may have a smaller effect on government expenditure; Strategy I may provide a more stable local labour supply in the long run if supported by education and childcare.
markingPoints: Uses sources and economic theory with logical presentation.
Strategy I short-run aggregate output effect is uncertain.
Strategy I long-run aggregate output rises when children join the labour force.
Strategy II raises SRAS/LRAS and aggregate output in short and long run.
Strategy I raises childcare expenditure and transfer payments.
Strategy I may raise long-run education/medical expenditure.
Strategy II has relatively small administrative costs.
Strategy I short-run labour productivity effect is limited.
Strategy I long-run productivity depends on education/training and resources per child.
Strategy II productivity effect depends on the high-skilled/low-skilled mix.
Provides evaluation comparing the two strategies.

parts.modelAnswer: 若把下調 5% 理解為下調 5 個百分點，新法定儲備比率 = 20% - 5% = 15%。新存款額 = 1 500 + (600 - 0.15 x 1 500) / 0.15 = 4 000 百萬元。新貨幣供應 = 4 000 + 100 = 4 100 百萬元。若把 5% 理解為百分比下調，亦接受新法定儲備比率 = 19%、新存款額 = 3 157.89 百萬元及新貨幣供應 = 3 257.89 百萬元的答案。
markingPoints: 新法定儲備比率 = 15%（百分點下調）。

questions.stem: 在某國，懲教所的大部分囚犯都使用香煙作為交易媒介，但社會大眾拒絕用香煙結算支付。

parts.modelAnswer: 香煙並不耐用，因為容易損壞，不能長時間儲藏。香煙亦並非同質，因為不同香煙的實物特徵不完全相同。它們亦不便攜帶，因高價值交易需大量香煙；也不可分割，因分割後總值會下降。

questions.stem: 假設甲、乙兩國每單位資源的產出如下。

parts.label: Q8
parts.prompt: 找出能令兩國在交易中互利的貿易比率範圍。列示你的計算。
parts.modelAnswer: 甲國生產 1W 的機會成本 = 10 / 4 = 2.5R；乙國生產 1W 的機會成本 = 6 / 3 = 2R。因此互利貿易比率範圍為 2R < 1W < 2.5R。等同地，0.4W < 1R < 0.5W。

questions.topicGroup: 影響短期總供應的因素
questions.keyPoint: 影響短期總供應的因素
questions.stem: 勞動人口下降是香港將來要面對的問題之一。

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: 假設政府有兩項策略以應對勞動人口下降的問題。策略 I：向家長提供額外托兒服務和發放額外現金，以提高出生率。策略 II：擴大現有的計劃以輸入更多勞工。參考資料 A-D，並就你對經濟科的認識，討論每項策略對總產出、政府支出及平均勞工生產力的影響，以評價該兩項策略。
parts.modelAnswer:
就總產出而言，策略 I 在短期的影響未能確定：額外現金可能令部分家長減少工作或辭職照顧孩子，令勞動人口和短期總供應下降；但額外托兒服務可令部分家長重投勞工市場，令勞動人口和短期總供應上升。長期而言，小孩長大後加入勞動人口，LRAS 和總產出會上升。策略 II 可即時增加勞力供應，令 SRAS 和 LRAS 上升，短期及長期總產出均上升。

就政府支出而言，策略 I 在短期會增加政府消費支出（托兒服務）及轉移支付（現金）。長期人口增加可能提高教育和公共醫療需求，但子女長大後亦可能照顧父母，減少長者福利需要。策略 II 可能需要增加行政人員處理申請，但相對其他支出並不顯著。

就平均勞工生產力而言，策略 I 在短期影響有限，因新生嬰兒未加入勞動人口。長期則取決於新一代的教育和培訓；若家庭資源有限，子女數量增加會令每名子女得到的資源減少，生產力或會下降，除非政府增加教育投資。策略 II 的影響取決於輸入高技術與低技術工人的比例。資料 D 顯示輸入專才人數遠高於 SLS 低技術工人，如高技術工人比例較高，平均勞工生產力可上升。

整體而言，策略 II 較能在短期提高產出，且對政府支出影響可能較小；策略 I 若配合教育及托兒支援，長遠可提供較穩定的本地勞力供應。
markingPoints: 運用資料及經濟理論，答案有邏輯。
策略 I 對短期總產出的影響未能確定。
策略 I 長期可因兒童加入勞動人口而提高總產出。
策略 II 在短期及長期提高 SRAS / LRAS 和總產出。
策略 I 增加托兒服務支出及轉移支付。
策略 I 長期可能增加教育 / 醫療支出。
策略 II 行政成本相對較小。
策略 I 短期對勞工生產力影響有限。
策略 I 長期生產力取決於教育、培訓及每名子女可得資源。
策略 II 生產力影響取決於高技術和低技術工人比例。

questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: Traffic congestion in the cross harbour tunnels during peak hours is a serious problem in Hong Kong.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Suppose there are two cross-harbour-tunnel-toll adjustment proposals to relieve the problem of congestion: Proposal I the government raises the toll of the CHT for private cars to $75; Proposal II the toll of the WHC for private cars is reduced to $20. Discuss which proposal each of the following groups of stakeholders would prefer: the owners of the WHC company; the politicians who are concerned about the income inequality in Hong Kong; the government economists who are concerned about government revenue and/or expenditure; ONE other group of stakeholders.
parts.modelAnswer: The WHC company would prefer Proposal I because a higher CHT toll would shift demand towards WHC. Politicians concerned about inequality may prefer Proposal II if they view tunnel tolls as regressive, though Proposal I can also be defended if private cars are mainly used by richer people. Government economists would likely prefer Proposal I because it can raise revenue. Another group such as taxi drivers or environmentalists would also tend to prefer Proposal I because congestion and pollution would fall.
markingPoints: Inequality concerns may support Proposal II or Proposal I depending on the argument.
Government revenue concerns support Proposal I.
Another group such as taxi drivers or environmentalists prefers Proposal I.

questions.keyPoint: Determine the profit-maximising output and price graphically and numerically
questions.stem: ABC Electricity Limited, the sole supplier of electricity in Country A, adopts uniform pricing.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: If the marginal cost is constant, explain how the profit-maximising output of ABC Electricity Limited will be determined. Indicate the output (Qm), the price (Pm) and the deadweight loss in Figure 2.
parts.modelAnswer: The profit-maximising output is determined by MR = MC. The firm chooses Qm where MR intersects MC, then charges Pm on the demand curve. The deadweight loss is the triangle between demand and MC beyond Qm.
markingPoints: Qm is where MR intersects MC.
Pm is on the demand curve above Qm.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: 假設現有以下兩項調整過海隧道收費的建議以舒緩擠塞問題：建議 I 政府將紅隧對私家車的收費提高至 $75；建議 II 將西隧對私家車的收費減低至 $20。參考以上各項資料並就你對經濟學的認識，討論以下每組持份者會偏好哪項建議：西隧公司的擁有者；關注本港市民收入不均的政客；關注政府收入及／或支出的政府經濟師；另外一組持份者。
parts.modelAnswer: 西隧公司會偏好建議 I，因為紅隧收費上升會把需求轉向西隧。關注收入不均的政客可按不同論點支持建議 II 或建議 I，但若把過海隧道費看成累退性負擔，建議 II 會較有利。關注政府收入的經濟師多半偏好建議 I，因為可帶來更多收入。其他持份者如的士司機或環保人士亦傾向建議 I，因為擠塞及污染會減少。
markingPoints: 西隧公司偏好建議 I。
收入不均論點可支持建議 II 或建議 I。
政府收入角度偏好建議 I。
其他持份者如的士司機或環保人士偏好建議 I。

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: A country considers acquiring more land by reclamation for building residential flats.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the opportunity cost of land reclamation will change if the maximum height of buildings on the reclaimed land is limited to two storeys for technical reasons.
parts.modelAnswer: The opportunity cost remains unchanged. The height limit reduces the value of the reclaimed land but does not change the highest-valued alternative forgone.
markingPoints: States that opportunity cost remains unchanged.
Explains that the highest-valued alternative forgone is unchanged.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: A country considers acquiring more land by reclamation for building residential flats.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the opportunity cost of land reclamation will change if there is a shortage of reclamation materials.
parts.modelAnswer: The opportunity cost increases because extra resources must be used to compete for scarce raw materials; both money and non-money cost rise.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem: Li Ka Shing Foundation offered an unconditional cash gift of $5 000 to each 2018 HKDSE candidate living in Yuen Long, Tuen Mun and Islands districts under the project 'Decide Well, Spend Wisely'.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Statement A: The project can improve the public examination results of candidates in those districts. Explain whether Statement A is a positive statement.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. It is a positive statement because it can be tested and refuted by facts.
markingPoints: Identifies it as a positive statement.
Explains that it is refutable by facts.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: Li Ka Shing Foundation offered an unconditional cash gift of $5 000 to each 2018 HKDSE candidate living in Yuen Long, Tuen Mun and Islands districts under the project 'Decide Well, Spend Wisely'.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Statement B: The project can improve equity in Hong Kong. Justify the statement.
parts.modelAnswer: The districts have lower average household income, so the cash gift narrows income inequality. It can also equalise opportunities by helping students from poorer backgrounds pursue higher education.

questions.topicGroup: Meaning of public ownership and examples of organisations or institutions in operating under public ownership
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of public ownership and examples of organisations or institutions in operating under public ownership

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt: Give ONE example of a public corporation in Hong Kong. With reference to the example, state TWO advantages of providing the service through a public corporation instead of a private enterprise.
parts.modelAnswer: Examples include the Airport Authority or Hong Kong Export Credit Insurance Corporation. A public corporation can obtain public information more easily, provide stable service at a lower price, and obtain government backing.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: Getting vaccinated is an effective way to prevent infection and protect oneself from flu viruses.

parts.label: Q4
parts.prompt: Using the concept of externality, explain why a government subsidy on seasonal influenza vaccination may improve economic efficiency.
parts.modelAnswer: Vaccination benefits other people by lowering their chance of infection, but the vaccinated person is not compensated. Marginal social benefit exceeds marginal private benefit and vaccination is under-consumed. A subsidy increases vaccination towards the efficient level.
markingPoints: Explains how subsidy raises consumption towards the efficient level.

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem: Wong's family and Chan's family live next door to each other.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Mr Wong teaches the children from both families English while Mrs Chan teaches them Japanese. State ONE economic concept involved and explain why this arrangement benefits both families.
parts.modelAnswer: It illustrates division of labour or comparative advantage. Each parent specialises in the subject that can be taught at lower opportunity cost, so both families receive better language teaching.
markingPoints: States division of labour or comparative advantage.
Explains specialisation or lower opportunity cost.

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: Wong's family and Chan's family live next door to each other.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: On Christmas Eve, the two families buy food ingredients and cook together instead of buying and cooking separately. State ONE economic concept involved and explain why the arrangement benefits both families.
parts.modelAnswer: It illustrates economies of scale. Bulk purchases may obtain discounts and joint cooking saves time while offering more food variety.
markingPoints: Explains a valid benefit of joint production.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate excess reserves, required and actual reserve ratios
questions.stem: The balance sheet of a banking system shows reserves of $300 million and deposits of $1 000 million. The legal reserve ratio is 20%.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the excess reserves of the banking system.
parts.modelAnswer: Excess reserves = $300 million - ($1 000 million x 20%) = $100 million.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The balance sheet of a banking system shows reserves of $300 million and deposits of $1 000 million. The legal reserve ratio is 20% and the public initially holds $200 million cash.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Suppose the public no longer holds cash and all banks lend out all excess reserves. Calculate the maximum possible change in money supply. Show your workings.
parts.modelAnswer: Old money supply is $1 200 million. New money supply is ($300 million + $200 million) x 1/20% = $2 500 million. The maximum possible increase is $1 300 million.
markingPoints: Finds new money supply using the multiplier.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has an absolute advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: Country A has twice the resources of Country B. Both allocate half of their resources to cars and half to toys. The total outputs are shown below.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain whether Country B has an absolute advantage in producing cars.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. With the same resources as Country A, Country B would produce 200 cars, more than Country A's 100 cars.
markingPoints: Compares output with the same resources.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: Country A has twice the resources of Country B. Both allocate half of their resources to cars and half to toys. The total outputs are shown below.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain whether Country B has a comparative advantage in producing cars.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. The opportunity cost of one car is one toy in Country A but only 0.6 toy in Country B, so Country B has the comparative advantage in cars.
markingPoints: Calculates Country B's opportunity cost and compares.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: Country A has twice the resources of Country B. Both allocate half of their resources to cars and half to toys. The total outputs are shown below.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The exchange ratio is 5 cars for 4 toys. Calculate the gain from trade for the car-importing country when it imports 10 cars. Show your workings.
parts.modelAnswer: The terms of trade are 1 car for 0.8 toy. The car-importing country saves 0.2 toy per car, so the total gain is 2 toys.
markingPoints: Finds the total gain of 2 toys.

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 某國家考慮透過填海取得更多土地興建住宅單位。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 若基於技術理由，填海土地上的建築物最高高度限於兩層，解釋填海的機會成本會否改變。
parts.modelAnswer: 機會成本不變。高度限制會降低填海土地的價值，但不會改變所放棄的最高價值選擇。
markingPoints: 解釋所放棄的最高價值選擇不變。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變

questions.keyPoint: 正面界外效應與經濟無效率；矯正界外效應
questions.stem: 接種疫苗是預防感染及保護自己免受流感病毒侵襲的有效方法。

parts.label: Q4
parts.prompt: 運用界外效應概念，解釋政府為接種季節性流感疫苗提供津貼為何可改善經濟效率。
parts.modelAnswer: 接種者會降低他人受感染機會，卻沒有從受惠者取得補償，因此邊際社會利益大於邊際私人利益，疫苗被消費不足。津貼令接種量增加至較有效率水平。
markingPoints: 解釋津貼使消費接近效率水平。

questions.stem: 銀行體系的資產負債表顯示儲備為 3 億元，存款為 10 億元；法定儲備比率為 20%，公眾原先持有 2 億元現金。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 假設公眾不再持有現金，而所有銀行放出全部超額儲備，計算貨幣供應的最大可能改變。列出計算步驟。
parts.modelAnswer: 原有貨幣供應為 12 億元。新貨幣供應為（3 億元 + 2 億元）x 1/20% = 25 億元，因此最大可能增加為 13 億元。
markingPoints: 用乘數找出新貨幣供應。

questions.keyPoint: 根據個案資料，解釋哪個國家在生產某物品上擁有絕對優勢
questions.stem: A 國的資源量是 B 國的兩倍，兩國各把一半資源生產汽車，另一半生產玩具。下表顯示兩國總產出。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: 解釋 B 國在生產汽車上是否有絕對優勢。
parts.modelAnswer: 有。若 B 國擁有和 A 國相同資源，便可生產 200 單位汽車，多於 A 國的 100 單位。

questions.keyPoint: 根據個案資料，解釋哪個國家在生產某物品上擁有比較優勢
questions.stem: A 國的資源量是 B 國的兩倍，兩國各把一半資源生產汽車，另一半生產玩具。下表顯示兩國總產出。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 解釋 B 國在生產汽車上是否有比較優勢。
parts.modelAnswer: 有。A 國生產一輛汽車的機會成本是一個玩具，B 國則為 0.6 個玩具，因此 B 國在汽車上有比較優勢。
markingPoints: 計算 A 國機會成本。
計算及比較 B 國機會成本。

questions.keyPoint: 計算貿易得益
questions.stem: A 國的資源量是 B 國的兩倍，兩國各把一半資源生產汽車，另一半生產玩具。下表顯示兩國總產出。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 交換比率為 5 輛汽車換 4 個玩具。當汽車入口國入口 10 輛汽車時，計算貿易得益。列出計算步驟。
parts.modelAnswer: 貿易條件為一輛汽車換 0.8 個玩具。汽車入口國每輛汽車節省 0.2 個玩具，總得益為 2 個玩具。
markingPoints: 找出總得益 2 個玩具。

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Miss Amy Au demonstrates cosmetic products with short videos on social media and sells Japanese cosmetics on her website.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Are the short videos on social media websites public goods or private goods? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: They are public goods because they are non-rivalrous in consumption: people can watch the same videos concurrently without affecting one another.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning and give examples of each type of internal expansion
questions.stem: Miss Amy Au sells Japanese cosmetic products on her website and starts selling Korean cosmetic products too.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: To what type of expansion does this belong? Give TWO possible reasons for it.
parts.modelAnswer: It is horizontal expansion. Possible motives include increasing market share, enjoying economies of scale, and exploiting the brand name.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: Miss Amy Au pays her personal assistant $12 000 per month to arrange daily schedules and meetings.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: From Miss Amy Au's viewpoint, suggest ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of this payment method.
parts.modelAnswer: Time-rate payment saves the cost of measuring output, but work incentive may be low.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: Miss Amy Au pays her video designer $1 000 per video to produce short videos for social media.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: From the employee's viewpoint, suggest ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of this payment method.
parts.modelAnswer: A higher output can give higher income, but income may be unstable.

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: The table shows China widened several individual income tax brackets from October 2018.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Is the individual income tax in China progressive, proportional, or regressive? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: It is progressive because taxpayers with higher income are charged a higher average tax rate.
markingPoints: Explains higher average tax rates for higher income.

visuals.caption: Changes in the individual income tax system in China effective from October 2018

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Deflationary gap
questions.stem: The table shows China widened several individual income tax brackets from October 2018. Suppose China has a deflationary output gap.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: With an AS-AD diagram, explain how the change in the income tax system affects the deflationary output gap in the short run.
parts.modelAnswer: Middle-income taxpayers face a lower average tax rate, so disposable income, consumption and aggregate demand rise. AD shifts right and the deflationary gap narrows in the short run.
markingPoints: Explains lower tax and higher disposable income.
Shows a rightward AD shift and a smaller deflationary gap.

visuals.caption: Changes in the individual income tax system in China effective from October 2018

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: China has a deflationary output gap. An economist suggests lowering banks' required reserve ratio instead of changing the income tax system.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Discuss the suggestion with ONE argument FOR and ONE argument AGAINST it.
parts.modelAnswer: For: monetary policy may raise investment and current or future productivity, and avoids worsening the government's fiscal balance. Against: tax cuts may narrow the income gap, while lower reserve requirements may not increase loans or money supply if banks do not expand lending.
markingPoints: Gives a valid argument for monetary policy.
Gives a valid argument against monetary policy.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: The Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link was launched in September 2018.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain the effect of launching the High Speed Rail on labour mobility in Hong Kong.
parts.modelAnswer: It increases geographical mobility of labour because the transportation network improves.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem: During non-holidays, some High Speed Rail trains have many empty seats.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: With a demand-supply diagram, explain why the situation may be inefficient.
parts.modelAnswer: The fare is above the market-clearing level, creating excess supply. Marginal benefit of an additional passenger exceeds marginal cost, so total social surplus could rise if more seats were sold.
markingPoints: Shows price above equilibrium and excess supply.
Explains MB exceeds MC / deadweight loss.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem: High Speed Rail fares in RMB are fixed, while fares in Hong Kong dollar are adjusted with the RMB-HKD exchange rate.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A depreciation of RMB against USD will result in an increase in total revenue, in HKD, from High Speed Rail tickets sold in Hong Kong. With a diagram, explain under what condition the statement is correct.
parts.modelAnswer: Under the linked exchange rate system, RMB depreciation lowers the fare in HKD. If demand is elastic, the percentage rise in quantity demanded exceeds the percentage fall in price, so total revenue in HKD rises.
markingPoints: Explains the fall in HKD fare.
States elastic demand as the condition.
Explains the total-revenue effect and shows it correctly.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: China and the United States imposed retaliatory tariffs during their 2018 trade war.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: The US imposed tariffs partly to reduce its trade deficits with China. In a demand-supply diagram, indicate the change in the total market value, net of tariff, of Chinese goods exported to the US.
parts.modelAnswer: The tariff shifts supply upward. Quantity falls and the market value net of tariff is lower; the diagram should show the loss in total market value net of tariff.
markingPoints: Shows the supply shift caused by tariff.
Shows lower quantity and lower net-of-tariff market value.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of trade surplus and deficit
questions.stem: China and the United States imposed retaliatory tariffs during their 2018 trade war.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain why the US may NOT succeed in reducing its trade deficits with China.
parts.modelAnswer: China may retaliate with tariffs on US goods. If the resulting fall in US exports to China outweighs the fall in US imports, the US trade deficit may enlarge.
markingPoints: Explains the possible worsening of the US trade deficit.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: Hong Kong is a major re-exporter between the US and China, and the US treats Hong Kong separately from China in trade matters.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 'Since Hong Kong-produced goods are not subject to higher tariffs, Hong Kong's total exports will not be affected.' Do you agree? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: No. Some Hong Kong re-exports are subject to the tariffs. Their value may fall, reducing Hong Kong's total exports, which include re-exports.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: The sources describe the China-US trade war, Hong Kong's re-exports, the US-Hong Kong Policy Act, and views from firms, an economist and an investor.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Discuss effects of the trade war on Hong Kong, including aggregate output, tax revenue and other economic variables.
parts.modelAnswer: Tariffs can reduce re-exports and aggregate demand, while falling stock prices reduce wealth and consumption. Firms may relocate, lowering SRAS and future output. Profits, income and stamp-duty tax revenue may fall. Unemployment may rise, the HKD may depreciate against RMB, and government expenditure may rise through support for affected workers or firms.
markingPoints: Explains effects on aggregate output with source use.
Explains other relevant variables such as unemployment, exchange rate or public expenditure.

questions.keyPoint: Determine the profit-maximising output and price graphically and numerically
questions.stem: Grape Limited is the only smartphone manufacturer in a country and uses uniform pricing.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain how profit-maximising output and price are determined. Indicate output Q1 and price P1 in Figure 3.
parts.modelAnswer: The firm chooses output where marginal revenue equals marginal cost, then sets price from the demand curve. The diagram should show the MR curve, Q1 and P1.
markingPoints: Explains price is read from demand.

questions.stem: Technology advance lowers the cost of electronic components of smartphones.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: Indicate the new output Q2 and price P2 in Figure 3.

questions.stem: Technology advance lowers the cost of electronic components of smartphones.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: Discuss the effect of the cost reduction on efficiency with Figure 3.
parts.modelAnswer: Efficiency worsens if the deadweight loss becomes larger. The diagram should show the original and new deadweight-loss areas.
markingPoints: States the possible effect on deadweight loss.
Shows old and new deadweight loss correctly.

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination
questions.stem: Grape Limited sells smartphones to students with a 30% discount.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain why the practice constitutes price discrimination.
parts.modelAnswer: The same smartphone is sold at different prices to different consumer groups, students and non-students, despite the same cost.
markingPoints: States different prices for the same product.
States different consumer groups / same cost.

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination
questions.stem: Grape Limited sells smartphones to students with a 30% discount.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: Give TWO conditions under which this type of price discrimination can be practised.
parts.modelAnswer: The market must be separable, and the price elasticities of demand in the submarkets must differ.

questions.keyPoint: Anti-competitive behaviours
questions.stem: Lemon Corporation licenses a smartphone operating system only on condition that the phone pre-installs its web browser.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Name the anti-competitive behaviour and state TWO ways it harms consumers.
parts.modelAnswer: It is a tie-in sale. It can lead to higher prices and less consumer choice.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: Figure 4 shows Country A's PPF. The world price of one unit of Good X is two units of Good Y.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain which good Country A exports if it engages in international trade.
parts.modelAnswer: Country A exports Good X because its opportunity cost of one X is 1.5 Y, below the world price of 2 Y.
markingPoints: Compares domestic opportunity cost with world price.

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with constant marginal cost)
questions.stem: Country A engages in international trade and always consumes 10 units of Good X.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: With Figure 4, calculate Country A's total gain from trade.
parts.modelAnswer: Before trade consumption is C0 (10,15); after trade production is P1 (20,0) and consumption is C1 (10,20). The gain from trade is five units of Good Y.
markingPoints: Shows correct production and CPF after trade.
Calculates the gain of five Y.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Indicate Country A's export and import volumes in Figure 4.
parts.modelAnswer: Country A exports Good X and imports Good Y; the diagram should show the correct X export and Y import volumes.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: The world price of Good X falls continuously.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Explain whether Country A's direction of trade necessarily remains the same.
parts.modelAnswer: No. If the world price falls below Country A's domestic opportunity cost, Country A no longer has a comparative advantage in Good X, so its direction of trade changes.
markingPoints: Explains loss of comparative advantage when world price falls sufficiently.

questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting the growth of an economy
questions.stem: Country A adopts a closed-door policy forbidding foreign trade, tourists and foreign workers.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Explain why economic growth in Country A worsens.
parts.modelAnswer: Excluding foreign workers reduces human capital and possible knowledge or skill spillovers. Closing trade reduces access to better capital goods and foreign R&D, lowering productivity and output growth.
markingPoints: Explains a valid channel to lower growth.
Connects it to productivity, capital or technical progress.

questions.keyPoint: Measurement of economic growth and development
questions.stem: Country A adopts a closed-door policy forbidding foreign trade, tourists and foreign workers.

parts.label: (f)
parts.prompt: Other than reasons about economic growth, explain why economic development in Country A worsens.
parts.modelAnswer: Health and education may deteriorate because the country loses access to imported medicine, better equipment, foreign doctors, teachers and students.
markingPoints: Connects it to health, education or quality of life.

questions.keyPoint: 私用品及共用品
questions.stem: 香港選美冠軍區詠恩在社交媒體網站發布短片示範化妝品用法，並在網站售賣日本化妝品。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 社交媒體網站上的短片是共用品還是私用品？解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 短片屬共用品，因為消費具有非競爭性，多人可同時觀看而不影響彼此。

questions.keyPoint: 了解各類內部擴張的含義並加以舉例
questions.stem: 區詠恩原來在網站售賣日本化妝品，後來也開始售賣韓國化妝品。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 這屬於哪類擴張？列出兩個可能理由。
parts.modelAnswer: 這是橫向擴張。理由包括增加市場佔有率、享有規模經濟及利用品牌名稱。

questions.keyPoint: 不同的付酬方式
questions.stem: 區詠恩每月支付私人助理 12 000 元安排日程及會議。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 從區詠恩角度，列出此付酬方式的一項好處及一項壞處。
parts.modelAnswer: 按時率計酬可節省量度產出的成本，但工作誘因可能較低。

questions.keyPoint: 不同的付酬方式
questions.stem: 區詠恩每段短片支付影片設計師 1 000 元。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 從僱員角度，列出此付酬方式的一項好處及一項壞處。
parts.modelAnswer: 產量較高可帶來較高收入，但收入可能不穩定。

questions.keyPoint: 累進稅、比例稅和累退稅
questions.stem: 表格顯示中國自 2018 年 10 月起調整個人所得稅稅階。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 中國個人所得稅是累進、比例還是累退稅？解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 是累進稅，因為收入較高的納稅人須繳付較高平均稅率。
markingPoints: 解釋高收入者平均稅率較高。

questions.stem: 表格顯示中國自 2018 年 10 月起調整個人所得稅稅階。假設中國有通縮產出差距。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 以 AS-AD 圖解釋個人所得稅制度改變在短期如何影響通縮產出差距。
parts.modelAnswer: 中等收入組別的平均稅率下降，可支配收入、消費和總需求上升。AD 向右移，短期通縮產出差距收窄。

questions.stem: 中國有通縮產出差距。有經濟學家建議降低銀行法定儲備比率，而非改變所得稅制度。

parts.label: (c)

questions.keyPoint: 勞力的流動性
questions.stem: 廣深港高速鐵路於 2018 年 9 月通車。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 解釋高鐵通車對香港勞工流動性的影響。
parts.modelAnswer: 高鐵改善交通網絡，因此提高勞工的地域流動性。

questions.topicGroup: 均衡價格及均衡數量的決定
questions.keyPoint: 市場不均衡：供不應求及供過於求
questions.stem: 非假日期間，高鐵部分班次有很多空位。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 以供需圖解釋該情況為何可能缺乏效率。
parts.modelAnswer: 車費高於市場出清水平，出現供過於求。多一名乘客的邊際利益大於邊際成本，若售出更多座位，總社會盈餘可上升。
markingPoints: 顯示價格高於均衡及供過於求。
解釋邊際利益大於邊際成本或有效率損失。

questions.chapterTitle: 需求和供應的價格彈性
questions.keyPoint: 需求價格彈性和總收入之間的關係
questions.stem: 高鐵票價以人民幣計固定，在香港出售的港元票價會按人民幣兌港元匯率調整。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 「人民幣兌美元貶值會令香港出售的高鐵票總收入（以港元計）上升。」以圖解釋該陳述在甚麼條件下正確。
parts.modelAnswer: 在聯繫匯率制度下，人民幣貶值令港元票價下降。若需求富彈性，需求量上升百分率大於價格下降百分率，港元總收入便上升。
markingPoints: 解釋總收入效果並正確畫圖。

questions.keyPoint: 分析自由貿易和關稅對小型開放經濟的價格、本地產出、進口、消費量及關稅收入造成的影響
questions.stem: 2018 年中美貿易戰期間，兩國互相加徵關稅。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: 美國加徵關稅的可能原因是減少對華貿易赤字。以供需圖顯示貿易戰期間中國輸往美國貨物的總市值（扣除關稅）如何改變。
parts.modelAnswer: 關稅令供應曲線向上移，交易量下降，扣除關稅後的總市值下降。
markingPoints: 顯示關稅造成的供應移動。
顯示數量及扣稅後市值下降。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 經常帳（主要組成部分：貨物、服務、收益及經常轉移）
questions.keyPoint: 貿易盈餘及貿易赤字的意思
questions.stem: 2018 年中美貿易戰期間，兩國互相加徵關稅。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 解釋美國為何未必能成功減少對華貿易赤字。

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances

parts.label: Q1
parts.prompt: Although air ticket fares and hotel rates are usually higher during holiday periods, many people still travel abroad. Explain, in terms of opportunity cost, why travelling abroad is not necessarily more expensive during holiday periods than non-holiday periods.
parts.modelAnswer: Full cost equals monetary cost plus time cost. Holiday travel may have lower time cost; if the time-cost saving exceeds the extra monetary cost, full cost is lower.
markingPoints: States full cost includes money and time cost.

parts.label: Q11
parts.prompt: Analyse the effects of the situation on Country Z's general living standard, aggregate output in the short run, and balance of payment.
parts.modelAnswer: Living standard falls as resources are diverted from goods and services, and conscripted males lose jobs, household income and consumption. questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Serine works in the Hong Kong branch of a multinational firm. Her preferences are: work in a firm in South Korea; work in a local firm without overtime; stay in the current firm.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the opportunity cost of switching to the local firm without overtime work will necessarily remain unchanged if the military threat from North Korea to South Korea becomes more intense.
parts.modelAnswer: No. The value of the highest-valued option forgone, working in South Korea, would fall.
markingPoints: States that the opportunity cost does not remain unchanged.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Serine works in the Hong Kong branch of a multinational firm. Her preferences are: work in a firm in South Korea; work in a local firm without overtime; stay in the current firm.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the opportunity cost of switching to the local firm without overtime work will necessarily remain unchanged if Serine wants to enjoy more leisure time.
parts.modelAnswer: No. Working time in South Korea may be long, so the first option becomes less preferred and the opportunity cost falls.
markingPoints: States that the opportunity cost does not remain unchanged.
