questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: Pokemon Go players move around to catch cyber-pets. The developer placed hotspots in areas where many players gather. Restaurants near the hotspots experience sharp business increases.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Based on the information, explain, in terms of externality, how placing the hotspots may result in inefficiency.
parts.modelAnswer: Restaurants receive positive external benefits from increased business without paying the developer. Marginal social benefit exceeds marginal social cost, so the number of hotspots near restaurants is below the efficient level.
markingPoints: Explains that restaurants receive uncompensated benefits.
Explains MSB exceeds MSC and the under-provision result.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: Restaurants near Pokemon Go hotspots benefit from increased business.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: How may the problem of inefficiency be relieved by market?
parts.modelAnswer: Restaurants may pay the game developer to increase nearby hotspots, or the developer may charge restaurants for placing more hotspots nearby.
markingPoints: Explains that it internalises the external benefit.

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 小玲在某跨國企業的香港分行工作。她有數個選項，其優先次序如下：前往一家位於南韓的企業工作；轉職到一家毋須加班工作的本地企業；留在目前企業。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 假若北韓對南韓的軍事威脅加劇，解釋在下列情況下，轉職到該毋須加班工作的本地企業的機會成本是否必然維持不變。
parts.modelAnswer: 不會。所放棄的最高價值選項，即前往南韓工作，價值會下降。
markingPoints: 指出機會成本不會維持不變。
解釋最高價值的放棄選項價值下降。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 小玲在某跨國企業的香港分行工作，並在南韓工作、轉職本地毋須加班企業及留在目前企業之間作選擇。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 假若小玲想享受更多閒暇的時間，解釋轉職到該毋須加班工作的本地企業的機會成本是否必然維持不變。
parts.modelAnswer: 不會。南韓的工作時間可能很長，令第一選項較不受偏好，機會成本下降。
markingPoints: 指出機會成本不會維持不變。
解釋南韓工作時間長的影響。
連繫偏好改變和較低機會成本。

questions.keyPoint: 不同的付酬方式
questions.stem: 史提芬是某餐廳的東主。他以月薪支付其侍應的工資，並容許他們保留顧客給予的小費。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: 以下列角度解釋為什麼上述安排較按時計薪為佳：(i) 僱員的角度。
parts.modelAnswer: 僱員只要付出更多努力及／或提供較佳服務，便有機會獲取較高收入。
markingPoints: 解釋更多努力或較佳服務的作用。

questions.keyPoint: 不同的付酬方式
questions.stem: 史提芬以月薪支付侍應工資，並容許他們保留小費。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 以下列角度解釋為什麼上述安排較按時計薪為佳：(ii) 僱主的角度。
parts.modelAnswer: 可降低監察侍應表現的成本，及／或提高侍應努力工作和提供較佳服務的誘因。
markingPoints: 指出可降低監察成本或提高工作誘因。

questions.topicGroup: 內部規模經濟/規模負經濟
questions.keyPoint: 內部規模經濟/規模負經濟
questions.stem: 由於開設了數間分店，該餐廳的平均生產成本上升了。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 以兩項理由，解釋為什麼出現這情況。
parts.modelAnswer: 企業規模可能過大，管理效率開始下降；未償還貸款龐大令額外借貸的邊際成本上升；或市場飽和令推廣成本上升。
markingPoints: 指出兩個有效的內部規模不經濟原因。
解釋每個原因如何提高平均成本。

questions.keyPoint: 列出不同市場結構的一般特徵
questions.stem: 下圖顯示 2015 年香港選擇按揭市場五大銀行的佔有率。

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt: 上述市場在 2015 年屬哪種市場結構？列出這市場結構的兩項特徵。
parts.modelAnswer: 屬寡頭市場。特徵包括少數主導廠商、進入障礙、廠商定價策略互相依賴及市場資訊不完全。

visuals.caption: 2015 年香港選擇按揭市場五大銀行的佔有率

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 正面界外效應與經濟無效率；矯正界外效應
questions.stem: 「Pokemon Go」是一款熱門遊戲，玩家需攜帶智能手機前往不同地方捕捉虛擬寵物。遊戲發展商在不同地區放置熱點，而適當熱點會吸引很多玩家聚集。一些在偏遠地區的餐廳發現生意急升，原因是它們位處這些熱點附近。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 根據上述資料，以界外影響為依據，解釋放置熱點如何可能導致缺乏效率。
parts.modelAnswer: 餐廳因生意增加而得到正外部得益，但沒有向遊戲發展商付費。邊際社會利益大於邊際社會成本，餐廳附近熱點數目低於效率水平。
markingPoints: 解釋餐廳獲得未付費的得益。
解釋 MSB 大於 MSC 及供應不足。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 正面界外效應與經濟無效率；矯正界外效應
questions.stem: 位於 Pokemon Go 熱點附近的餐廳獲得額外生意。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 市場如何可以減輕這缺乏效率的問題？
parts.modelAnswer: 餐廳可向遊戲發展商支付費用，以增加附近熱點；或發展商可向餐廳收費以在其附近放置更多熱點。
markingPoints: 指出一項有效市場交易。
解釋交易把外部得益內部化。

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem: Due to political instability, the currency of a country depreciates sharply and becomes highly volatile.

parts.label: Q5
parts.prompt: Which TWO functions of money may be weakened? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Store of value weakens because purchasing power over foreign goods and services falls. Standard of deferred payment weakens because volatile currency raises the cost of specifying future payments. Medium of exchange may also weaken if firms refuse it.
markingPoints: Identifies two valid functions of money.
Correctly explains why each function weakens.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: A general sales tax is introduced.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Why can the introduction of a general sales tax stabilise government revenue in times of economic downturn?
parts.modelAnswer: Consumption fluctuates less than income, so sales-tax revenue fluctuates less than income-tax revenue. A general sales tax also broadens the tax base.
markingPoints: Explains the lower fluctuation of consumption than income or the broader tax base.
Connects this to more stable tax revenue.

questions.keyPoint: Four basic principles of taxation
questions.stem: Consider direct taxes in Hong Kong.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Suggest ONE type of direct tax in Hong Kong that follows Adam Smith's tax principle of equality. Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: A standard tax rate on salaries tax, profits tax or property tax is proportional: every taxpayer pays the same proportion of the relevant income.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning of absolute advantage
questions.stem: Countries A and B each allocate half their resources to food and half to computers. Their outputs are shown in the table.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain whether Country B enjoys an absolute advantage in producing computers.
parts.modelAnswer: It is uncertain. Without knowing the total resources of both countries, output per unit of resource cannot be determined.
markingPoints: Explains why resource productivity cannot be determined.

visuals.caption: Total output when half of resources are allocated to each good

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: Countries A and B each allocate half their resources to food and half to computers. Their outputs are shown in the table.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain whether Country B will export computers.
parts.modelAnswer: With full specialisation, A can make 200 food or 100 computers; B can make 200 food or 200 computers. The opportunity cost of one computer is 2 food in A and 1 food in B, so B exports computers.
markingPoints: Identifies Country B as the computer exporter.

visuals.caption: Total output when half of resources are allocated to each good

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: The exchange ratio is 4 computers for 7 units of food. The computer-exporting country exports 16 computers.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the gain from trade for the computer-exporting country. Show your working.
parts.modelAnswer: Terms of trade are 7/4 = 1.75 food per computer. Country B gains 1.75 - 1 = 0.75 food per computer, so total gain is 12 food.
markingPoints: Finds the total gain of 12 food.

visuals.caption: Total output when half of resources are allocated to each good

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate excess reserves, required and actual reserve ratios
questions.stem: The banking system's balance sheet has $1,000 reserves, $2,000 loans and $3,000 deposits, with $250 excess reserves.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the required reserve ratio.
parts.modelAnswer: Required reserve ratio = (1,000 - 250) / 3,000 = 0.25, or 25%.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The banking system has $250 excess reserves. Banks lend out all excess reserves and the public holds no cash.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the change in deposits after credit creation. Show your working.
parts.modelAnswer: Change in deposits = $250 x 1/0.25 = $1,000.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Features of the four phases of a business cycle
questions.stem: Figures 1 and 2 show US GDP growth, interest rate and unemployment rate data. Point A is the 2009 GDP-growth observation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Refer to Figure 1. Identify the phase of business cycle in which point A is.
parts.modelAnswer: Depression or trough.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: The US had a sharp downturn in 2009.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: How may a reduction in interest rate help the US economy in 2009? Without using a diagram, explain your answer in the light of aggregate supply and/or aggregate demand.
parts.modelAnswer: A lower interest rate raises investment and/or consumption. Aggregate demand increases and aggregate output rises.
markingPoints: Explains the rightward AD effect and higher output.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Features of the four phases of a business cycle
questions.stem: Figures 1 and 2 show US GDP growth, interest rate and unemployment rate data for 2006-2015.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Discuss whether the data in Figures 1 and 2 are consistent with your answer in (b).
parts.modelAnswer: They are consistent: when the interest rate fell in 2009, GDP growth increased and the unemployment rate dropped. An alternative well-reasoned interpretation using the lag is acceptable.
markingPoints: States whether the data are consistent.
Uses the interest-rate, GDP-growth and unemployment-rate changes correctly.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.stem: The US seeks to increase aggregate output in the long run.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Suggest ONE policy that will help increase aggregate output in the long run. Briefly explain your answer.
parts.modelAnswer: Subsidising research and development, improving labour, importing labour, or investing in infrastructure raises potential output and shifts LRAS right.
markingPoints: Explains higher production capacity / a rightward LRAS shift.

questions.keyPoint: 貨幣的功能
questions.stem: 由於政局不穩，一個國家的貨幣急劇貶值並變得高度波動。

parts.label: Q5
parts.prompt: 貨幣的哪兩項功能可能被削弱？解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 儲藏價值功能會削弱，因為本幣兌外幣貶值令購買外國貨物和服務的能力下降。延遲支付標準功能也會削弱，因為貨幣高度波動令訂立未來付款條款的成本上升。
markingPoints: 指出兩項有效貨幣功能。
正確解釋每項功能為何削弱。

questions.keyPoint: 徵稅的影響
questions.stem: 政府引入一般銷售稅。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 為什麼引入一般銷售稅可在經濟不景時穩定政府收入？
parts.modelAnswer: 消費的波動小於收入，銷售稅收入的波動因而小於所得稅收入；一般銷售稅也可擴闊稅基。
markingPoints: 解釋消費波動較小或稅基較闊。

questions.keyPoint: 四個基本的徵稅原則
questions.stem: 考慮香港的直接稅。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 按 Adam Smith 提出的平等徵稅原則，舉出香港一種符合該原則的直接稅。解釋你的答案。
parts.modelAnswer: 薪俸稅、利得稅或物業稅的標準稅率均可。每位納稅人按其相關收入的相同比例繳稅，屬比例稅。

questions.keyPoint: 了解絕對優勢的含義
questions.stem: A 國和 B 國均各把一半資源生產食物，另一半生產電腦。下表顯示兩國總產出。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: 解釋 B 國是否在生產電腦上享有絕對優勢。
parts.modelAnswer: 不確定。若不知道兩國總資源量，便不能確定食物和電腦每單位資源的產出。
markingPoints: 解釋不能確定每單位資源的生產力。

visuals.caption: 兩國各把一半資源生產食物及電腦時的總產出

questions.keyPoint: 根據個案資料，解釋哪個國家在生產某物品上擁有比較優勢
questions.stem: A 國和 B 國各把一半資源生產食物及電腦。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 解釋 B 國是否會出口電腦。
parts.modelAnswer: 完全專門化時，A 國可生產 200 食物或 100 電腦；B 國可生產 200 食物或 200 電腦。A 國每部電腦的機會成本是 2 單位食物，B 國是 1 單位，因此 B 國出口電腦。
markingPoints: 找出 A 國機會成本。
找出 B 國機會成本。
指出 B 國出口電腦。

visuals.caption: 兩國各把一半資源生產食物及電腦時的總產出

questions.keyPoint: 計算貿易得益
questions.stem: 交換比率是 4 部電腦換 7 單位食物，電腦出口國出口 16 部電腦。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 計算電腦出口國的貿易得益，列出計算步驟。
parts.modelAnswer: 貿易條件是每部電腦換 7/4 = 1.75 單位食物。B 國每部電腦得益是 1.75 - 1 = 0.75 單位食物，總得益為 12 單位食物。
markingPoints: 找出總得益 12 單位食物。

visuals.caption: 兩國各把一半資源生產食物及電腦時的總產出

questions.keyPoint: 了解及計算超額儲備、法定及實際儲備比率
questions.stem: 銀行體系的資產負債表有 $1 000 儲備、$2 000 放款、$3 000 存款，並有 $250 超額儲備。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 找出法定儲備比率。

visuals.caption: 銀行體系的資產負債表

questions.keyPoint: 了解及計算存款、放款、貨幣供應等在存款創造/ 收縮過程後的最大及實際改變
questions.stem: 銀行體系有 $250 超額儲備，所有銀行放出全部超額儲備，公眾不持有現金。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 計算信貸創造後存款的改變，列出計算步驟。

visuals.caption: 銀行體系的資產負債表

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.keyPoint: 經濟周期四個階段的特點
questions.stem: 圖一和圖二顯示美國的本地生產總值增長率、利率和失業率數據；A 點是 2009 年的本地生產總值增長率。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 參考圖一，辨識 A 點所處的經濟周期階段。
parts.modelAnswer: 蕭條／谷底。

questions.keyPoint: 擴張性及緊縮性貨幣政策，包括改變法定儲備比率及貼現率
questions.stem: 美國在 2009 年經濟急劇下滑。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 不用圖形，根據總供應及／或總需求解釋減息如何有助美國經濟。
parts.modelAnswer: 減息令投資及／或消費增加，總需求上升，總產出隨之增加。
markingPoints: 解釋投資及／或消費增加。
解釋總需求右移及產出上升。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.keyPoint: 經濟周期四個階段的特點
questions.stem: 圖一和圖二顯示 2006 至 2015 年美國的經濟資料。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 討論圖一和圖二的資料是否與你在 (b) 的答案一致。
parts.modelAnswer: 一致：2009 年利率下跌後，本地生產總值增長率上升，失業率下降。考慮貨幣政策時滯的其他合理論證亦可接受。
markingPoints: 正確使用利率、GDP 增長及失業率的變動。

questions.topicGroup: 影響長期總供應的因素
questions.keyPoint: 影響長期總供應的因素
questions.stem: 美國希望在長期增加總產出。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 提出一項有助在長期增加總產出的政策，簡單解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 資助研發、改善勞工質素、輸入勞工或投資基建均可提高潛在產出，令 LRAS 向右移。
markingPoints: 解釋提高生產能力或 LRAS 向右移。

questions.keyPoint: Classification of private firms: sole proprietorship, partnership, private limited company and public limited company
questions.stem: MTR Corporation Limited provides railway services in Hong Kong and is a listed company.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State TWO differences between a listed company and a private limited company.
parts.modelAnswer: Shares of a listed company are freely transferable, it must disclose accounting information to the public, and it can issue shares and bonds to the general public; a private limited company cannot.

questions.topicGroup: Meaning of public ownership and examples of organisations or institutions in operating under public ownership
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of public ownership and examples of organisations or institutions in operating under public ownership
questions.stem: Some politicians suggest the government should buy back MTR shares so the company becomes wholly government-owned.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Discuss the suggestion by giving ONE argument FOR and ONE argument AGAINST it.
parts.modelAnswer: For: government can better control fares, reduce passengers' burden and help funding. Against: public ownership may lower efficiency and sensitivity to price signals, while the purchase has a high opportunity cost.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem: Table 1 shows MTR fare adjustments, passenger boardings and total revenue from 2012 to 2014.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Can we conclude that the increase in total revenue is a result of inelastic demand for local MTR services? Explain with a diagram.
parts.modelAnswer: No. Passenger numbers rose while fares rose, which implies demand shifted right. Both price and quantity transacted rose, so total revenue rose; the table cannot establish inelastic demand.
markingPoints: Explains higher price, quantity and total revenue.
Shows a rightward demand shift and the revenue increase.

visuals.caption: Business information about the local services of MTR

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Country X introduces a per-unit subsidy to education services of private universities.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Under what condition would students enjoy a larger share of subsidy benefit than private universities? Illustrate your answer with Figure 3.
parts.modelAnswer: Students receive the larger benefit when the price elasticity of demand for education is lower than the price elasticity of supply. The supply curve shifts down by the subsidy and the diagram shows consumer benefit exceeding producer benefit.
markingPoints: Shows the new price, quantity and larger consumer benefit.

visuals.alt: Demand-curve base for the education-services market
visuals.caption: Figure 3

movements: Add supply, equilibrium and the division of subsidy benefit to official Figure 3.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Add supply, equilibrium and the division of subsidy benefit to official Figure 3.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Maximisation of total social surplus: marginal benefit equals marginal cost
questions.stem: A per-unit subsidy is given to private-university education services.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 'The subsidy causes inefficiency even though both students and universities benefit.' Defend the statement by comparing marginal cost and marginal benefit in Figure 3.
parts.modelAnswer: At the subsidised quantity Q1, marginal cost is greater than marginal benefit, so output exceeds the efficient level even though both parties receive benefits.
markingPoints: States MC is greater than MB at Q1.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising opportunities
questions.stem: Private-university education is subsidised.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain whether subsidising education can help improve equity.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. It equalises opportunities because poorer students are less constrained by finance; education can raise their future income and reduce inequality over generations.
markingPoints: Links access to education to future income or intergenerational inequality.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Before Brexit, EU workers could freely work in Britain. British politicians propose requiring low-skilled EU workers to apply for a British work visa.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Referring to the British politicians' view, explain how labour mobility of low-skilled EU workers would be affected.
parts.modelAnswer: Geographical mobility would be lower because the visa requirement raises the cost of moving to Britain for work.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: British firm owners say visa requirements affect most firms; global investors say political uncertainty raises investment risk.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Discuss the effect of Brexit on aggregate output of Britain in the short run with the aid of a diagram.
parts.modelAnswer: Visas raise firms' labour cost so SRAS shifts left. Political uncertainty reduces investment, shifting AD left. Aggregate output falls.
markingPoints: Shows both shifts and lower output correctly.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: EU officials say British citizens may require a visa to visit or work in EU countries.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Referring to this view, which TWO components of current account in Britain's balance of payments may be affected? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Invisible trade/services fall because fewer British citizens visit EU countries. Primary income falls because fewer Britons work in the EU and receive wages; secondary income/remittances may also fall.
markingPoints: Explains how each component is affected.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning and examples of the three types of production; identify the type of production

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: To finance retirement protection, Proposal A raises the standard tax rate and progressivity of salaries tax; Proposal B uses fiscal reserves.

parts.label: (b)

parts.modelAnswer: Proposal A reduces disposable income and consumption, so AD and output fall; it can reduce after-tax income inequality. parts.label: (b)(i)

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination

parts.label: (b)(ii)

parts.modelAnswer: No. The bundle can lower marginal cost, including administration, marketing and installation costs, so the lower price can reflect lower cost.

parts.modelAnswer: This is market sharing/market allocation. Firms face less competition, can raise prices and earn more profit, or lower marketing cost in assigned markets.

questions.keyPoint: 影響經濟增長的因素
questions.stem: 甲國在 2000 年後開放進行國際貿易。表格顯示人均實質 GDP 及人類發展指數（HDI）。

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: 參考表格，解釋國際貿易如何影響甲國的經濟增長。
parts.modelAnswer: 國際貿易提升經濟增長：人均實質 GDP 上升；出口可提高總需求及實質 GDP。
markingPoints: 根據數據指出經濟增長較高。

questions.keyPoint: 量度經濟增長及經濟發展
questions.stem: 甲國在 2000 年後開放進行國際貿易。表格顯示人均實質 GDP 及人類發展指數（HDI）。

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: 參考表格，解釋國際貿易如何影響甲國的經濟發展。
parts.modelAnswer: 經濟發展沒有改變，因為 HDI 維持 0.68。更多人可能輟學參與貿易、污染可能加劇，或新疾病令預期壽命下降。

questions.topicGroup: Reasons for an upward-sloping short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve
questions.keyPoint: Reasons for an upward-sloping short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve

parts.label: Q5
parts.prompt: Explain, with ONE reason, why the short-run aggregate supply curve is upward-sloping.
parts.modelAnswer: When price rises, input prices adjust incompletely, so real factor cost falls and firms expand output; hence SRAS slopes upward.
markingPoints: States incomplete adjustment of input prices.
Explains lower real cost and higher output.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: One unit of clothing and toys requires 6 and 2 input units respectively in Country A. Countries A and B trade at 2 clothing for 11 toys.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Which good would Country A export? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Country A exports clothing: its opportunity cost of clothing is 3 toys, below the terms of trade of 11/2 toys per clothing.
markingPoints: Compares opportunity cost with terms of trade.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: Country A exports clothing under 2 clothing for 11 toys; transporting one clothing costs 2 toys borne by A.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate Country A’s gain per unit of export.
parts.modelAnswer: It receives 5.5 toys but gives up 3 toys and 2 toys transport cost, so gain = 5.5 - 2 - 3 = 0.5 toy.
markingPoints: Includes production and transport opportunity cost.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem: The banking system has $1,000m reserves, $4,000m deposits and public cash $500m; banks hold no excess reserves.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate monetary base and money supply.
parts.modelAnswer: Monetary base = reserves + cash = $1,500m. Money supply = deposits + cash = $4,500m.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The central bank increases required reserve ratio to 50%.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate change in monetary base and money supply. Show workings.
parts.modelAnswer: Monetary base is unchanged. Required reserves become $2,000m, deposits fall to $2,000m, so money supply falls from $4,500m to $2,500m: decrease $2,000m.
markingPoints: Calculates deposits and new money supply.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.keyPoint: Describe the process of deposit creation/contraction

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: Why is money supply often a few times more than monetary base?
parts.modelAnswer: Banks create deposits by lending out excess reserves; the banking multiplier makes deposits and money supply exceed the base.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.keyPoint: Describe the process of deposit creation/contraction

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: Under what situation will money supply equal monetary base?
parts.modelAnswer: When there are no bank deposits, so all money is cash.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)

parts.label: Q9

parts.modelAnswer: Quota abolition increases supply and Russia’s embargo lowers demand. Both shifts lower dairy price; the quantity effect is ambiguous.

解釋實質成本下降和產出增加。

parts.label: (a)

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Tobacco duty is increased to discourage smoking.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Without a diagram, justify: the rise may not effectively reduce the quantity of duty-paid cigarettes consumed.
parts.modelAnswer: Duty raises cigarette price and lowers quantity demanded. But addiction makes demand inelastic, so the percentage quantity fall is smaller than the percentage price rise; even a large duty rise may have little effect.
markingPoints: Explains higher price lowers quantity demanded.
Relates percentage quantity and price changes.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply

questions.stem: Tobacco duty rises and Customs crack down on illegal sellers of duty-not-paid cigarettes.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Is it possible that the quantity transacted of duty-not-paid cigarettes increases? Explain with a diagram.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. The crackdown shifts supply left, but duty-paid and duty-not-paid cigarettes are substitutes, so higher tobacco duty shifts demand for duty-not-paid cigarettes right. Quantity rises if the demand increase dominates the supply decrease.
markingPoints: Shows a higher final quantity when demand effect dominates.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Explain in terms of externality why overcrowding may be inefficient.
parts.modelAnswer: An extra passenger imposes unpriced time costs on others, so marginal social cost exceeds marginal private cost/benefit and passenger use exceeds the efficient level.

questions.keyPoint: Determine the profit-maximising output and price graphically and numerically
questions.stem: Super Power is the only licensed electricity supplier and applies uniform pricing.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Indicate profit-maximising Q1 and P1 in Figure 3 and explain.
parts.modelAnswer: It produces where MR=MC at Q1 and charges the price on the demand curve at Q1, P1.

visuals.alt: Figure 3: monopoly demand, marginal revenue and marginal cost
visuals.caption: Figure 3: monopoly demand, marginal revenue and marginal cost

questions.keyPoint: Explain why simple monopoly pricing is inefficient, i.e. MB > MC, and illustrate it with consumer surplus, producer surplus and deadweight loss
questions.stem: Figure 3 shows Super Power's uniform monopoly pricing.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why uniform pricing is inefficient.
parts.modelAnswer: At Q1 marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost, so output is below the efficient level and the omitted gains form deadweight loss.

visuals.alt: Figure 3: monopoly demand, marginal revenue and marginal cost
visuals.caption: Figure 3: monopoly demand, marginal revenue and marginal cost

questions.keyPoint: Variable costs and fixed costs
questions.stem: Government imposes a lump-sum tax on Super Power, independent of output.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain whether marginal cost rises.
parts.modelAnswer: No. A lump-sum tax is fixed cost and does not vary with output, so marginal cost is unchanged.
markingPoints: Explains fixed cost does not affect MC.

questions.keyPoint: Determine the profit-maximising output and price graphically and numerically
questions.stem: A lump-sum tax is imposed on Super Power.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: Indicate after-tax Q2 and P2 in Figure 3.
parts.modelAnswer: Q2=Q1 and P2=P1 because marginal cost, hence profit-maximising output and price, are unchanged.

visuals.alt: Figure 3: monopoly demand, marginal revenue and marginal cost
visuals.caption: Figure 3: monopoly demand, marginal revenue and marginal cost

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination
questions.stem: Super Power charges domestic users $1.20 and industrial users $0.90 for a unit of electricity.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Does this constitute price discrimination? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. Different groups of consumers pay different prices for the same electricity produced at the same cost.
markingPoints: Identifies distinct consumer groups and prices.

questions.keyPoint: Anti-competitive behaviours
questions.stem: Super Power takes over its major coal supplier, which supplies 90% of electricity raw materials.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Name the possible anti-competitive behaviour and explain how it restrains competition.
parts.modelAnswer: Merger. It restricts entry of potential competitors by controlling a crucial input supplier.

questions.keyPoint: Anti-competitive behaviours
questions.stem: Super Power's owners claim the coal-supplier takeover is not anti-competitive.

parts.label: (f)
parts.prompt: Justify the claim with ONE reason.
parts.modelAnswer: The merger may lower average cost through cheaper raw materials/economies of scale; if savings lower electricity prices, consumers benefit and it may not be anti-competitive.

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with increasing marginal cost)
questions.stem: Figure 4 has a PPF and an inside point N.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the country would produce at N.
parts.modelAnswer: No. N implies idle resources and production is not maximised.

visuals.alt: Figure 4: PPF, no-trade point E and world-price line AB
visuals.caption: Figure 4: PPF, no-trade point E and world-price line AB

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with increasing marginal cost)
questions.stem: At E, the domestic cost of one X is 2.5Y. The slope of AB is the world price of X.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the country has comparative advantage in X.
parts.modelAnswer: No. Domestic cost of X, 2.5Y, exceeds world price, 1Y; equivalently the PPF tangent slope at E is steeper than AB.
markingPoints: Compares domestic cost and world price.

visuals.alt: Figure 4: PPF, no-trade point E and world-price line AB
visuals.caption: Figure 4: PPF, no-trade point E and world-price line AB

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with increasing marginal cost)
questions.stem: The country engages in international trade in Figure 4.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Indicate its production point after trade and consumption possibility frontier.
parts.modelAnswer: Production is where a CPF parallel to AB is tangent to the PPF; the consumption possibility frontier is parallel to AB.

visuals.alt: Figure 4: PPF, no-trade point E and world-price line AB
visuals.caption: Figure 4: PPF, no-trade point E and world-price line AB

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with increasing marginal cost)
questions.stem: The country engages in international trade.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: With Figure 4, explain whether it gains from trade.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. It can consume beyond the no-trade PPF/CPF, including more of both X and Y after trade.

visuals.alt: Figure 4: PPF, no-trade point E and world-price line AB
visuals.caption: Figure 4: PPF, no-trade point E and world-price line AB

questions.keyPoint: Measurement of economic growth and development
questions.stem: After opening to trade, the country's HDI rises.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.prompt: Give ONE reason why international trade can raise HDI.
parts.modelAnswer: Trade can transfer superior technology, raise productivity and GDP, or spread health technology that raises life expectancy.

questions.keyPoint: The benefits and costs of economic growth
questions.stem: HDI rises after trade, but residents say their living standard has declined.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.prompt: Suggest TWO possible reasons.
parts.modelAnswer: Workers in import-substitute industries may become unemployed, income distribution may become more unequal, or pollution may increase through specialisation in more polluting goods.
markingPoints: Explains how each lowers living standard.

questions.keyPoint: 比較不同所有權形式的特徵及利弊
questions.stem: 麥當勞在香港是一家私人有限公司。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 寫出成立私人有限公司相較於成立公眾有限公司的一項優點和一項缺點。
parts.modelAnswer: 優點：較不易被收購或不用向公眾披露帳目。缺點：股份不能自由轉讓，亦不能向公眾發行股票集資。

questions.keyPoint: 了解各類內部擴張的含義並加以舉例
questions.stem: 麥當勞透過經營售賣優質咖啡的 McCafe 擴展業務。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 這屬哪一類擴張？解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 屬橫向擴張；快餐和咖啡屬相關但並非直接競爭的產品。
markingPoints: 解釋產品相關但不直接競爭。

questions.topicGroup: 貨幣價格（名義價格）和相對價格
questions.keyPoint: 將相對價格或全價格應用於需求定律，以解釋特定現象
questions.stem: McCafe 的意大利濃咖啡較星巴克便宜。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 提出兩個可能原因，解釋為什麼有這價格差異。
parts.modelAnswer: 例如咖啡質素較低、生產成本較低、環境較不舒適或品牌名稱較不吸引。
markingPoints: 解釋相關質素、成本或需求差異。

questions.topicGroup: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.keyPoint: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.stem: 麥當勞以過期肉類製成的產品其後被銷毀。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 解釋已銷毀產品的價值會否包括在香港本地生產總值內。
parts.modelAnswer: 不會。產品沒有在市場出售，故不計入產出；亦不是消費或投資開支。
markingPoints: 用生產面或支出面解釋。

questions.topicGroup: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.keyPoint: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.stem: 香港足球會聘請巴西著名足球員擔任為期兩個月兒童班教練，薪金 800 萬元，學費收入 300 萬元。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: 解釋對香港本地生產總值的影響。
parts.modelAnswer: GDP 增加 300 萬元，因為課程是居民生產單位在本年生產的服務。
markingPoints: 指出 GDP 增加 300 萬元。
解釋居民本年生產計入 GDP。

questions.topicGroup: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.keyPoint: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.stem: 巴西教練收取 800 萬元後返回巴西。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 解釋對香港本地居民生產總值的影響。
parts.modelAnswer: GNP 減少 500 萬元：GDP 增加 300 萬元，但教練的 800 萬元是從香港流出的要素收入。
markingPoints: 解釋 GDP 增加 300 萬元。
解釋 800 萬元收入流出。

questions.keyPoint: 不同的付酬方式
questions.stem: 球員甲每週收 $10,000；球員乙每場收 $8,000，另每進一球收 $10,000。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 從僱主角度，解釋合約乙較合約甲的兩項優勝之處。
parts.modelAnswer: 僱主可分擔風險，沒有比賽或入球時付款較少；按表現付酬亦降低監察成本並增加球員努力的誘因。
markingPoints: 解釋分擔風險／表現差時付款較少。
解釋較低監察成本或較強誘因。

visuals.caption: 兩位職業足球員的合約

questions.keyPoint: 勞力的流動性
questions.stem: 職業足球員退役後有時只能找到低薪工作。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 以勞工流動性解釋上述現象。
parts.modelAnswer: 他們的職業流動性低，因技能專門而不易轉移到其他工作。
markingPoints: 解釋技能專門／不可轉移。

questions.keyPoint: 香港的徵稅
questions.stem: 圖一顯示香港 2009 至 2013 年直接稅收入和名義本地生產總值轉變。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: 描述兩者關係並比較趨勢。
parts.modelAnswer: 兩者大致同方向變動，但直接稅收入的波動較名義 GDP 大。
markingPoints: 比較直接稅收入波動較大。

visuals.alt: 圖一：直接稅收入和名義本地生產總值轉變
visuals.caption: 圖一：直接稅收入和名義本地生產總值轉變

questions.keyPoint: 香港的徵稅
questions.stem: 圖一顯示直接稅收入和名義 GDP 轉變。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 簡單解釋 (a)(i) 所描述的關係。
parts.modelAnswer: 薪俸和利得稅受宏觀經濟情況影響很大；GDP 增長會增加薪酬和利潤收入，從而增加稅收。累進稅可令稅收波動更大。
markingPoints: 連繫 GDP 和薪酬／利潤收入。
連繫收入改變和直接稅收入。

visuals.alt: 圖一：直接稅收入和名義本地生產總值轉變
visuals.caption: 圖一：直接稅收入和名義本地生產總值轉變

questions.keyPoint: 直接稅與間接稅
questions.stem: 有人指香港稅基狹窄。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 舉出一個例子，解釋開徵新種類間接稅如何擴闊稅基。
parts.modelAnswer: 一般銷售稅或增值稅會令更多人士或物品納入稅網，從而擴闊稅基。

questions.chapterTitle: 需求和供應的價格彈性
questions.keyPoint: 影響需求價格彈性的因素
questions.stem: 政府增加煙草稅以減少吸煙。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 毋須圖表，論證增加煙草稅未必能有效減少已完稅香煙消費量。
parts.modelAnswer: 煙草稅提高價格並減少需求量；但吸煙者成癮，需求缺乏彈性，需求量百分比跌幅小於價格百分比升幅，因此加稅未必有效。
markingPoints: 解釋價格上升令需求量下降。
指出成癮令需求缺乏彈性。
比較需求量和價格的百分比變動。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋需求改變和供應改變如何影響均衡價格和數量
questions.stem: 政府增加煙草稅，同時海關打擊非法售賣未完稅香煙。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 未完稅香煙交易量有可能上升嗎？以圖解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 有可能。打擊令未完稅香煙供應減少；但已完稅和未完稅香煙是代替品，增加煙草稅令未完稅香煙需求增加。若需求增加效果較大，交易量上升。
markingPoints: 解釋代替效應令需求增加。
顯示最終數量較高的條件。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 經常帳（主要組成部分：貨物、服務、收益及經常轉移）
questions.keyPoint: 一宗交易會否及如何影響經常帳
questions.stem: 「個人遊」為香港帶來內地旅客。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 若內地旅客人數下降，香港經常帳如何受影響？
parts.modelAnswer: 旅遊服務出口下降，香港經常帳盈餘減少或赤字擴大。

questions.topicGroup: 總需求及/或總供應改變導致均衡產出水平和物價水平的改變
questions.keyPoint: 透過明確說明受影響的總需求組成部分及/ 或影響短期總供應及/或長期總供應的因素，解釋某情況會如何導致總需求、短期總供應及/ 或長期總供應轉變，因而令總需求曲線、短期總供應曲線及/或長期總供應曲線移動
questions.stem: 圖二的初始短期均衡產出高於充分就業產出 Yf；內地旅客人數下降。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 以圖二說明旅客減少如何令產出跌至 Yf。
parts.modelAnswer: 旅客減少令出口下降，總需求向左移，短期產出由 Y0 降至 Y1=Yf，恢復長期均衡。
markingPoints: 正確標示初始及新產出。

visuals.alt: 圖二：香港的總供應－總需求模型
visuals.caption: 圖二：香港的總供應－總需求模型

questions.topicGroup: 總需求及/或總供應改變導致均衡產出水平和物價水平的改變
questions.keyPoint: 由短期均衡達至長期均衡的機制
questions.stem: 香港初始有通脹差距，內地旅客人數下降。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 毋須圖表，解釋市場力量如何令長期產出下降至 Yf。
parts.modelAnswer: 要素市場有超額需求，推高要素價格和生產成本，短期總供應隨時間向左移，產出回到 Yf。
markingPoints: 指出通脹差距／要素超額需求。
解釋要素價格和成本上升。
解釋 SRAS 向左移及回到 Yf。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 負面界外效應與經濟無效率；把外部成本內在化
questions.stem: 大量旅客令公共交通系統超出負荷，所有乘客的交通時間增加。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 以界外影響解釋為什麼交通系統過分擠擁時會缺乏效率。
parts.modelAnswer: 額外乘客令其他乘客承受沒有補償的時間成本，邊際社會成本高於私人成本／利益，使用量超過效率水平。
markingPoints: 解釋未獲補償的時間成本。
連繫 MSC 和過度使用。

questions.keyPoint: 以圖和數例找出利潤極大化產量和價格
questions.stem: 超級電力是 X 市唯一持牌電力供應商，採取單一定價。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 在圖三以 Q1 和 P1 標示利潤極大化產量和價格，並簡單解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 在 MR=MC 處生產 Q1，再由需求曲線讀取 P1。

visuals.alt: 圖三：壟斷者的需求、邊際收益及邊際成本
visuals.caption: 圖三：壟斷者的需求、邊際收益及邊際成本

questions.keyPoint: 說明為何簡單壟斷定價缺乏效率，即邊際利益 > 邊際成本，並以消費 者盈餘、生產者盈餘和效率損失解釋
questions.stem: 圖三顯示超級電力採取單一定價。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 以圖三解釋單一定價為什麼缺乏效率。
parts.modelAnswer: 在 Q1，邊際利益大於邊際成本，產出低於效率水平，未實現得益構成效率損失。
markingPoints: 解釋 MB 大於 MC。

visuals.alt: 圖三：壟斷者的需求、邊際收益及邊際成本
visuals.caption: 圖三：壟斷者的需求、邊際收益及邊際成本

questions.keyPoint: 可變成本及固定成本
questions.stem: 政府向超級電力徵收不隨產量改變的定額稅。

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: 解釋邊際成本會否上升。
parts.modelAnswer: 不會。定額稅是固定成本，不隨產出改變，所以不影響邊際成本。
markingPoints: 解釋固定成本不影響 MC。

questions.keyPoint: 以圖和數例找出利潤極大化產量和價格
questions.stem: 超級電力被徵收定額稅。

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: 在圖三以 Q2 和 P2 標示稅後產量和價格。
parts.modelAnswer: Q2=Q1 和 P2=P1，因邊際成本、利潤極大化產量和價格均不變。

visuals.alt: 圖三：壟斷者的需求、邊際收益及邊際成本
visuals.caption: 圖三：壟斷者的需求、邊際收益及邊際成本

questions.keyPoint: 價格分歧
questions.stem: 超級電力向住宅用戶收每度 $1.2，向工業用戶收每度 $0.9。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 這種安排構成價格分歧嗎？解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 構成。兩組消費者為同一種、以相同成本生產的電力支付不同價格。
markingPoints: 指出不同消費群組及價格。

questions.chapterTitle: 反競爭行為與競爭政策
questions.keyPoint: 反競爭行為
questions.stem: 超級電力收購供應九成發電原料的主要煤供應商。

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: 寫出可能構成的反競爭行為名稱，並解釋如何限制競爭。
parts.modelAnswer: 合併。它控制關鍵投入供應商，限制潛在競爭者進入。

questions.chapterTitle: 反競爭行為與競爭政策
questions.keyPoint: 反競爭行為
questions.stem: 超級電力東主聲稱收購煤供應商不是反競爭。

parts.label: (f)
parts.prompt: 提出一個理由論證這聲稱。
parts.modelAnswer: 收購可透過較低原料成本／規模經濟減低平均成本；若把得益轉給消費者以降低電價，未必反競爭。
markingPoints: 指出降低成本／規模經濟。

questions.keyPoint: 以邊際成本遞增的生產可能線，說明比較成本及貿易得益
questions.stem: 圖四有一條 PPF 和 PPF 內的 N 點。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 解釋該國會否在 N 點生產。
parts.modelAnswer: 不會，因 N 點表示有閒置資源，沒有盡量生產。
markingPoints: 解釋閒置資源／產出未極大化。

visuals.alt: 圖四：生產可能線、E 點及世界價格線 AB
visuals.caption: 圖四：生產可能線、E 點及世界價格線 AB

questions.keyPoint: 以邊際成本遞增的生產可能線，說明比較成本及貿易得益
questions.stem: 在 E 點，生產 1 單位 X 的本地成本是 2.5Y；AB 斜率是 X 的世界價格。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 解釋該國生產 X 是否擁有比較優勢。

questions.keyPoint: 量度經濟增長及經濟發展
questions.stem: 開放貿易後，該國人類發展指數上升。

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.prompt: 舉出一項國際貿易可令 HDI 上升的原因。
parts.modelAnswer: 貿易可轉移較佳科技，提高生產力和 GDP，或引進醫療科技以延長預期壽命。

questions.keyPoint: 經濟增長的好處和代價
questions.stem: HDI 上升，但居民認為生活水平下降。

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.prompt: 提出兩個可能原因。
parts.modelAnswer: 進口替代產業工人可能失業；收入分配可能更不平均；或生產較污染物品的專業化令污染增加。
markingPoints: 解釋每項如何降低生活水平。

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Apple Inc. launches a new smartphone model. Some people spend hours logging into its website to buy it.

parts.label: Q1
parts.prompt: If the resale value of the new model falls, the opportunity cost of buying through Apple’s website will decrease. Do you agree? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Not necessarily. Full cost includes price plus time cost; a lower resale value is not a forgone option. Alternatively, lower speculative demand may reduce queuing time and time cost.
markingPoints: Explains full cost includes monetary and time cost.

questions.keyPoint: Classification of private firms: sole proprietorship, partnership, private limited company and public limited company
questions.stem: Sure-Star Education Group is a tutorial centre that can issue shares and bonds to the general public.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Name the type of business ownership of the Group.
parts.modelAnswer: A public limited/listed company.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of issuing shares and bonds to raise capital
questions.stem: Sure-Star can issue shares and bonds to the public.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: From owners’ viewpoint, explain ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of issuing shares over bonds.
parts.modelAnswer: Shares have no interest burden and no redemption obligation, but dilute control rights or raise takeover risk.

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: Sure-Star runs more tutorial classes in different districts.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Give THREE reasons why its average cost decreases.
parts.modelAnswer: Advertising cost is shared by more students, purchases of raw material are in bulk, and division of labour becomes more extensive.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The table shows a firm with two machines and rising labour input.

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt: State the law of diminishing marginal returns and explain whether the data illustrate it.
parts.modelAnswer: Holding technology constant, as more variable input is added to fixed factors, marginal product eventually falls. Yes: labour rises from 3 to 4 while marginal product falls from 18 to 14.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: Customers take restaurant-food photos and share them on social media; some high-end restaurants forbid photos.

parts.label: Q4
parts.prompt: Explain how the photo-taking-and-sharing behaviour may involve externality.
parts.modelAnswer: It may create negative externality by disturbing diners or disclosing dishes, lowering restaurant revenue without compensation. Alternatively, it can create uncompensated promotion benefits for restaurants.
markingPoints: Identifies a valid positive or negative externality.

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 蘋果公司推出新款智能電話，部分人花數小時登入其網站購買。

parts.label: Q1
parts.prompt: 若新型號轉售價值下跌，透過蘋果網站購買的機會成本會下降。你同意嗎？解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 不一定。全部成本包括價格和時間成本，轉售價值下降本身不是放棄的選項；但投機需求下降可減少排隊時間和時間成本。
markingPoints: 解釋全部成本包括金錢及時間成本。
正確論證其中一種結果。

questions.keyPoint: 私人廠商的分類：獨資、合夥、私人有限公司及公眾有限公司

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 指出集團的企業所有權類型。
parts.modelAnswer: 公眾有限公司／上市公司。

questions.topicGroup: 股票及債券作為資金來源

parts.label: (b)

parts.modelAnswer: 股份沒有利息負擔和贖回責任，但可攤薄控制權或增加被收購風險。

questions.topicGroup: 內部規模經濟/規模負經濟

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 列出三項平均成本下降的原因。
parts.modelAnswer: 廣告成本由更多學生分攤、大量購買原材料及更廣泛分工。
markingPoints: 列出三項內部規模經濟。

questions.topicGroup: 短期投入與產出的關係
questions.keyPoint: 邊際回報遞減定律
questions.stem: 表格顯示一間廠商有兩部機器及逐步增加的勞工投入。

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt: 說出邊際報酬遞減定律，並解釋上述數據是否說明該定律。
parts.modelAnswer: 技術不變下，增加可變要素於固定要素，邊際產出最終下降。是；勞工由 3 增至 4 時，邊際產出由 18 降至 14。

questions.stem: 近年不少顧客把餐廳食物拍照並在社交媒體分享，部分高級餐廳不准拍照。

parts.label: Q4
parts.prompt: 解釋顧客拍照及分享行為如何可能涉及界外效應。
parts.modelAnswer: 行為可能騷擾其他食客或披露菜式，令餐廳收入下降而沒有補償，構成負外部性；亦可能為餐廳帶來未付費宣傳得益。
markingPoints: 指出一種有效正或負外部性。
解釋未獲補償的外部影響。

questions.stem: The chart shows the market shares of the top 10 solar photovoltaic module manufacturers in 2012.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: What was the market structure of the solar PV module market? List TWO features of this market structure.
parts.modelAnswer: Monopolistic competition. It has many sellers, product differentiation, non-price competition and imperfect market information.

questions.keyPoint: Natural resources: land
questions.stem: Solar panels installed on residential roofs generate solar energy in sunny western provinces of China.

parts.label: (b)

parts.modelAnswer: Sunshine is land, because it is a natural resource or gift of nature.
markingPoints: Explains that it is a natural resource/gift of nature.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: The European Union imposes an anti-dumping tariff on solar panels produced in China.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Under what condition will producers bear a greater tariff burden than buyers? Illustrate your answer with a supply-demand diagram.
parts.modelAnswer: Producers bear the larger burden when demand is more elastic than supply. A tariff shifts supply upward; the diagram shows a higher buyer price, lower seller price and a larger producer burden.
markingPoints: States demand is more elastic than supply.
Shows the upward supply shift caused by tariff.
Shows higher price paid by buyers and lower price received by producers.
Shows the producer burden is larger.

questions.topicGroup: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.keyPoint: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.stem: A public clinic charges $45 for medical service, much less than private doctors.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: When a public clinic provides medical service for one patient, the resulting rise in gross domestic product will be $45. Do you agree? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: No. Public services are usually subsidised and supplied below market price. GDP records their market value at market price or factor cost, which is higher than $45.
markingPoints: Explains the subsidised price is below market price/factor cost.
Links the valuation method to GDP.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem: Figure 1 shows the public medical-service market. The supply curve reflects marginal social cost.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: With reference to Source A, explain how the price set by public clinics may lead to economic inefficiency in providing public medical service.
parts.modelAnswer: The $45 fee is below equilibrium. Quantity transacted is below equilibrium quantity, creating a shortage/underproduction. At the missing units, marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost, causing deadweight loss.
markingPoints: Shows quantity transacted below equilibrium quantity.
Explains MB exceeds MC/there is underproduction.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram for public medical service.
visuals.caption: Figure 1: public medical service

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: The Hospital Authority targets elderly people, low-income individuals and patients with chronic diseases.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: With reference to Source B, explain how the services provided by the Hospital Authority can enhance equity.
parts.modelAnswer: It can equalise income by subsidising medical services mainly used by low-income people, or equalise opportunities by enabling chronically ill patients to continue work and earn income.
markingPoints: Applies the explanation to a target group in Source B.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: Some people propose raising public-clinic fees to reduce waiting time.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Evaluate the argument in terms of equity and economic efficiency.
parts.modelAnswer: Equity may worsen because poor people may no longer afford treatment or lose work opportunities through poor health. Efficiency may improve because a higher price is closer to equilibrium, narrows the MB-MC gap and reduces deadweight loss.
markingPoints: Explains a higher price moves toward equilibrium.
Links the change to a smaller MB-MC gap/deadweight loss.

questions.topicGroup: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.keyPoint: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.stem: The chart shows Macau gaming-industry revenue and aggregate output from 2014 Q1 to 2015 Q2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: With reference to the diagram, describe and explain the trend of the importance of the gaming industry relative to Macau's aggregate output.
parts.modelAnswer: Its relative importance declined because gaming revenue fell faster than GDP at current market price.
markingPoints: Compares the fall in gaming revenue with GDP.

visuals.alt: Revenue from Macau's gaming industry and aggregate output, 2014 Q1 to 2015 Q2.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Macau gives every resident a cash transfer under a cash-sharing scheme.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, explain how the scheme affects output and price level in the short run.
parts.modelAnswer: Cash sharing raises residents' disposable income and consumption, shifting AD right. With SRAS unchanged, both output and price level rise.
markingPoints: Explains higher consumption and a rightward AD shift.
Shows higher output and price level.

questions.keyPoint: Socio-economic implications of changes in public expenditure
questions.stem: Gaming revenue falls. The government considers reducing investment expenditure while retaining cash sharing; an economist suggests suspending cash sharing and allocating the money to investment.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Discuss the economist's suggestion by giving arguments FOR and AGAINST it.
parts.modelAnswer: For: investment raises potential output over time, while cash sharing mainly raises AD and may vanish if residents save. Against: ending cash sharing during a downturn may reduce welfare and political stability; investment takes time and can be inefficient if administration costs are high or price signals are weak.
markingPoints: Gives valid arguments for shifting spending to investment.
Gives valid arguments against the suggestion.
Explains the relevant short-run or long-run effects.

questions.keyPoint: Types of division of labour
questions.stem: A public airport corporation hires security guards, technicians, engineers and financial managers.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: What economic principle is illustrated by this practice? Suggest THREE reasons why applying it can increase labour productivity.
parts.modelAnswer: Division of labour/specialisation. Practice makes perfect, workers can be matched to suitable jobs, training time is saved, and work stimulation or mechanisation may result.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: The airport corporation can finance a new runway by raising income tax (Proposal A) or charging every departing traveller a lump-sum fee (Proposal B).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: Discuss the effects of the two proposals on the current account in Country H's balance of payments.
parts.modelAnswer: A higher income tax lowers disposable income, consumption, AD and output, so imports fall and the current account improves. A departing-passenger fee raises airport-use cost, reducing incoming and outgoing travellers and both imports and exports of services; its current-account effect is ambiguous.
markingPoints: Explains Proposal A reduces imports through lower disposable income/AD.
Explains Proposal A improves the current account.
Explains Proposal B reduces travel and services trade.
Recognises the ambiguous current-account effect of Proposal B.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: The airport corporation can finance a new runway by raising income tax (Proposal A) or charging every departing traveller a lump-sum fee (Proposal B).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: Discuss the effects of the two proposals on the average flight distance for departing travellers of Country H.
parts.modelAnswer: Income tax may reduce average distance if travellers switch from unaffordable long-distance to short-distance flights, although relative prices are unchanged so it may have no effect. A lump-sum fee makes long-distance flights relatively cheaper, so a higher proportion of long-distance flights raises average distance.
markingPoints: Explains one valid effect or no effect for Proposal A.
Explains the lump-sum fee changes relative prices.
Links this to more long-distance travel and a higher average distance.

questions.keyPoint: Determine the profit-maximising output and price graphically and numerically
questions.stem: A franchised ferry company is the only public-transport provider between Central and Cheung Chau. Figure 2 shows demand and marginal cost.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: Suppose the ferry company uses simple monopoly pricing. Indicate output and price as Qm and Pm respectively in Figure 2.
parts.modelAnswer: Qm is where marginal revenue equals marginal cost; Pm is read from the demand curve at Qm.

visuals.alt: Demand and marginal-cost diagram for the Cheung Chau ferry monopoly.

questions.keyPoint: Explain why simple monopoly pricing is inefficient, i.e. MB > MC, and illustrate it with consumer surplus, producer surplus and deadweight loss
questions.stem: Figure 2 shows the demand and marginal-cost curves for the ferry company.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: With the aid of Figure 2, explain why simple monopoly pricing leads to a deadweight loss.
parts.modelAnswer: At Qm, marginal benefit is higher than marginal cost. The omitted output between Qm and the efficient quantity creates deadweight loss.
markingPoints: Explains MB exceeds MC at Qm.

visuals.alt: Demand and marginal-cost diagram for the Cheung Chau ferry monopoly.
visuals.caption: Figure 2

questions.keyPoint: Determine the profit-maximising output and price graphically and numerically
questions.stem: Fuel price has fallen in recent years.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: How does the reduction in fuel price affect the ferry company's marginal cost?
parts.modelAnswer: Marginal cost falls.

questions.keyPoint: Explain why simple monopoly pricing is inefficient, i.e. MB > MC, and illustrate it with consumer surplus, producer surplus and deadweight loss
questions.stem: Fuel price falls, but the ferry company produces the same quantity and charges the same price.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain whether economic efficiency is affected. Illustrate your answer in Figure 2.
parts.modelAnswer: Efficiency falls. The fall in marginal cost enlarges the gap between marginal benefit and marginal cost and increases deadweight loss because output remains below the new efficient quantity.
markingPoints: Explains the larger deadweight loss/lower efficiency.

Shows the lower MC or additional deadweight loss.

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination
questions.stem: Central-to-Cheung-Chau ferry fares are $13.20 for adults and $6.60 for children.

parts.modelAnswer: Yes. Adults and children are charged different prices for the same ferry service, which is produced at the same cost.

questions.keyPoint: Anti-competitive behaviours
questions.stem: Cheung Chau seafood restaurants simultaneously raise prices by 15% on public holidays.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain under what situation the student's claim that the restaurants engage in anti-competitive conduct may be correct.
parts.modelAnswer: It may be correct if restaurant owners agree to fix prices and raise them together, that is, collusion, breaching the first conduct rule under the Competition Ordinance.
markingPoints: Links it to the Competition Ordinance/first conduct rule.

questions.keyPoint: Anti-competitive behaviours
questions.stem: Cheung Chau seafood restaurants simultaneously raise prices by 15% on public holidays.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.prompt: Give ONE reason to support the teacher's view that there may be an alternative explanation.
parts.modelAnswer: Demand may rise because more visitors arrive on public holidays, or supply may fall because production cost rises, for example due to hiring more part-time workers.
markingPoints: States a valid demand or supply explanation.

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with increasing marginal cost)

parts.label: (a)

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: At Country A's no-trade production point, the domestic cost of one unit of X is four units of Y. Country B's PPF intercepts are 75 units of Y and 12 units of X.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: With reference to domestic production cost in both countries, explain in which good Country A has a comparative advantage.
parts.modelAnswer: Country A's opportunity cost of 1X is 4Y. Country B's is 75/12 = 6.25Y. Country A has lower opportunity cost in X, so it has comparative advantage in X.

parts.modelAnswer: PA is the point where Country A's PPF is tangent to the world-price line.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the answer in part (b) changes.
parts.modelAnswer: No. Both goods' productivity double by the same proportion, so Country B's opportunity costs are unchanged and Country A still has comparative advantage in X.

questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting the growth of an economy
questions.stem: Country A suffers brain drain: many highly educated residents migrate to other countries.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain TWO effects of brain drain on Country A's economic growth.
parts.modelAnswer: It lowers per-capita GDP and human capital/labour productivity; it can lower capital productivity because labour and capital are complementary, and slow research and development.
markingPoints: States two valid effects on economic growth.

questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting the growth of an economy
questions.stem: Country A suffers brain drain as highly educated residents migrate abroad.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.prompt: In the light of globalisation, suggest ONE government policy to relieve the problem. Briefly explain your answer.
parts.modelAnswer: For example, import high-skilled labour, offer scholarships to attract overseas students, relax immigration rules to target overseas talent, or introduce a return-migration policy.
markingPoints: Briefly explains how it relieves brain drain.

parts.prompt: 上述太陽能光電模組的市場屬哪種市場結構？列出該市場結構的兩項特點。
parts.modelAnswer: 壟斷性競爭。特點包括很多賣方、產品有少許差異、非價格競爭和市場資訊不完全。

questions.keyPoint: 天然資源：土地
questions.stem: 在陽光充沛的中國西部省份，很多住宅把太陽能電池板安裝在屋頂發電。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 解釋陽光在生產太陽能時屬哪種生產要素。

questions.chapterTitle: 需求和供應的價格彈性
questions.keyPoint: 影響需求價格彈性的因素
questions.stem: 歐盟對中國製造的太陽能電池板徵收反傾銷關稅。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 在甚麼條件下，生產商會比買家承受更高的關稅負擔？以供需圖說明。
parts.modelAnswer: 當需求較供應富彈性時，生產商承受較大負擔。關稅令供應曲線向上移；圖中買家支付的價格上升、生產商實收價格下降，且生產商負擔較大。
markingPoints: 指出需求較供應富彈性。
顯示關稅令供應向上移。
顯示買家價格上升和生產商實收價格下降。

questions.topicGroup: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.keyPoint: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.stem: 一家公立診所收取 45 元醫療服務費，遠低於私家醫生的收費。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 當一家公立診所向一名病人提供醫療服務，本地生產總值會因而增加 45 元。你同意嗎？試加解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 不同意。公共服務通常獲津貼並以低於市價提供；GDP 以市價或要素成本計算其價值，會高於 45 元。
markingPoints: 解釋津貼價格低於市價／要素成本。
連繫 GDP 的估值方法。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.topicGroup: 以供需圖輔助，分析市場干預對消費者盈餘、生產者盈餘和效率的影響
questions.keyPoint: 價格上限
questions.stem: 圖一顯示公共醫療服務市場；供應曲線完全反映其邊際社會成本。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 參考資料甲，解釋公立診所訂立的價格如何可能導致提供公共醫療服務缺乏經濟效率。
parts.modelAnswer: 45 元低於均衡價格，交易量低於均衡數量，造成短缺／供應不足。在缺少的服務數量上，邊際利益大於邊際成本，造成效率損失。
markingPoints: 顯示 45 元低於均衡價格。
顯示交易量低於均衡數量。
解釋邊際利益大於邊際成本／供應不足。

visuals.alt: 公共醫療服務的供求圖。
visuals.caption: 圖一：公共醫療服務

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(II)
questions.keyPoint: 收入均等化
questions.stem: 醫院管理局以長者、低收入人士和長期病患者為服務對象。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 參考資料乙，解釋醫院管理局提供的服務如何可以促進公平。
parts.modelAnswer: 它可透過補貼低收入人士較常使用的醫療服務以均等收入，或讓長期病患者繼續工作和賺取收入以均等機會。
markingPoints: 解釋收入均等化或機會均等化。
把解釋應用到資料乙的對象。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(II)
questions.keyPoint: 收入均等化
questions.stem: 有人認為公立診所應提高收費以減少輪候時間。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 以公平和經濟效率為依據，評估這個看法。
parts.modelAnswer: 公平可能惡化，因窮人或無力負擔服務，或因健康不佳失去工作機會。效率可改善，因較高價格更接近均衡，縮窄邊際利益和邊際成本的差距，減少效率損失。
markingPoints: 解釋一項不利的公平影響。
連繫較小的邊際利益－邊際成本差距／效率損失。

questions.topicGroup: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.keyPoint: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.stem: 圖表顯示 2014 年第一季至 2015 年第二季澳門博彩業收入和總產出。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 參考上圖，描述及解釋澳門的博彩業相對於該地區總產出的重要性趨勢。
parts.modelAnswer: 博彩業的相對重要性下降，因為博彩業收入下降的速度較以現時市價計的本地生產總值快。
markingPoints: 比較博彩業收入與 GDP 的跌幅。

visuals.alt: 2014 年第一季至 2015 年第二季澳門博彩業收入和總產出。
visuals.caption: 澳門博彩業收入和總產出

questions.topicGroup: 總需求及/或總供應改變導致均衡產出水平和物價水平的改變
questions.keyPoint: 透過明確說明受影響的總需求組成部分及/ 或影響短期總供應及/或長期總供應的因素，解釋某情況會如何導致總需求、短期總供應及/ 或長期總供應轉變，因而令總需求曲線、短期總供應曲線及/或長期總供應曲線移動
questions.stem: 澳門政府推行現金分享計劃，每位居民均可獲政府派發現金。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 以總供應－總需求圖輔助，解釋該現金分享計劃如何影響短期的產出和價格水平。
parts.modelAnswer: 現金分享提高居民可支配收入和消費，總需求向右移。在短期總供應不變下，產出和價格水平都上升。
markingPoints: 解釋消費增加及總需求向右移。
顯示產出和價格水平上升。

questions.keyPoint: 改變公共支出對社會經濟的影響
questions.stem: 博彩業稅收下跌，政府考慮減少投資開支但保留現金分享計劃；有經濟學者建議暫停現金分享，改把款項分配至投資。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 提出正反論點，討論經濟學者的建議。
parts.modelAnswer: 支持：投資長遠可增加潛在產出，現金分享主要提升總需求，若居民儲蓄則效果消失。反對：在經濟低迷時取消分享可降低社會福利和政治穩定；投資需時見效，行政成本高或對價格訊號不敏感時亦可缺乏效率。
markingPoints: 解釋相關短期或長期影響。

questions.keyPoint: 分工的種類
questions.stem: H 國的機場管理公司聘請保安員、技術員、工程師和財務經理等不同職員。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 該做法說明了哪項經濟原理？舉出三項理由，解釋為什麼應用該原理會提高勞工的生產力。
parts.modelAnswer: 分工／專業化。熟能生巧、把最合適的人安排到工作、節省訓練時間，以及可導致工作受到激勵或機械化。
markingPoints: 列出三項有效的生產力原因。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 經常帳（主要組成部分：貨物、服務、收益及經常轉移）
questions.keyPoint: 一宗交易會否及如何影響經常帳
questions.stem: 機場管理公司可透過增加入息稅（建議 A）或向每名離境旅客收取一筆固定費用（建議 B）為新跑道融資。

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: 討論兩個建議對 H 國國際收支平衡表中經常帳的影響。
parts.modelAnswer: 增加入息稅降低可支配收入、消費、總需求和產出，進口減少，經常帳改善。離境旅客費增加使用機場成本，減少進出境旅客和服務進出口，對經常帳的影響不確定。
markingPoints: 解釋建議 A 透過可支配收入／總需求減少進口。
解釋建議 A 改善經常帳。
解釋建議 B 減少旅遊和服務貿易。
指出建議 B 對經常帳的影響不確定。

questions.keyPoint: 徵稅的影響
questions.stem: 機場管理公司可透過增加入息稅（建議 A）或向每名離境旅客收取一筆固定費用（建議 B）為新跑道融資。

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: 討論兩個建議對 H 國離境旅客的平均飛行旅程距離的影響。
parts.modelAnswer: 入息稅可令旅客由負擔不起的長途航班轉到短途航班而降低平均距離，但因長短途航班相對價格不變，亦可沒有影響。固定費令長途航班相對較便宜，較多旅客選擇長途航班，平均距離上升。
markingPoints: 解釋建議 A 的一項有效影響或沒有影響。
解釋固定費改變相對價格。
連繫較多長途旅行和較高平均距離。

questions.keyPoint: 以圖和數例找出利潤極大化產量和價格
questions.stem: 長洲是香港的離島，只可乘渡輪前往；一間專營渡輪公司提供中環和長洲之間的公共運輸服務。圖二顯示需求和邊際成本。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: 假設渡輪公司以單一壟斷定價。在圖二以 Qm 和 Pm 分別標示產出量和價格。
parts.modelAnswer: Qm 在邊際收益等於邊際成本之處；Pm 由 Qm 向上至需求曲線讀取。

visuals.alt: 長洲渡輪壟斷的需求和邊際成本圖。
visuals.caption: 圖二

questions.keyPoint: 說明為何簡單壟斷定價缺乏效率，即邊際利益 > 邊際成本，並以消費 者盈餘、生產者盈餘和效率損失解釋
questions.stem: 圖二顯示渡輪公司的需求和邊際成本曲線。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 以圖二輔助，解釋為什麼該定價安排會導致效率損失。
parts.modelAnswer: 在 Qm，邊際利益高於邊際成本。Qm 與有效率數量之間未被生產的產出造成效率損失。
markingPoints: 正確顯示效率損失範圍。
解釋在 Qm 邊際利益大於邊際成本。

visuals.alt: 長洲渡輪壟斷的需求和邊際成本圖。
visuals.caption: 圖二

questions.keyPoint: 以圖和數例找出利潤極大化產量和價格
questions.stem: 燃料價格近年下降。

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: 燃料價格下降會如何影響渡輪公司的邊際成本？
parts.modelAnswer: 邊際成本下降。

visuals.alt: 長洲渡輪壟斷的需求和邊際成本圖。
visuals.caption: 圖二

questions.keyPoint: 說明為何簡單壟斷定價缺乏效率，即邊際利益 > 邊際成本，並以消費 者盈餘、生產者盈餘和效率損失解釋
questions.stem: 燃料價格下降後，渡輪公司維持相同產量和價格。

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: 解釋經濟效率會否受影響，並在圖二說明。
parts.modelAnswer: 效率下降。邊際成本下降令邊際利益和邊際成本的差距擴大；因產出仍低於新效率數量，效率損失增加。
markingPoints: 解釋效率損失增加／效率下降。
解釋產量不變時邊際利益－邊際成本差距擴大。
顯示較低邊際成本或額外效率損失。

visuals.alt: 長洲渡輪壟斷的需求和邊際成本圖。
visuals.caption: 圖二

questions.keyPoint: 價格分歧
questions.stem: 由中環至長洲的渡輪服務，成人費用為 13.20 元，小童費用為 6.60 元。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 解釋上述安排是否構成價格分歧。
parts.modelAnswer: 是。成人和小童兩組消費者就同一項、以相同成本生產的渡輪服務支付不同價格。
markingPoints: 指出不同消費群組支付不同價格。

visuals.caption: 由中環至長洲渡輪服務的費用

questions.chapterTitle: 反競爭行為與競爭政策
questions.keyPoint: 反競爭行為
questions.stem: 長洲多間提供海鮮菜式的餐廳同時在公眾假期加價 15%。

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.prompt: 解釋在甚麼情況下，學生指餐廳有反競爭行為的評論可能正確。
parts.modelAnswer: 若餐廳東主同意定價和一起加價，即串謀，便會違反《競爭條例》下的第一行為守則。
markingPoints: 連繫《競爭條例》／第一行為守則。

questions.chapterTitle: 反競爭行為與競爭政策
questions.keyPoint: 反競爭行為
questions.stem: 長洲多間海鮮餐廳在公眾假期同時加價 15%。

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.prompt: 提出一項理由支持老師「價格上升可能有另一個解釋」的回應。
parts.modelAnswer: 假期有較多遊客令需求增加，或因要聘請更多兼職員工等，生產成本上升令供應減少。
markingPoints: 提出一項有效需求或供應解釋。

questions.keyPoint: 以邊際成本遞增的生產可能線，說明比較成本及貿易得益
questions.stem: 圖三中 MN 和 TU 分別是甲國和乙國的生產可能線，甲國的生產可能線向原點凹入。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 解釋為什麼甲國的生產可能線是向原點凹入的。
parts.modelAnswer: 甲國生產 X 和 Y 的邊際成本均遞增。

visuals.alt: 甲國和乙國的生產可能線。
visuals.caption: 圖三

questions.keyPoint: 根據個案資料，解釋哪個國家在生產某物品上擁有比較優勢
questions.stem: 甲國沒有貿易時，生產 1 單位 X 的本地生產成本是 4 單位 Y；乙國的 PPF 截距是 75 單位 Y 和 12 單位 X。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 參考兩國的本地生產成本，解釋甲國在哪種物品上有比較優勢。
parts.modelAnswer: 甲國生產 1X 的機會成本為 4Y；乙國為 75/12 = 6.25Y。甲國生產 X 的成本較低，因此在 X 上有比較優勢。
markingPoints: 指出甲國在 X 上有比較優勢。

visuals.alt: 甲國和乙國的生產可能線。
visuals.caption: 圖三

questions.keyPoint: 以邊際成本遞增的生產可能線，說明比較成本及貿易得益
questions.stem: 虛線的斜率是物品 X 的世界價格。

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: 在圖三標示甲國在貿易後的生產點 PA。
parts.modelAnswer: PA 是甲國 PPF 與世界價格線相切之處。

visuals.alt: 甲國和乙國的生產可能線。
visuals.caption: 圖三

questions.keyPoint: 以邊際成本遞增的生產可能線，說明比較成本及貿易得益
questions.stem: 虛線的斜率是物品 X 的世界價格。

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: 在圖三標示甲國的貿易後消費點 CA；條件是甲國在貿易後消費相同數量的物品 X。
parts.modelAnswer: CA 位於世界價格線上、EA 的正上方，與 EA 有相同 X 座標。

visuals.alt: 甲國和乙國的生產可能線。
visuals.caption: 圖三

questions.keyPoint: 以邊際成本遞增的生產可能線，說明比較成本及貿易得益
questions.stem: 虛線的斜率是物品 X 的世界價格。

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.prompt: 在圖三標示甲國的進口量和出口量。
parts.modelAnswer: 甲國出口 X 的數量為 EA 至 PA 的水平距離，進口 Y 的數量為 EA 至 CA 的垂直距離。

visuals.alt: 甲國和乙國的生產可能線。
visuals.caption: 圖三

questions.keyPoint: 根據個案資料，解釋哪個國家在生產某物品上擁有比較優勢
questions.stem: 乙國的科技進步有助把物品 X 和 Y 的生產力增加一倍。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 解釋 (b) 部的答案會否改變。
parts.modelAnswer: 不會。兩種物品的生產力按相同比例增加，乙國的機會成本不變，甲國仍在 X 上有比較優勢。

questions.keyPoint: 影響經濟增長的因素
questions.stem: 甲國有人才流失問題，很多高學歷居民移居其他國家。

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.prompt: 解釋人才流失對甲國經濟增長的兩項影響。
parts.modelAnswer: 人均 GDP 和人力資本／勞工生產力下降；由於勞工和資本互補，資本邊際生產力可下降，研究和發展亦會放緩。
markingPoints: 指出兩項對經濟增長的有效影響。

questions.keyPoint: 影響經濟增長的因素
questions.stem: 甲國有高學歷居民移居其他國家的人才流失問題。

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.prompt: 根據全球化的概念，提出一項甲國政府可實行的政策以紓緩該問題，並簡單解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 例如輸入高技術勞工、提供獎學金吸引海外學生、放寬移民政策以吸引海外人才，或推行回流政策。
markingPoints: 簡單解釋政策如何紓緩人才流失。

questions.keyPoint: Definition of free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: MOOC teaching materials are online and free of charge.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain whether they are free goods.
parts.modelAnswer: No. They have positive marginal production cost/use value, or are produced from resources with alternative uses.
markingPoints: Explains scarcity or positive marginal cost.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: MOOC teaching materials are online and free of charge.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain whether they are public goods.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes, provided access is uncongested: one person's download and study do not reduce availability to others, so consumption is non-rivalrous.
markingPoints: States yes under the stated condition.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: One student takes a free MOOC; another takes a paid campus course with the same content and hours.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Will the cost of the MOOC necessarily be lower? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: No. The MOOC student's time cost and internet cost may exceed the campus student's time cost plus course fee, for example because online access and communication take extra time.
markingPoints: Explains a time or internet cost difference.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning and examples of the three types of production; identify the type of production
questions.stem: Many electronic-product retailers are located in Mong Kok.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: To which type of production do they belong? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Tertiary production, because retailing provides services.

questions.keyPoint: External economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: Many electronic-product retailers are located in Mong Kok.

parts.label: (b)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 從公平和總產出角度評估建議。
parts.modelAnswer: 延長免費教育可令較貧窮人士獲更多教育，均等機會並提高日後收入能力。教育開支增加可提升總需求，而人力資本提高長遠產出；但留校會減少目前勞力供應。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 從公平和總產出角度評估建議。
parts.modelAnswer: 福利可縮窄在職與失業人士的收入差距。它提高可支配收入、消費、總需求和產出，但亦可能削弱勞力供應誘因、導致技能退化並降低目前及日後產出。

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Serine prefers, in order, to work for the government as an administrative officer; to work in an accounting firm as a trainee; and to continue seeking a job without accepting an offer.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Analyse whether Serine's opportunity cost of choosing to work as an administrative officer will necessarily remain unchanged if the government reduces the starting salary of administrative officers.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. The salary reduction lowers the value of Serine's chosen option, but does not affect the highest-valued option forgone.
markingPoints: Explains that the highest-valued forgone option is unchanged.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Serine prefers, in order, to work for the government as an administrative officer; to work in an accounting firm as a trainee; and to continue seeking a job without accepting an offer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Analyse whether Serine's opportunity cost of choosing to work as an administrative officer will necessarily remain unchanged if the government provides unemployment benefits for all graduates seeking jobs.
parts.modelAnswer: No. Unemployment benefits may raise the value of continuing to seek a job above the trainee job. The highest-valued forgone option, and hence the opportunity cost, may then change.
markingPoints: Explains that the third option may become more valuable than the second.
Links this to a changed opportunity cost.

questions.keyPoint: Price floor

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt: With the aid of Figure 1, explain whether the rise in the price floor could enhance economic efficiency.
parts.modelAnswer: No. Pa is ineffective, whereas Pb is an effective price floor. Quantity falls below the efficient quantity, so marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost over the lost trades and deadweight loss results.
markingPoints: Explains the lower quantity and MB greater than MC.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain TWO possible undesirable effects of the fiscal policy on the US economy as a whole.
parts.modelAnswer: Higher taxes and lower government expenditure reduce aggregate demand and GDP. Higher income tax can also reduce work incentives, labour supply, employment and output.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Briefly discuss ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of printing money compared with the fiscal policy.
parts.modelAnswer: An increase in money supply can lower interest rates and raise investment, output and employment in the short run. In the long run it cannot raise output or employment, and excessive money growth can cause high inflation.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case

parts.modelAnswer: 不會。失業援助金可令第三選項的價值高於第二選項，故最高價值的放棄選項及機會成本可能改變。
