questions.stem: 亞榮在旺角開設一家售賣手提電話配件的店舖。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 舉出在亞榮的業務中所涉及可變成本的一個例子。試加以解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 購買配件的成本或兼職員工的工資；這些開支會隨店舖的產出轉變。
markingPoints: 舉出有效可變成本例子。

questions.keyPoint: 辨識市場結構種類
questions.stem: 亞榮在旺角開設一家售賣手提電話配件的店舖。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 指出香港的手提電話配件零售商屬於哪種市場結構。舉出兩個理由加以闡釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 壟斷性競爭。有很多沒有支配力的賣家，產品有差異，並可自由進出市場。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.topicGroup: 以供需圖輔助，分析市場干預對消費者盈餘、生產者盈餘和效率的影響
questions.keyPoint: 價格下限
questions.stem: 圖一顯示物品 X 的市場供應和市場需求曲線。政府把價格下限由 Pa 提升至 Pb。

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt: 以圖一輔助，解釋這樣提升價格下限能否改善經濟效率。
parts.modelAnswer: 不能。Pa 無效而 Pb 成為有效價格下限，交易量低於效率水平；在失去的交易中邊際利益高於邊際成本，因而出現無謂損失。
markingPoints: 解釋 Pb 成為有效價格下限。
解釋交易量下降及邊際利益大於邊際成本。
在圖中正確標示無謂損失和相關數值。

visuals.alt: 圖一：物品 X 的市場供應和需求曲線，價格下限由 Pa 提升至 Pb
visuals.caption: 圖一：物品 X 的市場供應和需求曲線，價格下限由 Pa 提升至 Pb

questions.keyPoint: 了解各類結合的含義並加以舉例
questions.stem: 大快樂集團經營連鎖餐廳，提供中式食物；集團設立快樂學院，為廚師和經理提供專業培訓。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 這屬於哪類擴張？試加以解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 縱向後向擴張。集團擴展至較早的生產階段，直接控制廚師和經理等生產要素的供應。
markingPoints: 解釋控制較早生產階段的投入供應。

questions.keyPoint: 列出各類結合的可能動機
questions.stem: 大快樂集團經營連鎖餐廳，提供中式食物；集團設立快樂學院，為廚師和經理提供專業培訓。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 解釋這項擴張的兩個好處。
parts.modelAnswer: 它可提供較穩定的廚師和經理供應、善用品牌，並為將受聘的畢業生度身訂造課程以縮短培訓時間。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.keyPoint: 利用消費物價指數及本地生產總值內含平減物價指數，計算判斷一般物價水平的變動比率（通脹率通縮率）
questions.stem: 細閱以下有關某經濟的資料。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 計算 2013 年的通脹率。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.keyPoint: 消費物價指數及本地生產總值內含平減物價指數的區別
questions.stem: 細閱以下有關某經濟的資料。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 解釋以消費物價指數和以本地生產總值平減物價指數量度物價水平轉變的一個不同之處。
parts.modelAnswer: 消費物價指數只包括消費物品，而本地生產總值平減物價指數包括消費物品和生產物品；或前者採固定籃子，後者每年籃子可變。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹和通貨緊縮的影響
questions.keyPoint: 解釋為何出現非預期通貨膨脹（緊縮）時，債務人會得益（受損），而債權人會受損（得益）
questions.stem: 人們預期由 2012 年至 2013 年物價水平沒有轉變。潔文在 2012 年以固定名義利率借入樓宇按揭貸款。

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: 當上表所示的物價改變出現，解釋潔文會得益還是受損。
parts.modelAnswer: 潔文得益，因非預期通脹降低還款的實質價值／購買力。
markingPoints: 解釋還款實質價值下降。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 名義利率及實質利率的關係
questions.keyPoint: 了解方程式：名義利率 = 實質利率 + 預期通脹率
questions.stem: 人們預期由 2012 年至 2013 年物價水平沒有轉變。瑪蓮在 2012 年投資一個項目，預期名義回報率為每年 12%，2013 年實際名義回報率為每年 15%。

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: 當上表所示的物價改變出現，解釋瑪蓮會得益還是受損。
parts.modelAnswer: 瑪蓮受損。實際實質回報率是 10%（15% - 5%），低於預期的 12% 實質回報率。
markingPoints: 與預期實質回報率比較。

questions.keyPoint: 香港的徵稅
questions.stem: 嘉琳是香港居民，在上海的一家媒體集團任職攝影師。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 嘉琳在上海所賺的薪金要在香港納稅嗎？試加以解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 不用。根據地域來源徵稅原則，非源自香港的入息不會被香港政府徵稅。

questions.keyPoint: 直接稅與間接稅
questions.stem: 嘉琳是香港居民，在上海的一家媒體集團任職攝影師。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 薪俸稅是一項直接稅，還是間接稅？試加以解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 是直接稅，因納稅人不能把稅項負擔轉嫁給別人。

questions.topicGroup: 財政政策對 物價及產出 水平的影響
questions.keyPoint: 擴張性財政政策的影響
questions.stem: 美國政府嘗試一方面加稅，另一方面減低財政開支，以減低其不斷增加的財政赤字。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 解釋上述財政政策對美國整體經濟可能引起的兩個不良效果。
parts.modelAnswer: 加稅及減少政府支出會減低總需求和本地生產總值；較高所得稅亦可削弱工作誘因、勞力供應、就業和產出。
markingPoints: 解釋兩項有效不良效果。
把每項連繫總需求、產出或勞力供應誘因。

questions.keyPoint: 擴張性及緊縮性貨幣政策，包括改變法定儲備比率及貼現率
questions.stem: 美國政府嘗試一方面加稅，另一方面減低財政開支，以減低其不斷增加的財政赤字。另一替代政策是印發鈔票以支付財政赤字。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 與上述財政政策相比，簡單討論這替代政策對美國經濟的一項好處和一項壞處。
parts.modelAnswer: 增加貨幣供應可降低利率、提高投資、短期產出及就業；但長期不能提高產出或就業，過度貨幣增長更可造成高通脹。

questions.keyPoint: 根據個案資料，解釋哪個國家在生產某物品上擁有比較優勢
questions.stem: 甲國每單位資源可產 12 單位紙張或 3 單位手錶；乙國可產 8 單位紙張或 4 單位手錶。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 乙國會根據其比較優勢出口哪種物品？試加以解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 手錶。乙國生產一隻手錶的機會成本是 2 單位紙張，低於甲國的 4 單位。

questions.keyPoint: 計算貿易得益
questions.stem: 甲國每單位資源可產 12 單位紙張或 3 單位手錶；乙國可產 8 單位紙張或 4 單位手錶。兩國以 2 單位手錶交換 5 單位紙張。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 計算甲國從每單位進口可賺得多少。
parts.modelAnswer: 貿易條件為一隻手錶換 2.5 單位紙張。甲國自產一隻手錶要放棄 4 單位紙張，因此每進口一隻手錶得益 1.5 單位紙張。
markingPoints: 計算 1.5 單位紙張的得益。

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the tax burden
questions.stem: A country imposes a per-unit tax on sellers for every bottle of soft drink sold.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Under what condition will buyers bear a greater tax burden than sellers? Illustrate your answer with a supply-demand diagram.
parts.modelAnswer: Buyers bear more when demand is less elastic than supply. A unit tax shifts supply upward in parallel; the price paid rises, quantity falls, and the buyers' tax burden is larger than the sellers' burden.
markingPoints: Shows the parallel upward supply shift.
Shows a higher buyers' price and lower quantity.
Correctly labels both tax burdens and their relative size.

visuals.alt: Blank supply-demand diagram for a per-unit soft-drink tax
visuals.caption: Blank supply-demand diagram for a per-unit soft-drink tax

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on consumer surplus
questions.stem: A country imposes a per-unit tax on sellers for every bottle of soft drink sold.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the same diagram in (a), indicate the change in consumer surplus after the tax is imposed.
parts.modelAnswer: Consumer surplus falls by the buyers' tax burden plus the triangular area caused by the fall in quantity.
markingPoints: Correctly indicates the reduction in consumer surplus.

visuals.alt: Blank supply-demand diagram for a per-unit soft-drink tax
visuals.caption: Blank supply-demand diagram for a per-unit soft-drink tax

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: A country imposes the same tax on each soft-drink bottle irrespective of bottle size.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain, using the law of demand, why the proportion of larger-bottle soft drinks sold will increase.
parts.modelAnswer: The same tax per bottle makes the tax per litre lower for a larger bottle, so large bottles become cheaper relative to small bottles. By the law of demand, consumers buy relatively more large bottles.
markingPoints: Explains why tax per volume is lower for large bottles.
Links it to relatively greater purchases of large bottles.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem: Source 1 shows China's falling birth rate and rising old-dependency ratio from 2002 to 2011.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: With reference to Source 1, briefly discuss the possible change in future government tax revenue.
parts.modelAnswer: A lower birth rate slows growth of the future workforce and may shrink it. With fewer workers paying taxes, future tax revenue may fall.
markingPoints: Links it to lower tax revenue.

visuals.alt: Source 1: China's birth rate and old-dependency ratio, 2002-2011
visuals.caption: Source 1: China's birth rate and old-dependency ratio, 2002-2011

questions.keyPoint: Socio-economic implications of changes in public expenditure
questions.stem: Source 1 shows China's falling birth rate and rising old-dependency ratio from 2002 to 2011.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: With reference to Source 1, briefly discuss the possible change in future public health and welfare expenditure.
parts.modelAnswer: A higher old-dependency ratio means a larger elderly share. Older people may have lower incomes and greater medical needs, so public welfare and health expenditure may rise.
markingPoints: Explains the higher elderly share and needs.
Links it to higher public expenditure.

visuals.alt: Source 1: China's birth rate and old-dependency ratio, 2002-2011
visuals.caption: Source 1: China's birth rate and old-dependency ratio, 2002-2011

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.stem: The Chinese government considers relaxing the one-child policy to raise the birth rate.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: With reference to Source 2, discuss the possible effect on aggregate output in the long run.
parts.modelAnswer: Relaxation is likely to raise the birth rate, producing a larger future labour force. Long-run aggregate supply and output therefore increase.
markingPoints: Links the policy to a higher birth rate.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Goodbaby International, Hong Kong stock code 1086, is a large manufacturer and supplier of infants' and children's products in China.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: To what type of business ownership does Goodbaby International belong?
parts.modelAnswer: A public limited company, or listed company.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Goodbaby International is a listed company.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain the difference between a partnership and Goodbaby International in terms of transfer of ownership.
parts.modelAnswer: A partner cannot transfer ownership without other partners' consent, while shares in a public limited company are freely transferable.
markingPoints: States that public-company shares are freely transferable.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Goodbaby International is a listed company.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain the difference between a partnership and Goodbaby International in terms of legal status.
parts.modelAnswer: A partnership has no separate legal status, while a public limited company has independent legal status.
markingPoints: States that a partnership lacks separate legal status.
States that a public limited company has it.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of buying shares and bonds from small investors’ point of view
questions.stem: The government may relax the one-child policy and Goodbaby International produces baby products.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Without using a diagram, explain why Goodbaby International's stock price rose after the information was published.
parts.modelAnswer: People expected a higher birth rate and future demand for baby products. Expected profit and dividends per share rose, increasing demand for the shares and hence the stock price.
markingPoints: Links higher expected dividends to demand for shares and price.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: The Hong Kong dollar rose from 10.2 to 12.5 yen. Japan exports automobiles to Hong Kong and their yen price is unchanged.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: With the aid of Figure 2, explain why this leads to an increase in the total export value, in yen, of Japanese automobiles to Hong Kong.
parts.modelAnswer: The yen depreciates against the Hong Kong dollar, making Japanese cars cheaper in HKD. Hong Kong demand and quantity rise while the yen price is unchanged, so total export value in yen rises.
markingPoints: Shows a rightward demand shift, higher quantity and higher total value.

visuals.caption: Change in the exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar against the Japanese yen

visuals.alt: Figure 2: price and quantity of Japanese automobiles exported to Hong Kong
visuals.caption: Figure 2: price and quantity of Japanese automobiles exported to Hong Kong

questions.keyPoint: Production/value added approach
questions.stem: Japanese automobile exporters receive 100 billion yen sales revenue in 2013.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Give TWO reasons why their contribution to Japan's GDP would be less than 100 billion yen in 2013.
parts.modelAnswer: Some factor inputs, such as parts or raw materials, are imported, so their value is not Japanese value added. Some cars sold in 2013 may have come from inventory and were not produced in that year.
markingPoints: Explains imported inputs or inventory treatment.

visuals.caption: Change in the exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar against the Japanese yen

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem: The Japanese central bank purchases government bonds from Japanese commercial banks.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain whether Japan's monetary base will be affected.
parts.modelAnswer: Monetary base equals cash in public circulation plus commercial-bank reserves. It increases because commercial banks receive more reserves.
markingPoints: States the definition of monetary base.
States that reserves and monetary base increase.

questions.keyPoint: Describe the process of deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The Japanese central bank purchases government bonds from Japanese commercial banks.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Describe the deposit creation or contraction process that may result. Explain whether the process would further affect the monetary base.
parts.modelAnswer: Bond purchases create excess reserves. Banks lend the excess reserves, loans are redeposited, and the process repeats until actual reserves equal required reserves. It does not further change monetary base because total cash plus bank reserves is unchanged by credit creation.
markingPoints: Describes excess reserves, lending and redepositing.
States no further change in monetary base and explains why.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: The Japanese central bank purchases government bonds from Japanese commercial banks.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain the short-run effects on Japan's output and price levels with an aggregate-supply-aggregate-demand diagram.
parts.modelAnswer: Bond purchases increase money supply and lower interest rates, increasing investment or consumption and aggregate demand. In the short run, AD shifts right and both output and the price level rise.
markingPoints: States higher short-run output and price level.
Shows the rightward AD shift and new equilibrium.

questions.keyPoint: Determine the profit-maximising output and price graphically and numerically
questions.stem: Ng Fung Hong is the only agent authorised to export live cattle to Hong Kong from the mainland.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: With the aid of Figure 3, explain how its profit-maximising output and price are determined. Indicate them as Qm and Pm.
parts.modelAnswer: A monopolist maximises profit where marginal revenue equals marginal cost. Draw MR and identify Qm at MR=MC, then read Pm from the demand curve.

visuals.alt: Figure 3: demand curve for live cattle with a marginal-cost curve to be added
visuals.caption: Figure 3: demand curve for live cattle with a marginal-cost curve to be added

questions.keyPoint: Compare the output, price and efficiency implications of a monopoly under simple monopoly pricing and a perfectly competitive market
questions.stem: The live-cattle export market is opened to competition and becomes perfectly competitive; marginal cost is unchanged.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: With the aid of Figure 3, explain the effects on output and price. Indicate them as Qc and Pc.
parts.modelAnswer: Under perfect competition, output is where marginal cost equals marginal willingness to pay. Price falls and quantity rises; Qc and Pc are at the demand-MC intersection.
markingPoints: States the competitive condition MC equals marginal willingness to pay.
Explains lower price and higher quantity.

visuals.alt: Figure 3: demand curve for live cattle with a marginal-cost curve to be added
visuals.caption: Figure 3: demand curve for live cattle with a marginal-cost curve to be added

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination
questions.stem: A supermarket advertises fresh-beef discounts: the second pound is 10% further off and the third pound is 20% further off.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Does the pricing practice constitute price discrimination? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Either conclusion can be justified. It is not price discrimination if every consumer receives the same discount with no market segmentation; it can be price discrimination because buyers of different quantities pay different average prices for the same beef produced at the same cost.

questions.keyPoint: Anti-competitive behaviours
questions.stem: Ng Fung Hong agrees to supply fresh beef solely to one supermarket chain on condition that the chain does not sell imported frozen beef.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.prompt: Name the anti-competitive behaviour and explain how it restrains competition.
parts.modelAnswer: Exclusive dealing. It forecloses third-party access to the chain's distribution network.

questions.keyPoint: Anti-competitive behaviours
questions.stem: Several dominant supermarket chains agree to offer fresh-beef discounts simultaneously.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.prompt: Name the anti-competitive behaviour and explain how it restrains competition.
parts.modelAnswer: Price fixing. Their collusive action can drive smaller retailers out of the market.
markingPoints: Explains the restraint on smaller rivals.

questions.keyPoint: Compare the output, price and efficiency implications of a monopoly under simple monopoly pricing and a perfectly competitive market
questions.stem: The live-cattle market is opened for competition.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Give ONE justification for introducing the competition policy.
parts.modelAnswer: More sellers can improve efficiency through competition, and consumers can receive lower prices, higher quantity and better quality.
markingPoints: Explains the consumer or efficiency benefit.

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with constant marginal cost)
questions.stem: Figure 4 shows the PPFs of Countries A and B. Both allocate resources evenly between Goods X and Y.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain why the PPFs are straight lines.
parts.modelAnswer: Marginal and average costs of producing X and Y are constant, so the opportunity cost of X in terms of Y, the PPF slope, is constant.
markingPoints: Links them to a constant opportunity cost and straight PPF.

visuals.alt: Figure 4: production possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B
visuals.caption: Figure 4: production possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with constant marginal cost)
questions.stem: Country A has twice the resources of Country B. Figure 4 shows their PPFs.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain whether Country A has an absolute advantage in producing Good X.
parts.modelAnswer: No. Country B can produce 8 units of X with all its resources. With the same resources, Country A can produce only 5 (=10/2) units, so it lacks absolute advantage in X.
markingPoints: Compares output using the same resources.

visuals.alt: Figure 4: production possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B
visuals.caption: Figure 4: production possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with constant marginal cost)
questions.stem: Country A has twice the resources of Country B. Figure 4 shows their PPFs.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain whether Country A has a comparative advantage in producing Good X.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. The opportunity cost of one X is 1Y in A (10/10) but 2Y in B (16/8), so A has comparative advantage in X.

visuals.alt: Figure 4: production possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B
visuals.caption: Figure 4: production possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with constant marginal cost)
questions.stem: The international price of one X is 1.5Y.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: Show the production point of Country A after specialisation on Figure 4.
parts.modelAnswer: Country A produces at (10, 0).

visuals.caption: Figure 4: production possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with constant marginal cost)
questions.stem: The international price of one X is 1.5Y.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: Show Country A's consumption possibility frontier when there is trade on Figure 4.
parts.modelAnswer: Draw a straight CPF through (10, 0) with X-intercept 10 and Y-intercept 15.

visuals.alt: Figure 4: production possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B
visuals.caption: Figure 4: production possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with constant marginal cost)
questions.stem: The international price of one X is 1.5Y and Country A trades 4 units of X.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.prompt: Show Country A's consumption point on Figure 4.
parts.modelAnswer: The consumption point is (6, 6).

visuals.alt: Figure 4: production possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B
visuals.caption: Figure 4: production possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B

questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting the growth of an economy
questions.stem: Country A's PPF shifts outward because of changes in government policies on human capital.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Suggest TWO possible policy changes in Country A.
parts.modelAnswer: Examples include a tax allowance or subsidy for further education, larger university teaching grants for more degree places, or a larger immigration quota for experts and professionals.

questions.topicGroup: 物品及服務的稅項（銷售稅）

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 解釋日本的貨幣基礎會否受影響。
parts.modelAnswer: 貨幣基礎 = 在公眾流通的現金 + 商業銀行的儲備。它會增加，因商業銀行有更多儲備。
markingPoints: 指出儲備及貨幣基礎增加。

questions.keyPoint: 描述存款創造/ 收縮的過程

parts.label: (b)

parts.modelAnswer: 購債令銀行有超額儲備，銀行貸出超額儲備，貸款再存入銀行系統，直至實際儲備等於法定儲備。存款創造不會再改變貨幣基礎，因公眾現金和銀行儲備的總和不變。
markingPoints: 描述超額儲備、放款和再存款。

questions.keyPoint: Distinguishing between free goods and economic goods

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The table below shows the input-output relationship of a firm.

parts.label: Q2
parts.prompt: State the law of diminishing marginal returns and explain whether the above data illustrate the law.
parts.modelAnswer: Holding technology constant, when more units of a variable factor are added successively to a given quantity of fixed factors, the marginal product of the variable factor will eventually diminish. The data do not illustrate the law because both workers and machines change, so no fixed factor is held constant.
markingPoints: Explains that the data do not illustrate it because all factors change.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: According to a United Nations report in 2008, the Gini coefficients of Hong Kong and Beijing were 0.53 and 0.22 respectively.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain how an increase in the standard tax rate of salaries tax will affect the post-tax Gini coefficient of Hong Kong.
parts.modelAnswer: It will be lower if the tax is progressive: the higher-income group pays more tax and its post-tax income falls proportionately more, while the income of the lower-income group is less affected.
markingPoints: States the post-tax Gini coefficient falls.
Explains the different effects on higher- and lower-income groups.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Country A has imposed an effective price ceiling on Good X.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Suppose Country A eliminates all illegal transactions of Good X. Can this price control ensure all lower-income buyers obtain the quantity of Good X they plan to purchase? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: No. The effective price ceiling creates excess demand. Non-price competition such as queuing emerges, and the new competitive criteria do not necessarily depend on income, so lower-income buyers are not guaranteed the planned quantity.
markingPoints: Explains non-price competition such as queuing.
Explains that allocation is not necessarily based on income.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: After the effective price ceiling, many citizens in Country B travel to Country A to purchase Good X.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Will the balance of invisible trade of Country A be affected? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. Transportation and other tourist-related spending by visitors are exports of services, so the invisible trade account increases.
markingPoints: States that invisible trade is affected.
Explains the increase in service exports.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem: Suppose the effective price ceiling is lowered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Will the change in price ceiling improve economic efficiency? Explain with the aid of a diagram.
parts.modelAnswer: No. The lower price ceiling reduces the quantity transacted and creates a larger deadweight loss, so total social surplus falls.
markingPoints: Explains the larger deadweight loss or lower total social surplus.
Shows the lower price ceiling and larger efficiency loss in a demand-supply diagram.

answerVisuals.alt: Marking-scheme diagram: a lower price ceiling increases deadweight loss.
answerVisuals.caption: Marking-scheme diagram: a lower price ceiling increases deadweight loss.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Losses to society caused by unemployment
questions.stem: Rising unemployment is one of the phenomena which occurs during economic recession.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State TWO losses to society caused by unemployment.
parts.modelAnswer: Loss of output, loss of human capital and political unrest are valid losses; any two earn marks.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Features of the four phases of a business cycle
questions.stem: Rising unemployment is one of the phenomena which occurs during economic recession.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Other than rising unemployment, give TWO other economic phenomena which would occur during economic recession.
parts.modelAnswer: Falling or negative real GDP growth, falling inflation or deflation, and falling business confidence, investment or consumption are valid examples; any two earn marks.

questions.keyPoint: Qualities of good money
questions.stem: '9999 gold is preferred to cigarettes when used as money.' Give TWO reasons to explain this argument.

parts.label: Q7
parts.prompt: Give TWO reasons.
parts.modelAnswer: Gold is more durable, is more generally accepted as a medium of exchange and is more homogeneous than cigarettes. Any two valid reasons are acceptable.
markingPoints: Gives two valid reasons based on the qualities of good money.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: A country's currency depreciates against its trading partners' currencies.

parts.label: Q8
parts.prompt: Will the depreciation necessarily lower the total import value of this country in terms of domestic currency? Explain with the aid of the diagram.
parts.modelAnswer: No. If demand for imports is inelastic, the percentage increase in price is greater than the percentage decrease in quantity demanded, so import value in domestic currency can rise. The diagram should show price rising and quantity demanded falling, with the gain in import value greater than the loss.
markingPoints: Explains the price and quantity changes and the resulting import-value change.

answerVisuals.alt: Marking-scheme diagram: inelastic import demand and a higher import value.
answerVisuals.caption: Marking-scheme diagram: inelastic import demand and a higher import value.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: Country A requires 2 working-hours to produce a unit of shirts while Country B requires 1 working-hour. Country A requires 10 working-hours to produce a unit of watches while Country B requires 4 working-hours.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the opportunity costs of producing 1 unit of shirts in terms of watches for Country A and Country B.
parts.modelAnswer: Country A: 1 shirt costs 2/10 = 0.2 watch. Country B: 1 shirt costs 1/4 = 0.25 watch.

questions.topicGroup: State the principle of comparative advantage
questions.keyPoint: State the principle of comparative advantage
questions.stem: Country A requires 2 working-hours to produce a unit of shirts while Country B requires 1 working-hour. Country A requires 10 working-hours to produce a unit of watches while Country B requires 4 working-hours.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State the principle of comparative advantage. According to this principle, explain which country would export shirts.
parts.modelAnswer: A country should specialise in and export the good for which it has the lower opportunity cost. Country A would export shirts because 0.2 watch is lower than Country B's 0.25 watch.
markingPoints: Identifies Country A and explains the lower opportunity cost.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: Country A requires 2 working-hours to produce a unit of shirts while Country B requires 1 working-hour. Country A requires 10 working-hours to produce a unit of watches while Country B requires 4 working-hours.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the range of terms of trade over which exchange between both countries is mutually beneficial.
parts.modelAnswer: For one shirt, the terms of trade must satisfy 0.2 watch < 1 shirt < 0.25 watch, or equivalently 4 shirts < 1 watch < 5 shirts.
markingPoints: Gives the correct mutually beneficial range.

questions.topicGroup: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.keyPoint: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.stem: In 2011, the Financial Secretary announced the 'Scheme $6000'. Mr Chan received $6000 through the scheme in 2011.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: Should this item of payment by the government be included in the calculation of Gross Domestic Product of Hong Kong in 2011? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: No. The payment is a transfer payment and is not made in exchange for current production, so it is not included in GDP.
markingPoints: Explains that it is a transfer payment without corresponding production.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of buying shares and bonds from small investors’ point of view
questions.stem: Mr Chan considers investing the $6000 either in shares or bonds issued by a listed company.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain with TWO reasons why bonds could be a better choice than shares for Mr Chan.
parts.modelAnswer: Bonds provide interest even when the company makes no profit, and bondholders have a higher priority than shareholders for repayment if the company is liquidated.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: The Scheme $6000 provides $6000 to each Hong Kong permanent resident aged 18 or above.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Do you think that the government should introduce the Scheme $6000 to improve equity in Hong Kong society? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Equity is a normative concept. The payment may improve income equality because it is a larger percentage increase for lower-income people, but it does not equalise opportunities or outcomes for people who are ineligible. A reasoned evaluation is required.
markingPoints: Explains that equity involves value judgement.
Gives a supported argument for or against improving equity.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: The Scheme $6000 provides $6000 to each Hong Kong permanent resident aged 18 or above.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: With the aid of a diagram, explain how the Scheme $6000 would affect the price and output levels of Hong Kong in the long run.
parts.modelAnswer: Disposable income and consumption expenditure increase, so aggregate demand shifts right. In the long run aggregate output is unchanged at the vertical LRAS, while the price level rises.
markingPoints: Explains the consumption and AD increase.
Explains the vertical LRAS and unchanged long-run output.
Shows a higher price level in the diagram.

answerVisuals.alt: Marking-scheme diagram: AD shifts right against a vertical LRAS.
answerVisuals.caption: Marking-scheme diagram: AD shifts right against a vertical LRAS.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Definitions of inflation and deflation
questions.stem: Hong Kong's inflation rate rose to 7.9% last month.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: What is inflation?
parts.modelAnswer: A persistent increase in the general price level.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Effects of inflation and deflation on different aspects
questions.stem: Many workers have their salaries increased during inflation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the real income of these workers would necessarily rise.
parts.modelAnswer: No. Real income falls if the percentage increase in the price level is greater than the percentage increase in nominal wages.
markingPoints: Compares the percentage changes in prices and nominal wages.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Nominal interest rate as the (opportunity) cost of holding money
questions.stem: The government has issued inflation-linked bonds. The interest rate is positively related to the actual inflation rate of the last half-year period.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: What is the opportunity cost of holding cash instead of bonds?
parts.modelAnswer: The nominal return of the bonds.
markingPoints: Identifies the nominal return of the bonds.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Effects of inflation and deflation on different aspects
questions.stem: The government has issued inflation-linked bonds. The interest rate is positively related to the actual inflation rate of the last half-year period.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Explain how bonds would relieve the effect of inflation on their holders.
parts.modelAnswer: The interest return on the bonds rises at the same rate as actual inflation, helping preserve the purchasing power of the invested money.

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: The local property market is considered to be overheated. Most private housing is constructed by several major property developers in Hong Kong.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State the market structure of the private housing market and list TWO features of this market structure.
parts.modelAnswer: Oligopoly. It has a few dominant firms, interdependence of pricing policies, product differentiation, non-price competition or barriers to entry; any two features are acceptable.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Chinachem Group is one of the property developers in Hong Kong. It does not list its shares on the stock market.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State TWO advantages and TWO disadvantages of being a private limited company instead of a listed company.
parts.modelAnswer: Advantages include tighter ownership control and no need to disclose accounting information publicly. Disadvantages include inability to issue shares to the general public and difficulty transferring ownership.
markingPoints: Gives two advantages and two disadvantages.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in demand
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in demand
questions.stem: The government re-introduces the Home Ownership Scheme, under which eligible citizens can purchase a living unit at a great discount.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, explain how the re-introduction of the Home Ownership Scheme would cool down the private housing market.
parts.modelAnswer: HOS units and private housing are substitutes. A larger supply of public housing reduces demand for private housing, shifting its demand curve left and lowering the price and quantity transacted.
markingPoints: Shows a lower price in the diagram.

answerVisuals.alt: Marking-scheme diagram: demand for private housing shifts left.
answerVisuals.caption: Marking-scheme diagram: demand for private housing shifts left.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: The government re-introduces the Home Ownership Scheme, under which eligible citizens can purchase a living unit at a great discount.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: Without the aid of a diagram, explain how the mortgage interest rate could be adjusted to cool down the private housing market.
parts.modelAnswer: Raise the mortgage interest rate. Some people will fail or be unwilling to borrow at the higher rate, so demand for private housing drops.
markingPoints: States that the mortgage interest rate should rise.
Explains the effect on borrowing and housing demand.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate excess reserves, required and actual reserve ratios
questions.stem: The table shows the balance sheet of the banking system. The public does not hold cash and there are $100 million excess reserves.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the required reserve ratio. Show your working.
parts.modelAnswer: Required reserve ratio = ($500 million - $100 million) / $2 000 million = 20%.
markingPoints: Subtracts excess reserves from total reserves.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of the banking system

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The table shows the balance sheet of the banking system. The public does not hold cash and there are $100 million excess reserves.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum possible amount of deposits if the banks are fully loaned up. Show your working.
parts.modelAnswer: Maximum deposits = $500 million x (1 / 0.2) = $2 500 million.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of the banking system

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The central bank injects $200 million newly-printed banknotes into the banking system.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: If the banks lend out all of their excess reserves, what will be the amount of money supply? Show your working.
parts.modelAnswer: The new excess reserves are $100 million + $200 million = $300 million, so total deposits created are $300 million x (1 / 0.2) = $1 500 million. With no cash held by the public, money supply is $3 500 million.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of the banking system

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: The central bank injects $200 million newly-printed banknotes into the banking system.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Based on the quantity theory of money, predict the effect of the monetary policy in (c) on the price level. State the assumption(s) needed to reach your conclusion.
parts.modelAnswer: MV = PY. If velocity is constant and real output is constant or rises by a smaller proportion, the increase in money supply raises the price level, with the percentage increase in prices equal to the percentage increase in money if output is unchanged.
markingPoints: States the required assumptions and links higher money supply to higher prices.

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination
questions.stem: Large supermarket chains around the world are alleged to practise price discrimination.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: What is price discrimination?
parts.modelAnswer: It is a pricing behaviour in which different prices are charged to different customers for the same goods for reasons unrelated to differences in cost.

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination
questions.stem: Large supermarket chains around the world are alleged to practise price discrimination.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State TWO conditions for price discrimination.
parts.modelAnswer: The seller must be a price searcher; markets must be separable and resale must be difficult or costly; and customers in different markets may have different demand elasticities or information costs. Any two conditions are acceptable.

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination
questions.stem: Customers pay less for the same products during a promotional period.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain whether this constitutes price discrimination.
parts.modelAnswer: No. The lower price during the promotion applies to all customers and the seller does not separate customers into markets.
markingPoints: Explains that all customers face the same promotion price.

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination
questions.stem: Customers with discount coupons pay less for the same products.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain whether this constitutes price discrimination.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. The cost of serving customers with or without coupons is the same, while coupon users are charged a lower price; the coupon can also screen customers who are more price-sensitive.
markingPoints: Explains same cost and different prices or different demand elasticities.

questions.keyPoint: Anti-competitive behaviours
questions.stem: Some supermarket chains agree to raise the prices of the same products simultaneously.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.prompt: What kind of anti-competitive business practice is described, and is it a horizontal or vertical agreement?
parts.modelAnswer: Price fixing; it is a horizontal agreement because it is between competing sellers at the same level of production.

questions.keyPoint: Anti-competitive behaviours
questions.stem: Some supermarket chains request suppliers not to supply the same products to other sellers.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.prompt: What kind of anti-competitive business practice is described, and is it a horizontal or vertical agreement?
parts.modelAnswer: Exclusive dealing; it is a vertical agreement because it is between firms at different stages of production or distribution.

questions.keyPoint: Anti-competitive behaviours
questions.stem: Supermarket chains are involved in anti-competitive business practices.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: State TWO ways in which anti-competitive business practices may harm consumers.
parts.modelAnswer: They may lead to higher prices, lower output, fewer choices, a loss of consumer surplus and less market competition. Any two are acceptable.

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with constant marginal cost)
questions.stem: AA and BB are the production-possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B respectively.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: Which country has a comparative advantage in producing Good X? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Country B. The opportunity cost of one unit of X is 1Y in Country A and 20/30 = 0.667Y in Country B, so Country B has the lower opportunity cost.

visuals.alt: Question diagram: PPFs AA and BB for Country A and Country B.
visuals.caption: Question diagram: PPFs AA and BB for Country A and Country B.

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with constant marginal cost)
questions.stem: AA and BB are the production-possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B respectively.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: Is mutually beneficial trade possible between these two countries? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. Their opportunity costs of producing X and Y differ, so specialisation and trade can create gains from trade.

visuals.alt: Question diagram: PPFs AA and BB for Country A and Country B.
visuals.caption: Question diagram: PPFs AA and BB for Country A and Country B.

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with constant marginal cost)
questions.stem: AA and BB are the production-possibility frontiers of Country A and Country B respectively.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If the terms of trade are 10 units of X in exchange for 8 units of Y, what will be the gain from trade per unit of X traded for each country?
parts.modelAnswer: Country A gains 1Y - 0.8Y = 0.2Y per X. Country B gains 0.8Y - 0.667Y = 0.133Y per X.

visuals.alt: Question diagram: PPFs AA and BB for Country A and Country B.
visuals.caption: Question diagram: PPFs AA and BB for Country A and Country B.

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with constant marginal cost)
questions.stem: Country B finds new resources that raise the output of both Good X and Good Y by the same proportion.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain whether your answer in (a)(i) would change.
parts.modelAnswer: No. Country B still has a comparative advantage in X because the opportunity cost does not change when both intercepts rise in the same proportion.

visuals.alt: Question diagram: PPFs AA and BB for Country A and Country B.
visuals.caption: Question diagram: PPFs AA and BB for Country A and Country B.

questions.keyPoint: Illustration of comparative costs and gains from trade with the aid of PPF (with constant marginal cost)
questions.stem: Country B discovers a new technology that improves the production method of Good Y.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain whether your answer in (a)(i) would change.
parts.modelAnswer: It is uncertain. Country B may no longer have a comparative advantage in X if the maximum possible output of Y rises above 30 units, changing its opportunity cost.
markingPoints: States that the result is uncertain.
Explains that the opportunity cost may change.

visuals.alt: Question diagram: PPFs AA and BB for Country A and Country B.
visuals.caption: Question diagram: PPFs AA and BB for Country A and Country B.

questions.keyPoint: Measurement of economic growth and development
questions.stem: The Human Development Index (HDI) of Country B increases after trade.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.prompt: What does HDI measure?
parts.modelAnswer: HDI measures economic and social development in health, education and living standard, such as life expectancy, years of schooling and gross national income per capita.

questions.keyPoint: International/regional comparison
questions.stem: The Human Development Index (HDI) of Country B increases after trade.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.prompt: Suggest ONE possible reason for such an increase.
parts.modelAnswer: Trade can increase production, business activity and employment in the import/export industry, raising income per capita; imported health products or technology can also improve health.
markingPoints: Gives one valid trade-related reason linked to an HDI dimension.

questions.keyPoint: 區分免費物品及經濟物品
questions.stem: 某物品是免費的，它便是「免費物品」。你同意嗎？試加解釋。

parts.label: Q1
parts.prompt: 你同意嗎？試加解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 不一定同意。生產該物品可能使用有其他用途的稀少資源，因此即使不收取金錢，它仍可能是經濟物品。
markingPoints: 解釋稀少性及其他用途。

questions.topicGroup: 短期投入與產出的關係
questions.keyPoint: 邊際回報遞減定律
questions.stem: 下表顯示某廠商投入與產出的關係。

parts.label: Q2
parts.prompt: 寫出邊際回報遞減定律，並解釋上述資料能否說明該定律。
parts.modelAnswer: 在技術維持不變下，若連續增加某一可變生產要素，而固定生產要素數量不變，該可變要素的邊際產量最終會遞減。上述資料不能說明該定律，因為工人和機器均有改變，沒有固定生產要素。
markingPoints: 解釋資料中所有生產要素均改變。

visuals.caption: 某廠商的投入與產出關係

questions.keyPoint: 了解各類結合的含義並加以舉例
questions.stem: 某電訊服務供應商成立一間向公眾提供貸款的信貸公司。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 解釋上述情況屬於哪類擴張。
parts.modelAnswer: 這是混合擴張，因為廠商擴展至不相關的行業。
markingPoints: 解釋新業務與原有業務不相關。

questions.keyPoint: 列出各類結合的可能動機
questions.stem: 某電訊服務供應商成立一間向公眾提供貸款的信貸公司。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 列出上述擴張的三個可能動機。
parts.modelAnswer: 可能動機包括分散產品或收入以分散風險、把原有品牌名稱用於其他產品、共用資源，以及享有規模經濟。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(II)
questions.keyPoint: 詮釋堅尼系數提供的資料
questions.stem: 根據聯合國 2008 年的一份報告，香港及北京的堅尼系數分別是 0.53 及 0.22。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 與北京比較，香港貧富之間的收入差距較闊或較窄？
parts.modelAnswer: 較闊，因為香港的堅尼系數較高。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(II)
questions.keyPoint: 詮釋堅尼系數提供的資料
questions.stem: 根據聯合國 2008 年的一份報告，香港及北京的堅尼系數分別是 0.53 及 0.22。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 解釋增加薪俸稅的標準稅率如何影響香港的除稅後堅尼系數。
parts.modelAnswer: 若薪俸稅具累進性，除稅後堅尼系數會下降：較高收入組別承擔較多稅款，除稅後收入按比例跌幅較大，而較低收入組別的收入受影響較小。
markingPoints: 指出除稅後堅尼系數下降。
解釋高、低收入組別所受影響不同。

questions.keyPoint: 分析（有效）價格上限對（貨幣）價格、交易量及總收入等的影響
questions.stem: 甲國對物品 X 實施一個有效的價格上限。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 假設甲國杜絕物品 X 的所有非法交易，這項價格管制能否確保所有較低收入買家取得他們計劃購買的物品 X 數量？試加解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 不能。有效價格上限造成供不應求，因而出現排隊等非價格競爭，而新的競爭準則不一定以收入為依據，所以不能保證低收入買家取得計劃數量。
markingPoints: 解釋排隊等非價格競爭。
解釋分配不一定按收入進行。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 經常帳（主要組成部分：貨物、服務、收益及經常轉移）
questions.keyPoint: 一宗交易會否及如何影響經常帳
questions.stem: 實施價格上限後，乙國很多市民前往甲國購買物品 X。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 甲國的無形貿易差額會否受影響？試加解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 會。旅客的交通及其他旅遊相關支出屬於服務出口，因此無形貿易帳會增加。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.topicGroup: 以供需圖輔助，分析市場干預對消費者盈餘、生產者盈餘和效率的影響
questions.keyPoint: 價格上限
questions.stem: 假設有效價格上限被調低。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 該價格上限的轉變會改善經濟效率嗎？以圖輔助解釋答案。
parts.modelAnswer: 不會。較低的價格上限令交易量減少及效率損失擴大，總社會盈餘因此下降。
markingPoints: 解釋效率損失擴大或總社會盈餘下降。

answerVisuals.alt: 評分參考圖：較低價格上限令效率損失擴大。
answerVisuals.caption: 評分參考圖：較低價格上限令效率損失擴大。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.keyPoint: 失業造成的社會損失
questions.stem: 經濟衰退其中一個現象是失業增加。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 寫出失業對社會造成的兩項損失。
parts.modelAnswer: 產出損失、人力資本損失及政治動盪均可接受，寫出其中兩項。
markingPoints: 寫出兩項有效社會損失。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.keyPoint: 經濟周期四個階段的特點
questions.stem: 經濟衰退其中一個現象是失業增加。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 除了失業增加外，舉出經濟衰退時會出現的兩個經濟現象。
parts.modelAnswer: 實質本地生產總值增長下降或為負、通脹下降或出現通貨緊縮，以及企業信心、投資或消費下降均可接受，寫出其中兩項。
markingPoints: 寫出兩項有效衰退現象。

questions.keyPoint: 良好貨幣的特質
questions.stem: 「當用作貨幣時，9999 金較香煙佳。」提出兩項理由解釋這個論點。

parts.label: Q7
parts.prompt: 提出兩項理由。
parts.modelAnswer: 金較耐用；作為交易媒介較普遍被接受；金的質量較同質，而香煙的質量可以不同。任何兩項有效理由均可接受。
markingPoints: 根據良好貨幣的特質提出兩項理由。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 匯率改變對進口及出口的影響
questions.keyPoint: 匯率改變對進出口價格（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）、進出口數量及進出口價值（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）的影響
questions.stem: 相對於其貿易伙伴的貨幣，某國的貨幣貶值。這貶值會否必然降低該國的進口總值（以本國貨幣計算）？以下圖輔助，試加解釋。

parts.label: Q8
parts.prompt: 這貶值會否必然降低進口總值？試加解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 不會。若進口需求缺乏彈性，價格的百分比升幅大於需求量的百分比跌幅，以本國貨幣計算的進口總值可能上升。圖中應顯示價格上升、需求量下降，而進口總值的增加大於損失。
markingPoints: 解釋價格、數量及進口總值的改變。

answerVisuals.alt: 評分參考圖：進口需求缺乏彈性及進口總值上升。
answerVisuals.caption: 評分參考圖：進口需求缺乏彈性及進口總值上升。

questions.keyPoint: 根據個案資料，解釋哪個國家在生產某物品上擁有比較優勢
questions.stem: 甲國需要 2 工時生產一單位的恤衫，而乙國則需要 1 工時。另一方面，甲國需要 10 工時生產一單位的手錶，而乙國則需要 4 工時。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 計算甲、乙兩國生產一單位恤衫（以手錶計算）的機會成本。
parts.modelAnswer: 甲國：一件恤衫的機會成本為 2/10 = 0.2 隻手錶。乙國：一件恤衫的機會成本為 1/4 = 0.25 隻手錶。

questions.keyPoint: 寫出比較優勢原理
questions.stem: 甲國需要 2 工時生產一單位的恤衫，而乙國則需要 1 工時。另一方面，甲國需要 10 工時生產一單位的手錶，而乙國則需要 4 工時。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 寫出比較優勢原理。根據此原理，解釋哪國會出口恤衫。
parts.modelAnswer: 一國應專門生產及出口其機會成本較低的物品。甲國生產恤衫的機會成本為 0.2 隻手錶，低於乙國的 0.25 隻，因此甲國出口恤衫。
markingPoints: 指出甲國並解釋機會成本較低。

questions.topicGroup: 了解貿易實現互惠互利的先決條件
questions.keyPoint: 了解貿易實現互惠互利的先決條件
questions.stem: 甲國需要 2 工時生產一單位的恤衫，而乙國則需要 1 工時。另一方面，甲國需要 10 工時生產一單位的手錶，而乙國則需要 4 工時。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 指出在交易中能令兩國皆有利的貿易比率範圍。
parts.modelAnswer: 一件恤衫的貿易比率須為 0.2 隻手錶 < 一件恤衫 < 0.25 隻手錶；等同於 4 件恤衫 < 一隻手錶 < 5 件恤衫。
markingPoints: 寫出正確的互利貿易比率範圍。

questions.topicGroup: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.keyPoint: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.stem: 財政司司長在 2011 年公布「$6000 計劃」，向每位十八歲或以上的香港永久居民派發 $6000。陳先生在 2011 年收取 $6000。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: 該筆政府支付的款項應否包括在 2011 年香港本地生產總值的計算內？試加解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 不應。這是轉移支付，並非用作交換當期生產，所以不包括在本地生產總值內。
markingPoints: 解釋轉移支付沒有相應的當期生產。

questions.topicGroup: 股票及債券作為資金來源
questions.keyPoint: 從小投資者的角度出發，購買股票及債券的優點和缺點
questions.stem: 陳先生考慮把 $6000 投資在某上市公司發行的股票或債券上。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 舉出兩項理由解釋為甚麼對陳先生來說，債券可以是較股票為佳的選擇。
parts.modelAnswer: 即使公司沒有盈利，債券仍可帶來利息回報；若公司清盤，債券持有人的償還優先次序高於股東。
markingPoints: 提出兩項債券持有人的有效優點。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(II)
questions.keyPoint: 收入均等化
questions.stem: 「$6000 計劃」向每位十八歲或以上的香港永久居民派發 $6000。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 你認為政府應否推行「$6000 計劃」以令香港社會更公平？試加解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 公平涉及規範性判斷。這項計劃可能改善收入均等，因為對低收入人士的收入百分比增幅較大；但它不能令機會或結果完全均等，例如非永久居民及未滿十八歲人士不能受惠。答案須有理據。
markingPoints: 解釋公平涉及價值判斷。
提出有理據的支持或反對評估。

questions.topicGroup: 總需求及/或總供應改變導致均衡產出水平和物價水平的改變
questions.keyPoint: 透過明確說明受影響的總需求組成部分及/ 或影響短期總供應及/或長期總供應的因素，解釋某情況會如何導致總需求、短期總供應及/ 或長期總供應轉變，因而令總需求曲線、短期總供應曲線及/或長期總供應曲線移動
questions.stem: 「$6000 計劃」向每位十八歲或以上的香港永久居民派發 $6000。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 以圖輔助，解釋長期而言「$6000 計劃」如何影響香港的物價和產出水平。
parts.modelAnswer: 可支配收入及消費支出增加，總需求曲線向右移。長期總供應曲線垂直，長期總產出不變，但物價水平上升。
markingPoints: 解釋消費及總需求增加。
解釋垂直的長期總供應及產出不變。
在圖中顯示物價水平上升。

answerVisuals.alt: 評分參考圖：總需求向右移及長期總供應垂直。
answerVisuals.caption: 評分參考圖：總需求向右移及長期總供應垂直。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹及通貨緊縮的定義
questions.keyPoint: 通貨膨脹及通貨緊縮的定義
questions.stem: 細閱以下的新聞節錄：香港通脹率在上月份升至 7.9%。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 甚麼是通脹？
parts.modelAnswer: 一般物價水平持續上升。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹和通貨緊縮的影響
questions.keyPoint: 通貨膨脹和通貨緊縮在不同方面的影響
questions.stem: 很多工人在通脹期間獲得加薪。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 解釋這些工人的實質收入會否必然上升。
parts.modelAnswer: 不會。若物價水平的百分比升幅大於名義工資的百分比升幅，工人的實質收入會下降。
markingPoints: 比較物價及名義工資的百分比變化。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 名義利率及實質利率的關係
questions.keyPoint: 名義利率是持有貨幣的（機會）成本
questions.stem: 政府發行與通脹掛鈎的債券，利率與過去半年實際通脹率正相關。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 持有現金而不持有與通脹掛鈎的債券的機會成本是甚麼？
parts.modelAnswer: 債券的名義回報。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹和通貨緊縮的影響
questions.keyPoint: 通貨膨脹和通貨緊縮在不同方面的影響
questions.stem: 政府發行與通脹掛鈎的債券，利率與過去半年實際通脹率正相關。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 解釋與通脹掛鈎的債券如何紓緩通脹對持有人的影響。
parts.modelAnswer: 債券利息回報會與實際通脹率以相同速度上升，有助保存投資金額的購買力。
markingPoints: 解釋與通脹掛鈎的回報。

questions.keyPoint: 列出不同市場結構的一般特徵
questions.stem: 本地房屋市場被視為過熱，大部分私人住宅由香港數家主要地產發展商興建。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 寫出私人住宅市場的市場結構，並列出該市場結構的兩項特徵。
parts.modelAnswer: 寡頭壟斷。特徵包括少數主導廠商、定價政策互相依存、產品可以有差異、非價格競爭或進入市場有障礙；任何兩項均可接受。

questions.keyPoint: 比較不同所有權形式的特徵及利弊
questions.stem: 華懋集團是香港的地產發展商之一，但沒有在股票市場上市。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 與上市公司比較，列出成為私人有限公司的兩項優點及兩項缺點。
parts.modelAnswer: 優點包括股權控制較嚴密，以及毋須向公眾披露會計資料；缺點包括不能向公眾發行股票集資，以及所有權轉讓較困難。
markingPoints: 列出兩項優點及兩項缺點。

questions.keyPoint: 需求改變的影響
questions.stem: 政府決定重新推出居者有其屋計劃，合資格市民可大幅折扣購買住宅單位。

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: 以需求和供應圖輔助，解釋重新推出居者有其屋計劃如何冷卻私人住宅市場。
parts.modelAnswer: 居屋單位與私人住宅是代替品。公共房屋供應增加，令私人住宅的需求下降，需求曲線向左移，私人住宅價格及成交量下降。

answerVisuals.alt: 評分參考圖：私人住宅需求曲線向左移。
answerVisuals.caption: 評分參考圖：私人住宅需求曲線向左移。

questions.keyPoint: 擴張性及緊縮性貨幣政策，包括改變法定儲備比率及貼現率
questions.stem: 政府決定重新推出居者有其屋計劃，合資格市民可大幅折扣購買住宅單位。

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: 在沒有圖的輔助下，解釋如何調整按揭利率以冷卻私人住宅市場。
parts.modelAnswer: 提高按揭利率。部分人士會無法或不願意以較高利率借款，私人住宅需求因而下降。
markingPoints: 解釋借貸及住宅需求的改變。

questions.keyPoint: 了解及計算超額儲備、法定及實際儲備比率
questions.stem: 下表顯示某經濟內銀行體系的資產負債表。公眾不持有現金，而銀行體系有 100 百萬元超額儲備。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 計算法定儲備比率，寫出你的計算步驟。
markingPoints: 從總儲備扣除超額儲備。

visuals.caption: 銀行體系的資產負債表

questions.keyPoint: 了解及計算存款、放款、貨幣供應等在存款創造/ 收縮過程後的最大及實際改變
questions.stem: 下表顯示某經濟內銀行體系的資產負債表。公眾不持有現金，而銀行體系有 100 百萬元超額儲備。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 若銀行完全貸出資金，計算存款的最大可能數額，寫出你的計算步驟。

visuals.caption: 銀行體系的資產負債表

questions.keyPoint: 了解及計算存款、放款、貨幣供應等在存款創造/ 收縮過程後的最大及實際改變
questions.stem: 中央銀行把 200 百萬元新印鈔票注入銀行體系。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 若銀行貸出所有超額儲備，貨幣供應量是多少？寫出你的計算步驟。
parts.modelAnswer: 新的超額儲備為 100 + 200 = 300 百萬元；存款總額增加 = 300 x（1 / 0.2）= 1 500 百萬元。公眾沒有持有現金，因此貨幣供應量為 2 000 + 1 500 = 3 500 百萬元。
markingPoints: 計算貨幣供應量為 3 500 百萬元。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 通貨膨脹與貨幣數量論
questions.keyPoint: 貨幣數量論的意思
questions.stem: 中央銀行把 200 百萬元新印鈔票注入銀行體系。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 根據貨幣數量論，預測 (c) 的貨幣政策對物價水平的影響，並寫出作出結論所需的假設。
parts.modelAnswer: MV = PY。若貨幣流通速度不變，而實質產出不變或升幅較貨幣供應小，貨幣供應增加會令物價水平上升；若產出不變，物價百分比升幅等於貨幣供應百分比升幅。
markingPoints: 列出假設並連繫貨幣供應增加與物價上升。

questions.keyPoint: 價格分歧
questions.stem: 世界各地大型超級市場連鎖店被指實行價格分歧。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 甚麼是價格分歧？
parts.modelAnswer: 價格分歧是指對相同物品向不同顧客收取不同價格，而差異並非由成本差異造成。

questions.keyPoint: 價格分歧
questions.stem: 世界各地大型超級市場連鎖店被指實行價格分歧。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 寫出價格分歧的兩項條件。
parts.modelAnswer: 賣方必須是價格搜尋者；市場必須可以分隔，物品轉售困難或成本高；不同市場的顧客需求彈性或資訊成本可以不同。任何兩項均可接受。

questions.keyPoint: 價格分歧
questions.stem: 顧客在推廣期內購買相同產品時可付較低價格。

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: 解釋這是否構成價格分歧。
parts.modelAnswer: 不構成。推廣期的低價適用於所有顧客，賣方沒有把顧客分隔成不同市場。
markingPoints: 解釋所有顧客面對相同推廣價格。

questions.keyPoint: 價格分歧
questions.stem: 持有折扣券的顧客購買相同產品時可付較低價格。

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: 解釋這是否構成價格分歧。
parts.modelAnswer: 構成。服務持有或不持有折扣券的顧客成本相同，但前者付較低價格；折扣券亦可篩選出對價格較敏感的顧客。
markingPoints: 解釋成本相同而價格不同或需求彈性不同。

questions.chapterTitle: 反競爭行為與競爭政策
questions.keyPoint: 反競爭行為
questions.stem: 一些超級市場連鎖店同意同時提高相同產品的價格。

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.prompt: 這是哪一種反競爭商業行為？屬於橫向協議還是縱向協議？
parts.modelAnswer: 價格訂定；屬於橫向協議，因為協議雙方是處於同一生產層次的競爭賣方。

questions.chapterTitle: 反競爭行為與競爭政策
questions.keyPoint: 反競爭行為
questions.stem: 一些超級市場連鎖店要求供應商不要把相同產品供應給其他賣家。

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.prompt: 這是哪一種反競爭商業行為？屬於橫向協議還是縱向協議？

questions.keyPoint: Distinguishing between free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: The HKSAR government periodically publishes statistics related to the Hong Kong economy.

parts.label: Q1
parts.prompt: Explain whether the statistics on the internet are free goods.
parts.modelAnswer: No. The statistics are produced using scarce resources with alternative uses. Even if no money is charged, providing them has an opportunity cost.

questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem: Income inequality exists in an economy.

parts.label: Q2
parts.prompt: Give TWO reasons for the existence of income inequality in an economy.
parts.modelAnswer: Differences in human capital can lead to different earnings. Discrimination based on gender or race can also cause some groups to earn less. Other valid reasons include unequal ownership of capital.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The table below shows the input-output relationship of a firm.

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt: State the law of diminishing marginal returns and explain whether the above data illustrate the law.
parts.modelAnswer: Holding technology constant, when more units of a variable factor are added successively to a given quantity of fixed factors, the marginal product eventually decreases. The data illustrate the law because marginal product falls from 600 to 300 and then 200 as labour rises from 3 to 5 units.
markingPoints: Shows that marginal product falls as labour increases.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: More customers go to karaoke lounges during weekends, but the services are provided at a higher price than on weekdays.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Why may more free time during weekends result in a higher market price for karaoke services?
parts.modelAnswer: More free time lowers the time cost of consuming karaoke services, so demand increases at each price. The demand curve shifts right and the market price rises.
markingPoints: Explains demand increasing and price rising.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: More customers go to karaoke lounges during weekends, but the services are provided at a higher price than on weekdays.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain whether customers going to karaoke lounges during weekends incur a higher or lower cost than on weekdays.
parts.modelAnswer: Not necessarily. Total cost includes the money price and the time cost. Although the weekend price is higher, free time makes the time cost lower, so the full cost may be higher or lower depending on the size of the two changes.
markingPoints: Explains why the full cost is uncertain.

parts.prompt: Suppose the excess reserves of the banks are $275. What is the required reserve ratio?
parts.modelAnswer: Required reserve ratio = (500 - 275) / 1 500 = 0.15, or 15%.

parts.prompt: Suppose there is a cash withdrawal of $300 from the banks. Explain whether the banks still have excess reserves immediately after the withdrawal.
parts.modelAnswer: Required reserves after the withdrawal = $1 200 x 0.15 = $180. Reserves after the withdrawal are $200, so the banking system still has $20 excess reserves.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Nominal interest rate as the (opportunity) cost of holding money
questions.stem: Consider the relationship between nominal and real interest rates.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why the nominal interest rate is the cost of holding money.
parts.modelAnswer: Money normally pays no interest. Holding money means giving up the return from interest-bearing assets, so the nominal interest rate is the opportunity cost of holding money.
markingPoints: Identifies the nominal interest rate as opportunity cost.

questions.topicGroup: Reasons for a downward-sloping aggregate demand (AD) curve
questions.keyPoint: Reasons for a downward-sloping aggregate demand (AD) curve
questions.stem: Consider the aggregate demand curve.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Give TWO reasons why the aggregate demand curve is downward-sloping.
parts.modelAnswer: Valid reasons include the wealth effect, the interest-rate effect and the exchange-rate or net-export effect. For example, a lower price level raises real wealth and lowers interest rates, increasing consumption and investment.
markingPoints: Gives and explains two valid effects.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem: Consider the aggregate demand curve.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 'Expansionary fiscal policy will have no effect on real income in the long run.' Do you agree? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Generally yes: expansionary fiscal policy shifts AD right and raises real income in the short run, but the long-run aggregate supply curve is vertical, so real income returns to potential income. If government spending is investment that increases the capital stock, long-run real income may rise.
markingPoints: Explains vertical LRAS and gives the investment qualification.

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.stem: The national income accounting equation is Y = C + I + G + NX.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Define national saving as S = Y - C - G. Show that S - I = NX.
parts.modelAnswer: Given Y = C + I + G + NX, S = Y - C - G = I + NX. Therefore S - I = NX.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of current account surplus and deficit
questions.stem: The national income accounting equation is Y = C + I + G + NX.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain why the fiscal deficit of an economy would be equal to its trade deficit when private saving equals investment.
parts.modelAnswer: S - I = NX and S = S^P + S^G. If S^P = I, then S^G = NX. A fiscal deficit means S^G is negative, so NX is negative by the same amount, which is a trade deficit.
markingPoints: Explains the equal and negative public-saving and net-export amounts.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of current account surplus and deficit
questions.stem: The national income accounting equation is Y = C + I + G + NX.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain the condition under which an economy could achieve a trade balance when it had a fiscal deficit.
parts.modelAnswer: With NX = S^P + S^G - I, NX is zero when the excess of private saving over domestic investment exactly offsets the fiscal deficit: S^P - I = -S^G.

parts.modelAnswer: The lower marginal cost shifts supply right. Price falls, quantity transacted rises, consumer surplus rises and producer surplus also rises if supply shifts in parallel.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Many governments face fiscal deficits and may consider increasing sales tax rates.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: With the aid of a diagram, explain how an increase in sales tax rates would affect the price level and output of an economy in the short run.
parts.modelAnswer: A higher sales tax reduces firms' willingness to supply and to invest. SRAS shifts left and AD shifts left. Output falls; the price level may rise or fall depending on which curve shifts by more.
markingPoints: Explains AD shifting left through investment.
Explains the price-level result is uncertain.

answerVisuals.alt: Marking-scheme AD-AS answer for the sales-tax shock.
answerVisuals.caption: Marking-scheme AD-AS answer for the sales-tax shock.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Many governments face fiscal deficits and may consider increasing sales tax rates.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: Do you think central banks could stabilize the price level through monetary policy after the increase in sales tax rates? What would be the effect on output? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: If the price level rises, contractionary monetary policy can reduce AD and stabilize prices, but output falls further. If the price level falls, expansionary monetary policy can raise AD and offset part of the output fall, but it may not fully stabilize output and prices.
markingPoints: Explains the appropriate monetary response for either price outcome.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Many governments face fiscal deficits and may consider increasing sales tax rates.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: Based on your answer in (b)(i), should central banks stabilize the price level through monetary policy after the increase in sales tax rates? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: A decision depends on the cost of output destabilization and society's preference between price stability and output stability. Stabilizing prices may worsen the output change, so it is not automatically desirable.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Some Hong Kong politicians have demanded a minimum wage law for low-income earners.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: With the aid of a diagram, explain how the introduction of an effective minimum wage would affect the number of workers employed.
parts.modelAnswer: A binding minimum wage above equilibrium raises the wage rate and creates excess supply of labour. Employment equals labour demanded and therefore decreases.

answerVisuals.alt: Marking-scheme minimum-wage diagram.
answerVisuals.caption: Marking-scheme minimum-wage diagram.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Some Hong Kong politicians have demanded a minimum wage law for low-income earners.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: With the aid of a diagram, explain how the introduction of an effective minimum wage would affect total wage earnings.
parts.modelAnswer: Total wage earnings may rise or fall depending on the price elasticity of labour demand. If demand is elastic, the percentage fall in employment exceeds the percentage rise in wages and earnings fall; if demand is inelastic, earnings rise.
markingPoints: Shows the relevant gain and loss areas.

answerVisuals.alt: Marking-scheme minimum-wage diagram.
answerVisuals.caption: Marking-scheme minimum-wage diagram.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: Some Hong Kong politicians have demanded a minimum wage law for low-income earners.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 'A minimum wage should be introduced to protect the interests of low-income workers.' Evaluate this proposal.
parts.modelAnswer: A minimum wage reduces employment for some workers. Workers who keep jobs may earn more, while workers who lose jobs suffer; the effect on total wage earnings depends on labour-demand elasticity. Whether it protects workers therefore requires a value judgement and depends on the evidence.

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination
questions.stem: Mobile phone services in Hong Kong are dominated by several providers.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: What is price discrimination?
parts.modelAnswer: It occurs when the same good produced at the same cost is sold to different customers at different prices or under different pricing arrangements.

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination
questions.stem: Mobile phone services in Hong Kong are dominated by several providers.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: State TWO conditions for practising price discrimination. Do the mobile phone service providers meet those conditions?
parts.modelAnswer: Two conditions are that sellers are price searchers and that markets can be separated, with different demand elasticities or information costs. Providers can set their own prices and customers choose different plans, but the markets may not be fully separable because plans are open to customers generally.
markingPoints: Applies them to mobile phone plans.

questions.keyPoint: Price discrimination
questions.stem: Mobile phone services in Hong Kong are dominated by several providers.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.prompt: Is charging a lower per-minute price for plans with more airtime an example of price discrimination? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes, if the plans are different pricing arrangements for the same additional services and the cost of serving customers is the same. Customers choosing different plans pay different per-minute prices. It is not price discrimination if every customer can freely choose the same plans on identical terms and the lower price only reflects a different package.
markingPoints: Explains same cost and different prices or the package qualification.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, cost of production, technology, price expectations, weather, number of sellers in the market, etc. affect individual supply and market supply
questions.stem: Mobile phone services in Hong Kong are dominated by several providers.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain why all sellers in a competitive market would charge a higher price when there is an increase in the cost of production.
parts.modelAnswer: A higher production cost shifts the supply curve left. At the original price there is excess demand, so the market price rises until a new equilibrium is reached.

questions.keyPoint: Anti-competitive behaviours
questions.stem: Mobile phone services in Hong Kong are dominated by several providers.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: Can we conclude that sellers raising prices at the same time is necessarily anti-competitive? What other evidence would be necessary? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: No. A common cost increase can logically cause all sellers to raise prices at the same time. Evidence of collusion between sellers, such as communication or an agreement, or data showing price changes unrelated to production costs, would be needed.
markingPoints: Identifies evidence of collusion or unrelated price changes.

parts.modelAnswer: 在技術不變下，連續增加某可變生產要素而固定生產要素數量不變，該可變要素的邊際產量最終會下降。資料能說明該定律，因為勞工增加時邊際產量由 600 降至 300 再降至 200。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋相關物品價格、收入、價格預期、天氣、市場消費者人數等因素如何影響個別需求及市場需求
questions.stem: 週末有較多顧客到卡拉 OK 會所，但服務價格較工作日高。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 為甚麼週末有較多空閒時間會令卡拉 OK 服務的市場價格上升？
parts.modelAnswer: 較多空閒時間令消費卡拉 OK 服務的時間成本下降，因此每個價格水平的需求增加，需求曲線向右移，市場價格上升。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 週末有較多顧客到卡拉 OK 會所，但服務價格較工作日高。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 解釋週末到卡拉 OK 會所的顧客所承擔的成本相對工作日較高還是較低。
parts.modelAnswer: 不一定。服務的總成本包括貨幣價格及時間成本。週末貨幣價格較高，但空閒時間令時間成本較低，最終總成本取決於兩者的變化幅度。

questions.topicGroup: 名義利率及實質利率的關係

questions.stem: 考慮名義利率和實質利率的關係。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: 名義利率和實質利率有甚麼分別？
parts.modelAnswer: 名義利率 = 實質利率 + 預期通脹率。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 名義利率及實質利率的關係
questions.keyPoint: 了解方程式：名義利率 = 實質利率 + 預期通脹率
questions.stem: 考慮名義利率和實質利率的關係。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 解釋名義利率在甚麼情況下會低於實質利率。
parts.modelAnswer: 當預期通脹率為負，即預期出現通貨緊縮時，名義利率會低於實質利率。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.topicGroup: 名義利率及實質利率的關係
questions.keyPoint: 名義利率是持有貨幣的（機會）成本
questions.stem: 考慮名義利率和實質利率的關係。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 解釋為甚麼名義利率是持有貨幣的成本。
parts.modelAnswer: 貨幣通常沒有利息回報。持有貨幣便放棄持有有息資產的回報，因此名義利率是持有貨幣的機會成本。
markingPoints: 指出名義利率是機會成本。

questions.topicGroup: 總需求（AD）曲線向右下斜的原因
questions.keyPoint: 總需求（AD）曲線向右下斜的原因
questions.stem: 考慮總需求曲線。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 舉出兩個原因解釋總需求曲線向右下斜。
parts.modelAnswer: 有效原因包括財富效應、利率效應及匯率或淨出口效應。例如物價水平下降會令實質財富增加及利率下降，消費和投資增加。
markingPoints: 舉出及解釋兩個有效效應。

questions.topicGroup: 財政政策對 物價及產出 水平的影響
questions.keyPoint: 擴張性財政政策的影響
questions.stem: 考慮總需求曲線。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 「擴張性財政政策長期不會影響實質收入。」你同意嗎？試加解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 一般同意：擴張性財政政策短期令總需求向右移及實質收入上升，但長期總供應曲線垂直，實質收入回到潛在收入。若政府支出用於投資並增加資本，長期實質收入也可能上升。
markingPoints: 解釋長期總供應垂直及投資例外。

questions.topicGroup: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.keyPoint: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.stem: 國民收入會計方程式為 Y = C + I + G + NX。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 定義國民儲蓄 S = Y - C - G，證明 S - I = NX。
parts.modelAnswer: 由 Y = C + I + G + NX，S = Y - C - G = I + NX，因此 S - I = NX。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 經常帳（主要組成部分：貨物、服務、收益及經常轉移）
questions.keyPoint: 經常帳盈餘及經常帳赤字的意思
questions.stem: 國民收入會計方程式為 Y = C + I + G + NX。

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: 若私人儲蓄等於投資，解釋為甚麼經濟的財政赤字會等於貿易赤字。
parts.modelAnswer: S - I = NX，而 S = 私人儲蓄 + 政府儲蓄。若私人儲蓄等於投資，政府儲蓄便等於 NX；財政赤字令政府儲蓄為負，因此 NX 以相同數額為負，即貿易赤字。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 經常帳（主要組成部分：貨物、服務、收益及經常轉移）
questions.keyPoint: 經常帳盈餘及經常帳赤字的意思
questions.stem: 國民收入會計方程式為 Y = C + I + G + NX。

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: 有財政赤字時，經濟在甚麼條件下仍可達致貿易平衡？
parts.modelAnswer: NX = 私人儲蓄 + 政府儲蓄 - 投資。當私人儲蓄超過國內投資的數額，剛好抵銷財政赤字時，NX = 0，經濟便有貿易平衡。
markingPoints: 解釋私人儲蓄盈餘抵銷財政赤字。

questions.topicGroup: 總需求及/或總供應改變導致均衡產出水平和物價水平的改變
questions.keyPoint: 透過明確說明受影響的總需求組成部分及/ 或影響短期總供應及/或長期總供應的因素，解釋某情況會如何導致總需求、短期總供應及/ 或長期總供應轉變，因而令總需求曲線、短期總供應曲線及/或長期總供應曲線移動
questions.stem: 世界各地很多政府面對財政赤字，可能考慮提高銷售稅率。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 以圖輔助，解釋提高銷售稅率如何在短期影響經濟的物價水平及產出。
parts.modelAnswer: 較高銷售稅降低廠商供應意欲及投資意欲，令短期總供應及總需求均向左移。產出下降；物價水平視乎兩條曲線的移動幅度而可能上升或下降。
markingPoints: 解釋短期總供應向左移。
解釋投資令總需求向左移。
指出產出下降及物價結果未確定。

questions.keyPoint: 擴張性及緊縮性貨幣政策，包括改變法定儲備比率及貼現率
questions.stem: 世界各地很多政府面對財政赤字，可能考慮提高銷售稅率。

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: 銷售稅率增加後，中央銀行可否透過貨幣政策穩定物價水平？該政策對產出有甚麼影響？
parts.modelAnswer: 若物價上升，緊縮性貨幣政策可減少總需求並穩定物價，但產出會進一步下降；若物價下跌，擴張性貨幣政策可增加總需求及抵銷部分產出跌幅。

questions.keyPoint: 擴張性及緊縮性貨幣政策，包括改變法定儲備比率及貼現率
questions.stem: 世界各地很多政府面對財政赤字，可能考慮提高銷售稅率。

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: 根據 (b)(i)，你認為中央銀行應否透過貨幣政策穩定物價？試加解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 穩定物價可能令產出波動更大，因此是否應該穩定物價要視乎產出穩定的成本及社會對物價穩定與產出穩定的取捨。

questions.keyPoint: 分析（有效）價格下限對（貨幣）價格、交易量及總收入等的影響

parts.modelAnswer: 高於均衡工資的有效最低工資令工資率上升並造成勞工供過於求；就業人數由勞工需求決定，因此下降。

answerVisuals.alt: 評分參考最低工資圖。

questions.keyPoint: 分析（有效）價格下限對（貨幣）價格、交易量及總收入等的影響

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 以圖輔助，解釋有效最低工資如何影響工人的總工資收入。
parts.modelAnswer: 總工資收入視乎勞工需求的價格彈性而上升或下降。若需求有彈性，就業百分比跌幅大於工資百分比升幅，收入下降；若需求缺乏彈性，收入上升。
