questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(II)
questions.keyPoint: 收入均等化
questions.stem: 一些香港政客要求為保安員及清潔工等低收入人士引入最低工資法。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 「應引入最低工資以保障低收入工人的利益。」評估這項建議。
parts.modelAnswer: 最低工資會令部分工人失去工作；保住工作者收入可能增加，失去工作者則受損。總工資收入取決於勞工需求彈性，因此是否保障工人需要作規範性判斷及參考實際證據。
markingPoints: 解釋彈性與總工資收入。

questions.keyPoint: 價格分歧
questions.stem: 香港的流動電話服務由數家供應商主導。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: 甚麼是價格分歧？
parts.modelAnswer: 價格分歧是指生產成本相同的相同物品，以不同價格或不同定價安排出售給不同顧客。

questions.keyPoint: 價格分歧
questions.stem: 香港的流動電話服務由數家供應商主導。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 列出實行價格分歧的兩項條件，並說明流動電話服務供應商是否符合。
parts.modelAnswer: 兩項條件是賣方為價格搜尋者，以及市場可以分隔並有不同需求彈性或資訊成本。供應商可以自行定價，顧客可選不同計劃；但計劃未必能完全把市場分隔，因為所有顧客均可選擇。

questions.keyPoint: 價格分歧
questions.stem: 香港的流動電話服務由數家供應商主導。

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.prompt: 若同一供應商向所有顧客提供相同附加服務，按更多通話時間計劃收取較低每分鐘價格是否價格分歧？解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 若不同計劃的附加服務相同而服務成本相同，顧客因選擇不同計劃而支付不同每分鐘價格，便構成價格分歧；若較低價格只是反映不同套裝內容，則不一定構成。
markingPoints: 解釋成本相同及價格不同或套裝例外。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋相關物品價格、生產成本、科技、價格預期、天氣、市場生產者人數等因素如何影響個別供應及市場供應
questions.stem: 香港的流動電話服務由數家供應商主導。

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: 解釋為甚麼競爭市場的所有賣方在生產成本增加時會收取較高價格。
parts.modelAnswer: 生產成本上升令供應曲線向左移。在原有價格下出現超額需求，市場價格上升至新的均衡。

questions.chapterTitle: 反競爭行為與競爭政策
questions.keyPoint: 反競爭行為
questions.stem: 香港的流動電話服務由數家供應商主導。

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: 賣方同時加價是否必然是反競爭？要有甚麼其他證據才可下此結論？

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Explain why interest can be regarded as an opportunity cost
questions.stem: Peter borrowed a book from Mary and promised to return it with a bookmark a month later.

parts.label: Q1
parts.prompt: Explain why the bookmark could be regarded as interest to both Peter and Mary.
parts.modelAnswer: For Peter, the bookmark is the cost paid for earlier availability of the book. For Mary, it is the premium or compensation received for deferring consumption.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning and give examples of each type of integration
questions.stem: A Chinese car manufacturer acquired a Swedish car manufacturer in 2010.

parts.label: Q2
parts.prompt: Explain which type of integration was involved and state THREE possible motives for this type of integration.
parts.modelAnswer: It is horizontal integration because both firms produce the same type of goods. Motives include better use of resources, economies of scale, benefit from the brand name and increased market share.
markingPoints: Identifies horizontal integration and gives three valid motives.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem: An earthquake damaged the production facilities of memory products such as SD cards, so their prices rose.

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt: With the aid of a diagram, explain under what condition total expenditure of Japanese consumers on memory products would fall.
parts.modelAnswer: The earthquake decreases supply and shifts supply left. Total expenditure falls if demand is elastic, because the percentage fall in quantity demanded is greater than the percentage rise in price.
markingPoints: Explains the percentage changes and lower expenditure.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of deadweight loss
questions.stem: A teacher said that an effective price ceiling may increase consumer surplus; a student said it may enhance efficiency.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: What is deadweight loss?
parts.modelAnswer: Deadweight loss is the loss in total social surplus, or potential gains from trade that are not captured when marginal benefit does not equal marginal cost.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem: A teacher said that an effective price ceiling may increase consumer surplus; a student said it may enhance efficiency.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: Do you agree with the teacher that an effective price ceiling may increase consumer surplus? Illustrate your answer in Figure 1.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes, it may increase consumer surplus for the consumers who obtain the good: the lower price creates a gain. However, other consumers may lose access and consumer surplus. The diagram should show the gain and loss areas.
markingPoints: Shows the gain and loss in consumer surplus.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: Do you agree with the student that if consumer surplus increases, the price ceiling may enhance economic efficiency? Explain with Figure 2.
parts.modelAnswer: No. A binding price ceiling reduces quantity transacted. Some mutually beneficial trades are lost because marginal benefit is greater than marginal cost, creating deadweight loss.

questions.topicGroup: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.keyPoint: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.stem: Mr Richardson, a British civil engineer, has worked for a large Hong Kong construction company for the past few years.

parts.label: Q5
parts.prompt: Is Mr Richardson's income counted in Hong Kong's GDP? Explain.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. His income is generated by current production carried out by a resident producing unit in Hong Kong, even though he remits part of it overseas.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: Economy A has introduced a labour importation scheme for skilled construction workers.

parts.label: Q6
parts.prompt: Suppose imported workers do not replace domestic workers. Explain how the unemployment rate will be affected.
parts.modelAnswer: The unemployment rate equals unemployed persons divided by the labour force. Imported workers increase the labour force while the number unemployed remains unchanged, so the unemployment rate decreases.
markingPoints: Explains labour force rises and unemployment unchanged.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Features of the four phases of a business cycle
questions.stem: Refer to the business cycle shown in Figure 3.

parts.label: Q7
parts.prompt: Identify the phase in which point A is located. Apart from real GDP growth, give THREE general economic phenomena in this phase.
parts.modelAnswer: Point A is in the trough or depression phase. Employment is low, unemployment is high, inflation is low or deflation may occur, aggregate demand is low and business confidence is low; any three are valid.

visuals.alt: Question Figure 3: real GDP growth rate and the long-term growth rate.
visuals.caption: Question Figure 3: real GDP growth rate and the long-term growth rate.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem: Demand deposits can be regarded as money.

parts.label: Q8
parts.prompt: Explain which TWO functions of money demand deposits can perform.
parts.modelAnswer: Demand deposits can serve as a medium of exchange because cheques facilitate buying and selling. They can also serve as a store of value because purchasing power can be held for future spending.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has an absolute advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: Country A and Country B possess the same amount of resources and produce food and computers.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain whether Country B has an absolute advantage in producing food.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. If both countries fully use their resources, Country B can produce more food, so it has an absolute advantage in food production.
markingPoints: Calculates or compares maximum food output.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: Country A and Country B possess the same amount of resources and produce food and computers.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain whether Country B has a comparative advantage in producing food.
parts.modelAnswer: Country A's opportunity cost of one unit of food is 100/200 = 0.5 computer. Country B's is 150/600 = 0.25 computer. Country B has the lower opportunity cost and therefore the comparative advantage.

questions.stem: Suppose the US dollar depreciates against the Euro under the linked exchange rate system.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Under the linked exchange rate system, how will the total number of Hong Kong tourists travelling to European countries be affected?
parts.modelAnswer: It decreases because the Hong Kong dollar depreciates against the Euro and European travel becomes more expensive in Hong Kong dollars.
markingPoints: States decrease and explains the currency effect.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Under the linked exchange rate system, how will the prices in Euro of Hong Kong toys exported to Europe be affected?
parts.modelAnswer: They decrease because the Hong Kong dollar depreciates against the Euro, making Hong Kong goods cheaper in Euro terms.
markingPoints: States decrease and explains the currency effect.

parts.modelAnswer: It is uncertain: the Hong Kong-dollar price rises, but the quantity demanded falls, so the total expenditure depends on the price elasticity of demand.
markingPoints: Explains price and quantity move in opposite directions.

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem: The prices of senior-secondary textbooks have increased sharply because publishers must publish new textbooks.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: What economic principle is illustrated by the production of textbooks involving authors, editors and graphic designers? Give THREE reasons why it can raise labour productivity.
parts.modelAnswer: It illustrates division of labour or specialization. Productivity can rise because practice makes perfect, workers can be matched to suitable jobs, training time is saved and job-rotation time is saved.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: The prices of senior-secondary textbooks have increased sharply because publishers must publish new textbooks.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the knowledge in the textbooks is a public good.
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. Knowledge is non-rival because one person's use does not reduce what is available to others, and it is difficult or costly to exclude others from using it.

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: The prices of senior-secondary textbooks have increased sharply because publishers must publish new textbooks.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: To which type of market structure do textbook publishers belong? State TWO features.
parts.modelAnswer: They may be oligopolists, with a few dominant sellers, interdependent policies, non-price competition and barriers to entry. Monopolistic competition with many sellers and heterogeneous products can also be accepted if justified.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: The prices of senior-secondary textbooks have increased sharply because publishers must publish new textbooks.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Explain how the School Textbook Assistance Scheme can enhance equity in Hong Kong society.
parts.modelAnswer: The subsidy raises the income of needy families while richer families cannot enjoy the same benefit. It helps equalize opportunities by allowing needy students to continue their studies, which may raise their future income and narrow the income gap.
markingPoints: Explains the possible long-run income effect.

parts.prompt: Illustrate the sold-out ticket phenomenon in a demand-supply diagram.
parts.modelAnswer: The supply of tickets is vertical at 600 000, while the price of $10 is below equilibrium. The result is excess demand or a shortage.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: Suggest TWO measures which would help relieve the ticket shortage and illustrate them in separate diagrams.
parts.modelAnswer: One measure is to raise the ticket price, which reduces the shortage. Another is to issue more tickets or extend the exhibition period, shifting supply right and reducing the shortage.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: State the function of price when touts sell tickets for $200.
parts.modelAnswer: Price performs a rationing function: tickets are distributed to buyers willing to pay at least $200.

questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: Evaluate the proposal that the government should raise the ticket price to kick out touts.
parts.modelAnswer: A higher official price may reduce touting and raise exhibition revenue, reduce queues and efficiency loss, and make tickets easier to obtain. However, it lowers consumer surplus and may exclude lower-income consumers. A reasoned judgement is required.

questions.keyPoint: Reasons for an upward-sloping short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve
questions.stem: Figure 4 shows aggregate supply and aggregate demand curves. The initial equilibrium is E0.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Why is the short-run aggregate supply curve upward-sloping?
parts.modelAnswer: Wages and other input prices are sticky in the short run. When output prices rise faster than input prices, firms become more profitable and supply more output.
markingPoints: Links higher output prices to greater output.

questions.stem: Figure 4 shows aggregate supply and aggregate demand curves. The initial equilibrium is E0.

parts.prompt: Explain how market forces help restore output to full-employment output Yf.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem: The table shows the balance sheet of a banking system. The public holds $500 million cash and banks hold no excess reserves.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the monetary base and money supply.
parts.modelAnswer: Monetary base = reserves $1 000 million + public cash $500 million = $1 500 million. Money supply = deposits $4 000 million + public cash $500 million = $4 500 million.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem: The table shows the balance sheet of a banking system. The public holds $500 million cash and banks hold no excess reserves.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: Explain whether lowering the minimum reserve ratio by 5% changes the monetary base.
parts.modelAnswer: No. The policy changes neither the amount of bank reserves nor the cash held by the public, so the monetary base is unchanged.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The table shows the balance sheet of a banking system. The public holds $500 million cash and banks hold no excess reserves.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the new money supply after the minimum reserve ratio falls by 5%.
parts.modelAnswer: The original reserve ratio is 1 000/4 000 = 0.25. The new ratio is 0.20. New deposits = 1 000 x (1/0.20) = $5 000 million, so new money supply = $5 500 million including public cash.

parts.prompt: According to the quantity theory of money, explain how the change in money supply affects the general price level in the long run.
parts.modelAnswer: MV = PY. Assuming velocity and long-run real output are constant, the increase in money supply raises the price level by the same percentage.

questions.stem: 彼德向瑪莉借了一本書，並承諾一個月後連同書簽歸還。

parts.label: Q1
parts.prompt: 解釋為甚麼書簽對彼德和瑪莉均可視為利息。
parts.modelAnswer: 對彼德來說，書簽是提早取得書本所付出的成本；對瑪莉來說，書簽是延遲消費所收到的溢價或補償。

questions.keyPoint: 了解各類結合的含義並加以舉例
questions.stem: 一家中國汽車生產商於 2010 年收購一家瑞典汽車生產商。

parts.label: Q2
parts.prompt: 解釋這個案涉及哪種結合，並列出這種結合的三個可能動機。
parts.modelAnswer: 這是水平結合，因為兩間公司生產同類物品。動機包括更靈活運用資源、規模經濟、品牌效益及增加市場佔有率。
markingPoints: 指出水平結合及三個有效動機。

questions.chapterTitle: 需求和供應的價格彈性
questions.keyPoint: 需求價格彈性和總收入之間的關係
questions.stem: 日本地震破壞記憶體產品如 SD 卡的生產設施，令產品價格上升。

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt: 以圖輔助，解釋在甚麼條件下日本消費者對記憶產品的總支出會下降。
parts.modelAnswer: 地震令供應減少，供應曲線向左移。若記憶產品的需求有彈性，需求量百分比跌幅大於價格百分比升幅，總支出便下降。
markingPoints: 解釋百分比變化及總支出下降。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 效率損失的意思
questions.stem: 一位老師說有效價格上限可能增加消費者盈餘，學生說它可能提升效率。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 甚麼是效率損失？
parts.modelAnswer: 效率損失是總社會盈餘的損失，或因邊際利益不等於邊際成本而未能攫取的潛在貿易得益。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.topicGroup: 以供需圖輔助，分析市場干預對消費者盈餘、生產者盈餘和效率的影響
questions.keyPoint: 價格上限
questions.stem: 一位老師說有效價格上限可能增加消費者盈餘，學生說它可能提升效率。

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: 你同意老師所說有效價格上限可能增加消費者盈餘嗎？以圖一說明。
parts.modelAnswer: 有可能同意。對成功取得物品的消費者，較低價格會帶來消費者盈餘得益；但其他消費者可能失去購買機會，因而有損失。圖中應顯示得益及損失面積。
markingPoints: 顯示消費者盈餘得益及損失。

questions.topicGroup: 以供需圖輔助，分析市場干預對消費者盈餘、生產者盈餘和效率的影響
questions.keyPoint: 價格上限
questions.stem: 一位老師說有效價格上限可能增加消費者盈餘，學生說它可能提升效率。

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: 你同意學生所說若消費者盈餘增加，價格上限可能提升經濟效率嗎？以圖二輔助解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 不同意。有效價格上限令交易量減少，部分邊際利益高於邊際成本的互利交易消失，因而出現效率損失。

questions.topicGroup: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.keyPoint: 本地生產總值及居民生產單位的意思；計算本地生產總值時 包括/不包括在內的項目
questions.stem: 英國土木工程師 Richardson 先生過去數年在香港大型建築公司工作。

parts.label: Q5
parts.prompt: Richardson 先生的收入會否計入香港的本地生產總值？解釋。
parts.modelAnswer: 會。收入來自香港常住生產單位在當地進行的當期生產，即使他把部分收入匯回英國也包括在香港本地生產總值內。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.keyPoint: 計算失業率及辨識勞動人口
questions.stem: 甲經濟推出計劃輸入熟練建築工人。

parts.label: Q6
parts.prompt: 假設輸入工人不取代本地工人，解釋輸入計劃如何影響失業率。
parts.modelAnswer: 失業率 = 失業人口 / 勞動人口。輸入工人令勞動人口增加，而失業人口維持不變，因此失業率下降。
markingPoints: 解釋分母增加而分子不變。

questions.chapterTitle: 經濟周期、一般物價水平的變動和失業
questions.keyPoint: 經濟周期四個階段的特點
questions.stem: 參考圖三所示的經濟周期。

parts.label: Q7
parts.prompt: 指出 A 點所在的經濟周期階段，並除實質本地生產總值增長率外列出三項一般經濟現象。
parts.modelAnswer: A 點位於蕭條或谷底。就業低、失業高、通脹低或出現通縮、總需求低及營商信心低均是有效現象，列出三項。

questions.keyPoint: 貨幣的功能
questions.stem: 活期存款可被視為貨幣。

parts.label: Q8
parts.prompt: 解釋活期存款可發揮哪兩項貨幣功能。
parts.modelAnswer: 活期存款可作交易媒介，支票可便利物品和服務的買賣；亦可作價值儲藏，讓人保存購買力作將來消費。

questions.keyPoint: 根據個案資料，解釋哪個國家在生產某物品上擁有絕對優勢
questions.stem: 甲、乙兩國擁有相同數量的資源，生產食物和電腦。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 解釋乙國生產食物是否有絕對優勢。
parts.modelAnswer: 有。若兩國完全運用資源，乙國能生產較多食物，因此在食物生產上有絕對優勢。

questions.keyPoint: 根據個案資料，解釋哪個國家在生產某物品上擁有比較優勢
questions.stem: 甲、乙兩國擁有相同數量的資源，生產食物和電腦。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 解釋乙國生產食物是否有比較優勢。
parts.modelAnswer: 甲國生產一單位食物的機會成本為 100/200 = 0.5 部電腦；乙國為 150/600 = 0.25 部電腦。乙國機會成本較低，所以有比較優勢。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 匯率改變對進口及出口的影響
questions.keyPoint: 匯率改變對進出口價格（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）、進出口數量及進出口價值（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）的影響
questions.stem: 假設美元兌歐元貶值，在聯繫匯率制度下考慮以下項目。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 在聯繫匯率制度下，前往歐洲國家的香港遊客總數如何改變？
parts.modelAnswer: 下跌，因為港元兌歐元貶值，前往歐洲旅遊以港元計算較昂貴。
markingPoints: 指出下跌並解釋貨幣影響。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 匯率改變對進口及出口的影響
questions.keyPoint: 匯率改變對進出口價格（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）、進出口數量及進出口價值（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）的影響
questions.stem: 假設美元兌歐元貶值，在聯繫匯率制度下考慮以下項目。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 在聯繫匯率制度下，香港出口到歐洲的玩具價格（以歐元計算）如何改變？
parts.modelAnswer: 下跌，因為港元兌歐元貶值，香港貨品以歐元計算較便宜。
markingPoints: 指出下跌並解釋貨幣影響。

questions.chapterTitle: 國際收支平衡表與匯率
questions.topicGroup: 匯率改變對進口及出口的影響
questions.keyPoint: 匯率改變對進出口價格（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）、進出口數量及進出口價值（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）的影響
questions.stem: 假設美元兌歐元貶值，在聯繫匯率制度下考慮以下項目。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 在聯繫匯率制度下，香港進口歐洲汽車的總支出（以港元計算）如何改變？
parts.modelAnswer: 未能確定。港元價格上升但需求量下降，總支出取決於需求的價格彈性。
markingPoints: 解釋價格及數量反向變化。

questions.keyPoint: 分工的好處及壞處
questions.stem: 高中教科書價格大幅上升，因出版商須為新課程出版新教科書。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 生產教科書涉及作者、編輯及繪圖設計師等專家，這說明甚麼經濟原理？列出三項提高勞工生產力的理由。
parts.modelAnswer: 這說明分工或專門化生產。熟能生巧、按最適合的人分配工作、節省訓練時間及節省轉換工作崗位時間均可提高生產力，列出三項。

questions.keyPoint: 私用品及共用品
questions.stem: 高中教科書價格大幅上升，因出版商須為新課程出版新教科書。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 解釋教科書內的知識是否共用品。
parts.modelAnswer: 是。知識屬非競爭性消費，一人使用不會減少他人可使用的數量；亦屬非排他性消費，排除他人使用的成本很大。

questions.keyPoint: 列出不同市場結構的一般特徵
questions.stem: 高中教科書價格大幅上升，因出版商須為新課程出版新教科書。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 香港的教科書出版商屬於哪種市場結構？列出兩項特徵。
parts.modelAnswer: 可屬寡頭壟斷，特徵包括少數主導廠商、策略互相影響、非價格競爭及不易加入市場。若以壟斷性競爭作合理解釋亦可接受。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(II)
questions.keyPoint: 收入均等化
questions.stem: 高中教科書價格大幅上升，因出版商須為新課程出版新教科書。

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: 解釋學校書簿津貼計劃如何改善香港社會的公平。
parts.modelAnswer: 津貼增加有需要家庭收入，而富有家庭不能獲同樣利益；它有助機會均等，讓有需要學生繼續學業，長遠可提高收入並收窄收入差距。

questions.keyPoint: 分析（有效）價格上限對（貨幣）價格、交易量及總收入等的影響
questions.stem: 清明上河圖電子動態版展覽的 600 000 張門票以 $10 出售並很快售罄。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt: 以需求供應圖說明門票售罄及市民買不到票的現象。
parts.modelAnswer: 供應曲線在 600 000 張票處垂直，而 $10 低於均衡價格，因此出現超額需求或短缺。

answerVisuals.alt: 短缺的評分參考圖。

questions.keyPoint: 分析（有效）價格上限對（貨幣）價格、交易量及總收入等的影響
questions.stem: 清明上河圖電子動態版展覽的 600 000 張門票以 $10 出售並很快售罄。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt: 建議兩項紓緩門票短缺的措施，並以兩幅圖說明。
parts.modelAnswer: 可提高票價以減少短缺；亦可發行更多門票或延長展覽期，使供應曲線向右移並減少短缺。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 配給功能
questions.stem: 清明上河圖電子動態版展覽的 600 000 張門票以 $10 出售並很快售罄。

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: 人們願意以至少 $200 購買黃牛票，這顯示價格發揮甚麼功能？
parts.modelAnswer: 價格發揮配給功能，把門票分配給願意支付至少 $200 的買家。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.topicGroup: 以供需圖輔助，分析市場干預對消費者盈餘、生產者盈餘和效率的影響

questions.stem: 清明上河圖電子動態版展覽的 600 000 張門票以 $10 出售並很快售罄。

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: 評估政府提高票價以踢走黃牛黨的建議。
parts.modelAnswer: 較高官方票價可減少炒賣、增加展覽收入、減少排隊造成的效率損失及令門票較易取得；但會降低消費者盈餘，亦可能排除低收入人士。答案須有立場及理據。

questions.topicGroup: 短期總供應曲線向右上斜的原因

questions.stem: 圖四顯示某經濟的總供應和總需求曲線，起初均衡為 E0。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 為甚麼短期總供應曲線向右上斜？
parts.modelAnswer: 短期工資及其他投入價格具黏性。當產出價格上升速度較投入價格快，廠商利潤增加，便會供應更多產出。
markingPoints: 解釋產出價格與產出的關係。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 以圖輔助，解釋市場力量如何令產出水平回復至全民充分就業產出 Yf。
parts.modelAnswer: 通縮產出缺口令生產要素市場出現超額供應，投入價格下跌。投入價格下跌令短期總供應增加，物價水平下跌，產出長期回復至 Yf。

questions.keyPoint: 了解中央銀行行動如何影響貨幣基礎
questions.stem: 下表顯示某經濟的銀行體系資產負債表，公眾持有 500 百萬元現金，銀行沒有超額儲備。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 計算貨幣基礎和貨幣供應量。
parts.modelAnswer: 貨幣基礎 = 銀行儲備 1 000 + 公眾現金 500 = 1 500 百萬元；貨幣供應 = 存款 4 000 + 公眾現金 500 = 4 500 百萬元。

questions.keyPoint: 了解中央銀行行動如何影響貨幣基礎
questions.stem: 下表顯示某經濟的銀行體系資產負債表，公眾持有 500 百萬元現金，銀行沒有超額儲備。

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: 法定儲備比率下調 5% 會否改變貨幣基礎？
parts.modelAnswer: 不會。政策不會改變銀行儲備或公眾持有的現金，因此貨幣基礎不變。

questions.keyPoint: Definition of free goods and economic goods

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Are all free goods necessarily free of charge? Explain. (3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. Free goods are available in sufficient quantity to satisfy all human wants, so there is no competition for them and people do not need to bid a price. They are therefore free of charge.
markingPoints: States that all free goods are free of charge.
Defines free goods as sufficiently available to satisfy all wants.
Explains that no competition or bidding price is needed.

questions.keyPoint: Definition of free goods and economic goods

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Are all free-of-charge goods necessarily free goods? Explain. (3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: No. Some free-of-charge goods, such as samples distributed on the street, are economic goods: producing them involves a cost and people would prefer more of them.
markingPoints: States that free-of-charge goods need not be free goods.
Gives an economic-good example, such as free samples.
Explains that production involves cost and people prefer more of the goods.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of issuing shares and bonds to raise capital
questions.stem:
In 2009, many Mainland companies chose to be listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange (e.g. China South
Locomotive & Rolling Stock Corporation Limited and BaWang International (Group) Holding Limited).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Suggest ONE possible reason to explain why these companies chose to be listed on the stock exchange
instead of issuing bonds to raise capital. (2 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: A company issuing ordinary shares has no obligation to pay dividends even when it makes a profit, so it has greater flexibility to retain profit for future development.
markingPoints: Issuing ordinary shares creates no compulsory dividend payment even when the company makes a profit.
The company has greater flexibility to retain profit for future development.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
In 2009, many Mainland companies chose to be listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange (e.g. China South
Locomotive & Rolling Stock Corporation Limited and BaWang International (Group) Holding Limited).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt:
Explain why the risk of these companies being taken over will be higher after they have been listed.
(2 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Once listed, shares can be freely traded on the stock exchange. A hostile company may buy enough shares to take over the listed company.
markingPoints: States that listed shares can be freely traded on the stock exchange.
Explains that a hostile company can buy a sufficient number of shares to take over the company.

questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem: It is observed that the prices of dinner buffets in hotels are higher at weekends.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: What is a consumer’s full cost of having a dinner buffet in a hotel? (2 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Full cost is explicit cost plus implicit cost. For a consumer, it is the buffet's market price plus the value of the highest-valued alternative use of the time spent having the buffet.
markingPoints: Defines full cost as explicit or out-of-pocket cost plus implicit cost.
Applies this to the market price of the buffet plus the highest-valued alternative use of the time involved.

questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem: It is observed that the prices of dinner buffets in hotels are higher at weekends.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt:
Using the fact that customers have more free time at weekends, explain why some customers are still
willing to have dinner buffets in hotels at weekends when the prices are higher. (3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: More free time at weekends lowers the time cost of dining. Although the explicit price is higher, the implicit cost is lower, so the weekend full cost may be lower.
markingPoints: More free time lowers the time cost of consuming the buffet.
The explicit price is higher but implicit cost is lower.
Explains that full cost at weekends may therefore be lower.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt:
Some public goods are free of charge, e.g. TV programmes and songs. Explain why this is so.
(3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Public goods are not excludable, so providers cannot easily identify or prevent free riders. Charging them may be too costly, so providers may supply the goods free of charge despite production costs.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital
questions.stem: How will the stock of capital goods in an economy be affected if

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: the three basic economic problems(4 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: The stock of capital goods will rise. Capital accumulation equals capital formation minus capital consumption. Reducing wear and tear lowers capital consumption, raises capital accumulation and hence raises the capital stock, other things being equal.
markingPoints: States that the stock of capital goods rises.
Uses capital accumulation = capital formation minus capital consumption.
Notes that reduced wear and tear lowers capital consumption.
Explains that lower capital consumption raises capital accumulation.
Concludes that the capital stock rises, other things being equal.
parts.markingSchemeNote: The suggested solution's opening line says 'fall', but its stated capital-accumulation chain concludes that the capital stock rises. The latter, internally consistent conclusion is retained.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem: Do the following exist in a one-man economy? Explain.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: scarcity (3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. Scarcity is a situation in which available resources are insufficient to satisfy all wants. It may still exist in a one-man economy because the resources available to that person may not satisfy all of that person's wants.
markingPoints: Defines scarcity as resources being insufficient to satisfy all wants.
States that scarcity can exist in a one-man economy.
Explains that one person's resources may still be insufficient for all wants.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: Do the following exist in a one-man economy? Explain.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: the three basic economic problems (4 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: The one person still has to decide what to produce and how to produce. But the society does not have to decide for whom to produce because there is only one person who receives the goods.
markingPoints: States that the what-to-produce problem remains.
States that the how-to-produce problem remains.
Explains that for-whom-to-produce is unnecessary with only one person.
Explains that there is no distribution among different people to decide.

questions.keyPoint: Definition of cost
questions.stem:
Mr. Wong is a doctor. He just inherited shop premises from his grandparents. He can use the premises to
open a clinic, or lease it out for $25,000 per month. He planned to open a clinic and form a partnership
with his partner. But he is now considering working as a professional photographer with an expected
monthly income of $15,000.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: What is Mr. Wong’s opportunity cost of using the premises to open a clinic? (2 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Opportunity cost is the highest-valued option forgone. Here it is leasing the premises out for $25,000 per month.
markingPoints: Defines opportunity cost as the highest-valued option forgone.
Identifies leasing out the premises for $25,000 per month.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Mr. Wong is a doctor. He just inherited shop premises from his grandparents. He can use the premises to
open a clinic, or lease it out for $25,000 per month. He planned to open a clinic and form a partnership
with his partner. But he is now considering working as a professional photographer with an expected
monthly income of $15,000.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt:
How will his cost of using the premises to open a clinic change if
an advertising company wants to hire him as a professional photographer for a monthly income
of $20,000? (2 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: The cost does not change because the highest-valued option forgone remains leasing out the premises for $25,000 per month.
markingPoints: States that the cost does not change.
Explains that the highest-valued option forgone is unaffected.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Mr. Wong is a doctor. He just inherited shop premises from his grandparents. He can use the premises to
open a clinic, or lease it out for $25,000 per month. He planned to open a clinic and form a partnership
with his partner. But he is now considering working as a professional photographer with an expected
monthly income of $15,000.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt:
How will his cost of using the premises to open a clinic change if
someone is willing to offer $33,000 per month to rent his premises? (2 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: The cost increases because the value of the highest-valued option forgone, leasing the premises, rises to $33,000 per month.
markingPoints: Explains that the value of the highest-valued option forgone rises.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Mr. Wong is a doctor. He just inherited shop premises from his grandparents. He can use the premises to
open a clinic, or lease it out for $25,000 per month. He planned to open a clinic and form a partnership

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
Mr. Wong is a doctor. He just inherited shop premises from his grandparents. He can use the premises to

questions.keyPoint: Types of division of labour
questions.stem:
Restaurant A, a new Chinese restaurant, is located next to restaurant B. In restaurant A, each of the staff
specialises in one production process. In restaurant B, each of the staff is responsible for many job duties,
including cleaning dishes, cooking, serving customers and so on.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
What is division of labour? Does division of labour exist in the above restaurants? If yes, what type of
division of labour is practised? (3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Division of labour is a production system in which workers specialise in producing a good or a stage of its production. Restaurant A practises division of labour, specifically complex division of labour; restaurant B does not.
markingPoints: Defines division of labour as workers specialising in a good or a stage of production.
Identifies Restaurant A as practising division of labour while Restaurant B does not.
Identifies Restaurant A's arrangement as complex division of labour.

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem:
Restaurant A, a new Chinese restaurant, is located next to restaurant B. In restaurant A, each of the staff
specialises in one production process. In restaurant B, each of the staff is responsible for many job duties,
including cleaning dishes, cooking, serving customers and so on.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt:
Angela, the owner of restaurant B, found that the productivity of the staff in restaurant A is much higher
than the productivity of the staff in restaurant B.
Why does restautant A’s arrangement lead to higher productivity for its staff? Explain TWO possible
reasons. (4 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Any two valid explanations include: assigning the best people to each task; practice makes perfect; saving time in training and moving between tasks; greater possibility of mechanisation; and more economical use of capital.
markingPoints: Any two valid reasons, such as selecting the best person for each task.
Time is saved in training and moving between tasks.
Division of labour increases the possibility of mechanisation.
Capital can be used more economically.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem:
Restaurant A, a new Chinese restaurant, is located next to restaurant B. In restaurant A, each of the staff
specialises in one production process. In restaurant B, each of the staff is responsible for many job duties,
including cleaning dishes, cooking, serving customers and so on.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt:
Angela, the owner of restaurant B, found that the productivity of the staff in restaurant A is much higher
than the productivity of the staff in restaurant B.
Angela practised division of labour in her restaurant but later found that the productivity of labour
actually dropped. Explain TWO other possible methods to raise the productivity of her staff.
(4 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Any two valid methods include improving education and training, working conditions, rewards and benefits, the quantity and quality of producer goods, or the method of organising labour.
markingPoints: Any two valid methods, including education and training.
Increasing the quantity or quality of producer goods.
Improving the method of organising labour.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem:
Restaurant A, a new Chinese restaurant, is located next to restaurant B. In restaurant A, each of the staff
specialises in one production process. In restaurant B, each of the staff is responsible for many job duties,
including cleaning dishes, cooking, serving customers and so on.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt:
Angela found that the staff of restaurant A was more productive, so she planned to attract them to work
for her by offering transport allowance and higher salaries. Explain how the occupational mobility and
the geographical mobility of labour of restaurant A would be affected. (4 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Occupational mobility does not change because the workers change jobs but not occupations. Geographical mobility does not change because their workplace does not move to a different location.
markingPoints: States that occupational mobility does not change because occupations do not change.
States that geographical mobility does not change because the two workplaces are next to each other.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt:
In recent years, Country X has gradually recovered from the effects of a financial crisis. Although the
government has increased the supply of land for private domestic premises, the price of priva te domestic
premises is still rising. Illustrate the above situation with the aid of a supply-demand diagram. (6 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Recovery raises income and shifts demand for private domestic premises from D0 to D1. More land shifts supply from S0 to S1. When demand rises more than supply, equilibrium price rises from P0 to P1 while quantity rises from Q0 to Q1.
markingPoints: Shows S0 shifting right to S1.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt:
If diminishing marginal returns set in when the 5th unit of labour is employed, can X be 70? Explain

parts.label: Q8
parts.prompt:
“According to the Quantity Theory of Money, if the central bank persistently reduces money supply, deflation
will result both in the short run and in the long run.” Do you agree? Explain. (9 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: No. In the short run, a money-supply decrease proportionally lowers nominal national income, which can come from lower price level and/or lower real GDP, so deflation is not necessary. In the long run, real output is unaffected and money supply is directly proportional to price level; a persistent money-supply decrease therefore causes proportional deflation.
markingPoints: States disagreement with deflation necessarily occurring in both periods.
Explains that lower money supply lowers nominal income proportionally in the short run.
Explains that short-run nominal-income decline may reflect lower price level and/or lower real GDP.
Concludes that deflation is not necessary in the short run.

When the demand increase is greater than the supply decrease, price and quantity transacted both rise.

Shows supply shifting left from S0 to S1.
Identifies new cars and second-hand cars as substitutes.
Explains that higher new-car prices increase demand for second-hand cars.
Shows demand shifting right from D0 to D1.

questions.stem: In Country X, the government has a huge budget surplus. The government decides to offer a cash handout of $6,000 to all permanent residents aged 18 or above regardless of their income level as well as to offer a production subsidy to the firms which take measures to reduce their level of pollution.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, explain how the above fiscal measures will affect the price level and the real GDP of Country X in the short run. (10 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: The production subsidy makes production more profitable, raising SRAS and shifting it right from SRAS0 to SRAS1; this lowers price level and raises real GDP. The cash handout raises wealth and private consumption, shifting AD right from AD0 to AD1; this raises price level and real GDP. Combined, real GDP rises from Y0 to Y1, while price level may rise, fall or remain unchanged depending on the relative shifts.
markingPoints: Explains that the production subsidy raises SRAS and shifts SRAS0 right to SRAS1.
States the subsidy lowers price level and raises real GDP in isolation.

Shows SRAS0, SRAS1, AD0, AD1, Y0 and Y1 on a correctly labelled diagram.
Concludes that real GDP rises from Y0 to Y1.
Explains that the combined price-level effect is ambiguous and depends on relative AD and SRAS changes.

The production subsidy raises short-run aggregate supply and shifts SRAS right from SRAS0 to SRAS1.

questions.stem: In Feb 2011, Vietnam devalues the Dong (its currency) to tackle trade deficit.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain how the devaluation of Dong can help reduce Vietnam’s trade deficit. (3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Dong devaluation lowers the foreign-currency price of Vietnam's exports, increasing export volume and export value in Dong. It raises the Dong price of imports, reducing import volume; with elastic import demand, import value in Dong falls. Net exports rise and the trade deficit narrows.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has an absolute advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem:

Robots (units)Motorbikes (units)Country A100150Country B350200
Explain which country has

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: an absolute advantage
parts.modelAnswer: Country B has absolute advantage. With equal resources, Country A would produce 400 robots or 600 motorbikes, while Country B would produce 700 robots or 400 motorbikes. Country B can produce more robots with the same resources.
markingPoints: Adjusts Country A's output to equal-resource quantities of 400 robots and 600 motorbikes.
Compares Country B's 700 robots with Country A's 400 robots.
Concludes that Country B has absolute advantage in robots.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem:
Suppose Country A has half the amount of resources of Country B. The two countries allocate their resources evenly between the production of robots and motorbikes. The following table shows their total output in a year.
Robots (units)Motorbikes (units)Country A100150Country B350200
Explain which country has

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt:
a comparative advantage
in producing robots.(6 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Country A's opportunity cost of one robot is 600 divided by 400, or 1.5 motorbikes. Country B's is 400 divided by 700, or about 0.57 motorbike. Country B has comparative advantage because its opportunity cost is lower.

parts.modelAnswer: No. An effective price floor puts market price above equilibrium price, so quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded and excess supply arises. parts.label: Q5
parts.prompt: In Country X, there has been a discussion about imposing an effective price floor on good X to discourage people from consuming it. However, some government officials warned that this would lead to a deviation from efficiency. Do you agree with the government officials? Explain your answer with the aid of a diagram. (5 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. Floor raises price P1 to P2 and lowers quantity Q1 to Q2. At Q2, MB exceeds MC, so expanding output raises total social surplus; the floor creates deadweight loss.

Identifies deadweight loss or loss of social surplus.

parts.label: (a)

Total revenue falls.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem:
Read the following news extract.
The inflation rate of the Euro zone turned negative in December 2014 for the first time for the past five years. The European Central Bank (ECB) aims to keep the inflation rate at around 2%. It is widely expected that the ECB will buy government bonds.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: According to the quantity theory of money, explain how the purchase of government bonds would affect the price level in the long run. (4 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: The quantity theory is MV = PY, where M is money stock, V velocity, P price level and Y real output. In the long run V and Y are constant. Bond purchases raise M, so P rises by the same percentage.

Suppose Country A is experiencing a fiscal deficit and a trade deficit. To reduce these deficits, a government official has made two proposals:
Proposal 1: raising the income tax rate
Proposal 2: revaluing the country’s currency against other currencies

For local students, the tuition fee for bachelor's degree programmes funded by the University Grants Committee (大學教育資助委員會) has been maintained at $42,100 per year since 1997.
Explain whether the opportunity cost of receiving tertiary education in Hong Kong has necessarily remained unchanged since 1997.(3 marks)

parts.label: Q1
parts.prompt:
For local students, the tuition fee for bachelor's degree programmes funded by the University Grants Committee (大學教育資助委員會) has been maintained at $42,100 per year since 1997.
Explain whether the opportunity cost of receiving tertiary education in Hong Kong has necessarily remained unchanged since 1997.(3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: No. Full cost includes tuition plus the highest-valued alternative use of study time. Income forgone from working may have changed even if tuition did not.

parts.label: (a)

questions.stem: Suppose labour is the only resource required to produce toys and clothing in Country A and Country B. Country A requires 4 working-hours to produce 1 unit of toys while Country B requires 5 working-hours. On the other hand, Country A requires 7 working-hours to produce a unit of clothing while Country B requires 9 working-hours.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain which country will export toys.(2 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Country B exports toys. A toy costs 4/7 = 0.57 clothing in A and 5/9 = 0.56 clothing in B, so B has comparative advantage.

Source C: Opinions of different parties
Government officials:
Currently most of the waste electrical and electronic equipment is exported. We cannot rely on handling WEEE this way because the foreign demand for second-hand products will decline and restrictions on imports will be tightened. Meanwhile, waste equipment not recycled will go to the landfills, which are about to reach their maximum capacity.
Environmentalist:
There are toxic substances in electrical appliances. For example, refrigerants (used in refrigerators and air conditioners) can destroy the ozone layer and contribute to global climate change. Printer cartridge irritates our respiratory system and may cause cancer. Improper disposal of electrical appliances could lead to adverse effect on health and the environment.

Sellers may shift the recycling levy to consumers by adjusting the prices. Meanwhile, there may be difficulties in arranging removal of the old appliance when buying a new one. Consumers may not have enough space if the new appliances arrive before the old one is removed.

questions.stem:
The life expectancy of Hong Kong citizens is one of the highest in the world. More people realised the importance of saving for retirement.
Source A: Conversation between a wage earner and a financial planner
Financial planner:The life expectancy of men in Hong Kong is about 80 years. You need to have enough savings to support your living for at least 20 years if you are going to retire at 60. First of all, you have to estimate how much you need to spend when you retire.

Financial planner:No. Your total expenditure would be much larger than today if you want to maintain the same living standard. Let me introduce some investment tools for you.

The Amazon rainforest, often referred to as the ‘lungs of the Earth’, is the world’s largest rainforest. In August, 2019, fires broke out across the Amazon rainforest.
Source A: An introduction to the Amazon rainforest
(Sources: Various newspapers)
Source B: News report on the Amazon rainforest fires
The fires in the Amazon rainforest have raised international concerns. The Group of Seven (G7) has agreed to provide US$200 billion for firefighting and aftercare efforts. Meanwhile, various international charity organisations have called for donations to help protect the rainforest.
The cause of the fires has remained unknown. Some people suspected that the fires are the results of farmers burning the forest to clear land for farming. Brazil’s President has signed a decree to ban the use of fire to make agricultural land.
Source C: Opinions on how to preserve the Amazon rainforest
A green group
Large firms should stop buying from Brazil meat products produced on burnt rainforest land. They should also stop using coffee beans, paper and timber produced in the Amazon areas.
A European fashion retailer
We have decided to stop importing leather from Brazil unless producers ensure the production process of leather would not pose any threat to the rainforest.
A citizen
The government should introduce stricter regulations and better enforce these laws to stop farmers from illegally logging and burning the rainforest.
A businessman
To protect the rainforest from further damage, Brazil should develop ecotourism in the Amazon as an industry to replace the lumber and agricultural industries.

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: THE CITY is an animation production house. An average of 160 hours are required to produce an animation of 30 minutes. It doubled all the factors of production to meet a deadline. As a result, the total cost of production also doubled. However, only 40 hours were saved in producing an animation of that length. Explain the above phenomenon with ONE economic concept.(3 marks)

parts.label: Q5
parts.prompt: THE CITY is an animation production house. An average of 160 hours are required to produce an animation of 30 minutes. It doubled all the factors of production to meet a deadline. As a result, the total cost of production also doubled. However, only 40 hours were saved in producing an animation of that length. Explain the above phenomenon with ONE economic concept.(3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: It is internal diseconomies of scale. When all factors are doubled, average production cost rises. The scale may be so large that internal communication and coordination problems increase average cost.
markingPoints: Relates doubled factors to higher average cost.

questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem:
In September 2020, China Evergrande Group (stock code: 3333), a real estate developer, announced it was offering a 30% discount on existing real estate properties to boost sales.
Suppose initially there was an excess supply in the market. With the aid of a diagram, explain under what condition the total revenue of China Evergrande Group would increase. (7 marks)

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt:
In September 2020, China Evergrande Group (stock code: 3333), a real estate developer, announced it was offering a 30% discount on existing real estate properties to boost sales.
Suppose initially there was an excess supply in the market. With the aid of a diagram, explain under what condition the total revenue of China Evergrande Group would increase. (7 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Total revenue rises when demand is elastic: the percentage fall in price is smaller than the percentage increase in quantity demanded. The diagram should show the original price above equilibrium, vertical supply, and a revenue gain larger than the loss.

parts.label: Q5
parts.prompt:
In January 2021, the South Korean government said it was considering levying taxes on alcoholic products to reduce people’s consumption of such products.
Using the law of demand, explain the effect of levying taxes on alcoholic products on the average quality of alcoholic products sold. (5 marks)
(Hint: The tax can be assumed to be per-unit for simplicity.)

questions.keyPoint: Distinguishing between free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: The Employees Retraining Board launched the Love Upgrading Special Scheme 5 in January 2022 to help the unemployed or underemployed upgrade their skills for self-enhancement. parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain whether the vocational skills courses are free goods to the participants.(2 marks)

markingPoints: States that the courses are not free goods.

parts.prompt:
In recent years, many people in Hong Kong like keeping dogs. However, many housing estates do not allow residents to keep dogs.
Explain how keeping dogs in these housing estates may involve externality. (3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: For example, barking may disturb other people without compensation from dog owners, so keeping dogs creates negative externality or external cost. questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem:
Mr. Cheung is a flower farmer who sells Chinese New Year flowers at a farm in Yuen Long.
Mr. Cheung decides to lower the price of his Chinese New Year flowers to attract customers to buy flowers at his farm. With the aid of a supply-demand diagram, explain under what condition Mr. Cheung’s total revenue will increase. (5 marks)

parts.label: Q6
parts.prompt:
Mr. Cheung is a flower farmer who sells Chinese New Year flowers at a farm in Yuen Long.
Mr. Cheung decides to lower the price of his Chinese New Year flowers to attract customers to buy flowers at his farm. With the aid of a supply-demand diagram, explain under what condition Mr. Cheung’s total revenue will increase. (5 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Demand for the flowers must be elastic. The percentage decrease in price is then smaller than the percentage increase in quantity demanded, so total revenue rises. The diagram must show the correct areas of gain and loss in total revenue, with gain larger than loss.
markingPoints: Compares the percentage fall in price with the percentage rise in quantity demanded.
Shows the correct gain and loss areas.
Shows gain in total revenue larger than loss.

movements: Price falls from P0 to P1.
Quantity demanded rises from Q0 to Q1.

parts.modelAnswer: For efficiency, eligible passengers use designated transport until marginal benefit equals $2; if marginal cost exceeds $2, over-production and deadweight loss occur, and lowering the age can increase it. Other valid effects include higher geographical labour mobility and labour supply because home-to-work transport costs fall. A complete response uses source evidence, evaluates assumptions, and communicates coherently.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem:
A furniture manufacturing company is hiring part-time workers to provide door-to-door furniture assembly and disassembly services. The following is the advertisement of the company.
Part-time Workers Wanted!
Salary: Commission based on amount for each order + Tips from customers
*Flexible working hours*

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: From the viewpoint of the owner of the furniture manufacturing company, explain TWO advantages of using the above wage payment method over time rate.(4 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Workers tend to work harder to earn more, so supervision cost is lower. Part of the business risk is also shared by workers. Award any two reasonable advantages.
markingPoints: States that workers have an incentive to work harder.
States that business risk is shared with workers.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem:
A furniture manufacturing company is hiring part-time workers to provide door-to-door furniture assembly and disassembly services. The following is the advertisement of the company.
Part-time Workers Wanted!
Salary: Commission based on amount for each order + Tips from customers
*Flexible working hours*

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: After hiring more workers, given that the number of trucks transporting furniture remains the same, the company finds that the average number of orders received by workers decreases, and the marginal product of the workers drops. State the law that explains this phenomenon and briefly explain why such law can be applied in this case.(5 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: This is the law of diminishing marginal returns. In the short run, as more units of a variable factor are added successively to a given quantity of fixed factor, marginal product eventually decreases, other things constant. Workers are variable factors and trucks are fixed factors.
markingPoints: Identifies the law of diminishing marginal returns.
States that a variable factor is added to a fixed factor.
States that marginal product eventually falls.
Identifies workers as variable factors and trucks as fixed factors.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem:
Refer to the following pricing arrangement of a boardgame café.
Fee
Half day pass
$100
Full day pass
$180
After the café implemented a rule requiring each customer to order at least one snack, the ratio of full day passes sold to half day passes sold has increased. Explain this phenomenon by the law of demand.(5 marks)

parts.label: Q2
parts.prompt:
Refer to the following pricing arrangement of a boardgame café.
Fee
Half day pass
$100
Full day pass
$180
After the café implemented a rule requiring each customer to order at least one snack, the ratio of full day passes sold to half day passes sold has increased. Explain this phenomenon by the law of demand.(5 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: The law of demand states that, ceteris paribus, a price rise (fall) causes quantity demanded to fall (rise). Adding the snack price lowers the relative price of a full-day pass in terms of a half-day pass. People therefore buy relatively more full-day passes, so the ratio rises.
markingPoints: Recognises that snack price is added.
Explains that the relative price of a full-day pass falls.
Applies the law of demand to more full-day passes relative to half-day passes.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt:
Suppose someone withdraws $1,500 from the banking system and holds it in cash.
Calculate the maximum possible amount of money supply. Show your working.(3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Cash in public circulation is $1,500. Bank reserves become $1,500, supporting maximum deposits of $1,500 x (1 / 25%) = $6,000. Maximum money supply is $1,500 + $6,000 = $7,500.

questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem: Since 2020, many mask factories have been set up in Hong Kong to produce masks.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Suppose the price of raw materials for masks has decreased. With the aid of a diagram, explain under what condition the total revenue of the mask factories would decrease.(7 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Lower production cost increases supply. If demand is inelastic, the percentage fall in price is greater than the percentage rise in quantity demanded, so total revenue falls. The diagram must show a rightward supply shift, correct gain and loss areas, and loss larger than gain.
markingPoints: Explains that lower raw-material cost increases supply.
States that demand must be inelastic.
Compares percentage fall in price with percentage rise in quantity demanded.

questions.stem: Since 2020, many mask factories have been set up in Hong Kong to produce masks.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt:
Wearing a mask can effectively prevent an individual from contracting viruses and from spreading viruses to others. Explain how the behaviour of wearing a mask may involve externality.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: A popular Hong Kong music group held a concert in 2022. Tickets were publicly sold through URBTIX requiring real-name registration. When the tickets went on sale, a large number of people flocked to the website for the tickets. Many people said that they were unable to access the website until after the tickets had been sold out.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Suppose the waiting time to access the website for two people who have bought the tickets is the same. Would their costs of buying the tickets at the same price necessarily be the same? Why?
(3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: No. Their time may have different alternative uses, so their time costs may differ.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem: A popular Hong Kong music group held a concert in 2022. Tickets were publicly sold through URBTIX requiring real-name registration. When the tickets went on sale, a large number of people flocked to the website for the tickets. Many people said that they were unable to access the website until after the tickets had been sold out.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt:
By using real-name registration for ticket sales, ticket buyers must provide their full names in English as shown on a valid Hong Kong identity document when buying the tickets, and they must also present their identity documents with the same names stated on the tickets when entering the venue.
‘It is fairer to sell the tickets using real-name registration.’ Explain whether this is a positive statement or a normative statement.(2 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: It is normative because it contains a value judgement about fairness and is not refutable by facts.
markingPoints: Explains value judgement or lack of factual refutability.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meaning of private property rights and its importance in a market economy
questions.stem: A popular Hong Kong music group held a concert in 2022. Tickets were publicly sold through URBTIX requiring real-name registration. When the tickets went on sale, a large number of people flocked to the website for the tickets. Many people said that they were unable to access the website until after the tickets had been sold out.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt:
By using real-name registration for ticket sales, ticket buyers must provide their full names in English as shown on a valid Hong Kong identity document when buying the tickets, and they must also present their identity documents with the same names stated on the tickets when entering the venue.
Will the private property rights for the ticket owners over the tickets be weakened using real-name registration? Explain.(3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Yes. Private property rights include exclusive use, income and transfer rights. Real-name registration confines the owner's right to sell or transfer the ticket.
markingPoints: States a private-property right including transfer.
Explains that transfer or sale is confined.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Mr. Chan operates a tutorial center in the form of a sole proprietorship. He is considering expanding his business.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Mr. Chan plans to introduce new shareholders and run the tutorial center as a private limited company. List ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of the change in the business ownership.(2 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Advantages include independent legal status or better continuity. A disadvantage is a higher profits tax rate. Award one valid advantage and one valid disadvantage.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: Mr. Chan operates a tutorial center in the form of a sole proprietorship. He is considering expanding his business.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: After hiring more tutors, Mr. Chan found that all classrooms are fully booked and the marginal product of tutors has dropped. State the law that explains this phenomenon and briefly explain why this law can be applied to this case.(5 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: The law of diminishing marginal returns applies: in the short run, more units of a variable factor are added to a fixed factor and marginal product eventually falls. Tutors are variable factors while centre equipment is fixed.
markingPoints: States variable factor added to fixed factor.
Identifies tutors as variable and equipment as fixed.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: Mr. Chan operates a tutorial center in the form of a sole proprietorship. He is considering expanding his business.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: The wages of the tutors of the tutorial center are calculated based on the number of students, but Mr. Chan has found that the turnover rate of the tutors is high. Suggest ONE wage payment method that Mr. Chan can adopt to reduce the turnover rate of the tutors as well as to improve their teaching quality. Briefly explain your answer.(2 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Use basic salary plus commission. Basic salary safeguards tutors' basic livelihood and reduces turnover; commission rewards performance and encourages harder work and better teaching.
markingPoints: States basic salary plus commission or another valid method.
Explains both lower turnover and quality incentives.

parts.label: (a)

parts.modelAnswer: Advantages include economies of scale from larger production scale and lower average costs, and diversified income that spreads risk between online and physical business. Award any two reasonable advantages.

parts.modelAnswer: Cash fails as a medium of exchange because it does not facilitate buying and selling in the shop.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: ‘Inflation will occur when the total output of an economy is growing slower than the money supply.’ Explain this statement in terms of the quantity theory of money.(4 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: QTM is MV = PY. With velocity constant, if M grows faster than real output Y, P must rise. A rise in P is inflation.
markingPoints: Defines M, V, P and Y.

parts.modelAnswer: Nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate. Expected inflation is positive, so nominal interest exceeds real interest.
markingPoints: Explains positive expected inflation makes nominal rate higher.

questions.stem:
Studies have pointed out that it takes hundreds of years for plastic shopping bags to completely decompose. Toxic substances are released during the decomposition process, leading to environmental pollution.
Starting from 31 December, 2022, Hong Kong has raised the minimum charge for each plastic shopping bag from $0.5 to $1. In terms of externality, explain how increasing the charge for plastic shopping bags can improve economic efficiency. (4 marks)

parts.label: Q5
parts.prompt:
Studies have pointed out that it takes hundreds of years for plastic shopping bags to completely decompose. Toxic substances are released during the decomposition process, leading to environmental pollution.
Starting from 31 December, 2022, Hong Kong has raised the minimum charge for each plastic shopping bag from $0.5 to $1. In terms of externality, explain how increasing the charge for plastic shopping bags can improve economic efficiency. (4 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Bag use causes pollution and users do not compensate affected people, creating a negative externality with MSC above MPC. Consumption exceeds the efficient level. A higher charge reduces use towards the efficient level and narrows the divergence between private and social cost.
markingPoints: Identifies pollution as a cost imposed on others.
Explains lack of compensation and negative externality.
States MSC exceeds MPC and consumption exceeds the efficient level.

parts.prompt:
Suppose the government has two strategies to improve elderly services.
Strategy I: Increasing the import quota on care workers for residential care homes
Strategy II: Providing a living allowance for carers of the elderly who are ageing in place (i.e. the elderly living at home rather than in residential care homes) (居家安老的長者)
With reference to the above sources and your own knowledge in Economics, discuss the effects of each strategy on the following variables in order to evaluate the two strategies.
- aggregate output
- government expenditure
- unemployment rate
(14 marks)

END OF PAPEREND OF PAPER
parts.modelAnswer: Strategy I increases labour supply, raising SRAS and LRAS and aggregate output. It may add only minor administration cost, and with local recruitment exhausted it raises labour force without replacing local workers, so unemployment rate falls. Strategy II may reduce labour supply if carers quit or reduce hours, lowering output. It raises transfer payments but can reduce care-home spending, so net expenditure is uncertain. Its unemployment effect is uncertain: workers may leave and vacancies may or may not be filled, while unemployed carers leaving the labour force can lower the rate. Strategy I is generally preferable for output and unemployment; its expenditure effect is smaller and more certain.
markingPoints: Explains each strategy's labour-supply and aggregate-output effects.
Evaluates the strategies for aggregate output.
Explains Strategy II transfer-payment and potential care-home-spending effects.
Uses unemployment-rate relationship for Strategy I.
Explains the alternative unemployment outcomes under Strategy II.
Uses source evidence on failed local recruitment and imported workers.
Presents a logical comparison and conclusion.

questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem:
In Country A, the air pollution problem is serious. The government is considering how to improve the air quality.
Source A: Major sources of air pollution in Country A
Exhaust gas from diesel vehicles
Emissions from power plants
Pollutants emitted by factories
Source B: News report on Country A’s government imposing an additional sewage charge on industrial firms
To encourage enterprises to proactively improve their production systems to reduce the emission of pollutants, the government announced that, effective immediately, an additional sewage charge will be levied on industrial firms. The additional sewage charge is calculated based on their output. All firms that emit pollutants during the production process have to pay this additional sewage charge based on their output.
The public generally welcome the measure and believe that pollutants emitted by industrial firms can be reduced and the air quality can be improved. However, many industrial firms said that the measure will make their business more difficult.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Source C: Some views on air pollutionAn elderly womanThe air pollution in the area where I live is very serious. I need to use an air purifier at home all the time.A doctorAir pollution affects health, causing issues such as nose and throat irritation, coughing, and may aggravate symptoms for people with chronic respiratory diseases.A diesel private car driverI am used to driving a car. If the government does not provide incentives, I think I will not consider changing my travel mode. On the other hand, the government can consider providing incentives to encourage drivers to switch to electric cars that cause less air pollution.
Refer to the above sources. Explain, in terms of externalities, how pollutants emitted by factories may result in inefficiency.(3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Pollution imposes uncompensated costs on others; MSC exceeds MSB and emissions exceed efficient output.

parts.prompt:
Suppose the government has the following two proposals to promote low-carbon development:Proposal I:to increase the electricity charges relief provided to eligible residential electricity accounts in order to support power companies in continuing their low-carbon transitionProposal II:to provide tax incentives for households that install renewable energy systems and generate electricity using themWith reference to the above sources and your own knowledge in Economics, discuss the effects of EACH proposal on Hong Kong, including:-income distribution,-aggregate output, and-government revenue and/or expenditure(14 marks)

END OF PAPEREND OF PAPER
parts.modelAnswer: Proposal I gives eligible electricity accounts relief, producing a larger percentage income gain for low-income households and more even distribution; it raises disposable income, consumption, AD and short-run output, while efficiency investment can raise LRAS and long-run output. It raises government expenditure, but new clean-energy industries may raise profits-tax revenue. Proposal II mainly benefits higher-income households able to install high-cost systems, making income distribution less even; it raises household renewable-system spending and AD in the short run. Tax incentives reduce tax revenue, though higher producer profits may raise profits-tax revenue.
markingPoints: Explains Proposal I government-expenditure and possible revenue effects.
Explains Proposal II tax-revenue and producer-profit effects.
Presents a coherent comparison with effective communication.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
In recent years, public dental services in Hong Kong have been facing a shortage of dentists, which has affected the services of government dental clinics. The situation has raised public concerns.
Source A: News extract about the registration arrangements for public dental services
Public dental services in Hong Kong primarily serve civil servants/retired civil servants and their eligible dependents, offering very limited services to the general public in urgent need. As of February 2024, there are 43 government dental clinics in Hong Kong, 11 of which allocate specific sessions each week, commonly referred to as ‘general public (GP) sessions (牙科街症)’, to provide free emergency dental treatment services to members of the public in need.
Starting from 11 June 2024, the preliminary registration time for the GP sessions at 9 government dental clinics has been adjusted from midnight on the day of service to 8 pm the day before. Due to the limited quota, each person can only register once, and the spots are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. Some citizens have stated that although the registration time has changed, people still must queue up outside the clinics. Those who are unable to register will need to leave the clinic and will not be eligible for treatment at the GP session the following day.
Source B: News extract about the suspension of Civil Servants Dental Service
The Department of Health has been facing a shortage of dentists. According to the government data, the vacancy rate for dentists in the Department of Health reached 29.7% (as of the beginning of July 2024). Due to the shortage of dentists, services at approximately a quarter of the dental clinics providing Civil Servants Dental Service have been suspended. The manpower at school dental clinics and dental clinics in public hospitals has also been affected.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Source C: Some views on Hong Kong’s dental labour marketA university professorThe Faculty of Dentistry at the University of Hong Kong is currently the only institution that trains dentists in Hong Kong. I think the government should establish a new dental school to increase the number of local dentists.A commentatorEven if the government raises the wage rate of public dentists, it is still difficult to alleviate the shortage of dentists faced by the government dental clinics.A dental graduateAdjusting the remuneration of public dentists can attract dental graduates to join public institutions instead of private institutions.
Refer to Source A. Explain whether the cost for citizens of using free emergency dental treatment services is necessarily the same.(3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: No. Full cost equals monetary cost plus time cost. Although treatment is free, queueing time has different opportunity costs because people have different alternative uses of time.
markingPoints: States costs need not be the same.

Country A’s economy experienced a recession this year. How would the deadweight loss in the market of durians be affected? Explain your answer with the aid of a supply-demand diagram.

(6 marks)

parts.label: Q3
parts.prompt:
The government of Country A began to impose a per-unit tax on durian farmers 10 years ago. Suppose durians are normal goods to residents of Country A.
Country A’s economy experienced a recession this year. How would the deadweight loss in the market of durians be affected? Explain your answer with the aid of a supply-demand diagram.
(Hint: Assume the supply and demand curves of durians shift in a parallel manner.)
(6 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Income falls in recession, so durian demand and quantity transacted fall. The tax wedge and the difference between marginal benefit and marginal cost are unchanged, so the deadweight loss is unchanged.

States tax deadweight loss is unchanged.
Shows equal original and new deadweight-loss areas.

answerVisuals.alt: A recession shifts durian demand left while a per-unit tax leaves the deadweight-loss area unchanged.

movements: Demand shifts left from D0 to D1.
The tax wedge remains t.
The original and new deadweight-loss areas are equal.

questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: Greece has announced that starting from 2025, it will charge different cruise passenger fees for popular islands during peak, shoulder and low seasons. For example, cruise passengers who get off in Mykonos and Santorini during peak season will be charged 20 euros (approximately HK$170) per person.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt:
Many residents of Santorini think that the city has become overcrowded due to too many tourists.
Explain, in terms of externalities, how too many tourists visiting Santorini may result in inefficiency.(3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: Tourism creates a negative externality: residents suffer uncompensated overcrowding. Marginal social cost exceeds marginal social benefit, so tourist quantity exceeds the efficient level.
markingPoints: Links MSC above MSB to overconsumption.

parts.modelAnswer: The fee raises marginal private cost and narrows the gap between MPC and MSC, reducing tourist quantity toward the socially optimal level.

Source C: Two news reports about the taxi industryAs of August 2024, there are 18,163 taxis in Hong Kong. The average daily taxi patronage is near 1 million. The government has introduced the taxi fleet regime, under which operators may assemble existing taxis to form fleets and apply to the Transport Department for a taxi fleet licence.
