The Smart Traffic Fund has approved three projects relating to taxi driving safety, hoping to make good use of technology to improve taxi driving safety.Source D: A news report about online ride-hailing platformsCurrently, some private cars are illegally offering personalised point-to-point transport services through online ride-hailing platforms. In response, the government is considering enacting legislation to regulate these platforms. The proposed approach is that the platforms will need to obtain licenses and meet some other requirements. Vehicles on these platforms will need to have a hire car permit and insurance coverage, and drivers who work for a platform will only be allowed to provide pre-arranged services through the platform.Secretary for Transport and Logistics said that enacting legislation to regulate online ride-hailing platforms will make it legal for people to become drivers on these platforms, thereby attracting more drivers to the industry. parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Suppose there are two suggestions to improve the personalised point-to-point transport services in Hong Kong.Suggestion ILegalise online ride-hailing platforms and lower the requirements for hire car permits.Suggestion IIOffer tax deductions to taxi operators for expenditures related to upgrading vehicle equipment, such as the installation of electronic payment tools and closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems.With reference to the above sources and your own knowledge in Economics, discuss which suggestion, suggestion I or II, the government will prefer in order to achieve EACH of the following policy objectives respectively.Objective 1:increasing the total revenue in the market described in each suggestionObjective 2:improving the government’s fiscal balance Objective 3:lowering the unemployment rate(14 marks)(Use a separate paragraph for each policy objective, comparing the effects of the two suggestions.)
parts.modelAnswer: For total revenue, both may work but II is more certain because equipment convenience raises taxi demand; I raises ride-hailing supply and revenue only if demand is elastic. For fiscal balance, I can raise salaries-tax revenue while II's tax deductions lower revenue, so I is preferable. For unemployment, I creates driver jobs and is preferable; taxi upgrades need not increase taxi-driver demand when licences are fixed.

parts.label: Q4
parts.prompt:
To reduce people’s consumption of high-sugar foods, the government of Country A levies a per-unit sales tax on the manufacturers of high-sugar foods.

In Hong Kong, the Northwest New Territories and the urban area are mainly connected by Tuen Mun Road and Tai Lam Tunnel. The traffic congestion on Tuen Mun Road has long been a concern of the public. The HKSAR Government has taken back the franchise of the Tai Lam Tunnel and has carried out a series of renewal arrangements.Source A: News extract about the HKSAR Government’s takeover of the Tai Lam TunnelThe franchise of the company responsible for operating Tai Lam Tunnel expired on 31 May 2025. The Tai Lam Tunnel has been handed over to the government, marking the end of its private operation phase.After the government took back the Tai Lam Tunnel, it promptly lowered the tunnel tolls and implemented a time-varying toll plan. For private cars, the previous toll was $58.The time-varying toll plan for private cars is now as follows:Sundays and general holidaysMondays to Saturdays$18Peak time slot$45Normal time slot$30Off-peak time slot$18At the same time, the government implemented HKeToll, a free-flow tolling service, in Tai Lam Tunnel, hoping that the new arrangements will attract more vehicles to use the tunnel and fully utilise its remaining capacity, as well as relieve the traffic pressure on Tuen Mun Road, which serves as an alternative route.(Source: various newspapers)Source B: Introduction to HKeTollHKeToll is a free-flow tolling system that allows drivers to pay tolls remotely, without having to stop and queue up at toll booths for payments when passing through the tunnel, reducing queuing time.When a vehicle passes through the toll point of the ‘HKeToll’ tunnel, the system will automatically detect the vehicle and collect the toll.Vehicle owners only need to open an HKeToll account, set up an automatic payment means (such as credit card, bank transfer or other electronic payment methods) and install a vehicle tag to the vehicle to use HKeToll.After the implementing of HKeToll, the toll booths of the relevant tunnels will be removed.(Source: Transport Department, HKSAR Government)
Source C: Some views on the Tai Lam TunnelA commentatorCurrently, there is spare capacity in the Tai Lam Tunnel and implementing the time-varying toll plan can help increase utilisation of the tunnel.A private car driverAlthough Tuen Mun Road is often congested during peak hours, I still use it frequently because it is free! The toll for the Tai Lam Tunnel during peak hours is too high.A Yuen Long residentTime and cost are important factors for me when deciding whether to take the bus or drive. After the implementation of the time-varying toll plan and HKeToll, it has become more convenient for me to drive to Kowloon. Although I will have to pay for petrol, I believe I will be driving more often.

Suppose there are two proposals to improve transport options for residents in the Northwest New Territories:Proposal Ito construct a new trunk road connecting the urban area with the Northwest New Territories (as an alternative to Tuen Mun Road)Proposal IIto provide fare subsidies for bus routes commuting between the Northwest New Territories and the urban areaWith reference to the above sources and your own knowledge in Economics, discuss the effects of each proposal on the following variables in order to evaluate the two proposals.-economic efficiency-income distribution-aggregate output(14 marks)
END OF PAPEREND OF PAPER
parts.modelAnswer: Proposal I diverts traffic from congested Tuen Mun Road, reducing unpriced external cost and moving car use closer to efficiency. It can help lower-income Northwest New Territories residents access higher-paid work. Construction raises investment and AD in the short run and capital/LRAS in the long run. Proposal II may create deadweight loss by expanding subsidised bus use, but can reduce car congestion and external cost. It directly raises disposable income for public-transport users, especially lower-income residents, and raises consumption and AD in the short run. Proposal I has the more certain efficiency and longer-run output effect; Proposal II more directly improves income distribution.

Oscar is considering his career path after university graduation. His order of preference is as follows:
First option: to work as an administrative officer in the government
Second option: to work as a junior accountant in an accounting firm
Third option: to study a master’s degree programme
Suppose Oscar has been awarded a scholarship for admission to the master’s programme by the university. Analyse whether Oscar’s opportunity cost for choosing to work as an administrative officer in the government will necessarily remain unchanged. (3 marks)

parts.label: Q1
parts.prompt:
Oscar is considering his career path after university graduation. His order of preference is as follows:
First option: to work as an administrative officer in the government
Second option: to work as a junior accountant in an accounting firm
Third option: to study a master’s degree programme
Suppose Oscar has been awarded a scholarship for admission to the master’s programme by the university. Analyse whether Oscar’s opportunity cost for choosing to work as an administrative officer in the government will necessarily remain unchanged. (3 marks)
parts.modelAnswer: No. The scholarship raises the value of the degree. If it becomes higher than the accountant option, the highest-valued forgone option changes, so opportunity cost changes.
markingPoints: Explains change in highest-valued forgone option.

在2025年11月，第十五屆全國運動會(全運會)於廣東、香港和澳門舉行，為香港首次參與承辦這項全國體育盛事。全運會期間，不少比賽在本地免費電視台中進行賽事直播。部分受歡迎的比賽項目的門票在開售不久已售罄。
在全運會首週，整體約有99萬人次旅客入境香港，當中內地旅客約有72萬，按周增加約10萬。一些酒店的房間在全運會期間預約爆滿。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 解釋本地免費電視台的賽事直播是否屬於共用品。(3分)

markingPoints: 解釋不具競爭性或不具排他性。

questions.stem: 假設政府對賣家在市場中售出的每瓶牛奶徵收從量稅。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
以圖輔助，解釋在甚麼情況下消費者的稅項負擔會大於生產者的稅項負擔。
(7分)
parts.modelAnswer: 當需求較供應低彈性。稅令供應向上移、價格上升、交易量下降；圖中消費者負擔較大。

movements: 供應曲線因稅向上移。
交易量下降。

questions.topicGroup: 貨幣價格（名義價格）和相對價格
questions.keyPoint: 將相對價格或全價格應用於需求定律，以解釋特定現象
questions.stem: 假設政府對賣家在市場中售出的每瓶牛奶徵收從量稅。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 有調查發現，在向牛奶徵收從量稅後，該國人民消費相對較多的大瓶裝牛奶。試以需求定律解釋這個現象。(4分)
parts.modelAnswer: 大瓶裝貨幣價格一般較高。從量稅使大瓶裝相對於小瓶裝的相對價格下降，按需求定律人們相對多購買大瓶裝。

questions.keyPoint: 不同的付酬方式
questions.stem: 假設政府對賣家在市場中售出的每瓶牛奶徵收從量稅。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt:
以下是某牛奶生產商的招聘廣告。
職位︰牛奶推銷員
工作時間︰上午10時至下午5時，每週工作3天
薪酬︰每月$8,000，另加佣金
從牛奶生產商的角度出發，解釋採用上述工資制度相對計時工資的一個優點和一個缺點。(2分)
parts.modelAnswer: 佣金鼓勵推銷員努力工作、降低監督成本；計算工資成本較高。

questions.keyPoint: 勞力的流動性
questions.stem:
香港特區政府近年積極發展北部都會區（北都）和鄰近區域，人們都關注該發展為香港帶來的經濟機遇和潛在影響。
資料A：有關北部都會區的簡介
根據《行政長官2025年施政報告》，北都是香港的戰略發展區域，具備巨大的經濟價值和發展潛力。北都預計可提供3,000多公頃新發展土地，在未來五年，將會有約7萬個房屋單位落成入伙，未來人口約佔全港的三分之一。
（資料來源：《行政長官2025年施政報告》）
資料B：有關「智綠產業港」的新聞報導
發展局建議在鄰近北部都會區的屯門西及龍鼓灘發展「智綠產業港」，當中約190公頃土地會透過填海建造。「智綠產業港」建議發展四個核心產業，分別是「綠色/新能源」、「先進建造業」、「循環經濟」和「現代物流業/內河碼頭」。計劃亦建議興建全新的跨灣橋連接龍鼓灘填海區，以應付新增的行車流量。計劃預計可創造35,000個就業機會。
（資料來源：綜合報導）
資料C：有關港鐵北環線的資料
北環線為推動北部都會區發展的主要交通基建項目，將建於古洞站及錦上路站之間，連接東鐵綫及屯馬綫，在新界北形成一個環狀鐵路網絡，縮短車程時間。北環線預計於2034年竣工。

2011-12年度起，醫院管理局（醫管局）推出計劃聘請符合指明條件的非本地培訓醫生，以紓緩人手緊絀的情況。2021年，政府推出新的特別註冊途徑，讓持有認可醫學資格的非本地培訓醫生，讓他們可在符合指明條件的情況下，在醫管局擔任醫生工作並獲得正式註冊，而申請人無需參加本地的執業資格試。

questions.stem:
西九文化區是香港重要的文化藝術項目。於2023年，到訪西九文化區的本地居民及旅客達1,260萬人次。近年其財政狀況引起公眾關注。
資料A：西九文化區的簡介
西九文化區內設有多項文化設施，包括香港故宮文化博物館和戲曲中心。此外，區內亦設有酒店、辦公室、餐飲及消閒設施。
西九文化區由西九文化區管理局（西九管理局）以自負盈虧的方式營運，而西九管理局為政府於2008年成立的非牟利法定機構。西九管理局需要確保西九文化區財務的可持續性。
（資料來源：西九文化區官方網站）
資料B：西九文化區的財政摘要
（資料來源：西九文化區管理局2023/24周年報告）
資料C：關於西九文化區的新聞報導
一位政府官員表示，西九管理局直接聘用的員工人數逾1,400人。若把間接產生的就業機會（如旅遊業相關配套）計算在內，西九文化區創造了逾10,000個就業機會。
（資料來源：綜合報導）

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
資料D：關於西九文化區的財政狀況的看法一位經濟科教師西九管理局或需削減聘請外地專才的職位數量以節省開支。一位時事評論員西九管理局的收入籌款、場地租用、門票收入、博物館商品銷售、銀行利息等。然而，目前的財政結構難以持續，西九管理局或需想辦法開源節流，以扭虧為盈。一位藝術界人士經營一家博物館涉及不同種類的成本，包括購買收藏品的開支、市場推廣開支等等。這些支出高昂，為西九管理局帶來財政壓力。一名會計師若西九管理局向私人地產發展商出售住宅發展項目，預計西九管理局可獲得一次性的巨額收入。然而，最近住宅物業市場低迷或會減低地產發展商對項目的興趣。

questions.stem:
西九文化區是香港重要的文化藝術項目。於2023年，到訪西九文化區的本地居民及旅客達1,260萬人次。近年其財政狀況引起公眾關注。
資料A：西九文化區的簡介
西九文化區內設有多項文化設施，包括香港故宮文化博物館和戲曲中心。此外，區內亦設有酒店、辦公室、餐飲及消閒設施。
西九文化區由西九文化區管理局（西九管理局）以自負盈虧的方式營運，而西九管理局為政府於2008年成立的非牟利法定機構。西九管理局需要確保西九文化區財務的可持續性。
（資料來源：西九文化區官方網站）

（資料來源：西九文化區管理局2023/24周年報告）

資料A：有關重新徵收酒店房租稅的報導
香港特區政府自2008年7月1日將酒店房租稅的稅率維持在0%。在2024-25年度財政預算案中，政府建議重新徵收酒店房租稅。由2025年1月1日起，酒店房租稅的稅率為房租的3%。

放寬香港酒店業輸入低技術外地勞工的限制

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt:
不少聖托里尼島的居民表示遊客過多導致城市非常擁擠。
以界外影響為依據，解釋過多的遊客到訪聖托里尼島如何可能導致缺乏效率。(3分)
parts.modelAnswer: 屬負面界外影響；居民受擠擁損害但無補償，MSC 高於 MSB，遊客數量高於效率水平。

parts.modelAnswer: 收費提高 MPC，收窄 MPC 與 MSC 差距，遊客數量降至較接近社會最優水平。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 「由於每名旅客都需要繳付等額的費用，不論其出發地，這會導致歐洲旅客佔到訪聖托里尼島的旅客比例下降，而亞洲旅客所佔的比例上升。」以需求定律解釋這論點。(4分)
parts.modelAnswer: 費用令長途旅客相對短途旅客的價格下降；按需求定律，長途旅客比例上升，短途旅客比例下降。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt:
有人指出即使徵收郵輪乘客費用，在旺季到訪聖托里尼島的遊客數目也未必會明顯減少。
根據該觀點，我們可就在旺季到訪聖托里尼島的旅程的需求及/或供應彈性得出甚麼結論？試解釋。(3分)
parts.modelAnswer: 需求缺乏彈性，需求量跌幅百分比小於價格升幅百分比。

資料B：市民對的士調整收費的看法
陳先生
新收費下，我在繁忙時段輪候的士所需的時間明顯縮短了。
李小姐
現時，很多的士都缺乏電子支付選項。我經常因為沒有足夠現金而未能即時乘搭的士。若的士不改善車輛設備，我認為加價是不合理的。

資料C：兩則有關的士行業的新聞節錄截至2024年8月，本港共有18,163輛的士，平均每日載客量約一百萬人次。政府引入的士車隊制度，讓營運者可集合現有的士組成車隊，向運輸署申請的士車隊牌照。政府會透過牌照條件規管的士車隊的營運和管理，並訂明車隊的士須安裝的裝置，以提升車隊的士的駕駛安全和服務質素。政府已推出十億元的「智慧交通基金」，資助企業及機構研究和應用與車輛有關的創新科技，以便利出行、提升道路網絡和路面使用效率，以及改善駕駛安全。「智慧交通基金」已批出三個與的士駕駛安全有關的項目，希望能善用科技，以提升的士駕駛安全。資料D：有關網約出租汽車平台的新聞報導 現時，一些私家車透過網約出租汽車平台非法提供個人化點對點交通服務。為此，政府正計劃立法規管這些平台。建議方向是平台公司需獲發牌及滿足一些其他的要求，包括平台下的車輛必須持有出租汽車許可證及保險保障，以及為平台服務的司機只可透過平台提供預約服務。運輸及物流局局長表示，立法規管網約車平台後，人們可合法地成為網約車平台司機，有助吸引司機入行，亦可確保市民的出行安全及權益。

questions.stem:

環保團體代表：
將農地轉為太陽能發電場有助減少依賴化石燃料，從而減少碳排放，有助緩解氣候變化問題。

若更多農地被改建為太陽能發電場，農作物市場的消費者盈餘將會受影響。

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt:
假設有以下兩項建議以提 振 香港的零售 市場 。
建議 I 向所有 居民 派發只限於香港零售商戶使用的消費券
建議 II 向香港零售商戶提供租金補貼
參考以上各項資料並就你對經濟學的認識，討論上述兩項建議對香港的影
響，包括：
- 本地零售商戶的利潤極大化產量
- 收入分布
- 一般物價水平
（提示：為了簡化，假設 香港 零售市場為 完全競爭市場 。 ）
(14 分 )
parts.modelAnswer: I 提高零售需求、MR 和產量；消費券按比例有較平均效果，AD 和物價上升。II 降低固定租金，利潤極大化產量不變，利益偏向店主、可加劇不平等；II 可提高 AD 又降低 SRAS，物價效果不確定。
markingPoints: 解釋 I 的 AD／物價。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem:
近年，香港公營牙科服務面對牙醫短缺問題，影響公營牙科診所服務，情況令人關注。
資料A：有關公營牙科服務登記安排的報導
香港的公營牙科服務主要為公務員/退休公務員及其合資格家屬服務，為有迫切需要的公眾提供的服務非常有限。截至2024年2月，全港設有43間政府牙科診所，其中11間每星期劃出特定時段，為有需要的市民提供免費緊急牙科治療(俗稱「牙科街症」)。
自2024年6月11日起，9間提供牙科街症服務的政府牙科診所的初步登記時間，已由服務當日凌晨零時提前至服務前一日晚上8時。由於名額有限，每人只可登記一次，先到先得。有市民表示，即使更改登記時間，市民仍然要在診所外排隊。未能成功登記的市民須離開診所，並無法在第二天的牙科街症時段獲得治療。
資料B：有關公務員牙科服務停運的報導
衞生署面對牙醫不足的問題。根據政府數據顯示，截至2024年7月初，衞生署的牙醫空缺率為29.7%。大約四分之一提供公務員牙科服務的診所因牙醫短缺而暫停服務，學童牙科診所、公立醫院的牙科診所的人手亦受影響。
資料C：對香港牙科勞工市場的一些看法
一名大學教授
香港大學牙醫學院是香港目前唯一一間培訓牙醫的院校，我認為政府應開設新牙醫學院以增加本地牙醫人手。
一名評論員
即使政府調高公營牙醫的工資率，公營牙科服務面對的牙醫短缺問題仍然難以舒緩。
一名牙科畢業生
調整公營牙醫的待遇可吸引牙科畢業生投身公營機構，而不是投入私人機構。

parts.prompt: 參考資料A。解釋市民使用免費緊急牙科治療服務的成本是否必然相同。(3分)
parts.modelAnswer: 否。全成本 = 金錢成本 + 時間成本。即使服務免費，排隊時間有不同的其他用途，時間成本未必相同。

資料A：有關公營牙科服務登記安排的報導
香港的公營牙科服務主要為公務員/退休公務員及其合資格家屬服務，為有迫切需要的公眾提供的服務非常有限。截至2024年2月，全港設有43間政府牙科診所，其中11間每星期劃出特定時段，為有需要的市民提供免費緊急牙科治療(俗稱「牙科街症」)。
自2024年6月11日起，9間提供牙科街症服務的政府牙科診所的初步登記時間，已由服務當日凌晨零時提前至服務前一日晚上8時。由於名額有限，每人只可登記一次，先到先得。有市民表示，即使更改登記時間，市民仍然要在診所外排隊。未能成功登記的市民須離開診所，並無法在第二天的牙科街症時段獲得治療。
資料B：有關公務員牙科服務停運的報導
衞生署面對牙醫不足的問題。根據政府數據顯示，截至2024年7月初，衞生署的牙醫空缺率為29.7%。大約四分之一提供公務員牙科服務的診所因牙醫短缺而暫停服務，學童牙科診所、公立醫院的牙科診所的人手亦受影響。
資料C：對香港牙科勞工市場的一些看法
一名大學教授
香港大學牙醫學院是香港目前唯一一間培訓牙醫的院校，我認為政府應開設新牙醫學院以增加本地牙醫人手。
一名評論員
即使政府調高公營牙醫的工資率，公營牙科服務面對的牙醫短缺問題仍然難以舒緩。
一名牙科畢業生
調整公營牙醫的待遇可吸引牙科畢業生投身公營機構，而不是投入私人機構。

假設有以下兩項建議以改善香港公營牙科服務人手緊絀的問題。
建議I︰派發「牙科醫療券」，資助市民使用私營牙科服務
建議II︰聘請更多非本地培訓牙醫提供公營牙科服務
參考以上各項資料並就你對經濟學的認識，討論以下每組持份者會偏好哪項建議(建議I或II)：
-關注低收入人士能否及時獲得牙科服務的政客
-私營牙科診所的東主
（提示：你可討論為甚麼某組持份者偏好某項建議，或為甚麼該組持份者並不偏好另一建議。）

假設政府有以下兩項有關推動低碳發展的建議。
建議I︰調高向合資格電力住宅用戶提供的電費紓緩金，以支持電力公司繼續進行低碳轉型
建議II：為安裝可再生能源系統及使用可再生能源系統發電的住戶提供稅務優惠
參考以上各項資料並就你對經濟學的認識，分別討論上述兩項建議對香港的影響，包括：
-收入分布
-總產出
-政府收入及/或支出
(14分)

parts.modelAnswer: I 令低收入住戶的收入較大百分比增加，分布較平均；可支配收入、消費、AD 和短期產出上升，能源效率可提升 LRAS 和長期產出；政府支出上升，潔淨能源新產業或增加利得稅。II 主要惠及能承擔高安裝成本的高收入住戶，分布較不平均；安裝支出提高 AD 和短期產出；稅務優惠減少稅收，但生產者利潤上升或提高利得稅。

visuals.caption: 資料D：關於推動可再生能源的使用和進行低碳轉型的一些看法
rows: 我認為政府應更大力發展可再生能源。安裝可再生能源系統涉及的成本高昂。如果政府撥款資助住戶於其處所內安裝可再生能源系統，例如太陽能發電系統，相信會有更多住戶參與。
即使電力公司上調電費，一般市民的生活成本不會大幅上升。進行低碳轉型對市民的影響不大。
電力公司在低碳轉型過程中，嘗試透過提高能源系統的效率，減少使用非可再生燃料來發電。投資潔淨能源基建亦有助建立新產業。

questions.keyPoint: 私用品及共用品
questions.stem: 某影片分享平台上不少人內容創作者除了提供免費影片外，亦設立會員制，觀眾付費成為該頻道的會員後，便可享有會員專屬福利，例如會員獨享影片、直播等。

parts.prompt: 解釋影片平台上的會員獨享影片是否共用品。(3分)

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 總社會盈餘達致最大：邊際利益等於邊際成本
questions.stem: 現時，香港不少政府服務的收費都低於成本。為舒緩財政壓力，有人提出政府應調整各項政府收費，包括與民生相關的政府服務收費，例如康樂及文化事務署的康體設施。提出正反論點各一以討論提高這些康體設施收費這建議。(4分)

parts.label: Q4
parts.prompt: 現時，香港不少政府服務的收費都低於成本。為舒緩財政壓力，有人提出政府應調整各項政府收費，包括與民生相關的政府服務收費，例如康樂及文化事務署的康體設施。提出正反論點各一以討論提高這些康體設施收費這建議。(4分)
parts.modelAnswer: 支持：收費接近均衡價格，MB 與 MC 差距收窄，效率改善。反對：低收入人士或無法負擔，失去運動及提升健康／收入能力機會，機會均等下降、社會較不公平。

parts.label: (b)

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 外賣平台不時以豁免運費作為推廣活動。試運用需求定律，解釋此舉會如何影響小額訂單的數量相對大額訂單的數量的比例。(4分)

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)

questions.stem:
甲國的空氣污染問題嚴重，政府正考慮如何改善空氣質素。
資料A：甲國的空氣污染的主要來源
來自柴油車輛的廢氣
發電廠的排放
工廠排放的污染物
資料B：關於甲國政府向工業廠商徵收附加排污費的新聞報導
為促進企業主動改善生產系統，以減少排放污染物，政府宣布即日起向工業廠商徵收一項附加排污費。附加排污費從量計算，凡廠商在生產過程中排放出廢氣污染物，均須按其產量繳付此附加排污費。
市民普遍歡迎有關措施，認為可減少工業廠商排放污染物，改善空氣質素。然而，有不少工業廠商表示有關措施讓他們的經營變得更困難。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 參考以上各項資料，以界外影響為依據，解釋工廠排放的污染物如何可能導致缺乏效率。(3分)
parts.modelAnswer: 污染令他人承受健康損害等成本，工廠沒有補償，存在界外損害；MSC 大於 MSB，排放量高於效率水平。

(11分)

資料B：關於政府推出建造業及運輸業輸入勞工計劃及優化現有「補充勞工計劃」的資料

假設政府有以下兩項策略以改善安老服務。

- 政府支出
- 失業率
(14分)

試卷完試卷完
parts.modelAnswer: 策略 I 增加勞力供應，SRAS、LRAS 及短長期產出上升；行政成本可能上升但不顯著，且本地招聘已不足，失業人口不變而勞動人口上升，失業率下降。策略 II 可令照顧者辭職或減時，勞動人口、供應和產出或下降；轉移支付上升但院舍支出或下降，淨政府支出及失業率不確定。策略 I 對產出和失業率較有利，政府支出影響亦較小且確定。

questions.stem: 政府宣布於2022年9月將普通長者生活津貼和高額長者生活津貼合併，合併後的長者生活津貼將採用現時普通津貼較寬鬆的資產上限，並按高額津貼的金額發放。現正領取普通生活津貼的長者，會轉為領取高額津貼，每月多領近1,000元。

questions.keyPoint: 私人廠商的分類：獨資、合夥、私人有限公司及公眾有限公司
questions.stem:
鐵路運輸在香港公共運輸系統上十分重要，鐵路網絡在香港的覆蓋範圍亦日趨完善。
資料A：有關東鐵綫過海段通車的新聞節錄
香港鐵路有限公司(港鐵)(股票編號︰0066)為香港提供鐵路服務，其中東鐵綫過海段於2022年5月15日正式通車，是香港第四條過海鐵路。東鐵綫過海段造價約915億元，由政府斥資興建，香港鐵路有限公司負責興建及營運。
（資料來源：綜合報導）
資料B：東鐵綫的基本資料
東鐵綫全綫長約46公里，是繼荃灣綫、將軍澳綫及東涌綫後的第四條過海鐵路，以金鐘作新終點站，過海段新增了會展站。
全綫有四個轉綫站，連接五條現有鐵路綫，包括屯馬綫、觀塘綫、荃灣綫、港島綫及南港島綫。金鐘站成為四綫轉乘的超級轉車站。
（資料來源：香港鐵路有限公司官方網站）

東鐵綫過海段通車後，巴士客量全日整體下跌約2萬人次。某過海巴士線的特別班次服務的載客率更由以往七成下跌至約兩成。政府考慮稍後按乘客實際需要，分階段調整巴士服務安排。資料C：對東鐵綫過海段通車後巴士客量變化的報導 資料D：對東鐵綫過海段通車的一些看法一名評論員新界北部地區的交通變得更便利，預期這些地區的商舖和住宅物業的租金和價格都會上升。一名巴士司機東鐵綫過海段通車後，很多巴士乘客可能會轉為乘搭鐵路，我擔心工作可能會受到影響！一名銀行職員我住在大埔，我習慣駕駛私家車上班。我以往不會考慮到港島區工作，東鐵綫過海段通車後我或許會考慮。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:

markingPoints: 指出上市／公眾有限公司。

鐵路運輸在香港公共運輸系統上十分重要，鐵路網絡在香港的覆蓋範圍亦日趨完善。
資料A：有關東鐵綫過海段通車的新聞節錄
香港鐵路有限公司(港鐵)(股票編號︰0066)為香港提供鐵路服務，其中東鐵綫過海段於2022年5月15日正式通車，是香港第四條過海鐵路。東鐵綫過海段造價約915億元，由政府斥資興建，香港鐵路有限公司負責興建及營運。
（資料來源：綜合報導）
資料B：東鐵綫的基本資料
東鐵綫全綫長約46公里，是繼荃灣綫、將軍澳綫及東涌綫後的第四條過海鐵路，以金鐘作新終點站，過海段新增了會展站。
全綫有四個轉綫站，連接五條現有鐵路綫，包括屯馬綫、觀塘綫、荃灣綫、港島綫及南港島綫。金鐘站成為四綫轉乘的超級轉車站。
（資料來源：香港鐵路有限公司官方網站）

parts.label: (f)
parts.prompt:
考生須以短文形式回答(f)部。評分準則包括運用資料及經濟理論，內容切題，鋪排合乎邏輯，以及表達清晰。
假設政府現有以下兩項有關香港的公共運輸系統的建議。建議I︰重組巴士路線，包括取消部分載客量低的巴士路線建議II︰興建新的鐵路支綫參考以上各項資料，並就你對經濟學的認識，分別討論政府為求達成以下每項政策目標時，會偏好哪個建議。目標1：降低市民的交通成本目標2：增加政府將來的收入目標3：降低失業率(14分)(就每項政策目標比較兩個策略的影響時，同學須開新段。)
試卷完試卷完
parts.modelAnswer: 取消路線可令鐵路擠迫、時間成本上升；新支綫可降低金錢及時間成本，故目標一偏好 II。兩者可增收入，但新支綫可推高物業價值、印花稅及薪俸稅，收入作用較強。取消路線可令司機失業，新支綫創造職位，故降低失業率偏好 II。需同時討論反向效果。
markingPoints: 比較兩建議的交通成本。
解釋新支綫降低金錢或時間成本。
解釋取消路線的收入效果。
解釋新支綫物業、印花稅或薪俸稅效果。
解釋取消路線可增失業。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 聘請更多工人後，在運載傢俱的貨車數量不變的情況下，該公司發現工人的平均訂單數目比以往少，工人的邊際產出下降了。寫出解釋這現象的定律，並簡單解釋為甚麼該定律可應用於此個案。(5分)
parts.modelAnswer: 邊際回報遞減定律：短期內，當可變生產要素不斷增加、固定生產要素維持不變，在其他因素不變下，邊際產量最終會下跌。工人是可變要素，貨車是固定要素。
markingPoints: 指出邊際回報遞減定律。

questions.topicGroup: 貨幣價格（名義價格）和相對價格
questions.keyPoint: 將相對價格或全價格應用於需求定律，以解釋特定現象
questions.stem: 參閱以下某桌上遊戲店的收費安排。收費半日券$100全日券$180在該店要求每位顧客必須惠顧最少一份小食後，全日券的售出量相對半日券的售出量的比例上升。試以需求定律解釋這個現象。(5分)

parts.label: Q2
parts.prompt: 參閱以下某桌上遊戲店的收費安排。收費半日券$100全日券$180在該店要求每位顧客必須惠顧最少一份小食後，全日券的售出量相對半日券的售出量的比例上升。試以需求定律解釋這個現象。(5分)
parts.modelAnswer: 需求定律指其他因素不變下，價格上升（下降）令需求量下降（上升）。加上小食價格後，全日券相對於半日券的價格下降；相對半日券，人們購買更多全日券，比例上升。
markingPoints: 解釋全日券相對價格下降。
應用需求定律說明相對購買較多全日券。

questions.keyPoint: 人造資源：資本
questions.stem:
海洋公園是香港其中一個主題樂園，每年吸引不少訪客前往遊玩。近年其財政狀況引起公眾關注，有些人擔心它會倒閉。
資料A：海洋公園的簡介
海洋公園位於香港島南面，由海洋公園公司管理，是本地及海外遊客最喜愛的景點之一。公園提供海洋主題景點和機動遊戲，亦飼養了不同品種的昆蟲、魚類、鳥類和海洋哺乳類動物供遊客觀賞，是集娛樂、教育與保育並重的教育主題公園。
（資料來源：香港海洋公園官方網站）
資料B：有關海洋公園水上樂園開幕的新聞報導
海洋公園水上樂園在2021年9月21日正式開幕，是亞洲首個全年並全天候開放的臨海水上樂園，設室內及戶外玩樂設施。
水上樂園開幕當日的成人和小童票價分別為$320和$225。水上樂園門票採用「動態定價系統」，即售價會根據季節性、平日或週末調節，在公眾假期，票價可升至$400以上。海洋公園預料水上樂園每年可為海洋公園帶來逾3億元的收入。
（資料來源：綜合報導）
資料C：海洋公園2019/20和2020/21財政年度的訪客數量及入場券收入
（資料來源：海洋公園公司業績報告）

資料D︰關於政府向海洋公園公司提供補助金的新聞報導2016年至2019年間，海洋公園持續出現虧損。受2019冠狀病毒病疫情影響，遊客數目大減，市民減少外出，海洋公園在2020至2021年間更多次關閉，嚴重影響公園的收入，海洋公園公司在營運和發展上面對巨大的財政挑戰。政府向海洋公園撥款，供海洋公園支付其營運開支，及償還公司的商業貸款，以避免海洋公園倒閉。（資料來源：綜合報導） 資料E：對海洋公園或面臨倒閉的看法一名內地遊客我的兒子十分喜歡到海洋公園遊玩。若公園倒閉，我們未必會再來香港了！一名海洋公園員工海洋公園公司聘請大量員工，一旦海洋公園倒閉，我們便會失去工作。一名區議員一些旅客到訪海洋公園後會前往鄰近地區的食肆，海洋公園倒閉將會影響這些食肆的收入。一名會計師海洋公園公司日後仍可能會因出現虧損而再需要政府撥款。

海洋公園位於香港島南面，由海洋公園公司管理，是本地及海外遊客最喜愛的景點之一。公園提供海洋主題景點和機動遊戲，亦飼養了不同品種的昆蟲、魚類、鳥類和海洋哺乳類動物供遊客觀賞，是集娛樂、教育與保育並重的教育主題公園。
（資料來源：香港海洋公園官方網站）
資料B：有關海洋公園水上樂園開幕的新聞報導
海洋公園水上樂園在2021年9月21日正式開幕，是亞洲首個全年並全天候開放的臨海水上樂園，設室內及戶外玩樂設施。
水上樂園開幕當日的成人和小童票價分別為$320和$225。水上樂園門票採用「動態定價系統」，即售價會根據季節性、平日或週末調節，在公眾假期，票價可升至$400以上。海洋公園預料水上樂園每年可為海洋公園帶來逾3億元的收入。
（資料來源：綜合報導）
資料C：海洋公園2019/20和2020/21財政年度的訪客數量及入場券收入
（資料來源：海洋公園公司業績報告）

資料D︰關於政府向海洋公園公司提供補助金的新聞報導2016年至2019年間，海洋公園持續出現虧損。受2019冠狀病毒病疫情影響，遊客數目大減，市民減少外出，海洋公園在2020至2021年間更多次關閉，嚴重影響公園的收入，海洋公園公司在營運和發展上面對巨大的財政挑戰。政府向海洋公園撥款，供海洋公園支付其營運開支，及償還公司的商業貸款，以避免海洋公園倒閉。（資料來源：綜合報導） 資料E：對海洋公園或面臨倒閉的看法一名內地遊客我的兒子十分喜歡到海洋公園遊玩。若公園倒閉，我們未必會再來香港了！一名海洋公園員工海洋公園公司聘請大量員工，一旦海洋公園倒閉，我們便會失去工作。一名區議員一些旅客到訪海洋公園後會前往鄰近地區的食肆，海洋公園倒閉將會影響這些食肆的收入。一名會計師海洋公園公司日後仍可能會因出現虧損而再需要政府撥款。

近年香港不少人喜歡飼養狗隻，然而不少屋苑都不允許住戶飼養狗隻。

questions.keyPoint: 人造資源：資本
questions.stem: 有「地球之肺」之稱的亞馬遜雨林是全球最大的雨林。2019年8月，亞馬遜雨林發生了一場大火。資料一：亞馬遜雨林的簡介(資料來源：綜合報導)資料二：亞馬遜雨林大火的新聞報導亞馬遜雨林的大火引起國際關注。七大工業國集團(G7)同意提供2,000萬美元協助救災及善後工作。多個國際慈善機構亦於全球多個國家呼籲民眾捐助以保護亞馬遜雨林。大火的成因仍然眾說紛紜。有些人懷疑有農民以焚燒方式開墾土地，釀成山火。巴西總統已簽署禁令，暫時禁止農民以焚燒的方式清理農地。 (資料來源：綜合報導)資料三：對保育亞馬遜雨林的一些看法環保組織大型企業應該停止向巴西購買由破壞雨林所得的土地畜牧生產的肉類製品，以及停止使用來自亞馬遜地區的咖啡、紙張和木材。歐洲服飾零售商我們決定停止從巴西進口皮革，除非生產商能確保在生產皮革的過程中不會危害雨林。市民政府應該訂立更嚴格的法規，以及加強執法。阻止農民非法砍伐及焚燒樹林。商人為避免雨林進一步受到損害，巴西應在亞馬遜地區發展生態旅遊，讓旅遊業逐漸取代伐木業及農業。亞馬遜雨林是全球最大的雨林，面積達550萬平方公里，其中60%的面積位於巴西。亞馬遜雨林蘊藏着豐富的天然資源。受到非法砍伐的威脅，亞馬遜雨林的面積正不斷縮小。一些非法份子砍伐樹林以出售木材，或非法焚燒雨林以開墾土地作為牧場和耕地。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 根據資料一，解釋亞馬遜雨林中被開墾的耕地屬哪種生產要素。(2分)
parts.modelAnswer: 屬資本，因這些耕地是生產過程中所運用的人造資源。

visuals.text: 亞馬遜雨林面積達 550 萬平方公里，其中 60% 位於巴西，蘊藏豐富天然資源。非法砍伐樹木出售木材及非法焚燒雨林開墾牧場和耕地，令面積不斷縮小。

visuals.caption: 資料三：對保育亞馬遜雨林的一些看法
rows: 大型企業應該停止向巴西購買由破壞雨林所得的土地畜牧生產的肉類製品，以及停止使用來自亞馬遜地區的咖啡、紙張和木材。
我們決定停止從巴西進口皮革，除非生產商能確保在生產皮革的過程中不會危害雨林。
政府應該訂立更嚴格的法規，以及加強執法。阻止農民非法砍伐及焚燒樹林。
為避免雨林進一步受到損害，巴西應在亞馬遜地區發展生態旅遊，讓旅遊業逐漸取代伐木業及農業。

questions.stem: 有「地球之肺」之稱的亞馬遜雨林是全球最大的雨林。2019年8月，亞馬遜雨林發生了一場大火。資料一：亞馬遜雨林的簡介(資料來源：綜合報導)資料二：亞馬遜雨林大火的新聞報導亞馬遜雨林的大火引起國際關注。七大工業國集團(G7)同意提供2,000萬美元協助救災及善後工作。多個國際慈善機構亦於全球多個國家呼籲民眾捐助以保護亞馬遜雨林。大火的成因仍然眾說紛紜。有些人懷疑有農民以焚燒方式開墾土地，釀成山火。巴西總統已簽署禁令，暫時禁止農民以焚燒的方式清理農地。 (資料來源：綜合報導)資料三：對保育亞馬遜雨林的一些看法環保組織大型企業應該停止向巴西購買由破壞雨林所得的土地畜牧生產的肉類製品，以及停止使用來自亞馬遜地區的咖啡、紙張和木材。歐洲服飾零售商我們決定停止從巴西進口皮革，除非生產商能確保在生產皮革的過程中不會危害雨林。市民政府應該訂立更嚴格的法規，以及加強執法。阻止農民非法砍伐及焚燒樹林。商人為避免雨林進一步受到損害，巴西應在亞馬遜地區發展生態旅遊，讓旅遊業逐漸取代伐木業及農業。亞馬遜雨林是全球最大的雨林，面積達550萬平方公里，其中60%的面積位於巴西。亞馬遜雨林蘊藏着豐富的天然資源。受到非法砍伐的威脅，亞馬遜雨林的面積正不斷縮小。一些非法份子砍伐樹林以出售木材，或非法焚燒雨林以開墾土地作為牧場和耕地。

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: 根據資料一及二，解釋為甚麼禁令未必能成功減輕這缺乏效率的問題。(2分)
parts.modelAnswer: 政府嚴格執行禁令的成本高昂，可能無法阻止農民非法焚燒雨林。

questions.stem:
對本地學生而言，由大學教育資助委員會所資助的學士學位課程的學費自1997年起，就一直維持在每年$42,100。
解釋於香港接受高等教育的機會成本是否必然自1997年以來一直維持不變。(3分)

parts.label: Q1
parts.prompt:
對本地學生而言，由大學教育資助委員會所資助的學士學位課程的學費自1997年起，就一直維持在每年$42,100。
解釋於香港接受高等教育的機會成本是否必然自1997年以來一直維持不變。(3分)
parts.modelAnswer: 否。全成本包括學費及所花時間價值最高的其他用途；即使學費不變，放棄工作的收入也可能改變。

questions.stem: 香港每年有大約7萬公噸的廢電器電子產品被棄置。有見及此，政府於2018年推行生產者責任計劃以推動回收及妥善處理棄置的廢電器電子產品。資料一：回收的廢電器電子產品數量年份出口作循環再造(千公噸)在本地循環再造(千公噸)回收的循環再造物品總量(千公噸)2009年50.014.064.02010年51.010.061.02011年56.110.666.72012年49.8 6.256.02013年49.6 6.255.82014年52.6 2.955.52015年54.0 4.558.52016年51.0 4.455.4(資料來源：環境保護署)資料二：廢電器電子產品生產者責任計劃計劃適用於多種電器（包括電腦、打印機、掃描器、顯示器、空調、洗衣機、雪櫃及電視機）的銷售商。當消費者購買新的電器時，銷售商必須安排免費上門移走舊電器，送交指定的本地循環再造商處理，並直接向政府支付循環再造徵費（參閱下表）。計劃不適用於直接從外國購買自用的電器。循環再造徵費電腦、打印機或掃描器每件15元顯示器每件45元空調、洗衣機每件125元雪櫃、電視機每件165元(資料來源：環境保護署)資料三：不同人士的意見政府官員：目前大部分的廢電器電子產品都是出口作循環再造。我們不能依賴這種方式處理廢棄的電器，因為外地對二手產品的需求將會逐漸減少，而外國對廢電器電子產品的進口限制亦會愈趨嚴格。同時，未被回收的廢電器電子產品會被送到垃圾堆填區，而垃圾堆填區亦快將不勝負荷。環保人士：電器中含有有毒物質，例如用於雪櫃及空調的雪種可對臭氧層造成破壞並導致全球氣候變化。打印機的碳粉盒會刺激我們的呼吸系統並可能導致癌症。用不恰當的方式處理廢置的電器會對我們的健康和環境構成不良影響。消費者：銷售商或會透過調整價格將循環再造徵費轉嫁給消費者。同時，購買新電器安排移走舊電器亦存在困難，若新電器在舊電器移走前到達，消費者家中可能沒有空間擺放。

questions.stem: 香港每年有大約7萬公噸的廢電器電子產品被棄置。有見及此，政府於2018年推行生產者責任計劃以推動回收及妥善處理棄置的廢電器電子產品。資料一：回收的廢電器電子產品數量年份出口作循環再造(千公噸)在本地循環再造(千公噸)回收的循環再造物品總量(千公噸)2009年50.014.064.02010年51.010.061.02011年56.110.666.72012年49.8 6.256.02013年49.6 6.255.82014年52.6 2.955.52015年54.0 4.558.52016年51.0 4.455.4(資料來源：環境保護署)資料二：廢電器電子產品生產者責任計劃計劃適用於多種電器（包括電腦、打印機、掃描器、顯示器、空調、洗衣機、雪櫃及電視機）的銷售商。當消費者購買新的電器時，銷售商必須安排免費上門移走舊電器，送交指定的本地循環再造商處理，並直接向政府支付循環再造徵費（參閱下表）。計劃不適用於直接從外國購買自用的電器。循環再造徵費電腦、打印機或掃描器每件15元顯示器每件45元空調、洗衣機每件125元雪櫃、電視機每件165元(資料來源：環境保護署)資料三：不同人士的意見政府官員：目前大部分的廢電器電子產品都是出口作循環再造。我們不能依賴這種方式處理廢棄的電器，因為外地對二手產品的需求將會逐漸減少，而外國對廢電器電子產品的進口限制亦會愈趨嚴格。同時，未被回收的廢電器電子產品會被送到垃圾堆填區，而垃圾堆填區亦快將不勝負荷。環保人士：電器中含有有毒物質，例如用於雪櫃及空調的雪種可對臭氧層造成破壞並導致全球氣候變化。打印機的碳粉盒會刺激我們的呼吸系統並可能導致癌症。用不恰當的方式處理廢置的電器會對我們的健康和環境構成不良影響。消費者：銷售商或會透過調整價格將循環再造徵費轉嫁給消費者。同時，購買新電器安排移走舊電器亦存在困難，若新電器在舊電器移走前到達，消費者家中可能沒有空間擺放。

parts.label: (f)
parts.prompt:
考生須以短文形式回答(f)部。評分準則包括運用資料及經濟理論，內容切題，鋪排合乎邏輯，以及表達清晰。

parts.modelAnswer: 好處包括減少污染和界外成本、舒緩堆填區、增加回收業本地生產總值和提高電器平均質素。弊處包括消費者付更高價格、移走舊電器的行政費、出口減少和進口增加令經常帳變差，以及累退徵費擴闊收入差距。
markingPoints: 堆填區或 GDP 好處。

questions.stem: 香港於2015年2月27日開始實施法定侍產假。合資格的男性僱員有權就其配偶或伴侶每次分娩享有 3 天侍產假。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 假設不少北上工作的男性工人計劃回港找尋工作。假設香港的職位數量維持不變，解釋上述現象會如何影響香港的失業率。(4分)
parts.modelAnswer: 失業率 = 失業人口/勞動人口。兩者均等額增加，但失業人口百分比升幅較大，失業率上升。
markingPoints: 解釋失業人口百分比升幅較大。

questions.keyPoint: 匯率改變對進出口價格（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）、進出口數量及進出口價值（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）的影響
questions.stem: 在2014年，日圓兌港元的匯率下跌超過10%。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 解釋以上的匯率變動會如何影響到香港旅遊的日本旅客數目。 (3分)
parts.modelAnswer: 香港旅遊以日圓計較昂貴，到港日本人減少。

questions.topicGroup: 匯率改變對進口及出口的影響
questions.keyPoint: 匯率改變對進出口價格（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）、進出口數量及進出口價值（以本地貨幣及外幣計算）的影響
questions.stem: 在2014年，日圓兌港元的匯率下跌超過10%。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 毋須運用圖表，解釋在甚麼條件下，以上的匯率變動會導致香港從日本進口的貨品總值(以港元計算)上升。(3分)
parts.modelAnswer: 日本貨港元價格下降、需求量上升。若需求有彈性，數量升幅百分比大於價格跌幅，進口價值上升。
markingPoints: 解釋價格下降、數量上升。

questions.keyPoint: 可變成本及固定成本
questions.stem: 過去十年，網上購物成為一個潮流。資訊科技的發展令經營網上商店的成本下降。

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.prompt:
同一件貨品在網上商店的價格一般較實體商店為低。
試舉出兩個可能原因解釋這現象。(4分)
parts.modelAnswer: 例如營運成本較低（不需大量售貨員）、售後服務較少、網購需較長送貨時間。

questions.keyPoint: 了解輔助品、代替品、正常物品及劣等物品的含義
questions.stem: 過去十年，網上購物成為一個潮流。資訊科技的發展令經營網上商店的成本下降。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.prompt:
同一件貨品在網上商店的價格一般較實體商店為低。
解釋為甚麼這可能會導致店舖的租金下降。(3分)
parts.modelAnswer: 網店與實體店貨品有競爭性需求。較低價網購替代品令實體店貨品需求下降，對店舖的派生需求及租金下降。
markingPoints: 解釋實體店貨品需求下降。
連繫店舖派生需求和租金下降。

questions.keyPoint: 了解及計算最大及實際銀行乘數
questions.stem: 過去十年，網上購物成為一個潮流。資訊科技的發展令經營網上商店的成本下降。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 網上購物的流行同時帶動了電子貨幣的發展，人們更頻繁地使用電子貨幣。以圖輔助，解釋這現象會如何影響名義利率。(5分)
parts.modelAnswer: 交易性貨幣需求下降；貨幣供應不變，貨幣需求由 Md0 左移至 Md1，名義利率由 r0 降至 r1。

answerVisuals.alt: 電子貨幣使用增加後的貨幣市場
answerVisuals.caption: 官方答案圖

movements: 電子貨幣使用更頻密令交易性貨幣需求下降。
貨幣供應不變，貨幣需求由 Md0 左移至 Md1，名義利率由 r0 降至 r1。
diagramDetails.answerFocus: 官方圖確認名義利率下降。

questions.keyPoint: 需求改變的影響
questions.stem:
細閱以下的新聞節錄。
…… 食水含鉛風波蔓延全港，從不同的公共屋邨單位抽取的水樣本的抽驗結果顯示，部分食水中的鉛含量較一般為高。同時，部分學校的驗水結果亦顯示有水樣本含鉛量超標 ……

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 食水含鉛事件引起公眾對食水安全的關注，不少人都因而自行在家中安裝濾水器。試以圖輔助，說明濾水器生產商收入的變化。(4分)
parts.modelAnswer: 濾水器需求上升，D0 向右移至 D1；價格和交易量由 P0、Q0 升至 P1、Q1，生產者收益增加。
markingPoints: 圖示 D0 右移至 D1。

answerVisuals.alt: 濾水器需求增加後的生產者收益
answerVisuals.caption: 官方答案圖

movements: 食水含鉛關注令需求由 D0 向右移至 D1。
均衡價格和數量上升，生產者收益增加。
diagramDetails.answerFocus: 官方圖顯示需求增加後收益上升。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(I)
questions.keyPoint: 總社會盈餘達致最大：邊際利益等於邊際成本
questions.stem:
細閱以下的新聞節錄。
…… 食水含鉛風波蔓延全港，從不同的公共屋邨單位抽取的水樣本的抽驗結果顯示，部分食水中的鉛含量較一般為高。同時，部分學校的驗水結果亦顯示有水樣本含鉛量超標 ……

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 政府計劃津貼受影響的學校安裝濾水器。假設津貼是按從量的方式提供予濾水器生產商，以圖輔助，解釋提供該津貼是否有效率。(8分)
parts.modelAnswer: 沒有效率。津貼使供應右移、消費者價由 P0 降至 P1、製造商收取價升至 P2，產量由 Q0 增至 Q1；額外產量的 MC 大於 MB，產生淨損失。
markingPoints: 圖示消費者價低、製造商價高。
指出額外產量 MC 大於 MB。

answerVisuals.alt: 濾水器從量津貼及效率
answerVisuals.caption: 官方答案圖

movements: 從量津貼令供應由 S0 向右移至 S1。
消費者價下降、製造商收取價上升，產量增加至 MC 大於 MB 的 Q1。
diagramDetails.answerFocus: 官方圖確認過度生產和淨損失。

questions.chapterTitle: 效率、公平和政府的角色(II)
questions.keyPoint: 收入均等化
questions.stem:

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt:

(3分)
parts.modelAnswer: 公屋居民多屬低收入住戶；免費安裝提高其實質收入、縮窄與高收入住戶的差距，有助收入均等化。
markingPoints: 連繫收入差距或均等化。

questions.stem: 為冷卻過熱的經濟，政府建議對物品及服務開徵銷售稅。評價這個建議。(4分)

parts.label: Q8
parts.prompt: 為冷卻過熱的經濟，政府建議對物品及服務開徵銷售稅。評價這個建議。(4分)
parts.modelAnswer: 支持：銷售稅可降低產出、收窄通脹差距並增加稅收。反對：銷售稅屬累退，會擴大收入差距；若非暫時性，可能降低產出並導致失業。
markingPoints: 解釋宏觀經濟或稅收好處。

questions.keyPoint: 區分免費物品及經濟物品
questions.stem: 香港連鎖快餐店麥當勞於2013年3月18日早上六時至十一時期間，在二百三十家分店同時免費送出一千個煙肉蛋漢堡。不少人一早便在店外排隊，其中以長者最多。二十三萬個煙肉蛋漢堡不消兩小時便派光，遲來者唯有失望而回。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 那些免費送出的煙肉蛋漢堡是否免費物品？試加解釋。(2分)
parts.modelAnswer: 不是。數量不足以滿足所有人的慾望，人們想要更多，故是經濟物品。
markingPoints: 說明稀少或人們想要更多。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 香港連鎖快餐店麥當勞於2013年3月18日早上六時至十一時期間，在二百三十家分店同時免費送出一千個煙肉蛋漢堡。不少人一早便在店外排隊，其中以長者最多。二十三萬個煙肉蛋漢堡不消兩小時便派光，遲來者唯有失望而回。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 以機會成本的概念解釋為什麼排隊領取免費煙肉蛋漢堡的人主要是長者。(3分)
parts.modelAnswer: 長者在該時段一般不用上班，其時間最高價值的其他用途較其他人低，排隊的機會成本較低。
markingPoints: 說明長者一般不用上班。
指出時間的最高價值其他用途。
得出排隊機會成本較低。

questions.stem: 香港連鎖快餐店麥當勞於2013年3月18日早上六時至十一時期間，在二百三十家分店同時免費送出一千個煙肉蛋漢堡。不少人一早便在店外排隊，其中以長者最多。二十三萬個煙肉蛋漢堡不消兩小時便派光，遲來者唯有失望而回。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 假設麥當勞於一個月後把煙肉蛋漢堡的售價提高10%。以圖輔助，解釋在甚麼情況下麥當勞從售賣煙肉蛋漢堡所得的總收入會上升。(5分)
parts.modelAnswer: 價格上升令需求量減少。若需求低彈性，需求量減少百分率小於價格增加百分率，總收入減少面積小於增加面積，故總收入上升。
markingPoints: 說明價格上升時需求量下降。
比較數量和價格的百分比變化。
圖示價格、數量和收入面積。

questions.keyPoint: 人力資源：企業家職能
questions.stem:
位於天水圍天秀路的天秀墟於2013年2月8日正式開幕，它由東華三院營運及管理，提供二百多個廉租攤檔以售賣日常用品，目標是：
(1)創造區內就業機會
(2)協助弱勢社群自力更生
在成功申請攤檔的人士中，超過七成是經由社工推薦，包括低收入人士、領取綜援者、失業人士以及有就業困難者如新來港人士和少數族裔等。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 你認為天秀墟可以達到上述兩項目標嗎？試加解釋。(4分)
parts.modelAnswer: 可以。廉租攤檔讓區內人士以自僱形式營生；多數成功申請者是低收入、綜援、失業或有就業困難的弱勢社群，可藉經營攤檔自力更生。
markingPoints: 說明廉租攤檔創造自僱機會。
連繫經營攤檔和自力更生。

parts.modelAnswer: 貿易平衡錄得盈餘。因另外兩個經常帳項目為零，經常帳等於淨出口；經常帳盈餘表示淨出口為正，即貿易盈餘。

questions.keyPoint: 識別及計算選擇一個選項時涉及的成本（顯性成本及隱含成本）

parts.label: Q1
parts.prompt:
很多香港人都喜歡在假期外出旅遊。與非假期期間比較，假期期間的旅行團團費較高。因此，有些人
認為在非假期期間外遊的機會成本必定較低。你同意這說法嗎？試解釋。 (6 分)
parts.modelAnswer: 不同意。完全成本 = 顯性成本 + 隱性成本。非假期團費令顯性成本較低，但可能須放棄收入，時間成本較高，故完全成本高低不確定。

說明時間成本可較高，例如放棄收入。

有些人建議政府應向電子產品徵收從量銷售稅以替代回收處理費，稅款由生產者支付。假設電子產品的供應彈性較需求彈性高。試以一幅圖輔助，解釋買家還是賣家的稅項負擔較大。(6分)

試卷完 試卷完
parts.modelAnswer: 從量稅令供應由 S0 上移至 S1，兩曲線垂直距離為稅額。因供應較需求有彈性，買家承擔較大稅項負擔，即使由賣家繳交。
markingPoints: 圖示 S0 上移至 S1。
標示價格、數量及兩方稅負。
指出垂直差距為從量稅。

questions.keyPoint: 免費物品及經濟物品的定義

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 是否所有免費物品都必定是免費的？試解釋。 (3 分)
parts.modelAnswer: 是。免費物品數量足以滿足所有慾望，沒有人競爭亦毋須出價，故免費。

questions.keyPoint: 免費物品及經濟物品的定義

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: 是否所有免費的物品都必定是免費物品？試解釋。 (3 分)
parts.modelAnswer: 否。免費樣本是經濟物品，生產涉及成本，人們也想要更多。
markingPoints: 舉免費樣本等經濟物品例子。
說明有生產成本及人們想要更多。

questions.topicGroup: 股票及債券作為資金來源
questions.keyPoint: 發行股票及債券籌集資金的優點和缺點
questions.stem:
2009 年，不少內地公司（如中國南車股份有限公司和霸王國際（集團）控股有限公司）選擇在香港股
票市場上市。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 試提出一個原因，解釋為甚麼這些公司選擇在股票市場上市，而不是發行債券籌集資金。 (2 分)
parts.modelAnswer: 發行普通股的公司即使獲利也不一定須派股息，可保留盈利作未來發展，較有彈性。

questions.keyPoint: 比較不同所有權形式的特徵及利弊

2009 年，不少內地公司（如中國南車股份有限公司和霸王國際（集團）控股有限公司）選擇在香港股
票市場上市。

parts.label: (b)

parts.modelAnswer: 上市股份可在股票市場自由買賣，敵對公司可買入足夠股份收購公司。

questions.keyPoint: 識別及計算選擇一個選項時涉及的成本（顯性成本及隱含成本）
questions.stem: 從觀察所得，酒店自助晚餐周末時的價格較高。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 試指出顧客到酒店享用自助晚餐的全成本。 (2 分)
parts.modelAnswer: 全成本是顯性成本和隱含成本之和，即自助晚餐市價加上花時間用餐所放棄的最高價值用途。
markingPoints: 應用至市價及時間最高價值替代用途。

questions.keyPoint: 識別及計算選擇一個選項時涉及的成本（顯性成本及隱含成本）
questions.stem: 從觀察所得，酒店自助晚餐周末時的價格較高。

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt:
顧客在周末擁有較多空閒時間。根據這事實，解釋為甚麼即使酒店自助晚餐的價格在周末較高，
部分顧客仍然願意在周末光顧。 (3 分)
parts.modelAnswer: 周末空閒時間多，時間成本較低。雖顯性成本較高，隱含成本較低，故全成本可能更低。
markingPoints: 空閒時間多令時間成本低。
指出顯性成本較高而隱含成本較低。

questions.keyPoint: 私用品及共用品

questions.keyPoint: 稀少性的意思

questions.keyPoint: 成本的定義
questions.stem: 王先生是一位醫生。他剛繼承了祖父母的一個舖位。他可以在該舖位開設診所，或將舖位出租以賺取每月$25,000的租金。他原本開設診所，並與另一名合夥人成立合夥。不過，他現在考慮會否作為一個專業攝影師，以賺取$15,000的月薪。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 王先生在舖位開設診所的機會成本是甚麼？(2分)
parts.modelAnswer: 機會成本是放棄的最高價值選項，即每月 $25,000 出租舖位。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 王先生是一位醫生。他剛繼承了祖父母的一個舖位。他可以在該舖位開設診所，或將舖位出租以賺取每月$25,000的租金。他原本開設診所，並與另一名合夥人成立合夥。不過，他現在考慮會否作為一個專業攝影師，以賺取$15,000的月薪。

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt:
以下的情況會令王先生在舖位開設診所的成本如何改變？
一間廣告公司希望以月薪$20,000聘請王先生為專業攝影師。(2分)
parts.modelAnswer: 不變，放棄的最高價值選項仍是每月 $25,000 出租舖位。
markingPoints: 說明最高價值放棄選項未變。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 王先生是一位醫生。他剛繼承了祖父母的一個舖位。他可以在該舖位開設診所，或將舖位出租以賺取每月$25,000的租金。他原本開設診所，並與另一名合夥人成立合夥。不過，他現在考慮會否作為一個專業攝影師，以賺取$15,000的月薪。

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt:
以下的情況會令王先生在舖位開設診所的成本如何改變？
有人願意以每月$ 33,000租用他的舖位。(2分)
parts.modelAnswer: 上升，因最高價值放棄選項的價值升至每月 $33,000。
markingPoints: 說明最高價值放棄選項價值上升。

questions.keyPoint: 解釋在不同情況下成本如何改變
questions.stem: 王先生是一位醫生。他剛繼承了祖父母的一個舖位。他可以在該舖位開設診所，或將舖位出租以賺取每月$25,000的租金。他原本開設診所，並與另一名合夥人成立合夥。不過，他現在考慮會否作為一個專業攝影師，以賺取$15,000的月薪。

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.prompt:
以下的情況會令王先生在舖位開設診所的成本如何改變？
王先生的母親不容許他將舖位出租。(2分)
parts.modelAnswer: 出租不再是可用選項；只有開診所一個選項，無選擇故無機會成本。
markingPoints: 說明無選擇故無機會成本。

questions.keyPoint: 比較不同所有權形式的特徵及利弊
questions.stem: 王先生是一位醫生。他剛繼承了祖父母的一個舖位。他可以在該舖位開設診所，或將舖位出租以賺取每月$25,000的租金。他原本開設診所，並與另一名合夥人成立合夥。不過，他現在考慮會否作為一個專業攝影師，以賺取$15,000的月薪。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: 王先生與合夥人計劃均分診所的利潤。這是否意味他們投放的資本必定相同？試解釋。(2分)
parts.modelAnswer: 否。協定利潤分享比例不必等於資本投入比例。
markingPoints: 說明利潤分配可與資本投入比例不同。

questions.keyPoint: 分工的種類
questions.stem: 甲餐廳位於乙餐廳旁，是一間新開張的中式餐館。甲餐廳內的每名員工都專門負責不同的工序。相反，乙餐廳的每名員工都要負責多種工作，包括洗碗、烹調、招待客人等等。

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: 寫出分工的定義。以上兩間餐廳有沒有實施分工？如有的話，它們實施的是哪類型的分工？(3分)
parts.modelAnswer: 分工是工人專門生產一件物品或一個生產階段。甲餐廳有分工，屬複雜分工；乙餐廳沒有。

questions.keyPoint: 分工的好處及壞處
questions.stem: 甲餐廳位於乙餐廳旁，是一間新開張的中式餐館。甲餐廳內的每名員工都專門負責不同的工序。相反，乙餐廳的每名員工都要負責多種工作，包括洗碗、烹調、招待客人等等。

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt:
乙餐廳的老闆詩雅發現，在上述安排下，甲餐廳員工的生產力遠高於乙餐廳員工的生產力。
為甚麼甲餐廳員工的生產力會較高？試解釋兩個可能原因。(4分)
parts.modelAnswer: 例如按任務安排最適合的人、熟能生巧、節省培訓和轉換工序時間、較易機械化或更經濟運用資本；任答兩項。

questions.keyPoint: 勞工生產力
questions.stem: 甲餐廳位於乙餐廳旁，是一間新開張的中式餐館。甲餐廳內的每名員工都專門負責不同的工序。相反，乙餐廳的每名員工都要負責多種工作，包括洗碗、烹調、招待客人等等。

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt:
乙餐廳的老闆詩雅發現，在上述安排下，甲餐廳員工的生產力遠高於乙餐廳員工的生產力。
詩雅後來在她的餐廳實施分工，但她發現員工的生產力反而下降了。試解釋另外兩個可提高員工生產力的方法。(4分)
parts.modelAnswer: 例如改善教育培訓、工作環境、待遇福利、生產者物品數量質量或勞工組織方法；任答兩項。

questions.keyPoint: 勞力的流動性
questions.stem: 甲餐廳位於乙餐廳旁，是一間新開張的中式餐館。甲餐廳內的每名員工都專門負責不同的工序。相反，乙餐廳的每名員工都要負責多種工作，包括洗碗、烹調、招待客人等等。

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt:
由於詩雅發現甲餐廳員工的效率較高，她計劃透過提供交通津貼和提高工資吸引他們為她工作。試解釋這會怎樣影響甲餐廳員工的職業流動性和地域流動性。(4分)

試卷完 試卷完
parts.modelAnswer: 職業流動性不變，因職業不變；地域流動性不變，因兩餐廳相鄰，工作地點沒轉到另一地區。
markingPoints: 指出職業流動性不變並解釋。
指出地域流動性不變並解釋。

questions.keyPoint: Relationship between scarcity, competition and discrimination
questions.stem: Which of the following is implied in a society where scarcity exists?

choices.text: Both A and B are correct.

questions.explanation: Scarcity forces choices. Each choice has an opportunity cost and scarce resources create competition; exchange is not implied.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of interest
questions.stem: Interest

choices.text: is the price paid for earlier consumption.
may exist in a society without exchange.
may exist in a one-man economy.

questions.explanation: Interest is the cost paid to obtain resources or consumption earlier rather than later. It can exist without money or exchange.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem: Scarcity

choices.text: exists for both economic goods and free goods.
exists as long as human wants are unlimited.
does not exist in a one-man economy.
is the source of all economic problems.

questions.explanation: Scarcity arises because resources are insufficient for all wants, creating the fundamental economic problems. Unlimited wants alone do not guarantee scarcity.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: May is choosing between buying a laptop computer and a desktop computer. Which of the following will change May's cost of buying a laptop?

choices.text: The battery of the laptop computer she wants goes out very quickly.
Many kinds of software cannot be installed in the laptop computer she wants.
Performance of the desktop computer May wants is not as good as the producer claims.
May's uncle is going to give a laptop computer to her as birthday gift.

questions.explanation: The cost of choosing the laptop is the value of the best forgone alternative. A less satisfactory desktop lowers that alternative's value and changes the laptop's opportunity cost.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem: Scarcity implies

choices.text: all goods must have a high market price.

questions.explanation: Scarcity means resources are insufficient relative to wants, so people compete and discriminate in allocation. It does not require specialisation or high prices for every good.

questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem: In cinema A, customers are given a coupon for each ticket bought. The coupons can be used to exchange the following gifts:

choices.text: 4 cans of coke, 1 film camera and 1 mobile phone

questions.explanation: With 20 coupons, Diane can exchange for four cans of Coke, one film camera, or two cinema tickets. The highest-valued forgone option is four cans of Coke; the mobile phone needs an extra $1 000.
questions.postVisualStem: Diane has 20 coupons. What is Diane's opportunity cost of using 20 coupons to exchange for two cinema tickets?

questions.keyPoint: Definition of free goods and economic goods
questions.stem:
Which of the following descriptions about goods are correct?

(1) No one wants any of a free good.
(2) Natural resources are free goods.
(3) Free-of-charge goods may be economic goods.
(4) A good may be regarded as a free good or an economic good in different circumstances.
questions.explanation: A free good can be wanted but plentiful relative to wants. A free-of-charge sample may be an economic good, and scarcity can differ by place or time.

questions.keyPoint: Distinguishing between free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: In economics, rainfall in the Sahara Desert is ____________ because ____________.

choices.text: an economic good ... only a small amount of water is found in the desert
a free good ... anyone can get it without paying a cost
an economic good ... people prefer more of it
a free good ... it has no alternative uses

questions.explanation: Rainfall is scarce in the Sahara and people would prefer more of it. It is therefore an economic good; payment and alternative uses are not the test.

questions.keyPoint: Relationship between scarcity and choice
questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding choice is correct?

choices.text: When scarcity does not exist, people still need to make choices.
When there is only one option, people may still need to decide whether to choose it or not.
With more than one choice, an individual's cost of choosing an option is the sum of values of the remaining options.
When resources and human wants are both limited, people may still need to choose.

questions.explanation: Even with limited wants and resources, choices are needed whenever available resources cannot satisfy all relevant wants. The cost of a choice is the highest-valued, not the sum of all, alternatives forgone.

questions.keyPoint: Definition of cost
questions.stem: Which of the following is a cost of building a theme park in Hong Kong?

choices.text: the entrance fee of the park
the expenses involved in recruiting the staff

questions.explanation: Noise pollution is a real cost imposed during construction. The entrance fee is revenue, while maintenance and recruitment occur after the building decision.

questions.keyPoint: Use of the circular flow model to explain why GDP can be measured by three different approaches
questions.stem: Below is the circular flow model of an economy.

choices.text: household's consumption expenditure ... factors of production
cost of production ... final goods and services
firm's revenue ... final goods and services

questions.explanation: The money flow from households to firms is consumption expenditure. The corresponding real flow from households to firms is factors of production.

visuals.alt: Circular flow diagram linking firms and households, with money and real flows X and Y.
visuals.caption: Circular flow model

movements: Flow X is the money flow of households' consumption expenditure to firms.
Flow Y is the real flow of factors of production from households to firms.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option A correctly identifies flow X as consumption expenditure and flow Y as factors of production.

questions.postVisualStem: Flow X refers to the flow of ____________ while Flow Y is the flow of ____________.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Exchange is a condition for specialisation
questions.stem: If exchange is absent, with specialisation of production,

choices.text: all people in the economy enjoy a higher living standard.
people do not need to produce everything they need.
people can produce goods at a lower opportunity cost.

questions.explanation: Specialisation lets people focus on activities with lower opportunity cost. Without exchange they cannot obtain all other goods through trade, so the other conclusions do not follow.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem: A normative statement
questions.explanation: A normative statement contains a value judgement and cannot be proved or refuted purely by factual evidence.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: The government of Country X is planning to strengthen national defense by producing more tanks. What basic economic problem(s) is/are related?
questions.explanation: Choosing to produce more tanks is a decision about the type and quantity of output, so it concerns what to produce.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem: When compared with a market economy, a command economy

choices.text: has more resources owned by the government.
has more productive activities guided by price signals.
has a more even income distribution.

questions.explanation: A command economy relies more on public ownership and central planning. The other statements are not necessary features.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem:
Which of the following goods in Hong Kong are mainly guided by price signals in their resource allocation?

(1) rice
(2) water supply
(3) petroleum
(4) electricity supply
questions.explanation: Rice and petroleum are mainly allocated through market prices. Water and electricity supply have substantial government or regulated provision.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem:
Which of the following largely determine the allocation of goods and services in a planned economy?

(1) consumers' demand
(2) government planning
(3) consumers' purchasing power
questions.explanation: In a planned economy, central government planning rather than consumer purchasing power or market demand largely determines allocation.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meaning of private property rights and its importance in a market economy
questions.stem: Which of the following regarding private property rights is correct?

choices.text: Private property rights are totally absent in a planned economy.
If private property rights are not well-protected, people may not engage in exchange.
If one possesses the right to transfer a good, he or she must also possess the exclusive rights to use and to derive income from the good.
With well-defined private property rights, there will be no competition for goods and services.

questions.explanation: Secure property rights encourage exchange because people can rely on ownership and transfer. Planned economies may still have some private rights, and property rights do not remove scarcity or competition.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: When a firm becomes unlisted,

choices.text: it is not a legal entity anymore.
its number of shareholders must be reduced if the existing number of shareholders exceeds 200.

questions.explanation: An unlisted company can remain a legal entity and issue shares privately. A private limited company is limited to 200 members, so an unlisted firm exceeding that limit must reduce its shareholders.

questions.keyPoint: Classification of private firms: sole proprietorship, partnership, private limited company and public limited company
questions.stem: Tony is one of the partners of an accounting firm in Hong Kong. Which of the following is correct?

choices.text: Tony's liability is not confined to his investment in the firm.
He needs to share profits with his partners equally.
The accounting firm may be a private limited company.

questions.explanation: Partners generally have unlimited liability. Their profit-sharing ratio is agreed by the partners, and a partnership is not a separate legal entity that a partner can sue.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: A ____________ has the fewest ways to raise capital.
questions.explanation: A sole proprietor relies mainly on personal funds, borrowing and retained profit, while companies can raise capital through additional shareholders and securities.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
If a firm is a ____________, it is possible for its owners to sue the company.

(1) sole proprietorship
(2) partnership
(3) private limited company
(4) public limited company
questions.explanation: Private and public limited companies are separate legal entities, so their owners may sue the company. A sole proprietorship and partnership are not separate from their owners in this way.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Tina, a small investor, prefers to buy shares of public limited companies rather than shares of private limited companies. This may be because

choices.text: she wants to transfer her ownership more easily.
she wants to have a higher rate of return.
she wants to enjoy limited liability.
she wants to have the right to sue the company.

questions.explanation: Shares in public listed companies are generally more transferable through the stock exchange. Limited liability and the right to sue are available to owners of both forms of company.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of issuing shares and bonds to raise capital
questions.stem: Which of the following ways of raising capital will reduce the flexibility of a firm in retaining profits for future development?
questions.explanation: Ordinary shareholders may expect dividends from profits, reducing a firm's flexibility to retain them. Bonds and bank loans require contractual interest payments rather than profit distribution.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible motive for a firm to change from a sole proprietorship to a private limited company?

choices.text: The owners can raise funds by inviting new shareholders to join the firm.
Financial information of the company can be kept secret.
Shares of the company can be traded in the stock market.
The profits tax rate will be lower.

questions.explanation: A private limited company can admit new shareholders to raise capital. Its shares are not publicly traded, and changing form does not necessarily lower the tax rate.

questions.keyPoint: Classification of private firms: sole proprietorship, partnership, private limited company and public limited company
questions.stem: Refer to the table below.

choices.text: public limited company ... private limited company
There is not enough information to tell.

questions.explanation: Limited liability and the number of owners alone do not identify a form of firm. Firm A could be a one-person private company and Firm B could be either a private or public limited company.
questions.postVisualStem: Firm A is a _____________ while firm B is a ____________.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning and examples of the three types of production; identify the type of production
questions.stem: Production

choices.text: refers to the processes of turning natural resources into output.
helps solve the problem of scarcity.

questions.explanation: Production creates utility and can include unpaid services, so it need not generate a monetary return. It may use non-natural inputs and cannot eliminate scarcity.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem:
Which of the following regarding producer goods and consumer goods is/are correct?

(1) A good may be a producer good or a consumer good, depending on how it is used.
(2) Consumer goods directly satisfy human wants while producer goods do not directly satisfy human wants.
(3) Both consumer goods and producer goods must be private goods.
questions.explanation: A good's classification depends on its use. Consumer goods directly satisfy wants, whereas producer goods are inputs; either kind may be public or private.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Private goods

choices.text: must have a high market value.
are goods used to produce other goods and services.
may be consumed by many individuals at the same time.
have a positive cost of serving it to an additional consumer after they have been produced.

questions.explanation: Private goods are rival and excludable. Serving one more consumer has a positive marginal cost or reduces availability to others, unlike a non-rival public good.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning and examples of the three types of production; identify the type of production
questions.stem: The table below shows the employment distribution of three countries in a certain year.

choices.text: in terms of employment, the tertiary sector is the largest sector in Country B and Country C.
the number of people engaged in the tertiary sector in Country B is the largest.
Country A is less developed than Country B and Country C.
in Country A, the secondary sector contributed most to gross domestic product (GDP).

questions.explanation: The tertiary sector has the largest employment share in B and C. Percentages alone cannot compare worker numbers, development levels, or GDP contributions.
questions.postVisualStem: From the above table, we can conclude that

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem:
Which of the following are the advantages of practising division of labour?

(1) Labour productivity can be raised.
(2) Occupational mobility of labour can be raised.
(3) Capital can be utilised more intensively.
(4) Machines can be used to replace workers.
questions.explanation: Division of labour raises productivity and enables more intensive use of specialised capital. It may lower occupational mobility, while mechanisation does not necessarily replace workers.

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem: With division of labour,

choices.text: only workers with the highest productivity are employed.
training time of workers can be shortened.
time in moving around tasks increases.

questions.explanation: Specialisation shortens training because each worker learns a narrower task. It saves, rather than increases, time moving between tasks; quality need not always improve.

questions.keyPoint: Natural resources: land
questions.stem: Which of the following is classified as 'land'?
questions.explanation: Land consists of natural resources. Trees in a rainforest are naturally occurring; fertilised soil and cloud-seeded rainfall incorporate human effort, while abandoned farmland has been modified by production.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital
questions.stem: In economics, a house is classified as __________ and return from renting it out is classified as __________.
questions.explanation: A house is a man-made resource used to provide housing services, so it is capital. The return to capital is interest.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital
questions.stem: Which of the following is a difference between capital and land?

choices.text: Capital requires human effort in production while land does not.
Capital may increase while the quantity of land is fixed.
The use of capital involves costs while the use of land does not cost anything.
Capital is occupationally mobile while land is not.

questions.explanation: Capital is man-made and requires human effort to produce, whereas land is a natural resource. The other descriptions are not generally valid distinctions.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following events will not lead to a change in the labour supply of Hong Kong?

choices.text: an increase in the number of public holidays
many people plan to retire later due to the financial turmoil
an increase in the number of people immigrating to Hong Kong
a fall in the unemployment rate

questions.explanation: A fall in unemployment changes the quantity of labour employed, not the labour supply. The other events change willingness, availability or the number of workers.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: Refer to the table.
questions.explanation: With equal output per worker-hour, X x 10 is proportional to 36 000 and Y x 12 to 54 000. Hence X:Y = (36 000/10):(54 000/12) = 4:5.
questions.postVisualStem: If the productivities of workers in both firms are the same, the ratio of X to Y would be

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: Suppose tour guides of a travel agency are paid by a percentage of the company's profit instead of the traditional 'basic salary plus commission' scheme. Which of the following is a result?

choices.text: an increase in income received by the tour guides
an increase in the cost of supervising the tour guides
an improvement in the quality of service provided by the tour guides
an increase in the business risk borne by the travel agency owner

questions.explanation: Linking pay to company profit gives guides an incentive to improve service and help the firm's overall performance. Their income and risk are not certain to move in the directions stated.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Geographical mobility of labour in Hong Kong increases if

choices.text: the government launches a large-scale retraining programme.
the MTRC lowers the fares of all routes.
immigrating to Hong Kong becomes more difficult due to the tightening of immigration policies.
some firms provide a housing allowance for staff living in distant districts.

questions.explanation: Lower transport fares reduce the cost of travelling between home and workplaces, increasing geographical mobility. Retraining affects occupational mobility.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following occupations has the lowest geographical mobility?

choices.text: There is not enough information to tell.

questions.explanation: Geographical mobility depends on circumstances such as transport, housing and job availability, not merely an occupation label. There is not enough information to rank these occupations.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem: The existence of scarcity implies that

choices.text: both rich and poor people cannot satisfy all their wants.
resources in the world are limited.
people have to use price competition to allocate resources.
people are not in a barter economy.

questions.explanation: Scarcity means available resources are insufficient to satisfy all wants, regardless of a person's income. It does not require price competition or a non-barter economy.

questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem:
Miss Lee is a bank manager. Recently she took a two-week unpaid leave and spent her holiday in Australia with her family. Which of the following should be included in her cost of taking the trip?

(1) the expense for a round-trip air ticket from Hong Kong to Australia
(2) the wage forgone during the two weeks
(3) Miss Lee's medical expenses during her trip
questions.explanation: Airfare and medical expenses are explicit costs, while unpaid leave is an implicit cost. All three are included in the trip's full cost.

questions.keyPoint: Definition of cost
questions.stem: The Hong Kong government has approved the construction of the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link. Which of the following would NOT affect the cost of constructing the railway to Hong Kong?

choices.text: The affected residents in the New Territories demand from the government a greater amount of compensation.
The construction damages the natural environment along the railway.
There is an increase in the wages of construction workers.
The fee for the railway will be expensive, so few people will choose it.

questions.explanation: Compensation, environmental damage and construction wages are costs of construction. A future ticket fee affects demand for rail travel, not the cost of building the railway.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of interest
questions.stem: The fact that people pay interest to get goods earlier implies that

choices.text: the costs of earlier availability of goods and deferring consumption of goods are the same.
people with lower degrees of positive time preference tend to be borrowers.
some people are willing to defer their consumption in return for a compensation.

questions.explanation: Lenders defer consumption only when compensated by interest. Borrowers tend to have a higher, not lower, positive time preference.

questions.keyPoint: Distinguishing between free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: Which of the following comes closest to a free good in economics?

choices.text: the movies available on the Internet for free
sea water in the Pacific Ocean

questions.explanation: Sea water in the Pacific is plentiful relative to wants and is closest to a free good. Free-of-charge services can still use scarce resources.

questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem: The following are the goods that Simon wants to buy.

choices.text: a pair of sport shoes and a calculator

questions.explanation: The watch costs all $500. The highest-valued feasible alternative forgone is the pair of sport shoes; the calculator would leave $300 unused and is a lower-ranked alternative.
questions.postVisualStem: If Simon has $500 pocket money only, which of the following is the opportunity cost of buying a watch?

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem: Hong Kong is a mixed economy. For example, in Hong Kong, the rents for public housing are determined by ___________ while the charges for internet services are determined by ___________.
questions.explanation: Public housing rents are set by the government, while internet-service charges are mainly determined by market forces.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meaning of private property rights and its importance in a market economy
questions.stem: Janet is the president of the Computer Club at a school. Every day, she stays in the computer room to finish her homework and helps maintain order in the room. Which of the following goods is most likely a private property for her?

choices.text: the game console left by a student in the computer room
the computer she uses in the computer room
the pen she buys and uses to finish her homework
the notebook she uses to record students' names

questions.explanation: The pen Janet bought and uses is most clearly under her exclusive ownership. The other items are owned by the school, club or another student.

questions.keyPoint: Classification of private firms: sole proprietorship, partnership, private limited company and public limited company

choices.text: Both Firm A and Firm B are not listed companies.
Firm B can issue bonds to raise capital but Firm A cannot.
Firm A has to pay a higher profits tax rate than Firm B.
Both firms have to be dissolved if one of their owners goes bankrupt.

questions.explanation: Firm A is a limited company and Firm B is a partnership. A limited company faces the higher profits-tax rate, and a partnership may dissolve when a partner becomes bankrupt.

visuals.caption: Firm comparison
rows: needs the consent of other owners

questions.postVisualStem: According to the above information, which of the following is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
Compared to a limited company, a sole proprietorship enjoys

(1) a simpler set-up procedure.
(2) a higher degree of autonomy.
(3) a wider source of capital.
(4) a lower profits tax rate
questions.explanation: A sole proprietor has a simple setup and autonomy and normally faces the lower unincorporated profits-tax rate. Its capital sources are narrower, not wider.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Which of the following descriptions about public goods is INCORRECT?

choices.text: Public goods may not be provided to users free of charge.
Goods that are not equally available to all users at the same time can also be public goods.
The cost of charging users for public goods may be very high.
The more users served by public goods, the higher the cost of serving extra customers.

questions.explanation: Public goods are non-rival, so serving an extra user has zero or negligible marginal cost. Charging may still occur and exclusion can be costly.

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem: Margaret, Elaine and Oscar own a coffee shop together. In the coffee shop, they are responsible for different duties according to their abilities: Margaret serves the customers; Elaine is responsible for making the drinks; Oscar cooks the dishes. Which of the following descriptions is CORRECT?

choices.text: The coffee shop adopts a simple division of labour.
The coffee shop produces consumer goods and producer goods.

questions.explanation: Specialising tasks according to ability is complex division of labour and raises productivity. Cooking is secondary production and the shop's output is consumer goods.

questions.keyPoint: Natural resources: land
questions.stem: Trees in the tropical rainforest in Malaysia belong to __________, while trees in Hong Kong Park belong to __________.
questions.explanation: Naturally growing rainforest trees are land. Trees planted and maintained in Hong Kong Park embody human effort and are capital.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following government policies CANNOT raise the mobility of labour?

choices.text: providing fare subsidies to the residents living in remote areas
injecting capital into the Continuing Education Fund to encourage people to learn new techniques

questions.explanation: Fare subsidies and railways raise geographical mobility, while training raises occupational mobility. A minimum wage law does not directly raise either form.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The input-output relationship of a firm is as below.
questions.explanation: Total output is 6, 20, 39, 60 and 80. Marginal product rises to 21 for the fourth machine and falls to 20 for the fifth, so diminishing marginal returns set in after the fourth machine.
questions.postVisualStem: Diminishing marginal returns set in after the ____ unit of machines is employed.

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: Large enterprises can usually obtain loans from banks at lower interest rates than small firms. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Large firms can obtain cheaper finance because of their own large scale, which is an internal economy of scale.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The following table shows the cost schedule of a competitive firm.
questions.explanation: At the profit-maximising output, price equals marginal cost. The fourth unit raises total cost from $50 to $80, giving marginal cost of $30.
questions.postVisualStem: If its profit-maximising output is 4 units, what will be the market price?

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem: The largest cosmetics retail chain in a city acquires the second largest cosmetics retail chain. Which of the following is the MOST possible objective for the former's action?
questions.explanation: Acquiring a major rival in the same retail market is a lateral integration intended to expand market share.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning and give examples of each type of integration
questions.stem: A construction company merges with a cement factory. This is an example of
questions.explanation: A cement factory supplies an input to a construction company. Merging with it is external backward integration.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem:
In order to spread risk, a magazine publisher can consider

(1) acquiring a toy factory.
(2) merging with a textbook publisher.
(3) acquiring another magazine publisher.
questions.explanation: Conglomerate expansion into toys and diversification into textbooks spread risk. Acquiring another magazine publisher concentrates risk in the same market.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem:
Company A is a shoe manufacturer. There is always unsold stock in its warehouse. Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?

(1) The prevailing price of shoes is below the market clearing level.
(2) There is a downward pressure on the price of shoes.
(3) The quantity of shoes transacted equals the quantity of shoes demanded.
questions.explanation: Unsold stock is excess supply: price is above equilibrium and falls under pressure. The quantity actually transacted equals quantity demanded.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: When an effective price ceiling is imposed on good X,

choices.text: the prevailing price is higher than the market clearing price.
an increase in the demand for good X will lead to an increase in quantity transacted.
there is a surplus of good X.
the quantity supplied is smaller than the quantity demanded.

questions.explanation: An effective ceiling lies below equilibrium, creating excess demand: quantity supplied is less than quantity demanded.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the wedding planning service market in Country X. E0 is the original equilibrium point.
questions.explanation: More marriages increase demand from D0 to D2, while entry increases supply from S0 to S2. Their intersection is E3.

visuals.alt: Wedding planning market with demand curves D0-D2, supply curves S0-S2 and equilibria E0-E4.

movements: Compare the indicated demand and supply curve shifts across the five equilibria.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Match the stated wedding-market change to the correct supply-demand option.

questions.postVisualStem: In recent years, the number of people getting married has been increasing. The promising prospects also attract new firms into the market. The new equilibrium point will be at __________.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: In recent years, the production cost of chemical fertilisers increases drastically. On the other hand, the use of chemical fertilisers is not as popular as before because of their negative effect on health. As a result, the price of chemical fertilisers _____________ and their quantity transacted _____________.

choices.text: increases ... may increase, decrease or remain unchanged
decreases ... may increase, decrease or remain unchanged
may increase, decrease or remain unchanged ... increases
may increase, decrease or remain unchanged ... decreases

questions.explanation: Higher production cost reduces supply and declining popularity reduces demand. Both shifts reduce quantity, while the price effect is indeterminate.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in demand
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in demand
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the market of instant camera film.

choices.text: The production cost of instant camera films increases.
The price of digital cameras increases.
The price of instant cameras increases.
The use of instant cameras becomes more popular again.

questions.explanation: Instant cameras and their film are complements. A higher instant-camera price lowers film demand, shifting D0 left to D1.

visuals.alt: Demand for instant camera film shifts left from D0 to D1.

movements: Demand for instant-camera film shifts left from D0 to D1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Identify the market result of the leftward demand shift.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following will lead to a change in the demand curve from D₀ to D₁?

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: There is a poor harvest of sugar cane in India. As a result, people begin to substitute glucose for sucrose. Which of the following diagrams would describe the above situation best?
questions.explanation: Glucose is a substitute for sucrose. A poor sugar-cane harvest makes sucrose scarcer and raises demand for glucose, shifting glucose demand right as in diagram D.

visuals.alt: Four supply and demand diagrams for sucrose and glucose markets.

movements: Compare the demand and supply movements in each of the four options.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Select the pair of market diagrams consistent with the relationship between sucrose and glucose.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem:
Due to an increase in the cost of production, the price of notebooks increases from $4 to $6 and the quantity transacted decreases by 33%. Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?

(1) There is an increase in the demand for notebooks.
(2) The demand for notebooks is inelastic.
(3) The total revenue decreases.
questions.explanation: The price rise is caused by a supply decrease, not demand. Price rises 50% while quantity falls 33%, so demand is inelastic and total revenue rises.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Because of water pollution, the catch of tuna decreases. As a result, the price and the quantity of tuna transacted change by 40% and 55%, respectively. We can conclude that

choices.text: the demand for tuna is inelastic.
the demand for tuna is elastic.
the supply of tuna is inelastic.
the supply of tuna is elastic.

questions.explanation: A supply decrease causes the movement along demand. Quantity changes proportionately more than price, so the demand for tuna is elastic.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem: Mr. Chan is a kitchen cabinet manufacturer. He can raise his total revenue by lowering the price of his kitchen cabinets if the demand for his kitchen cabinets is
questions.explanation: When demand is elastic, the percentage increase in quantity exceeds the percentage decrease in price, so cutting price raises total revenue.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: When the price of coffee increases, Samuel spends the same amount on it while Keith buys the same amount of coffee. Samuel's demand for coffee is __________ while Keith's demand for coffee is __________.
questions.explanation: Samuel's unchanged expenditure shows unitary elasticity. Keith's unchanged quantity shows perfectly inelastic demand.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the tax burden
questions.stem: Suppose the government imposes a per-unit sales tax on producers rather than consumers. Given that the demand is more elastic than the supply, which of the following is CORRECT?

choices.text: Consumers' tax burden will be smaller than producers' tax burden.
Consumers' tax burden will be larger than producers' tax burden.
The tax burden will be borne by consumers only.
The tax burden will be borne by producers only.

questions.explanation: Tax incidence depends on elasticities, not on whom the tax is legally imposed. The more elastic demand side bears the smaller burden.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: Which of the following about an effective quota and a price floor is INCORRECT?

choices.text: Both of them may lead to a fall in total revenue.
Both of them lead to market disequilibrium.
Both of them lead to higher market prices.
Both of them lead to a fall in the quantity transacted.

questions.explanation: An effective quota creates no excess demand or supply at the quota quantity; a price floor creates excess supply. Therefore they do not both necessarily lead to market disequilibrium.

questions.keyPoint: Identify the type of market structure
questions.stem: After acquiring California Karaoke Box, New York Karaoke Box becomes the only karaoke services provider in Country X. The market structure of karaoke services in Country X will change from ____________ to ____________.
questions.explanation: Two major providers form an oligopoly; after one acquires the other and becomes the only provider, the market becomes a monopoly.

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a monopolistically competitive market?

choices.text: Firms can enter or exit the market easily.
There are several dominant sellers and other sellers have a small market share only.
Neither sellers nor buyers have complete information about the market.
There are many buyers and sellers in the market.

questions.explanation: Several dominant sellers describe oligopoly. Monopolistic competition has many sellers, relatively easy entry and imperfect information.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Maximisation of total social surplus: marginal benefit equals marginal cost
questions.stem: Efficiency is achieved when

choices.text: consumer surplus is maximised while producer surplus is minimised.
total benefit is equal to total cost.
the difference between total benefit and total cost is maximised.

questions.explanation: Efficiency means total social surplus is maximised, which is the difference between total benefit and total cost.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: Frank and Ada are colleagues. Frank always chats with others loudly during office hours, and this is disturbing to Ada. Assume Ada has the right to work in a quiet environment. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: Frank will stop chatting with others during office hours.
There will be no divergence between private and social costs.
There will be no divergence between private and social costs only if Frank stops chatting with others during office hours.
There will be no divergence between private and social costs if Frank is required to pay a compensation to Ada according to the marginal external cost imposed by his chatting.

questions.explanation: A payment equal to marginal external cost internalises the external cost, making private and social cost coincide. The entitlement alone does not ensure that Frank stops chatting.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: The construction of the South Island Line (East) by the MTR Corporation will shorten travelling time in several districts. As a result, people need to pay more for buying private housing units in these districts. Which of the following is CORRECT?

choices.text: There is a divergence between private and social costs, and the government should provide subsidies to people who are going to buy private housing units in these districts to reduce the divergence.

There is a divergence between private and social benefits, and the government should provide subsidies to people who have already bought private housing units in these districts to reduce the divergence.
There may be no divergence between private and social costs.
There is no divergence between private and social costs unless the government provides subsidies to people who are going to buy private housing units in these districts.

questions.explanation: A higher market price for homes does not by itself show any divergence between private and social costs. The information is consistent with no divergence.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Lorenz curve
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the Lorenz curves of Country X and Country Y.
questions.explanation: Country Y's Lorenz curve lies closer to the line of equality, so its income distribution is more even and its Gini coefficient is lower. A Lorenz curve does not show average income.

visuals.alt: Lorenz curves for Country X and Country Y.

movements: Compare each Lorenz curve with the line of equality.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Identify the country with the more unequal income distribution.

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following is/are CORRECT?

(1) The Gini coefficient of Country Y is higher than that of Country X.
(2) The income distribution of Country Y is more even than that of Country X.
(3) The average income of households in Country Y is higher than that of Country X.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: The higher the Gini coefficient of a country,

choices.text: the lower the income of the low-income group of the country.
