questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.stem: An increase in the full-employment output level is caused by an increase in
questions.explanation: More infrastructure increases productive capacity and the full-employment output level. The other changes affect money demand, aggregate demand or saving preference.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Deflationary gap
questions.stem: Suppose an economy is initially operating at the long-run equilibrium. An increase in ______________would result in a deflationary gap.
questions.explanation: A higher profits tax rate reduces investment and aggregate demand. Starting from long-run equilibrium, the resulting fall in aggregate demand creates a deflationary gap.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: If Country X's productivity of every good is twice that of Country Y,

choices.text: the gain from trade of Country X will be greater than that of Country Y.
mutually beneficial trade between the two countries is still possible.
Country X will not import any good from Country Y.
Country X has a lower opportunity cost in producing every good than Country Y.

questions.explanation: If Country X's productivity is exactly twice Country Y's for every good, the two countries have the same opportunity costs. There is no comparative advantage to support mutually beneficial trade, so Country X will not import from Country Y.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.keyPoint: Meaning and role of foreign and official reserves in the balance of payments accounting
questions.stem: If a country records an increase in reserve assets in a certain fiscal year,

choices.text: its current account must be in surplus.
its capital and financial account must be in deficit.
it must be running a trade surplus.
the balance of payments is in surplus.

questions.explanation: An increase in official reserve assets records a balance-of-payments surplus in the accounting presentation; it does not by itself require a current-account or trade surplus.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of a quota on domestic price, domestic consumption, domestic production and import quantity for a small open economy
questions.stem: A country imposes an import quota on cement. The diagram below shows the country's supply of and demand for cement. P is the world price of cement.

choices.text: the increase in producer surplus is equal to the sum of areas a, b and d.
the decrease in consumer surplus is equal to the sum of areas a, b, c and d.
area c becomes a deadweight loss.
the effect on total social surplus is uncertain.

questions.explanation: The higher price reduces consumer surplus by areas a+b+c+d. Producer surplus rises by a, quota rent is b, and c+d are deadweight losses.

visuals.alt: Cement import-quota diagram with demand D, supply S, world price P, quota-raised price P', and areas a, b, c and d.

movements: The quota raises domestic price from P to P-prime and reduces imports.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Identify surplus, revenue and deadweight-loss areas under an import quota.

questions.postVisualStem: If the domestic price of cement increases from P to P' after the import quota is imposed,

choices.text: a decrease in the number of British visiting Hong Kong.
a decrease in the number of Hong Kong people visiting Britain.
an increase in the quantity of US garments exported to Hong Kong.
an increase in the quantity of British toys exported to Hong Kong.

questions.explanation: The GBP depreciates against the USD. Because HKD is linked to USD, the HKD appreciates against the GBP, making Britain cheaper for Hong Kong visitors and British goods cheaper in Hong Kong.

questions.stem: The following table shows the supply and demand schedules of good X.

choices.text: the market price of good X will be $66.
the market price of good X will increase by $8.
the quantity transacted of good X will be 500 units.
the quantity transacted of good X will increase by 300 units.

questions.explanation: With a quota of 200 units the price is $54. Raising it to 500 makes the quota ineffective because the market equilibrium is 400 units at $62. The price therefore rises by $8.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules of good X

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The following table shows the total cost schedule of a firm. The firm is a price-taker.
questions.explanation: Marginal cost is $60, $75, $90, $105 and $120. The firm produces three units at a price of $90. Producer surplus is $90 - $60 + $90 - $75 + $90 - $90 = $45; profit is revenue $270 minus total cost $255, or $15.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the market price of its product is $90. The total producer surplus and profit of the firm are ___________ and ___________ respectively.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which of the following behaviour is CONSISTENT with the law of demand?

choices.text: A removal of unemployment allowance decreases the employed population.
When the government increases the financial aid to the low-income group, Mrs. Chan, a recipient of the aid, works longer hours per day.
When the government reduces the amount of tax levied on red wine, Mr. Wong still spends $1,000 on buying red wine every month.
An increase in the salaries tax rate will lead to an increase in the general price level.

questions.explanation: A lower tax reduces the money price of red wine. If expenditure stays at $1,000, the quantity bought must increase, which is consistent with the law of demand.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on producer surplus
questions.stem: The following shows the supply-demand diagram of good X in a perfectly competitive market.

choices.text: The marginal benefit of consuming the last unit increases.

questions.explanation: The rightward supply shift lowers marginal cost and expands output. It raises producer surplus and consumer surplus, increases total social surplus, and lowers the marginal benefit of the last unit consumed.

visuals.alt: Supply curve shifts right from S0 to S1 against a downward-sloping demand curve.
visuals.caption: Increase in supply

movements: Supply shifts right from S0 to S1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Identify the price and quantity effect of increased supply.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: The following shows the supply-demand diagram of good X in a perfectly competitive market.

choices.text: the consumer surplus is equal to area ABEPe.
the deadweight loss is equal to area ECF.
the producer surplus is equal to area PeC0.
the total social surplus is equal to area ABF0.

questions.explanation: At the quota quantity Qq, total social surplus is total benefit (area ABQq0) less total cost (area 0FQq), which is area ABF0. The other areas do not state the corresponding surplus or deadweight loss correctly.

visuals.alt: Supply-demand diagram with quota quantity Qq, price Pq and labelled areas A to F.
visuals.caption: Quota and surplus

movements: The quota limits imports and raises the domestic price to Pq.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Identify consumer surplus, producer surplus, quota rent and deadweight-loss areas.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: The supply schedule of a competitive firm
questions.stem:
For a firm in a perfectly competitive market,

(1) it is a price taker.
(2) its marginal cost schedule is identical to its supply schedule.
(3) its marginal revenue is equal to the market price.
questions.explanation: A perfectly competitive firm takes the market price as given, so marginal revenue equals price. Its marginal-cost schedule represents the quantity it supplies at each price.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Maximisation of total social surplus: marginal benefit equals marginal cost
questions.stem:
Under which of the following situations is economic efficiency attained?

(1) Marginal private benefits are equal to marginal private costs.
(2) The benefits of both producers and consumers are maximised.
(3) Deadweight loss does not exist.
questions.explanation: Economic efficiency means total social surplus, including the gains to producers and consumers, is maximised and there is no deadweight loss. Equality of marginal private benefit and marginal private cost alone does not ensure this when external effects exist.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: The following table shows the Gini coefficient of economy A in recent years.
questions.explanation: The falling Gini coefficient shows a more even income distribution. It does not show the absolute nominal-income gap or whether the economy is in recession.
questions.postVisualStem:
Based on the above information, which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?

(1) The income distribution becomes more even.
(2) The difference in nominal income between high-income households and low-income households decreases.
(3) Economy A is in recession.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: If the government raises the effective minimum wage for foreign domestic helpers, which of the following is the most likely effect?

choices.text: There will be no non-price competition.
The demand for local domestic helpers will decrease.
Income distribution will become more uneven.
The change in total wage earnings of foreign domestic helpers will be uncertain.

questions.explanation: An effective minimum wage raises the wage but reduces employment. Total wage earnings can rise or fall depending on the elasticity of demand for foreign domestic helpers.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: The following table shows the statistical data of an economy.
questions.explanation: GDP at market prices is 2,200 + 1,500 + 750 + 250 + 500 = $5,200 million. GDP at factor cost is $5,200 - $150 indirect tax + $100 subsidies = $5,150 million.
questions.postVisualStem: The GDP at factor cost is $___________ million.

questions.keyPoint: Relationship between scarcity and choice
questions.stem:
The existence of scarcity implies that

(1) discrimination always exists.
(2) all goods must have a nominal price.
(3) people have to make choice.
questions.explanation: Scarcity makes choice necessary and can lead to competition or discrimination, but neither discrimination nor a nominal price must always exist.

questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem: Mr. Ho spent $1,000 on buying a limited edition model car. He is considering keeping the model car or selling it to his friend for $1,500. How much is Mr. Ho's cost of keeping the model car?
questions.explanation: The $1,000 purchase is sunk. Keeping the car means giving up the $1,500 that he could receive by selling it.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of interest
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about interest is/are CORRECT?

(1) Interest is the premium for obtaining goods or resources earlier.
(2) Interest must take the form of money.
(3) Interest rate and present consumption are positively related.
questions.explanation: Interest is the premium for earlier availability of resources. It need not be money, and a higher interest rate tends to encourage saving rather than present consumption.

questions.keyPoint: Describe the inter-relationship between the three types of production
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the relationship between the three types of production is CORRECT?

choices.text: Primary production provides raw materials only for secondary production.
Secondary production provides only finished goods for other types of production.
Tertiary production provides different kinds of services for other types of production.
The three types of production can be independent or interdependent, which varies among different countries.

questions.explanation: Tertiary production supplies services used by other sectors. Primary and secondary production can also supply inputs to more than one type of production, while the three sectors are normally interdependent.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The following table shows the weekly production of a firm. Two inputs are used in the production process, namely machines and labour.
questions.explanation: With machines fixed, the marginal products of extra workers must fall. The last increase must be below 15 units, so total product with eight workers must be below 145.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose diminishing marginal returns exists in the firm. X

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: A boss is going to hire a secretary. He is considering between paying the secretary a monthly salary and a floating salary which varies according to the number of tasks he/she completed. Which of the following is NOT a possible result for the boss choosing to pay the secretary a monthly salary?

choices.text: The cost of monitoring the secretary's output quality tends to be lower.
The secretary tends to have higher working incentive.
The cost of measuring the secretary's output tends to be lower.
The secretary tends to have more stable income.

questions.explanation: A floating, output-related salary generally gives a stronger incentive to work. A monthly salary can avoid measuring each task, support stable income, and place greater emphasis on quality monitoring.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Suppose an owner turned his firm from a partnership into a public limited company. Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

choices.text: The risk of the firm being taken over will be lower.
The firm has to disclose its financial statements to the public.
The firm's shares can be freely transferred.
The firm will have a wider source of capital.

questions.explanation: A public limited company must disclose information, can transfer shares freely and has wider access to capital. Its transferable shares make a takeover more, not less, possible.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: If the government increases the per-unit tax imposed on plastic bags from $0.5 to $1,

choices.text: consumers' tax burden will be larger than retailers' tax burden.
retailers' total revenue net of tax may increase.
consumers' total expenditure on plastic bags may remain unchanged.

questions.explanation: A higher unit tax raises the price paid by consumers and lowers quantity. Total consumer expenditure can stay unchanged when the price rise and quantity fall offset each other. The tax shares and revenue cannot be determined without elasticities.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: Suppose more people are attracted by advertisements to use smartphones and this leads to a drop in the number of fixed line telephone users. As a result, there are a 20% decrease in the price of fixed line telephone and a 40% change in the quantity transacted respectively. We can conclude that

choices.text: the demand for fixed line telephones is elastic.
the demand for fixed line telephones is inelastic.
the supply of fixed line telephones is elastic.
the supply of fixed line telephones is inelastic.

questions.explanation: The switch to smartphones decreases demand for fixed-line telephones. Along the supply curve, quantity falls by 40% while price falls by 20%, so price elasticity of supply is 2 and supply is elastic.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: Refer to the diagram below. E0 is the initial equilibrium of the market of health care products in Hong Kong.
questions.explanation: More products increase supply, shifting supply right. Safety concerns decrease demand, shifting demand left. The new equilibrium is Ed, where S1 and D1 meet.

visuals.alt: Supply and demand curves S0-S2 and D0-D2 with equilibrium points Ea, Eb, Ec, Ed and E0.
visuals.caption: Health care products market

movements: Compare the demand and supply shifts around the labelled equilibria.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Select the health-care market result consistent with the stated change.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose more health care products have been introduced in the market in recent years. At the same time, people are in doubt of buying these products as some of the products are found to contain ingredients which may have side effects on health. The new equilibrium point in the diagram will be ___________.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: If the gross national product of an economy is smaller than its gross domestic product, it implies that

choices.text: the factor income earned by residents outside the economy territory is smaller than the factor income earned by non-residents within the economy territory.
capital inflow is greater than capital outflow.
GDP at market prices is larger than GDP at factor cost.

questions.explanation: GNP equals GDP plus net income from abroad. GNP below GDP means net income from abroad is negative, so residents earn less abroad than non-residents earn within the economy.

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of nominal GDP and real GDP
questions.stem: In a certain period, the general price level of an economy rises, while its nominal GDP decreases. We can conclude that the inflation rate ___________, and the GDP at constant market prices ___________.
questions.explanation: A rising general price level means the inflation rate is positive. Since nominal GDP falls despite higher prices, real GDP at constant market prices must fall.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: The following diagram shows a change in aggregate demand of an economy.

choices.text: a decrease in people's desire to save

questions.explanation: The diagram shows a rightward shift of aggregate demand. A higher price level causes a movement along an AD curve, not a shift. The other changes can raise aggregate demand.

visuals.alt: Aggregate demand curve shifts right from AD0 to AD1.
visuals.caption: Increase in aggregate demand

movements: Aggregate demand shifts right from AD0 to AD1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Identify the resulting short-run output and price-level change.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following will NOT cause the above movement of the aggregate demand curve?

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: An abnormally dry climate largely reduced harvest of crops globally. In the short run, the price level of a crop-importing country will ___________ and its real GDP will ___________.
questions.explanation: Lower global crop harvest raises imported input and food prices, shifting short-run aggregate supply left. In the short run, price level rises and real GDP falls.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: Which of the following will lead to a shift of the money demand curve to the right?

choices.text: The nominal income of households decreases.
The government sells government bonds to the public.

questions.explanation: A higher price level raises the transaction demand for money and shifts money demand right. A change in the nominal interest rate causes movement along the demand curve.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money demand and money supply curves of an economy. Point E is the original equilibrium.
questions.explanation: Lower real output decreases transaction demand for money, shifting demand from Md0 to Md2. A lower discount rate increases money supply, shifting it from MS0 to MS1. Their new intersection is X.

visuals.alt: Money-demand curves Md0 to Md2 and vertical money-supply curves MS2 to MS1 with labelled points W, X, Y and Z.
visuals.caption: Money market equilibrium

movements: Compare money-demand shifts against the vertical money-supply curves.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Identify the interest-rate effect of the stated money-market change.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the real output of the economy decreases and the central bank lowers the discount rate. The new equilibrium point will be at ___________.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The table below shows the balance sheet of a banking system.
questions.explanation: Required reserves are $250 - $50 = $200, so the required reserve ratio is 20%. The initial $50 excess reserve can support $250 more deposits and the new $100 deposit can support $500 more. Maximum deposits are therefore $1,000 + $250 + $500 = $1,750.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.postVisualStem: The amount of excess reserves in the banking system is $50. A customer deposits $100 into his bank account. If the banking system is fully loaned up, the maximum amount of deposits in the banking system is ___________.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem:
Miss Chow withdraws HK$10,000 from her savings account in a licensed bank and deposits the sum to a current account in another licensed bank.

The immediate effect of the above actions on the Hong Kong's money supply would be:

choices.text: M1 increases and M2 remains unchanged.
M2 increases and M3 remains unchanged.

questions.explanation: A saving deposit is included in M2 but not M1, while a current-account deposit is included in both M1 and M2. The transfer raises M1 but leaves M2 unchanged.

questions.keyPoint: Qualities of good money
questions.stem: Which of the following assets has the highest liquidity?
questions.explanation: Savings deposits can be converted into a means of payment most quickly and with the lowest risk of loss, so they are the most liquid asset listed.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Measurements of the general price level
questions.keyPoint: Calculate/Determine the rate of change in the general price level (inflation/ deflation rate) by using the CPI and the implicit price deflator of GDP
questions.stem: When the increase in inflation rate is slowing down, the ___________ is increasing.

choices.text: real rate of return on holding money

questions.explanation: A slowing increase in the inflation rate still means a positive inflation rate. The general price level therefore continues to increase, though more slowly.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: Which of the following parties will gain when unexpected inflation occurs?

choices.text: debtors of a bank whose interest rates of the loans are adjusted according to the inflation rate
retired people who receive a fixed amount of elderly allowance
banks which issue bonds at fixed interest rates
investors who hold bonds at fixed interest rates

questions.explanation: A bank that issues fixed-interest bonds is a debtor. Unexpected inflation lowers the real value of its fixed repayments, so it gains. The other listed parties either have payments adjusted for inflation or lose purchasing power.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Deflationary gap
questions.stem: Suppose an economy is in long-run equilibrium. Which of the following will lead to the existence of a deflationary gap?

choices.text: a decrease in the required reserve ratio
destruction of infrastructures due to an earthquake
an issuance of new money by the central bank
a reduction of public expenditure by the government

questions.explanation: A reduction in public expenditure decreases aggregate demand. Starting from long-run equilibrium, output falls below potential output and creates a deflationary gap.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the quantity theory of money is CORRECT?

choices.text: In the short run, an increase in money supply will lead to an increase in nominal national income by the same proportion.
In the short run, a once-and-for-all increase in money supply will lead to inflation.
In the long run, increasing money supply is the only way to achieve economic growth.
In the long run, altering money supply will not affect nominal national income.

questions.explanation: Under the quantity theory, with velocity unchanged, a proportional rise in money supply produces the same proportional rise in nominal national income in the short run. A once-and-for-all change in money supply changes the price level, rather than causing continuing inflation.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: When ___________, the government can try to offset its effect on national income by using an expansionary monetary policy.

choices.text: firms are pessimistic about their business prospects
the international crude oil price decreases

questions.explanation: Pessimistic firms reduce investment and aggregate demand, lowering national income. Expansionary monetary policy can lower interest rates and support investment and aggregate demand.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate
questions.stem: When the nominal interest rate is 8% and the expected inflation rate is 6%,

choices.text: the real rate of return of holding cash is 0.
the real rate of return of holding cash is -6%.

questions.explanation: The expected real interest rate equals nominal interest rate minus expected inflation: 8% - 6% = 2%.

questions.keyPoint: Direct tax and indirect tax
questions.stem: In Hong Kong, air passenger departure tax is a kind of ___________ and ___________ tax.
questions.explanation: Air passenger departure tax is imposed on spending rather than income, so it is indirect. A fixed payment is a larger proportion of a lower-income person's income, so it is regressive.

questions.keyPoint: Four basic principles of taxation
questions.stem: In Hong Kong, people can use various methods to make their tax payment, including via the internet, by phone or using automated teller machines (ATM). This arrangement is in accordance with the ___________ principle of taxation put forth by Adam Smith.
questions.explanation: Making payment available online, by phone and at ATMs makes it convenient for taxpayers to pay their taxes.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of a quota on domestic price, domestic consumption, domestic production and import quantity for a small open economy
questions.stem: Suppose a small open economy reduces the import quota on an imported good. Which of the following is CORRECT?

choices.text: There will be a rise in both domestic consumption of the good and the consumer surplus.
There will be a fall in both domestic production of the good and the producer surplus.
There will be an increase in the domestic price of the good and a decrease in the value of the import quota.
The world price of the good will remain unchanged and there will be an increase in the deadweight loss.

questions.explanation: Reducing a binding import quota makes imports more restricted. In a small open economy the world price is unchanged, while the tighter quota raises domestic price and increases the deadweight loss.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem:
Suppose both Country A and Country B produce only good X and good Y. If the opportunity cost of producing 1 unit of good X in Country A is higher than that in Country B,

(1) Country A has a comparative advantage in producing good Y.
(2) Country A has an absolute advantage in producing good Y.
(3) Country B has a comparative advantage in producing good X.
(4) Country B has an absolute advantage in producing good X.
questions.explanation: Country B has the lower opportunity cost of X and therefore a comparative advantage in X. With only two goods, Country A has the comparative advantage in Y. Opportunity cost alone gives no information about absolute advantage.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: The following table shows the amount of outputs that can be produced by Country A and Country B with ALL the resources they have.

choices.text: 1 unit of chocolate = 1.35 units of corn
1 unit of chocolate = 1.43 units of corn
1 unit of chocolate = 1.5 units of corn
1 unit of chocolate = 1.53 units of corn

questions.explanation: Country A's opportunity cost of one unit of chocolate is 30/24 = 1.25 units of corn, compared with 50/35 for Country B, so A exports chocolate. Its gain of 0.1 unit of corn per chocolate requires terms of trade of 1.25 + 0.1 = 1.35 units of corn per chocolate.
questions.postVisualStem: If the gain from trade per unit of exports of Country A is 0.1 units of corn, which of the following is the terms of trade between the two countries?

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Sammy is a comic books lover. Every week, he visits comic bookstores and buys 2 comic books no matter what the prices of the comic books are. From this we can conclude that his demand for comic books is
questions.explanation: Quantity demanded remains exactly two regardless of price, so the price elasticity of demand is zero: perfectly inelastic.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: In recent years, domestic sports equipment companies play an active role in advertising and innovating new products. This results in a 10% increase in the product price and a 30% increase in the total expenditure on domestic sports equipment. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: The total revenue of foreign sports equipment companies may rise or fall depending on the elasticity of demand.
The quantity demanded of imported sports equipment remains unchanged.
The demand for the domestic sports equipment is inelastic.
The quantity transacted of the domestic sports equipment increases.

questions.explanation: Advertising increases demand while innovation raises supply. As total expenditure rises by 30% despite a 10% rise in price, the quantity transacted of domestic equipment must have increased.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: Wearing contact lenses is becoming popular nowadays. At the same time, the technology of producing contact lens solutions is advanced. Which of the following diagrams could represent a result of the above events?
questions.explanation: Contact lenses and their solutions are complements, so greater popularity shifts demand for solutions right. Better production technology shifts supply right. Diagram C shows both shifts in the contact-lens-solutions market.

visuals.alt: Four supply-demand diagrams for contact lenses or contact lens solutions labelled A to D.
visuals.caption: Effects on contact lens solutions

movements: Compare the demand and supply changes in the four options.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Choose the contact-lens or lens-solution market diagram that fits the scenario.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: The following shows the advertisements of a telecommunication service provider for its smartphone monthly plan.

choices.text: The demand for telecommunication service will increase.
Relatively more people will choose Plan A.
The price of Plan A relative to Plan B will increase.
The consumer surplus for Plan B will rise while that for Plan A will drop.

questions.explanation: Plan A's price falls from $148 to $128 and Plan B's from $198 to $178. Plan A becomes cheaper relative to Plan B (128/178 is lower than 148/198), so relatively more people choose Plan A.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose all other services provided by the two plans are the same. After the special prices are offered, which of the following statements about the telecommunication service is correct?

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is the demand-supply diagram of a milk powder market. E0 is the original equilibrium point.
questions.explanation: A consumer subsidy increases demand, while a product recall decreases supply. The diagram's intersection of higher demand and lower supply is E4.

visuals.alt: Milk-powder supply and demand curves with equilibrium points E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Milk powder market

movements: Compare the labelled demand and supply shifts in the milk-powder market.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Select the market outcome consistent with the stated condition.

questions.postVisualStem: To encourage people to give birth, a subsidy is provided to milk powder consumers. Meanwhile, some brands of milk powder in the market are recalled as the powder is contaminated. The new equilibrium point in the milk powder market will be ________.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply schedule of good X and answer Questions 16 and 17.

choices.text: the total revenue of the complements of good X will increase.
the total tax revenue will be $32.
the total expenditure of consumers on good X will be $98.
consumers will bear a larger proportion of tax burden than producers.

questions.explanation: The original equilibrium is $6 and 16 units. With a $2 tax, consumers pay $7 and producers receive $5, so quantity is 14. Consumer expenditure is $7 x 14 = $98.
questions.postVisualStem: If the government imposes a per unit tax of $2 on good X,

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of demand

choices.text: the demand for good X is elastic.
the demand for good X is inelastic.
the supply of good X is elastic.
the elasticity of supply of good X is higher than its elasticity of demand.

questions.explanation: From $6 to $7, quantity demanded falls from 16 to 14: percentage quantity change is smaller than percentage price change, so demand is inelastic over this range.
questions.postVisualStem: With reference to the above question, within the range of the original and new market prices,

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: An oligopolist

choices.text: is a dominant seller which its market share is over 50%.
must follow other oligopolists' action so as to earn higher profit.
faces no competition from new firms as they are difficult to enter the market.
can adjust the price to maximise its profit.

questions.explanation: An oligopolist is a price searcher and can adjust price to maximise profit. It is interdependent with rivals but need not follow them, and entry barriers do not mean no possible new competition.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem:
If the government reduces the amount of per unit subsidy on a good,

(1) producer surplus will decrease.
(2) the price of the good will increase.
(3) deadweight loss will be smaller.
questions.explanation: Reducing a unit subsidy shifts supply upward, raising the consumer price and lowering producer surplus. It also reduces the distortion from the subsidy, so deadweight loss becomes smaller.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Lorenz curve
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the Lorenz curves of a country in years 20X4 and 20X9:

choices.text: the income distribution became more even.
the total income of the country remained unchanged.
the income of the low income group increased.

questions.explanation: The 20X9 Lorenz curve lies closer to the line of equality than the 20X4 curve, showing a more even income distribution and a lower Gini coefficient. It does not show total or absolute income.

visuals.alt: Lorenz curves A (year 20X4) and B (year 20X9), with B closer to the line of equality.
visuals.caption: Lorenz curves

movements: Curve B is closer to the line of equality than curve A.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Infer the change in income inequality between the two years.

questions.postVisualStem: According to the above diagram, from year 20X4 to year 20X9,

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are normative statements?

(1) Decreasing the salaries tax rate aggravates income inequality.
(2) Decreasing the salaries tax rate is the best way to improve employment.
(3) People's disposable income will increase after decreasing the salaries tax rate.
(4) The government should boost the economy by decreasing the salaries tax rate during deflation.
questions.explanation: Statements (2) and (4) include value judgments about the best policy or what government should do. Statements (1) and (3) are positive statements that can be tested against evidence.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Suppose the government plans to build elderly hostels on an urban renewal site. In which of the following situations will the cost of building the elderly hostels decrease?

choices.text: The proposal of building the elderly hostels is finally abolished.
The import price of raw materials used for building the elderly hostels decreases.
A statutory minimum wage is enforced during the building of elderly hostels.
The occupation rate of the elderly hostels is low after they are completed.

questions.explanation: Cheaper imported raw materials reduce the value of resources required for the project, so its opportunity cost falls. Abolishing the project or its later occupancy rate does not reduce the cost of building it.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between interest rate, current consumption and saving
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about interest is correct?

choices.text: Interest must be in the form of money.
Interest does not exist if there is deflation.
People will defer their current consumption if the interest rate decreases.
People will defer their current consumption if the interest rate increases.

questions.explanation: A higher interest rate increases the return to saving and the cost of present consumption, so people are more likely to defer consumption. Interest need not be paid in money and can exist during deflation.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Indoor badminton courts managed by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department are ________ because ________.

choices.text: private goods ... people have to pay when they use the badminton courts
private goods ... they are excludable and rival in consumption
public goods ... no one has an exclusive right to use them
public goods ... they are provided by the government

questions.explanation: The courts are excludable because access can be restricted and rival because one person's use reduces availability to others. Government provision or payment alone does not determine whether a good is public or private.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem:
Which of the following would increase the occupational mobility of labour in an economy?

(1) the retirement age is lowered to 50 years old
(2) subsidy is provided to people who take courses under the retraining programme
(3) the entrance requirement is lowered for many professional jobs in the labour market
questions.explanation: Retraining raises workers' skills and lower entry requirements reduce barriers to changing occupation. A lower retirement age affects labour-force size rather than occupational mobility.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem: The labour supply of Hong Kong will decrease if

choices.text: more companies provide full-pay paternity leave for their employees.
the government lowers the minimum working age.
the average working hours of labour increases.
the government relaxes controls on importing labour.

questions.explanation: Paid paternity leave reduces the labour supplied during the leave period. Lowering the minimum working age, longer working hours and looser controls on imported labour increase available labour supply.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: Miss Lo is the owner of a shop selling handmade accessories. She pays her designers and craftsmen wages on a piece rate basis. Which of the following would be a possible reason for Miss Lo choosing to pay her workers on a piece rate instead of a time rate basis?

choices.text: This can reduce the fluctuation on the monthly expenditure on wages.
This can lower the cost of measuring contribution of workers.
This can improve the quality of output.

questions.explanation: Piece-rate pay rewards output directly and can strengthen the incentive to produce. It can make wage expenditure less stable and may require more checking of output quality.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership

choices.text: Both firms cannot issue shares to the public.
Firm A has more capital than Firm B.
Firm A is at a greater risk of being taken over by others than Firm B.
Firm B bears less liability than Firm A.

questions.explanation: Firm A's freely transferable ownership makes a takeover easier than for Firm B, whose transfer needs other owners' consent. The table does not establish either firm's capital or liability.

questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: Refer to the following table showing revenue and production costs of a competitive firm.

choices.text: the maximum profit the firm can make is $29.
the profit-maximising output level of the firm is 4 units.
the fixed cost of the firm is $5.

questions.explanation: Profit is total revenue minus total cost: $17, $23, $27, $29, $29 and $27 at outputs 2 to 7. The maximum is therefore $29. Revenue rises by $11 per unit, so price is $11 rather than $10.

questions.stem: The following table shows the information of a firm during a certain period.

choices.text: The firm changed its payment method from piece rate to time rate.
There is a higher degree of specialisation in production.
The 10 most productive workers left the firm for study.

questions.explanation: Output per worker per day rose from 8,000 / (50 x 8) = 20 to 10,000 / (40 x 10) = 25. Greater specialisation can raise productivity; the other changes would tend to reduce it.

At the end of the period

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem:
Which of the following policies can help improve income inequality?

(1) to build more public housing
(2) to implement minimum wage law
(3) to abolish the anti-competitive law
questions.explanation: Public housing and a minimum wage can raise the real income of lower-income households. Abolishing competition law can increase market power and does not improve income equality.

questions.keyPoint: Expenditure approach
questions.stem: Refer to the following table.

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of nominal GDP and real GDP
questions.stem: Country A's real GDP grew at a higher rate than its nominal GDP. At the same time, its population dropped. As a result,
questions.explanation: If real GDP grows faster than nominal GDP, the general price level must fall, so the inflation rate is negative. A GDP deflator is a positive index, and the other effects cannot be inferred.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: There is an increasing number of housewives trained to be post-natal care workers. If all of them are employed after training, what will be the effect on the unemployment rate of Hong Kong?

choices.text: The unemployment rate will remain unchanged.
The effect on the unemployment rate cannot be determined.

questions.explanation: The newly employed workers enter the labour force as employed people. The number unemployed is unchanged while the labour force rises, so unemployment rate falls.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.stem: Which of the following will cause an increase in aggregate supply?

choices.text: a drop in a sales tax rate

questions.explanation: A lower sales tax reduces firms' production costs and shifts short-run aggregate supply right. The other changes either raise costs, reduce productive resources, or affect aggregate demand.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand (AD) curves, the short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curves and long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve of a country. Point E0 is the initial equilibrium point.
questions.explanation: A higher profits tax lowers investment and shifts AD left to AD1. Short-run equilibrium moves to E1; falling output and prices shift SRAS right until long-run output is restored at E2.

visuals.alt: AD, SRAS and LRAS diagram with points E0 to E3.
visuals.caption: Profits-tax rise

diagramDetails.answerFocus: Identify the economic condition represented by the selected equilibrium.

questions.postVisualStem: When the government increases the profits tax rate, the short-run equilibrium is at ________ and the long-run equilibrium is at ________.

questions.explanation: A maximum deposit expansion of $1,500 million from $300 million reserves implies a 20% required reserve ratio. Suppose the maximum amount of deposits the banking system can expand is $1,500 million. Which of the following statements is correct?

(1) The required reserve ratio for the banking system is 25%.
(2) The maximum amount of loans the banking system can make is $1,200 million.
(3) The excess reserves of the banking system are $140 million.

questions.keyPoint: Definitions of M1, M2 and M3 in
questions.stem:
Wyman receives HK$300,000 from overseas. He then deposits half of the amount as a demand deposit with a licensed bank and HK$100,000 as a time deposit with a deposit-taking company. He keeps the remainder as cash in hand.

What will be the immediate effect of the above actions on the Hong Kong dollar money supply?

choices.text: M1 will increase by HK$50,000 while M2 and M3 will increase by HK$150,000.
M1 will increase by HK$200,000 and M3 will increase by HK$300,000.
M2 will increase by HK$100,000 and M3 will increase by HK$250,000.
M2 will increase by HK$150,000 and M3 will increase by HK$200,000.

questions.explanation: Cash in hand and demand deposits are in M1, so M1 rises by $150,000 cash plus $150,000 demand deposit? The overseas cash enters as $300,000: $150,000 demand deposit and $50,000 cash count in M1, while the $100,000 deposit-taking-company time deposit is in M3 only. Thus M1 rises $200,000 and M3 $300,000.

questions.keyPoint: How central bank functions are carried out in
questions.stem: Which of the following central bank functions is performed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority?

choices.text: providing banking services for the government
determining the interest rate in Hong Kong

questions.explanation: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority manages Hong Kong's foreign exchange reserves. It does not collect taxes or set interest rates under the linked exchange-rate system.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem:
People hold more money for transaction as their nominal income increases. To stabilise the interest rate, the central bank can

(1) lower the discount rate.
(2) lower the required reserve ratio.
(3) sell government bonds to the public.
(4) print more money.
questions.explanation: Higher transaction demand raises interest rates. Lowering the discount rate or required reserve ratio, and printing money, all increase money supply to offset this. Selling bonds reduces money supply.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of current account surplus and deficit
questions.stem: In an open economy, the government has a budget balance and there is a trade surplus. If there is a decrease in private consumption expenditure, the government will have a ________ and there will be a current account ________.
questions.explanation: Lower private consumption raises private saving. With investment unchanged, the sectoral-balance identity requires a government budget deficit while the current-account surplus remains.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: Which of the following persons will most likely lose if there is unexpected deflation in Hong Kong?

choices.text: a foreigner borrowing HK$10,000 from a bank in Hong Kong at fixed rate
a foreigner receiving a fixed amount of monthly salary in Hong Kong dollars
a Hong Kong resident holding cash
a Hong Kong resident holding ibond of which the interest is paid at a rate linked to the inflation in Hong Kong

questions.explanation: Unexpected deflation raises the real value of a fixed Hong Kong-dollar debt, so the fixed-rate borrower loses.

questions.keyPoint: Taxation in
questions.stem:
Mr. Cheung is the owner of a toy shop and is also employed as an consultant of a fashion design company. Which of the following taxes does he need to pay to the HKSAR Government?

(1) stamp duty
(2) salaries tax
(3) profits tax
(4) property tax
questions.explanation: His employment income is subject to salaries tax and his shop profit to profits tax. Nothing indicates a property transfer or rental income.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem:
Suppose the government increased her spending on arts development. This will result in

(1) an increase in aggregate demand.
(2) an increase in real GDP in the short run.
(3) an increase in budget deficit.
(4) an increase in aggregate output in the long run.
questions.explanation: Government spending raises aggregate demand and short-run real GDP. Spending on arts development can raise productive capacity and long-run output; a deficit is not certain without revenue information.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: In Hong Kong, the basic allowance of the salaries tax increased from $108,000 to $120,000 for the year of assessment 2012/13 and onwards. This would lead to

choices.text: an increase in the proportion of tax revenue in total government revenue.
an increase in the ratio of direct taxes to indirect taxes.
a more even post-tax income distribution of Hong Kong citizens.

questions.explanation: A larger basic allowance reduces tax paid by lower-income taxpayers proportionately more, improving the post-tax income distribution. It does not determine the budget or tax-revenue ratios.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Which of the following can offset the effect of a decrease of the required reserve ratio on the price level?

choices.text: an increase in the desire to import

questions.explanation: A lower required reserve ratio expands money supply and aggregate demand. More saving lowers consumption and aggregate demand, offsetting upward pressure on the price level.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: The following table shows the number of chocolate and soft drinks that Country A and Country B can produce with all of their resources. Both countries allocate all their resources evenly to produce the two products.

choices.text: Country A will gain 0.1 units of chocolate per unit of exports.
Country A will gain 0.6 units of soft drinks per unit of imports.
Country B will gain 1 unit of soft drinks per unit of exports.
Country B will gain 0.8 units of chocolate per unit of imports.

questions.explanation: Country A gives up 2.5 soft drinks for one chocolate, while the trade price is 2 soft drinks. It gains 0.5 soft drink per imported chocolate, equivalent to 0.1 chocolate per export.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: For a mutually beneficial trade to occur between two countries,

choices.text: the terms of trade must lie between the opportunity costs of the two countries.
the transportation cost must be zero.
the resource endowments of the two countries must be different.
the two countries must have an absolute advantage in producing either one good.

questions.explanation: Both countries gain only when the terms of trade lie between their respective opportunity costs. Zero transport cost and absolute advantage are not necessary.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies

choices.text: a rise in the price (in terms of HK$) of exports from U.K. to Hong Kong.
a rise in the number of tourists from U.K. to the US.
a drop in the total value (in terms of Pound) of exports from Hong Kong.
a drop in the quantity of exports from Hong Kong to U.K..

questions.explanation: The pound appreciates against the US dollar, and Hong Kong dollar follows the US dollar. Hong Kong exports become more expensive to UK buyers, reducing export quantity.
