diagramDetails.answerFocus: Before tax, equilibrium is price $5 and quantity 6. After tax, buyers pay $6, producers receive $4 and quantity is 5; the per-unit tax is $2 and tax revenue is $10.

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: The broadband service market in Hong Kong is an oligopoly because

choices.text: the broadband service providers can adjust the prices of their services.
the services provided by different broadband service providers are different.
the broadband service providers advertise their services on television.
there are only a few dominant broadband service providers in Hong Kong.

questions.explanation: An oligopoly has a small number of dominant sellers. Firms in several imperfectly competitive market structures can adjust prices, differentiate services or advertise, so those features alone do not identify oligopoly.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: A government provides a per-unit subsidy to the producers of influenza vaccines. Which of the following statements about the influenza vaccines market is CORRECT?

choices.text: The lower market price reduces producer surplus.
The lower market price raises consumer surplus.
Total revenue (excluding subsidy) of producers will increase.
If the supply is more elastic than the demand, producers' share of subsidy will be greater than consumers' share of subsidy.

questions.explanation: A producer subsidy shifts supply down to consumers, lowering the market price and raising consumer surplus. Producers also receive the subsidy, so a lower market price does not itself show lower producer surplus; sales revenue excluding subsidy is indeterminate. The less elastic side receives the larger share of a subsidy, so more elastic producers would not receive the greater share.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: A government abolishes the effective quota on the production of a good. As a result,

choices.text: total revenue of producers will increase.
the quantity transacted of the good will decrease.
quality of the good will improve.

questions.explanation: An effective quota restricts output below the competitive equilibrium and creates deadweight loss. Abolishing it allows quantity transacted to move towards the efficient level, so total social surplus and efficiency improve. The effects on producers' revenue and product quality are not certain.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are positive statements?

(1) Hongkongers' high demand for tiny flats will continue.
(2) Buyers of tiny flats are normally youngsters moving out of the family home.
(3) With the continued high demand for tiny flats, prices will climb higher.
(4) As interest rates on mortgage loans are low, those who can afford to buy a flat should buy one now.
questions.explanation: Statements (1), (2) and (3) are claims about facts or causal relationships that can be tested against evidence. Statement (4) says what people should do, so it is normative.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of interest
questions.stem: Mr. Chan works in Central. Recently, he has purchased a Home Ownership Scheme flat in Tai O with a mortgage loan. In which of the following situations will his cost of purchasing the flat increase?

choices.text: The travel time to and from Central increases due to traffic congestion.

questions.explanation: Mortgage interest is the cost of obtaining the loaned funds earlier. A higher mortgage interest rate therefore raises the cost of purchasing the flat; the other items are costs of owning, using or repairing it after purchase.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of interest
questions.stem:
Which of the following is regarded as an interest in economics?

(1) the half-yearly return on iBonds to the bond holders
(2) the same-day return discount offered by the MTRC to Octopus Card holders
(3) the handling charge on credit card overdraft
questions.explanation: The iBond return and the charge for a credit-card overdraft are payments connected with borrowing or lending resources over time, so they are interest in economics. The MTR same-day return discount is a fare discount, not interest.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a public good?

choices.text: a pair of serving chopsticks (公筷)

questions.explanation: A free-to-air television programme is non-excludable and non-rivalrous for viewers, which are the defining features of a public good. The other services or objects can be restricted, congested or used by one person at a time.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following will cause the occupational mobility of Hong Kong labour to increase?

choices.text: More career guidance services are provided by schools.
More foreign workers are imported by local industries.
More transport subsidy is provided to low-income earners.
A wider variety of training courses are provided by the Employees Retraining Board.

questions.explanation: A wider range of retraining courses equips workers with skills for changing occupations, directly increasing occupational mobility. Career guidance and transport subsidies do not by themselves provide the relevant retraining, while imported workers concern labour supply.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem: Hong Kong's labour supply will decrease if

choices.text: more companies pay for overtime work.
the number of Hong Kong people emigrating abroad increases.
most of the government departments extend their office hours.
the number of associate degree places provided by post-secondary institutions decreases.

questions.explanation: When more Hong Kong people emigrate, fewer people are available and willing to work in Hong Kong, so the local labour supply falls. The other changes do not necessarily reduce the number of workers available in Hong Kong.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: Some travel agencies are starting to pay their tour guides fixed salaries and getting rid of service fees that the guides used to collect from the tourists at the end of tours. Which of the following would be a result of this change in the wage payment method?

choices.text: more stable income for tour guides

questions.explanation: Replacing variable service fees with fixed salaries makes tour guides' pay less dependent on tourist spending and demand, so their income becomes more stable. It does not necessarily lower labour costs, improve service or reduce the need for supervision.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: The table below shows the information of two Hong Kong firms.

choices.text: The ownership of firm A can be transferred without the consent of other owners while the ownership of firm B can only be transferred with the consent of other owners.
The owners of firm A bear limited liability while the owners of firm B bear unlimited liability.
Firm A cannot issue shares and bonds to the public while firm B can.
Firm A pays a higher profits tax rate than firm B.

questions.explanation: Firm A discloses accounting information to the public, so it is a public limited company; firm B is a private limited company. Shares in a public limited company can be transferred freely, whereas a private limited company's shares require other owners' consent. Both have limited liability, and neither liability nor the profits-tax rate distinguishes them in the stated way.

visuals.caption: Information of two Hong Kong firms
rows: If one of the owners withdraws, the firm can still exist.
If one of the owners withdraws, the firm can still exist.

questions.postVisualStem: According to the above information, in Hong Kong, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the production information of a competitive firm.
questions.explanation: A competitive firm maximises profit where price equals marginal cost, provided price covers average variable cost. The table gives only average variable cost at each output, not marginal cost, so the profit-maximising output cannot be determined.

visuals.caption: Production information of a competitive firm

questions.postVisualStem: If the price of the product is $12, the firm will produce _______ units of output in order to maximise its profit.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following helps raise the average labour productivity?

choices.text: reducing the number of days of paid annual leave

questions.explanation: Improving the flow of work reduces delays and makes each worker's output per unit of time higher. The other measures may change hours worked or employment, but do not necessarily raise average labour productivity.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an example of divergence between private and social costs/benefits?

choices.text: The owner of a house builds some trees and the leaves fall to the garden of the house.
A flight passenger reclines his seat and causes inconvenience to the passenger behind him.
A driver breaks the speed limit and causes a traffic accident.
A professor puts his academic research report on the Internet and lets the public download the report for free.

questions.explanation: In A, both the benefit of the trees and the fallen leaves affect the same house owner, so there is no external effect. B and C impose negative external costs on others, while D creates a positive external benefit for the public.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Lorenz curve
questions.stem:
If the Lorenz curves of Country A and Country B are identical, this implies that

(1) their national incomes are the same.
(2) their Gini coefficients are the same.
(3) the bottom 20% of households share the same percentage of total income.
questions.explanation: Identical Lorenz curves show identical cumulative income shares at every population proportion, so the bottom 20% share the same proportion of total income and the areas used to calculate their Gini coefficients are the same. A Lorenz curve does not show the countries' absolute national incomes.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem: Kevin and Jason have the same academic qualifications, but their incomes are totally different. This may be because

choices.text: All of the above are correct.

questions.explanation: Income can differ despite equal academic qualifications because people can have different natural abilities and hours worked, and discrimination associated with nationality can affect earnings. All three factors may contribute to income inequality.

questions.keyPoint: Expenditure approach
questions.stem: The table below shows the data of a country in a certain year.
questions.explanation: The official key marks C (20 ... 10). There is a source inconsistency to keep visible: applying the stated expenditure data gives 100 + 70 - 10 + X + 40 - 50 = 180, so X = 30, while GDP at factor cost gives Y = 10. The official marking-scheme answer is retained for fidelity; the arithmetic conflict should be reviewed by a teacher.

visuals.caption: Data of a country in a certain year
rows: Total imports of goods and services
Total exports of goods and services

questions.postVisualStem: If the GDP at market prices is $180 million and the GDP at factor cost is $170 million, the values of X and Y are ______ and ______ respectively.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: Which of the following would be included in Hong Kong's GNP only?

choices.text: the expenditure of tourists on accommodation in Hong Kong
the dividend received by a Hong Kong resident from his investment in Shanghai's stock market
the income earned by an American accountant from working in an accounting firm in Hong Kong for a year
the wages earned by a French artist from working in a gallery in Hong Kong for half a year

questions.explanation: A Hong Kong resident's dividend from an overseas investment is net factor income from abroad, so it is included in Hong Kong GNP but not GDP. Tourist accommodation spending is part of domestic production, while the foreign workers' incomes are generated in Hong Kong and do not fit the 'GNP only' description.

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of nominal GDP and real GDP
questions.stem: The population, nominal GDP and the general price level of a country increases by 2%, 4% and 5% respectively compared to the same period in the previous year. We can conclude that the real GDP of the country _________ and the per capita nominal GDP _________.
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP rises by less than the general price level, so real GDP falls. Nominal GDP rises by 4% while population rises by 2%, so nominal GDP per person increases.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem:
If an economy's labour force and unemployed population increase at the same time with the extent of the former _________ the latter, then the unemployment rate will _________.

(1) greater than ... increase
(2) greater than ... decrease
(3) equal to ... remain unchanged
questions.explanation: The unemployment rate is unemployed people as a percentage of the labour force. If the labour force's percentage increase is greater than the unemployed population's, the rate falls; if their percentage increases are equal, the rate is unchanged. Statements (2) and (3) are correct.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem:
Both the price level and employment level of a country increases. Which of the following would be the possible causes?

(1) The basic allowance of salaries tax increases.
(2) The profits tax rate increases.
(3) The government imposes a sales tax.
(4) There is an economic recovery in major trading countries.
questions.explanation: A higher salaries-tax allowance increases disposable income and consumption, while an economic recovery in trading partners raises exports. Both shift aggregate demand right, increasing price and employment. A profits-tax rise reduces investment incentives and a sales tax is a cost-side shock, so neither gives the stated combination.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.stem: Suppose a country is initially at the long run equilibrium. If there is a global increase in oil price, __________________ in the short run and __________________ in the long run.

choices.text: the short run aggregate supply will decrease ... the short run aggregate supply will increase to the original level
the short run aggregate supply will decrease ... aggregate demand will increase and the employment level will restore to the full-employment level
aggregate demand will decrease ... aggregate demand will increase to the original level
aggregate demand will decrease ... the short run aggregate supply will increase and the employment level will restore to the full-employment level

questions.explanation: Higher oil prices raise production costs and decrease short-run aggregate supply. In the long run, lower output and employment put downward pressure on factor prices, shifting short-run aggregate supply back to its original position and restoring full-employment output.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Suppose a banking system has reserves of $300 million (including excess reserves of $100 million) and loans of $700 million. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: If all the excess reserves are lent out, the deposits of the banking system can be increased by $500 million.
The maximum amount of loans that the banking system can provide is $800 million.

questions.explanation: The balance sheet implies deposits of $1,000 million. Required reserves are $200 million, so the required reserve ratio is 20% and the maximum multiplier is 5. Lending all $100 million excess reserves allows deposits to rise by $100 x 5 = $500 million; the actual multiplier is not 5 and the maximum loans are not merely $800 million.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem:
Elaine receives a remittance of HK$200,000 from overseas. She deposits HK$20,000 as a demand deposit in a licensed bank and buys $50,000-worth of negotiable certificates of deposit issued by that bank. She deposits the rest as a time deposit in a deposit-taking company.

The immediate effects of the above actions on the money supply of Hong Kong are: M2 increases by __________ and M3 increases by __________.
questions.explanation: M2 includes the $20,000 demand deposit and $50,000 negotiable certificate of deposit with the licensed bank. M3 additionally includes the $130,000 time deposit with the deposit-taking company, so M2 rises by $70,000 and M3 by $200,000.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: An increase in people's wealth affects _________________, leading to a _________________ shift of money demand curve.
questions.explanation: Wealth affects the amount people wish to hold as an asset. Higher wealth raises asset demand for money, shifting the money-demand curve rightward.

questions.keyPoint: How central bank functions are carried out in
questions.stem:
Which of the following are performed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority?

(1) settling and clearing transactions among commercial banks
(2) issuing coins
(3) carrying out monetary policy
questions.explanation: The HKMA carries out Hong Kong's monetary policy and is responsible for issuing coins. Interbank settlement and clearing are carried out through the relevant clearing system rather than being a direct HKMA function.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem: Which of the following is/are the impact(s) of the central bank buying government bonds from the public?
questions.explanation: Buying bonds pays funds into the public and banking system, expanding the monetary base and money supply. This lowers interest rates, encourages consumption and can create inflationary pressure.

questions.keyPoint: Surplus budget, deficit budget and balanced budget
questions.stem: A country has a fiscal deficit and a trade deficit. If the country raises its import tariff, holding all other things constant, its fiscal deficit will _______________ and its trade deficit will _______________.
questions.explanation: An import tariff raises government revenue, improving the fiscal balance and reducing the fiscal deficit. It also reduces imports, so the trade deficit decreases, holding other factors constant.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: A country's inflation rate of the first quarter of a certain year was expected to be 3%, but it turned out to be 4%. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: A person holding all of his wealth as cash would have gained.
An employer of a foreign domestic helper who signed a one-year contract would have gained.
A firm repaying a fixed-rate bank loan would have lost.
An insurance company would have lost.

questions.explanation: Inflation is higher than expected. The real value of cash falls, borrowers repaying fixed-rate loans gain, and an employer paying a pre-agreed nominal wage gains because the real wage cost is lower than expected.

questions.keyPoint: Taxation in
questions.stem: According to the tax system in Hong Kong, which of the following incomes generated in Hong Kong is NOT taxable?
questions.explanation: Hong Kong does not generally tax capital gains from the sale of shares. Employment income including bonuses, business profits and director's remuneration are taxable when the relevant conditions are met.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.stem: In September 2014, the Hong Kong government announced plans for seven new rail projects, which cost around $110 billion. Which of the following would be resulted?

choices.text: In the long run, the full-employment output level will increase.
In the short run, the output level will increase.
In the long run, the change in the price level is uncertain.
Both options A and B are correct.

questions.explanation: Rail projects add to investment expenditure in the short run, increasing aggregate demand and output. Once completed, the extra transport infrastructure raises productive capacity, increasing long-run full-employment output.

questions.keyPoint: Direct tax and indirect tax
questions.stem: The table below shows the composition of the government revenue of an economy in recent years.
questions.explanation: Percentages alone do not show whether the absolute amounts in statement (1) changed. In Year 4, indirect tax is 45% and direct tax 40%, so statement (2) is true. The direct-to-indirect ratio falls from 55:25 to 40:45, making statement (3) true.
questions.postVisualStem:
According to the above information, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The amount of direct tax collected decreased while the amount of indirect tax collected increased during the period.
(2) In Year 4, the amount of indirect tax collected was more than that of direct tax.
(3) The ratio of direct tax to indirect tax decreased during the period.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: A government imposes effective quotas on imported raw materials, but the general price level remains unchanged. Which of the following is a possible reason?
questions.explanation: Quotas on imported raw materials raise firms' costs and put upward pressure on prices. A higher discount rate is contractionary monetary policy: it reduces borrowing, aggregate demand and the offsetting pressure on the general price level.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem:
The amount of resources of Country A is double that of Country B in the production of good X and good Y. With all of the resources, Country A can produce 18 units of good X or 6 units of good Y, while Country B can produce 10 units of good X or 14 units of good Y.

Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) Country A has an absolute advantage in producing good X.
(2) Country A has a comparative advantage in producing good X.
(3) 1 unit of good X in exchange for 0.8 units of good Y is a mutually beneficial terms of trade for the two countries.
questions.explanation: Country A has a comparative advantage in X because its opportunity cost of 1 X is 1/3 Y, lower than Country B's 1.4 Y. Country A does not have an absolute advantage in X after allowing for its double resource endowment: its output per unit of resource is lower. A price of 1 X for 0.8 Y lies between the countries' opportunity costs, so it is mutually beneficial.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: Suppose the terms of trade that both countries agreed is 1 unit of good X in exchange for 1 unit of good Y. Also, the countries exporting and importing good X have to pay a transport cost of 0.1 units of good Y. To trade 4 units of good X, the gain from trade of Country B is _____ units of good Y.
questions.explanation: Country B's opportunity cost of producing 1 X is 1.4 Y. Importing X costs 1 Y plus 0.1 Y transport, so it gains 0.3 Y per X. For 4 X, total gain is 4 x 0.3 = 1.2 Y.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of a quota on domestic price, domestic consumption, domestic production and import quantity for a small open economy
questions.stem: A small open economy imposes an effective quota on an imported good. Lowering the quota limit will cause

choices.text: the world price of the good to increase.
the quality of the good to decrease.
the total expenditure on the good to increase.

questions.explanation: A lower binding quota restricts imports more tightly and raises the domestic price. Domestic producers move up their supply curve, so domestic production increases. The world price is unchanged for a small open economy.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem:
The exchange rate of the Japanese yen against the US dollar continues to fall since the beginning of 2013. This would lead to

(1) an increase in the competitiveness of goods exported from Japan in Hong Kong.
(2) a decrease in the number of Japanese tourists visiting Hong Kong.
(3) an increase in the total value of Hong Kong exports to Japan (in terms of the Japanese yen).
(4) an increase in the total value of Hong Kong imports from Japan (in terms of the Japanese Yen).
questions.explanation: A weaker yen makes Japanese exports cheaper in Hong Kong, raising their competitiveness. Hong Kong becomes more expensive for Japanese visitors, so their number falls. The weaker yen raises the yen value of Hong Kong imports from Japan; the change in Hong Kong exports to Japan in yen is not determined from the information given.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: Which of the following is included in the invisible export in the current account of Hong Kong?

choices.text: the expenditure of a Hong Kong resident buying the tickets of a show in Macau
the tuition fee paid by an American student to a university in Hong Kong
the amount of money paid by a Korean firm for buying cosmetic products from a Hong Kong firm
the amount of money paid by a resident in Shanghai buying shares of a Hong Kong listed company through a broker in Shanghai

questions.explanation: Tuition paid by an overseas student to a Hong Kong university is an export of education services, so it is an invisible export in the current account. A is an import of services, C is a visible export of goods and D belongs to the financial account.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem:
Which of the following will increase the geographical mobility of labour in an economy?

(1) The government subsidises public transport for the elderly.
(2) A new cross harbour tunnel is built.
(3) More private institutions provide retraining programmes.
(4) Because of severe economic downturn, many people choose to emigrate to other countries.
questions.explanation: A new cross-harbour tunnel reduces the cost of travelling between places of work, and emigration is geographical movement of labour. Subsidised elderly transport is not a general labour-mobility measure, while retraining mainly raises occupational mobility.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in demand
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in demand
questions.stem:
An increase in the demand for residential buildings will lead to an increase in ______________.

(1) the price of residential buildings.
(2) the quantity transacted of commercial buildings.
(3) the wage rate of construction workers.
questions.explanation: Higher demand for residential buildings raises their equilibrium price. It also raises derived demand for construction workers and hence their wage rate. Commercial buildings are not necessarily affected in the stated direction.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Measuring price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: In a car park, there are many parking spaces not rented out. The car park therefore decreases its monthly parking fee by 20%. As a result, the number of parking spaces rented out increases by 5%. We can conclude that

choices.text: the demand for the parking spaces is elastic.
the demand for the parking spaces is inelastic.
the supply of the parking spaces is elastic.
the supply of the parking spaces is inelastic.

questions.explanation: The percentage change in quantity demanded is 5% and the percentage change in price is 20%, so the absolute price elasticity of demand is 5 / 20 = 0.25. Since it is below one, demand is inelastic.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following demand-supply diagram shows the market of Korean food in Hong Kong. E0 is the initial equilibrium point. If the cost of importing ingredients from Korea increases and more people want to try Korean food after the broadcasting of a new TV programme introducing Korean food, the new equilibrium will be at ________.
questions.explanation: A higher cost of imported ingredients decreases supply from S0 to S1. The television programme raises demand from D0 to D2. The resulting equilibrium is E2.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram of the Hong Kong market for Korean food, with supply curves S0-S2, demand curves D0-D2 and equilibria E0-E4.
visuals.caption: Korean food market in Hong Kong

movements: A higher import cost shifts supply from S0 to S1.
A television programme that makes Korean food more popular shifts demand from D0 to D2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The intersection of S1 and D2 is E2.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: If the Hong Kong government raises the per-unit tobacco tax,

choices.text: the tobacco tax collected by the Hong Kong government will increase.
the total expenditure on cigarettes in Hong Kong will increase.
there will be more cigarette smuggling in Hong Kong.
the total sales volume of cigarettes in Hong Kong will increase.

questions.explanation: A higher tobacco tax creates a larger price gap between taxed and untaxed cigarettes, making smuggling more attractive. The effects on tax revenue and total expenditure depend on elasticities, while legal sales volume will not increase.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply schedule for good X.

choices.text: the market price of good X will fall by $1.
total subsidy paid by the government is $3,500.
consumers' share of the subsidy will be $500 more than producers' share of the subsidy.

questions.explanation: Initially, equilibrium is $6 and 400 units. With a $3 subsidy, buyers pay $4 while producers receive $7 and 500 units are sold. Consumers gain $2 per unit ($1,000) and producers gain $1 per unit ($500), so consumers' share is $500 larger.
questions.postVisualStem: If the government provides a per-unit subsidy of $3 to the producers of good X,

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: The market structure of mobile communication services in Hong Kong is

choices.text: monopolistic competition because plans provided by different companies are different.
monopolistic competition because companies need to engage in price competition and non-price competition.
an oligopoly because the pricing strategies of the companies are interdependent.
an oligopoly because there are several dominant companies in the market.

questions.explanation: Hong Kong mobile communication is characterised by several dominant providers, which is the defining feature of an oligopoly. Product differences and competition also occur in other market structures; the question's market description is identified most directly by the small number of dominant firms.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price floor
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram of the labour market in Country X. Pw is the current level of minimum wage.

choices.text: Producer surplus may increase, decrease or remain unchanged.
Surplus of labour may increase or decrease.

questions.explanation: Raising the minimum wage changes neither the labour-supply curve nor its position. An effective higher price floor reduces efficiency and raises surplus labour. The change in producer surplus can be positive, negative or zero depending on the shapes of demand and supply.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram of a labour market with supply S, demand D and current minimum wage Pw.
visuals.caption: Labour market with a minimum wage

movements: Raising the effective minimum wage moves the price floor upward.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: A higher effective minimum wage does not shift labour supply. Its effect on producer surplus depends on the demand and supply curves, while it does not improve efficiency.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government raises the minimum wage rate. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem:
Which of the following services provided by the government will generate beneficial externalities?

(1) primary education
(2) public medical services
(3) recreational facilities
questions.explanation: Primary education creates benefits such as a better-informed workforce, public medical services reduce disease spillovers, and recreational facilities can improve public health and community amenity. All three can therefore create beneficial externalities.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: Which of the following policies helps equalise income among individuals in Hong Kong?

choices.text: increasing the value of the Health Care Voucher (醫療券) for the elderly

questions.explanation: Increasing Health Care Vouchers transfers support to elderly recipients and helps equalise income. Building universities mainly equalises opportunities, abolishing property tax favours property owners, and a general sales tax is not an income-equalising measure.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem:
Which of the following exist(s) in a one-man economy?

(1) scarcity
(2) specialisation
(3) exchange
questions.explanation: Scarcity exists whenever resources are limited relative to human wants, even with only one person. Specialisation and exchange require more than one economic participant.

questions.keyPoint: Definition of free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: Free goods

choices.text: are goods that people do not prefer.
may not be free of charge.
can be obtained without any cost.

questions.explanation: A free good is available without opportunity cost. It need not have unlimited physical supply, and it is defined by the absence of cost rather than by whether people prefer it or a money price is printed.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: Study the following circular flow diagram.

choices.text: factors of production ... household's consumption expenditure
final goods and services ... cost of production
final goods and services ... firm's revenue

questions.explanation: The real flow at X is the final goods and services that firms provide for households. The money flow at Y is the firm's payment for productive factors, so it is a cost of production.

visuals.alt: Circular-flow diagram connecting firms and households through the product and factor markets; solid arrows show money flow and dashed arrows show real flow.
visuals.caption: Circular flow of money and real resources

curves: Solid arrows show money flow.
Dashed arrows show real flow.
movements: At the product market, final goods and services flow from firms to households.
At the factor market, the firm's payments for factors are a cost of production.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: X is final goods and services, while Y is cost of production.

questions.postVisualStem: X and Y represent ____________ and ____________ respectively.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem: Compared to a market economy, a command economy has

choices.text: more resources owned by the government.
fewer government interventions in the market.
more production guided by price signals.

questions.explanation: In a command economy, the government owns or controls a larger share of resources and directs production. Market prices play a smaller role, while national income is not necessarily lower.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a profit-maximising price taker in the short run.
questions.explanation: At 3 units, marginal cost is $35, so the initial price is $35 and profit is $105 - $95 = $10. A $10 price increase makes the profit-maximising output 5, where marginal cost is $45. New profit is $225 - $180 = $45, an increase of $35.

visuals.caption: Cost-output relationship of a profit-maximising price taker in the short run

questions.postVisualStem: The price taker currently produces 3 units of output. If the price of its product increases by $10, the profit of the firm will

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning and give examples of each type of integration
questions.stem: A luxury watch exporter opens a factory to produce luxury watches for export using its own brand name. This is an example of ______________ that has an advantage of ______________.

choices.text: forward expansion ... enjoying economies of scale
forward expansion ... spreading risk through diversification
backward expansion ... ensuring a reliable supply of input
backward expansion ... reducing the number of competitors

questions.explanation: By establishing a factory to produce the watches it exports, the exporter expands backward towards production. Controlling that stage helps ensure a reliable supply of the product or input needed for its export business.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The following table shows the input-output relationship of a price taker.
questions.explanation: With X = 800, marginal product can rise initially and then fall from 500 units for the fourth worker to 400 units for the fifth worker, so diminishing marginal returns can occur. Each other value would require marginal product to rise again after it has already fallen.

visuals.caption: Input-output relationship of a price taker

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the firm encounters diminishing marginal returns. Which of the following is a possible value of X?

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Mrs. Chan formed a partnership with Mr. Wong two years ago. Mr. Wong withdraws from the partnership recently so that Mrs. Chan becomes a sole proprietor. As a result,

choices.text: the liability of the firm becomes limited.
the profits tax rate paid is lower.
the firm is no longer a legal entity.

questions.explanation: A sole proprietorship and a partnership both have unlimited liability and are not separate legal entities. A sole proprietor can make decisions without consulting a partner, so decision-making can be quicker.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: The following table shows the production information of a firm in different periods.

choices.text: The firm increases the amount of overtime allowance so that each worker works longer hours.
The firm changes the wage payment method from piece rate to time rate.
The firm employs more unskilled workers.
The firm replaces some old machines with newer ones.

questions.explanation: Labour productivity rises from 4,000 / 1,500 to 5,000 / 1,800 units per working hour. Replacing old machines with newer ones can make each worker more productive; the other changes do not explain the increase.

visuals.caption: Production information of a firm in different periods

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following is a possible reason for the difference between the labour productivity of Year 1 and Year 2?

questions.keyPoint: Meaning and examples of the three types of production; identify the type of production
questions.stem: Tim is an accounting officer in a garment factory. He engages in
questions.explanation: The garment factory's activity is manufacturing, which is secondary production. Tim's accounting work supports that manufacturing activity within the firm, so it is classified as secondary production in this context.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: When the government imposes an effective quota on imported rice,

choices.text: the average quality of imported rice will increase.
the average price of imported rice will decrease.
the consumer surplus of the imported rice market will increase.
the consumer surplus of the local rice market will decrease.

questions.explanation: An effective import quota restricts the quantity available. With the quantity constrained, importers have an incentive to improve quality to compete for buyers. The quota does not lower the imported-rice price or raise its consumer surplus, and its effect on the local rice market cannot be concluded without further information.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Lorenz curve
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the Lorenz curves of Country X in 2013 and 2015.
questions.explanation: The 2015 Lorenz curve is closer to the line of equality, so income distribution is more equal and the Gini coefficient is lower. A Lorenz curve gives income shares rather than absolute income, so it cannot show that the bottom 60% households' total income increased.

visuals.alt: Lorenz curves of Country X in 2013 and 2015, showing the 2015 curve closer to the line of equality.
visuals.caption: Lorenz curves of Country X in 2013 and 2015

curves: The dashed 2015 Lorenz curve lies closer to the line of equality than the dotted 2013 curve.
movements: The 2015 income distribution is more equal than the 2013 distribution.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Statements (1) and (3) follow: income distribution becomes more equal and the Gini coefficient decreases. The graph alone does not establish a change in the bottom 60% households' total income.

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about Country X between 2013 and 2015 are CORRECT?

(1) Income distribution becomes more equal.
(2) The total income of the bottom 60% of the households increases.
(3) Gini coefficient decreases.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: The supply of milk will become more elastic when

choices.text: more people drink milk for good health.
the market price of milk falls.
more food products contain milk as an ingredient.

questions.explanation: With more dairy farmers, the industry can adjust output more easily when price changes, making market supply more elastic. The other changes affect demand or the current market price rather than the responsiveness of supply.

questions.topicGroup: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.keyPoint: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.stem: The following shows some recent activities of a firm. Which one should be included in the calculation of gross domestic product (GDP) of the current year?

choices.text: issued $100,000,000 worth of bonds to the public this year
bought a second-hand machine worth $500,000 this year
sold $100,000 worth of goods this year but are produced last year
produced $200,000 worth of goods this year but are unsold

questions.explanation: GDP includes current production, whether it is sold immediately or added to inventories. Bond issues and second-hand purchases are financial or resale transactions, while goods produced last year were already counted in last year's GDP.

questions.keyPoint: Growth rate of GDP
questions.stem: Study the following table carefully.

choices.text: The purchasing power of money decreased in 2014.
The per capita real GDP increased in 2014.
The per capita nominal GDP decreased in 2014.

questions.explanation: In 2014, real GDP grew by 4% while population grew by 3%, so per capita real GDP increased by about 1%. Real GDP did not decrease. The table does not establish the purchasing power of money, and per capita nominal GDP also increased because nominal GDP growth exceeded population growth.

visuals.caption: Year-on-year changes in GDP and population
columns: Year-on-year percentage change in nominal GDP
Year-on-year percentage change in real GDP

questions.postVisualStem: Base on the table above, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: In calculating Hong Kong's GNP, which of the following items should be included?

choices.text: the yearly rental income received by a Canadian investor from the apartment he owns in Hong Kong
the prize received by a Hong Kong resident from the Mark Six lottery
the salary of a Hong Kong resident working in the branch office of Hang Seng Bank in Mainland China for three months
the money received by a Hong Kong resident from selling shares in the stock market of Hong Kong

questions.explanation: GNP includes income earned by Hong Kong residents from production, wherever it takes place. The Hong Kong resident's salary earned in Mainland China is included. The other items are foreign-resident income earned in Hong Kong, a transfer payment, or a financial transaction.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.stem:
The price of crude oil has been falling sharply recently. Which of the following will increase in the short run?

(1) price level
(2) real GDP
(3) aggregate demand
(4) short run aggregate supply
questions.explanation: Lower crude-oil prices reduce firms' production costs, shifting SRAS right. In the short run, real GDP rises and the price level falls; aggregate demand does not shift merely because production costs fall.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.stem: Which of the following will most likely lead to an increase in the potential output level of an economy?

choices.text: an increase in the birth rate
an increase in the inflation rate
an increase in the interest rate

questions.explanation: A higher birth rate enlarges the future labour force and can raise an economy's productive capacity. Net exports affect aggregate demand, while changes in inflation or interest rates do not by themselves raise potential output.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Inflationary gap
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram. The economy is currently at E0.

choices.text: There is an excess demand for labour.
In the long run, the quantity of output will be at Y0.
In the long run, the price level will be lower than P0.

questions.explanation: At E0, output Y0 is above LRAS potential output Y1, so the economy has an inflationary gap and excess demand for labour. In the long run, output returns to Y1 and the price level rises rather than falls.

visuals.alt: AD-AS diagram with short-run equilibrium E0 to the right of LRAS at output Y0, while potential output is Y1.
visuals.caption: AD-AS diagram with an inflationary gap

curves: LRAS is vertical at Y1.
AD slopes down and SRAS slopes up, intersecting at E0.
movements: Short-run output Y0 exceeds potential output Y1, creating an inflationary gap.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: At output above potential, there is excess demand for labour. In the long run output returns to Y1 and the price level rises above P0.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the economy is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: How central bank functions are carried out in
questions.stem:
In Hong Kong, which of the following are the functions of a central bank performed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority?

(1) managing foreign exchange reserves
(2) acting as the lender of last resort
(3) issuing one-thousand-dollar notes
questions.explanation: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority manages the Exchange Fund's foreign exchange reserves and serves as lender of last resort. Hong Kong banknotes, including $1,000 notes, are issued by note-issuing banks rather than directly by the HKMA.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual banking multipliers
questions.stem: The following table is the balance sheet of a banking system.

choices.text: The maximum amount of loans is $6,000.

questions.explanation: Deposits rise from $5,000 to $10,000 while total reserves remain $2,000, so the required reserve ratio is 2,000 / 10,000 = 20%. The maximum banking multiplier is therefore 1 / 0.2 = 5.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.postVisualStem: If all banks lend out their excess reserves and there is no cash leakage, the amount of deposits will be doubled. Which of the following statements about the banking system is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate
questions.stem: Which of the following will lead to a decrease in the nominal interest rate?

choices.text: People expect deflation to occur soon.
The risk of holding bonds increases.

questions.explanation: Nominal interest rate equals real interest rate plus expected inflation. Expected deflation lowers expected inflation, reducing the nominal interest rate. The other changes reduce money supply or raise the risk premium and tend to raise interest rates.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem: Country X enters a war with another country. Its government keeps printing more money to support military expenses. Which of the following functions of money performed by Country X's currency would be affected?
questions.explanation: Persistent money creation can cause inflation and erode the purchasing power of currency, impairing its function as a store of value.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem:
Margaret withdraws HK$2,000,000 from her savings deposit with a licensed bank. Then she deposits HK$900,000 as a time deposit with the same bank and $1,000,000 as a time deposit with a restricted licence bank. She keeps the remaining in a safe at home.

What will be the immediate effect of the above actions on the money supply of Hong Kong?

choices.text: M1 will remain unchanged and M2 will decrease by HK$1,000,000.
M1 will increase by HK$100,000 and M2 will increase by HK$1,000,000.
M1 will increase by HK$100,000 and M3 will remain unchanged.
Both M2 and M3 will decrease by HK$1,000,000.

questions.explanation: The HK$100,000 held as cash raises M1. The time deposit at the licensed bank remains in M2, while the time deposit at the restricted licence bank is included in M3 but not M2. Thus M3 is unchanged overall.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: Which of the following policies can raise GDP and improve the budget deficit at the same time?

choices.text: subsidising production of local infant industries
increasing the tariff on imported goods
imposing quota limits on imported goods

questions.explanation: A higher tariff raises government revenue and can divert spending towards domestic production, raising GDP while improving the budget balance. A subsidy worsens the deficit, while a profits-tax rise or quota does not provide the same direct combination.

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the change in the salaries tax system of an economy.
questions.explanation: The old system has tax payment directly proportional to income. The new system has a tax-free threshold, so its average tax rate rises with income.

visuals.alt: Tax-payment graph showing old and new salaries tax systems.
visuals.caption: Old and new salaries tax systems

curves: The old line begins at the origin.
The new line begins after a tax-free threshold.
movements: The new system makes the average tax rate rise with income.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The old system is proportional; the new system is progressive.

questions.postVisualStem: The old salaries tax system is a ______________ and the new salaries tax system is a ______________.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Transaction equation and velocity of circulation (V)
questions.stem: The following table shows the data of an economy.

choices.text: The general price level increased by 20%.
The general price level did not change.

questions.explanation: Nominal GDP and real GDP both rose by 20%. Since nominal GDP equals price level times real GDP, the general price level did not change.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the economy between 2010 and 2014 is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: In the long run, which of the following government policies will only cause an increase in the general price level without raising the real output of an economy?

choices.text: selling government bonds to the public

questions.explanation: Lowering the required reserve ratio is expansionary monetary policy. In the long run real output returns to potential output, leaving a higher general price level.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.explanation: The labour force is 4,000 / 0.08 = 50,000. Underemployment is 5% of the labour force, so the underemployed population is 2,500.
questions.postVisualStem: According to the above data,

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: If the inflation rate is positive but lower than the level people expected,

choices.text: the purchasing power of money will increase.
people will hold more monetary assets and fewer real assets.
people earning fixed income will gain.

questions.explanation: Actual inflation below expected inflation benefits creditors such as bank depositors because repayments have a higher-than-expected real value. Positive inflation still lowers money's purchasing power.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: The table below shows the outputs of Country A and Country B per unit of resources.

choices.text: 1 unit of machines = 0.9 units of shoes
1 unit of machines = 1 unit of shoes
1 unit of machines = 1.1 units of shoes
1 unit of machines = 1.2 units of shoes

questions.explanation: Country A's opportunity cost of one machine is 20/24 shoes, while Country B's is 10/8 shoes. After the 0.3-shoe transport cost, 1.2 shoes per machine lies within the mutually beneficial range.
questions.postVisualStem: The country exporting machines needs to pay 0.3 units of shoes per unit of export as transport cost. Which of the following is a mutually beneficial terms of trade for the two countries?

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem:
When two countries trade with each other, which of the following affect the countries' gains from trade?

(1) a change in production combination of the two countries under autarky
(2) a change in factor endowments of the two countries
(3) a change in resources required per unit of output
(4) a change in transaction costs
questions.explanation: Gains from trade depend on comparative costs and transaction costs. Changes in resources required per unit of output or transaction costs affect them; a production combination under autarky and factor endowments alone do not necessarily do so.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of a quota on domestic price, domestic consumption, domestic production and import quantity for a small open economy
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the market of a good in a small open economy. Sq is the supply curve with an import quota imposed on the good. Pw is the world price of the good and Pq is the price with quota.

choices.text: Domestic production will increase from Q1 to Q2.
There will be an excess demand for the good.
The total revenue of local producers will increase by Pq x (Q2 - Q1).
Consumer surplus may increase or decrease.

questions.explanation: The quota raises the domestic price to Pq and domestic producers expand output from Q1 to Q2. The market clears with restricted imports; the change in producer revenue is not just Pq times the additional output, and consumer surplus falls.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram of a small open economy with world price Pw and higher quota price Pq.
visuals.caption: Import quota in a small open economy

curves: S is domestic supply without quota.
Sq represents supply with the import quota.
movements: The quota raises price from Pw to Pq and domestic production from Q1 to Q2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Domestic production rises from Q1 to Q2 after the quota.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the situation after imposing the import quota on the good is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT included in the calculation of Hong Kong's current account balance?

choices.text: A Hong Kong resident buys an air ticket to Taiwan from a Hong Kong airline.
A Hong Kong resident buys a travel insurance policy from a Japanese insurance company.
A Japanese resident rents a house in Hong Kong.
A Japanese resident donates a sum of money to a charity fund in Hong Kong.

questions.explanation: A transaction between a Hong Kong resident and a Hong Kong airline is domestic and does not enter the current account. The other options are cross-border services, income or current transfers.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.keyPoint: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.stem:
Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong,

(1) the market exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar relative to the US dollar may be higher or lower than US$1 to HK$7.8.
(2) when the US dollar appreciates against Renminbi, the Hong Kong dollar also appreciates against Renminbi.
(3) when the US dollar appreciates against the Japanese yen, the number of Japanese visiting Hong Kong will increase.
questions.explanation: The market rate can move around the linked rate within the Convertibility Zone. The Hong Kong dollar moves with the US dollar against other currencies. A stronger US/Hong Kong dollar makes Hong Kong relatively more expensive for Japanese visitors, so statement (3) is false.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which of the following cases CANNOT be illustrated by the law of demand?

choices.text: When the government imposes a heavier penalty on drug abuse, fewer people take drugs.
When an additional lump-sum first registration tax is imposed on imported cars, the average quality of imported cars improves.
When an ad valorem tax is levied on wine, people buy relatively more high-quality wine than low-quality wine.
The price of second-hand residential properties drops when the supply of first-hand residential properties increases.

questions.explanation: An ad valorem tax raises the prices of high-quality and low-quality wine by the same percentage, so their relative price is unchanged. It therefore cannot explain a switch towards high-quality wine using the law of demand. The other cases can be explained by a rise in full price, a change in relative price, or a change in the price of a substitute.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem:
Currently, Hong Kong's construction industry is facing the problem of labour shortage. This implies that

(1) the prevailing wage rate of the construction workers is below the equilibrium level.
(2) the existing Statutory Minimum Wage is ineffective.
(3) there is non-price competition for employing construction workers.
questions.explanation: A shortage means quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the prevailing wage, so the wage is below equilibrium and employers may compete through non-wage benefits. It does not establish that the statutory minimum wage is ineffective; that policy need not be the cause of the shortage.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is the demand-supply diagram of the traditional airline services market. E0 is the original equilibrium point.
questions.explanation: Travelling with low-cost airlines lowers demand for traditional airline services, shifting demand from D0 to D1. Cheaper fuel lowers cost and increases supply from S0 to S2. The new equilibrium is E4.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram of the traditional airline-services market, with supply curves S0 to S2, demand curves D0 to D2 and equilibria E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Traditional airline-services market

movements: A trend towards low-cost airlines decreases demand for traditional airline services, shifting demand from D0 to D1.
A fall in fuel price lowers production cost, increasing supply from S0 to S2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The new equilibrium is E4, the intersection of S2 and D1.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose there is a trend of travelling with low-cost airlines and at the same time the price of fuel decreases. The new equilibrium point in the diagram will be ________.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: When the price of good X decreases, both the price and quantity transacted of good Y decrease. It is most likely that good X and good Y are ______________ respectively.
questions.explanation: A lower price of butter increases demand for butter and decreases demand for margarine, its substitute. The leftward shift in the demand curve for margarine lowers both its equilibrium price and quantity transacted.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem: Depreciation of the Japanese yen causes the price of imported Japanese food to fall. In which of the following situations will the imported Japanese food sellers' total revenue fall?

choices.text: The demand for imported Japanese food is elastic.
The demand for imported Japanese food is inelastic.
The supply of imported Japanese food is elastic.
The supply of imported Japanese food is inelastic.

questions.explanation: When demand is inelastic, the percentage increase in quantity demanded is smaller than the percentage fall in price. Therefore price times quantity, or total revenue, falls. The elasticity of supply does not determine this direct total-revenue effect.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: The table below shows the demand and supply schedules for good X without any market intervention.

choices.text: the quantity transacted will rise by 200 units.
the market price will drop by $4.
the quality of good X will improve.
the total expenditure on good X will increase by $800.

questions.explanation: With an effective quota of 300 units, price is $16 and total expenditure is $4,800. Raising the quota to 500 makes it ineffective because the free-market equilibrium is 400 units at $14. Quantity transacted rises by 100 units and total expenditure becomes $5,600, an increase of $800.

visuals.caption: Demand and supply schedules for good X without market intervention

questions.postVisualStem: If the government raises the quota from 300 units to 500 units,

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem:
Suppose Country A imposes an effective price floor on imported good X. We can conclude that

(1) the total revenue received by domestic producers of good X will increase.
(2) the import volume of good X will decrease.
(3) total expenditure on imported good X will increase if the demand for imported good X is inelastic.
questions.explanation: An effective price floor raises the domestic price. Domestic output and domestic producers' total revenue rise, while domestic consumption falls and so imports fall. For imported good X, the higher price raises total expenditure when its demand is inelastic.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem:
Suppose the government raises the per-unit tax on good X by $30. As a result, its market price increases from $40 to $50 and the quantity transacted changes by 10%. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The demand for good X is inelastic.
(2) The demand for good X is more elastic than its supply.
(3) Total revenue (net of tax) of the producers of good X will decrease.
questions.explanation: The consumer price rises by 25% while quantity changes by 10%, so demand is inelastic. Consumers bear $10 and producers bear the remaining $20 of the higher tax; the side bearing more tax is less elastic, so supply is less elastic than demand. Producers receive a lower net price and sell fewer units, so their net total revenue falls.

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the market structure of commercial banks in Hong Kong?

choices.text: The services they provide are homogeneous.
There is imperfect information about their services.
The market is dominated by a few sellers.

questions.explanation: Commercial banks provide differentiated services and compete through interest rates, service quality and other non-price methods. The market has several dominant banks and imperfect information, so homogeneous services are not a feature.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram of good X in a perfectly competitive market. A price ceiling is set at Pc.

choices.text: The total revenue of good X will increase.
The consumer surplus will remain unchanged.

questions.explanation: The ceiling remains binding. Supply at Pc does not change, so the quantity transacted, producers' total revenue and producer surplus do not increase. The rise in demand enlarges the shortage and increases the deadweight loss; consumer surplus changes rather than remaining unchanged.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram for a perfectly competitive market with demand D, supply S and a binding price ceiling Pc below equilibrium.
visuals.caption: Market with a price ceiling

movements: An increase in demand shifts the demand curve rightward while the price ceiling remains binding.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: At Pc, quantity supplied and producers' total revenue stay unchanged. A larger shortage raises the deadweight loss, while consumer surplus does not remain unchanged.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the demand for good X increases. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about scarcity is/are CORRECT?

(1) When there is no scarcity, there will be no market price.
(2) A good is scarce if the quantity of it available is small.
(3) When there is a shortage, there must be scarcity.
questions.explanation: Without scarcity, no opportunity cost has to be paid and a market price cannot arise. A small available quantity does not by itself prove scarcity, because scarcity depends on wants relative to supply. A shortage is an excess demand at a price and can occur only for an economic good, so it implies scarcity.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Kathy is the owner of a seafood retail shop. She is going to close the shop for 10 days and go on a trip to Japan with her family. In which of the following situations will the cost of closing the shop increase?

choices.text: The attraction that Kathy wants to visit is closed for maintenance.
The flight departing Hong Kong is delayed for an hour.

questions.explanation: The cost of closing the shop is the value of the best forgone alternative. Higher seafood demand raises the profit Kathy gives up by not operating the shop. The attraction closing and the flight delay affect the trip itself, but do not raise the opportunity cost of closing the business.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
In June 2015, the Hong Kong Housing Authority's Subsidised Housing Committee approved the adjustment of income and asset limits for the Interim Scheme of Extending the Home Ownership Scheme (HOS) Secondary Market to White Form Buyers applicants. The income and assets limits were raised to $48,000 and $1.6 million respectively.

The above case is related to the ______________ question(s) in economics.

(1) 'what to produce'
(2) 'how to produce'
(3) 'for whom to produce'
questions.explanation: The policy changes the eligibility criteria for access to subsidised housing. It determines who can receive the housing, so it concerns the 'for whom to produce' problem rather than what or how to produce.

questions.keyPoint: Classification of private firms: sole proprietorship, partnership, private limited company and public limited company
questions.stem: Mr. Wong and Mr. Chan have changed the type of business ownership of their firm. They are now subject to limited liability. However, ownership of the firm can still only be transferred with the consent of the other owner. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: There is a greater risk of the firm being taken over.
The firm has turned from a partnership to a public limited company.
The firm now has to disclose its accounting information to the public.
The firm now has separate legal status.

questions.explanation: Limited liability together with restricted transfer of ownership identifies a private limited company. A private limited company has separate legal status, need not disclose its accounts publicly, and is less exposed to takeover because shares cannot be freely transferred.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem:
Many Korean restaurants play K-POP music. The music is

(1) a free good.
(2) a capital good.
(3) a private good.
(4) a public good.
questions.explanation: The music is used by the restaurant in supplying its dining service, so it is a capital good. Listening by one diner does not reduce other diners' enjoyment, and the music is jointly consumed in the restaurant, so it is a public good. It is not a free good because providing it involves opportunity cost.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem:
A government subsidises firms to increase job vacancies for persons with disabilities and provide training and support for them. As a result,

(1) occupational mobility of labour will increase.
(2) the supply of labour will increase.
(3) there will be a greater degree of division of labour.
questions.explanation: Training and support improve workers' ability to move between occupations. The policy also draws more persons with disabilities into employment, increasing labour supply. It does not necessarily create a greater degree of division of labour.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about the waiters in restaurant A and restaurant B.

choices.text: Restaurant A's cost of monitoring service quality is higher.
Waiters of restaurant A earn a more stable income.
Restaurant B's cost of calculating wages is lower.
Waiters of restaurant B tend to provide better service.

questions.explanation: Restaurant A uses a time-rate payment, while Restaurant B combines a lower time rate with tips. Tips give Restaurant B's waiters an incentive to provide better service, but make their income less stable and make wage calculation more complicated, not less costly. Time-rate pay also requires Restaurant A to monitor service quality more closely.

visuals.caption: Information about waiters in restaurant A and restaurant B

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

questions.topicGroup: Understand the definition of the short run and the long run
questions.keyPoint: Understand the definition of the short run and the long run
questions.stem: The table below shows the production information of a firm with two inputs, labour and machines.
questions.explanation: Average cost rises from $2 to $6 as output increases. Machines remain fixed while labour changes, so the firm is in the short run. Marginal product eventually falls as another worker is added, so diminishing marginal returns apply. Diseconomies of scale concern the long run and cannot be concluded here.
questions.postVisualStem:
From the above information, we can conclude that

(1) The average cost is increasing.
(2) The firm suffers from diseconomies of scale.
(3) The firm is operating in the short run.
(4) The law of diminishing marginal returns applies to the firm.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the production information of a price-taking firm. There is a fixed cost of $2.
questions.explanation: At 3 units, variable cost is $44 - $2 = $42, so average variable cost is $14. Marginal cost of the third unit is $44 - $28 = $16; a price-taking firm's profit-maximising output is where price equals marginal cost, so price is $16. Revenue is $48 and total cost is $44, giving profit of $4.

visuals.caption: Production information of a price-taking firm

questions.postVisualStem:
