choices.text: the amount of dividend received by a U.S. resident distributed by a listed company in Hong Kong
the amount of money a U.S. resident received from selling shares of a listed company in Hong Kong
the amount of rent received by a Hong Kong resident from a house located in the U.S.
the amount of money a Hong Kong resident used to purchase a house in the mainland of China

questions.explanation: GNP equals GDP plus net factor income from abroad. Dividends paid from Hong Kong production to a U.S. resident are factor income paid abroad and must be deducted. Income received by a Hong Kong resident abroad is added, while share transactions and overseas asset purchases are not relevant factor income in GDP.

questions.keyPoint: Production/value added approach
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the production chain of a good in economy X.
questions.explanation: The local farm adds $200. The local manufacturer adds $850 - $200 = $650. Local retailers add $1,420 - $630 = $790 at market prices, but $100 is tax, so their factor-cost value added is $690. Total GDP at factor cost is $200 + $650 + $690 = $1,540.

visuals.alt: Production chain from a local farm to a local manufacturer and local retailers, with sales to foreign retailers, foreign consumers and local consumers.
visuals.caption: Production chain in economy X

movements: The local farm sells raw materials to the local manufacturer for $200.
The manufacturer sells $630 to local retailers and $220 to foreign retailers.
Local retailers sell $770 to foreign consumers and $650 to local consumers, including $100 tax.

questions.postVisualStem: What is the contribution of the production chain to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at factor cost of economy X?

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Measurements of the general price level
questions.keyPoint: Calculate/Determine the rate of change in the general price level (inflation/ deflation rate) by using the CPI and the implicit price deflator of GDP
questions.stem:
The Composite Consumer Price Index for July 2017 was 104.7, which was 2% higher than that of July 2016. This implies that

(1) the price of clothing had increased.
(2) the GDP deflator had increased by the same percentage.
(3) the general price level had increased.
questions.explanation: A higher composite CPI shows that the general price level, measured by this consumer basket, has risen. It does not prove that every component such as clothing rose, and the GDP deflator covers a different basket and need not change by the same percentage.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate
questions.stem:
The nominal interest rate is 8% and the expected inflation rate is 3%. If the actual inflation rate turns out to be higher than expected,

(1) the actual inflation rate is smaller than the nominal interest rate.
(2) the nominal interest rate is greater than the actual real interest rate.
(3) the expected real interest rate is greater than the actual real interest rate.
questions.explanation: The official answer key marks D. Under the paper's intended reading, actual inflation is above the expected 3% but below the 8% nominal rate. Nominal interest then exceeds actual real interest, and expected real interest (8% - 3%) is greater than actual real interest because actual inflation is higher than expected.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: An increase in the basic allowance of the salaries tax affects the _______ in GDP and results in a _______ shift of the aggregate demand curve.
questions.explanation: A larger salaries-tax allowance raises disposable income, which raises private consumption expenditure. Consumption is a component of aggregate demand, so the AD curve shifts rightward.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Features of the four phases of a business cycle
questions.stem: The diagram below shows a business cycle.

choices.text: There are more and more inventories remain unsold.
The government budget runs into a deficit.
The sales revenue of retailers is decreasing.
The number of applicants for unemployment benefits is increasing.

questions.explanation: At X, real-GDP growth is slowing below its average rate. Unsold inventories can build up, retailer sales can fall and unemployment-benefit applications can rise. A government budget deficit is least directly implied by this position on the cycle.

visuals.alt: Business-cycle curve for percentage change in real GDP over time, crossing a dashed average-growth-rate line and marked at point X on a downward movement.
visuals.caption: Business cycle

curves: The business-cycle curve rises above and falls below the average growth rate.
movements: At X, growth is slowing and lies below the average growth rate, while still above zero.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Unsold inventories, falling retailer sales and rising unemployment-benefit applications fit a downturn; a government budget deficit is least directly implied.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following phenomena is LEAST likely to be observed at point X?

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Deflationary gap
questions.stem: The existence of a deflationary gap indicates that

choices.text: the general price level is decreasing continuously.
the real GDP is smaller than the nominal GDP.
the short-run equilibrium output level falls below the full-employment output level.
there is a gap between the expected inflation rate and the actual inflation rate.

questions.explanation: A deflationary gap occurs when short-run equilibrium output is below full-employment output. It does not require a continuously falling price level, and it is unrelated to the usual difference between nominal and real GDP or between expected and actual inflation.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand (AD) curves, short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curves and long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve of an economy. Suppose initially the economy operates at E0.

choices.text: expansionary ... AD0 will shift to AD1
expansionary ... SRAS0 will shift to SRAS1
contractionary ... AD0 will shift to AD1
contractionary ... SRAS0 will shift to SRAS1

questions.explanation: E0 lies to the right of LRAS0, so the economy has an inflationary gap. A contractionary monetary policy reduces aggregate demand and shifts it left from AD0 to AD1, restoring the long-run equilibrium.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with AD0, AD1, SRAS0, SRAS1, vertical LRAS0 and initial equilibrium E0 to the right of LRAS0.
visuals.caption: Restoring long-run equilibrium with monetary policy

curves: AD0 and AD1 slope downward.
SRAS0 and SRAS1 slope upward.
LRAS0 is vertical.
movements: E0 lies to the right of LRAS0, indicating an inflationary gap.
A contractionary monetary policy shifts AD left from AD0 to AD1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option C restores long-run equilibrium through a leftward AD shift.

questions.postVisualStem: If the government restores the long run equilibrium by a/an ____________ monetary policy, _______________.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem: The inflation rate of Venezuela in 2016 was 720% and some people in Venezuela keep their wealth as electronic money, such as Bitcoin. In this case, Bitcoin performs the function of a ______________ because ______________.

choices.text: medium of exchange ... Bitcoin can be used to purchase goods and services
store of value ... the purchasing power of wealth was preserved in the form of Bitcoin
unit of account ... the price of goods and services can be expressed in terms of Bitcoin
standard of deferred payment ... Bitcoin can be used for future payment

questions.explanation: With very high inflation, people keep wealth in Bitcoin to preserve its purchasing power. This is the store-of-value function of money; the question is not about using Bitcoin in a transaction, quoting prices or settling a future debt.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem:
Hong Kong legal tender held by licensed banks is included in the _________________.

(1) monetary base
(2) money supply M1
(3) money supply M2
questions.explanation: Legal tender held by licensed banks forms part of the monetary base. It is not money held by the non-bank public, so it is not included in M1 or M2.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Refer to the following balance sheet of a banking system. The excess reserves of the banking system is $200 million.
questions.explanation: Required reserves are $2,000 million - $200 million = $1,800 million, so the required reserve ratio is 20% of the initial $9,000 million deposits. Buying $500 million of bonds leaves $1,500 million reserves. Once fully loaned up, maximum deposits are $1,500 million / 20% = $7,500 million.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government sells $500 million worth of bonds to the commercial banks. What will be the maximum amount of deposits if the banking system is fully loaned up?

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: The quantity theory of money implies that

choices.text: the real output level remains unchanged.
the velocity of circulation of money is equal to one.
an increase in money supply will lead to a rise in the price level by a larger proportion when the real output decreases.
a rise in nominal output will lead to an increase in money supply by the same proportion.

questions.explanation: The quantity theory uses MV = PY. For a given velocity, if money supply rises while real output falls, the price level must rise by a proportion greater than the money-supply increase. It does not require real output to be unchanged, velocity to equal one, or money supply to respond mechanically to nominal output.

questions.keyPoint: Direct tax and indirect tax
questions.stem: Which of the following is the difference between a direct tax and an indirect tax?

choices.text: The imposition of an indirect tax will result in a more even income distribution than a direct tax.
The tax revenue of a direct tax is higher than that of an indirect tax.
The tax base of a direct tax is wider than that of an indirect tax.
The tax burden of a direct tax cannot be shifted while the tax burden of an indirect tax can be shifted.

questions.explanation: A direct tax is imposed on the person intended to bear it and its burden cannot normally be shifted. An indirect tax is imposed on goods or services and may be passed on through a higher price. Income-distribution effects, revenue and tax-base width are not general distinctions.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem:
When the government increases unemployment benefits, which of the following are likely to increase?

(1) aggregate demand
(2) general price level
(3) unemployment rate
questions.explanation: Higher unemployment benefits are expansionary fiscal policy: transfer recipients have more disposable income, so aggregate demand and, other things equal, the general price level increase. More generous benefits can also reduce the incentive to take up employment, making the unemployment rate likely to increase. The official key therefore marks all three statements.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of fiscal policy
questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a contractionary fiscal policy?

choices.text: A private company reduces its investment expenditure in Hong Kong.
The government increases its expenditure on infrastructure.
A commercial bank decides to hold more excess reserves.
The government increases the progressivity of income tax.

questions.explanation: Contractionary fiscal policy uses government taxation or expenditure to reduce aggregate demand. Increasing the progressivity of income tax reduces disposable income for higher-income earners. The other options describe a private investment decision, expansionary government spending and a banking decision rather than contractionary fiscal policy.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Deflationary gap
questions.stem: Which of the following measures used to eliminate a deflationary (output) gap is LEAST likely to result in inflation?

choices.text: The central bank lowers the required reserve ratio.
The government increases its expenditure on social welfare.
The government increases its subsidies to private firms.
The central bank buys government bonds from the public.

questions.explanation: Lowering the required reserve ratio, increasing welfare spending and buying government bonds are expansionary measures that raise aggregate demand and can push up the price level. A subsidy to private firms can raise short-run aggregate supply, increasing output while putting downward pressure on prices, so it is least likely to cause inflation.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: Country A and Country B produce good X and good Y only. Country A has a comparative advantage in producing good X. Which of the following statements about Country A is CORRECT?

choices.text: Country A uses fewer resources to produce 1 unit of good X than Country B.
Country A has an absolute advantage in producing good X.
Country A has a comparative disadvantage in producing good Y.
Country A owns more resources than Country B.

questions.explanation: With two countries and two goods, if Country A has a comparative advantage in X, its opportunity cost of X is lower and its opportunity cost of Y is higher than Country B's. Country A therefore has a comparative disadvantage in Y. Comparative advantage does not imply an absolute advantage, a particular resource quantity or lower resource use per unit.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: The following table shows the amount of good X or good Y that Country A and Country B can produce with the same amount of resources.

choices.text: Country B enjoys both absolute advantage and comparative advantage in producing good Y.
Country A would gain from importing good X if 1 unit of good Y can be exchanged for more than 0.25 units of good X.
If the transportation cost per unit of good X traded is greater than 0.167 units of good Y, there will be no trade between Country A and Country B.
The gain from trade of Country B from exporting 1 unit of good X is 1.6 units of good Y.

questions.explanation: Country A's opportunity cost of 1 unit of X is 4 units of Y, while Country B's is 2.4 units of Y. Country A gains by importing X whenever 1 unit of Y buys more than 0.25 units of X, because that is cheaper than producing X itself. Country B has comparative advantage in X, not Y, and the other statements do not follow from the production possibilities.

visuals.caption: Output with the same amount of resources

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT included in the calculation of the balance of Hong Kong's current account?

choices.text: a Hong Kong resident receives interest from deposits in an overseas bank
a Hong Kong resident borrows a bank loan from an overseas bank
a Hong Kong resident donates food and water to Macau residents after a typhoon hits Macau
a Hong Kong resident receives wages from working in an overseas branch of a local bank

questions.explanation: Interest and wages received from abroad are income-account items, while donations of goods are current transfers. Borrowing from an overseas bank is a financial-account transaction, so it is not included in the current account.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Balance of payments and balance of the BOP account
questions.keyPoint: The balance of payments is always balanced in the accounting sense
questions.stem: The table below shows the items of the balance of payments of Country A in a certain year.
questions.explanation: The current account is 15 - 22 + 22 - 12 - 6 + 10 = $7 million. The capital and financial account has a $17 million credit balance, so the $24 million debit entry for reserve assets makes total credits and debits both $80 million. The account is balanced in the accounting sense; reserve accumulation offsets a surplus rather than a deficit.

visuals.caption: Balance of payments of Country A

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The current account balance is $7 million.
(2) The balance of payments account is in balance.
(3) There is a balance of payments deficit of $24 million.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of trade surplus and deficit
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the percentage change in the

choices.text: the value of total imports has increased.
the visible trade balance has improved.
the value of imports of services has increased.
the current account balance has improved.

questions.explanation: The total-import line remains above zero, so the value of total imports increased in each year. A chart of percentage changes in total imports and exports cannot establish a change in the visible trade balance, imports of services or the current account balance.

visuals.alt: Line chart of percentage changes in total exports and total imports from 2015 to 2017. The total-export line stays above zero and ends above the total-import line, while the total-import line stays above zero and slopes down after 2015.
visuals.caption: Percentage changes in total exports and total imports

curves: Total exports rises from 2015 to a peak in 2016, then falls while remaining above zero in 2017.
Total imports decreases from 2015 to 2016, then declines slightly further while remaining above zero in 2017.
movements: The total-export and total-import percentage-change lines cross between 2015 and 2016.
Both series show positive percentage changes in every year shown.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Because the total-import percentage change is positive throughout, the value of total imports has increased from 2015 to 2017. The chart alone does not determine the trade balance, services imports or the current-account balance.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: If the government of a small country abolishes the tariff imposed on an imported good,

choices.text: the world price of the good will decrease.
the total expenditure of consumers on the good will increase.
the total revenue of domestic producers of the good will decrease.
the domestic consumption of the good will decrease.

questions.explanation: A small country cannot affect the world price. Removing a tariff lowers the domestic price, which expands domestic consumption but reduces the quantity supplied and price received by domestic producers. Their total revenue therefore decreases; consumers' total expenditure is not known without demand elasticity.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem:
Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, when the US dollar depreciates against the Japanese Yen,

(1) the aggregate demand of Hong Kong will increase.
(2) the employment of Hong Kong will increase.
(3) total import value from Japan (in terms of Hong Kong dollar) will decrease.
questions.explanation: Because the Hong Kong dollar is linked to the US dollar, it also depreciates against the yen. Hong Kong exports become cheaper to Japanese buyers, so net exports, aggregate demand and employment tend to rise. Japanese imports become more expensive in Hong Kong dollars, so statement (3) is not correct.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: Refer to the following table.

choices.text: Factory A has a higher degree of division of labour.
Factory A pay its workers at piece rate while factory B pays at time rate.
Factory B provides more training for its workers than factory A.
Factory B uses fewer machines than factory A.

questions.explanation: Factory A produces 10,000 units in 200 hours while Factory B produces 12,000 units in 180 hours, so Factory B has higher labour productivity. More training for Factory B can explain that difference. The other statements would tend to make Factory A more productive or Factory B less productive.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following is a possible reason for the difference between the labour productivity of factory A and factory B?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Maximisation of total social surplus: marginal benefit equals marginal cost
questions.stem: Efficiency is attained when

choices.text: the marginal social benefit is equal to marginal social cost.
total social benefit is equal to total social cost.
price mechanism is used to allocate resources.

questions.explanation: Efficiency means total social surplus is maximised. This occurs where marginal social benefit equals marginal social cost. Equal income distribution and use of the price mechanism do not by themselves ensure efficiency, and equality of total benefit and total cost is not the condition for maximisation.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which of the following is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

choices.text: People tend to buy better seats at a concert when the charge for online ordering service is raised.
A reduction in per-unit tariff on imported cosmetics results in an improvement in the average quality of cosmetics.
More flats are sold when people expect the property prices to rise.
People tend to have more expensive meals when they travel abroad.

questions.explanation: A tariff reduction lowers the money price of imported cosmetics, but it does not imply a rise in their average quality. The other cases can be explained through changes in relative price or full price, or through expected future prices, without contradicting the law of demand.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: Which of the following would most likely lead to a decrease in the demand for shark fin?

choices.text: More people prefer not to eat shark fin for the reason of environmental protection.
The punishment for illegal shark hunting has risen.
Shark hunters raise the selling price of shark fin.
It is more difficult to hunt a shark as the number of sharks has decreased in recent years.

questions.explanation: A change in consumers' preferences against eating shark fin shifts its demand curve left. Higher penalties for hunting and greater difficulty in hunting affect supply, while a higher selling price causes a movement along the demand curve rather than a decrease in demand.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem: The table below shows the relationship between the price and the total expenditures of two consumers on good X.
questions.explanation: Consumer A's total expenditure rises as price rises, which shows inelastic demand. For consumer B, total expenditure divided by price is 9 units at every price, so quantity demanded is unchanged and demand is perfectly inelastic.

visuals.caption: Price and total expenditure on good X

questions.postVisualStem: From the above table, we can conclude that consumer A's demand for good X is ___________ and consumer B's demand for good X is ___________.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X.

choices.text: buyers' total expenditure on good X would increase by $160.
the subsidy benefit enjoyed by the sellers would be $420.
the subsidy benefit enjoyed by the buyers would be $280.
the total amount of subsidy provided would be $720.

questions.explanation: Initially equilibrium is $6 and 120 units. With a $3 subsidy, buyers pay $4 while sellers receive $7, and 140 units are transacted. Buyers gain $2 per unit, so their subsidy benefit is $2 x 140 = $280. Their expenditure falls by $160, sellers gain $140 and total subsidy is $420.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: If the government provided a $3 per-unit subsidy on good X,

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The population in economy A increases and there is a bad harvest of rice in economy A. The equilibrium quantity of rice in economy A ___________.
questions.explanation: A larger population increases demand, tending to raise equilibrium quantity, while a bad harvest decreases supply, tending to lower it. The final change in equilibrium quantity depends on the relative sizes of the two shifts.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Suppose the government raised an effective minimum wage. Which of the following would LEAST likely occur?

choices.text: The employers would tend to adopt more capital to replace labour.
The total social surplus would increase.
The excess supply of labour would be larger.
It would be more difficult for low-skilled workers to get a job.

questions.explanation: A higher effective minimum wage is a price floor. It creates more excess supply of labour, encourages substitution of capital for labour and makes it harder for lower-skilled workers to find jobs. It creates rather than raises total social surplus, so B is least likely.

questions.keyPoint: Identify the type of market structure
questions.stem: The market structure of hair salons in Hong Kong can be regarded as

choices.text: monopolistic competition because hair salons in Hong Kong provide homogeneous services.
monopolistic competition because there are many hair salons providing differentiated services.
oligopoly because the set-up cost of a hair salon is huge.
oligopoly because hair salons in Hong Kong are price searchers.

questions.explanation: Monopolistic competition has many sellers offering differentiated products or services. Hair salons differ in service, style, reputation and location; neither high set-up costs nor price searching alone establishes an oligopoly.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: In 2017, the government paid additional assistance of one month to recipients of Comprehensive Social Security Assistance (CSSA). Which of the following about this policy is CORRECT?

choices.text: It worsens the income distribution of Hong Kong because not every citizen can benefit from the policy.
It helps equalise opportunities as recipients can use the money for studies.
It reduces the post-tax post-social transfer Gini coefficient of Hong Kong.
The income distribution remains unchanged as every low-income family under the CSSA scheme can receive the money.

questions.explanation: Additional CSSA transfers raise the income of eligible low-income households, helping equalise income and reducing measured inequality after tax and social transfers. A lower Gini coefficient records this improvement; the transfer is not an equal-opportunity policy merely because money could be used for studies.

questions.keyPoint: Distinguishing between free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about free goods is CORRECT?

choices.text: People would not compete for free goods.
People prefer economic goods to free goods.
Free goods cannot be producer goods.
The demand for free goods is smaller than the demand for economic goods.

questions.explanation: Free goods are not scarce relative to demand, so people do not need to compete for them. Whether people prefer a good, whether it is a producer good and the size of demand do not distinguish free goods from economic goods.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between interest rate, current consumption and saving
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about interest is CORRECT?

choices.text: Interest does not exist when there is deflation.
Interest only exists in a market economy.
A fall in interest rate increases future consumption.
An increase in interest rate increases saving.

questions.explanation: A higher interest rate raises the return to saving and the opportunity cost of current consumption, so saving tends to increase. Interest can exist during deflation and outside a market economy, while a lower interest rate tends to make current rather than future consumption relatively more attractive.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Which of the following comes closest to the nature of a public good?

choices.text: the weather forecast provided by the Hong Kong Observatory
a book in a public library

questions.explanation: A weather forecast is largely non-rival and non-excludable, so it most closely resembles a public good. A rental unit, museum visit and library book can be congested or restricted to particular users.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Mr. Chan and Mr. Lee are bus drivers of a bus company. They earn the same salaries. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: Their costs of quitting their job are the same.
Their costs of quitting their job would increase if the bus company raises their salary.
Their costs of working as a bus driver are the same.
Their costs of working as a bus driver would decrease if there are more job opportunities in the economy.

questions.explanation: A salary rise increases the income forgone by quitting the job, so the cost of quitting rises. Equal salaries alone do not show that the two workers have the same best alternative or the same cost of working, and more job opportunities raise rather than reduce the opportunity cost of working as a bus driver.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership

choices.text: The profitability of firm A is higher.
Firm A pays a higher profits tax rate than firm B.
Owners of firm B enjoy limited liabilities while owners of firm A do not.

questions.explanation: Firm A is a public limited company and Firm B is a private limited company: both have separate legal personality and limited liability. The table does not reveal profitability or tax rates.

visuals.caption: Features of Firm A and Firm B
rows: Continues to exist when one of the owners goes bankrupt
Continues to exist when one of the owners goes bankrupt

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of buying shares and bonds from small investors’ point of view
questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of buying bonds over shares from the viewpoint of investors?

choices.text: The return of bonds is more stable than that of shares.
The market price of shares may decrease while that of bonds is fixed.
The bondholders have voting rights in the annual general meeting while shareholders do not.
Bonds can be freely transferable in the market while the transfer of shares requires consent of other owners.

questions.explanation: Bondholders normally receive fixed interest, so their return is more stable than the dividend and capital return on shares. Bond prices can change, shareholders rather than bondholders have voting rights, and shares can generally be freely transferred on a stock exchange.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour

choices.text: labour supply ... more types of jobs require licences
average labour productivity ... more imported workers are allowed to work in Hong Kong
geographical mobility ... a company provides housing subsidy for workers who have been working for 5 years
occupational mobility ... the government provides training courses for unemployed persons

questions.explanation: Training courses help unemployed workers acquire skills for different occupations, increasing occupational mobility. More licensing requirements restrict labour supply, imported workers do not necessarily raise average productivity, and a housing subsidy conditional on five years of service does not improve geographical mobility.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The following table shows the cost-output relationship of a price taker.
questions.explanation: A fixed-cost increase does not change marginal cost, so the profit-maximising output of a price taker is unchanged. Profit falls by the $5 fixed-cost increase, whereas producer surplus is total revenue minus total variable cost and remains unchanged.

visuals.caption: Cost-output relationship of a price taker

questions.postVisualStem: The market price is $6. Suppose the fixed cost increases by $5. At the profit-maximising output level, the firm's profit will ___________ and total producer surplus will ___________.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning and give examples of each type of integration
questions.stem: A toy manufacturing company can obtain more information about the preference of consumers by engaging in ___________ while it can diversify its business to spread risk by engaging in ___________.
questions.explanation: Forward integration into distribution or retailing gives a manufacturer closer contact with consumers and more information about their preferences. Conglomerate integration expands into unrelated activities, helping diversify risk.

questions.keyPoint: Variable costs and fixed costs
questions.stem:
A public hospital increases the number of beds in a ward to admit more patients. Which of the following are variable costs involved in admitting more patients by just adding more beds?

(1) costs of preparing meals for patients
(2) expenses on medicine
(3) salary of doctors
(4) costs of buying medical machinery (e.g. X-ray machine)
questions.explanation: Meals and medicine rise with the number of patients admitted, so they are variable costs. With only more beds added, doctors' salaries and the cost of medical machinery do not vary with the extra patients and are fixed costs in this situation.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: The following table shows the Gini coefficient of Hong Kong from 2006 to 2016.

choices.text: the income of low-income households decreased.
the amount of transfer payment to the poor decreased.
the tax system in Hong Kong is likely to be progressive.

questions.explanation: In every year, the post-tax Gini coefficient is lower than the original-income Gini coefficient. Taxation and transfers therefore reduce measured income inequality; this is consistent with a progressive tax system. The table does not show the income of low-income households, the amount of transfers or the cost of living.

visuals.caption: Gini coefficient of Hong Kong from 2006 to 2016
rows: Gini coefficient based on original household income
Gini coefficient based on post-tax household income

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising opportunities
questions.stem:
The Non-means-tested Subsidy Scheme (免入息審查資助計劃) provides subsidy for students pursuing self-financing undergraduate programmes in Hong Kong. Eligible students can receive an annual subsidy of $30,000.

Which of the following would likely occur after the implementation of this scheme?

(1) Income inequality would decrease.
(2) Opportunities would be more equalised.
(3) Labour productivity would increase in the future.
questions.explanation: The subsidy supports access to tertiary education and so helps equalise opportunities. More education and training can raise future labour productivity. It also reduces the financial burden of eligible students and their families, helping reduce income inequality.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on producer surplus
questions.stem: If the government increases the effective quota on instant noodles and at the same time instant noodles become more popular, the producer surplus in the market of instant noodles ___________.
questions.explanation: A larger effective quota tends to lower domestic price and producer surplus by increasing imports, whereas greater popularity raises demand and tends to raise both. The final change in producer surplus depends on the relative sizes of the two effects.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram of a good with a price ceiling set at P1 by the government.
questions.explanation: At P1, the effective ceiling constrains quantity to the amount supplied. P2 is above equilibrium, so the ceiling becomes ineffective and quantity transacted rises to equilibrium; (1) is false. Consumer surplus may rise or fall because the original rationing arrangement is unknown, while deadweight loss decreases when the quantity moves to the efficient equilibrium level.

visuals.alt: Supply-demand diagram with supply S, demand D, a lower price ceiling P1 and a higher ceiling P2 above equilibrium.
visuals.caption: Supply-demand diagram with price ceilings P1 and P2

curves: Supply S slopes upward.
Demand D slopes downward.
movements: The price ceiling rises from P1 to P2.
P1 is effective, while P2 lies above equilibrium and is ineffective.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The quantity transacted rises when the effective ceiling is removed. Consumer surplus may rise or fall because the original allocation among consumers is not specified, and deadweight loss decreases as quantity moves toward equilibrium.

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following will be the results of raising the price ceiling of the good to P2?

(1) The quantity transacted of the good will remain unchanged.
(2) The consumer surplus may increase or decrease.
(3) The deadweight loss will decrease.

questions.keyPoint: Expenditure approach
questions.stem: Refer to the following table.
questions.explanation: GDP at market prices is $475 million: GDP at factor cost ($480 million) less the $5 million subsidy. By the expenditure approach, GDP = C + I + G + X - M. Hence G = 475 - 220 - 80 - 5 - (18 + 25) + (33 + 20) = $180 million. Profits tax is a direct tax and is not included in this conversion.
questions.postVisualStem: The government consumption expenditure for that year is $ ___________ million.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of per capita GDP
questions.stem: The aggregate output of economy A decreases by 3% and its general price level and population drop by 6% and 4% respectively. As a result, Country A's per capita nominal GDP will ___________ and the per capita real GDP will ___________.
questions.explanation: Real output falls by 3%, but population falls by 4%, so real GDP per capita rises. Nominal GDP falls because both output and the general price level fall; this fall is larger than the fall in population, so nominal GDP per capita falls.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: Suppose imported workers left Hong Kong after several huge construction projects had been completed. Hong Kong's labour force would ___________ and the unemployment rate would ___________.
questions.explanation: Imported workers who leave Hong Kong are no longer in its labour force, so the labour force falls. Completion of the major construction projects reduces employment opportunities and increases unemployment relative to the remaining labour force, so the unemployment rate rises.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: Which of the following can offset the effect of a decrease in tax allowance on aggregate demand?

choices.text: a fall in the general price level
a decrease in the transaction demand for money

questions.explanation: A lower tax allowance reduces disposable income, consumption expenditure and aggregate demand. A decrease in transaction demand for money lowers the nominal interest rate, encouraging investment and raising aggregate demand. A general price-level fall is a movement along, not a shift of, the AD curve; better technology affects aggregate supply, and lower transfer payments reduces aggregate demand further.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Inflationary gap
questions.stem: Inflationary (output) gap

choices.text: will be narrowed when the households spend a higher proportion of their income.
will be narrowed when the economy suffers from a financial crisis.
will be widened when the assets demand for money increases.
will be widened when the government introduces general sales tax.

questions.explanation: A financial crisis reduces consumption and investment, shifting aggregate demand left and narrowing an inflationary gap. A higher propensity to consume expands aggregate demand. Higher asset demand for money tends to raise the nominal interest rate and reduce investment, while a general sales tax reduces consumption; both would narrow rather than widen the gap.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: A report revealed that there are loopholes in some common mobile payment systems which may cause users to suffer monetary loss. Some people stopped using mobile payment systems. As a result,

choices.text: the transaction demand for money will decrease.
the maximum banking multiplier will increase.
the nominal interest rate will increase.

questions.explanation: When people stop using mobile payments, they hold more money for transactions. With money supply unchanged, this increase in money demand raises the nominal interest rate. It does not change the maximum banking multiplier or the monetary base.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The following table shows the balance sheet of a banking system. The required reserve ratio is 20%.
questions.explanation: Required reserves are 20% of $4,800 million, or $960 million, leaving $40 million excess reserves. Lending this out increases loans and deposits while reserves remain in the banking system. The actual reserve ratio falls and the actual banking multiplier rises, so (2) and (3) are correct.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.postVisualStem:
If the banks lend out all the excess reserves, which of the following are CORRECT?

(1) The amount of reserves would decrease.
(2) The amount of loans would increase.
(3) The actual banking multiplier would increase.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money demand and money supply curves of an economy. The original equilibrium point is at E.
questions.explanation: A lower discount rate raises money supply from MS0 to MS2. More popular electronic payment lowers money demand from MD0 to MD1. Their intersection is point D.

visuals.alt: Money-demand and money-supply diagram with the initial equilibrium E at MS0 and MD0, alternative supply levels MS1 and MS2, demand curves MD1 and MD2, and points A to D.
visuals.caption: Money demand and money supply curves

curves: Money-supply curves MS1, MS0 and MS2 are vertical.
Money-demand curves MD1, MD0 and MD2 slope downward.
movements: A lower discount rate raises money supply from MS0 to MS2.
More popular electronic payment lowers money demand from MD0 to MD1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The two changes move equilibrium from E to D.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the central bank reduces the discount rate and electronic payment becomes more popular. The new equilibrium point will be at ___________.

questions.keyPoint: Definitions of M1, M2 and M3 in
questions.stem:
Mark withdraws HK$200,000 from his savings account. Then he deposits HK$120,000 as a time deposit and HK$50,000 as a demand deposit with a licensed bank. He remits the remainder overseas.

What will be the immediate effect of the above actions on the Hong Kong dollar money supply?

choices.text: M1 will increase by HK$50,000 and M2 will decrease by HK$50,000.
M1 will increase by HK$50,000 and M2 will decrease by HK$120,000.
M2 will decrease by HK$30,000 and M3 will remain unchanged.
Both M2 and M3 will decrease by HK$30,000.

questions.explanation: The $50,000 demand deposit is included in M1, M2 and M3, and the $120,000 time deposit remains in M2 and M3. The $30,000 remitted overseas leaves Hong Kong dollar deposits, so both M2 and M3 decrease by $30,000.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: When there is unexpected deflation, which of the following parties will lose?

choices.text: An employee who receives a fixed monthly salary
A bank which lends mortgage loans at a flexible rate
An investor who holds fixed rate debenture issued by a private firm
A government which pays a fixed pension to retired employees

questions.explanation: Unexpected deflation raises the real value of fixed nominal payments. Fixed-salary employees and fixed-rate debenture holders gain purchasing power, whereas a government paying fixed pensions bears a higher real burden. A flexible mortgage rate can adjust.

questions.keyPoint: Direct tax and indirect tax
questions.stem:
Which of the following are direct taxes in Hong Kong?

(1) profits tax
(2) estate duty
(3) rates on property
(4) property tax
questions.explanation: Profits tax and property tax are direct taxes. Estate duty and rates are indirect taxes in the classification used here.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: Consider the following data of an economy.

choices.text: nominal national income remains unchanged in year 2.
the velocity of circulation of money decreases in year 2.
there is an increase in the price level in year 2.
the money supply grows slower than the price level in year 2.

questions.explanation: With velocity assumed constant in the quantity theory, money supply rises by 50% while real output rises by 20%. The price level must therefore rise (by 25%), so C is correct.
questions.postVisualStem: According to the quantity theory of money, we can conclude that

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Which of the following policies would most likely lead to a fall in the price level?

choices.text: The government increased the required reserve ratio and imposed a general sales tax at the same time.
The government increased its expenditure on social welfare and sold government bonds to the commercial banks at the same time.
The government raised the discount rate and the profits tax rate at the same time.
The government bought government bonds from the public and reduced the tax allowance at the same time.

questions.explanation: A higher discount rate is contractionary monetary policy and a higher profits-tax rate is contractionary fiscal policy. Both lower aggregate demand and tend to reduce the price level. The other pairs include opposing effects or a sales tax that can raise firms' costs.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Deflationary gap
questions.stem: There is a deflationary (output) gap in the economy. Which of the following is the advantage of market forces over using expansionary monetary policy to restore the economy to its long-run equilibrium?

choices.text: The employment level will be higher.
The purchasing power of money will be higher.
The real output will be higher.
The fiscal balance will be higher.

questions.explanation: Market forces lower wages and production costs, shifting SRAS right. This restores output with a lower price level, so money has greater purchasing power. Expansionary monetary policy restores output by raising AD and does not provide that price-level advantage.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: Suppose economy A initially operates at the full-employment equilibrium and the trade balance of the economy is balanced. In the short run, an appreciation in the currency of its major trading partners will result in ___________ and ___________ of economy A.

choices.text: an increase in the price level ... trade surplus
an increase in the price level ... trade deficit
a decrease in real output ... trade surplus
a decrease in real output ... trade deficit

questions.explanation: An appreciation of trading partners' currencies makes economy A's exports cheaper to them and imports more expensive to its residents. Net exports and aggregate demand rise, producing a trade surplus and a higher price level in the short run.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: In the Chief Executive's 2017 Policy Address, the government proposed a reduction in the profits tax rate for the first $2 million of profits of enterprises. At the same time, the government proposed an additional tax deduction for research and development expenditure. Which of the following best illustrates the effect of the above changes on the price and output levels?
questions.explanation: A lower profits-tax rate raises aggregate demand, while an additional deduction for research and development encourages investment and raises productive capacity. The suitable diagram therefore shifts both AD and LRAS right, as shown in B.

visuals.alt: Four AD-AS diagram options labelled A to D, including a diagram with AD and LRAS both shifting right.
visuals.caption: Alternative price-output effects of fiscal policies

curves: AD curves slope downward; SRAS curves slope upward; LRAS curves are vertical.
movements: A lower profits-tax rate raises aggregate demand.
An additional research-and-development tax deduction raises long-run aggregate supply.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option B shows both AD and LRAS shifting right.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: Which of the following is favourable to the balance of payments of Hong Kong?

choices.text: A Hong Kong investor increases his investment in Vietnam.
Hong Kong imports more goods from Japan.
A Hong Kong firm buys shares of a US company.
A Hong Kong investors receives rent from a flat in Japan.

questions.explanation: Rent received from a property abroad is an income receipt in Hong Kong's current account, improving its balance of payments. The other transactions are payments abroad or financial outflows.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem:
A small country has imposed a per-unit tariff on imported good X. If the demand for good X in the country increases,

(1) the domestic price of good X will increase.
(2) the import volume will increase.
(3) the tariff revenue will increase.
questions.explanation: For a small country, the tariff fixes the domestic price at world price plus the tariff, so (1) is false. Higher demand raises import volume at that price, so tariff revenue also rises; (2) and (3) are correct.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: The following table shows the number of man-hours required by Country A and Country B in the production of watches and clothes.

choices.text: The net gain from trade of Country A is 0.5 units of watches when 5 units of clothes are traded.
If the transportation cost for 1 unit of clothes is 0.4 units of watches, trade will still take place between the two countries.
The total gain of the two countries from trading 1 unit of clothes is 0.5 units of watches.

questions.explanation: Country A has comparative advantage in watches and imports clothes. One unit of clothes costs Country A 1.6 watches to produce but costs 1.5 watches through trade, a gain of 0.1 watch per unit of clothes. For five units, Country A gains 0.5 watches.

visuals.caption: Man-hours required to produce watches and clothes

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the terms of trade is 1 unit of clothes = 1.5 units of watches. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.keyPoint: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.stem: Refer to the following table.

choices.text: a decrease in the total value (in terms of Euro) of European exports to Hong Kong.
an increase in the total value (in terms of Euro) of Hong Kong exports to Europe.
a decrease in the number of Hong Kong tourists to the US.
a decrease in the volume of Hong Kong exports to Europe.

questions.explanation: The euro appreciates against the US dollar. Since the Hong Kong dollar is linked to the US dollar, European goods become more expensive in Hong Kong and Hong Kong imports from Europe fall; their total value in euros decreases.
questions.postVisualStem: Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, the above change in the exchange rate between the Euro (€) and the US$ would lead to

questions.keyPoint: Currency issuing system in
questions.stem: Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong,

choices.text: the market exchange rate between the HK dollar and the US dollar is controlled by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.
an appreciation of the HK dollar against Renminbi would lead to an appreciation of the US dollar against Renminbi.
Hong Kong dollar banknotes are fully backed by foreign exchange reserves.
If the US has a trade deficit, Hong Kong would also have a trade deficit.

questions.explanation: Under Hong Kong's currency-board arrangement, banknotes are fully backed by foreign exchange reserves. The HKMA maintains the linked-rate system rather than directly fixing every market rate, and Hong Kong's trade balance need not match that of the United States.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: Which of the following is CORRECT when diminishing marginal returns set in?

choices.text: The firm is operating in the short run.
The firm is suffering a loss.
The firm has to reduce the variable input to maximise profit.

questions.explanation: The law of diminishing marginal returns applies in the short run, when at least one input is fixed. Marginal product can remain positive, and diminishing returns do not by themselves determine profit or the optimal use of the variable input.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: In a factory that assembles mobile phones, workers are paid by piece rate while managers are paid by time rate. This is because

choices.text: high-ranking job positions are generally paid by time rate.
the cost of measuring output is lower for workers than managers.
managers are generally more hard-working than workers.
the income of managers is usually higher than that of workers.

questions.explanation: Individual workers' output can be measured relatively cheaply, so a piece rate can be used to link pay to output. A manager's contribution is harder to measure as a separate number of units, making time rate more suitable.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem: In which of the following pairs does the demand for the first good create a derived demand for the second one?

choices.text: drinking straws and iced lemon tea
plastic cups and iced lemon tea

questions.explanation: Lemon is an input used to produce iced lemon tea. Demand for the final product therefore creates derived demand for lemons. The first good in the other pairs does not create demand for the second as a production input.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the tax burden
questions.stem: When the government imposes a per-unit tax on good X, there will be a greater rise in good X's price when

choices.text: good X is a habit-forming good.
there are many substitutes for good X.
firms that produce good X have excess capacity.
the factors used to produce good X have high mobility.

questions.explanation: Consumers bear a larger share of a per-unit tax when demand is relatively inelastic. A habit-forming good normally has inelastic demand, whereas many substitutes make demand more elastic.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, cost of production, technology, price expectations, weather, number of sellers in the market, etc. affect individual supply and market supply
questions.stem: The present supply of residential housing units will decrease if

choices.text: the property developers expect the price of residential housing units to increase.
the government raises the stamp duties levied on buyers who are non-Hong Kong permanent residents.
the banks tighten the requirements for applying a mortgage loans.
the average wage of construction workers fall.

questions.explanation: If developers expect a higher future price, they may withhold current supply. A higher buyer stamp duty and tighter mortgage requirements affect demand, while lower construction wages reduce costs and tend to increase supply.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: HK Express and Hong Kong Airlines are two HNA Group airlines. Suppose HK Express offers discounts on its flights. Which of the following diagrams is CORRECT?
questions.explanation: Flights of HK Express and Hong Kong Airlines are substitutes. A discount on HK Express flights shifts demand for Hong Kong Airlines left, lowering its equilibrium price and quantity; diagram D shows this result.

visuals.alt: Four demand-supply diagram options for flights of HK Express and Hong Kong Airlines after HK Express offers discounts.
visuals.caption: Effects of HK Express discounts on airline-flight markets

curves: The relevant effect is a leftward demand shift for Hong Kong Airlines, a substitute airline.
movements: HK Express discounts draw passengers away from Hong Kong Airlines.
Hong Kong Airlines' demand shifts left, reducing its equilibrium price and quantity.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option D correctly shows the demand decrease for Hong Kong Airlines.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: In order to reduce traffic accidents, the government raised the maximum penalties for drink driving from 3-year imprisonment to 5 years. As a result, the number of traffic accidents decreased by 20%. Which of the following concepts can be used to explain the above phenomenon?
questions.explanation: A higher penalty raises the full price of drink driving. By the law of demand, a higher full price reduces the quantity demanded of the activity, which can reduce traffic accidents.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram.
questions.explanation: With the ceiling at Pa, consumer surplus is a + c and producer surplus is e. With the floor at Pb, consumer surplus is a + b and producer surplus is c + d + e. The changes are therefore b - c and c + d respectively.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram with price ceiling Pa, price floor Pb, quantities Qa and Qb, and labelled areas a to e.
visuals.caption: Consumer and producer surplus under a ceiling and a floor

curves: Supply S slopes upward and demand D slopes downward.
movements: The effective price ceiling at Pa is abolished.
An effective price floor at Pb is imposed.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Consumer surplus changes by b - c and producer surplus changes by c + d.

questions.postVisualStem:
After the government abolished the price ceiling at Pa and imposed a price floor at Pb, the changes in consumer

surplus and producer surplus were represented by ______ and ______ respectively.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: The Star Ferry (天星小輪) raised the fares for the Tsim Sha Tsui - Central route in 2017. The table below shows the adult fare for weekdays before and after the rise.

choices.text: More adult passengers would choose the seats at the lower deck.
The behaviour of adult passengers would not be affected as the increase is not significant.
The total revenue of the Star Ferry would increase.
The total number of adult passengers would decrease.

questions.explanation: A fare rise raises the money price of the ferry service, reducing quantity demanded by the law of demand. The table alone does not establish the change in total revenue. The lower-deck fare rises by a larger percentage, so it is not relatively more attractive.

visuals.caption: Star Ferry adult fares: Tsim Sha Tsui - Central (weekdays)

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following is an effect of the fare increase?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the Gini Coefficient based on per capita income in Republic of South Africa (RSA) from 2006 to 2015.
questions.explanation: The male Gini coefficient falls from 0.70 to 0.65, so inequality among males narrows. RSA's overall coefficient falls from 0.72 to 0.68, showing improved overall equality. The chart cannot determine the income gap between males and females, so (1) does not follow.

visuals.alt: Bar chart of Gini coefficients for male, female and the Republic of South Africa in 2006, 2009, 2011 and 2015.
visuals.caption: Gini coefficients in the Republic of South Africa

movements: The male Gini coefficient falls from 0.70 in 2006 to 0.65 in 2015.
RSA's overall coefficient falls from 0.72 to 0.68.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The chart supports statements (2) and (3), but Gini coefficients do not establish the size of the income gap between males and females.

questions.postVisualStem:
Based on the above diagram, we can conclude that

(1) the income gap between males and females has become wider.
(2) the income diversification across males are narrowed.
(3) the overall income inequality in Republic of South Africa is improved.

questions.keyPoint: Distinguishing between free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: Burberry, a luxury brand, is reported to destroy its unsold inventories to maintain the brand image. These unsold inventories are __________ because __________.

choices.text: free goods ... more of them are not preferred
free goods ... they are not sold in the market
private goods ... they belong to Burberry
economic goods ... some people are willing to pay a price to obtain them

questions.explanation: The goods remain scarce relative to demand: some consumers are willing to pay for them. Being unsold or owned by a private firm does not make a good free, and a good need not be currently sold to be an economic good.

questions.keyPoint: Relationship between scarcity, competition and discrimination
questions.stem:
A famous singer is going to hold a concert at Hong Kong Coliseum and many fans are concerned about the allocation method of the tickets. Which of the following methods of allocating the concert tickets would be discriminatory?

(1) Tickets are sold by auction.
(2) Tickets are distributed by random selection.
(3) Tickets are sold to members of fan club only.
questions.explanation: All three methods distinguish among potential buyers. Auction favours those able and willing to pay more, random selection excludes unsuccessful applicants, and fan-club-only sales exclude non-members; each is a discriminatory allocation method under scarcity.

questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem: A convenience store has launched a promotion campaign. Customers can get a coupon for every purchase of $60 for redeeming the following kitchenware:

choices.text: an acrylic mug and a stainless steel kitchen knife
an acrylic mug, a stainless steel kitchen knife and $5,400

questions.explanation: Using 90 coupons for the frying pan means giving up the best alternative use of the same coupons: one 60-coupon stainless steel kitchen knife plus one 30-coupon acrylic mug. The $5,400 spent to obtain the coupons is already incurred and is not the opportunity cost of the redemption choice.
questions.postVisualStem: What is the opportunity cost for Jenny to use 90 coupons to redeem an iron frying pan?

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Which of the following are normative statements?

(1) Stop using plastic drinking straws will save plenty of marine life.
(2) It is unpleasant to drink cold drinks without using plastic drinking straws.
(3) We should stop using plastic drinking straws to save the environment.
questions.explanation: Statement (1) is a testable positive claim. Statements (2) and (3) contain value judgments about what is unpleasant and what people should do, so they are normative.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem:
Which of the following are guided by price signals in Hong Kong?

(1) The consumption decision by government officials
(2) The decision by Hang Seng Bank to lend out mortgage loans
(3) The decision by the government to raise the price of public swimming pools managed by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department
questions.explanation: Private consumption choices and a commercial bank's lending decision respond to prices, including interest rates. The government pricing of public swimming pools is an administrative decision rather than one guided by market price signals.

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: The table below shows the production of good X in a firm which employs two factors of production only, namely capital and labour.

choices.text: the firm enjoys economies of scale.
the firm suffers from diseconomies of scale.
the law of diminishing marginal returns sets in when 25 units of labour are employed.
the optimal scale of production is 185 units of output.

questions.explanation: When both capital and labour increase by the same proportion, output rises by a smaller proportion. Average cost rises from $3 per unit at 100 units to $3.60 at 250 units, showing diseconomies of scale. The table cannot identify a short-run diminishing-marginal-returns point or the profit-maximising scale.
questions.postVisualStem: From the above data, we can conclude that

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the owners of a private limited company in Hong Kong is CORRECT?

choices.text: They are subject to a higher salaries tax rate than the owners of a partnership.
Their ownership of the firm cannot be transferred.
They have to disclose their own financial information to the public.
The amount of dividend they receive is not fixed.

questions.explanation: Dividends are a residual return and are not fixed. Private-company shares can be transferred subject to the company's rules, and owners are not automatically subject to a higher salaries-tax rate or required to disclose their personal financial information publicly.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning and give examples of each type of integration
questions.stem: Kelvin Financial is a publishing company that publishes financial magazines. Recently, it has acquired two companies as illustrated in the following diagram:
questions.explanation: A publisher acquiring a bookstore moves forward toward retail distribution, so X is forward integration. Fashion Today operates at the same production stage as Kelvin Financial, so Y is lateral integration.

visuals.alt: Kelvin Financial, a publisher of financial magazines, acquires PopRead, a bookstore chain, at X and Fashion Today, another publisher, at Y.
visuals.caption: Acquisitions by Kelvin Financial

movements: X links a publisher to a bookstore chain.
Y links two publishing companies.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Acquiring PopRead is forward integration because it moves toward retail distribution. Acquiring Fashion Today is lateral integration because both firms publish magazines.

questions.postVisualStem: PopRead is a bookstore chain while Fashion Today is a publishing company that publishes fashion magazines. To Kelvin Financial, the types of integration shown by X and Y are __________ integration and __________ integration respectively.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following will lead to an increase in both labour supply and average labour productivity in Hong Kong?

choices.text: More retired elderly people migrate to Hong Kong.
More firms install high-tech equipment in production.
The government extends the current 12-year free education to 15 years.
More people migrate to Hong Kong through Quality Migrant Admission Scheme.

questions.explanation: The Quality Migrant Admission Scheme attracts skilled working-age people, increasing the labour force and average labour productivity. Retired migrants do not raise labour supply, high-tech equipment does not itself raise labour supply, and longer free education affects future rather than current labour supply.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: When the fixed cost of a firm in a perfectly competitive market increases, its profit-maximising output level will __________ and the producer surplus will __________.
questions.explanation: An increase in fixed cost does not change marginal cost, so the competitive firm's profit-maximising output is unchanged. Producer surplus is total revenue minus total variable cost, so it also remains unchanged; profit falls because fixed cost rises.

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a difference between perfect competition and monopoly?

choices.text: New firms are free to enter the industry in perfect competition while there are entry barriers in monopoly.
A monopolist can raise the price without losing all customers while a firm under perfect competition will lose all customers when raising the price.
A monopolist is regulated by the government while a firm under perfect competition is not.
A firm under perfect competition would not advertise its products while a monopolist may do so.

questions.explanation: Entry barriers, downward-sloping demand and advertising incentives distinguish the two structures. Government regulation is not an inherent feature of every monopoly, so C is not a general difference.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the market situation of good A after a per-unit subsidy of $30 is provided by the government.

choices.text: the total amount of subsidy provided would be $450.
the total expenditure of consumers would decrease.
the total revenue (including the subsidy) received by producers would decrease.

questions.explanation: Reducing the subsidy lowers the price received by producers including subsidy and reduces the quantity transacted, so producers' total revenue decreases. The new buyer price, subsidy amount and consumer expenditure cannot be fixed from the diagram without knowing the relevant elasticities.

visuals.alt: Supply-demand diagram for good A with original equilibrium price $100 and quantity 30, after a $30 unit subsidy.
visuals.caption: Unit subsidy on good A

curves: Supply slopes upward and demand slopes downward.
movements: The original equilibrium is $100 at 30 units.
The diagram is stated to apply after a $30 unit subsidy.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: A lower subsidy reduces the total revenue received by producers including the subsidy. The change in consumers' total expenditure cannot be concluded without demand elasticity.

questions.postVisualStem: If the per-unit subsidy was reduced by half,

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: During the 2018 FIFA World Cup, many shopping malls broadcast football matches to attract visitors. Which of the following is an example of the divergence between private and social benefits?

choices.text: Visitors watching the matches blocked the passageways in the mall.
Residents nearby were disturbed by the noise without receiving compensation.
Shops around these shopping malls recorded higher sales revenue as the number of visitors increased.
The working staff of the shopping malls watched the football matches when they were on duty.

questions.explanation: The malls' broadcast attracts visitors, creating higher sales for nearby shops that do not pay for that benefit. This is an external benefit, so social benefit exceeds the mall's private benefit.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: Which of the following amounts should be deducted from the gross domestic product of Hong Kong in order to calculate the gross national income of Hong Kong?

choices.text: the rental income received by a local company from the tenants of its apartments in Japan
the dividend paid by HK Electric to a retired Japanese permanently living in Hong Kong
the salary earned by a British teacher working in an international school in Hong Kong for 10 months
the remittance a Hong Kong resident sent to his children studying in Australia

questions.explanation: GNI measures production income received by Hong Kong residents. The British teacher's locally produced income is included in GDP but is income to a non-resident and is deducted in moving to GNI.
