The other choices are resident income abroad, a Hong Kong resident's dividend, or a transfer.

questions.keyPoint: Uses and limitations of national income statistics
questions.stem: Country A has a higher per capita real GDP but a lower average living standard than Country B. Which of the following is a possible reason for this?

choices.text: The inflation rate of Country A is higher.
The working hours of people in Country B are shorter.
The population size of Country B is smaller.
The income distribution in Country A is more even.

questions.explanation: Per capita real GDP does not record leisure. People in Country B may work fewer hours and enjoy more leisure, producing a higher average living standard despite lower measured per capita output.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: The potential output and the aggregate demand would increase at the same time if

choices.text: a higher proportion of the population entered the labour force.
the government introduced the general sales tax.
the government lowered the tolls of tunnels and bridges.
more firms invested in research projects launched by universities.

questions.explanation: Research investment raises current investment expenditure, a component of aggregate demand, and improves technology and productive capacity, raising potential output.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Which of the following would cause the aggregate output and the price level to change in the opposite direction in the short run?

choices.text: an increase in the people's desire to save and to invest
a fall in air passenger departure tax and a rise in stamp duties
an increase in oil prices and a reduction in the quota for imported workers
an improvement in production technology and a fall in imports

questions.explanation: Higher oil prices raise production costs and a lower imported-worker quota reduces labour supply. Both shift short-run aggregate supply left, reducing output while raising the price level.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve

choices.text: The government raises the minimum legal working age and reduces its spending on education.
The government raises the retirement age for civil servants and reduces import tariffs.
The government raises the unemployment benefits for those who are unemployed for more than three months.
There is a stock market boom and the currency of the economy depreciates against those of its trading partners.

questions.explanation: Higher unemployment benefits raise disposable income and aggregate demand. They can also reduce labour-force participation or wage pressure, shifting SRAS left; this matches the rightward AD shift and leftward SRAS shift in the diagram.

visuals.alt: AD-AS diagram with AD shifting right from AD0 to AD1 and SRAS shifting left from SRAS0 to SRAS1, raising price level from P0 to P1 and output from Y0 to Y1.
visuals.caption: Changes in AD and short-run AS

curves: AD slopes downward and SRAS slopes upward.
movements: AD shifts right from AD0 to AD1.
SRAS shifts left from SRAS0 to SRAS1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Higher unemployment benefits raise AD and can reduce labour supply, raising wage costs and shifting SRAS left.

questions.postVisualStem: The diagram above shows the aggregate demand curves and short run aggregate supply curves of an economy. Which of the following best explains the above changes?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: Some mobile payment tools offer discounts at various stores and restaurants to attract more users. When more people use these mobile payment tools,

choices.text: the transaction demand for money will decrease.
the function of money as a unit of account will be weakened.
the real interest rate will decrease.

questions.explanation: Mobile payment makes transactions easier with a lower need to hold money for spending. It reduces transaction demand for money; it does not by itself change money supply, the unit-of-account function or the real interest rate.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual banking multipliers
questions.stem: Study the following balance sheet of a banking system. The required reserve ratio is 20%.

choices.text: The actual reserve ratio will increase.
The actual banking multiplier will increase.

questions.explanation: Initially the actual banking multiplier is $1,600m / $400m = 4. After $100m is withdrawn, deposits are $1,500m and reserves are $300m, so it becomes 5. Cash held by the public replaces reserves, leaving the monetary base unchanged.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the public withdraw $100 million from the banking system and hold it as cash. Which of the following is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem: Tommy sold a negotiable certificate of deposit issued by a licensed bank to Jackie and received a cheque of $100,000. Tommy deposited the cheque into his savings account. The immediate effect of the above transactions is:

choices.text: Both M1 and M2 increase by $100,000.
M1 decreases by $100,000 and M2 remains unchanged.
M3 decreases by $100,000 and M2 remains unchanged.
Both M2 and M3 increase by $100,000.

questions.explanation: A chequeable deposit is transferred into a savings deposit. M1 falls by $100,000 while M2, which includes both forms of deposit, is unchanged.

questions.keyPoint: Assumptions of maximum change in deposits
questions.stem: Which of the following is CORRECT when the required reserve ratio is 100%?

choices.text: The maximum banking multiplier becomes zero.
The money supply remains unchanged if the banking system receives cash deposits from the public.
The money supply cannot be altered by the government.
Deposit creation can be carried out as long as there is sufficient demand for loans.

questions.explanation: With a 100% required reserve ratio, banks cannot create extra deposits through lending. Converting public cash into bank deposits leaves the money supply unchanged; the maximum multiplier is 1, not zero.

questions.keyPoint: Qualities of good money
questions.stem: Coin is better than shell to serve as a unit of account in terms of ___________.
questions.explanation: Coins of the same denomination are homogeneous, giving a consistent unit for quoting and comparing prices. Shells are not as uniform.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate
questions.stem: The nominal interest rate of a one-year bond is 5%, and the expected inflation rate is 1%. Suppose the general price level turns out to fall by 3%. The cost of holding money is ___________ and the realised real rate of return of holding bonds is ___________.
questions.explanation: The opportunity cost of holding money is the nominal interest rate, 5%. With 3% deflation, the realised real bond return is approximately 5% - (-3%) = 8%.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: Suppose the tax allowance in Hong Kong increases by 3% while both the nominal wages and the general price level decrease by 5%. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The government tax revenue would decrease.
The income gap between the rich and the poor would be wider.
The real wages after tax would remain unchanged.
More people would fall into the tax net.

questions.explanation: A larger tax allowance reduces taxable income, so tax revenue falls. A falling price level raises, rather than leaves unchanged, real wages for a given nominal after-tax wage; the tax net does not widen.

questions.keyPoint: Surplus budget, deficit budget and balanced budget
questions.stem: When the government recorded a budget deficit,

choices.text: the government must have a deficit budget.
the aggregate output would increase in the short run.
it means that the actual expenditure is higher than its planned expenditure.
it means that the actual expenditure is higher than its actual revenue.

questions.explanation: A recorded budget deficit means actual government expenditure exceeds actual government revenue. It does not by itself show the planned budget or guarantee an output change.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Transaction equation and velocity of circulation (V)
questions.stem: According to the equation of exchange, which of the following is possible when money supply and the general price level grow at the same rate?

choices.text: The growth rate of the velocity of circulation of money is higher than that of the real output.
The velocity of circulation of money and the real output fall at the same rate.
The velocity of circulation of money remains unchanged while the real output falls.
The velocity of circulation of money remains unchanged while the real output grows at the same rate as the general price level.

questions.explanation: From MV = PY, equal growth rates of M and P imply that V and real output Y must grow at the same rate. They can both fall at the same rate, as in B.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Suppose there is a stock market crash in a country. Which of the following can stabilise the interest rate and the price level in the country at the same time?

choices.text: The central bank reduces the required reserve ratio for the banking system.
The government increases the transfer payment provided to the poor.
The national income of the country's trading partners increases.
The central bank sells government bonds to the commercial banks.

questions.explanation: A stock-market crash reduces aggregate demand and can increase money demand for safe holdings. Lowering the reserve ratio expands money supply, offsetting upward interest-rate pressure and supporting aggregate demand and the price level.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Deflationary gap
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand (AD) curve, the short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve and the long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve of an economy. Which of the following policies can help the economy restore to the long run equilibrium?

choices.text: to abolish the tariff on imports
to increase the progressivity of profits tax
to increase the subsidies to small and medium enterprises
to narrow the tax band of salaries tax

questions.explanation: The economy has a deflationary gap because output lies below Yf. Higher subsidies to small and medium enterprises can expand demand and/or reduce production costs, helping output move toward long-run equilibrium.

visuals.alt: AD-AS diagram with current short-run equilibrium left of vertical LRAS at full-employment output Yf.
visuals.caption: Deflationary gap

curves: AD slopes downward, SRAS upward and LRAS is vertical.
movements: The AD-SRAS intersection is to the left of LRAS.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: A subsidy to small and medium enterprises can raise aggregate demand and help close the deflationary gap.

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the changes in the salaries tax structure of an economy.

choices.text: increase the work incentive of all workers
lead to a reduction in the number of people paying at the standard tax rate

questions.explanation: The new diagram reaches the lower standard rate at a higher income, so fewer taxpayers pay the standard rate. It does not show a narrower tax base or necessarily stronger incentives for every worker.

visuals.alt: Tax-rate-versus-income graph comparing old and new salaries tax structures, both rising to a standard-rate plateau, with the new structure's plateau lower and reached later.
visuals.caption: Old and new salaries-tax structures

curves: Both structures are progressive before reaching a standard-rate plateau.
movements: The new standard rate is lower and applies at a higher income threshold.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Fewer people pay the standard tax rate under the new structure.

questions.postVisualStem: Compared to the old tax structure, the new tax structure will ___________.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison between tariff and quota
questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of imposing a quota over imposing a per-unit tariff on imports for a small open economy?

choices.text: The quality of imported goods can be higher.
The price of imported goods can be lower for local consumers.
The government can have better control over the quantity of imports.
The government can receive more tax revenue.

questions.explanation: A quota directly fixes the maximum import quantity, whereas the resulting import volume under a tariff varies with demand and supply conditions.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: The following table shows the number of output that Countries A and B produce with 6 units of resources. Both countries allocate one-third of their resources in the production of apples and the remainder in the production of bread.
questions.explanation: Country A produces 18 apples with two resource units and 32 bread with four, so (1) is correct. Country B's opportunity cost of an apple is one bread, not two. Country A's apple opportunity cost is 8/9 bread, lower than Country B's one bread, so it has comparative advantage in apples.

visuals.caption: Output with six units of resources

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(

1) Country A can produce either 9 units of apples or 8 units of bread with one unit of resources.
(2) The opportunity cost of producing 1 unit of apples in Country B is 2 units of bread.
(3) Country A has a comparative advantage in producing apples.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: Which of the following would be a mutually beneficial terms of trade between Country A and Country B?

choices.text: 1 unit of apples = 0.52 units of bread
1 unit of apples = 0.95 units of bread
1 unit of apples = 1.1 units of bread
1 unit of apples = 1.8 units of bread

questions.explanation: Country A's opportunity cost of one apple is 8/9 bread and Country B's is one bread. A mutually beneficial terms of trade must lie between these values; 0.95 bread does.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem:
An insurance company in Hong Kong recruited local insurance agents to promote its business in mainland China. These insurance agents received commissions from the company. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) Both the GDP and GNI of Hong Kong rise.
(2) The invisible trade balance of Hong Kong improves.
(3) The net factor income from abroad increases.
questions.explanation: The Hong Kong insurance service sold to Mainland clients raises Hong Kong GDP and GNI and is an invisible export, improving the invisible-trade balance. The commissions are paid by a Hong Kong company to local agents, not net factor income from abroad.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: Refer to the following table.

choices.text: an increase in the number of tourists from Hong Kong to Britain.
an increase in the price (in terms of US dollar) of imports from Britain to the United States.
a fall in the total value (in terms of British Pound) of exports from Britain to Hong Kong.
a fall in the total value (in terms of US dollar) of exports from the United States to Britain.

questions.explanation: The pound appreciates against the Hong Kong dollar and, under the linked rate, against the US dollar. British goods become more expensive in Hong Kong, reducing Hong Kong imports from Britain and their total value in pounds.
questions.postVisualStem: Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, the above change in the exchange rate between Hong Kong dollar (HK$) and British Pound (£) would lead to

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The following table shows the cost-output relationship of a price taker.
questions.explanation: At 4 units, total revenue is $460 and total cost is $340 ($120 fixed cost plus $220 variable cost), giving profit of $120. The fourth unit adds $115 to total revenue and exactly covers its marginal cost, while producing a fifth unit reduces profit.

visuals.caption: Cost-output relationship of a price taker

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the market price is $115. What are the profit-maximising output and profit respectively?

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The following table shows a production plan of a firm which employs two factors only, namely labour and machinery.
questions.explanation: With machinery fixed at 3 units, marginal products of successive workers are 3, 5, 6, 5, 1 and -2. Marginal product first falls when the fourth worker is employed.
questions.postVisualStem: The marginal product of labour starts diminishing when the _______ unit of labour is put to work.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the supply and demand curves for CD albums in Hong Kong. The original equilibrium is at E0.
questions.explanation: Higher input cost decreases supply and more popular streaming decreases demand. On the given diagram, the intersection after both leftward shifts is E1.

visuals.alt: Supply curves S0, S1 and S2 and demand curves D0, D1 and D2 for CD albums, with equilibrium points E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: CD-album market

movements: Higher raw-material costs shift supply left from S0 to S2.
More popular music-streaming platforms shift demand left from D0 to D2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The simultaneous leftward supply and demand shifts give the new equilibrium E1.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the raw materials for producing CDs become more expensive and online music streaming platforms become more popular. The new equilibrium point will be at __________.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand and supply schedules for good X.

choices.text: The sellers’ revenue net of tax will be $350.
The total tax revenue will be $50.
The buyers’ total expenditure on good X will increase by $30.
The tax burdens borne by the buyers and the sellers are equal.

questions.explanation: Before the tax, equilibrium is $12 and 35 units. A $2 increase in the buyers' price takes it to $14 and lowers quantity demanded to 25. Suppliers receive $10 net of tax at 25 units, so the $4 tax is split equally: buyers pay $2 more and sellers receive $2 less per unit.

visuals.caption: Demand and supply schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: After the government imposes a per-unit tax on good X, the market price of good X increases by $2. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, cost of production, technology, price expectations, weather, number of sellers in the market, etc. affect individual supply and market supply
questions.stem: ABC Express is a courier company operating in Hong Kong. Which of the following will result in a decrease in the supply of the services provided by ABC Express?

choices.text: The competitors of ABC Express raise the charges for courier services.
The competitors of ABC Express raise the salaries of their staff members.
More customers give negative comments about the services provided by ABC Express on the Internet.

questions.explanation: Higher pay offered by rival firms raises ABC Express's cost of retaining or hiring workers, shifting its supply left. Lower fuel costs increase supply, a competitor's higher service charge affects demand for ABC Express, and negative reviews affect demand rather than its supply.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which of the following is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

choices.text: People tend to order more expensive wines in more high-class restaurants.
If the service charge that applied to all dishes increased from 10% to 15%, customers would tend to order more expensive dishes.
People tend to order more expensive dishes in restaurants when there is long queuing time.
Tourists from other countries tend to order more expensive dishes than local customers in restaurants.

questions.explanation: When the same service-charge rate rises for every dish, relative prices of dishes are unchanged. A tendency to order more expensive dishes cannot be explained by the law of demand; the other cases can reflect changes in full or relative price, or different consumers' demand.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand and supply schedules for a good.
questions.explanation: The relevant price-floor adjustment reduces price from $13 to $12, causing quantity demanded to rise from 10 to 12. Quantity demanded changes by a greater percentage than price, so demand is elastic in this range.
questions.postVisualStem: After the level of price floor on the good is adjusted, the quantity transacted of the good increases from 10 units to 12 units. The elasticity of _____________ is ____________ within the relevant price range.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the subsidy
questions.stem: Suppose the market price of good X decreases by $3 after the government provides a per-unit subsidy of $5 to the producers of good X. This implies that

choices.text: the demand for good X is inelastic.
the supply of good X is inelastic.
the elasticity of demand for good X is higher than the elasticity of supply of good X.
the elasticity of demand for good X is lower than the elasticity of supply of good X.

questions.explanation: Consumers receive $3 of the $5 subsidy through the lower price, while producers receive $2. The side receiving the larger share is the less elastic side, so demand is less elastic than supply.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the supply and demand curves for good X.

choices.text: will increase ... may increase or decrease
will decrease ... may increase or decrease
may increase or decrease ... will increase
may increase or decrease ... will decrease

questions.explanation: Relaxing the effective quota increases quantity and lowers price, so consumer surplus rises. Producer surplus may rise because more units are sold or fall because the price is lower; the diagram alone does not fix the net effect.

visuals.alt: Demand and supply curves for good X with quota lines S1 and S2, where S2 is to the right of S1.
visuals.caption: Quota adjustment for good X

movements: The quota expands from S1 to S2, permitting a larger quantity.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The expansion lowers the controlled price and increases quantity, so consumer surplus increases. The producer-surplus effect is ambiguous because the lower price and larger quantity work in opposite directions.

questions.postVisualStem:
After the quota set on the good is adjusted, the supply curve of the good shifts from S1 to S2. In the market of the

good, the consumer surplus __________ while the producer surplus _____________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: Suppose the pre-tax Gini coefficient of an economy increased over the past 10 years while the post-tax Gini coefficient decreased in the same period. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The average income of low-income households of the economy decreased over the past 10 years.
The general living standard declined over the past 10 years.
The tax system of the economy is likely to be progressive.
The Lorenz curve of the economy based on post-tax income was closer to the line of perfect income inequality 10 years ago.

questions.explanation: A lower post-tax Gini coefficient means post-tax income became more equal. Therefore, 10 years ago its Lorenz curve was farther from the line of equality and closer to the line of perfect inequality. The changes do not by themselves establish income levels, living standards, or the tax system's progressivity.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: The MTR Corporation increased the frequency of trains during rush hours to meet the needs of passengers. The above case is related to the _______ question(s) in economics.

choices.text: "how to produce" and "for whom to produce"

questions.explanation: Increasing train frequency changes the quantity and type of transport service supplied to passengers. It is therefore a decision about what to produce, rather than the production technique or the allocation of output among people.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Wendy is a Hong Kong citizen and she is going to travel to Thailand for leisure. She bought a non-transferable economy class air ticket. Which of the following will decrease her cost of having the trip?

choices.text: The price of air tickets to Thailand decreases after Wendy has bought her ticket.
The airline upgrades Wendy to business class for free when she checks in at the airport.
The Thai baht depreciates against the Hong Kong dollar.
The food she enjoys during her trip is better than expected.

questions.explanation: A depreciation of the Thai baht makes the Thai goods and services Wendy gives up Hong Kong dollars to obtain cheaper. Her non-transferable ticket is already committed, a free upgrade improves quality rather than lowering the trip's opportunity cost, and unexpectedly good food does not reduce what she gives up.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of interest
questions.stem: Matthew lent a suitcase to Andy and asked him to return it with souvenirs. Which of the following statements about the above situation is CORRECT?

choices.text: There is no interest because no money is involved.
The souvenirs are regarded as interest to Andy but not to Matthew.
Both the suitcase and the souvenirs are regarded as interest to Andy because he has to return the suitcase with souvenirs to Matthew afterwards.
The souvenirs are regarded as interest to Matthew because they are the compensation he receives for deferring consumption of the suitcase.

questions.explanation: Interest is compensation for allowing another person to use a resource earlier; it does not have to be money. Matthew gives up current use of the suitcase and receives souvenirs as that compensation.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem: "The average quality of output would be higher if workers were paid by piece rate instead of time rate." This statement is a __________ statement because _________________.

choices.text: positive ... it can be tested against objective facts

questions.explanation: The statement makes a causal prediction that can be compared with evidence. It does not express a value judgement, and being positive does not mean it must always be true.

questions.keyPoint: Definition of free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: A fitness centre offers free yoga lessons to university students. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The yoga lessons are free goods to university students but economic goods to other customers.
The yoga lessons are economic goods because more of the yoga lessons are preferred.
The fitness centre is not maximising its profit.
The university students do not have to compete for the yoga lessons because they are free of charge.

questions.explanation: A zero money price does not make a service a free good. Students prefer more lessons and the centre's capacity is scarce, so the lessons are economic goods; competition may still be necessary and the offer can be consistent with profit maximisation.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem:
According to a survey, the overall average staff turnover rate in Hong Kong was 10.9% in the first half of 2018. The average turnover rate of the retail industry was 18.0% while that of the financial services/banking/insurance industry was 5.7%.

Which of the following best explains the difference in turnover rate among these industries?

choices.text: The productivity of workers in the financial services/banking/insurance industry is higher.
Workers in the retail industry have higher occupational mobility than workers in the financial services/banking/insurance industry.
Workers in the retail industry are usually paid by basic salary plus commission while workers in the financial services/banking/insurance industry are usually paid by time rate.
The geographical mobility of workers in the retail industry is higher than workers in the financial services/banking/insurance industry.

questions.explanation: Staff turnover measures people changing jobs. Retail work generally requires less specialised training, so workers can move between occupations more readily; productivity, payment method, and geographical mobility do not directly explain the stated industry turnover difference.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of issuing shares and bonds to raise capital
questions.stem: China Grand Pharmaceutical and Healthcare Holdings Limited (遠大醫藥健康控股有限公司, stock code: 512) is a company that produces pharmaceutical products. In August 2018, it issued more shares to raise capital. The capital raised would be used to acquire Sirtex Medical Limited, an Australian medical device company.

choices.text: The acquisition can ensure a higher profit for the company.
The acquisition can reduce competition by turning a competitor into a partner.
From the viewpoint of the company, issuing shares can raise more capital than issuing bonds.
For existing shareholders who did not subscribe to the new shares, their power of control over the company will be diluted.

questions.explanation: New shares increase the number of shares outstanding. Existing shareholders who do not buy them own a smaller proportion of voting rights, so their control is diluted; neither higher profit nor reduced competition is ensured, and shares do not necessarily raise more capital than bonds.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: The major shareholder of Hopewell Holdings Limited (stock code: 0054) proposed privatisation of the company, which, if successful, will lead to the company getting delisted from the stock exchange. From the viewpoint of existing shareholders, which of the following is a possible motive behind this?

choices.text: to reduce the risk of being taken over
to have a wider source of capital

questions.explanation: Privatisation removes publicly traded shares, making it harder for another party to buy shares on the stock exchange and mount a takeover. Delisting narrows, rather than widens, the source of capital and does not itself create economies of scale or better continuity.

questions.keyPoint: Identify the type of market structure
questions.stem: The market structure of free television programme services in Hong Kong is regarded as ____________ because _________________.

choices.text: an oligopoly ... there are only a few dominant television broadcasting companies in the market
an oligopoly ... the set-up cost of a television broadcasting company is very high
a monopoly ...Television Broadcast Limited (TVB) has a much higher market share than its competitors
a monopolistic competition ... television broadcasting companies are providing heterogeneous television programmes

questions.explanation: An oligopoly is characterised by a few dominant firms. High set-up cost is a possible barrier to entry, not the defining evidence in the statement; a high market share does not alone establish monopoly, and differentiated programmes do not make the market monopolistic competition when only a few dominant firms operate.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following is the least mobile in terms of occupational mobility?
questions.explanation: A pilot's specialist training, qualifications and licensing are least transferable to other occupations. The other jobs generally have skills that can be used in a wider range of work.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: When a per-unit subsidy of $5 is provided to the producers of a good,

choices.text: both consumer surplus and producer surplus would decrease.
the producer surplus would increase while the consumer surplus would decrease.
the market price would decrease by $5.
the sum of the increase in consumer surplus and producer surplus would be smaller than the total amount of the subsidy provided.

questions.explanation: A per-unit subsidy raises producer and consumer surplus, but it also creates a deadweight loss. The combined gains in consumer and producer surplus are therefore less than the government's total subsidy payment; the consumer price need not fall by the full $5.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: After the opening of Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge, more tourists have visited Tung Chung. Some Tung Chung residents complain about the noise created by them while the shops in Tung Chung have recorded higher revenue. Which of the following statements about this situation is CORRECT?

choices.text: The tourists should compensate Tung Chung residents for the nuisance.
Government intervention is required to improve efficiency.
The number of tourists deviates from its efficient level.
Efficiency would be improved if shops gave compensation to Tung Chung residents.

questions.explanation: Tourist visits generate an external noise cost for residents that is not reflected in the visitors' private decision. Consequently, the market number of visitors differs from the socially efficient level. Compensation need not come from shops and government intervention is not the only possible response.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising opportunities
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about equity is CORRECT?

choices.text: Equity must be achieved in a planned economy while it may not be achieved in a market economy.
Policies that can equalise income may not help equalising opportunity.
Wealthy countries tends to aim at achieving efficiency instead of equity.
When there is a trade-off between equity and efficiency, efficiency should be a priority.

questions.explanation: Equalising income and equalising opportunity are different ethical objectives. For example, a transfer can narrow current income differences without ensuring equal access to education or other opportunities; the other statements treat normative choices as automatic rules.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: Refer to the following table.
questions.explanation: Net exports are $68 million. GDP at market prices is $754 million: $350 + ($120 + $8 - $12) + $220 + $68. GDP at factor cost is $748 million after subtracting $9 million indirect taxes and adding $3 million subsidies. GNI is higher because net income from abroad is positive ($13 million).
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The net exports was positive.
(2) The GDP at factor cost was $748 million.
(3) The GDP was smaller than the gross national income (GNI).

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of nominal GDP and real GDP
questions.stem: Suppose a closed economy produces good X and good Y only. The output of Year 1 and Year 2 are as follows:

choices.text: The nominal GDP in Year 2 is higher than that in Year 1.
The real GDP in Year 2 is higher than that in Year 1.
The GDP deflator in Year 2 is higher than that in Year 1.
The general living standard in Year 2 is higher than that in Year 1.

questions.explanation: Nominal GDP falls from $570 in Year 1 to $558 in Year 2. Real output also falls when valued at either year's prices, while the relative price movement makes the GDP deflator higher in Year 2. GDP information alone cannot establish the change in general living standard.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Inflationary gap
questions.stem: An inflationary (output) gap will exist if

choices.text: the short run equilibrium output level is higher than the potential output level.
there is a persistent increase in general price level.
there is an upward pressure on input prices.
the nominal output is larger than the real output.

questions.explanation: An inflationary output gap is the excess of short-run equilibrium output over potential output. Persistent inflation or rising input prices can occur for other reasons, and nominal output being larger than real output reflects prices rather than an output gap.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem: In the third quarter of 2018, Japan recorded a deflationary output gap for the first time in almost two years. Which of the following policies can the government introduce to eliminate the output gap and increase the price level at the same time?

choices.text: The government increases the sales tax rate.
The government reduces the spending on social welfare.
The government decreases the spending on education.
The government increases the tax allowance of the salaries tax.

questions.explanation: Raising the salaries-tax allowance increases disposable income and aggregate demand. This expansionary fiscal policy raises output toward potential and raises the price level; the other measures reduce aggregate demand.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Features of the four phases of a business cycle
questions.stem:
The following phenomena are observed in an economy:

(1) increasing number of job vacancies
(2) increasing amount of retail revenue
(3) decreasing number of bankruptcy petitions
(4) rising inflation rate

The economy is in the _______ phase of a business cycle.
questions.explanation: Rising vacancies and retail revenue, fewer bankruptcies, and a rising inflation rate show economic activity expanding from a low point. These are features of the recovery phase, rather than a trough, peak, or recession.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: Which of the following events would most likely lead to an increase in the nominal interest rate?

choices.text: National income rises and the use of electronic money becomes more widespread.
The stock market becomes more volatile and the central bank lowers the discount rate.
The liquidity of interest bearing assets decreases and the central bank raises the required reserve ratio.
The income payment interval changes from a monthly basis to a weekly basis and people expect a higher price level.

questions.explanation: Less liquid interest-bearing assets increase the demand for money, while a higher required reserve ratio reduces money supply. Both changes raise the nominal interest rate. The other pairs have offsetting effects.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Study the following balance sheet of a banking system. The amount of excess reserves in the banking system is $50 million.

choices.text: The monetary base will be $616 million.
The maximum banking multiplier will be 3.
The maximum possible amount of money supply will be $1,600 million.
The maximum possible amount of loans will be $1,120 million.

questions.explanation: Actual required reserves are $430 million ($480 million less $50 million excess reserves), so the original required reserve ratio is 25%. After it rises to 30%, deposits can be $1,600 million at most, leaving $480 million reserves and therefore $1,120 million loans. The monetary base remains $580 million including the public's $100 million cash.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the public always hold $100 million cash and the required reserve ratio is increased by 5%. Which of the following statements about the banking system is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Definitions of M1, M2 and M3 in
questions.stem:
Which of the following are included in Hong Kong’s money supply M2?

(1) savings deposits with licensed banks
(2) reserves held by licensed banks
(3) legal tender held by the non-bank public
questions.explanation: M2 includes deposits with licensed banks, including savings deposits, and legal tender held by the non-bank public. Bank reserves are not part of the public's money supply.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: Study the diagram below.

choices.text: the nominal interest rate was lower than the realised real interest rate.
the cost of living was decreasing.
tenants who had signed a fixed rental contract gained.

questions.explanation: The deflator's percentage change remains positive, so the price level rises despite a falling inflation rate. With unexpected inflation, a tenant's fixed nominal rental payment becomes less burdensome in real terms, so the tenant gains.

visuals.alt: A downward-sloping line above zero showing the percentage change in the GDP deflator declining toward zero over time.
visuals.caption: Change in GDP deflator

movements: The GDP deflator continues to rise, but at a declining positive rate, before the inflation rate reaches zero.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: There is unanticipated inflation, not deflation. A tenant with a fixed rental contract benefits because the fixed nominal payment loses purchasing power.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose people did not expect any change in the price level in the above period. In the above period,

questions.keyPoint: How central bank functions are carried out in
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority?

choices.text: to maintain the stability of the exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar
to determine the deposit interest rate of commercial banks
to maintain Hong Kong’s status as an international financial centre
to promote the stability of the banking system

questions.explanation: The HKMA maintains monetary and banking stability, including the linked exchange-rate system, but commercial banks determine their own deposit interest rates.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: Last year, some university graduates in an economy joined the labour force, of which 95% found a job. Suppose these university graduates did not replace any workers. The unemployment rate __________.
questions.explanation: The official solution identifies a fall in the unemployment rate: employment rises substantially as the new graduates enter jobs, while only 5% of the new entrants remain unemployed.

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: The air passenger departure tax in Hong Kong is a/an ____________ because _________________.

choices.text: direct tax ...the entire tax burden is borne by passengers
indirect tax ... the higher-income earners pay proportionately less tax
proportional tax ... the tax payment is the same regardless of the income of passengers
regressive tax ... the average tax rate decreases as income increases

questions.explanation: The same fixed departure tax is a smaller percentage of income for higher-income passengers. Its average tax rate therefore decreases as income rises, which is the definition of a regressive tax.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: The following table shows the changes in the salaries tax structure of an economy.

choices.text: More people will fall into the tax net.
The tax revenue collected from the salaries tax will decrease.
The government will run into a budget deficit.

questions.explanation: The new lower marginal tax rate for a further income band and the higher basic allowance reduce the marginal and average tax burden for many taxpayers. This strengthens the reward from earning additional income and so increases work incentive; the other outcomes are not certain.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the basic tax allowance is increased at the same time. Which of the following is most likely to be a result of the above changes in the tax system?

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: According to the classical quantity theory of money, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: An increase in money supply would lead to a higher price level and real output.
Any change in the price level would lead to the same proportional change in money supply.
Changes in money supply would have no effect on the real output.
Both velocity of circulation of money and nominal output are assumed to be constant.

questions.explanation: In the classical quantity theory, real output and velocity are assumed constant in the relevant comparison. A change in money supply changes the price level proportionally and does not change real output.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Deflationary gap
questions.stem: Suppose an economy initially operates at the full-employment equilibrium and the government expenditure equals its tax revenue. Supposing there is a stock market crash, there will be ___________ and ___________ .
questions.explanation: A stock-market crash reduces wealth and consumption, shifting aggregate demand left and creating a deflationary gap. Tax revenue falls while government expenditure is unchanged, converting the initially balanced budget into a fiscal deficit.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand (AD) curves, the short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curves and the long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curves of an economy. The economy initially operates at E0 and the potential output level is Y1. The long run equilibrium will be at _____________.
questions.explanation: At E0, output exceeds potential output Y1. Upward pressure on input prices shifts SRAS0 left to SRAS1, returning real output to Y1 at E1 in the long run.

visuals.alt: AD0 and AD1, SRAS0 and SRAS1, and a vertical LRAS at potential output Y1, with points E0 to E3.
visuals.caption: AD-AS long-run adjustment

movements: E0 lies to the right of LRAS, above potential output Y1.
Rising input prices shift SRAS0 left to SRAS1 while AD0 is unchanged.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The long-run adjustment returns output to potential Y1 at E1.

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: The consumption tax in Japan is imposed on the consumption of all goods and services. The Japanese government proposed to raise the consumption tax rate from 8% to 10% by October 2019. The increase in the consumption tax rate would lead to _____________.
questions.explanation: A broad consumption tax is regressive because lower-income households spend a larger proportion of income on consumption. Raising its rate therefore tends to make post-tax income distribution more uneven; the tax base does not widen and aggregate output does not rise.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning of comparative advantage
questions.stem: A country has a comparative advantage in producing good X. Which of the following statements about this country is CORRECT?

choices.text: The country has an absolute advantage in producing good X.
The country can produce the same amount of good X with fewer resources than other countries.
The country would enjoy a larger gain from trade than its trading partners.
In producing 1 unit of good X, it forgoes a smaller amount of another good than other countries.

questions.explanation: Comparative advantage means a lower opportunity cost. The country gives up less of the other good for one unit of X; it does not require absolute advantage or imply a larger share of trade gains.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: The following table shows data about Country A.

choices.text: The opportunity cost of producing 1 unit of Good X is 1 unit of Good Y.
With one unit of resources, Country A can produce same amount of Good X or Good Y.
The gain from trade of exporting 1 unit of Good X is 5/3 units of Good Y.

questions.explanation: The international-trade data show Country A exports 30 units of X and imports 60 units of Y. Comparing the specialisation-and-trade outcome with the no-trade outcome gives a gain of 5/3 units of Y for each unit of X exported.

visuals.caption: Country A: output and consumption with trade
rows: Total output with no international trade
Total output with specialisation and international trade

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about Country A is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem:
Consider a small open economy with an import tariff imposed on a good. If the economy reduced the tariff rate on the good, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The domestic consumption would increase.
(2) The revenue of domestic producers would decrease.
(3) The total amount of tariff revenue would decrease.
questions.explanation: A lower tariff reduces the domestic price, so domestic consumption rises and domestic producers receive less revenue. The tariff-revenue effect is ambiguous because the tariff per unit falls but import quantity rises.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.keyPoint: Meaning and role of foreign and official reserves in the balance of payments accounting
questions.stem: The following table shows information about the balance of payments of a country:
questions.explanation: A $20 million fall in foreign reserves finances a balance-of-payments deficit, not a surplus. With net capital outflow of $12 million, the current-account deficit is $8 million; given visible-trade surplus of $15 million and net income deficit of $5 million, invisible trade must be an $18 million deficit.
questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the amount of foreign exchange reserves of the country decreases by $20 million. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) There is an invisible trade deficit of $18 million.
(2) There is a current account deficit of $8 million.
(3) There is a balance of payment surplus of $20 million.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: When a country’s currency ___________ against its trading partners’ currencies, the total import value (in terms of domestic currency) will increase if the country’s demand for imports is ____________.
questions.explanation: An appreciation reduces the domestic-currency price of imports. If import demand is elastic, the percentage increase in import volume is larger than the percentage fall in price, increasing total import value in domestic currency.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Which of the following will increase the elasticity of demand for pay television programme services?

choices.text: More free videos are available online.
A higher fee is charged for pay television programme services.
Some free television providers shut down.
The quality of pay television programme services improves.

questions.explanation: More free online videos are close substitutes for pay television, so consumers can switch more easily when the fee changes. Greater availability of substitutes makes demand more elastic.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which of the following is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

choices.text: A high-income earner always travels in economy class rather than business class on flights.
After the government imposes an effective price ceiling on apples, people tend to buy higher-quality apples.
After the government imposes an effective quota on cosmetic products, the average quality of imported cosmetic products falls.
After the Transport Department installs speed enforcement cameras at a highway, vehicles’ average speed along the road section decreases.

questions.explanation: A binding quota raises the relative price of lower-quality imported cosmetics because they use up the same scarce quota. Consumers should tend to substitute toward higher-quality products, not lower-quality ones; the other statements can be explained by changes in full or relative price.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the demand and supply curves of oil. The original equilibrium point is E0.
questions.explanation: Renewable energy reduces demand for oil, while damaged facilities reduce oil supply. The intersection after both leftward shifts is E1 on the given diagram.

visuals.alt: Supply curves S0, S1 and S2 and demand curves D0, D1 and D2 for oil, with equilibrium points E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Oil market

movements: More renewable-energy use shifts demand left from D0 to D2.
Damaged oil facilities shift supply left from S0 to S2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The two leftward shifts give the new equilibrium E1 on the diagram.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose more firms use renewable energy for power generation. Meanwhile, oil facilities in some oil producing countries are attacked and damaged. The new equilibrium point is _____________.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply schedule of good X.

choices.text: The change in consumer surplus is uncertain.
The total revenue of producers will decrease by $48.
Consumers’ total expenditure on good X will decrease by $16.

questions.explanation: The lower effective quota reduces the amount that can be bought and sold. Using the stated $2 market-price change and the new quota quantity, consumers' total expenditure falls by $16; consumer surplus and total social surplus both fall rather than becoming uncertain or increasing.
questions.postVisualStem: After the government lowers the effective quota on good X to 10 units, the market price of good X changes by $2. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: After bubble milk tea (珍珠奶茶) gains wide popularity in Japan, its price and quantity transacted increase by 20% and 300% respectively. We can conclude that

choices.text: the demand for bubble milk tea is elastic.
the supply for bubble milk tea is elastic.
the demand for bubble milk tea is inelastic.
the supply for bubble milk tea is inelastic.

questions.explanation: The popularity change shifts demand, causing quantity to increase by a far larger percentage than price. This response indicates an elastic supply curve; the information does not measure price elasticity of demand.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply schedule of a good.

choices.text: its market price will increase by $6.
sellers’ total revenue after tax will increase by $18.
The tax burdens of buyers and sellers are both $45.

questions.explanation: Before tax, equilibrium is $27 at 16 units. With the $6 tax, buyers pay $30 and sellers receive $24 at 15 units. Each side bears $3 per unit on 15 units, so each bears $45; tax revenue is $90.
questions.postVisualStem: If the government imposes a $6 per-unit tax on the good,

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in supply
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in supply
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the supply curves of construction workers.

choices.text: increase, as construction workers are a factor of production for building private housing.
decrease, as the supply of private housing is derived from the supply of construction workers.
decrease, as construction workers and private housing are in joint supply.
remain unchanged, as the supply of construction workers will not affect the demand for private housing.

questions.explanation: The leftward shift in the supply of construction workers raises wage cost. As workers are an input in housing construction, the supply of private housing falls and its equilibrium price rises.

visuals.alt: Supply of construction workers shifts left from S1 to S2.
visuals.caption: Supply of construction workers

movements: The supply curve shifts left from S1 to S2, raising the cost of construction workers.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Construction workers are an input into housing construction. Their higher cost decreases the supply of private housing and increases its price.

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the diagram above, the price of private housing will

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem:
On June 19, 2019, the Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited announced the abolishment of minimum-balance fees for personal bank accounts. Later on the same day, Bank of China (Hong Kong) and Standard Chartered Hong Kong made the same move and cancelled the minimum-balance fees for personal bank accounts.

Which of the following is the MOST likely explanation for the above phenomenon?

choices.text: The market is jointly controlled by several large banks.
Banks are interdependent in their strategies.
Services provided by different banks are homogenous.
The banking industry in Hong Kong is perfectly competitive.

questions.explanation: Firms in an oligopoly react strategically to major rivals' decisions. The same-day matching of fee changes shows interdependence, rather than simply the number of large banks or homogeneous services.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: The table below shows the Gini coefficients of Macau.

choices.text: Government benefits and subsidies worsened income inequality.
Government benefits and subsidies were more effective in improving income equality.
The quality of life of low-income groups dropped.

questions.explanation: In both years, including government benefits and subsidies lowers the Gini coefficient. The reduction is 0.04 in 2017/18, compared with 0.03 in 2012/13, so benefits and subsidies were more effective in improving income equality in the later year.

visuals.caption: Gini coefficients of Macau
rows: Gini coefficient after excluding government welfare benefits and subsidies

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising opportunities
questions.stem:
Refer to the following news extract.

Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The plan does not help equalise income, as students cannot resell the tablet computers for profit.
The plan does not help equalise opportunities, as tablet computers are not necessities for learning.
The plan helps equalising opportunities, as it helps raise the productivity of students from middle-and low income groups.
Since all students can get a tablet computer, income distribution will remain unchanged.

questions.explanation: Providing tablets for education gives students, especially those from lower-income backgrounds, better access to a learning resource and can raise their productivity. That improves equality of opportunity; it is distinct from directly equalising current income.

visuals.title: News extract
visuals.text: The government announced a scheme under which tablet computers would be provided to tertiary students for educational purposes. All students enrolled in local tertiary programmes are eligible to this scheme. The tablet computers provided cannot be resold for profit and should be returned upon graduation or dropout.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Which of the following are positive statements?

(1) The agriculture sector accounts for less than 1% of Hong Kong’s GDP.
(2) Hong Kong should develop agriculture to become less dependent on food imports.
(3) Locally-produced fruits and vegetables are very far from meeting the needs of Hong Kong.
(4) If large areas of agricultural land are used for building public housing estates, the waiting time for public housing will be reduced to three years or less.
questions.explanation: Statements (1), (3), and (4) are factual or causal claims that can be tested against evidence. Statement (2) uses 'should' and is a normative value judgement.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem: Nan Fung Cotton Mills (南豐紗廠) was once the most productive textile mill in Hong Kong. Later, Nan Fung Group redeveloped the mill into an arts and retail complex. This is an example of using ___________ to solve the problem of ____________.
questions.explanation: A private firm responds to market incentives when it changes from textile production to arts and retail services. The decision changes the type of output, so it addresses what to produce.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: The Western Harbour Tunnel adjusted its tolls with effect from June 1, 2019.

choices.text: For private car drivers, the opportunity cost of using the Western Harbour Tunnel during peak hours must increase.
For motorcyclists, the opportunity cost of using the Western Harbour Tunnel during peak hours remains unchanged.
For taxi drivers, the opportunity cost of using the Western Harbour Tunnel during peak hours remains unchanged if they are carrying passengers, as the tolls are paid by passengers.
For bus passengers, the opportunity cost of taking a bus through the Western Harbour Tunnel during peak hours decreases.

questions.explanation: Eased congestion reduces travel time, so bus passengers give up less time when travelling through the tunnel. Opportunity cost includes time as well as the money toll, and it can change even where the money toll does not.

visuals.caption: Western Harbour Tunnel tolls from June 1, 2019

questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below show the cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm.
questions.explanation: Marginal costs are $5, $9, $13, $17 and $21. A price-taking firm chooses 4 units when market price is $17, since the fourth unit's marginal cost is $17 and the fifth's is $21. At 4 units, total revenue is $68 and total cost is $59, so profit is $9.

visuals.caption: Cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The law of diminishing marginal returns

choices.text: states that as a firm keeps increasing its output, it will eventually suffer losses.
states that as a firm keeps increasing the quantity of a variable factor, marginal product will decrease eventually in the short run.
states that the marginal product of a firm will eventually decrease in the long run.
is about the relationship between the quantity of variable factors and the total product of a firm in the short run.

questions.explanation: With at least one input fixed in the short run, adding more units of a variable factor eventually makes its marginal product fall. The law does not state that a firm must make losses and does not apply to the long run where all factors are variable.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Total product, average product and marginal product
questions.stem: The table below shows the input-output relationship of a firm. The firm employs two inputs only, namely capital and labour.

choices.text: The average product of capital is the highest when 5 units of capital are used.
The average product of capital is the highest when 6 units of capital are used.
Since labour is a fixed factor, the above information does not illustrate the law of diminishing marginal returns.
Since the total product keeps increasing, the above information does not illustrate the law of diminishing marginal returns.

questions.explanation: Average product of capital is 11, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 13 units respectively, so it peaks at 5 units. Labour being fixed is precisely the short-run setting for diminishing marginal returns, and total product can still rise while marginal product falls.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: In Hong Kong, which of the following is a feature of a private limited company?

choices.text: It is less profitable than a public limited company.
It operates on a larger scale than sole proprietorships and partnerships.
There is no upper limit on the number of owners.
Its shareholders may not be involved in the company’s management.

questions.explanation: Shareholders of a private limited company may be passive owners while directors manage the firm. Profitability and scale are not defining features, and the number of owners is limited.

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem: Making an online video involves different job roles, such as actors, photographers, makeup artists and directors. Which of the following is an advantage of the above arrangement?

choices.text: Workers are less likely to be unemployed.
Workers specialising in one task will find their job more interesting.
The best people can be chosen for each job.
Workers have stronger incentive to work as teamwork creates a pleasant atmosphere.

questions.explanation: Division of labour lets each task be allocated to people with the most suitable skills. It can make work repetitive and can increase vulnerability to unemployment, so the other statements are not general advantages.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem: In September, 2019, the Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (stock code: 0388) made a bid to take over the London Stock Exchange. Which of the following is the LEAST likely motive behind this expansion plan?

choices.text: to expand business to other markets

questions.explanation: An acquisition may reduce competition, create economies of scale, or provide access to other markets, but it cannot ensure a higher profit. Profit remains uncertain after expansion.

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: The table below shows the output-cost relationship of a firm.

choices.text: the firm’s profit-maximising output is 3,000 units.
diseconomies of scale sets in when total output exceeds 2,000 units.
the optimal scale of production is 3,000 units.
the firm enjoys economies of scale.

questions.explanation: Average cost falls from $35 at 1,000 units to $31.50 at 2,000 and $30 at 3,000. A falling long-run average cost indicates economies of scale; profit-maximising output and optimal scale require revenue or further cost information.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem: The government imposes an effective price ceiling on bottled water. At the same time, the production cost of bottled water increases. The producer surplus of bottled water ______________.
questions.explanation: An effective price ceiling lowers the money price producers receive, and a higher production cost raises marginal cost. Both changes reduce producer surplus, so it must decrease.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on consumer surplus
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram of good X.

choices.text: remain unchanged ... may increase or decrease

questions.explanation: The demand curve shifts from D1 to D2 while supply is unchanged. Equilibrium quantity rises, so the marginal cost along the upward-sloping supply curve increases. The demand increase raises consumer surplus in the diagram.

visuals.alt: A fixed supply curve S and a demand curve shifting right from D1 to D2 for good X.
visuals.caption: Demand shift for good X

movements: Demand shifts right from D1 to D2 while the supply curve is unchanged.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The higher equilibrium quantity moves up the unchanged supply curve, so marginal cost increases. The demand increase raises consumer surplus on the diagram.

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of nominal GDP and real GDP
questions.stem: The table below shows the GDP data of an economy in two years.

choices.text: Population remained unchanged from year 1 to year 2.
The general price level fell in year 2.
In year 2, nominal GDP was higher than real GDP.

questions.explanation: Population falls by 2% in each year. In Year 2, per-capita real GDP grows by 3%, more than enough to offset the 2% population fall, so total real output rises. Nominal growth exceeds real growth, indicating a rising rather than falling price level; nominal and real GDP levels cannot be compared directly without a base year.

columns: Growth rate (relative to the previous year) (%)
