questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: Which of the following will push up the unemployment rate of a country?

choices.text: The government lowers the statutory minimum wage level.
The government provides financial assistance to the long-term unemployed.
There is a significant increase in university places.
The government raises the subsidies for small and medium enterprises.

questions.explanation: Financial assistance can reduce the incentive for some long-term unemployed people to accept available jobs, tending to increase unemployment. A lower minimum wage, more university places, and more support for small and medium enterprises can instead reduce unemployment pressure.

questions.topicGroup: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.keyPoint: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.stem:
Which of the following are included in the calculation of Hong Kong’s GDP?

(1) Income earned by a foreign domestic helper working in Hong Kong
(2) Income earned by a Hong Kong investor who held a seminar in Hong Kong on investing in properties in Japan
(3) Rental income earned by a retired Hong Kong businessman from leasing his property in the United Kingdom
questions.explanation: GDP records production within Hong Kong regardless of the producer's nationality. The domestic helper's work and the seminar take place in Hong Kong, while rental income from a UK property is production outside Hong Kong.

questions.keyPoint: Production/value added approach
questions.stem: The following shows the production chain of a good in economy X.
questions.explanation: Local producers' value added is $400 of output less $60 local materials and $80 imported materials, or $260. Local retailers' market-price value added is $640; deducting the $60 tax included in sales to local consumers gives $580 at factor cost.

visuals.alt: Production chain linking local and imported materials, local producers, local retailers, and local and overseas consumers with values shown on each transaction.
visuals.caption: Production chain in economy X

movements: Local producers sell to local retailers and overseas consumers.
Local retailers sell to overseas consumers and local consumers.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Local producers add $260 of value. Local retailers add $640 at market price, less the $60 indirect tax, so their GDP-at-factor-cost contribution is $580.

questions.postVisualStem: The contributions of local producers and local retailers to the economy’s GDP at factor cost are __________ and __________ respectively.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.stem: Country A imports a large number of workers from Country B. Which of the following will cause Country A’s short run aggregate supply curve to shift to the left?

choices.text: Country A announces that it would abolish the quota on imported workers.
Firms in Country A adopt automated production technology to replace labour.
The average education level of labour in Country B increases.
Country B is in the phase of recovery, where the average wage level of its labour increases.

questions.explanation: Higher wages in Country B raise the cost of imported labour for Country A's firms, reducing short-run aggregate supply. The other changes raise labour availability, productivity, or production technology and shift SRAS right.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Refer to the following balance sheet of a banking system in an economy. Suppose the economy has a monetary base of $500 million, and the banking system has excess reserves of $30 million.

choices.text: Its monetary base will decrease by $200 million.
Its reserves will increase by $20 million.
Its money supply will increase by $720 million.

questions.explanation: Initial public cash is $200 million because reserves are $300 million within a $500 million monetary base. Required reserves are $270 million, giving a 25% required reserve ratio. After all cash is deposited and banks hold no excess reserves, deposits become $2,000 million and money supply rises from $1,280 million to $2,000 million, an increase of $720 million.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the public deposit all the cash into the banks and the banks no longer hold excess reserves. After the deposit creation process is completed, which of the following statements about the banking system is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: How central bank functions are carried out in
questions.stem:
In the first half of 2019, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has issued several virtual banking licences (虛擬銀行牌照) to allow qualified applicants to run virtual banking business. A HKMA spokesperson said they would assess the financial capability and risk management capability of applicants when considering applications.

In the above case, which central bank function does the HKMA perform?

choices.text: to act as a clearing house for transactions between commercial banks
to act as the government’s adviser

questions.explanation: Licensing virtual banks and assessing applicants' financial and risk-management capacity are supervisory functions over the monetary sector.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem:
Refer to the following news extract.

According to the above information, which functions of money can Libra perform?

(1) store of value
(2) standard of deferred payment
(3) medium of exchange
questions.explanation: Being pegged to a basket of currencies at fixed rates supports Libra's stability as a store of value, and the stated payments use makes it a medium of exchange. The extract gives no evidence that it serves as a standard of deferred payment.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate
questions.stem: Suppose the nominal interest rate is 3%, and the general price level is expected to remain unchanged. If the actual deflation rate is 4%, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: University scholarship holders who receive a fixed amount of money will lose.
The cost of holding cash is negative.
Expected real interest rate will be lower than the actual real interest rate.
The actual rate of return on holding cash is negative.

questions.explanation: The expected real interest rate is 3% because expected inflation is zero. Actual deflation of 4% makes the actual real interest rate 7%, so expected real interest is lower. A fixed scholarship and cash both gain purchasing power under unanticipated deflation.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Refer to the table below.

choices.text: policy II and policy III only

questions.explanation: Policy I is contractionary because it raises the required reserve ratio and sells government bonds. Policy II lowers money demand through wider stored-value payment access and raises money supply through an open-market purchase. Policy III is expansionary because it lowers the discount rate and required reserve ratio. Policies II and III therefore lower the nominal interest rate.

visuals.caption: Policies
rows:

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem: On August 15, 2019, Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po announced a 100% reduction in salaries tax for 2018/19, subject to a ceiling of $20,000. This measure would _________________.

choices.text: narrow the income gap between the rich and the poor
increase the consumption expenditure of Hong Kong people

questions.explanation: A salaries-tax rebate raises taxpayers' disposable income and tends to increase consumption expenditure. It reduces government revenue rather than increasing government expenditure, and it does not broaden the tax base or necessarily narrow the income gap.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram.

choices.text: The velocity of circulation of money is increasing.

questions.explanation: Using the quantity theory with velocity constant, growth in real output equals money-supply growth less growth in the general price level. The diagram shows this difference increasing, so real output is increasing. The positive growth rate of the general price level does not mean that the cost of living is falling.

visuals.alt: Growth rates of the general price level and money supply over time; the general-price-level growth rate slopes down and the money-supply growth rate slopes up.
visuals.caption: Growth rates in the quantity theory of money

movements: The money-supply growth rate rises while the growth rate of the general price level falls.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: With the velocity of circulation held constant, the widening gap between money-supply growth and price-level growth indicates rising real output under the quantity theory of money.

questions.postVisualStem: According to the quantity theory of money, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: Which of the following is a difference between progressive tax and regressive tax?

choices.text: Progressive tax violates Adam Smith's equity principle of taxation, but regressive tax does not.
A regressive tax system builds up a broader tax base than a progressive tax system.
A regressive tax system allows the government to collect more tax.
The income distribution becomes more even under a progressive tax system than under a regressive one.

questions.explanation: A progressive tax takes a larger proportion of income from higher-income earners and therefore tends to make post-tax income distribution more even than a regressive tax. The other statements are not inherent differences between the two systems.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Measurements of the general price level
questions.keyPoint: Calculate/Determine the rate of change in the general price level (inflation/ deflation rate) by using the CPI and the implicit price deflator of GDP
questions.stem: The chart below shows the Composite Consumer Price Index of Hong Kong from 2010 to 2018.

choices.text: consumers' standard of living kept falling.
The implicit price deflator of GDP increased.
The purchasing power of money decreased.
The Composite Consumer Price Index kept rising at an increasing rate.

questions.explanation: The CPI rises from 81.8 to 107, so a given amount of money buys less and its purchasing power decreases. The chart does not establish the GDP deflator or standard of living, and the annual CPI increases are not accelerating throughout.

visuals.alt: Composite Consumer Price Index rises from 81.8 in 2010 to 107 in 2018, with annual index values shown.
visuals.caption: Composite Consumer Price Index of Hong Kong, 2010-2018

movements: The CPI rises throughout the period, though not at an increasing rate in every year.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: A higher CPI means a lower purchasing power of money. The chart alone does not determine the GDP deflator or the standard of living.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: A country increases a sales tax imposed on sellers from 8% to 10%. At the same time, shopping coupons are provided by the government to low-income families.
questions.explanation: A higher sales tax raises firms' costs and shifts SRAS left. Shopping coupons raise consumption expenditure and shift AD right. Option A shows those two shifts.

visuals.alt: Four aggregate-demand and aggregate-supply diagram options labelled A to D, with curve shifts shown by arrows.
visuals.caption: Aggregate-output policy options

movements: A higher sales tax shifts SRAS left.
Shopping coupons for low-income families shift AD right.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option A is the only diagram that combines a leftward SRAS shift with a rightward AD shift.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following diagrams can best illustrate the effect of the above two policies on aggregate output?

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.stem: Which of the following would reduce the short run and long run aggregate supply of an economy?

choices.text: Economic recession leads to a decrease in the desire to consume, and some producers shut down their businesses.
More local consumers choose to consume in neighbouring countries.
The government cuts tax rebates on firms' expenditure on research and development.
A typhoon attack causes widespread power failure across the country.

questions.explanation: Cutting tax rebates for research and development lowers firms' incentive to improve technology. That reduces productive capacity in the long run and can also reduce short-run aggregate supply. The other options affect aggregate demand or only short-run production conditions.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Deflationary gap
questions.stem: Suppose an economy has a fiscal deficit and a deflationary (output) gap exists. _______________ would help reduce the deflationary (output) gap without worsening the fiscal deficit.

choices.text: An increase in the government's transfer payments
The central bank buying government bonds from the public
Reducing government expenditure on public services

questions.explanation: An open-market purchase is expansionary monetary policy: it raises money supply, lowers interest rates and increases aggregate demand without increasing the government's fiscal deficit. Higher transfer payments worsen the deficit, while the other two policies are contractionary.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of fiscal policy
questions.stem:
Which of the following is/are contractionary fiscal policy/policies?

(1) The central bank selling government bonds to the public
(2) The government imposes vacancy tax on first-hand residential properties
(3) The government introduces wage cuts on civil servants
questions.explanation: Selling government bonds is contractionary monetary policy, not fiscal policy. A vacancy tax raises government revenue and wage cuts reduce public expenditure, so (2) and (3) are contractionary fiscal policies.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: Before trade, Country A and Country B each uses 40% of their resources on producing watches and the rest on producing bread. The output of the two countries are as below:

choices.text: Country A has an absolute advantage and a comparative advantage in producing watches.
Country A has an absolute advantage in producing bread, while Country B has an absolute advantage in producing watches.
Only the total output of bread would increase after complete specialisation.
If the terms of trade is 1 unit of watches = 2.5 units of bread, there would be no trade between the two countries.

questions.explanation: Country A's opportunity cost of one watch is 4/3 units of bread, while Country B's is 2 units of bread. Mutually beneficial terms of trade must lie between them. At 2.5 units of bread per watch, Country B would not benefit from importing watches, so there would be no trade.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the case above is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the demand-supply diagram of good X in a small open economy.

choices.text: The domestic price of good X will be Pw.
The domestic price of good X will be equal to Pw + t.
The domestic price of good X will be higher than Pw + t.
The supply curve of good X will shift to the left.

questions.explanation: A small importing country takes the world price as given. The tariff raises its domestic price by exactly t to Pw + t. The rightward demand shift changes the amounts bought, sold and imported, but does not shift domestic supply or raise the price above Pw + t.

visuals.alt: Small open economy diagram with an upward supply curve S, demand curves D1 and D2, the world price Pw, and quantity Y1.
visuals.caption: Good X in a small open economy

movements: An import tariff raises the domestic price from Pw to Pw + t.
The demand curve shifts right from D1 to D2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: For a small importing economy, the domestic price remains Pw + t after the tariff; the demand increase changes quantities but not that price.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem:
Which of the following would be included in the calculation of Hong Kong's current account balance?

(1) Expenses of a Hong Kong athlete participating in an overseas competition
(2) A Hong Kong resident placing an international order for a toy model through a Hong Kong agent
(3) Expenses of a Hong Kong resident buying bonds of a British company through a local bank
questions.explanation: Overseas competition expenses are imports of services, and the international toy order is a goods transaction, so both enter the current account. Buying foreign bonds is a financial-account transaction, even when completed through a local bank.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: In which of the following situations is profit maximised?

choices.text: Total revenue is equal to total cost.
Marginal revenue is equal to zero.
The difference between marginal cost and marginal revenue is zero.

questions.explanation: Profit is maximised at an output where marginal revenue equals marginal cost, provided the usual profit-maximising condition holds. Equal total revenue and total cost merely means zero profit.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The following table shows the cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm.
questions.explanation: Initially, the firm produces four units, earning $72 and paying total cost of $58, so profit is $14. After every marginal cost falls by $4, total cost is $42 at four units and $60 at five units; profit is $30 at either output. Profit therefore rises by $16.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in demand
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in demand
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the demand curve of music CDs.

choices.text: A famous Korean singer passes away.
The price of music CDs increases.
The number of online music streaming platforms increases.
People expect the price of music CDs to increase.

questions.explanation: More online music streaming platforms make a substitute more available, reducing demand for music CDs and shifting the demand curve left from D1 to D2. A change in the CD price is a movement along demand, while expected price rises tend to increase current demand.

visuals.alt: Demand for music CDs shifts left from D1 to D2, with price and quantity axes.
visuals.caption: Demand for music CDs

movements: Demand shifts left from D1 to D2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: More online music streaming platforms provide substitutes for music CDs, reducing demand for CDs and shifting the curve left.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following situations would most likely lead to the shift of the demand curve from D₁ to D₂?

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem: In which of the following pairs does the demand for the first good create a derived demand for the second one?
questions.explanation: Doctors are labour inputs used by hospitals to provide health-care services. Demand for hospitals' services therefore creates derived demand for doctors. The other pairs are consumer goods that are complements or substitutes, not a final product and a factor of production.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem: Holding other factors constant, when the price of good X falls, the change in the total revenue of good Y will be uncertain if __________.

choices.text: good X and good Y are substitutes
good X and good Y are complements
good X and good Y are in joint supply
the demand for good Y is derived from the demand for good X

questions.explanation: If X and Y are jointly supplied, a lower price of X reduces the incentive to supply both goods, shifting Y's supply left. Y's price rises and quantity sold falls, so the change in its total revenue depends on the elasticity of demand for Y and is uncertain.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: When there are more people interested in yoga and more people teaching yoga, the equilibrium quantity of yoga courses __________.

choices.text: may increase, decrease or remain unchanged

questions.explanation: More interested people increase demand, while more teachers increase supply. Both changes raise the equilibrium quantity, although their effects on price work in opposite directions.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the supply and demand curves of self-service laundry services. E0 is the initial equilibrium point.
questions.explanation: Household washing machines are substitutes for laundry services, so their lower price shifts demand from D0 to D2. More laundries shift supply from S0 to S1. The new equilibrium is E4.

visuals.alt: Supply curves S2, S0 and S1, demand curves D2, D0 and D1, and equilibrium points E0 to E4 for self-service laundry services.
visuals.caption: Self-service laundry services

movements: Cheaper household washing machines shift demand left from D0 to D2.
More self-service laundries shift supply right from S0 to S1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The intersection of D2 and S1 is E4.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the price of household washing machines decreases and the number of self-service laundries increases by 20% compared to last year. The new equilibrium point will be at __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Which of the following would raise the elasticity of demand for the smartphones produced by Apple Inc.?

choices.text: Samsung raises the selling price of its smartphones.
Apple Inc. lowers the selling price of its smartphone accessories.
Samsung launches a new model of smartphone.
The firm producing phone screens for Apple Inc. has excess capacity in production.

questions.explanation: A new Samsung smartphone creates an additional close substitute, making consumers more responsive to changes in Apple's smartphone price. The other changes do not increase the availability of substitutes for Apple's phones.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: Suppose there is an increasing number of people raising pets. Which of the following situations would cause a smaller increase in the price of pet products?

choices.text: the stock of pet products in the market is low
the producers of pet products have excess capacity in production
the workers producing pet products have low occupational mobility
licences are required to produce pet products

questions.explanation: Excess production capacity makes supply more elastic, so an increase in demand can be met mainly with a larger quantity and a smaller rise in price. The other conditions make supply less elastic.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
The following is the interface of an online shopping platform.

Which of the following situations would lower someone's opportunity cost of buying a bottle of disinfectant on the above platform using home delivery?

(1) Location of the pickup store is further than expected.
(2) The online shopping platform waives the delivery fee for all orders.
(3) The disinfectant is delivered to his home two days earlier than scheduled.
questions.explanation: If store pickup becomes less convenient, its value as the next-best alternative falls. Waiving the delivery fee also lowers the sacrifice required for home delivery. Delivery two days earlier improves the benefit received rather than lowering its opportunity cost.

visuals.title: Online shopping platform
visuals.text:
Online Shopping Street
Product: Disinfectant (500ml)
Quantity: 1
Price: $50

Pickup method:
- Store pickup
- Home delivery (Delivery fee $20, deliver in 1 week)

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are normative statements?

(1) The stock of masks is not enough for all people in Hong Kong.
(2) Mask producers should sell masks to the elderly first.
(3) Retailers should not raise the price of masks when there is an outbreak of disease.
(4) Surgical masks are more effective in preventing infection than dust masks.
questions.explanation: Statements (2) and (3) use 'should' and make value judgements, so they are normative. Statements (1) and (4) can be checked against facts and are positive statements.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: After conducting a survey, a bookstore decides to source more travel guidebooks to meet the demand of customers. The above case is related to the __________ question(s) in Economics.

choices.text: 'what to produce' and 'for whom to produce'

questions.explanation: The bookstore is deciding the type and quantity of guidebooks to stock. That is a decision about what to produce, not about the allocation of output or the production technique.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about a market economy is CORRECT?

choices.text: Most resources are allocated by merchants.
Private property rights exist in the economy.
Non-price competition does not exist in the economy.
People in the economy are richer than those in a command economy.

questions.explanation: A market economy recognises private property rights and allocates resources mainly through market forces. It can have non-price competition, and it does not guarantee a higher income level than a command economy.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem: Xiaomi Corporation (Stock Code: 1810) is a producer of electronic products. In 2019, it planned to expand its business to the banking industry via opening a virtual bank in Hong Kong and a digital bank in Singapore. Which of the following statements about Xiaomi Corporation is CORRECT?

choices.text: Its shareholders can only transfer shares with the consent of other shareholders.
Its shareholders are responsible for those business decisions made by another shareholder.
This expansion can raise its market share.
This expansion can spread risk by business diversification.

questions.explanation: Expanding from electronic products into banking is diversification, which can spread business risk. A public limited company's shares are transferable, shareholders have limited liability, and the expansion does not necessarily raise Xiaomi's market share in its original market.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of issuing shares and bonds to raise capital
questions.stem: From the viewpoint of existing shareholders, which of the following is the advantage of issuing shares instead of bonds to raise capital?

choices.text: Issuing shares will not increase the risk of the company being taken over by others.
The company has no obligation to pay dividends.
Issuing shares can raise more capital than issuing bonds.
Shareholders of the company can enjoy limited liability.

questions.explanation: Unlike interest on bonds, dividends are not a fixed legal obligation. Existing shareholders can benefit from the lower financial commitment. Issuing more shares can dilute control and does not guarantee more capital, while limited liability is not an advantage created by choosing shares over bonds.

questions.keyPoint: Describe the inter-relationship between the three types of production
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the relationship of the three stages of production.
questions.explanation: Secondary production turns raw materials into producer goods and uses services. Tertiary production supplies services and receives producer goods. Thus Y is secondary production, X is tertiary production and Z is primary production.

visuals.alt: A three-way diagram of production stages with X at the top, Y at the lower left and Z at the lower right. Arrows are labelled Producer goods, Services and Raw materials.
visuals.caption: Relationship between the three stages of production

movements: Primary production supplies raw materials to secondary production.
Secondary production supplies producer goods to tertiary production.
Tertiary production supplies services to secondary production.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: X is tertiary production and Y is secondary production; the remaining stage Z is primary production.

questions.postVisualStem: X and Y stand for __________ and __________ respectively.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital
questions.stem:
Which of the following are capital of a claw-machine shop?

(1) claw machines
(2) coin exchange machines
(3) soft toys
(4) the premises
questions.explanation: Capital comprises man-made resources used in production. The machines, the shop premises and soft toys used to provide the claw-machine service are all produced resources used by the business.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem: The French government proposes to raise the age at which workers can receive a full pension from 62 to 64. The __________ in France will __________.
questions.explanation: Raising the full-pension age gives people an incentive to remain in employment for longer, increasing the labour supply. It does not directly determine occupational mobility.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: Some property agencies pay their employees a basic salary plus commission, while some pay a commission only. Compared to those paying a commission only, which of the following statements about agencies paying a basic salary plus commission is CORRECT?

choices.text: The employees have a higher income.
The cost of calculating wages is lower.
The performance of the employees is better.
Fewer employees will quit when the economy turns down.

questions.explanation: A basic salary gives employees a more stable income when sales are weak, reducing the incentive to quit in a downturn. It does not guarantee higher income or performance, and calculating both a salary and commission is not simpler.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X.

choices.text: The tax burden borne by the sellers is $12.
The total sales revenue (net-of-tax) decreases by $2.
The demand for good X is more elastic than the supply of them.
Within the range of the original and the new equilibrium prices, the elasticity of demand of good X is smaller than one.

questions.explanation: Before tax, equilibrium is $14 and 7 units. After the tax, buyers pay $16 and sellers receive $12 for 6 units. Sellers bear $2 per unit for 6 units, or $12 in total. The other statements do not follow from the schedule.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: When the government imposes a per-unit tax on good X, the quantity transacted of good X decreases by 1 unit. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X, on which a per-unit subsidy of $2 is provided by the government.

choices.text: The total sales revenue of sellers will increase by $400.
The total subsidy granted by the government will increase by $800.
The ratio of the buyers' subsidy benefit to the sellers' subsidy benefit will not change.
The change in buyers' total expenditure on good X's substitutes is uncertain.

questions.explanation: With a $2 subsidy, buyers pay $12 and sellers receive $14 for 400 units. With a $4 subsidy, buyers pay $11 and sellers receive $15 for 450 units. In both cases buyers and sellers each receive half of the per-unit subsidy, so their benefit ratio remains unchanged.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the per-unit subsidy provided by the government increases from $2 to $4. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Identify the type of market structure
questions.stem: The market structure of the Western restaurant market in Hong Kong is regarded as ___________, because ____________________________.

choices.text: perfect competition ... Western restaurants can enter or exit the market without restriction
monopolistic competition ... there are many Western restaurants selling heterogeneous products
oligopoly ... many Western restaurants engage in non-price competition
oligopoly ... Western restaurants can raise their prices without losing all customers

questions.explanation: Western restaurants are numerous and differentiate their food, service and ambience, which is monopolistic competition. Non-price competition and some price-setting power do not by themselves show oligopoly.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: A government increases the effective quota on good X. At the same time, the price of good X's complements decreases. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The market price of good X will increase.
The total social surplus will increase.

questions.explanation: Relaxing an effective quota reduces the distortion and deadweight loss. A lower price of complements raises demand for X. The combined changes increase total social surplus, while the directions of consumer surplus, producer surplus and price are not those stated in the other options.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on consumer surplus
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram of good X.

choices.text: may increase or decrease ... will increase
may increase or decrease ... may increase or decrease

questions.explanation: Supply is perfectly inelastic, so quantity stays fixed. Because the two demand curves are parallel, the rise in price exactly offsets the upward shift in willingness to pay at that quantity, leaving consumer surplus unchanged. Producer surplus rises with the higher price.

visuals.alt: A vertical supply curve S and a demand curve shifting right from D1 to D2 for good X.
visuals.caption: Demand shift with perfectly inelastic supply

movements: Demand shifts right from D1 to D2 while supply is perfectly inelastic.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Quantity is fixed. The price rise increases producer surplus, while the consumer-surplus effect depends on the size of the demand shift and price change.

questions.postVisualStem: If the demand curve of good X shifts parallelly from D₁ to D₂, the consumer surplus ___________ and the producer surplus ____________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price floor
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram of good X.

choices.text: the deadweight loss will remain unchanged.
the excess demand for good X will be eliminated.

questions.explanation: The higher effective price floor raises the price received by producers on the quantity sold, increasing producer surplus on the diagram. It creates excess supply and a deadweight loss; it does not eliminate excess demand, and consumer surplus does not increase.

visuals.alt: Demand curve D, supply curve S, and two horizontal price levels P1 and P2, with P2 above P1.
visuals.caption: Price floor of good X

movements: The price floor is raised from P1 to P2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: At a higher effective price floor, consumer surplus can increase depending on how the reduced quantity available is allocated; a deadweight loss is created and excess supply is not eliminated.

questions.postVisualStem: If the government raises the price floor of good X from P₁ to P₂,

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem:
Refer to the following news excerpt.

This is an example of divergence between private and social _________ and the _________ solution is being considered to reduce the divergence.
questions.explanation: A symptomatic patient's travel can impose infection risks on others that the patient does not bear, so marginal social cost exceeds marginal private cost. Laws that punish harmful behaviour are a government solution to internalise that external cost.

visuals.title: News excerpt
visuals.text: The government of a country worries that if a novel coronavirus pneumonia patient with symptoms travels overseas, the virus will be spread, and more people will be infected. The government is considering passing laws to punish behaviours that harm public health.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: There are street performers who sing and dance in Tuen Mun Park. Some park users think the performances create noise nuisance for others. Which of the following statements about the above case is CORRECT?

choices.text: The quantity of street performances is at the socially optimal level.
If the street performers pay the park users who feel annoying for allowing them to keep performing in the park, efficiency will be improved.
There is a divergence between private and social costs and the performances are under-produced.
The government should ban street performance to improve efficiency.

questions.explanation: The nuisance is a negative externality, so street performances tend to be over-produced rather than socially optimal. A negotiated payment to affected users can internalise the external cost and improve efficiency; a complete ban is not necessarily efficient.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising opportunities
questions.stem:
Due to a decline in the local student population, the enrolment of some self-financing post-secondary institutions is far less than the number of places available. The government raises the subsidy amount of the Non-means-tested Subsidy Scheme for Self-financing Undergraduate Studies in Hong Kong in the 2019/20 academic year to $31,300. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The excess supply of self-financing undergraduate programmes will decrease.
(2) The deadweight loss will increase.
(3) The above measure helps equalise opportunities.
questions.explanation: The subsidy raises demand for the programmes, reducing excess supply and the associated deadweight loss. It also helps students access education, so it equalises opportunities. Statements (1) and (3) are correct.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem:
Which of the following policies can reduce the Gini coefficient based on post-tax post-social transfer monthly household income in Hong Kong?

(1) providing a cash subsidy for those who have been on the waiting list for public housing over three years
(2) raising the eligible age for the elderly Comprehensive Social Security Assistance Scheme from 60 to 65
(3) raising the subsidy amount of the Public Transport Fare Subsidy Scheme
questions.explanation: A cash subsidy for households waiting for public housing and a larger public-transport fare subsidy support lower-income households and can narrow post-transfer income inequality. Raising the eligible age for elderly assistance removes support from some recipients, so it does not reduce the Gini coefficient.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which of the following is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

choices.text: When the lump-sum delivery fee for online shopping increases, consumers tend to buy more every time they purchase.
When the government imposes an ad valorem tax on all first-hand residential properties, the average quality of residential properties sold increases.

When the airport departure tax, which charges a fixed amount for any passenger, is abolished, the number of short-distance trips increases by a smaller percentage than the number of long-distance trips.
After the fixed penalty for illegal parking is raised, the number of illegal parking prosecutions decreases.

questions.explanation: Removing a fixed airport-departure tax reduces the full price of a short trip by a larger percentage than that of a long trip. The law of demand therefore predicts a larger, not smaller, percentage increase in short-distance trips. The other cases can be explained by changes in full or relative price.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings of joint supply and competitive supply
questions.stem: Suppose wearing leather shoes becomes more popular. This will lead to a decrease in the __________ leather belts if leather belts and leather shoes are in _______________.
questions.explanation: Leather shoes and belts in competitive supply compete for productive resources. More popular shoes draw resources toward shoe production, decreasing the supply of belts.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings of complements, substitutes, normal and inferior goods
questions.stem: The Hong Kong government considers raising the environmental levy on plastic shopping bags from $0.5 to $1 each. This measure will lead to an increase in __________.

choices.text: the supply of plastic shopping bags
the government revenue from the levy
consumers' total expenditure on non-woven shopping bags
consumers' total expenditure on plastic shopping bags

questions.explanation: The higher levy raises the full price of plastic bags. Non-woven bags are substitutes, so demand and total expenditure on them increase. Government levy revenue and plastic-bag expenditure are not guaranteed to rise because quantity demanded of plastic bags falls.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the tax burden
questions.stem: When a government imposes a per-unit tax on a good, consumers' tax burden is equal to producers' tax burden. This implies that

choices.text: the market price of the good remains unchanged.
the demand for the good is unitarily elastic.
the demand for the good is perfectly inelastic.
the demand for the good is as elastic as the supply of it.

questions.explanation: The side with the less elastic curve bears more of a unit-tax burden. Equal tax burdens therefore imply demand and supply have equal elasticity at the relevant equilibrium.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand and supply schedules for good X.

choices.text: The surplus of good X will decrease by 2 units.
It will be more difficult for poor people to buy good X.
The quantity transacted will decrease by 1 unit.
Consumers' total expenditure on good X will increase by $22.

questions.explanation: At the $12 ceiling, only 4 units are supplied and consumers spend $48. At the $14 ceiling, 5 units are supplied and consumers spend $70. Expenditure therefore rises by $22; the shortage falls rather than a surplus arising, and quantity transacted increases by one unit.

visuals.caption: Demand and supply schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government increases the price ceiling from $12 to $14. According to the above table, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: The following is the demand-supply diagram of good X.

choices.text: If the government provides a per-unit subsidy of $8 for good X, total revenue including the subsidy will decrease by $12.
If the government sets a price floor on good X at $22, the quantity transacted will be between 12 units and 15 units.
If the government imposes a quota of 18 units on good X, the market price will increase by $4.
If the government imposes a per-unit tax of $8 on good X, consumers' tax burden will be $96.

questions.explanation: A $22 price floor is above equilibrium. Demand at that price is between 12 and 15 units, and this demand-limited amount is the quantity transacted. The other conclusions do not follow from the numerical guides in the diagram.

visuals.alt: Demand curve D and supply curve S for good X, intersecting at E with price $20 and quantity 15. Dashed guides mark prices $16 and $24 and quantities 12 and 18.
visuals.caption: Demand and supply of good X

movements: A price floor at $22 lies above the equilibrium price and limits quantity transacted by demand.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: At a $22 price floor, the quantity demanded lies between 12 and 15 units, so that is the quantity transacted.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the initial equilibrium point is point E. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: In Hong Kong, the charges of telecommunications service providers are different. This is because

choices.text: there are many telecommunications service providers in the market.
the services provided by telecommunications service providers are heterogeneous.
huge investment is required to enter the telecommunications service market.

questions.explanation: Telecommunications plans differ in coverage, data allowances, contracts and service features. Such heterogeneous services allow providers to charge different prices.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Rationing function
questions.stem:
After a famous basketball player passed away, the prices of his second-hand signature basketball shoes have increased by around 6 times.

The above case illustrates the ___________ function of price because ___________.

choices.text: allocative ... the prices transmit information about consumer preference to the producers
allocative ... the producers can increase the supply to earn a higher profit
rationing ... the shoes were distributed to the fans who love him the most
rationing ... the shoes were distributed to the highest-valued buyers

questions.explanation: The sharply higher price allocates the scarce shoes to consumers willing and able to pay the most, who are the highest-valued buyers. That is the rationing function of price.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on consumer surplus
questions.stem: If there is an increase in people's acceptance of electronic books, the marginal cost of electronic books will _____________ and the consumer surplus ____________.
questions.explanation: Higher acceptance raises demand for electronic books. Along the upward-sloping supply curve, the higher equilibrium output has a higher marginal cost, while the demand increase raises consumer surplus.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between marginal benefit and demand
questions.stem: The Hong Kong government has not issued urban taxi licences since 1994. In recent years, there has been an increasing number of people using illegal private car hire services (commonly known as 'white licence car services'). Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The marginal benefit of urban taxi licences would decrease.
The quantity demanded of urban taxi licences would decrease.
There would be a surplus of urban taxi licences.
The total value of urban taxi licences might increase, decrease or remain unchanged.

questions.explanation: Illegal private car-hire services are substitutes for licensed taxis, lowering the marginal benefit of an additional urban taxi licence. The fixed licence supply does not imply a surplus, and the other statements are not the direct conclusion about marginal benefit.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Mr. Chan planned to visit Wuhan in China. He was informed that there was an outbreak of the novel coronavirus in Wuhan before setting off for the city. The opportunity cost for Mr. Chan to continue going to Wuhan would _____________ because _____________.

choices.text: increase ... he had to buy masks to prevent infection before setting off for the city
increase ... there was a higher chance for him to get infected
remain unchanged ... the number of days he would stay in the city did not change
decrease ... tourist attractions in the city might be temporarily closed

questions.explanation: A higher chance of infection is an additional cost of continuing the trip, so the opportunity cost rises. The cost of masks is only a money expense if he chooses to buy them, and unchanged travel days or closed attractions do not establish a lower opportunity cost.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
Which of the following cases are related to the problem of 'for whom to produce'?

(1) A Japanese restaurant introduces a vegetarian menu.
(2) The government raises the maximum income limit for public rental housing.
(3) A university increases the number of places to admit more overseas students.
questions.explanation: The public-rental-housing income limit determines who can receive housing, and admitting more overseas students determines who receives university places. Both concern for whom to produce. A vegetarian menu concerns what to produce.

questions.topicGroup: Meaning of public ownership and examples of organisations or institutions in operating under public ownership
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of public ownership and examples of organisations or institutions in operating under public ownership
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about public corporations in Hong Kong is CORRECT?

choices.text: Public corporations will not suffer a loss.
Staff of public corporations are civil servants.
The services provided by public corporations are all free of charge.
Public corporations are financially independent of the government.

questions.explanation: Public corporations are separate legal entities with their own finances, although they are government-owned. They may make losses, their staff are not necessarily civil servants, and they may charge for services.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
The owners of a firm bear unlimited liability. If they want to expand the business, they can _____________ to raise capital.

(1) invite other people to join the firm and be an owner
(2) borrow from banks
(3) issue shares to the public
questions.explanation: Unlimited liability indicates a sole proprietorship or partnership. It can add owners or borrow from banks, but it cannot issue shares to the public because that requires a public limited company with limited liability.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: The weather forecast service provided by Hong Kong Observatory is a ____________.

choices.text: public good because it is provided by a government department
public good because it can be consumed by many people concurrently
free good because the cost of serving an additional person is zero
free good because people do not need to pay for the weather forecast service

questions.explanation: Weather forecasts are non-rival in consumption: many people can use the same forecast at the same time. Government provision or a zero money price does not by itself define a public or free good.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital
questions.stem:
Which of the following are capital of a zoo?

(1) the zoo guides
(2) the drinks brought into the zoo by the visitors
(3) the travel brochures printed by the zoo
(4) the animals raised in the zoo
questions.explanation: Capital is a man-made resource used in production. The zoo's brochures and animals are used to provide its service. Guides are labour, and drinks brought in by visitors are consumer goods rather than the zoo's capital.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following measures may raise the labour supply and average labour productivity of Hong Kong at the same time?

choices.text: providing a subsidy to enterprises for installing advanced machines
providing more on-the-job training for workers
relaxing licensing requirements for overseas specialist doctors to work in Hong Kong

questions.explanation: Relaxing the licensing requirements admits more specialist doctors into the workforce and raises its average productivity. The other measures may affect working conditions, capital or skills, but do not clearly increase both the labour supply and average labour productivity at once.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem:
Some restaurants allow their waiters to keep the tips given by the customers for themselves while some require their waiters to hand over all the tips.

Compared to the restaurants that require their waiters to hand over all the tips, the restaurants that allow their waiters to keep the tips

(1) have a lower cost of monitoring the performance of the waiters.
(2) transfer part of the business risk to the waiters.
(3) have a lower cost of measuring the output of the waiters.
questions.explanation: Tips give waiters an incentive to provide good service, reducing monitoring cost. Their variable income also transfers part of the business risk to them. The arrangement does not reduce the cost of measuring their output.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of internal expansion
questions.stem: Hong Kong Television Network Limited (stock code: 1137) operates an online shopping platform. In February 2020, the company announced that it had purchased mask machines from overseas and expanded its business into mask production. Which of the following is the LEAST likely motive behind the expansion?

choices.text: to earn a higher profit for the company
to extend its brand name to other products
to spread risk by business diversification

questions.explanation: Buying machinery to add mask production is internal expansion and diversification. Higher profit, brand extension and risk spreading are plausible motives, but it does not reduce competition by acquiring or combining with a competitor.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm.
questions.explanation: At three units, total revenue is $18. Average variable cost is $4, so total variable cost is $12 and total cost is $13 after adding fixed cost. Profit is $18 - $13 = $5, which is higher than at the other outputs.

visuals.caption: Cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the market price is $6 and the fixed cost is $1. What is the profit of the firm?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Disincentive effects of taxes and transfers
questions.keyPoint: Explain why some policy instruments that aim at equalising income (e.g. taxes and transfers) may have disincentive effects
questions.stem: The Hong Kong government plans to provide a cash allowance for people who are unemployed for one month or longer through the Community Care Fund. Which of the following statements about the measure is CORRECT?

choices.text: This will lead to an increase in the unemployment rate because people's opportunity cost of quitting their jobs will decrease.
This will help equalise opportunities because the unemployed will tend to have a higher incentive to look for a job.
This will increase income inequality because the employed cannot enjoy the cash allowance.
This will increase the gross domestic product because government consumption expenditure will increase.

questions.explanation: A cash allowance available after becoming unemployed reduces the financial cost of quitting a job, so it can create a disincentive to remain employed and raise unemployment. It does not give unemployed people a higher incentive to find work, and transfer payments are not government consumption expenditure in GDP.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem:
Refer to the following policies.

Policy (1): raise the standard tax rate of the salaries tax
Policy (2): provide extra cash allowance for receivers of Comprehensive Social Security Assistance Scheme
Policy (3): provide a public transport subsidy for working people

Which of the above policies can reduce the post-tax post-social transfer Gini coefficient?
questions.explanation: A higher salaries-tax standard rate reduces post-tax income at the upper end, extra CSSA helps lower-income households, and a public-transport subsidy for working people can benefit lower-income workers. Each measure can reduce the post-tax post-social transfer Gini coefficient.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: A Hong Kong resident received rental income from a residential property in Japan. Hong Kong's gross domestic product of the current year would _________ while the gross national income would _________.
questions.explanation: The rental income is produced outside Hong Kong, so it is not part of Hong Kong GDP. As income received by a Hong Kong resident from abroad, it increases Hong Kong GNI.

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of nominal GDP and real GDP
questions.stem: Suppose a closed economy produces rice and garments only. The output of Year 1 and Year 2 are as follows:
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP is $624 in Year 1 and $690 in Year 2, so (1) is true. Using either year's prices, real GDP is higher in Year 1 because the fall in garment output more than offsets the rise in rice output, so (2) is false. Prices are higher in Year 2, hence money has lower purchasing power then and (3) is true.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the economy are CORRECT?

(1) The nominal GDP in Year 1 is lower than that in Year 2.
(2) The real GDP in Year 1 is lower than that in Year 2.
(3) The purchasing power of money in Year 1 is higher than that in Year 2.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of per capita GDP
questions.stem: The general price level of Country A decreases by 1%. Its population and nominal GDP increase by 4% and 2% respectively. As a result, the per capita nominal GDP of Country A will __________ and its per capita real GDP will __________.
questions.explanation: Per capita nominal GDP changes by roughly 2% minus 4%, so it falls. Real GDP rises by roughly 2% plus 1% because the price level falls, but real GDP per capita still falls after the 4% population increase.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.stem: The government of a country plans to build a theme park to attract more tourists. Which of the following best illustrates the effect of the above plan on the country ten years later?
questions.explanation: Tourist spending increases aggregate demand. Ten years later the new theme park also increases productive capacity, so long-run aggregate supply shifts right. Diagram C shows both changes.

visuals.alt: Four AS-AD diagram options. Option C shows AD shifting right from AD1 to AD2 and LRAS shifting right from LRAS1 to LRAS2.
visuals.caption: Possible long-run effects of building a theme park

movements: More tourists increase aggregate demand.
The theme park expands productive capacity, shifting LRAS right in the long run.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option C is correct because both aggregate demand and long-run aggregate supply rise ten years later.

questions.topicGroup: Licensed banks, restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies in
questions.keyPoint: Features of the three types of deposit-taking institutions
questions.stem: William wants to deposit HK$180,000 for two months in an authorised institution in Hong Kong. Which of the following types of account can he choose and earn the highest return?

choices.text: a current account with a licensed bank
a time deposit account with a licensed bank
a time deposit account with a restricted licence bank
a time deposit account with a deposit-taking company

questions.explanation: A licensed bank can accept a two-month deposit of HK$180,000, whereas restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies have higher minimum deposit requirements. A time deposit earns more interest than a current account.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem:
Winnie withdraws HK$300,000 from her current account with a licensed bank. Then she keeps HK$50,000 at home. She deposits HK$100,000 into her savings account and remits the remainder overseas.

What will be the immediate effect of the above actions on the Hong Kong dollar money supply?

choices.text: M1 will decrease by HK$250,000 and M2 will decrease by HK$50,000.
M1 will decrease by HK$250,000 and M2 will decrease by HK$150,000.
M2 will increase by HK$100,000 and M3 will decrease by HK$150,000.
M2 will remain unchanged and M3 will decrease by HK$150,000.

questions.explanation: The $50,000 held as cash remains in M1. Moving $100,000 to savings removes it from M1 but keeps it in M2, while the $150,000 remitted overseas leaves M1, M2 and M3. M1 therefore falls by $250,000 and M2 falls by $150,000.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about an economy.

choices.text: The banking system can expand its total deposits to $9,000.
The maximum possible amount of loans is $5,250.
The maximum possible amount of money supply is $6,750.

questions.explanation: With $500 held as cash, actual bank reserves are $1,500. The actual banking multiplier of 3 implies actual deposits of $4,500, so the required reserve ratio is $1,000 / $4,500. At that ratio, $1,500 of bank reserves can support maximum deposits of $6,750 and therefore maximum loans of $5,250.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the public always hold $500 cash. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money demand and money supply curves of an economy. The original equilibrium point is at E.
questions.explanation: A more volatile stock market increases asset demand for money, while a lower required reserve ratio increases money supply. The two shifts meet at B in the diagram.

visuals.alt: Money demand curves Md0, Md1 and Md2, money supply curves MS0, MS1 and MS2, and points A, B, C, D and E. E is the original equilibrium.
visuals.caption: Money market

movements: A more volatile stock market shifts money demand right from Md0 to Md2.
A lower required reserve ratio increases money supply from MS0 to MS2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The two changes move the equilibrium from E to B.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the stock market becomes more volatile and the central bank reduces the required reserve ratio. The new equilibrium point will be at __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Effects of inflation and deflation on different aspects
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the growth rate of GDP deflator of Country A.

choices.text: the general price level remains unchanged.
the nominal GDP is equal to the real GDP.
the purchasing power of money is decreasing.

questions.explanation: The GDP deflator grows at a positive rate throughout the period, so the general price level rises. As prices rise, each unit of money buys less and the purchasing power of money decreases.

visuals.alt: The growth rate of GDP deflator remains above zero throughout the period.
visuals.caption: Growth rate of GDP deflator of Country A

movements: The growth rate remains positive throughout the period.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: A positive GDP-deflator growth rate means the general price level rises, so the purchasing power of money falls.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Nominal interest rate as the (opportunity) cost of holding money
questions.stem: Assume that the nominal interest rate is 4% and the expected inflation rate is 2%. If the actual inflation rate is 3%, ______________.

choices.text: the cost of holding money will be 4%
the nominal rate of return on holding money will be 1%
people who receive a fixed amount of monthly unemployment benefit will gain
people who pay a fixed amount of monthly rental payment will lose

questions.explanation: The opportunity cost of holding money is the nominal interest rate, which is 4%. Actual inflation affects realised real returns and redistributes purchasing power, but it does not change this stated nominal holding cost.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: According to the quantity theory of money, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: If the price level increases, the money supply will increase by the same percentage.
If the money supply increases, the price level may decrease.
If the money supply increases by 5%, the nominal output may increase by less than 5%.
If the nominal output increases, the velocity of circulation of money will increase.

questions.explanation: From MV = PY, a larger money supply does not by itself determine the price level: a sufficiently large rise in real output can more than offset it. The other statements impose relationships not implied by the quantity equation.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: Country A's government recruits retired medical staff to fill job vacancies. Country A's labour force will __________ and the unemployment rate will __________.
questions.explanation: The recruited retirees join the labour force and become employed. The number of unemployed is unchanged while the labour force is larger, so the unemployment rate falls.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Which of the following will reduce the effectiveness of an expansionary monetary policy on real output?

choices.text: There is insufficient demand for loans.
The public deposit most of their cash into the banking system.
The actual reserves of commercial banks are lower than the required reserves.

questions.explanation: Expansionary monetary policy relies on lower interest rates and greater lending. Insufficient demand for loans prevents the increased lending capacity from translating into spending and real-output growth.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: Refer to the following AS-AD diagram.

choices.text: raising the statutory minimum wage rate
simplifying the procedures for importing foreign labour
selling government bonds in the open market

questions.explanation: E1 is to the left of LRAS. Easier importation of labour expands aggregate supply and helps the economy move toward long-run equilibrium. The other policies are contractionary or raise production costs.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with LRAS to the right of short-run equilibrium E1, showing a deflationary gap.
visuals.caption: AS-AD diagram

movements: The initial short-run equilibrium E1 lies to the left of LRAS.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Simplifying the import of foreign labour lowers production costs and expands aggregate supply, helping the economy move toward long-run equilibrium.

questions.postVisualStem:
The economy initially operates at E1. Which of the following policies can help restore the economy to its long

run equilibrium?

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Deflationary gap
questions.stem: Suppose there is a deflationary gap in a country. An academic suggests the government reduce the discount rate or increase the production subsidy for small-sized enterprises to restore the economy to its long run equilibrium. Which of the following is the advantage of an increase the production subsidy for small-sized enterprises over a reduction in the discount rate to narrow the deflationary gap?

choices.text: Income distribution will be more even.
The unemployment rate will be lower.
The real output level will be higher.
The cost of living will be lower.

questions.explanation: A lower discount rate is expansionary monetary policy and shifts AD right, tending to raise the price level. A production subsidy lowers firms' costs and shifts SRAS right, allowing the gap to close with a lower cost of living.

questions.keyPoint: Direct tax and indirect tax
questions.stem: Some stakeholders from the hotel industry suggest the government exempt them from paying rates to help the industry cope with the impact of a reduction in the number of tourists. Which of the following statements about the suggestion is CORRECT?

choices.text: Hong Kong's general price level will increase.
The proportion of direct tax revenue in total government revenue will increase.
There will be a fiscal deficit.

questions.explanation: Rates are an indirect tax. Exempting hotels reduces this indirect-tax revenue, so the proportion of direct-tax revenue in total government revenue rises. The exemption neither guarantees a higher general price level nor implies a fiscal deficit.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: Suppose the labour requirement for the production of computers and rice in Japan and Thailand is as follows:
questions.explanation: Thailand uses fewer hours for rice and has the lower opportunity cost of rice, so it has both absolute and comparative advantage in rice. Japan uses fewer hours for computers and has the lower opportunity cost of computers, so it has both advantages in computers.

visuals.caption: Labour requirement in Japan and Thailand

questions.postVisualStem:
According to the above table, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) Thailand has a comparative advantage and an absolute advantage in producing rice.
(2) Japan has a comparative advantage and an absolute advantage in producing computers.
(3) Thailand has a comparative advantage in producing rice but has no absolute advantage in producing it.
(4) Japan has a comparative advantage in producing computers but has no absolute advantage in producing it.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: Suppose the transportation cost for 1 unit of rice is 0.1 units of computers and it is borne by the exporting country. Which of the following is the mutually beneficial terms of trade between Japan and Thailand?

choices.text: 1 unit of rice = 0.2 units of computers
1 unit of rice = 0.3 units of computers
1 unit of computers = 0.55 units of rice
1 unit of computers = 2.45 units of rice

questions.explanation: Japan's opportunity cost of one rice is 0.4 computers and Thailand's is 0.125 computers. As Thailand exports rice, its transport cost raises the lower bound to 0.225 computers per rice. A rate of 0.3 lies between 0.225 and 0.4, so both countries gain.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of a quota on domestic price, domestic consumption, domestic production and import quantity for a small open economy
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the imposition of an
questions.explanation: Higher factor prices shift domestic supply left. Since the import quota fixes import volume, the domestic price rises, while domestic production falls rather than rises. Thus only (1) and (2) are correct.

visuals.alt: Demand curve D1, domestic supply curve S, quota-adjusted supply curve Sq, world price Pw and a fixed import quota.
visuals.caption: Import quota on good X in a small open economy

movements: A higher production-factor price shifts domestic supply left.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: With a binding quota, import volume remains fixed. The leftward domestic-supply shift raises the domestic price and lowers domestic production.
