import quota on good X in a small open economy.

Suppose the price of the factors of production for producing good X increases. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The import volume of good X will remain unchanged.
(2) The domestic price of good X will increase.
(3) The quantity of domestically produced good X will increase.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Deflationary gap
questions.stem: An economy initially operates at its long run equilibrium and the total import value equals total export value. Suppose people's desire to save increases. In the short run, there will be ___________ and ___________.

choices.text: a deflationary (output) gap ... a trade surplus
a deflationary (output) gap ... a trade deficit
an inflationary (output) gap ... a trade surplus
an inflationary (output) gap ... a trade deficit

questions.explanation: Higher desired saving lowers consumption expenditure and aggregate demand, creating a deflationary gap. Lower domestic demand reduces imports, so with exports initially equal to imports the economy moves to a trade surplus.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Balance of payments and balance of the BOP account
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of balance of payment surplus and deficit
questions.stem: The following table shows the information about the balance of payments of a country.

choices.text: There is an invisible trade surplus of $19 million.
The current account deficit is $36 million.
The balance of payments surplus is $30 million.
The country's gross domestic product is greater than its gross national income.

questions.explanation: A $30 million increase in reserve assets records a balance-of-payments surplus of $30 million before the reserve adjustment. The other statements conflict with the accounting entries; in particular, positive net factor income from abroad means GNI exceeds GDP.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: The exchange rates of the Hong Kong dollar (HKD) against the Australian dollar (AUD) and the US dollar (USD) between October and December 2019 were as follows:

choices.text: The competitiveness of Hong Kong exports to Australia would decrease.
The number of US tourists to Australia would decrease.
The prices (in terms of USD) of US exports to Australia would increase.
The total value (in terms of AUD) of Hong Kong exports to Australia would decrease.

questions.explanation: The AUD appreciates against the HKD while the USD depreciates against the HKD, so the AUD appreciates against the USD. Australia becomes more expensive for US tourists, reducing their number. The other stated effects do not necessarily follow.

visuals.caption: Exchange rates of the HKD
visuals.sourceNote: Source: Census and Statistics Department, HKSAR Government

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.keyPoint: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong is CORRECT?

choices.text: The public can exchange for US dollars at the linked rate with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.
The Hong Kong dollar is linked to various currencies such as the US dollar, the euro and the renminbi.
The market exchange rate of the Hong Kong dollar against the US dollar is determined by market force.
The money supply (M3) of Hong Kong is fully backed up by the US dollar.

questions.explanation: The HKD market exchange rate against the USD is determined by market forces within the convertibility-zone arrangement. The linked rate concerns the currency-issuing banks and HKMA, links to the USD only, and does not fully back M3 with US dollars.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: The table below shows the ticket pricing of a concert.
questions.explanation: A fixed service charge is a larger percentage addition to the regular ticket's full price, so (1) is consistent. A discount should raise demand for both ticket types, so (2) is inconsistent. Travel cost makes the premium ticket relatively less expensive for overseas audiences, so (3) is also inconsistent.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

(1) When the fixed service charge for ticket purchases increases, the ratio of premium seat tickets sold to regular seats tickets sold increases.
(2) When a 10% off discount is offered on ticket purchases, more people will buy premium seat tickets and fewer people will buy regular seat tickets.
(3) Audience from abroad are more likely to buy regular seat tickets than local audience.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The equilibrium quantity of Apple smartphones will increase if the price of raw materials for producing Apple smartphones __________ and the prices of smartphones produced by other brands __________.
questions.explanation: Cheaper raw materials lower production cost and increase supply. Smartphones from other brands are substitutes, so their higher prices increase demand for Apple smartphones. Both changes increase equilibrium quantity.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: More people have become vegetarians in recent years. At the same time, the price of pig feed has increased. Which of the following diagrams could represent a result of the above events?
questions.explanation: More vegetarians reduce demand for pork, while costlier pig feed lowers its supply. Diagram C shows both a leftward demand shift and a leftward supply shift in the pork market.

visuals.alt: Four demand-supply diagram options. Option C is for pork and shows demand shifting left from D1 to D2 and supply shifting left from S1 to S2.
visuals.caption: Possible market effects of more vegetarians and higher pig-feed prices

movements: More vegetarians reduce demand for pork from D1 to D2.
Higher pig-feed prices raise production cost and reduce pork supply from S1 to S2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option C represents the two changes in the pork market.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Measuring price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the market demand curve for good X.
questions.explanation: Using the midpoint formula, percentage quantity change is 10 / 13 and percentage price change is 17 / 21.5. The arc elasticity is therefore about 0.97.

visuals.alt: Demand curve D with point A at price $30 and quantity 8, and point B at price $13 and quantity 18.
visuals.caption: Market demand curve for good X

movements: Price falls from $30 to $13 while quantity demanded rises from 8 to 18.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Arc elasticity = (10 / 13) / (17 / 21.5) = 0.97, using midpoint percentages.

questions.postVisualStem: The arc elasticity of demand between A and B is __________.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X.

choices.text: The amount of per-unit tax is $2.
The ratio of consumers' tax burden to producers' tax burden is 1:2.
Buyers' total expenditure on good X would decrease by $60.
Sellers' total sales revenue would decrease by $240.

questions.explanation: Initially, equilibrium is $16 and 30 units. The tax reduces quantity to 20 units, with buyers paying $18 and sellers receiving $12, so the unit tax is $6. Consumers bear $2 and producers bear $4 per unit, giving a 1:2 burden ratio. Market-value sales fall from $480 to $360, not by $240.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: After the government imposed a per-unit tax on good X, the quantity transacted changes by 10 units. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Identify the type of market structure
questions.stem: The market of the banking industry in Hong Kong is an example of

choices.text: perfect competition, because market information about banking services in Hong Kong is perfect.
monopolistic competition, because there are over 100 licensed banks in Hong Kong.
monopolistic competition, because services provided by banks are heterogeneous.
oligopoly, because the banking service market in Hong Kong is dominated by a few banks.

questions.explanation: Although there are many licensed banks, a few banks dominate Hong Kong's banking-service market. This is the defining feature of oligopoly.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram of a good with the government setting a quota at Q1.

choices.text: There will be an excess supply of the good.
Consumers' total expenditure on the good will decrease.
The market price of the good will be higher than PA.
The price of the complement of the good will decrease.

questions.explanation: Raising an effective quota increases quantity and lowers the controlled price, but the price remains above PA until the quota stops binding. The higher quantity increases demand for complements, so their price tends to rise rather than fall.

visuals.alt: Demand curve D, original supply S0, effective vertical quota supply S1 at Q1, and original equilibrium price PA.
visuals.caption: Effective production quota

movements: The effective quota is raised but remains below the market-equilibrium quantity.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The market price falls when the quota is raised but remains above PA while the quota remains effective.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government raises the quota on the good while the quota is still effective. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Price ceiling
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the demand-supply diagram of agricultural products in Country A.

choices.text: the consumer surplus in the agricultural product market will decrease, and the consumer surplus in the fertiliser market will increase.
the producer surplus in the agricultural product market may increase or decrease, and the producer surplus in the fertiliser market will decrease.
the total social surplus in both the agricultural product and fertiliser markets will decrease.
there will be a deadweight loss in both the agricultural product and fertiliser markets.

questions.explanation: The effective price ceiling reduces quantity transacted and total social surplus in the agricultural-products market. Because fertiliser is an input for agricultural production, lower output reduces fertiliser demand and its total social surplus too.

visuals.alt: Demand curve D, supply curve S and effective price ceiling P1 below equilibrium in the agricultural-products market.
visuals.caption: Price ceiling on agricultural products

movements: The effective ceiling P1 lowers quantity transacted in the agricultural-products market.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The price ceiling creates deadweight loss in agriculture. Less agricultural output lowers fertiliser demand, reducing total social surplus in the fertiliser market too.

questions.postVisualStem: If the government sets a price ceiling of P1 on agricultural products,

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: 'The imposition of a per-unit tax by the government must worsen efficiency.' The statement is ______, because ____________________.

choices.text: correct ... the government's tax revenue will be smaller than the decreases in consumer surplus and producer surplus
correct ... any form of market intervention will worsen efficiency
incorrect ... a per-unit tax will increase the private marginal cost of people creating negative externalities
incorrect ... a per-unit tax will narrow the divergence between private and social benefits

questions.explanation: A unit tax on an activity with negative externalities raises the private marginal cost faced by the decision maker. It can therefore internalise the external cost and improve efficiency rather than necessarily worsening it.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: Which of the following is a way to lessen the problem of divergence between private and social benefits?

choices.text: to impose a road user charge on drivers during peak hours
to provide scholarships to outstanding students
to raise tariffs on imported cigarettes

questions.explanation: Scholarships subsidise education, which generates positive external benefits. They increase consumption toward the socially efficient level and reduce the divergence between private and social benefits.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Tom can choose to spend his summer holidays either working in a fast food shop or taking a Japanese-language course. Which of the following will result in an increase in the opportunity cost of taking a Japanese-language course?

(1) The fast food shop provides free meals to its workers.
(2) Working conditions in the fast food shop are poor.
(3) The class time of the Japanese-language course is lengthened by 30 minutes.
(4) Operators of the Japanese-language course shift to online teaching, leading to a lower quality of teaching.
questions.explanation: Free meals raise the value of the best forgone option, working at the fast-food shop. A longer class also requires Tom to give up more time that could have been spent working. Poor working conditions and lower course quality do not increase this opportunity cost.

questions.keyPoint: Distinguishing between free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about economic goods is CORRECT?

choices.text: The price of an economic good must be higher than zero.
Economic goods do not exist in a planned economy.
Economic goods will be distributed through non-price competition at zero price.
An economic good brings people more satisfaction than a free good.

questions.explanation: Economic goods are scarce relative to wants, so they need to be allocated by some form of competition. They can be allocated by non-price competition even when the money price is zero; planned economies also face scarcity.

questions.topicGroup: Meaning of public ownership and examples of organisations or institutions in operating under public ownership
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of public ownership and examples of organisations or institutions in operating under public ownership
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the Airport Authority Hong Kong is CORRECT?

choices.text: It is financially independent from the government.

questions.explanation: The Airport Authority Hong Kong is a statutory body operating under public ownership and is financially independent from the government. It can face competition and make losses, and it is not a government department.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership

choices.text: Firm A is larger than Firm B in size.
Firm B is required to disclose its accounting information to the public while Firm A is not.
Owners of Firm A enjoy limited liability while those of Firm B are subject to unlimited liability.

questions.explanation: Firm A has the features of a public limited company: separate legal personality, perpetual succession and the ability to issue shares to the public, so its owners have limited liability. Firm B is a partnership and its owners have unlimited liability.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of issuing shares and bonds to raise capital
questions.stem: In February 2020, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (stock code: 981) issued US$600 million bonds. For existing shareholders, which of the following is an advantage of issuing bonds instead of shares?

choices.text: The company can raise more capital.
The company is not required to disclose its accounting information to the public.
They have priority in getting back their capital if the company liquidates.
Their power of control over the company will not be diluted.

questions.explanation: Issuing more shares changes ownership proportions and can dilute existing shareholders' control. Issuing bonds does not add shareholders, so their control is not diluted. Bondholders, rather than existing shareholders, have priority in liquidation.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital
questions.stem: Mr Chan is the owner of a fitness centre. He has purchased some gym equipment, and he pays his fitness instructors under a basic salary plus commission scheme. The income earned by Mr Chan consists of ________, while the income earned by his fitness instructors consists of ________.

choices.text: profit and interest ... wage and profit

questions.explanation: Mr Chan combines entrepreneurship with the use of capital, so his factor income includes profit and interest. The fitness instructors supply labour and receive wage, whether it is paid as basic salary, commission or both.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: The input-output relationship of a firm is as follows. The firm employs two factors only: workers and machines.

choices.text: The firm provides more training for its workers.
The firm pays its workers at time rate instead of piece rate.
The working environment in the firm is poorer.

questions.explanation: Labour productivity rises from 4,250 / (100 x 8.5) = 5 to 4,576 / (110 x 8) = 5.2 units per worker-hour. More training can raise productivity; the number of machines is unchanged, while time-rate pay and a poorer environment would not explain the improvement.

visuals.caption: Input-output relationship of the firm
rows: Number of working hours per worker per day

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following is a possible reason for the change in the firm's labour productivity?

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: The payment method for couriers of an online takeaway ordering platform changes as follows.

choices.text: The income of the couriers will be more stable.
The cost of monitoring the couriers' output will increase.
Wage payment made by the ordering platform will decrease.
The ordering platform transfers part of the business risk to the couriers.

questions.explanation: Under the new piece-rate-only arrangement, couriers' income depends more on the number of deliveries available and completed. This is less stable and transfers part of the platform's demand risk to couriers; it also makes output easier to observe.

visuals.alt: Courier payment changes from $40 per hour plus $15 per delivery to $35 per delivery only.
visuals.caption: Change in courier payment method

movements: Payment changes from a combined time-rate and piece-rate scheme to a piece-rate-only scheme.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Removing the hourly component makes couriers' pay depend more on the number of deliveries, transferring part of the business risk from the platform to couriers.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning and give examples of each type of internal expansion
questions.stem: Mother company of Japanese discount chain store Don Quijote opened its first Don Don Donki store in Hong Kong in 2019. As of September 2020, the company has opened branches in Tsim Sha Tsui, Tsuen Wan and Causeway Bay. This is an example of _________ expansion.
questions.explanation: Opening additional branches selling the same type of retail service expands the firm at the same stage of production. That is horizontal internal expansion.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The following table shows the cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm.
questions.explanation: At $16, the firm produces six units because the sixth unit's marginal cost is $16. At $15, it produces five units. Dropping the sixth unit lowers total variable cost by its marginal cost of $16; profit falls from $96 - $64 = $32 to $75 - $48 = $27, a decrease of $5.

visuals.caption: Cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the market price has decreased from $16 to $15. The total variable cost of the firm will _________, and its profit will __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem: The following table shows the Gini coefficients by industry classification of 2011 and 2016 (based on monthly income from main employment).

choices.text: The difference in human capital among workers is greater in the information and communications industry than in the construction industry.
The difference in income between workers in the two industries has narrowed.
The information and communications industry tend to pay workers by the month, while the construction industry tend to pay workers by the day.
Information and communications workers enjoy a higher average income than construction workers.

questions.explanation: The information and communications industry has the higher Gini coefficient in both years, showing more uneven income distribution within that industry. A wider difference in workers' human capital can explain the greater inequality; different average incomes or pay periods do not.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following may explain the difference in Gini coefficients of the construction industry and the information and communications industry?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: During Covid-19 pandemic in 2019, the government of Japan announced a 100,000-yen subsidy to every citizen. Which of the following statements about this policy is CORRECT?

choices.text: It increases the income inequality as larger households can receive larger amounts of subsidy.
As the subsidy is given to all citizens, income distribution remains unchanged.
It helps equalise income if there are more people in low income households than high income households.
It helps equalise opportunities as people can use the subsidy for further studies.

questions.explanation: A fixed subsidy per citizen can raise the total income of low-income households by more in aggregate when more people live in such households. In that case it helps equalise income. Giving every individual the same amount does not automatically leave the household income distribution unchanged.

questions.keyPoint: Expenditure approach
questions.stem: Refer to the table below.
questions.explanation: GDP is $650 million because GNI is $620 million and net factor income from abroad is -$30 million. Net exports are $105 million, so G = 650 - 300 - 100 - (-15) - 105 = $160 million.
questions.postVisualStem: Government consumption expenditure is $_______ million.

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of nominal GDP and real GDP
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the gross domestic product (GDP) of Country A.

choices.text: The nominal GDP has been increasing since 2016.
The price level increased every year between 2016 and 2019.
The price level between 2017 and 2019 was higher than that in 2016.

questions.explanation: The price level is represented by the relationship between nominal and real GDP. In each of 2017, 2018 and 2019, the nominal-real gap indicates a price level higher than in 2016. The graph does not show an uninterrupted rise in nominal GDP or in the price level each year.

visuals.alt: Nominal and real GDP of Country A from 2016 to 2019. Nominal GDP is above real GDP in 2017, 2018 and 2019, with a wider separation than in 2016.
visuals.caption: GDP of Country A

movements: The gap between nominal and real GDP is greater in 2017, 2018 and 2019 than in 2016.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: A higher nominal-GDP-to-real-GDP ratio means a higher price level, so the price level in each year from 2017 to 2019 is above that in 2016.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about Country A is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: Which of the following will lead to an increase in both aggregate output and price level in the short run?

choices.text: There is a decrease in the desire to save.
There is an appreciation in the currency of the economy.
Firms expect the future price level to rise.

questions.explanation: A lower desire to save raises consumption expenditure and shifts aggregate demand right. With upward-sloping SRAS, this increases both short-run output and the price level.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand (AD) curve, short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve and long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve of an oil-importing country. The economy initially operates at E0.
questions.explanation: Cheaper imported oil lowers production costs and shifts SRAS right from SRAS0 to SRAS1, moving short-run equilibrium to E1. In the long run, the economy adjusts back to its long-run equilibrium at E0.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram for an oil-importing country, with AD0, SRAS0, SRAS1, SRAS2, LRAS and equilibrium points E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: AS-AD diagram of an oil-importing country

movements: A sharp fall in imported oil prices lowers production costs, shifting SRAS right from SRAS0 to SRAS1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The short-run equilibrium moves from E0 to E1. In the long run, adjustment returns the economy to its original long-run equilibrium E0.

questions.postVisualStem: If the international oil price decreases sharply, the short run equilibrium of the country will be at __________, and the long run equilibrium will be at ____________.

questions.keyPoint: Definition of money
questions.stem: Some bakeries sell mooncake coupons before the Mid-Autumn Festival. These coupons can be used in exchange for mooncakes. Mooncake coupons are NOT money, because

choices.text: they are not issued by the government.
they are not generally acceptable as a medium of exchange.
it is difficult to divide them into smaller denominations.
they are issued only during a particular period.

questions.explanation: Money must be generally acceptable as a medium of exchange. Mooncake coupons can be used only for a narrow purpose and are not generally accepted in payment for goods and services.

questions.keyPoint: Definitions of M1, M2 and M3 in
questions.stem:
Kate received HK$500,000 from overseas remittance. She put HK$300,000 as demand deposit in a bank, and the remainder as time deposit in a licensed bank.

The immediate effect of the above actions on the money supply of Hong Kong would be:

choices.text: M1 increases by HK$300,000 and M2 increases by HK$200,000.
M2 increases by HK$300,000 and M3 increases by HK$500,000.
M1 increases by HK$300,000 and M3 remains unchanged.
M2 and M3 both increase by HK$500,000.

questions.explanation: The demand deposit increases M1 by $300,000. Both the demand deposit and the time deposit at a licensed bank are included in M2 and M3, so each rises by the full $500,000.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem: Study the following balance sheet of a banking system. The amount of excess reserves is $80 million.
questions.explanation: Initial required reserves are $720 million ($800m reserves less $80m excess), so the required reserve ratio is 20%. Of the $150m newly issued notes, $100m is held as cash and $50m enters bank reserves. With excess reserves rising by $20m, required reserves rise by $30m, supporting $150m extra deposits. Money supply therefore rises by $100m cash plus $150m deposits, or $250m.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.postVisualStem: If the central bank issues newly printed banknotes worth $150 million, excess reserves will increase by $20 million and the cash held by the non-bank public will increase by $100 million. The money supply of the economy will increase by $ __________ million.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem:
Which of the following is/are possible reason(s) for the actual amount of deposits created to be smaller than the maximum possible amount?

(1) Banks decide to hold excess reserves.
(2) There is insufficient demand for loans.
(3) The required reserve ratio is 100%.
questions.explanation: Banks holding excess reserves or facing insufficient loan demand prevent the maximum deposit-creation process from occurring. A 100% required reserve ratio changes the maximum possible amount itself; it does not make actual deposits smaller than that maximum.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: Which of the following will offset the effect of widespread use of electronic payment tools on nominal interest rate?

choices.text: The risk of holding interest-bearing assets increases.
The central bank buys government bonds in the open market.
The central bank lowers the required reserve ratio.

questions.explanation: Widespread electronic payment reduces transaction demand for money and puts downward pressure on the nominal interest rate. Greater risk of interest-bearing assets raises asset demand for money, offsetting that downward pressure. The other changes also tend to lower the rate.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: Study the following information about an economy.

choices.text: The inflation rate in year 2 is lower than that in year 1.
The nominal GDP in year 1 is the same as that in year 2.
The velocity of circulation of money increases.
The price level decreases in year 2.

questions.explanation: With the same 5% money-supply growth and a constant velocity of circulation, nominal GDP grows by 5% in both years. Inflation is therefore 5% minus real-GDP growth: 3% in Year 1 and 2% in Year 2, so the Year 2 inflation rate is lower.
questions.postVisualStem: According to the quantity theory of money, which of the following is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: If the nominal interest rate of a bond is higher than the expected inflation rate but lower than the actual inflation rate,

choices.text: holders of the bond will lose from the unexpected inflation.
the nominal rate of return on holding the bond will decrease.
the real rate of return on holding cash will be greater than zero.
the cost of holding cash will decrease.

questions.explanation: Actual inflation is unexpectedly higher than anticipated. It reduces the real value of the fixed nominal bond payments, so bondholders lose. The nominal bond return and nominal opportunity cost of holding cash do not change merely because actual inflation differs from expected inflation.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: The following table shows the information of an economy.
questions.explanation: The labour force rises from 5,380 + 930 = 6,310 thousand to 5,340 + 1,020 = 6,360 thousand. The unemployment rate rises from about 14.7% to 16.0%, while the underemployment rate falls from about 11.5% to 9.9%. All three statements are correct.
questions.postVisualStem:
Compared with 2018, in 2019,

(1) the labour force increased.
(2) the unemployment rate increased.
(3) the underemployment rate decreased.

questions.keyPoint: Four basic principles of taxation
questions.stem:
Study the following news excerpt about an adjustment to the profits tax rates regime in Hong Kong.

From the year of assessment 2018/19 onwards, the profits tax rate for sole proprietorships and partnerships has been changed from 15% to 7.5% on the first $2 million of profits and 15% on the remainder; that for limited companies has been changed from 16.5% to 8.25% on the first $2 million of profits and 16.5% on the remainder.

The above change in the profits tax rates regime is LEAST in line with the __________ principle of taxation put forward by Adam Smith.
questions.explanation: The two-tier arrangement gives lower tax rates to the first $2 million of profits, regardless of the taxpayer's overall ability to pay. It is therefore least aligned with the equity principle. The published rates provide certainty and do not by themselves conflict with convenience or economy in collection.

questions.keyPoint: Direct tax and indirect tax
questions.stem: Which of the following is a difference between direct tax and indirect tax?

choices.text: The tax base of direct tax is broader than that of indirect tax.
During a recession, the decrease in direct tax revenue is less than the decrease in indirect tax revenue.
Direct tax helps reduce income inequality, while indirect tax increases income inequality.
The burden of direct tax cannot be shifted to other parties, while that of indirect tax can.

questions.explanation: A direct tax is imposed on the person intended to bear it and cannot be shifted, whereas an indirect tax can be passed on through a change in price. The other statements are not general differences.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem:
To broaden the tax base, the government of Country A is considering the two proposals below:

Proposal I: Introduce a general sales tax
Proposal II: Reduce the basic allowance for the salaries tax

Which of the statements about the above policies is CORRECT?

choices.text: Proposals I and II are both expansionary fiscal policies.
Proposal I will not affect people's work incentive, while Proposal II will reduce some people's incentive to work.
Proposals I and II will both lead to an increase in the price level of Country A.
Proposal I will increase income inequality, while Proposal II will reduce income inequality.

questions.explanation: A general sales tax affects consumption rather than the after-tax reward to working, while reducing the basic salaries-tax allowance raises some workers' marginal tax burden and can reduce their incentive to work. The policies are not both expansionary and their effects on income inequality are not as stated.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Refer to the AS-AD diagram below. The economy operates at A initially.

choices.text: The government increases the subsidies to firms.
The government increases transfer payments to the poor.
The government lowers the discount rate.
The central bank sells government bonds in the open market.

questions.explanation: Point A is a deflationary gap, to the left of LRAS. Lowering the discount rate is expansionary monetary policy: it increases money supply, lowers interest rates and raises aggregate demand toward long-run equilibrium.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with short-run equilibrium A to the left of LRAS, showing a deflationary gap.
visuals.caption: AS-AD diagram

movements: Initial equilibrium A lies to the left of LRAS.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The economy has a deflationary gap. Lowering the discount rate is expansionary monetary policy, shifting AD right toward long-run equilibrium.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following monetary policies can help the economy restore to the long run equilibrium?

questions.keyPoint: Surplus budget, deficit budget and balanced budget
questions.stem: Suppose economy A initially operates at long run equilibrium and the government expenditure equals government revenue. ___________ will result in a fiscal surplus and a deflationary (output) gap in the economy.

choices.text: An increase in the profits tax rate
A decrease in government expenditure on national defence
An increase in the required reserve ratio
An increase in tariffs on imported goods

questions.explanation: Reducing government expenditure while revenue is unchanged creates a fiscal surplus and lowers aggregate demand, producing a deflationary gap. The other policies do not necessarily create both results.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem: Suppose there is a reduction in government expenditure and the amount of fixed tax payments. If the decrease in government expenditure is greater than the decrease in fixed tax payments, the effect on aggregate output is
questions.explanation: Lower government expenditure directly reduces aggregate demand. A reduction in fixed taxes raises disposable income and consumption by less than the tax cut because part is saved. Since the fall in government expenditure is larger, aggregate output falls overall.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: The following table shows the number of man-hours required by Country A and Country B in the production of soy beans and computers.
questions.explanation: Country A's opportunity cost of one computer is 8 soy beans and Country B's is 5. Country A imports computers and pays 0.2 soy beans transport cost, so its effective import cost must not exceed 8. Terms of trade of 5.2 and 7 meet the condition for both countries, while 8 does not leave Country A a gain after transport cost.

visuals.caption: Labour requirements of Country A and Country B

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the transportation cost for each unit of computers is 0.2 units of soy beans and it is borne by the importing country. Which of the following would be a mutually beneficial terms of trade between Country A and Country B?

(1) 1 unit of computers = 5.2 units of soy beans
(2) 1 unit of computers = 7 units of soy beans
(3) 1 unit of computers = 8 units of soy beans

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem:
Suppose the opportunity cost of producing 1 unit of good X is 1.5 units of good Y for Country A and 3 units of good Y for Country B.

According to the above information, we can determine

(1) which country has an absolute advantage in producing good X.
(2) which country will export good X according to the principle of comparative advantage.
(3) the total gain from trading 1 unit of good X between the two countries.
questions.explanation: Country A has the lower opportunity cost of X and will export it. The total gain from trading one unit of X is the difference in the two opportunity costs, 3 - 1.5 = 1.5 units of Y. Absolute advantage cannot be inferred from opportunity costs alone.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: The following is the supply-demand diagram of good X in a small open economy.

choices.text: The import volume of good X will remain unchanged.
The domestic price of good X will be equal to its world price.
The economy's tariff revenue will decrease.
The total revenue of domestic producers will decrease.

questions.explanation: After the world price drops by t, the domestic price including the tariff falls from Pw + t to the old Pw. Domestic quantity supplied and the price both fall, so domestic producers' total revenue decreases. Imports rise and tariff revenue does not necessarily decrease.

visuals.alt: Small-open-economy demand and supply diagram with world price Pw and tariff-inclusive domestic price Pw plus t.
visuals.caption: Tariff on good X in a small open economy

movements: The world price falls by t while the tariff remains t.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The domestic price falls from Pw + t to the old Pw. Both domestic price and domestic output fall, so domestic producers' total revenue decreases.

questions.postVisualStem:
Initially the world price of good X is Pw, and the economy imposes a tariff on the imports of good X at $t. Suppose

the world price of good X drops by $t. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem:
May is a Hong Kong resident, and she plans to take a three-month English-language course in Britain. Which of the following will be included in the calculation of the balance of payments of Hong Kong?

(1) She pays tuition fees to an English-language school in Britain.
(2) She rents a flat in Britain.
(3) She buys a round-trip ticket from Hong Kong to London with a Hong Kong-based airline.
questions.explanation: Tuition paid to a British school and rent paid for a British flat are imports of services and are recorded in Hong Kong's balance of payments. The ticket is purchased from a Hong Kong resident airline, so it is not an external transaction for Hong Kong's BOP.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: The table below shows the change in the exchange rate of the US dollar to the Japanese yen (yen).
questions.explanation: The US dollar depreciates against the yen. Because the HKD is linked to the USD, the yen appreciates against the HKD: Japan becomes more expensive to Hong Kong tourists, US exports become cheaper to Japan, and Japanese exports become more expensive to Hong Kong. All three statements follow.

visuals.caption: US dollar to Japanese yen exchange rate

questions.postVisualStem:
Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, the above change in the exchange rate would lead to

(1) a decrease in the number of Hong Kong tourists to Japan.
(2) an increase in the total value (in terms of the US dollar) of US exports to Japan.
(3) a decrease in the total value (in terms of the Japanese yen) of Japanese exports to Hong Kong.

questions.keyPoint: Variable costs and fixed costs
questions.stem:
During the COVID-19 pandemic, some restaurants closed at night. Which of the following are variable costs that restaurants can save on by shortening the opening hours?

(1) electricity fees
(2) expenses for purchasing meat and vegetables
(3) interest on bank loans
(4) wages paid to a part-time staff by time rate
questions.explanation: Electricity, ingredients and time-rate pay for a part-time worker fall when the restaurant operates for fewer hours, so they are variable costs. Interest on bank loans does not vary with opening hours and is fixed in this context.

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: Study the following production data of a firm. The only input required is labour.

choices.text: the optimal scale of production is 30 units of output.
diminishing marginal returns set in after 20 units of labour are employed.
the firm enjoys internal economies of scale.
the firm suffers from internal diseconomies of scale.

questions.explanation: All inputs are variable, so the firm operates in the long run and diminishing marginal returns does not apply. Average cost falls from $0.53 to $0.46 to $0.42 as scale rises, showing internal economies of scale; the data do not establish an optimal scale.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, we can conclude that

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of internal expansion
questions.stem: In June 2020, Country Garden (碧桂園), a property developer, opened a restaurant using robots as staff. Which of the following is most likely the motive behind the expansion?

choices.text: to spread risk through product diversification
to ensure the supply of factors of production
to ensure a market outlet for its products

questions.explanation: Opening a restaurant is conglomerate expansion into an unrelated industry. It can spread risk through product diversification; it is neither backward nor forward expansion, and it does not raise the property developer's market share.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm.
questions.explanation: Marginal costs are $20, $25, $35, $50 and $60, so the price-taking firm produces 4 units when price is $50. Profit is $200 minus $140 = $60. Producer surplus is revenue minus variable cost: $200 - ($140 - $10 fixed cost) = $70.

visuals.caption: Cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the market price is $50. At the profit-maximising output level, the firm's producer surplus and profit are _________ and _________ respectively.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which of the following is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

choices.text: After a listed company announced that its profit is higher than expected, both the price and the turnover of its shares increases.
People tend to eat more at buffet dinners compared to other types of dinners.
After the provision of unemployment benefits, the number of unemployed increases.
After the government abolishes the per-unit tax on red wine, the quality of red wine sold improves.

questions.explanation: Abolishing the same per-unit tax lowers both prices by the same amount, raising the relative price of higher-quality red wine. The law of demand then predicts relatively less high-quality wine, so average quality should worsen rather than improve. The other phenomena are consistent with changes in relative or full prices.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem: Suppose the wage rate remains unchanged. Which of the following can alleviate the excess supply in the labour market of a country?

choices.text: introducing more machines to replace labour
subsidising part of employees' salary for employers

questions.explanation: A wage subsidy to employers increases their demand for labour and reduces excess supply. More foreign workers raise labour supply, while machines replacing workers and tighter labour protections reduce labour demand, each worsening excess supply.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem: The demand for ________ can be regarded as a derived demand for ________.
questions.explanation: Construction workers are an input used to produce private housing, so demand for private housing creates derived demand for construction workers. The other pairs either describe substitutes, two production inputs, or reverse the final-good and input relationship.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is the demand-supply diagram of the coffee bean market. E0 is the original equilibrium point.
questions.explanation: Coffee machines and coffee beans are complements, so lower coffee-machine prices shift coffee-bean demand from D0 to D1. A good harvest shifts supply from S0 to S1. Their intersection is E2.

visuals.alt: Coffee bean market demand-supply diagram with curves D0 to D2, S0 to S2 and equilibrium points E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Coffee bean market

movements: A fall in the price of coffee machines, a complement, increases demand for coffee beans from D0 to D1.
A good harvest increases the supply of coffee beans from S0 to S1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The new equilibrium is E2, where D1 and S1 intersect.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the price of coffee machines dropped and there is a good harvest of coffee beans due to climate change. The new equilibrium point of the coffee beans market will be at ________.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in demand
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in demand
questions.stem: Which of the following would most likely lead to an increase in the total expenditure on iPhones produced by Apple Inc.?

choices.text: Improvement in the production technology of chips reduces the production cost of Apple Inc.
People expect Apple Inc. to lower the price of iPhones.
Xiaomi Corporation (小米集團) lowers the price of its smartphones.
The mobile system of iPhones' major competitor has security issues.

questions.explanation: Security issues with a major competitor increase demand for iPhones, raising both equilibrium price and quantity, so total expenditure rises. A production-cost fall changes supply and has an uncertain expenditure effect; expected lower prices and a cheaper substitute both reduce current demand for iPhones.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Measuring price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: The table below shows the relationship between the price of sandwiches and the producers' total revenue.

visuals.caption: Price and total revenue of sandwiches

questions.postVisualStem: What is the arc elasticity of demand for sandwiches within the above price range?

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Jeremy received three job offers after graduating from university. His order of preference is shown below:

choices.text: The pressure of working in a bank is greater than expected.
The bank increases the annual leave for employees.
The working hours of research assistants are longer than expected.
The government raises the starting salary of executive officers.

questions.explanation: The highest-valued option forgone is working as a management trainee in a bank. More annual leave raises the value of that option and therefore raises the opportunity cost of taking the research-assistant job. Changes to the chosen job or the third-ranked option do not change the highest-valued option forgone.

items: First preference: to work as a management trainee in a bank
Second preference: to work as a research assistant at a university
Third preference: to work as an executive officer for the government
visuals.alt: Jeremy's ranked job preferences

questions.postVisualStem: Assuming Jeremy's order of preference does not change, which of the following will increase Jeremy's opportunity cost of working as a research assistant at a university?

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about scarcity is CORRECT?

choices.text: A good is not scarce if everyone owns it.
A good whose quantity is limited must be scarce.
If resources are evenly distributed, scarcity does not exist.
The problem of scarcity cannot be solved through the price mechanism.

questions.explanation: Scarcity exists when available resources cannot satisfy all wants. A good may remain scarce even if everyone owns some of it, and limited quantity alone does not prove scarcity. The price mechanism allocates resources but cannot satisfy all wants, so it cannot solve scarcity.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Which of the following are normative statements?

(1) The government should prohibit factories from emitting pollutants to avoid damage to the ecological environment.
(2) Completely prohibiting factories from emitting pollutants would worsen economic efficiency.
(3) A good ecological environment is more important than economic development.
questions.explanation: Statements (1) and (3) contain value judgements about what should be done or what is more important, so they are normative. Statement (2) makes a factual, refutable claim about economic efficiency and is positive.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem: Hong Kong is regarded as a market-oriented economy because _____________.

choices.text: all resources are owned by private individuals
Hong Kong's income distribution is uneven
most of the resources are allocated by the price mechanism
most of the resources are used to produce consumer goods

questions.explanation: A market-oriented economy allocates most resources through the price mechanism. It need not have all resources privately owned, an uneven income distribution is not defining, and resources can be used to produce either consumer or producer goods.

questions.keyPoint: Classification of private firms: sole proprietorship, partnership, private limited company and public limited company
questions.stem: Kevin and Mavis jointly set up a firm. They are legally responsible for each other's decisions.

choices.text: The firm needs to disclose its accounting information to the general public.
The firm can issue shares to the public to raise capital.
Their losses may be greater than the amount of their investment in the company.
They can transfer their ownership without the consent of the other.

questions.explanation: The firm is a partnership: partners are legally responsible for one another's decisions and have unlimited liability, so their losses may exceed their investment. A partnership neither issues public shares nor needs public disclosure, and transfer of ownership requires the other partner's consent.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of issuing shares and bonds to raise capital
questions.stem: In February 2021, Bossini International Holdings Limited (stock code: 0592), a clothing retailer, announced it would issue shares to raise capital. Which of the following is an advantage of issuing shares over bonds from the viewpoint of the existing shareholders?

choices.text: The existing shareholders' control over the company is not affected.
The company has no obligation to redeem the shares.
The risk of the company being taken over by others is not affected.
Issuing shares can raise more capital.

questions.explanation: Shares have no maturity date, so the company is not obliged to redeem them, unlike bonds. Issuing new shares can dilute existing shareholders' control and raise takeover risk, and it does not necessarily raise more capital than bonds.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

choices.text: The knowledge in a textbook is a public good while the textbook is a private good.
Bus service is a public good while the bus is a private good.
A movie is a public good while a Blu-ray disc of the movie is a private good.
A firework display is a public good while the fireworks used are a private good.

questions.explanation: Bus service is rival in consumption: as more people use it, less service is available to other passengers. It is therefore not a public good. The other examples correctly distinguish a non-rival service or idea from a rival physical item.

questions.keyPoint: Recognise the contribution of each type of production to the economy
questions.stem: The following table shows the employment distribution of an economy.

choices.text: the number of workers engaged in primary production decreased.
the output of consumer goods decreased.
the relative importance of tertiary production in terms of employment increased.
the living standard of people increased.

questions.explanation: The employment share of tertiary production rose from 59% to 63%, so its relative importance in employment increased. The table gives neither total employment, output nor living-standard information, so the other conclusions cannot be drawn.
questions.postVisualStem: From the above table, we can conclude that from 2015 to 2020,

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following will increase the occupational mobility of labour in an economy?

choices.text: There is a greater degree of specialisation in production.
The government relaxes the licensing requirements for some professions.
Educational institutions raise the admission standards of courses of continuing education.
The transportation network of the economy becomes more complete.

questions.explanation: Relaxing licensing requirements makes it easier for workers to enter those occupations, increasing occupational mobility. Greater specialisation and harder access to continuing education reduce mobility, while a better transport network improves geographical rather than occupational mobility.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem:
Private tutors are usually paid by time rate because

(1) the output of private tutors is difficult to measure.
(2) this can increase the work incentive of private tutors.
(3) private tutors tend not to shirk.
questions.explanation: Private tutors' output is not standardised and is difficult and costly to measure, so time rate lowers the cost of calculating wages. Under time rate, pay does not directly depend on output, so it does not increase work incentive; a tendency not to shirk is not a reason for selecting the payment method.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Suppose the government has imposed an effective price floor in the wool market. If the price of mutton increases sharply,

choices.text: consumers' total expenditure on wool will remain unchanged.
the price floor may become ineffective.
the excess supply of wool will decrease.
the change in total revenue of wool producers is uncertain, depending on the price elasticity of demand for wool.

questions.explanation: Wool and mutton are in joint supply. A higher mutton price increases the supply of wool. With an effective price floor, the market price and quantity transacted of wool remain unchanged, so consumers' total expenditure remains unchanged. The price floor remains effective and excess supply rises.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Country A implements rent control on separate units of sub-division of flat units (commonly known as 'sub-divided units'). It sets a maximum rent per square foot for residential units with a size below 40 square metres, while residential units with a size equal to or greater than 40 square metres are not restricted. Which of the following would LEAST likely occur?

choices.text: Property owners' incentive to renovate the sub-divided units will increase.
Low-income people will find it harder to rent the residential units with a size below 40 square metres.
Property owners will have a higher incentive to convert the sub-divided units into residential units with a larger size.
There will be a black market in the rental market for sub-divided units.

questions.explanation: Rent control removes the additional rental return from improving a controlled unit, so owners are less, not more, willing to renovate it. Excess demand can make it harder for low-income people to rent, encourage conversion to unrestricted larger units and create a black market.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X.

choices.text: The surplus of good X will decrease by 2 units.
The quantity transacted will increase by 3 units.
Producers' total revenue will increase by $16.
The market price will drop by $2.

questions.explanation: At a quota of 9 units, price is $30 and total revenue is $270. At a quota of 12 units, the quota becomes ineffective and equilibrium is 11 units at $26, so total revenue is $286. Revenue increases by $16; quantity transacted rises by 2 and price falls by $4.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government increases the quota from 9 units to 12 units. According to the above table, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Suppose the supply of good X is perfectly inelastic. When the government provides a per-unit subsidy to the producers of good X, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: Consumers' total expenditure will remain unchanged.
The market price of good X will fall.
The total revenue of producers (including the subsidy) will remain unchanged.
Consumers will enjoy the entire subsidy.

questions.explanation: With perfectly inelastic supply, a per-unit subsidy does not shift the supply curve or change price and quantity transacted. Consumers' expenditure therefore remains unchanged, while producers receive the entire subsidy and their total revenue including subsidy rises.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram of good X.
questions.explanation: Before raw-material prices fall, the no-tax supply curve is S0 and the taxed supply curve is S1. The tax distance is t. The lower raw-material price shifts no-tax supply to S2 and taxed supply to S0. Consumers' tax burden is area P0ceP2 and the deadweight loss is area cfh.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram with D, supply curves S0 to S2, prices P1, P0, P2 and P0 minus t, and marked areas a to h.
visuals.caption: Per-unit tax after raw-material price falls

movements: A per-unit tax shifts the supply curve upward by t from S0 to S1.
A lower raw-material price shifts the no-tax supply curve from S0 to S2; the taxed supply curve then coincides with S0.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: After the fall in raw-material price, consumers' tax burden is area P0ceP2 and deadweight loss is area cfh.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose after the government levies a per-unit tax (t) on good X, the market price of good X increases from P0 to P1. Subsequently, the price of raw materials of good X decreases and the market price of good X falls back to P0. The consumers’ tax burden and the deadweight loss are ____________ and ____________ respectively after the decrease in the price of raw materials.

questions.keyPoint: Identify the type of market structure
questions.stem: The market of accommodation services in Hong Kong can be regarded as

choices.text: perfect competition, because there are many hotels, guesthouses and hostels providing accommodation services in Hong Kong.
monopolistic competition, because there are many hotels, guesthouses and hostels providing heterogeneous services in Hong Kong.
oligopoly, because the cost of opening a hotel is high.
oligopoly, because hotels, guesthouses and hostels are interdependent in their marketing strategies.

questions.explanation: Many accommodation providers offer heterogeneous services, which is monopolistic competition. Many sellers alone is not unique to perfect competition, and the market is not dominated by a few large firms as an oligopoly would be.

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about a monopolist is CORRECT?

choices.text: The monopoly power of a monopolist comes from the government.
A monopolist does not need to promote their business through advertisements.
A monopolist can raise its price without losing all customers.
There is no substitute for the products sold by a monopolist.

questions.explanation: A monopolist is a price searcher and can raise price without losing every customer. Monopoly power can also come from superior resources or natural monopoly, a monopolist can advertise, and a monopoly's product has no close substitute rather than no substitute at all.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem:
Which of the following can be ways to lessen the problem of divergence between private and social costs in Hong Kong?

(1) to increase the tobacco tax
(2) to collect a levy based on the amount of solid waste discarded by households
(3) to collect a levy on vehicles entering congested roads during peak hours
questions.explanation: All three levies raise the marginal private cost of an activity that imposes external costs: smoking, waste disposal or congestion. They reduce the activity and help internalise the divergence between private and social costs.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem: Which of the following occupations is MOST likely to have the largest income inequality among the workers?
questions.explanation: Actors and actresses are likely to differ substantially in natural ability and human capital, producing the largest income inequality among the listed occupations.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: The chart below shows the Gini coefficients of Hong Kong from 2001 to 2016.

choices.text: the income level of Hong Kong people increased.
the living standard of low-income households increased.
the government increased the amount of social transfers to low-income households.
the tax system and social transfers in Hong Kong reduced income inequality.

questions.explanation: In every year, the Gini coefficient based on post-tax post-social transfer household income is lower than the coefficient based on original household income. This shows that tax and social transfers reduced inequality. The chart does not show income levels, living standards or the amount of social transfers.

visuals.alt: Bar chart of Hong Kong Gini coefficients from 2001 to 2016 before and after tax and social transfers.
visuals.caption: Hong Kong Gini coefficients, 2001-2016

labels: Gini coefficient (based on original household income)
Gini coefficient (based on post-tax post-social transfer household income)
diagramDetails.answerFocus: In every year, the post-tax post-social transfer Gini coefficient is lower, so the tax system and social transfers reduced income inequality.
