questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem:
An online shop launches a promotion campaign which waives the fixed shipping fee for each order. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The ratio of higher-priced goods sold to lower-priced goods sold will decrease.
(2) More lower-priced goods will be sold.
(3) The profit of the online shop will increase.
questions.explanation: Waiving a fixed shipping fee raises the relative price of higher-priced goods, so relatively fewer higher-priced goods are bought. It lowers the monetary cost of buying from the shop, increasing sales including lower-priced goods. Profit is uncertain because the cost of waiving fees and extra revenue may differ in size.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: In order to reduce illegal parking, the government has increased the penalty for illegal parking. As a result, the number of illegal parking cases has decreased. Which of the following concepts can be used to explain the above phenomenon?

choices.text: the law of diminishing marginal returns

questions.explanation: The higher penalty raises the monetary cost of illegal parking. By the law of demand, the number of illegal parking cases falls.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: Suppose Hong Kong employers need to pay a higher handling fee for hiring Indonesian domestic helpers. At the same time, the average wage level in the Philippines has increased. Which of the following diagrams could represent a result of the above events?
questions.explanation: Indonesian and Filipino domestic helpers are substitutes, so a higher cost of hiring Indonesian helpers shifts demand for Filipino helpers right. Philippine local labour and Filipino helpers are in competitive supply, so a higher Philippine wage shifts supply of Filipino helpers to Hong Kong left. Option C shows both changes.

visuals.alt: Four labour-market diagrams for Indonesian or Filipino domestic helpers with demand and supply shifts.
visuals.caption: Domestic-helper labour market options

movements: A higher handling fee for Indonesian domestic helpers raises demand for Filipino domestic helpers because they are substitutes.
A higher Philippine wage level reduces the supply of Filipino domestic helpers to Hong Kong because the two labour supplies are in competitive supply.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option C shows the Filipino-helper market with demand shifting right (D1 to D2) and supply shifting left (S1 to S2).

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in supply
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in supply
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the market demand curve for private schools.

choices.text: The government approves an increase in the fees of private schools.
The government approves more applications for opening private schools.
Fewer people are willing to engage in educational services.
More people emigrate to other countries.

questions.explanation: From A to B, price falls and quantity rises along the market demand curve. More approved applications increase the supply of private-school services, causing exactly those equilibrium changes. The other options either move along demand in the opposite direction or reduce demand or supply.

visuals.alt: Private-school market demand curve with equilibrium positions A and B, where B is lower and to the right of A.
visuals.caption: Private-school market demand curve

movements: The movement from A to B has lower price and higher quantity demanded along the same demand curve.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: More approved applications to open private schools increase supply, lowering equilibrium price and increasing equilibrium quantity.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following reasons can best explain the change of the equilibrium position in the private school market from A to B?

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings of joint supply and competitive supply
questions.stem:
Other things being constant, an increase in the price of good X will cause the total revenue of good Y to decrease if

(1) good X and good Y are substitutes.
(2) good X and good Y are complements.
(3) good X and good Y are in joint supply and the demand for good Y is inelastic.
(4) good X and good Y are in competitive supply and the demand for good Y is inelastic.
questions.explanation: A higher price of X lowers demand for complementary Y, reducing Y's revenue. With joint supply, a higher X price increases supply of Y; if Y demand is inelastic, price falls proportionally more than quantity rises and revenue falls. Substitutes raise Y demand, while competitive supply reduces Y supply and raises Y revenue when demand is inelastic.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand and supply schedules for good X. Suppose the government raises the price ceiling from $20 to $26. Based on the table, which of the

choices.text: The market price will increase to $26.
The quantity transacted will decrease by 3 units.
Total sales revenue will increase by $32.
There will be a surplus of 1 unit in the market.

questions.explanation: With a $20 ceiling, eight units are transacted and revenue is $160. A $26 ceiling is ineffective because equilibrium is $24 and eight units; revenue becomes $192, an increase of $32. There is neither surplus nor shortage.

visuals.caption: Demand and supply schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: After the government increases the quota of good X from 10 to 15 units, the market price of good X drops from $30 to $27. Which of the following is CORRECT?

choices.text: The consumers' total expenditure on good X will decrease.
There will be a shortage of good X in the market.
The market price of substitutes for good X will increase.
Within the above price range, the demand for good X is elastic.

questions.explanation: Total expenditure rises from $300 (10 x $30) to $405 (15 x $27). Because price falls while quantity transacted rises and expenditure rises, the percentage quantity change exceeds the percentage price change, so demand is elastic. A quota does not create a shortage here and lower X price lowers demand and price for its substitutes.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand and supply schedules for good X.

choices.text: All of the above are incorrect.

questions.explanation: Before tax, equilibrium is $11. After tax, consumers pay $14, so their burden is $3 per unit. The taxed supply schedule implies producers receive $8, so the $6 tax gives producers a $3 burden per unit. Each side bears $30 on ten units, a ratio of 1:1.

visuals.caption: Demand and supply schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose after the government imposing a per-unit tax on good X, the market price of good X increases by $3. The ratio of consumers' tax burden to producers' tax burden is ___________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on producer surplus
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram of good X. Suppose the demand for good X changes from D1 to D2. The producer surplus will increase by __________ and

choices.text: area (C + D + E) ... area (A + B + C + D + E)

questions.explanation: Initially producer surplus is E and total social surplus is B + C + E. After demand rises, producer surplus is C + D + E, so it rises by C + D. Total social surplus becomes A + B + C + D + E, so it rises by A + D.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram with vertical supply S, demand shift D1 to D2, prices P1 and P2, and areas A to G.
visuals.caption: Producer and total social surplus after demand rises

movements: Demand shifts right from D1 to D2 while supply remains unchanged.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Producer surplus increases by C + D. Total social surplus increases by A + D.

questions.postVisualStem: the total social surplus will increase by __________.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem:
When the government provides a per-unit subsidy to the producer of a good,

(1) the consumer surplus will increase.
(2) the producer surplus will increase.
(3) the total social surplus will increase.
questions.explanation: A per-unit subsidy lowers market price and increases quantity, raising consumer surplus. Producers receive a higher gross price and sell more, raising producer surplus. Part of the subsidy is captured by neither side as deadweight loss, so total social surplus falls rather than rises.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Miss Lee bought a car. In which of the following situations will her opportunity cost of using the car increase?

(1) The price of the car in the second-hand market increases.
(2) The performance of the car is worse than she expected.
(3) There are reports that the brake system of this car model is defective.
(4) The price of gasoline decreases.
questions.explanation: Using the car means forgoing the money from selling it, so a higher second-hand price raises its opportunity cost. A defective brake system raises the avoidable expected medical cost of using the car. Worse performance lowers the value of use, while cheaper gasoline lowers the monetary cost.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Which of the following are positive statements?

(1) Levying a vacant property tax will cause the prices of residential properties to decrease.
(2) Levying a capital gain tax can help improve income inequality.
(3) Increasing the salaries tax rate will not affect people's work incentive.
questions.explanation: All three statements make claims that are refutable by facts and contain no value judgement, so all are positive statements.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: A bookshop decides to adopt a 'pay what you want' pricing scheme in which customers can decide the price of each book they buy. The above case is related to the ____________ question(s) in economics.

choices.text: 'what to produce' and 'for whom to produce'

questions.explanation: Choosing a pricing scheme determines how books are distributed among people in society. It therefore concerns the 'for whom to produce' basic economic problem.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: There are three private broadcasters in Hong Kong offering free television programmes. These free television programmes are

choices.text: economic goods, because their demand is greater than their supply.
free goods, because people can watch the television programmes without paying any charges.
public goods, because a person's consumption of a television programme will not reduce the amount available to others.
private goods, because they are produced by private firms.

questions.explanation: Television programme services are non-rival in consumption, so they are public goods. Free of charge does not mean a good is free, and whether a good is private depends on rivalry and excludability, not the firm's ownership.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning and examples of the three types of production; identify the type of production
questions.stem: Ryan employs Jessie to produce instructional cooking videos with a fixed monthly salary. Jessie shoots these videos with her smartphone at home. Jessie engages in _____________ and her income consists of _____________.
questions.explanation: Jessie provides a teaching service, so she engages in tertiary production. Her effort is labour and earns wages; the smartphone used in production is capital and earns interest.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem:
Which of the following is/are labour at a tutorial centre?

(1) students
(2) the receptionist who is paid a fixed monthly salary
(3) the tutors who are paid by a profit-sharing scheme
(4) the shareholders who do not participate in the management of the tutorial centre
questions.explanation: The receptionist and tutors provide human effort and are labour regardless of their payment method. Students are not inputs of the tutorial centre, while non-managing shareholders bear business risk and provide entrepreneurship rather than labour.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following is the most mobile in terms of occupational mobility?
questions.explanation: A porter generally requires less specialised skill than the other occupations. The worker is therefore more willing and able to move to another occupation, giving higher occupational mobility.

questions.keyPoint: External economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: In recent years, more and more companies have participated in the research and development of electric vehicles, leading to an increase in the price of raw materials used to produce electric vehicle batteries. In this case, the electric car companies

choices.text: suffer from external diseconomies of scale.
suffer from internal diseconomies of scale.

questions.explanation: Expansion of the electric-vehicle industry raises raw-material prices and long-run average costs for firms in that industry. This is an external diseconomy of scale because it arises from the industry's growth rather than a single firm's scale.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem: In March 2021, American chip supplier Qualcomm acquired the chip start-up Nuvia for US$1.4 billion. Which of the following is the LEAST likely motive behind the expansion?

choices.text: to spread risks through business diversification
to strive for a higher market share
to strive for a higher profit for the company

questions.explanation: The acquisition is horizontal expansion because the two firms produce the same type of product. It therefore cannot diversify business risk, while higher market share, higher profit and economies of scale can be motives for horizontal expansion.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: Which of the following will cause the profit-maximising output of a price-taking firm to decrease?

choices.text: The marginal cost of each unit of output decreases.
The average cost of each unit of output increases by the same amount.

questions.explanation: A market-price rise or lower marginal cost raises profit-maximising output, while a fixed-cost change does not affect marginal revenue or marginal cost. If average cost rises by the same amount at every output, marginal cost also rises by that amount, so profit-maximising output falls.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of the divergence between private and social costs?

choices.text: After a car manufacturer announced a price cut, the sales of other car manufacturers dropped significantly.
A factory dumped pollutants into a river without giving compensation to residents downstream.
A restaurant distributes unsold food to the poor.
A factory installed an exhaust emission control device.

questions.explanation: Dumping pollutants without compensating affected residents imposes an external cost, so social cost exceeds the factory's private cost. The restaurant example concerns an external benefit, while the other cases do not create this divergence.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: The table below shows the Gini coefficients of Singapore in 2019 and 2020.
questions.explanation: The wider gap between the before-tax-and-transfer and after-tax-and-transfer Gini coefficients shows that welfare and tax policies narrowed inequality more effectively in 2020. Equal before-tax Gini coefficients do not show unchanged household incomes or an unchanged Lorenz-curve shape.

visuals.caption: Singapore Gini coefficients
rows: Based on household income from work per household member before accounting for government transfers and taxes
Based on household income from work per household member after accounting for government transfers and taxes

Based on the above information, we can conclude that:

(1) income before accounting for government transfers and taxes for high income households and that for low income households remained unchanged in Singapore.
(2) the effectiveness of welfare and tax policies in narrowing the income gap increased in Singapore.
