questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: To calculate the gross national income of Hong Kong, which of the following should be added to the GDP of Hong Kong?

choices.text: rental income earned by a Hong Kong resident from a property in Japan
dividends received by a Singapore resident from a listed company in Hong Kong
salary earned by a British resident who worked in a restaurant in Hong Kong for six months
salary earned by a Hong Kong resident who worked in the Hong Kong branch of an American bank

questions.explanation: GNI equals GDP plus factor income earned by residents outside the economic territory minus factor income earned by non-residents within it. The rental income in Japan is an external factor income of a Hong Kong resident. Options B and C are non-resident income in Hong Kong, while D is already included in Hong Kong GDP and GNI.

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of nominal GDP and real GDP
questions.stem: Suppose a closed economy produces soybeans and cloth only. The output of year 1 to year 3 is as follows.

choices.text: The nominal GDP in year 2 is higher than that in year 1 and year 3.
The inflation rate of the economy is greater than zero in year 2 and year 3.
The real GDP of the economy has been increasing since year 1.
The cost of living in year 3 is lower than that in year 2.

questions.explanation: Using year 1 as base, nominal GDP is $2,600, $2,628 and $2,796, while real GDP is $2,600, $2,580 and $2,730. The implicit GDP deflator rises from 100 to 101.86 to 102.42, so inflation is positive in years 2 and 3; year-3 nominal GDP is higher than year 2, real GDP first falls, and cost of living rises in year 3.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the economy is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: Which of the following will cause the aggregate demand curve of a country to shift to the left?

choices.text: The government raises the minimum wage level.
The government increases its expenditure on social welfare.
The global economy is in recession.

questions.explanation: A global recession lowers net exports and therefore aggregate demand. A higher minimum wage affects SRAS, more welfare spending raises disposable income and consumption, and a lower price level is a movement along rather than a shift of the AD curve.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand curve, the short run aggregate supply curve and the long run aggregate supply curve of an economy. The economy is initially at E0.

choices.text: a decrease in people's desire to save and an increase in government subsidies on research and development
a decrease in government spending on infrastructure and an increase in population
a decrease in the price of raw materials and a reduction in government transfer payments
a reduction of risk in the stock market and more residents migrating to other places

questions.explanation: Lower raw-material prices increase SRAS. Lower government transfer payments reduce disposable income, consumption and AD. This gives the diagram's rightward SRAS shift and leftward AD shift without moving LRAS.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with LRAS, SRAS0 shifting right to SRAS1, and AD0 shifting left to AD1 from initial equilibrium E0.
visuals.caption: AS-AD movements

movements: A lower raw-material price shifts SRAS right from SRAS0 to SRAS1.
A reduction in government transfer payments lowers disposable income and consumption, shifting AD left from AD0 to AD1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option C produces the displayed rightward SRAS shift and leftward AD shift while LRAS is unchanged.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following can best explain the movement of the aggregate demand curve and the short run aggregate supply curve shown in the above diagram?

questions.keyPoint: Qualities of good money
questions.stem:
Compared to gold, banknotes are a better form of money. This is because banknotes are more _____________.

(1) scarce
(2) portable
(3) generally acceptable
questions.explanation: Gold is more scarce because its quantity is limited. Banknotes are lighter and so more portable, and they are accepted by more shops in payment for goods and services.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem: Which of the following will lead to an increase in the monetary base?

choices.text: The public withdraws money from the banking system.
The public's demand for bank loans decreases.
The central bank raises the required reserve ratio.
The central bank lowers the discount rate.

questions.explanation: Lowering the discount rate makes borrowing from the central bank cheaper and increases bank reserves, raising the monetary base. The other changes either shift cash between public circulation and reserves or affect deposits without changing cash in circulation plus bank reserves.

questions.keyPoint: Definitions of M1, M2 and M3 in
questions.stem: Suppose the money supply data of Hong Kong is as follows.
questions.explanation: Monetary base is $280 billion, including $200 billion reserves, so cash in public circulation is $80 billion. M2 is cash plus all deposits with licensed banks plus eligible licensed-bank certificates of deposit: $80 + $2,250 + $360 = $2,690 billion.

visuals.caption: Hong Kong money supply data
rows: Legal tender held by all authorised institutions
All types of deposits with licensed banks
Negotiable certificates of deposit issued by licensed banks (other than those held by authorised institutions)
Deposits with restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies
Negotiable certificates of deposit issued by restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies (other than those held by authorised institutions)

questions.postVisualStem: The money supply M2 is $_____________ billion.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual banking multipliers
questions.stem: Study the following balance sheet of a banking system. Suppose the public hold $200 million cash and the banks do not hold excess reserves.

choices.text: withdraw $50 million cash from the banking system
withdraw $100 million cash from the banking system
deposit $50 million cash into the banking system
deposit $100 million cash into the banking system

questions.explanation: The maximum bank multiplier is 3 ($1,350 million deposits divided by $450 million reserves). Withdrawing $50 million leaves $400 million reserves and raises public cash to $250 million, allowing maximum deposits of $1,200 million and money supply of $1,450 million.

visuals.caption: Balance sheet of a banking system

questions.postVisualStem: If the public ______________, the maximum possible amount of money supply will be $1,450 million.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money demand and money supply curves of an economy. The original equilibrium point is at E.
questions.explanation: More popular electronic wallets reduce transaction demand for money, shifting money demand from Md0 to Md1. A lower required reserve ratio raises the maximum possible deposits and money supply, shifting money supply from Ms0 to Ms2. The new equilibrium is therefore D.

visuals.alt: Money demand and money supply diagram showing Md0, Md1, Md2, Ms0, Ms1, Ms2 and equilibrium points A, B, C, D and E.
visuals.caption: Money demand and money supply

movements: More use of electronic wallets reduces transaction demand for money, shifting the money-demand curve from Md0 to Md1.
A lower required reserve ratio raises the maximum possible deposits and money supply, shifting the money-supply curve from Ms0 to Ms2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The intersection of Md1 and Ms2 is point D.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the use of electronic wallets is becoming more popular and the central bank lowers the required reserve ratio. The new equilibrium point will be at _____________.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Features of the four phases of a business cycle
questions.stem: In the diagram below, A is situated in a certain phase of the business cycle.

choices.text: Companies' sales volumes are at a low level.
Applications for bankruptcy are at a high level.

questions.explanation: Point A is at the trough of the business cycle. At a trough, the general price level is low, so an increasing inflation rate is the least likely observation. High unemployment, low sales volumes and more bankruptcy applications are consistent with a trough.

visuals.alt: Business-cycle graph of percentage change in real GDP around an average growth rate, with point A at the trough.
visuals.caption: Business cycle point A

movements: Point A is the trough phase of the business cycle.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: At a trough the general price level is low, so an increasing inflation rate is the least likely observation.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following phenomena is the LEAST likely to be observed at point A?

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Nominal interest rate as the (opportunity) cost of holding money
questions.stem: Suppose the expected inflation rate is 4% and the nominal interest rate is 5%. If the actual inflation rate is 2%, the cost of holding money is ______________ and the real rate of return on holding money is ____________.
questions.explanation: The opportunity cost of holding money equals the nominal interest rate, which is 5%. Money has a nominal return of 0%, so its real rate of return is 0% minus the actual inflation rate of 2%, or -2%.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: Refer to the following information on an economy.

choices.text: the velocity of circulation of money

questions.explanation: Under the quantity theory of money, MV = PY and the velocity of circulation is assumed to be constant. Since money supply falls from $120 million to $100 million, nominal GDP (PY) decreases. The information does not establish a change in the inflation or unemployment rate.
questions.postVisualStem: According to the quantity theory of money, ______________ in year 2 has decreased.

questions.keyPoint: Direct tax and indirect tax
questions.stem:
Which of the following is/are direct tax(es) in Hong Kong?

(1) profits tax
(2) dividend tax
(3) bets and sweeps tax
(4) capital gains tax
questions.explanation: Profits tax is a direct tax. As of March 2021, Hong Kong has no dividend tax or capital gains tax, while bets and sweeps tax is an indirect tax.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: In a certain year, the nominal wage rate decreases by 4% while the general price level increases by 2%. If the government reduces the salaries tax allowance by 5%,

choices.text: the government's salaries tax revenue will decrease.
people's real income after tax will increase.
more people will fall into the tax net.

questions.explanation: The lower nominal wage and higher price level reduce the real wage, and a lower tax allowance further reduces real income after tax. Because the tax allowance falls by a larger percentage than nominal wages, more people earn an income above the allowance and fall into the tax net. The change in tax revenue is uncertain and work incentive falls, rather than rises.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Refer to the following AS-AD diagram of an economy.

choices.text: providing production subsidies to small and medium enterprises
raising the standard tax rate of the salaries tax
selling government bonds in the open market

questions.explanation: At E, output is above LRAS, so aggregate demand must decrease to restore long-run equilibrium. A higher salaries-tax rate lowers disposable income, consumption and AD. The lower output reduces transaction demand for money, so the nominal interest rate falls. The other policies either push output further up or raise the nominal interest rate.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with a vertical LRAS curve, upward SRAS curve and downward AD curve intersecting at E to the right of LRAS.
visuals.caption: AS-AD long-run equilibrium

movements: Initial equilibrium E lies to the right of LRAS, so aggregate demand must fall to restore long-run equilibrium.
A higher salaries-tax rate lowers disposable income and consumption, shifting AD left and reducing transaction demand for money.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option B restores output to LRAS without raising the nominal interest rate.

questions.postVisualStem: The economy operates at E initially. Which of the following policies can help the economy restore to the long run equilibrium without increasing the nominal interest rate?

questions.topicGroup: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.keyPoint: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.stem:
The government is going to begin the construction of the MTR Northern Link. During the construction period, Hong Kong's ___________ will increase.

(1) employment rate
(2) gross domestic product
(3) potential output level
questions.explanation: The project creates employment and production activities, so the employment rate and GDP increase during construction. Hong Kong's productive capacity does not increase until the project is completed, so potential output remains unchanged.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: The table below shows data on Country A.

choices.text: The opportunity cost of producing 1 unit of good X is 0.67 units of good Y.
The terms of trade is 1 unit of good X = 1.6 units of good Y.
If the transportation cost per unit of good X is 0.5 units of good Y, Country A will not trade with another country.
The gain from trade of importing 1 unit of good X is 1.1 units of good Y.

questions.explanation: The opportunity cost of 1 unit of good X is 1.5 units of good Y: (150 - 75) / 50. The terms of trade is 0.4 units of good Y per unit of good X: (150 - 120) / 75. Therefore the gain from importing 1 unit of good X is 1.1 units of good Y, which exceeds the transportation cost in option C.

visuals.caption: Country A output and consumption
rows: Total output with no international trade
Total output with specialisation and international trade

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about Country A is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning of absolute advantage
questions.stem: A country has an absolute advantage in producing good X. Which of the following statements about this country is CORRECT?

choices.text: The opportunity cost of producing good X in this country is lower than that in other countries.
This country has a comparative advantage in producing good X.
This country needs to use more resources than other countries to produce the same amount of good X.
This country can produce more units of good X than other countries with the same resources.

questions.explanation: Absolute advantage means higher productivity: the country can produce more units of good X with the same resources. A lower opportunity cost defines comparative advantage, which does not necessarily accompany absolute advantage.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: Suppose a small open economy imposes an import tariff on good X and the demand for good X in the economy increases. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The import volume of good X will remain unchanged.
The market price of good X will increase.
The domestic production of good X will decrease.
The total import value of good X will increase.

questions.explanation: A tariff raises the market price and domestic production of good X. An increase in demand does not change the market price or domestic production in a small open economy, but it raises import volume, offsetting the tariff's reduction in imports. The import-volume and total-import-value changes are therefore uncertain, while the market price increases.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: Suppose initially the value of exports is equal to the value of imports in economy A. If ___________, the price level of the economy will increase and there will be a trade deficit.

choices.text: the government of economy A imports more foreign labour
economy A's trading partners experience economic recovery
the currency of economy A appreciates
the investment incentive of the firms in economy A increases

questions.explanation: Greater investment incentive raises investment expenditure and aggregate demand. Price and output rise; as output rises, imports rise and a trade deficit results. The other changes either lower the price level, raise net exports, or both.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Balance of payments and balance of the BOP account
questions.keyPoint: The balance of payments is always balanced in the accounting sense
questions.stem: The following table shows the information about the balance of payments of a country in a certain year.
questions.explanation: The balance of payments is $20 million. The current account is $(65 + 25 + X - 10) million and the capital and financial account, excluding reserve assets, is -$30 million (20 - 50). Therefore 20 = (65 + 25 + X - 10) - 30, so X = -30.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, the value of X is __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem:
Mavis participated in the Working Holiday Scheme in 2019 and went to Australia to work for three months. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The salary she earned in Australia is included in the calculation of Hong Kong's GNI in 2019.
(2) The salary she earned in Australia needs to be taxed in Hong Kong.
(3) The salary she earned in Australia is included in the calculation of Hong Kong's current account balance.
questions.explanation: The salary is factor income earned by a Hong Kong resident outside the economic territory, so it is included in Hong Kong's GNI and current account as external factor income. Under the source principle, salary earned outside Hong Kong does not need to be taxed in Hong Kong.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.keyPoint: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong is CORRECT?

choices.text: The money supply M1 of Hong Kong has to be fully backed by the US dollar.
A balance of payments surplus in the United States will lead to a balance of payments surplus in Hong Kong.
If the US dollar depreciates against the Renminbi continuously, the volume of goods exported from Hong Kong to the Mainland of China will increase.
The public can convert US dollars at the Hong Kong Monetary Authority at an exchange rate of US$1 = HK$7.8.

questions.explanation: If the US dollar depreciates against the Renminbi, the Hong Kong dollar also depreciates under the linked exchange rate system. Hong Kong exports become cheaper in Renminbi and the Mainland buys more. Hong Kong dollar banknotes in the monetary base, not M1, are fully backed by US dollars, and only note-issuing banks can convert US dollars at the Hong Kong Monetary Authority at the linked rate.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem: The demand for __________ can be regarded as a derived demand for __________.
questions.explanation: Actors are factors of production used to produce free television programmes. Demand for the programmes therefore creates derived demand for actors. The other options either reverse the relationship or name goods or inputs that are jointly or competitively demanded.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings of joint supply and competitive supply
questions.stem: When two goods are in competitive supply, an increase in the __________ a good will result in a decrease in the __________ the other good.
questions.explanation: When demand for one competitively supplied good rises, its price rises. Producers switch resources towards that good, decreasing the supply of the other good.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: As people become more aware of food safety issues, hormone-free meat becomes very popular. As a result, the price of hormone-free meat changes by 50% and its quantity transacted changes by 30%. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The demand for hormone-free meat is elastic.
The demand for hormone-free meat is inelastic.
The supply of hormone-free meat is elastic.
The supply of hormone-free meat is inelastic.

questions.explanation: Food-safety awareness increases demand, so both equilibrium price and quantity rise. The 30% increase in quantity supplied is smaller than the 50% price increase, so the price elasticity of supply is inelastic.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand and supply schedules for good X.

choices.text: The market price will drop to $12.
The quantity transacted will remain unchanged.
The total expenditure on good X will increase by $50.
The shortage of good X will disappear.

questions.explanation: At the $16 price floor, 10 units are transacted. At $12, the price floor is ineffective, so the market reaches equilibrium at $14 and 15 units. Total expenditure rises from $160 ($16 x 10) to $210 ($14 x 15), an increase of $50. The $16 floor creates a surplus, not a shortage.

visuals.caption: Demand and supply schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government lowers the price floor from $16 to $12. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand and supply schedules for good X.
questions.explanation: Before tax, equilibrium is $8 and 19 units. After tax, it is $9 and 18 units, so consumers and producers each bear $18 of the tax burden. The price rises by $1, not $2. Consumer expenditure rises from $152 ($8 x 19) to $162 ($9 x 18).

visuals.caption: Demand and supply schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the government imposes a per-unit tax of $2 on good X. Which of the following are CORRECT?

(1) The ratio of consumers' tax burden to producers' tax burden is 1:1.
(2) The market price of good X increases by $2.
(3) Consumers' total expenditure on good X increases.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the subsidy
questions.stem: Suppose a per-unit subsidy is provided for good X. If the demand for good X is __________ and the supply of good X is __________, the consumers' share of the subsidy will be smaller than the producers' share of the subsidy.
questions.explanation: For a per-unit subsidy, the more elastic side receives the smaller share. Consumers receive the smaller share only when demand is more elastic than supply, as in option D.

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: The market structure of fruit stores in Hong Kong is NOT perfectly competitive because

choices.text: there are many fruit stores in the market.
the prices of fruits are not fixed.
there is no restriction on fruit stores entering the market.
the fruits sold in different fruit stores are heterogeneous.

questions.explanation: Products in perfect competition are homogeneous. Heterogeneous fruit products mean the market is not perfectly competitive; many sellers and free entry are compatible with perfect competition.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on consumer surplus
questions.stem:
The bumper harvest of cocoa beans has reduced the price of chocolate. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The total revenue from selling chocolate will increase.
(2) The consumer surplus in the market of chocolate will increase.
(3) The marginal benefit of the last unit of chocolate will decrease.
questions.explanation: A bumper cocoa harvest increases chocolate supply, lowering price and increasing quantity. Consumer surplus rises, while a downward-sloping demand curve means marginal benefit of the last unit falls. Total revenue is uncertain because it depends on price elasticity of demand.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: Country A imposes an effective quota on soft drinks. Assuming that the quota is still effective, when more people worry about the impact of soft drinks on health,

choices.text: the consumer surplus in the soft drink market will decrease.
the producer surplus in the soft drink market will decrease.
the excess demand in the soft drink market will decrease.
the efficiency loss in the soft drink market will increase.

questions.explanation: Health concerns decrease demand. With the quota still effective, price falls while quantity transacted remains unchanged, reducing producer surplus. Consumer surplus remains unchanged, an effective quota does not create excess demand, and the gap between marginal benefit and marginal cost narrows so deadweight loss falls.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of the divergence between private and social costs?

choices.text: A supermarket gives out food items that are near their expiry dates for free.
A laundry shop accidentally dyed the clothes of a few customers. The customers affected accept compensation from the laundry shop.
A vehicle repair shop emits strong smell, and the shop does not give any compensation to affected shops nearby.
Music coming from a music school disturbs lessons of a neighbouring tutorial school, and the tutorial school and the music school are owned by the same person.

questions.explanation: The repair shop imposes an uncompensated external cost on nearby shops, so social cost exceeds private cost. Giving food away creates an external benefit, accepted compensation internalises the cost, and a disturbance within one owner's businesses is private rather than external.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Carmen can only choose to take a swimming course or a fencing course in her leisure time. Which of the following will increase Carmen's opportunity cost of taking a fencing course?

(1) The price of fencing equipment increases.
(2) The swimming course is taught by the swimming athlete Carmen admires the most instead of another tutor.
(3) The fencing course is more interesting than Carmen expected.
questions.explanation: A higher price of fencing equipment raises the monetary cost of the fencing course. A more highly valued swimming course raises the value of the alternative forgone. A more interesting fencing course only raises the value of the chosen option, not its opportunity cost.

questions.keyPoint: Explain why past expenditure which is irrecoverable is not a cost
questions.stem: Miss Ma bought a second-hand residential unit and she spent $100,000 to renovate the unit. Which of the following would be the LEAST important factor for Miss Ma to choose between living in the unit by herself or renting it out?

choices.text: The neighbours of the unit are very friendly.
Miss Ma has spent a lot of time following up the renovation project.
The average rent of residential units decreases.
High costs are involved in finding suitable tenants.

questions.explanation: The time spent following up the renovation project is a past expenditure. It is irrecoverable and does not affect the current choice between living in the unit and renting it out.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Mr. Lee said, 'The increase in the amount of unemployment assistance by the government can encourage people to seek jobs actively.'
Miss Ho said, 'The government has spent too much public funds on the Consumer Voucher Scheme.'

Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: Mr. Lee's statement is a normative statement because value judgement is not involved in the statement.
Mr. Lee's statement is a positive statement because it is refutable by facts.
Miss Ho's statement is a normative statement because most people do not agree with it.
Miss Ho's statement is a positive statement because it is consistent with the real world data.

questions.explanation: Mr. Lee's statement is positive because it can be tested against objective facts. Miss Ho's statement contains a judgement about whether the expenditure is too much, so it is normative; whether people agree with it is irrelevant.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: A restaurant holds a sharing day every week, providing free nutritious lunch sets designed for the elderly. The above case is related to the __________ question(s) in economics.

choices.text: 'what to produce' and 'for whom to produce'

questions.explanation: Choosing lunch sets concerns what to produce. Designing the lunch sets for the elderly concerns how the food is distributed among people in society, so it is a for-whom-to-produce question.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Tam Jai International Co. Limited, which operates restaurant chains TamJai Yunnan Mixian (譚仔雲南米線) and TamJai SamGor Mixian (譚仔三哥米線), was officially listed on Stock Exchange of Hong Kong on 7 October 2021. After becoming a listed company, Tam Jai International Co. Limited

choices.text: must pay dividends to its shareholders.
has to pay a higher profits tax rate.
has a lower risk of being taken over.
must disclose its accounting information to the public.

questions.explanation: A public limited company must disclose accounting information to the public. It is not obliged to pay dividends, its profits-tax rate is the same as that of a private limited company, and freely traded shares increase the risk of a takeover.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Seats in the students' study rooms under the Leisure and Cultural Services Department are normally allocated on a first-come-first-served basis. The seats in the students' study rooms are __________ because __________.

choices.text: public goods ... the government provides these seats for public use
public goods ... anyone can use these seats on a first-come-first-served basis
private goods ... there is a production cost involved in providing these seats
private goods ... the seats are rival in consumption

questions.explanation: The seats are rival in consumption: once someone uses a seat, one fewer seat is available to others. They are therefore private goods.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: The following is the contract of a salesperson at a boutique.

choices.text: The boutique will have a lower cost of calculating wages.
The boutique can transfer part of the business risk to the salesperson.
The salesperson will have a lower work incentive.
The income of the salesperson will be more stable.

questions.explanation: When boutique business is poor, the salesperson receives less commission, transferring part of the business risk to the salesperson. Commission raises work incentive, makes income less stable, and increases rather than lowers the cost of calculating wages.
questions.postVisualStem: Compared to time rate only, which of the following about the above payment method is CORRECT?

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The table below shows the production plan of a firm. The firm employs two inputs only, namely machines and labour.
questions.explanation: Marginal products for the first four machines are 10, 15, 20 and 21. For marginal product to fall with the fifth machine, X - 66 must be smaller than 21, so X must be smaller than 87. At X = 87, marginal product would be unchanged.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the above data illustrate the law of diminishing marginal returns. The value of X __________.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the input-output relationship of a price-taking firm. Suppose the fixed cost of the firm is $5.

choices.text: the profit of the firm is $12.
the firm suffers from diseconomies of scale.
the optimal scale of production is 4 units.

questions.explanation: Total costs are $10, $22, $36, $52 and $70, giving marginal costs of $5, $12, $14, $16 and $18. At a market price of $16, profit is maximised at 4 units where marginal cost equals price. Profit is $16 x 4 - $52 = $12. Fixed cost means this is short-run analysis, so diseconomies of scale are not applicable.

visuals.caption: Input-output relationship of a price-taking firm

questions.postVisualStem: When the market price is $16,

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem: Jollibee, a fast food chain, bought shares of Tim Ho Wan (添好運), a dim sum chain, in 2018 and completed acquiring all shares of Tim Ho Wan in September 2021. Which of the following is the LEAST likely motive behind the integration?

choices.text: to take advantage of brand names
to diversify sources of income and spread risk
to ensure a reliable supply of factors of production

questions.explanation: This is a lateral integration: the firms make related but non-competing products. Brand-name benefits, risk diversification and economies of scale are possible motives, but Tim Ho Wan is unlikely to supply the factors of production required by Jollibee.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: Which of the following will NOT lead to a decrease in the Gini coefficient based on post-tax post-social transfer monthly household income in Hong Kong?

choices.text: to relax the eligibility for the Government Public Transport Fare Concession Scheme for the Elderly and Eligible Persons with Disabilities (the $2 Scheme)
to provide a fixed amount of electricity charges subsidy to each eligible residential electricity account
to lower the double ad valorem stamp duty imposed on buyers of a second residential property
to impose a sales tax on luxury goods

questions.explanation: Owners of more than one residential property generally have higher income. Lowering their double ad valorem stamp duty reduces their tax while low-income households are unaffected, raising rather than reducing the post-tax-and-transfer Gini coefficient. The other measures favour low-income households relatively more or tax high-income households relatively more.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: To calculate Hong Kong's gross national income, which of the following should be deducted from Hong Kong's gross domestic product?

choices.text: the salary earned by a Hong Kong resident from working in the Hong Kong branch of a British company
the dividend received by a Hong Kong resident from the shares of a Japanese company
the rent paid by a Japanese to a Hong Kong resident for renting a residential unit in Hong Kong
the salary earned by a Briton from working in a design company in Hong Kong for half a year

questions.explanation: GNI equals GDP plus factor income earned by residents outside the economic territory, minus factor income earned by non-residents within it. The Briton is a non-resident, so his Hong Kong-earned salary is deducted from GDP. The dividend in option B is external factor income of a resident and is added.

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of nominal GDP and real GDP
questions.stem: Consider the following information about an economy.
questions.explanation: Per capita nominal GDP is unchanged while population rises by 4%, so nominal GDP rises. Nominal GDP rises while real GDP falls by 1%, which means the general price level rises.

visuals.caption: Growth rates relative to the previous year

questions.postVisualStem: Compared to the previous year, the nominal GDP has __________ and the general price level has __________ in the economy in the current year.

questions.keyPoint: Uses and limitations of national income statistics
questions.stem: In which of the following situations would the per capita real GDP of a country overstate the living standard of its people?

choices.text: The general price level increased sharply.
Population declined due to emigration wave.

questions.explanation: Consuming fewer non-market goods reduces living standards but is not reflected in GDP, so per capita real GDP overstates living standards. Per capita real GDP already adjusts for price and population changes. More even income distribution raises living standards without being captured, so it would make per capita real GDP understate them.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem:
The MTR Corporation Limited (MTR) plans to construct the Northern Link. The new line will connect the East Rail Line and the Tuen Ma Line, and a loop of railway around the North New Territories and Kowloon will be formed after the construction is completed. Which of the following will increase due to the construction of the Northern Link?

(1) Hong Kong's GDP
(2) Hong Kong's geographical mobility of labour
(3) Hong Kong's occupational mobility of labour
(4) Hong Kong's potential output level
questions.explanation: Construction is gross investment and raises GDP. More convenient transport reduces workers' travel cost and raises geographical, not occupational, mobility. The completed Northern Link raises productive capacity and potential output.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: Suppose the major trading partner of a country experiences economic recovery. At the same time, the government of the country decides to lower the profits tax rate. Which of the following diagrams can best describe the effect of the above events?
questions.explanation: Economic recovery in a major trading partner raises exports and net exports, while a lower profits-tax rate raises investment. Both increase aggregate demand, shifting AD to the right with no direct SRAS or LRAS shift. This is option D.

visuals.alt: Four AS-AD diagram options showing combinations of shifts in AD, SRAS and LRAS.
visuals.caption: AS-AD diagram options

movements: Economic recovery of a major trading partner raises exports and net exports, shifting AD right.
A lower profits-tax rate raises investment expenditure, also shifting AD right.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Only option D shows the required rightward shift from AD0 to AD1 with SRAS unchanged.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Study the following diagram.

choices.text: The world price of oil decreases.
Producers expect the price level to increase.

questions.explanation: The move from E to A is caused by an increase in SRAS. A lower world oil price reduces production cost and shifts SRAS right. Greater investment shifts AD right, greater desire to import shifts AD left, and higher expected price levels reduce current SRAS.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with LRAS, SRAS and AD, showing the short-run equilibrium move from E to A at a lower price level and higher output.
visuals.caption: AS-AD equilibrium movement

movements: A fall in the world price of oil lowers production cost and shifts SRAS right.
With AD unchanged, short-run equilibrium moves from E to A.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option C is the supply-side event consistent with the displayed movement.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the short run equilibrium point of an economy moves from E to A. Which of the following is a possible reason for the change in the equilibrium point?

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: When there is a/an __________, market forces will cause the __________ to increase and the economy will restore to its long run equilibrium.

choices.text: inflationary (output) gap ... short run aggregate supply
inflationary (output) gap ... long run aggregate supply
deflationary (output) gap ... short run aggregate supply

questions.explanation: A deflationary gap creates excess supply in the factor market, putting downward pressure on input prices. Production cost falls, SRAS increases, and the economy returns to long-run equilibrium.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem: As a form of money, jewels can better perform the function of a __________ than shells because jewels are more __________.
questions.explanation: The value of money depends on relative scarcity. Jewels have a more limited supply than shells, so their value is more stable and they perform better as a store of value.

questions.topicGroup: Licensed banks, restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies in
questions.keyPoint: Features of the three types of deposit-taking institutions
questions.stem:
Miss Lee plans to put $200,000 as a time deposit for three months. Which of the following financial institutions in Hong Kong can accept her deposits?

(1) licensed banks
(2) restricted licence banks
(3) deposit-taking companies
questions.explanation: Licensed banks and deposit-taking companies can accept the $200,000 time deposit. Restricted licence banks accept deposits of HK$500,000 or above only.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Study the following information.

choices.text: The money supply will be $310 million.
The amount of deposits will be $240 million.
The amount of loans will be $180 million.

questions.explanation: The published Paper 1 answer key marks D. Its worked calculation on the same Suggested Solution gives deposits of $300 million, loans of $240 million and money supply of $310 million, so the source is internally inconsistent; D is retained for marking-key fidelity.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose later all banks loan out their excess reserves and all the loans are re-deposited into the banking system. Which of the following statements about the banking system is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money demand and money supply curves of an economy. The original equilibrium point is E.
questions.explanation: Weekly rather than monthly payments reduce transaction demand for money, shifting the money-demand curve left to M_d1. Selling government bonds reduces money supply, shifting the money-supply curve left to M_S1. The new equilibrium is D.

visuals.alt: Money demand and money supply curves with equilibrium points A to E.
visuals.caption: Money demand and money supply diagram

movements: Weekly payments reduce transaction demand for money, shifting money demand left from M_d0 to M_d1.
The central bank's sale of government bonds reduces money supply, shifting money supply left from M_S0 to M_S1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The two leftward shifts move equilibrium from E to D, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose most employers choose weekly payments over monthly payments. At the same time, the central bank sells government bonds to the public. The new equilibrium point will be __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Features of the four phases of a business cycle
questions.stem:
The following phenomena are observed in Country A:

(1) The investment expenditure is decreasing.
(2) The purchasing power of money is rising.
(3) The labour employment level is decreasing.

Country A is in the __________ phase of a business cycle.
questions.explanation: Falling investment and employment, together with rising purchasing power of money (falling general price level), are features of the recession phase of the business cycle.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Effects of inflation and deflation on different aspects
questions.stem: Which of the following people will benefit from unexpected inflation?

choices.text: a flat owner who receives a fixed amount of rent
an elderly person who receives a fixed amount of Old Age Living Allowance
an employer who pays his workers a fixed monthly wage
a lender who lends money to his friend at a floating interest rate

questions.explanation: Unexpected inflation reduces the real purchasing power of fixed payments. The employer benefits because the real value of the fixed wage paid falls. The flat owner and elderly recipient lose, while a floating rate adjusts with inflation and protects the lender.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Nominal interest rate as the (opportunity) cost of holding money
questions.stem: Suppose the nominal interest rate is 5% and the expected inflation rate is -2%. If the actual inflation rate turns out to be 1%, the cost of holding cash and the actual real interest rate will be __________ and __________ respectively.
questions.explanation: The opportunity cost of holding cash is the nominal interest rate, 5%. The actual real interest rate is 5% minus actual inflation of 1%, which is 4%.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem:
According to the quantity theory of money, in the short run, if the growth rate of money supply is higher than that of the price level, __________.

(1) real output will increase
(2) nominal output will remain unchanged
(3) the velocity of circulation of money will decrease
questions.explanation: Using MV = PY with velocity assumed constant, money supply growing faster than the price level means real output must rise. Nominal output rises with money supply rather than remaining unchanged, and there is no implied fall in velocity.

questions.keyPoint: Taxation in
questions.stem: According to the tax system of Hong Kong, which of the following incomes is subject to taxation?

choices.text: the monthly salary received by a Hong Kong resident from working in Australia
the profits earned by a Frenchman from operating a company in Hong Kong
the dividend received by an American from holding shares of a listed company in Hong Kong
the revenue received by a Hong Kong resident from selling a second-hand car

questions.explanation: Hong Kong applies the source principle: income and profits earned in Hong Kong are taxable. The Frenchman's business profits are earned in Hong Kong. Overseas employment income is not Hong Kong-sourced, Hong Kong has no dividend tax, and a private sale of a second-hand car is not taxable revenue.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Which of the following would offset the effect of an increase in the discount rate on aggregate output?

choices.text: security issues found in the electronic payment systems
a decrease in the desire to save
an increase in the required reserve ratio
a decrease in the basic allowance of the salaries tax

questions.explanation: A higher discount rate reduces money supply, raises interest rates, and lowers consumption and investment, so aggregate output falls. A lower desire to save raises private consumption and aggregate demand, offsetting that contractionary effect. The other options also reduce aggregate demand or money supply.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: Refer to the following AS-AD diagram of an economy.

choices.text: to sell government bonds to commercial banks

questions.explanation: E is to the right of LRAS, so the economy has an inflationary output gap. Selling government bonds to commercial banks reduces money supply, raises the interest rate and shifts AD left. Both output and the price level fall towards long-run equilibrium. The other policies either raise AD or increase the price level.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with equilibrium E to the right of LRAS.
visuals.caption: AS-AD long-run equilibrium diagram

movements: At E, aggregate output is above the LRAS level, indicating an inflationary output gap.
A reduction in aggregate demand moves output left towards LRAS and lowers the price level.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Selling government bonds to commercial banks reduces money supply and aggregate demand, which is option B.

questions.postVisualStem: The economy initially operates at E. Which of the following policies can help the economy restore to its long run equilibrium without increasing the price level?

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: Which of the following policies would reduce the budget deficit and narrow the income gap at the same time?

choices.text: to increase the standard rate of the salaries tax
to provide additional school textbook assistance to children from low-income families
to increase the rent of public housing
to raise the fee for public medical services

questions.explanation: Increasing the standard salaries-tax rate raises government revenue and reduces high-income households' disposable income, so it can reduce both the budget deficit and the income gap. The other measures either increase public expenditure or burden low-income households relatively more.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem:
To improve the sewage treatment system, suppose the government imposes a sewage treatment tax on households. The amount of tax collected will be equal to the amount of expenditure on improving the system. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The effect on aggregate demand will be expansionary.
(2) In the short run, the output level will increase.
(3) In the long run, the price level will decrease.
questions.explanation: Equal increases in government expenditure and taxes have an overall expansionary effect on aggregate demand, so short-run output rises. In the long run, the higher AD raises rather than lowers the price level, making statement (3) false.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: The following table shows the amount of umbrellas or computers that Country A and Country B can produce with ALL their resources.
questions.explanation: The opportunity cost of one umbrella is 3 computers in Country A and 0.75 computer in Country B. Country B therefore has comparative advantage in umbrellas, will specialise in them, and will export them. At a terms of trade of one umbrella for two computers, each imported umbrella gives Country A one computer of gain, or 10 computers for 10 umbrellas. The resource information is insufficient to establish absolute advantage.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) Country B has an absolute advantage in producing umbrellas.
(2) Country B will specialise in producing umbrellas and export them.
(3) If the terms of trade is 1 unit of umbrellas = 2 units of computers, the total gain from trade for the umbrella-importing country from trading 10 units of umbrellas is 10 units of computers.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: Suppose a small open economy abolishes the import tariff imposed on good X. Which of the following MUST increase?

choices.text: the quantity of domestically produced good X
consumers' total expenditure on good X

questions.explanation: Removing a tariff lowers the domestic market price to the world price, increasing the quantity imported. Domestic output falls, while the effect on consumers' total expenditure depends on demand elasticity.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.keyPoint: Meaning and role of foreign and official reserves in the balance of payments accounting
questions.stem: The following table shows the information about the balance of payments of a country in a certain year.
questions.explanation: The current account is $80 million (80 + 20 - 30 + 10), while the capital and financial account excluding reserve assets is -$20 million (30 - 50). The balance is therefore a $60 million surplus, matched by a $60 million increase in reserve assets.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, reserve assets __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: The following table shows the change in the exchange rate of the US dollar (USD) against Indian rupee (INR).

choices.text: an increase in the total value of Indian exports to the US (in terms of the US dollar)
a decrease in the total value of US exports to India (in term of the US dollar)
an increase in the competitiveness of Indian exports to Hong Kong
a decrease in the number of Indian tourists visiting the US

questions.explanation: The US dollar depreciates against the Indian rupee. Indian exports become more expensive in US dollars, so US quantity demanded falls; with inelastic import demand, the percentage price rise exceeds the fall in quantity and their US-dollar value rises. US exports become cheaper in rupees, so their US-dollar value rises. The linked Hong Kong dollar also depreciates against the rupee, reducing rather than increasing Indian-export competitiveness in Hong Kong, and US travel becomes cheaper for Indians.

visuals.caption: US dollar to Indian rupee exchange rate

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the demand for imports is inelastic in both the US and India. The above change in the exchange rate will lead to __________.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Karen considers teaching drawing in a gallery or taking a fine art programme in a university in France. Which of the following would increase Karen's cost of taking a fine art programme in France?

choices.text: The gallery raises the salaries of all teachers.
The teaching quality of the fine art programme is not as good as Karen expected.
The climate in France is pleasant and Karen enjoys living in France.

questions.explanation: Karen's cost of taking the programme is the value of teaching in the gallery, her best forgone option. A higher gallery salary raises that value and therefore the opportunity cost. Closing the gallery removes the alternative, while the other changes affect the value of studying rather than the forgone option.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem: If a good is scarce,

choices.text: the quantity of the good is not sufficient to satisfy all people's wants.
there is a shortage of the good.
everyone in the world wants to obtain the good.
the good will not be free of charge.

questions.explanation: Scarcity means available resources or goods are insufficient to satisfy all wants. It does not necessarily create a market shortage, mean that every person wants the good, or prevent it from being supplied free of charge.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem:
To restaurant owners, the free drinking water provided to customers is a ____________.

(1) free good
(2) producer good
(3) consumer good
(4) private good
questions.explanation: The water is produced from scarce resources, so it is an economic rather than a free good. It is used to produce catering service, making it a producer good, and it is rival and excludable, making it a private good.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meaning of private property rights and its importance in a market economy
questions.stem:
Mr. Li owns a residential unit and lives with his family. He has the right to

(1) hold a birthday party for his son in the unit.
(2) rent out the room of his son for income.
(3) refuse the teacher of his son to enter his unit.
questions.explanation: The unit is Mr. Li's private property, so he has the full bundle of property rights, including use, deriving income and excluding others.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: After changing the firm's form of business ownership, firm A would have an independent legal status while the firm's financial status can still be kept confidential. We can conclude that firm A may have changed from a ___________ to a ___________.

choices.text: private limited company ... public limited company

questions.explanation: A partnership has no independent legal status. A private limited company is a separate legal entity but need not disclose its financial information publicly, so the stated change can be from partnership to private limited company.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible reason for a firm to choose to be a private limited company instead of a public limited company?

choices.text: The risk of being taken over will be lower.
The firm will earn a higher rate of return.
The firm can issue shares and bonds.
The firm pays a lower profits tax rate.

questions.explanation: Private-company shares are not freely transferable, so the risk of takeover is lower. Both forms can issue shares and bonds and face the same profits-tax rate; their form does not determine the rate of return.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: There are metered parking spaces in many places in Hong Kong. Drivers can park their cars in the metered parking spaces after paying fees. Which of the following statements about these parking spaces is CORRECT?

choices.text: These parking spaces are allocated on a first-come-first-served basis, so they are public goods.
These parking spaces are rival in consumption, so they are private goods.
Anyone can pay to use these parking spaces, so they are consumer goods.
People need to pay to use these parking spaces, so they are economic goods.

questions.explanation: When one driver uses a parking space, fewer spaces are available to others. The spaces are therefore rival in consumption and are private goods. Payment or first-come-first-served allocation does not define these classifications.

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem:
Mr. Wong is the owner of a renovation company. The company employs many workers for different stages of a renovation project, including painters, plumbers and water and electrical technicians. Mr. Wong is responsible for contacting customers. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) Mr. Wong is an entrepreneurship and his workers are labour.
(2) Mr. Wong's company adopts complex division of labour.
(3) The workers do not need to learn every task involved in a project, thus training time can be reduced.
questions.explanation: Mr. Wong makes decisions and bears business risk, so he is entrepreneurship, while the workers are labour. Different specialists perform different stages of production, which is complex division of labour and reduces the training needed for each worker.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following would reduce the occupational mobility of labour in an economy?

choices.text: The government tightens the quota for importing foreign workers.
The government establishes more licensing systems to regulate practitioners of different industries.
The railway network of the economy becomes more comprehensive.
The government offers a wider variety of training programmes.

questions.explanation: More licensing requirements raise the training time and resources needed to enter occupations, increasing the cost of changing occupations. This reduces workers' ability and willingness to move between occupations.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem:
Jimmy is a hairstylist. He earns a salary of $20,000 a month. In addition, he can earn a commission of $200 for being the designated hairstylist.

From the viewpoint of Jimmy, which of the following is an advantage of the above arrangement over receiving a monthly salary only?

(1) It is possible for Jimmy to earn a higher income.
(2) Jimmy can earn a more stable income.
(3) The cost of monitoring Jimmy's service quality is lower.
questions.explanation: Commission gives Jimmy a chance to earn more by providing better service. It makes income less stable, and lower monitoring cost is an advantage to the salon rather than to Jimmy.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The following table shows the input-output relationship of a firm. The only inputs required are machines and labour.
questions.explanation: Machines are fixed while labour varies, so the firm operates in the short run. Total product rises from 840 to 1,000 when labour rises from 7 to 8, so marginal product falls from 180 to 160 and diminishing marginal returns apply. Economies of scale cannot be concluded from short-run data.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the above firm are CORRECT?

(1) The firm is operating in the short run.
(2) The law of diminishing marginal returns applies.
(3) The firm enjoys economies of scale.

questions.keyPoint: Variable costs and fixed costs
questions.stem: Study the following information about the opening hours of a beauty salon.
questions.explanation: Disposable gloves and air-conditioning expenditure rise with the longer opening hours, so they are variable costs. Premises rent and accounting-staff salary do not vary with the hours in the stated period, so they are fixed costs.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following are the variable cost(s) involved in the extra hours of operation for the beauty salon on weekends and public holidays?

(1) expenses on purchasing disposable gloves
(2) the rental of the premises
(3) expenses on air conditioning
(4) the salary paid to the accounting staff

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem: The following is the market share of property developers in a country.

choices.text: to spread risk by business diversification
to build up goodwill of the company

questions.explanation: The acquisition is horizontal integration between firms in the same business. It can reduce competition, build goodwill and create economies of scale, but it does not diversify the business and therefore is least likely to spread risk.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose Giant Real Estate has acquired Capital Property. Which of the following is the LEAST likely motive behind the acquisition?

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a firm.
questions.explanation: At price $21, profit-maximising output is 4 units, total revenue is $84 and total cost is $72, so profit is $12. At price $19, output is 3 units, total revenue is $57 and total cost is $51, so profit is $6. Profit therefore falls by $6 and total cost falls from $72 to $51. Rising average cost indicates diseconomies, not economies, of scale.
questions.postVisualStem:
Based on the above table, we can conclude that when the market price decreases from $21 to $19,

(1) the firm will enjoy economies of scale.
(2) the profit of the firm will decrease by $6.
(3) the total cost of the firm will decrease from $72 to $51.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which of the following is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

choices.text: When the fine for littering increases, fewer people litter.
When people visiting Hong Kong need to quarantine, their average number of stay days after quarantine increases.
When the government increases the per-unit tax on tobacco products, the quantity of high-quality tobacco products sold decreases.
When the cost of transporting fruits from South Korea to Hong Kong increases, the average quality of fruits imported from South Korea decreases.

questions.explanation: Higher transport cost lowers the relative price of high-quality fruit when both qualities incur the same increase. Demand shifts towards high-quality fruit, so the average quality should rise rather than fall. The other statements are consistent with demand responding to changes in full or relative price.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: A courier company adjusts its fare as follows:

choices.text: Total expenditure of sender will increase.
Demand for the service of the courier company will decrease.
Orders of the courier company will increase.
The average weight of each parcel will increase.

questions.explanation: The first kilogram becomes more expensive while the marginal charge for later weight is unchanged. Heavier parcels become cheaper relative to lighter parcels, so the proportion of heavier parcels rises and average parcel weight increases. Orders and quantity demanded fall, while total expenditure is uncertain.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements is CORRECT after the adjustment of the fare?

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram of infant formula milk powder. The initial equilibrium point is E0.
questions.explanation: A lower birth rate reduces demand, shifting the demand curve left. More manufacturers increase supply, shifting the supply curve right. The combined movements take equilibrium from E0 to E3.

visuals.alt: Infant formula milk powder demand and supply diagram with equilibrium points E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Infant formula milk powder demand and supply

movements: A lower birth rate shifts demand left from D0 to D2.
More manufacturers shift supply right from S0 to S1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The two shifts move equilibrium from E0 to E3, so option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the birth rate decreases and, at the same time, more manufacturers enter the infant formula milk powder market. The new equilibrium point will be at _____________.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: S is the supply curve for laptop computers. Which of the following reasons can best explain the change of the equilibrium position in the laptop computer market from A to B?

choices.text: The price of raw materials of producing laptop computers decreases.
Several laptop computer manufacturers close down.
Laptop computer retailers offer interest-free instalment plans for customers.
The price of tablet computers decreases.

questions.explanation: The movement from A to B is along an unchanged supply curve, showing lower demand for laptops. Tablet computers are substitutes, so a lower tablet price decreases demand for laptops. The other options shift supply or increase demand.

visuals.alt: Laptop computer market with an upward-sloping supply curve and equilibrium moving from A to B.
visuals.caption: Laptop computer equilibrium movement

movements: The movement from A to B is along an unchanged supply curve, so demand decreases.
A fall in the price of substitute tablet computers decreases demand for laptops.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Only option D causes the movement from A to B.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: To encourage the public to exercise more, the government has built cycling tracks in many districts. More people have taken up cycling since then. As a result, the price of bicycles has increased by 10% and the quantity transacted has increased by 50%. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The demand for bicycles is elastic.
The demand for bicycles is inelastic.
The supply of bicycles is elastic.
The supply of bicycles is inelastic.

questions.explanation: The cycling tracks increase demand, so price and quantity both rise. The 50% rise in quantity supplied is greater than the 10% rise in price, showing elastic supply.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X.

choices.text: consumers will bear a larger tax burden than producers.
consumers' total expenditure will decrease by $4.
producers' total revenue net of tax will decrease by $36.
the total government tax revenue will be $44.

questions.explanation: Before tax, equilibrium is $16 and 11 units. With a $4 tax, consumers pay $18 and 10 units are traded, leaving producers $14. Each side bears $20, consumer expenditure rises by $4, and producers' net revenue falls from $176 to $140, a $36 fall. Tax revenue is $40.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules for good X
