questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about monopoly is CORRECT?

choices.text: A monopolist must earn a positive profit.
A firm needs to obtain government authorisation to become a monopolist.
The goods supplied by a monopolist are necessities.
A monopolist can adjust its price freely without losing all customers.

questions.explanation: A monopolist faces the market demand curve and can change price without losing every customer. It need not earn positive profit, need government authorisation, or produce necessities.

questions.keyPoint: Give examples of monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly
questions.stem: Which of the following markets is the closest example of an oligopoly in Hong Kong?
questions.explanation: Property agency is closest to oligopoly because a small number of major firms dominate the market. Water supply is closer to monopoly, while hotel accommodation and hairdressing have many providers.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Allocative function
questions.stem:
In recent years, the demand for high-quality fruits has increased. It has prompted many firms to import high-quality fruits from all over the world for sale in Hong Kong.

The above case illustrates the _________ function of price because __________.

choices.text: allocative ... more resources are allocated to import high-quality fruits
allocative ... high-quality fruits will be distributed to users with the highest value
rationing ... more people are willing to sell high-quality fruits
rationing ... the demand for high-quality fruits increases

questions.explanation: Higher demand and price signal firms to allocate more resources to importing high-quality fruit. That is the allocative function of price, rather than its rationing function.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the demand and supply curves of a good.

choices.text: The consumer surplus will increase by area acP0P2.
The producer surplus will increase by area bcP0P1.
The new deadweight loss will be area acg.
The deadweight loss will decrease by area abfg.

questions.explanation: Reducing the tax shifts the tax-inclusive supply curve down from S2 to S1, lowering price and raising quantity. Deadweight loss falls from area acg to area bcf, so the reduction is area abfg.

visuals.alt: Demand and supply diagram showing no-tax supply and two tax-inclusive supply curves with labelled areas.
visuals.caption: Tax reduction and deadweight loss

movements: Lowering the tax shifts the tax-inclusive supply curve down from S2 to S1.
Quantity transacted rises and the deadweight-loss area falls from acg to bcf.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The reduction in deadweight loss is area abfg, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the government lowers the tax on the good from t2 to t1. Which of the following statements is

CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: The supply of organic grapes is perfectly inelastic. Suppose the government imposes an effective price ceiling on organic grapes. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: Consumers' total expenditure on organic grapes will remain unchanged.
The quantity transacted of organic grapes will decrease.
There will be a surplus in the organic grape market.
The producer surplus in the organic grape market will decrease.

questions.explanation: With perfectly inelastic supply, quantity transacted is unchanged. An effective ceiling lowers the market price, so consumer expenditure and producer surplus fall. It creates a shortage, not a surplus.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Suppose the government has decided to provide a per-unit subsidy to local hotels and, at the same time, staying in local hotels for vacation has become popular since the Outbound Travel Alert on all overseas territories was issued. If the supply is not perfectly inelastic, which of the following statements about the local hotel market is CORRECT?

choices.text: Consumers' total expenditure on local hotel room rentals will increase.
The market price of local hotel rooms will decrease.

questions.explanation: The subsidy increases supply while the travel change increases demand. Quantity rises but the effects on price and consumers' expenditure are uncertain. A per-unit subsidy creates deadweight loss, and both changes increase producer surplus.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem:
Country A has imposed an effective quota on paper. Suppose electronic leaflets and bills are now more commonly used to reduce the use of paper. Which of the following statements about the paper market are CORRECT?

(1) The quota may become ineffective.
(2) The producer surplus will decrease.
(3) The deadweight loss will decrease.
questions.explanation: The use of electronic alternatives reduces paper demand. If demand falls below the quota limit, the quota becomes ineffective. Producer surplus falls whether the quota remains effective or not, and lower demand narrows the marginal-benefit and marginal-cost gap, reducing deadweight loss.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: Mr. Cheung's son often plays ball at home. Miss Li, who lives in the apartment below Mr. Cheung's, often complains to him that the noise of his son playing ball is very annoying. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: If Mr. Cheung needs to compensate Miss Li for the noise, there will be no divergence between private and social costs.
If Mr. Cheung needs to compensate Miss Li for the noise, the noise generated from Mr. Cheung's home will be reduced.
If Miss Li receives compensation from Mr. Cheung, she will not complain about the noise any more.
Economic efficiency can be achieved only when the government intervenes and asks Mr. Cheung to compensate Miss Li.

questions.explanation: Compensation raises the marginal private cost of generating noise, so Mr. Cheung reduces the noise. It narrows, but does not necessarily eliminate, the divergence between private and social cost. Private bargaining can also correct an externality without government intervention.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Lorenz curve
questions.stem: Study the following Lorenz curves of Country A and Country B.

choices.text: The income distribution of Country A is less even than that of Country B.
The high-income group in Country A is richer than that in Country B.
The income gap of Country B is wider than that of Country A.
The Gini coefficient of Country B is smaller than that of Country A.

questions.explanation: Country B's Lorenz curve is farther from the line of perfect equality, so its income gap is wider and its Gini coefficient is larger. A Lorenz curve shows distribution, not the absolute income of high-income households.

visuals.alt: Lorenz curves for Country A and Country B, with Country B's curve farther from equality.
visuals.caption: Lorenz curves of Country A and Country B

movements: Country B's curve is farther from the line of perfect equality than Country A's.
A curve farther from equality indicates a wider income gap and a larger Gini coefficient.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Country B has the wider income gap, making option C correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about Country A and Country B is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: Suppose an economy's Gini coefficient based on post-tax post-social transfer monthly household income is lower than the Gini coefficient based on original monthly household income. We can conclude that

choices.text: the living quality of low-income households has improved.
the taxes and welfare transfers can help reduce income inequality.
the amount of welfare transfers given by the government to low-income households is not sufficient.
the tax system of the economy is likely to be regressive.

questions.explanation: A lower post-tax-and-transfer Gini coefficient means taxes and welfare transfers reduce the measured income inequality. It does not by itself establish living quality, sufficient welfare transfers, or a regressive tax system.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Kevin is making plans for the summer holidays. He has several options and his order of preference is shown below:

First option: to learn to drive a car
Second option: to work as an intern at a TV station
Third option: to work as a research assistant in a university

Suppose Kevin's order of preference remains unchanged. Which of the following will lower Kevin's opportunity cost of working as an intern at a TV station?

choices.text: Kevin finds that he does not enjoy driving a car.
The requirements for Hong Kong full driving licence holders to apply for an International Driving Permit are relaxed.
The TV station reduces the salary for interns.
The market demand for people specialised in the subject in which Kevin works as a research assistant in the university increases.

questions.explanation: The opportunity cost is the value of Kevin's highest-valued forgone option, learning to drive. Finding driving less enjoyable lowers that value. The other changes either raise that value, affect the chosen option, or affect only the third option.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are normative statements?

(1) The economic losses caused by network attacks initiated by hackers amounted to billions of dollars.
(2) The government should help private enterprises improve cybersecurity.
(3) Installing a firewall is the best way to prevent network attacks.
questions.explanation: Statements (2) and (3) contain value judgements and cannot be settled by facts alone. Statement (1) is a factual, refutable claim and is positive.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: Electric vehicle chargers have been installed in some car parks in Hong Kong to provide charging services to electric vehicle drivers. The above case is related to the __________ question(s) in economics.

choices.text: 'what to produce' and 'for whom to produce'
'how to produce' and 'for whom to produce'

questions.explanation: Installing chargers determines the service to produce. Providing it to electric-vehicle drivers also concerns for whom the service is produced; the case does not identify the production method.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Ricky is the only owner of an audiovisual production company. He does not have to bear legal responsibility for the company. Which of the following statements MUST be true?

choices.text: The company needs to disclose its accounting information to the public.
The company can raise capital by issuing shares or bonds to the public.
Ricky's loss is confined to the amount of his investment.
The company will no longer exist if Ricky dies.

questions.explanation: Ricky has limited liability, so the firm is a limited company and his loss is limited to his investment. A private limited company need not disclose accounts or issue shares publicly, and a company remains a legal entity after its owner dies.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem:
Some bus compartments are equipped with USB charging ports, and passengers can use the charging ports free of charge. These charging ports are generally allocated on a first-come-first-served basis.

These charging ports are __________, because ___________.

choices.text: public goods ... these charging ports are free for the public to use
public goods ... these charging ports are non-rival in consumption
private goods ... these charging ports are excludable in consumption
private goods ... anyone can use these charging ports on a first-come-first-served basis

questions.explanation: A port being used by one passenger can be withheld from others, so it is excludable and rival. Free use does not make a good public.

the relative importance of primary production in terms of employment decreased.
the number of workers engaged in secondary production decreased.
the contribution of tertiary production to GDP increased.

questions.explanation: Primary production's employment share fell from 5% to 4%, so its relative importance in employment fell. The table does not state total employment, worker numbers or GDP.

Firm A practises a higher degree of division of labour than firm B.

questions.explanation: Firm A produces 100/(15 x 8) = 0.83 units per man-hour; firm B produces 100/(10 x 8) = 1.25. More training can account for firm B's higher productivity. The other three reasons predict the opposite.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: In a hospital, which of the following people have the lowest occupational mobility?
questions.explanation: Doctors require extensive specialist knowledge and training, making the opportunity cost of changing occupation highest. Their occupational mobility is therefore lowest.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem:
Doctors at public hospitals are usually paid by time rate instead of being paid according to the number of patients they treat because

(1) it can increase their productivity.
(2) the cost of measuring their output is very high.
(3) it can reduce the cost of public hospitals monitoring their treatment quality.
questions.explanation: Doctors' output is non-standardised and costly to measure. Time rate also avoids the incentive to rush treatment and reduces quality-monitoring cost, but does not raise productivity directly.

questions.keyPoint: Variable costs and fixed costs
questions.stem:
During the COVID-19 epidemic, many airlines cancelled their flights. Which of the following are fixed costs that airlines cannot save by cancelling the flights?

(1) salary of the flight attendants
(2) expenses on purchasing fuel
(3) interest on bank loans
(4) salary of the accounting staff
questions.explanation: Loan interest and accounting-staff salary do not vary with the number of flights, while flight-attendant pay and fuel expenditure can be saved when flights are cancelled.

questions.keyPoint: External economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: After an industrial building is revitalised, many restaurants choose to open in the building, which attracts many customers, and the marketing costs of the restaurants are reduced. In this case, the restaurants in the building

choices.text: suffer from external diseconomies of scale.
suffer from internal diseconomies of scale.

questions.explanation: The expansion of the restaurant cluster reduces marketing costs for each restaurant. This lowers long-run average cost through an external economy of scale.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The following table shows the cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm.
questions.explanation: Initially profit is highest at 4 units: $104 - $92 = $12. With the new costs, profit is highest at 5 units: $130 - $110 = $20, so both output and profit rise.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem:
The government of a country provides a per-unit subsidy on electric cars. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) If the demand for electric cars is elastic, total sales revenue will increase.
(2) People will buy fewer high-quality electric cars.
(3) The ratio of high-quality electric cars sold to total electric cars sold will decrease.
questions.explanation: A subsidy lowers price and raises quantity; with elastic demand, sales revenue rises. It raises sales of high-quality cars too, but makes high-quality cars relatively more expensive, lowering their share of total sales.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem:
The elderly care service sector in Hong Kong faces persistent labour shortages. A 2020 survey showed that there were near 6,000 vacancies in the sector. Which of the following can alleviate the above situation?

(1) to import more foreign workers
(2) to provide subsidies to employees of the elderly care service sector
(3) to introduce more machines to replace labour
questions.explanation: Importing workers and employee subsidies increase labour supply. Machinery substitutes for labour and reduces labour demand, so all three reduce excess demand for labour.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the demand-supply diagram for local workers in Country A. E0 is the initial equilibrium point.
questions.explanation: Retirement shifts local labour supply left. More imported workers lower foreign wages; as foreign and local labour are substitutes, demand for local labour also shifts left. The new equilibrium is E4.

visuals.alt: Labour demand and supply diagram with E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Local-worker labour market

movements: Retirement reduces local labour supply from S0 to S2.
More imported workers lower the foreign-worker wage and reduce demand for local substitutes from D0 to D2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The two leftward shifts meet at E4, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose more local workers decide to retire. At the same time, the government increases the quota for importing foreign workers. The new equilibrium point will be ____________.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem:
Read the following news excerpt.

On 19 December 2021, some public transport operators, including those of buses, MTR and trams, offered free rides. A minibus operator revealed that, because minibuses did not offer free rides, their total revenue on that day decreased by 80%.

Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) There was an excess supply of minibus service.
(2) The demand for the public transport services that offered free rides remained unchanged.
(3) There was an excess demand for services provided by the public transport operators that offered free rides.
questions.explanation: Free rides lower the price of substitute services and reduce demand for minibuses, leaving excess supply. The free ride changes quantity demanded rather than demand for the free services, and price zero creates excess demand for an economic good.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the tax burden
questions.stem: Suppose a per-unit tax is levied on good X. If the demand for good X is ___________, and the supply of good X is ___________, the consumers' tax burden will be smaller than the producers' tax burden.
questions.explanation: The more elastic side bears the smaller share of a tax. Consumers bear less only when demand is more elastic than supply, as in option D.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem:
Suppose a country abolishes the effective quota on good X, and at the same time good X becomes more popular. Which of the following statements about the market of good X are CORRECT?

(1) The price may increase or decrease.
(2) The consumer surplus will decrease.
(3) Total social surplus will increase.
questions.explanation: Removing an effective quota lowers price while higher demand raises it, so the price change is uncertain. Consumer surplus rises, not falls, and removing quota deadweight loss together with higher demand raises total social surplus.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers

Suppose the per-unit tax on good X decreases from t2 to t1. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: According to the Mass Transit Railway By-laws, people who smoke in any part of the railway premises are subject to a $5,000 fine. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The fine causes the quantity of cases of smoking in the railway premises to reach the socially optimal level.
The fine increases the marginal private cost of smokers.
The fine is a market solution to the divergence between private and social costs.
People do not smoke in the railway premises any more.

questions.explanation: A fine makes smoking more costly to the offender and therefore increases marginal private cost. It need not equal the marginal external cost or eliminate smoking, and it is a government rather than market solution.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem:
Refer to the following proposals.

Proposal (1): raising the standard tax rate of the salaries tax
Proposal (2): introducing a progressive rating system for the profits tax
Proposal (3): raising the amount of Comprehensive Social Security Assistance Schemes

Which of the above proposals help reduce the income gap in Hong Kong without raising the price level?
questions.explanation: Higher salaries and progressive profits tax narrow the income gap and lower aggregate demand, so they do not raise the price level. Higher social assistance raises low-income households' income but also raises aggregate demand and the price level.

questions.stem: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand curve, the short run aggregate supply curve and the long run aggregate supply curve of an economy. The economy is initially at E0.

choices.text: an increase in government transfer payments and an increase in government expenditure on education
an increase in the number of tourists and an occurrence of a large-scale strike in the economy
a decrease in asset demand for money and a decrease in the profits tax rate
a decrease in the price of raw materials and a decrease in the salaries tax rate

questions.explanation: Lower raw-material prices increase SRAS. A lower salaries-tax rate raises disposable income and consumption, increasing AD. This matches the diagram's rightward shifts of SRAS and AD.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: Which of the following will cause an economy's price level and aggregate output to increase in the short run?

choices.text: Consumers expect the future price level to increase.
The economy's major trading partner experiences a recession.

questions.explanation: Expected future inflation raises current consumption, shifting AD right. The other changes lower consumption, investment or net exports and shift AD left.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: Study the following diagram.

choices.text: The government reduces the import tariff.
The government distributes cash to citizens.

questions.explanation: A lower import tariff can reduce net exports and AD, creating a deflationary gap. Lower input prices then raise SRAS and restore output to LRAS at the lower price level A.

visuals.caption: Long-run adjustment

movements: A fall in aggregate demand creates a deflationary output gap.
Lower input prices then shift SRAS right, returning output to LRAS at a lower price level.

questions.topicGroup: Licensed banks, restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies in
questions.keyPoint: Features of the three types of deposit-taking institutions
questions.stem:
Miss Wong wants to deposit $100,000 for three months. Which of the following financial institutions in Hong Kong can accept her deposit?

(1) licensed banks
(2) restricted licence banks
(3) deposit-taking companies
questions.explanation: Licensed banks and deposit-taking companies can accept this deposit. Restricted licence banks can accept deposits only of HK$500,000 or above.

questions.keyPoint: Definitions of M1, M2 and M3 in
questions.stem: Mr. Tai withdraws HK$100,000 cash from a deposit-taking company. He keeps half of the amount as cash at home and remits the remainder overseas. What will be the immediate effect of the above actions on the money supply of Hong Kong?

choices.text: Both M1 and M2 will increase by HK$50,000.
M1, M2 and M3 will decrease by HK$50,000.

questions.explanation: The withdrawal raises M1 and M2 by $100,000 while leaving M3 unchanged. Keeping $50,000 cash at home changes nothing; remitting the other $50,000 overseas reduces all three measures by that amount. M1 and M2 therefore rise by $50,000.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Study the following information. Suppose banks do not hold excess reserves.

choices.text: the maximum amount of deposits will be $350 million.
the money supply will remain unchanged.
the monetary base will increase by $10 million.
the maximum amount of loans will decrease by $280 million.

questions.explanation: Initial reserves are $80m and deposits are $400m, giving a 20% required reserve ratio. After the withdrawal, reserves are $70m, so maximum deposits are $70m / 20% = $350m.
questions.postVisualStem: If the public withdraw $10 million from the banking system and hold it in cash,

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money demand curve (Md) and money supply curve (Ms) of an economy. The original equilibrium point is at E.

choices.text: will increase ... may increase or decrease

questions.explanation: A lower discount rate raises money supply, lowering the nominal interest rate and raising quantity of money. Greater asset liquidity lowers money demand and lowers the interest rate further, without changing the conclusion on quantity.

visuals.alt: Money demand and supply diagram with original equilibrium E.
visuals.caption: Money demand and supply

movements: A lower discount rate increases money supply.
Greater liquidity of interest-bearing assets lowers money demand.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Both changes reduce the nominal interest rate; money quantity rises because of the supply increase, so option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government lowers the discount rate and the liquidity of interest-bearing assets increases. The nominal interest rate __________ and the quantity of money __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Nominal interest rate as the (opportunity) cost of holding money
questions.stem: Suppose the nominal interest rate of a bond is 3%. If the actual inflation rate is higher than expected,

choices.text: the nominal rate of return of holding cash will decrease.
the cost of holding cash will increase.
the actual real interest rate will be higher than the nominal interest rate.
the actual real rate of return of the bond will be lower than expected.

questions.explanation: Actual real return equals the nominal interest rate less actual inflation. Higher-than-expected actual inflation makes real bond return lower than expected; the cost of holding cash remains the nominal interest rate.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem:
Suppose the growth rate of the price level is increasing. If the growth rate of the money supply is increasing and is higher than the growth rate of the price level, according to the quantity theory of money,

(1) nominal output is increasing.
(2) real output is increasing.
(3) the velocity of circulation of money is decreasing.
questions.explanation: Under MV = PY with velocity assumed constant, faster money growth means nominal output rises. If money grows faster than the price level, real output also rises; nothing implies falling velocity.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: Which of the following will most likely cause the unemployment rate of an economy to decrease?

choices.text: The government relaxes the policy on importing foreign workers.
The government raises the unemployment benefits.
There is a decrease in the number of places in post-secondary education.

questions.explanation: Firms expanding create more jobs and lower unemployment. Imported labour can displace local workers, higher benefits reduce work incentive, and fewer education places may expand the labour force without assuring jobs.

questions.keyPoint: Taxation in
questions.stem:
Ms. Cheung is a nurse at a private hospital in Hong Kong. She owns a residential unit in the Mainland and receives rental income from leasing it. Recently, she has purchased a first-hand residential unit in Hong Kong and has since lived in it. According to the information, which type(s) of tax does Ms. Cheung need to pay to the Hong Kong government?

(1) property tax
(2) stamp duty
(3) salaries tax
questions.explanation: Hong Kong applies a source principle, so rent earned in the Mainland is not subject to property tax. She pays stamp duty on the first-hand Hong Kong purchase and salaries tax on Hong Kong employment income.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the change in the salaries tax structure of an economy.

choices.text: reduce the work incentive of the high-income group.
widen the income gap between the rich and the poor.

questions.explanation: The new structure raises the high-income group's tax rate, reducing work incentive. Tax allowance is unchanged, the income gap narrows, and the revenue effect is uncertain.

visuals.alt: Old and new salaries-tax structures plotted against income.
visuals.caption: Salaries-tax structure

movements: The new rate is lower for lower incomes and higher for high incomes.
The tax allowance is unchanged.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The higher high-income tax rate reduces high-income work incentive, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Compared to the old tax system, the new tax system will

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem:
If the government imposes a sales tax on most of the goods and services, which of the following would occur?

(1) Gross domestic product will increase.
(2) Income distribution will be more uneven.
(3) The government will have a fiscal surplus.
questions.explanation: Sales tax is regressive and makes the income distribution more uneven. It reduces consumption and GDP; without expenditure information, a fiscal surplus cannot be concluded.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: Refer to the AS-AD diagram below.

choices.text: inflationary (output) gap ... an increase in the unemployment benefit
inflationary (output) gap ... an increase in the progressivity of income tax
deflationary (output) gap ... a decrease in the profits tax rate
deflationary (output) gap ... an open market sale of government bonds

questions.explanation: E0 output is below LRAS, creating a deflationary output gap. Lowering profits tax raises investment and AD, moving output right toward long-run equilibrium.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with E0 to the left of long-run aggregate supply.
visuals.caption: Deflationary output gap

movements: E0 lies below full-employment output, so the economy has a deflationary gap.
A lower profits-tax rate raises investment and shifts AD right.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option C correctly identifies the gap and restorative policy.

questions.postVisualStem: The economy operates at E0 initially. There is a/an ____________ and __________ can help restore the economy to its long run equilibrium.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem:
Country A is facing fiscal deficit and trade deficit. Which of the following may improve the fiscal deficit and trade deficit at the same time?

(1) an increase in money supply
(2) a decrease in the basic allowance of the salaries tax
(3) an appreciation of Country A's currency
questions.explanation: A lower basic allowance increases tax revenue and reduces disposable income, lowering imports. More money raises income and imports, while currency appreciation has uncertain trade effects and may worsen fiscal revenue.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: The following table shows the amounts of consumption of two goods in Country A and Country B before trade. Assume both countries use half of the resources to produce milk and half to produce juice.
questions.explanation: The opportunity cost of one milk is 2 juice in Country A and 0.8 juice in Country B. Mutually beneficial terms must fall strictly between 0.8 and 2, so 1.25 works.
questions.postVisualStem: If 1 unit of milk can be exchanged for _________ units of juice, both countries can gain from trade.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of a quota on domestic price, domestic consumption, domestic production and import quantity for a small open economy
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the market situation of good X in a small open economy.

choices.text: the domestic price of the good will remain unchanged.
the quantity of imports will increase.
the domestic production of the good will increase.
the shortage of the good will be eliminated.

questions.explanation: The quota remains binding after the world price rises, so domestic price is P1 in both cases. The quota keeps imports at Q2 - Q1 and domestic production at Q1; there is no shortage.

visuals.alt: Small open economy demand and supply diagram with P0, P1, Q1 and Q2.
visuals.caption: Import quota in a small open economy

movements: At P0 the quota is Q2 minus Q1.
When world price rises to P1, the quota remains binding and domestic price stays P1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The domestic price remains P1, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: P0 is the world price of the good and the import quota imposed by the government is (Q2 - Q1) units. If the world price of the good increases to P1,

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Balance of payments and balance of the BOP account
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of balance of payment surplus and deficit
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about the balance of payments of an economy in a certain year.
questions.explanation: Services give an invisible-trade deficit of $10m. Current-account balance is (50 - 10) + (15 - 25) + (40 - 20) + (10 - 25) = $35m. A $20m reserve-asset decrease indicates a BOP deficit of $20m; GNI exceeds GDP because net factor income is positive.
questions.postVisualStem:
According to the above information, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The economy’s gross national income is smaller than its gross domestic product.
(2) The invisible trade deficit is $10 million.
(3) The current account surplus is $35 million.
(4) The balance of payments deficit is $20 million.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.keyPoint: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.stem:
Under the linked exchange rate system of Hong Kong, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The monetary base of Hong Kong is fully backed by the US dollars.
(2) The market exchange rate of the US dollar against the Hong Kong dollar is fixed at US$1 = HK$7.8.
(3) If the US dollar depreciates against other currencies, the average price of Hong Kong imports will tend to decrease.
(4) If the US dollar depreciates against other currencies, the total value of Hong Kong exports (in terms of the Hong Kong dollar) will increase.
questions.explanation: Hong Kong's monetary base is fully backed by US dollars. The linked rate is an official convertibility undertaking, not a fixed market rate. A weaker US dollar makes Hong Kong imports cost more in HK dollars and boosts export value in HK dollars.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Jason is planning to use the electronic consumption vouchers issued by the government for consumption. He has several options and his order of preference is as follows.

First option: to buy a mountain bike
Second option: to have a buffet dinner at a hotel
Third option: to buy a smartphone

Which of the following factors would LEAST likely affect the cost-benefit analysis for Jason's consumption choice?

choices.text: As a result of the celebrity effect, the resale price of the mountain bike increases sharply.
The hotel offers discounts for buffet dinners.
The functions of the smartphone are not as good as Jason expects.
More freebies are given when purchasing the smartphone.

questions.explanation: Jason chooses the mountain bike because its value exceeds that of the next best alternative, the buffet dinner. A poorer smartphone only lowers the value of the third option, so it does not change the benefit or opportunity cost of choosing the bike.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Refer to the following statements made by Mr. Chan and Miss Ho.

Mr. Chan: The suspension of evening dine-in services has led to an increase in takeout orders at restaurants.
Miss Ho: Measures introduced by the government's Anti-epidemic Fund are not enough to help restaurants.

__________ statement is __________ because __________.

choices.text: Mr. Chan's ... positive ... a value judgement is involved in the statement
Mr. Chan's ... normative ... it is inconsistent with real-world data
Miss Ho's ... positive ... it correctly describes the real-world situation
Miss Ho's ... normative ... it is not refutable by facts

questions.explanation: Mr. Chan's claim is a factual and refutable causal claim. Miss Ho's use of 'not enough' is a value judgement, so it is normative and cannot be settled by facts alone.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: In the 2022-23 Budget, the financial secretary proposed continuing to strengthen community and residential care services and social work services to support the elderly, persons with disabilities and children, involving an additional annual expenditure of over $1.9 billion. This suggestion is related to the __________ question(s) in economics.

choices.text: 'how to produce' and 'for whom to produce'
'what to produce' and 'for whom to produce'

questions.explanation: The proposal decides which services to provide and identifies the groups who will receive them. It does not state a method of production.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
Mr. Wong is considering the following two investments:

(1) setting up a photography company in the form of a sole proprietorship
(2) joining a friend's photography company as a partner

Which of the following is a possible reason for Mr. Wong deciding to set up a photography company in the form of a sole proprietorship?

choices.text: He can enjoy a higher degree of autonomy.
He is subject to a lower profits tax rate.
He does not need to use his personal assets to settle the debts of the business.
He wants the business to have better continuity.

questions.explanation: A sole proprietor can make decisions without approval from partners, giving greater autonomy. Sole proprietorships and partnerships have the same profits-tax treatment, both have unlimited liability, and neither has the continuity of a legal entity.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem:
In April 2022, the government distributed anti-epidemic service bags to all households in Hong Kong. The bag included rapid antigen test kits, proprietary Chinese medicine, masks, etc.

These anti-epidemic service bags are __________ because they ___________.

choices.text: private goods ... are excludable in consumption
economic goods ... are goods used for final consumption
free goods ... are free for the public to use
capital goods ... can be used to produce other goods and services

questions.explanation: A recipient can exclude others from consuming the bag and its contents, so it is a private good. Being supplied free of charge does not make it a free good.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem:
Jinny runs a hair salon. Under the previous wage payment scheme, she found that her workers were inefficient and had poor service attitudes. After she adopted a new wage payment scheme, the number of customers served each day increased and fewer customer complaints about her workers were received.

The previous wage payment scheme may have been a _________ scheme and the new one may be a _________ scheme.

choices.text: time rate ... basic salary plus commission

questions.explanation: Time-rate pay is not directly linked to output or service quality. Basic salary plus commission can preserve a basic income while rewarding output and service, matching the higher number served and fewer complaints.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem:
Firm A and firm B produce the same good. The labour supply of both firms is the same while firm A's output is twice firm B's. Which of the following is a possible reason for the difference in labour productivity between firm A and firm B?

(1) Firm A uses time rate while firm B uses piece rate to pay their workers.
(2) More capital goods are used in firm A.
(3) Firm A practises a higher degree of division of labour.
questions.explanation: Firm A has higher output per unit of labour. More capital goods and greater division of labour can raise productivity, whereas time rate rather than piece rate would tend to weaken the incentive to produce.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The table below shows the average product of a firm. Only machines and labour are used in the production.
questions.explanation: Machines are fixed, so the firm has fixed cost. Total product rises by 100, 155 and 225 as another worker is added, so marginal product is rising and the data do not show diminishing marginal returns. The firm is operating in the short run, so economies of scale cannot be inferred.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the above information is/are CORRECT?

(1) The firm has a fixed cost.
(2) The law of diminishing marginal returns does not apply to the firm.
(3) The firm enjoys economies of scale.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem:
Mr. Hui runs a bicycle shop selling various types of bicycles. He is considering expanding the business to spread his business risk.

Which of the following CANNOT achieve Mr. Hui's objective?

choices.text: setting up a store nearby providing a bicycle rental service
setting up a cycling school for children

questions.explanation: Buying another bicycle shop keeps the business exposed to the same bicycle-retail market. The other options add different sources of income and can diversify business risk.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a price taker.
questions.explanation: Original total costs are $60, $84, $110, $138 and $168. Adding $1 to average cost raises total cost to $63, $88, $115, $144 and $175, so marginal cost also rises by $1. At price $27, marginal cost equals price at 5 units and profit is $135 - $115 = $20.

visuals.caption: Cost-output relationship of a price taker

questions.postVisualStem:
If the average cost of every unit of output increases by $1 and the market price is $27,

(1) the profit-maximising output is 5 units.
(2) the marginal cost of every unit of output will increase by $1.
(3) the maximum profit is $20.

questions.keyPoint: Variable costs and fixed costs
questions.stem: Anson runs an indoor photography studio. In which of the following situations will Anson increase his production to maximise his profit?

choices.text: The hourly wage of photographers falls.
The monthly rental payment for the studio decreases.

questions.explanation: The hourly wage is a variable cost. Its fall lowers marginal cost, so the profit-maximising output rises. Rent and registration fee are fixed costs, while a higher electricity fee raises marginal cost.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: People of Country A love to eat oysters. Suppose the government of Country A imposes a per-unit tax on each kilogram of oysters. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The proportion of high-quality oysters sold in Country A will increase.
The total weight of oysters consumed by the people of Country A will increase.
The total expenditure of the people of Country A on oysters will decrease.
The average quality of oysters sold in Country A will decrease.

questions.explanation: A per-unit tax raises the money price of each quality by the same amount. High-quality oysters therefore become cheaper relative to low-quality oysters, so consumers buy more high-quality oysters relative to low-quality oysters. Quantity falls and total expenditure is uncertain.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem:
If the price of ___________ decreases, the demand for __________ will increase.

(1) air travel ... airports
(2) construction materials ... houses
(3) film cameras ... film
questions.explanation: Air travel creates derived demand for airports, and film cameras and film are complements. Cheaper construction materials affect the supply of houses rather than their demand.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: The following table shows the total expenditure of Kevin and Brian on online games.

choices.text: greater than 1 and smaller than infinity ... 0
greater than 1 and smaller than infinity ... 1

questions.explanation: Kevin's total expenditure falls as price rises, which indicates elastic demand. Brian's total expenditure is constant, which indicates unitary elasticity.
questions.postVisualStem: Kevin's elasticity of demand for online games is ____________ while Brian's elasticity of demand for online games is ____________ (without regard to its negative sign).

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: When the supply of good X decreases, its price and quantity transacted change by 10% and 5% respectively. Which of the following best explains the extent of the changes in the price and quantity transacted of good X?

choices.text: There are many close substitutes for good X.
The expenditure on good X accounts for a small proportion of people's income.
The factors of production for good X are easily available.
A low level of technology is required to produce good X.

questions.explanation: The larger percentage rise in price than fall in quantity shows inelastic demand. Demand is more inelastic when the good takes only a small share of income; the other relevant demand factor would make it more elastic, while C and D concern supply elasticity.

questions.keyPoint: Give examples of monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly
questions.stem: The vegetable retail market in Hong Kong is most likely an example of ______________ because ______________.

choices.text: monopolistic competition ... different retailers charge different prices
monopolistic competition ... there are many vegetable retailers in the market and their products are heterogeneous
oligopoly ... a few retailers have significantly larger market shares than the others
oligopoly ... the retailers take into account the pricing strategies of other retailers when making decisions

questions.explanation: Vegetable retailers are numerous and their goods and services can differ by quality, freshness and location. Those features make monopolistic competition the closest description.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Calculate producer surplus
questions.stem: The following table shows the marginal cost schedule of a coffee producer.
questions.explanation: At $12, the producer surplus is ($12 - $10) + ($12 - $11) + ($12 - $12) = $3. At $13, it is $3 + $2 + $1 + $0 = $6. It therefore increases by $3.

visuals.caption: Marginal cost schedule of a coffee producer

questions.postVisualStem: If the price of coffee increases from $12 to $13, the producer surplus will __________.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand and supply schedules for good X.

choices.text: the producers can receive a higher total sales revenue.
the sales volume will remain unchanged.
the demand for good X's substitutes will increase.

questions.explanation: The equilibrium is $20 and 20 units. At the $25 floor, only 15 units are demanded, so revenue falls from $400 to $375 and consumer surplus falls. The higher price raises demand for substitutes.

visuals.caption: Demand and supply schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: If the government sets a price floor of $25 on good X,

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram for good X.
questions.explanation: At Q1 the quota is effective. Raising it to Q2 makes it ineffective, so price falls and quantity rises to equilibrium. Consumer surplus rises and the quota's deadweight loss disappears; effects on revenue and producer surplus are uncertain.

visuals.alt: Demand and supply diagram for good X with quota levels Q1 and Q2.
visuals.caption: Effective and ineffective quota levels

movements: Increasing the quota from Q1 to Q2 makes the quota ineffective.
The market returns to equilibrium with a lower price and higher quantity transacted.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Consumer surplus and total social surplus increase, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
If the government increases the quota from Q1 to Q2, __________ will increase.

(

1) total sales revenue
(2) producer surplus
(3) consumer surplus
(4) total social surplus

questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the subsidy
questions.stem: After the government provides a per-unit subsidy of $3 for producers of milk, the market price of milk decreases by $2. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: Within the range of the original and new market prices, the elasticity of demand for milk is smaller than its elasticity of supply.
The ratio of producers' share of the subsidy to consumers' share of the subsidy is 3:2.
The change in the total revenue including the subsidy is uncertain.

questions.explanation: Consumers receive $2 of the $3 subsidy and producers receive $1, so demand is less elastic than supply. Producer surplus and revenue including subsidy increase, and the producer-to-consumer share is 1:2.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: A shopping mall sets up decorations in common areas for the public to rest and take photos. Which of the following will most likely be a positive external effect of the shopping mall's action?

choices.text: The waiting time of people for using the washrooms in the mall increases.
Business of the convenience stores near the mall increases greatly.
Rentals of the shops in the mall increase.
The problem of traffic congestion near the mall worsens.

questions.explanation: Nearby convenience stores can gain extra sales from the decorations without compensating the mall. That unpaid benefit to a third party is a positive external effect.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem: Which of the following can best explain why income inequality among private piano teachers tends to be larger than that among security guards?

choices.text: The market demand for private piano teachers is larger.
The supply of private piano teachers is more elastic.
Private piano teachers have a larger difference in natural abilities.
The average working hours of private piano teachers are shorter.

questions.explanation: Natural ability differs more among private piano teachers, so highly gifted teachers can earn much more than the average. This wider variation in human capital and ability leads to a wider income gap.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem:
Which of the following may lead to an increase in aggregate output and a narrower income gap in Hong Kong at the same time?

(1) launching the Working Family Allowance Scheme for eligible low-income families
(2) building more public housing
(3) decreasing the progressivity of the salaries tax
questions.explanation: The allowance raises low-income households' income and consumption. More public housing raises government expenditure and the real income of low-income households. Lower tax progressivity can raise output but widens the income gap.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: Consider the following gross domestic product (GDP) data of Country A.
questions.explanation: GDP at factor cost = private consumption + gross investment + government consumption + net exports - indirect taxes + subsidies. Hence 1,500 = 700 + (X - 50) + 500 + 100 - 15 + 50, giving X = 215.
questions.postVisualStem: If Country A's GDP at factor cost is $1,500 million, the value of X is ____________.

questions.keyPoint: Growth rate of GDP
questions.stem: The following table shows gross domestic product (GDP) data of an economy in a certain year.

choices.text: both the real GDP and the per capita nominal GDP increased.
both the real GDP and the per capita nominal GDP decreased.
the real GDP increased and the per capita nominal GDP decreased.
the real GDP decreased and the per capita nominal GDP increased.

questions.explanation: The price level falls by 2% while nominal GDP rises by 1.2%, so real GDP rises. Per capita nominal GDP changes by 1.012 / 1.025 - 1, which is negative.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the information above, we can conclude that in that year,

questions.keyPoint: Uses and limitations of national income statistics
questions.stem:
Which of the following are the reasons why a country's per capita real GDP is more accurate than its nominal GDP in reflecting people's standard of living?

(1) It considers the population size.
(2) It considers the effect of the general price level.
(3) It considers the effect of income distribution.
(4) It includes the value of non-market goods and services.
questions.explanation: Per capita real GDP adjusts GDP for population and the price level. It still does not show the distribution of income or include non-market goods and services.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.explanation: A recession abroad reduces exports, while a higher salaries-tax rate reduces disposable income and consumption; both reduce AD. Expected inflation shifts SRAS, and tax incentives raise investment and AD.

visuals.alt: Aggregate demand curve shifting left from AD0 to AD1.
visuals.caption: Leftward shift of aggregate demand

movements: A recession in a major trading partner reduces exports and net exports.
A higher salaries-tax rate reduces disposable income and consumption.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Both events shift AD left, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following are possible reasons for the above movement of the aggregate demand curve?

(1) A major trading partner suffers an economic recession.
(2) The government raises the salaries tax rate.
(3) Firms expect the general price level to increase.
(4) The government increases tax incentives for firms.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Country A is an importer of fuel. If ___________, Country A's ___________ will decrease.

choices.text: the price of fuel increases sharply ... price level in the short run
Country A's equipment for delivering fuel is seriously damaged ... price level in the long run
the fuel-exporting country imposes an embargo on fuel ... output level in the short run
Country A develops a substitute for fuel ... output level in the long run

questions.explanation: An embargo cuts the availability of a factor of production and shifts SRAS left, reducing short-run output. The other events either raise price or raise long-run output.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Inflationary gap
questions.stem: An economy initially has an inflationary (output) gap. Which of the following would NOT help the economy narrow the inflationary (output) gap?

choices.text: The government raises the business registration fee.
The price of raw materials falls.
The government cancels the production subsidies provided to firms.

questions.explanation: Cheaper raw materials shift SRAS right and raise output, widening an existing inflationary gap. The other options reduce AD or SRAS, lowering output toward long-run equilibrium.

questions.topicGroup: Licensed banks, restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies in
questions.keyPoint: Features of the three types of deposit-taking institutions
questions.stem:
Which of the following deposits CANNOT be accepted by a restricted licence bank?

(1) a time deposit of HK$100,000
(2) a demand deposit of HK$500,000 for three months
(3) a negotiable certificate of deposit of HK$600,000 for one month
questions.explanation: Restricted licence banks may accept time deposits and negotiable certificates of deposit of at least HK$500,000, but cannot accept demand deposits. Therefore (1) and (2) cannot be accepted.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem:
Miss Li withdraws HK$10,000 from her time deposit account with a licensed bank. She remits HK$3,000 overseas. Then she puts the remainder into her current account with the same bank.

What is the immediate effect of the above actions on the Hong Kong dollar money supply?

choices.text: M1, M2 and M3 will decrease by HK$3,000.
M1 will increase by HK$7,000, while M2 and M3 will decrease by HK$3,000.
M2 will decrease by HK$10,000 and M3 will remain unchanged.
Both M2 and M3 will decrease by HK$7,000.

questions.explanation: The withdrawal from a time deposit changes $10,000 from M2 to M1, leaving M2 and M3 unchanged. Sending $3,000 abroad lowers all measures by $3,000; returning $7,000 to a current account changes none. Hence M1 rises $7,000 while M2 and M3 fall $3,000.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual banking multipliers
questions.stem:
A banking system adopts a fractional reserve system. Suppose the banks hold excess reserves after lending. Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?

(1) The deposit creation ability of the banking system is not maximised.
(2) The money supply will be greater than the monetary base.
(3) The actual banking multiplier will be greater than the maximum banking multiplier.
questions.explanation: Excess reserves mean banks have not loaned out every possible amount, so deposit creation is not maximised. Because lending has occurred, deposits exceed reserves and money supply exceeds monetary base. Excess reserves make the actual multiplier smaller than the maximum multiplier.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Features of the four phases of a business cycle
questions.stem: Study the following diagram.
questions.explanation: Point A is the trough, where real GDP growth is at its lowest. Business confidence is low and unemployment is high; imports tend to fall and transfer payments tend to rise.

visuals.alt: Business-cycle graph showing point A below the average growth rate.
visuals.caption: Business-cycle trough

movements: Point A is the trough, where real GDP growth is lowest.
Business confidence is low and unemployment is high in a trough.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Only statements (1) and (2) describe point A, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following are phenomena that would occur at point A?

(1) Business confidence is at a low level.
(2) The unemployment rate is at a high level.
(3) The volume of imports increases.
(4) Government expenditure on transfer payments decreases.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem:
Suppose that, in a period of inflation, the expected real interest rate of an economy is 4% and the actual real interest rate is 2%. Which of the following people will gain?

(1) unemployed people who receive a fixed amount of unemployment assistance every month
(2) property owners who repay fixed-rate mortgage loans
(3) tenants who rent residential units at a fixed rental
(4) retired people who hold inflation-linked bonds issued by the government
questions.explanation: Actual inflation is higher than expected. Fixed nominal repayments and rents lose real value, so borrowers and tenants gain. A fixed unemployment payment loses real value, while inflation-linked bonds protect their holders.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: According to the quantity theory of money, when the central bank reduces the required reserve ratio,

choices.text: the velocity of circulation of money will decrease.

questions.explanation: A lower required reserve ratio raises money supply. With velocity assumed constant under MV = PY, nominal output rises proportionately. The result does not require velocity to fall, deflation, or an increase in real output.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem:
The money supply of an economy decreased while its monetary base remained unchanged. Which of the following could explain the above situation?

(1) The central bank raised the discount rate.
(2) The central bank raised the required reserve ratio.
(3) The central bank sold government bonds to the public.
questions.explanation: A higher required reserve ratio causes deposit contraction and lowers money supply without directly changing cash in circulation or bank reserves, so monetary base is unchanged. A higher discount rate or an open-market sale also reduces the monetary base.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: Which of the following will cause the unemployment rate in Hong Kong to increase?

choices.text: The government reduces the assistance to the unemployed.
Some new graduates who studied abroad are recruited by Hong Kong companies and return to Hong Kong to work, and do not replace any domestic workers.
Multinational enterprises invest in Hong Kong.
The government raises the statutory minimum wage.

questions.explanation: A higher statutory minimum wage raises employers' labour costs and can cause layoffs, increasing unemployment. The other events encourage job search, expand employment, or increase the labour force while leaving unemployment unchanged.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of taxation
questions.stem: The following table shows a change in the salaries tax structure of an economy.
questions.explanation: The unchanged basic allowance means the tax base is unchanged. Lower average tax rates for lower-income earners narrow the income gap. The total revenue effect is uncertain because work incentive and taxable income may rise.
questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the basic tax allowance remains unchanged. Compared to the old tax structure, the new tax structure will

(1) narrow the tax base.
(2) narrow the income gap between the rich and the poor.
(3) reduce the total tax revenue.

questions.keyPoint: Taxation in
questions.stem:
Mr. Chan is a Hong Kong resident. According to the tax system of Hong Kong, which of the following incomes is/are subject to taxation?

(1) the amount received by Mr. Chan from selling a residential unit in the Mainland
(2) the salary received by Mr. Chan from working in a coffee shop in Hong Kong
(3) the dividends received by Mr. Chan from holding shares of a Hong Kong bank
questions.explanation: Hong Kong uses a source principle, so income earned outside Hong Kong is not taxed. Salary from Hong Kong employment is taxable, while dividend income is not subject to Hong Kong tax.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram.

choices.text: The government lowers the discount rate.
The government raises the import tariff.
The transportation cost for raw materials decreases.

questions.explanation: Greater desired saving reduces consumption and shifts AD left. The resulting deflationary gap lowers input costs, shifts SRAS right and returns output to LRAS at the lower price level A. The other choices do not create that path.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with equilibrium moving from E to A on LRAS.
visuals.caption: Long-run adjustment after lower aggregate demand

movements: Higher desired saving reduces consumption and shifts AD left.
Lower input prices then shift SRAS right, returning output to LRAS at A.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: An increase in desired saving can create this adjustment, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: The long run equilibrium point of an economy changes from E to A. Which of the following is a possible reason for the change?

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Which of the following would offset the effect of lowering the required reserve ratio on aggregate output?

choices.text: a reduction in government transfer payments
an open market purchase of government bonds
a decrease in the asset demand for money

questions.explanation: Lowering the required reserve ratio is expansionary: money supply rises, interest rate falls and AD rises. Lower transfer payments reduce consumption and AD, offsetting the output effect. The other changes are expansionary.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: The following table shows the number of man-hours required to produce tomatoes and bananas in Country A and Country B.
questions.explanation: Country A has the lower opportunity cost of bananas: 3 tomatoes per banana, compared with 5 in Country B. Its gain per banana exported is 4 - 3 - 0.5 = 0.5 tomato, so ten bananas give a gain of 5 tomatoes.

visuals.caption: Man-hours needed to produce tomatoes and bananas

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the banana-exporting country exports 1 unit of bananas in exchange for 4 units of tomatoes. At the same time, the banana-exporting country needs to pay 0.5 units of tomatoes in transportation costs per unit of export. What is the total gain for the banana-exporting country from exporting 10 units of bananas?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of a quota on domestic price, domestic consumption, domestic production and import quantity for a small open economy
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the imposition of a quota on an imported good in a small open economy.
questions.explanation: At the higher world price, the quota remains binding. Domestic consumption stays 75 and domestic production stays 45, so imports are 30 units and their value is 30 x $30 = $900. Domestic producer revenue is unchanged.

visuals.alt: Small open economy demand and supply diagram with quota supply Sq and world prices of $20 and $30.
visuals.caption: Import quota in a small open economy

movements: When the world price rises to $30, the quota remains binding at 30 imported units.
Domestic consumption and production remain 75 and 45 units respectively.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Imports are 30 units at $30, so their value is $900 and option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
If the world price of the good increases to $30,

(1) the domestic consumption of the good will decrease by 15 units.
(2) the revenue of domestic producers of the good will increase by $750.
(3) the total import value of the good will be $900.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem:
A Japanese man came to Hong Kong to work as a sushi chef in a hotel for six months. Which of the following would be included in the calculation of Hong Kong's current account balance?

(1) the money he spent on a flight to Hong Kong on a Hong Kong airline
(2) the money he spent on buying shares of a listed company in Hong Kong
(3) the salary he received for his work in the hotel
questions.explanation: His spending on a Hong Kong airline is a services transaction, and his salary is income paid to a non-resident; both enter the current account. Buying shares is a capital and financial account transaction.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: The following table shows the change in the exchange rate between the US dollar (USD) and the Japanese yen (JPY).
questions.explanation: USD 2,000 buys JPY 212,600 in January. In December this converts to 212,600 / 112.6 = USD 1,888.1, so Katie loses about USD 111.9.
questions.postVisualStem:
Katie exchanged USD 2,000 for JPY in January. Then she sold the sum for USD in December.

In the above transactions, Katie _____________.

questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem: Miss Tang spent $8,000 on buying a computer two years ago. Suppose she can resell it for $2,000. Alternatively, she needs to spend $3,000 on upgrading the computer hardware before she can continue to use it. What is her cost of continuing to use the computer?
questions.explanation: Continuing to use the computer gives up the $2,000 resale value and requires a $3,000 upgrade. The past $8,000 purchase is irrecoverable, so the cost is $5,000.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Karson is a secondary school student. He is considering which extracurricular activity to join. He has several options and his order of preference is as follows.

First option: Joining the choir
Second option: Joining the astronomical society
Third option: Joining the soccer team

Which of the following factors would be LEAST likely to affect the cost-benefit analysis for Karson's choice?

choices.text: The choir changes their practice venue to somewhere farther away from Karson's home.
The astronomical society purchases a more advanced telescope for stargazing.
The soccer team invites a famous football player for demonstrations and coaching.
Karson's best friend quits the soccer team.

questions.explanation: The first choice has the choir's value as its benefit and the astronomical society's value as its cost. A friend leaving the third option lowers only that option's value and does not affect this cost-benefit analysis.

questions.keyPoint: Definition of free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: An electrical appliance retail chain provides free delivery service for any purchase of or above a specified amount. The delivery service is __________________ because ___________________.

choices.text: an economic good ... the marginal cost of providing the delivery service is positive
an economic good ... the delivery service can satisfy customers' wants
a free good ... the delivery service is free of charge
a free good ... more is not preferred

questions.explanation: Delivery uses scarce drivers, vehicles and fuel, so its marginal cost is positive and it is an economic good. Free-of-charge provision does not make a good free.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
Which of the following are related to the 'for whom to produce' problem?

(1) The government announced that only target groups were eligible for free seasonal influenza vaccines.
(2) The government launched an electronic platform that allows parents to submit admission applications and make school choices.
(3) The government introduced several measures to prevent unauthorised transfers of user permits for recreation and sports facilities.
questions.explanation: Eligibility for vaccines and controls over permit transfers determine who receives the services. The electronic platform concerns how applications are processed, so it is about how to produce.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Cyrus plans to set up a retail firm selling sports equipment in Hong Kong. He is considering setting up a sole proprietorship or a private limited company. Which of the following is a possible reason for him to choose to set up a sole proprietorship?

choices.text: A sole proprietorship has wider sources of capital compared to a private limited company.
A sole proprietorship is subject to a lower profits tax rate compared to a private limited company.
A sole proprietorship does not need to disclose its accounting information to the public while a private limited company needs to do so.
A sole proprietorship is not a legal entity while a private limited company is a legal entity.

questions.explanation: A sole proprietorship faces the lower profits-tax rate. It has narrower sources of capital, a private limited company can keep its accounts confidential, and the sole proprietor's lack of separate legal status creates unlimited liability rather than an advantage.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
