questions.stem: Study the following information about firm A and firm B.

choices.text: Firm B cannot keep its accounting information confidential while firm A can.
Owners of both firm A and firm B enjoy limited liability.
Firm A has a higher risk of being taken over by others than firm B.
Firm B earns a higher profit than firm A.

questions.explanation: Firm A is a partnership, while firm B is a public limited company with more than 50 owners and lasting continuity. Public limited companies must disclose accounts, whereas partnerships need not. The other claims do not follow.

visuals.caption: Information about firm A and firm B
rows: If an owner goes bankrupt, the firm has to be dissolved.
If an owner goes bankrupt, the firm can still exist.

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above table, which of the following descriptions of firm A and firm B is CORRECT?

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: The following diagram shows some traffic signs on a road.
questions.explanation: The information supplied by a traffic sign is non-rival and non-excludable, so it is a public good. The physical sign is made from scarce materials and can be controlled, so it is a private good.

visuals.alt: Road traffic signs showing bus-lane restrictions.
visuals.caption: Traffic signs

movements: The information is non-rival and non-excludable.
The physical signs are rival and excludable when used as materials.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The instructions are public goods and the signs are private goods, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: The instructions conveyed by the traffic signs are ____________ while the traffic signs are ____________.

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem:
When a key opinion leader (KOL) produces a video introducing tourist attractions in Hong Kong, he hires different people for different roles, such as actors, photographers, scriptwriters and makeup artists.

This is an example of ______________ division of labour because ____________________.

choices.text: simple ... each employee is responsible for one job
simple ... each employee cooperates with the others
complex ... each employee has their own specialty
complex ... each employee is involved in a different stage of video production

questions.explanation: Complex division of labour means workers specialise in different stages of producing a good or service. Each role contributes to a distinct stage of producing the video.

questions.keyPoint: Natural resources: land
questions.stem:
In August 2022, the government installed a floating photovoltaic system mock-up at Shing Mun River in Sha Tin, as part of a pilot trial. The electricity generated will mainly be used by nearby government facilities.

In the above case, the sunlight in the production of solar energy belongs to ___________ because ________________.

choices.text: capital ... the amount of sunlight cannot be increased by human efforts
capital ... cost is involved in using sunlight
land ... it is a natural resource endowed by nature
land ... the sunlight collected by human effort becomes a man-made resource used in the production process

questions.explanation: Sunlight is a natural resource, so it is land. It is not transformed by human effort before being sunlight; the equipment that collects it is capital.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem:
Refer to the following news article.

In order to attract more overseas talent to work in Hong Kong, the government launches the Top Talent Pass Scheme. Eligible people, including high-income earners and graduates of designated universities, are allowed to stay in Hong Kong for 24 months.

Which of the following would likely occur after the implementation of the scheme?

(1) Hong Kong's labour productivity will increase.
(2) The geographical mobility of graduates from designated universities will increase.
(3) The occupational mobility of Hong Kong workers will increase.
questions.explanation: Attracting well-qualified talent can raise average labour productivity and gives overseas graduates more ability to move geographically to work in Hong Kong. It does not change Hong Kong workers' ability or willingness to change occupation.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about a firm.

choices.text: Worker morale improves due to the reduction in working hours.
The firm uses more capital goods.
The firm does not provide adequate training for new workers.
The wage payment method is changed from time rate to piece rate.

questions.explanation: Average labour productivity falls from 600 / (15 x 8) = 5 to 675 / (20 x 7.5) = 4.5 units per man-hour. Inadequate training for the new workers can explain the fall; the other changes would tend to raise productivity.

visuals.caption: Firm output and labour input
rows: Number of working hours per worker per day

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following is a possible reason for the change in the average labour productivity of the firm?

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Total product, average product and marginal product
questions.stem: The table below shows the input-output relationship of a firm.
questions.explanation: Total product is 4, 10, 18, 28 and 30 as labour rises. Average product is 4, 5, 6, 7 and 6 respectively, so it is highest at four units of labour and total product is 28.
questions.postVisualStem: When the quantity of labour is _____ units, the average product of labour is the highest and the total product is ________ units.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm.
questions.explanation: At four units, marginal cost and market price are $8. Total revenue is $32, total variable cost is $20 and fixed cost is $8. Profit is $4 and producer surplus is $12.

visuals.caption: Cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the profit-maximising output level is 4 units and the average fixed cost at 4 units is $2. The profit and the producer surplus of the firm are ______ and ______ respectively.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: Mr. Cheung runs a leather product store selling homemade leather products. Which of the following will reduce its profit-maximising output?

choices.text: The cost of importing leather increases.
The rental of the store increases.
The wage rate of part-time workers decreases.

questions.explanation: A higher leather-import cost raises marginal cost and reduces the profit-maximising output. Rent is fixed cost, higher demand raises output, and a lower part-time wage reduces marginal cost.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: A conveyor belt sushi restaurant uses different colored plates to represent sushi of different prices. The diagram below shows their prices.
questions.explanation: White-plate sushi becomes more expensive, so less is demanded. Its relative price rises from 18/27 to 20/29, so less white-plate sushi is bought relative to black-plate sushi. The revenue effect is uncertain.

visuals.alt: White sushi plate priced at $18 and black sushi plate priced at $27.
visuals.caption: Relative prices of sushi plates

movements: A $2 rise raises both money prices.
White plates become more expensive relative to black plates.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Less white-plate sushi is sold and its ratio to black-plate sushi falls, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the conveyor belt sushi restaurant raises the prices of all dishes by $2. According to the law of demand,
which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?

(1) Less white-plate sushi will be sold.
(2) The ratio of white-plate sushi sold to black-plate sushi sold will decrease.
(3) The total revenue of the restaurant will increase.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely to increase the demand for second-hand cars?

choices.text: People expect the price of second-hand cars to fall.
The interest rate on vehicle loans falls.
Car manufacturers lower the price of new cars.
More second-hand cars are scrapped due to equipment failure.

questions.explanation: Lower vehicle-loan interest reduces the full cost of buying a second-hand car and raises demand. The other changes reduce demand or reduce supply rather than demand.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in supply
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in supply
questions.stem: Refer to the demand curve (D) for air services between Hong Kong and Japan.

choices.text: Japan cancels all the epidemic prevention measures restricting entry.
The number of foreign passengers travelling to Japan via connecting flights through Hong Kong decreases.
The price of fuel for aircraft falls.
A design flaw is found in a certain model of aircraft used in providing air services. Flights using that model have to be suspended.

questions.explanation: A to B is a movement down along an unchanged demand curve, requiring an increase in supply. A lower aircraft-fuel price lowers production cost and shifts supply right.

visuals.alt: Air-services demand curve with equilibrium moving from A to B.
visuals.caption: Air-services equilibrium movement

movements: A to B is a movement down along demand.
A lower aircraft-fuel price increases supply.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: A supply increase lowers price and raises quantity, making option C correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following reasons can best explain the change of the equilibrium position from A to B?

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is the demand-supply diagram of beef. The initial equilibrium point is E₀.
questions.explanation: Cheaper cattle feed increases beef supply. Cheaper plant-based meat lowers its price and reduces demand for substitute beef. The rightward supply shift and leftward demand shift meet at E4.

visuals.alt: Beef market demand and supply diagram with E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Beef market with two simultaneous changes

movements: Cheaper cattle feed shifts beef supply right.
Cheaper plant-based meat shifts demand for beef left.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The two shifts move equilibrium from E0 to E4, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the price of cattle feed falls. At the same time, the production cost of plant-based meat (food made from plant materials that tastes like meat) drops due to improved production technology. The new equilibrium point will be _____.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem: The demand for ___________ can be regarded as a derived demand for ____________.

choices.text: public healthcare services ... private healthcare services

questions.explanation: Hair stylists are factors of production, and their demand derives from demand for hairdressing services. Flour's demand is derived from bread, not the reverse; the other pairs are substitutes or complements.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Good X and good Y are in joint supply. When the price of good Y decreases, the equilibrium price of good X changes by 15%, while the quantity transacted decreases from 210 units to 190 units. Which of the following best explains the above change?

choices.text: Good X has many close substitutes.
There are many barriers for firms to enter the market of good X.
Firms producing good X have spare production capacity.
Good X is a habit-forming good.

questions.explanation: A lower price of jointly supplied Y decreases supply of X. Quantity falls by 10%, less than the 15% price change, showing inelastic demand for X. Habit-forming goods tend to have inelastic demand.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: During the peak season of influenza, the average waiting time for accident and emergency services increases. The government urges citizens with mild illnesses to seek treatment at private hospitals or clinics. As a result, the price of private medical services has changed by 5% and the quantity transacted has changed by 10%. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The demand for private medical services is elastic.
The demand for private medical services is inelastic.
The supply of private medical services is elastic.
The supply of private medical services is inelastic.

questions.explanation: The policy increases demand for private medical services, so both price and quantity rise. Quantity supplied rises by a larger percentage than price, showing elastic supply.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X.

choices.text: the quantity transacted will increase by 8 units.
consumers' total expenditure will decrease by $80.
there will be a surplus of 8 units of good X in the market.
the demand for good X's complements will decrease.

questions.explanation: Before intervention, 20 units are traded at $10, giving expenditure of $200. At the $6 ceiling, only 20 supplied units are traded and expenditure is $120. There is a shortage, and demand for complements rises.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: If the government imposes a price ceiling on good X at $6,

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X. Given that the supply curve of good X is upward sloping.
questions.explanation: The original quantity is 16; after demand rises it is 18. An effective 16-unit quota, a $10 floor, and a $6 unit tax each restore quantity to 16. A subsidy increases it further.

visuals.caption: Demand schedules before and after a demand increase

questions.postVisualStem:
After the demand for good X increases, the equilibrium price of good X increases from $4 to $8. Which of the following policy/policies can the government implement to restore the quantity transacted of good X to its original level?

(1) impose a quota of 16 units on good X
(2) impose a price floor on good X at $10
(3) impose a per-unit tax of $6 on good X
(4) provide a per-unit subsidy of $4 to the producers of good X

questions.keyPoint: Give examples of monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly
questions.stem: The figure below shows the sales data of different brands of smartphones in Country A in 2022.

choices.text: oligopoly ... different smartphone brands engaged in non-price competition
oligopoly ... several dominant sellers controlled the smartphone market in Country A
monopolistic competition ... smartphones produced by different brands were heterogeneous products
monopolistic competition ... the smartphone sellers were interdependent in their marketing strategies

questions.explanation: The sales data show several brands with large market shares and very little sold by other brands. Several dominant sellers are the defining feature of oligopoly.

visuals.alt: Bar chart showing smartphone sales by brand in Country A.
visuals.caption: Smartphone sales by brand

movements: Four brands account for nearly all sales.
Several large sellers dominate the market.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The data support oligopoly because several dominant sellers control the market, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, we can conclude that the market structure of smartphones in Country A in 2022 can be regarded as ______________ because ________________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on consumer surplus
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the demand and supply curves of good X.

choices.text: area (V + W + X) ... area (V + W + Y)

questions.explanation: Consumer surplus falls from V + W + X to V, a loss of W + X. Total social surplus falls from V + W + X + Y + Z to V + W + Y, a loss of X + Z.

visuals.alt: Demand and supply diagram with supply shifting left from S0 to S1 and areas V to Z.
visuals.caption: Surplus changes after a cost increase

movements: A production-cost increase shifts supply left.
Consumer surplus falls by W + X and total social surplus falls by X + Z.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option A states both changes correctly.

questions.postVisualStem: The production cost of good X increases and the supply curve of good X shifts from S₀ to S₁. The change in consumer surplus equals ___________ and the change in total social surplus equals ___________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X.
questions.explanation: The quota makes price $9. Consumer surplus is ($10 - $9) + ($9 - $9) = $1, and producer surplus is ($9 - $4) + ($9 - $5) = $9.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government sets a quota of 2 units on good X. After the imposition of the quota, the consumer surplus will be _________ while the producer surplus will be ______.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem:
A country imposes a per-unit tax on good X. When the demand for good X increases, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The producer surplus will increase.
(2) Total tax revenue will increase.
(3) The gap between marginal benefit and marginal cost will be widened.
questions.explanation: Higher demand raises quantity traded and the producer price net of the unchanged tax, increasing producer surplus and total tax revenue. The tax wedge between marginal benefit and marginal cost remains the same.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: The government issues a penalty ticket to a restaurant for poor sanitation, which has caused a rodent infestation that seriously affects nearby residents. If poor sanitary conditions continue, the restaurant will face a higher penalty. Which statement is CORRECT?

choices.text: The restaurant should give compensation to residents living nearby.
After the restaurant is fined, efficiency will be restored.
Fining the restaurant is the only way to improve efficiency.
Fining the restaurant increases the marginal private cost of the restaurant and improves efficiency.

questions.explanation: The fine makes poor sanitation more costly to the restaurant, internalising part of the external cost and improving efficiency. It need not restore efficiency exactly, and market solutions may also be possible.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the Gini coefficient of Country A.

choices.text: income for high-income households increased while income for low-income households decreased between 1981 and 2006.
the government cut the amount of transfer payments to the poor between 2016 and 2021.
Country A's tax system was likely to be progressive between 1981 and 2021.
High-income households paid the least amount of tax.

questions.explanation: The post-tax Gini coefficient is lower than the original-income Gini coefficient throughout, showing taxation reduces income inequality. That is consistent with a progressive tax system; the chart does not show absolute incomes, transfers, or tax payments.

visuals.alt: Line graph of original-income and post-tax Gini coefficients from 1981 to 2021.
visuals.caption: Gini coefficients before and after tax

movements: The post-tax Gini coefficient is lower in every year.
Taxation therefore reduces measured income inequality.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: This is consistent with a progressive tax system, so option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: From the diagram above, we can conclude that

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising opportunities
questions.stem:
Which of the following would help equalise opportunities?

(1) The government provides tablet computers to students from families with financial difficulties so they can participate in online classes.
(2) The government distributes consumption vouchers to all people aged 18 or above.
(3) The government provides an allowance to employers who employ people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: Tablets remove an education barrier faced by low-income students, while an employer allowance improves employment opportunities for people with disabilities. Equal vouchers do not give low-income people extra resources to improve future income-earning power.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Mr. Cheung is considering renting out his residential unit in a private housing estate. Which of the following would increase the cost of renting out the unit?

choices.text: The management fee borne by Mr. Cheung increases.
The average rent of residential units in the same housing estate increases.
The government raises the property tax rate.
The market price of residential units decreases.

questions.explanation: A higher property tax is an additional money cost of renting the unit. Management fee is paid either way, higher rent raises the benefit, and a lower sale price lowers the opportunity cost.

visuals.alt: Photograph of a private housing estate.
visuals.caption: Private housing estate

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of interest
questions.stem:
Suppose Kevin lent a new smartphone to his brother. His brother promised to return the smartphone along with a smartphone case to Kevin one month later. The smartphone case can be regarded as

(1) a free good to Kevin.
(2) the cost of using the smartphone to Kevin's brother.
(3) interest to Kevin.
(4) interest to Kevin's brother.
questions.explanation: The case is the brother's cost of earlier use and Kevin's compensation for deferring consumption, so it is interest to both. It is an economic, not free, good.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meaning of private property rights and its importance in a market economy
questions.stem:
Miss Lee runs a self-service bakery store. Customers can make cakes in the store and use the ingredients and baking equipment provided.

Miss Lee has the right to ____________ while customers have the right to ___________.

choices.text: sell the ingredients for income ... take away the ingredients to make cakes at home later
use the baking equipment to make cakes of different flavours ... sell the ingredients for income
transfer the store for income ... lease the baking equipment to others for income
hold a baking class in the store for income ... use the baking equipment in the store to make cakes for their friends

questions.explanation: The owner has exclusive rights to use, receive income from and transfer the equipment and ingredients. Customers only have the permitted right to use them in the store.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: The following table shows information about two firms in Hong Kong. Based on the information, which statement is CORRECT?

choices.text: Neither firm can issue shares or bonds to the public.
Both firms pay the same profits tax rate.
Firm A requires the consent of other shareholders to transfer ownership, while firm B does not.
Firm A has an independent legal status while firm B does not.

questions.explanation: Firm A is a public limited company because it discloses accounts and has continuity. Firm B is a partnership, so it lacks separate legal personality.

visuals.caption: Information about two firms
rows: If one owner goes bankrupt, the firm continues to exist.
If one owner goes bankrupt, the firm has to be dissolved.
Required to disclose to the public
Not required to disclose to the public

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: The fan club of a popular singer gives out free ice cream from trucks at designated times and locations, on a first-come-first-served basis while stocks last. This free ice cream is __________ because ___________.

choices.text: a free good ... the public do not need to pay for it
an economic good ... it can be used to produce other goods and services
a private good ... it is rival in consumption
a public good ... it is non-excludable in consumption

questions.explanation: Each ice cream eaten reduces what remains for others, so it is rival in consumption and a private good. Being free of charge does not make it a free good.

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem:
Mr. Lee owns a coffee shop. After hiring an employee to serve customers and operate the cash register, he specialises in making coffee. Which statements are CORRECT?

(1) Mr. Lee can save on production tools purchased for the shop.
(2) Mr. Lee can save the time spent on switching tasks.
(3) Mr. Lee's income includes profit and interest.
questions.explanation: Specialisation saves task-switching time, but the same production tools remain needed. As entrepreneur and capital owner, Mr. Lee receives profit and interest.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: Refer to the following information.

choices.text: Factory A adopts a time rate scheme while factory B adopts a piece rate scheme.
Factory B provides more training to workers.
Factory B's working environment is better.
Factory A uses more advanced capital goods.

questions.explanation: Factory A produces five units per man-hour while Factory B produces four. More advanced capital goods at Factory A can explain its higher productivity.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following is a possible reason for the difference between the average labour productivity of factory A and factory B?

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour

choices.text: more young people choose to continue their studies after graduating from university ... geographical mobility of labour
the government constructs a new railway ... occupational mobility of labour
the government cancels the annual quota of the Quality Migrant Admission Scheme ... average labour productivity
there is an increase in the number of public holidays ... supply of labour

questions.explanation: Removing the quota allows more qualified overseas workers to work in Hong Kong, raising average labour productivity. The other pairs do not describe the stated effect.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The table below shows the input-output relationship of a firm.
questions.explanation: The fourth marginal product is 42. The fifth must be below 42, so total product is below 198 and average product is below 39.6; only 39 is possible.
questions.postVisualStem: Diminishing marginal returns sets in when the 4th unit of labour is employed. The average product of 5 units of labour may be ________ units.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a price taker.
questions.explanation: Marginal cost is $14 at output three. Producer surplus is $11 and profit is $42 - $36 = $6. Rising marginal cost shows diminishing returns; fixed cost shows a short-run firm.
questions.postVisualStem:
If the market price of the good is $14, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) At the profit-maximising output level, the total producer surplus is $11.
(2) At the profit-maximising output level, the profit is $6.
(3) The law of diminishing marginal returns applies to the firm.
(4) The firm operates in the long run.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem:
Sushiro, a Japanese sushi restaurant chain, has opened an izakaya restaurant known as Sugidama in Hong Kong. This expansion

(1) extends its brand name to other markets.
(2) reduces competition.
(3) helps spread business risk.
questions.explanation: The related diversification extends the brand and spreads risk, but producing related rather than directly competing goods does not itself reduce competition.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Consumers' preferences for Japanese eggs are similar in Japan and Hong Kong. The table shows quantities of high-quality and average-quality Japanese eggs sold. If transport cost per type is the same, which figure(s) are inconsistent with the law of demand?
questions.explanation: Equal transport cost makes high-quality eggs relatively cheaper in Hong Kong, so its quantity ratio to average-quality eggs must exceed Japan's 1:2.2. Only (3) satisfies that.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, cost of production, technology, price expectations, weather, number of sellers in the market, etc. affect individual supply and market supply
questions.stem: Which would most likely lead to a reduction in the supply of hotel services in Hong Kong?

choices.text: The government distributes free air tickets for flights to Hong Kong to foreign tourists.
More applications for converting hotels into residential premises are approved.
The government provides more subsidies for training programmes in the hotel industry.
The average price of hotel services decreases.

questions.explanation: Converting hotels to residential premises reduces the number of hotel-service suppliers at every price. The other events either increase demand, lower production cost, or cause a movement along supply.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: A country imports high-quality and low-quality red wine. Which will cause consumers' expenditure on imported low-quality red wine to decrease?

choices.text: Transportation cost paid by consumers for each imported bottle decreases.
A ship carrying high-quality red wine sinks.
A ship carrying low-quality red wine sinks.
Low-quality red wine is inferior and people's income generally increases.

questions.explanation: For an inferior good, higher income reduces demand and expenditure. The other cases give an uncertain expenditure effect or raise demand for low-quality wine.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: Under the One-for-One Replacement scheme, eligible owners scrap and de-register an old private car and first register a new electric private car to receive a higher first-registration-tax concession. Which diagram represents the situation?
questions.explanation: The scheme encourages switching to electric cars. Demand for electric cars rises, while demand for internal-combustion cars falls; the visual's option C shows this.

visuals.alt: Four demand-supply diagrams for petrol and electric private cars.
visuals.caption: One-for-One Replacement scheme

labels: Private cars with an internal combustion engine
movements: The concession encourages switching to electric cars.
Demand for electric cars rises and demand for internal-combustion cars falls.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option C shows the demand increase for electric cars and is correct.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the tax burden
questions.stem:
After a per-unit tax on good X, total tax revenue is $300 and consumers' tax burden is $100. Which combinations of price elasticity may lead to this result?

(1) elastic demand; elastic supply
(2) elastic demand; inelastic supply
(3) inelastic demand; elastic supply
(4) inelastic demand; inelastic supply
questions.explanation: Consumers bear a smaller tax share, so demand must be more elastic than supply. That is possible in (1), (2) and (4), but not (3).

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: Refer to the demand-supply diagram for good X.
questions.explanation: At Q3 the quota is ineffective, so the market clears at P2 and Q2. There is no excess supply, and price does not rise to P3.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram for good X with quota limits Q1 and Q3.
visuals.caption: Increasing a quota limit

movements: At Q1 the quota is effective and price is P3.
At Q3 the quota is ineffective and the market clears at P2 and Q2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Only statement (2) is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
If the government increases the quota limit from Q₁ to Q₃,

(1) the market price of good X will increase to P₃.
(2) consumers’ total expenditure on good X will be (P₂ × Q₂).
(3) there will be an excess supply of good X.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram of good X. S0 and S1 are the supply curves before and after the government’s provision of a per-unit subsidy respectively.
questions.explanation: The subsidy shifts supply down by $2. Quantity rises from five to six, giving total subsidy $12. Revenue remains $30, so demand is unitary rather than inelastic.

visuals.alt: Demand curve and old and new supply curves for good X.
visuals.caption: Per-unit subsidy

movements: The subsidy shifts supply down by $2.
Price falls from $6 to $5 and quantity rises from five to six units.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The per-unit subsidy is $2 and total subsidy is $12, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the above situation are CORRECT?

(1) The government provides a per-unit subsidy of $2 to producers of good X.
(2) Within the range of the original and new prices, demand is inelastic.
(3) The total amount of subsidy is $12.

questions.keyPoint: Give examples of monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly
questions.stem: The market structure of wedding photography services in Hong Kong can be regarded as

choices.text: oligopoly because wedding photography companies can charge their own prices
oligopoly because wedding photography companies engage in non-price competition
monopolistic competition because companies are interdependent in pricing
monopolistic competition because photography companies provide different wedding photography services

questions.explanation: Differentiated services are a defining feature of monopolistic competition. Price-setting and non-price competition also occur in other imperfectly competitive markets.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on consumer surplus
questions.stem: The following table shows the marginal benefit schedule of a coffee consumer.
questions.explanation: At $17, consumer surplus is $6 over four units. At $18 it is $3 over three units, so consumer surplus falls by $3.
questions.postVisualStem: If the price of coffee increases from $17 to $18, the consumer surplus will __________.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem:
The government has an effective price ceiling on good X. The price of substitutes falls and the government raises the ceiling, which remains effective. In the market for good X,

(1) producer surplus will increase.
(2) quantity transacted will increase.
(3) deadweight loss will increase.
questions.explanation: The higher effective ceiling raises quantity transacted and producer surplus. The shortage distortion becomes smaller, so deadweight loss decreases rather than increases.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: Which is NOT an example of the divergence between private and social costs?

choices.text: Police block traffic lanes because of an accident caused by a drunk driver.
Fruit and vegetables grown by a house owner attract birds whose excrement dirties a neighbour's garden.
An audience member makes loud noises while watching a movie in a cinema.
A construction company pays a farmland owner for permission to dump construction waste on the farmland.

questions.explanation: Payment to the owner internalises the cost of dumping waste. In the other cases, third parties suffer external costs without compensation.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem:
Which proposals reduce the Gini coefficient based on post-tax post-social-transfer monthly household income in Hong Kong?

(1) increasing the charge on plastic shopping bags
(2) increasing marginal salaries-tax rates
(3) waiving rent for elderly people in public rental housing
questions.explanation: Higher marginal salaries tax narrows the income gap, and rent waiver targets generally low-income elderly people. A uniform bag charge takes a larger income share from poorer people.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: The following diagram shows a production chain of farm products in Country A.
questions.explanation: At factor cost, manufacturers' contribution is $4,000 + $2,000 - $50 - $200 + $800 = $6,550.

visuals.alt: Production chain of farm products in Country A.
visuals.caption: Farm-product production chain

movements: Manufacturers use inputs worth $2,000 and $50 and sell $7,000 of output.
Their $800 subsidy is included in GDP at factor cost.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Value added at factor cost is $6,550, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the above production chain has included a subsidy of $800 that is given to local farm product manufacturers. The contribution of local farm product manufacturers to Country A’s GDP at factor cost is __________.

questions.keyPoint: Growth rate of GDP
questions.stem: Consider the following statistical data about Country A.
questions.explanation: In 20X2, nominal GDP fell 2% while population fell 3%, so per-capita nominal GDP rose. Real GDP rose 1%, so the lower nominal GDP implies a lower price level.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about Country A is/are CORRECT?

(1) Per capita nominal GDP increased in 20X2.
(2) Real GDP in 20X2 remained unchanged.
(3) The general price level decreased in 20X2.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: Billy, a professor from South Korea, teaches a six-month Hong Kong university course. He receives a $100,000 salary, then returns to South Korea. The income from the course is $80,000. Organising the course leads to ___________ in Hong Kong's GDP and ___________ in Hong Kong's GNI.
questions.explanation: The resident university's $80,000 production raises GDP. Billy is a non-resident, so his $100,000 factor income is deducted in moving to GNI: net GNI change is -$20,000.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: Which measure may increase Hong Kong's aggregate output but at the same time worsen income inequality?

choices.text: reducing the standard rate of salaries tax
tightening eligibility for the Comprehensive Social Security Assistance Scheme
increasing health-care vouchers for eligible elderly people
distributing consumption vouchers to all residents

questions.explanation: A lower standard salaries-tax rate raises high-income earners' disposable income and consumption, lifting AD and output while widening the income gap.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem:
Free Lunch at Schools provides free lunch to primary students from low-income families. Which statements are CORRECT?

(1) The programme improves equity.
(2) It increases aggregate demand.
(3) Government spending on it is excluded from GDP.
(4) It leads to a fiscal deficit.
questions.explanation: The targeted transfer improves equity and raises government expenditure, hence AD. The lunch output is included in GDP, and more spending alone does not prove a fiscal deficit.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram.

choices.text: A large number of factories are temporarily closed because of a labour strike.
The central bank prints more money.
The stock market in the largest export market declines.
Transportation cost for raw materials decreases.

questions.explanation: More money raises AD, causing an inflationary gap. Higher input prices then reduce SRAS and return output to LRAS at a higher long-run price level A.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with long-run equilibrium moving from E to A.
visuals.caption: Long-run equilibrium movement

movements: More money shifts AD right and creates an inflationary gap.
Higher factor prices shift SRAS left until output returns to LRAS at A.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Only option B produces the illustrated new long-run equilibrium.

questions.postVisualStem: The initial equilibrium point of Country A is at E. If the new long run equilibrium point is at A, which of the following is a possible reason for the change in the equilibrium point?

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem:
Universities build additional teaching and research facilities. Which statements are CORRECT?

(1) During construction, unemployed population decreases.
(2) In the short run, aggregate output increases.
(3) In the long run, price level increases.
questions.explanation: Construction raises derived demand for labour and investment, reducing unemployment and raising short-run output. It expands productive capacity, so long-run price level falls rather than rises.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Inflationary gap
questions.stem: Initially an economy operates at long-run equilibrium. Which results in an inflationary output gap?

choices.text: Regulations on disposal of construction waste are tightened.
The quota for importing overseas labour increases.

questions.explanation: Currency depreciation raises net exports and AD, pushing short-run output above full-employment output. The other changes cause a deflationary gap or increase productive capacity.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem:
A magazine offers a one-year subscription for $240, reduced from $360. If a customer buys at the discounted price, which functions does money perform?

(1) medium of exchange
(2) unit of account
(3) store of value
(4) standard of deferred payment
questions.explanation: Money is used to exchange for the subscription and to state its price. The payment neither stores purchasing power nor settles a future debt.

questions.topicGroup: Licensed banks, restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies in
questions.keyPoint: Features of the three types of deposit-taking institutions
questions.stem:
Josie wins $100,000 and plans to place it as a three-month demand deposit. Which Hong Kong financial institutions can accept it?

(1) licensed banks
(2) restricted licence banks
(3) deposit-taking companies
questions.explanation: Only licensed banks may accept demand deposits. Restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies cannot accept them.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem: Which transaction decreases Hong Kong's M1 money supply?

choices.text: Mr. Cheng withdraws $5,000 from a licensed-bank current account and holds cash.
Ms. Chan deposits $5,000 cash into a licensed-bank savings account.
Mr. Chau transfers $5,000 from a licensed-bank time deposit to a current account.
Ms. Wong withdraws $5,000 from a deposit-taking-company time deposit and remits it overseas.

questions.explanation: Depositing cash into a savings account reduces notes and coins held by the public, while savings deposits are not M1. The other actions leave M1 unchanged or increase it.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual banking multipliers
questions.stem: The following table shows the balance sheet of the banking system of a country. The monetary base of the country is $700. The banks hold excess reserves of $100.
questions.explanation: Required reserve ratio is 20%. Deposits rise from $2,000 to $3,000 and money supply becomes $100 cash plus $3,000 deposits. Loans rise by $900, not $300.
questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the public deposit $100 cash into the banking system. If the banks lend out all of their excess reserves, which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?

(1) The deposits will increase by $1,000.
(2) The loans will increase by $300.
(3) The money supply will be $3,100.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money demand and money supply curves of an economy. The original equilibrium point is at E.
questions.explanation: Default risk raises asset demand for money, shifting money demand right. A higher required reserve ratio lowers money supply, shifting it left; their intersection is A.

visuals.alt: Money-demand and money-supply diagram labelled A to E.
visuals.caption: Money demand and supply

movements: Default risk raises asset demand for money.
A higher required reserve ratio lowers money supply.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The new equilibrium is point A, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the bonds issued in the economy are at risk of default, which weakens people’s confidence in holding the bonds. At the same time, the central bank raises the required reserve ratio. The new equilibrium point will be at __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: Which statement about the quantity theory of money is CORRECT?

choices.text: When real output rises, increasing money supply makes price level fall.
When real output grows faster than money supply, price level falls.
When price level rises, money supply rises by the same percentage.
With constant velocity, lower money supply increases real output.

questions.explanation: With MV = PY and constant velocity, money growing more slowly than real output implies a fall in the price level. The other assertions do not follow.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: In inflation, nominal interest on a fixed-interest bond exceeds expected inflation. If expected inflation exceeds actual inflation,

choices.text: real return on holding cash exceeds its nominal return
nominal return on holding cash is greater than zero
expected real interest rate is lower than actual real interest rate

questions.explanation: Expected real interest is nominal interest less expected inflation, while actual real interest uses actual inflation. A higher expected than actual rate makes expected real interest lower.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem:
Unemployment rate is 5%. Which would lower it?

(1) Graduates return from overseas to seek work and 3% fail to find a job.
(2) Long-term unemployed workers emigrate.
(3) Some retirees return to work.
questions.explanation: In each case the unemployed population rises less than the labour force, falls with the labour force, or stays unchanged while labour force rises. Each reduces the unemployment rate.

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: Which diagrams show a tax system that results in a more even income distribution?
questions.explanation: Diagrams (2), (3) and (4) are progressive tax systems, which narrow post-tax income differences. Diagram (1) is proportional.

visuals.alt: Four diagrams of tax payment or tax rate against taxable income.
visuals.caption: Tax systems and equity

movements: Diagrams (2), (3) and (4) represent progressive tax systems.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option C is correct.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Firms are pessimistic and decrease investment. The central bank sells government bonds in the open market. Which policy can stabilise output and interest rate together in the short run?

choices.text: Government issues more licences for electronic payment tools.

questions.explanation: The shocks lower output and raise interest rate. More electronic-payment licences reduce transaction money demand, lowering interest rate and raising consumption and investment to restore output.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: Before international trade, Country A and Country B each divides all their resources equally between production of good X and production of good Y. The output of the two countries is as follows:

choices.text: increase by 10 units ... increase by 10 units
increase by 10 units ... increase by 40 units
increase by 40 units ... decrease by 10 units
increase by 10 units ... decrease by 40 units

questions.explanation: Country B has comparative advantage in X and Country A in Y. Total output moves from 50 X and 120 Y to 60 X and 160 Y.
questions.postVisualStem: If both countries completely specialise their production and trade with each other, the total output of good X will _______ while the total output of good Y will _______.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: The diagram shows imposition of a tariff on good X in a small open economy.

choices.text: Import volume after the tariff is Q4 - Q1.
If tariff is reduced, domestic production will exceed Q2.
If world price falls, government tariff revenue will exceed (Q3 - Q2) x t.
If tariff rises, excess demand will be less than Q3 - Q2.

questions.explanation: A lower world price expands imports, so the unchanged per-unit tariff produces higher revenue. Imports after tariff are Q3 - Q2, and no excess demand exists in a small open economy.

visuals.alt: Tariff diagram for good X in a small open economy.
visuals.caption: Tariff in a small open economy

movements: A lower world price increases imports and tariff revenue with the per-unit tariff unchanged.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Only option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: P₀ is the world price of good X. Which of the following statements about good X is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: The following table shows some information about the balance of payments of Country A.

choices.text: Capital and financial account is in deficit.
Balance of payments is in deficit.

questions.explanation: Current-account surplus is $200 + $250 + $25 - $70 = $405 million. A current-account surplus is matched by a capital-and-financial-account deficit; positive net factor income makes GNI exceed GDP.

visuals.caption: Balance of payments of Country A

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above data, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: Exchange rate: 1 January 2022, HKD 1 = JPY 14.76; 1 January 2023, HKD 1 = JPY 16.79. Mr. Wong converts HKD 5,000 to yen on 1 January 2022, earns 1% annual interest, then converts back on 1 January 2023. He ______________.
questions.explanation: HKD 5,000 becomes JPY 73,800, then JPY 74,538 after interest. At the new rate this equals about HKD 4,439, a loss of about HKD 561.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Charlotte can study a bachelor's degree programme in Hong Kong or the UK. Which would increase her opportunity cost of studying in the UK?

(1) A Hong Kong university gives Charlotte an admission scholarship.
(2) The Hong Kong dollar depreciates against the British pound.
(3) University life in the UK is more boring than she expected.
questions.explanation: The scholarship raises the value of the highest-valued forgone option, and depreciation raises the Hong Kong-dollar cost of UK study. A less enjoyable chosen option changes benefit, not opportunity cost.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem: Mr. Chan says development of high-tech industries will increase Hong Kong's per capita GDP. Miss Lee says high-tech industry is the most important industry in Hong Kong. __________ statement is __________ because __________.

choices.text: Mr. Chan's ... normative ... value judgement is involved
Mr. Chan's ... positive ... it can be rejected by fact
Miss Lee's ... normative ... it is agreed on by some scholars
Miss Lee's ... positive ... it is consistent with facts

questions.explanation: Mr. Chan's claim can be tested against facts, so it is a positive statement. Miss Lee's claim contains a value judgement.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
Under the $2 Public Transport Fare Concession Scheme, people aged 60 or above travel at $2 per trip. Politicians suggest increasing the fare to $3. Which statements are CORRECT?

(1) The suggestion will not affect their opportunity cost of taking public transport.
(2) It concerns the 'for whom to produce' problem.
(3) It uses government command to solve the basic economic problem.
questions.explanation: A higher fare increases money cost, so (1) is false. The concession determines access to public transport and is set by government command, making (2) and (3) correct.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Firm A has 30 owners and unlimited liability. Firm B has 50 owners and limited liability. Which statement is CORRECT?

choices.text: Firm A need not disclose financial information while Firm B does.
If an owner goes bankrupt, Firm A must dissolve while Firm B continues.
Firm B has a higher takeover risk than Firm A.
Neither firm can issue shares to the public.

questions.explanation: Firm A is a partnership and lacks continuity. Firm B is a limited company and continues to exist if an owner goes bankrupt.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Which statement about public goods is CORRECT?

choices.text: Books in public libraries are public goods.
Public goods are goods provided by government.
Cost of producing an additional unit of a public good is zero.
Additional cost of serving an extra consumer to use a public good is zero.

questions.explanation: Public goods are non-rival: once provided, serving an extra consumer costs zero. A library book is rival, public goods need not be government-provided, and production cost need not be zero.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital
questions.stem: The following photo shows a carpark in Hong Kong.
questions.explanation: The barrier and lighting are man-made resources used in producing car-park services. Parked cars are not production inputs.

visuals.alt: Photograph of a car park with a gate barrier and lighting facilities.
visuals.caption: Car park

questions.postVisualStem:
Which items in the diagram are the capital of the carpark?

(1) the gate barrier in the carpark
(2) lighting facilities in the carpark
(3) cars parked in the carpark

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: Both labour supply and average labour productivity decreased. Which best explains this?

choices.text: More enterprises adopted artificial intelligence to replace workers.
More residents moved to work in neighbouring areas.
Degree of division of labour decreased.

questions.explanation: Retirement of experienced workers lowers labour supply and average labour productivity. The other changes do not necessarily reduce both.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The table below shows the production plan of a firm. It employs two factors of production only, namely labour and machines.
questions.explanation: Marginal product of the eighth worker must be below 27, so total product is below 132 and average product X is below 16.5.
questions.postVisualStem: If the above data illustrates the law of diminishing marginal returns, the value of X ________.

questions.keyPoint: External economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: In Country A, as more online food-delivery platforms launch, average salary of couriers increases. The platforms
questions.explanation: Industry expansion increases competition for couriers and raises input cost for all platforms. This is an external diseconomy of scale.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm.
questions.explanation: Original profit maximisation is at 9 units where MC is $21. New MC reaches the $19 price at 7 units, and new profit is $19 x 7 - $91 = $42.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the average cost for each unit of output increases by $2 and the market price decreases from $21 to $19. The profit-maximising output of the firm will ________ while the profit will __________.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem:
Sega Sammy Holdings proposes acquiring Rovio Entertainment. Which are likely motives?

(1) enjoy economies of scale
(2) reduce competition
(3) ensure higher profit
(4) increase market share
questions.explanation: The horizontal acquisition can bring economies of scale, reduce competitors and increase market share. It cannot guarantee higher profit.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Refer to the following figure.

choices.text: Compared with B, C imports a greater proportion of high-quality apples from A.
Average quality of apples sold in C is lower than in B.
When transport cost falls, total expenditure on imported apples in B and C will decrease.
When transport cost rises, both B and C import fewer apples.

questions.explanation: The same per-unit transport cost lowers the relative price of high-quality apples more for farther Country C, so C imports a higher proportion of high-quality apples. Option B contradicts this.

visuals.alt: Map diagram with Country A, B and C and distances of 30 km and 120 km.
visuals.caption: Apple export distance

movements: Country C is farther from Country A than Country B.
A fixed per-unit-per-kilometre transport cost changes relative prices.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Country C has a higher proportion of high-quality apples, so option B is inconsistent with the law of demand.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose Country A exports apples to Country B and Country C. The cost of transporting 1 unit of apples per kilometre is fixed. Which of the following is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem:
When price of beef rises, __________ will increase. Assume supply and demand curves of plant-based meat and leather shift in parallel.

(1) consumers' spending on plant-based meat
(2) producer surplus in plant-based meat
(3) consumer surplus in leather
(4) total revenue of leather producers
questions.explanation: Plant-based meat is a substitute, so its demand, spending and producer surplus increase. Leather is jointly supplied with beef, so higher beef price raises leather supply and consumer surplus. Leather revenue is uncertain.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in demand
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in demand
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the supply curve (S) of electric vehicles.

choices.text: More traditional automakers enter the electric-vehicle market.
Studies suggest electric vehicles perform poorly in cold environments.
Government offers tax exemptions to electric-vehicle buyers.

questions.explanation: Poor performance news lowers demand, moving equilibrium down along the unchanged supply curve from A to B.

visuals.alt: Electric-vehicle market with equilibrium changing from A to B along supply curve S.
visuals.caption: Electric-vehicle demand reduction

movements: Poor cold-environment performance reduces demand.
Equilibrium moves down along unchanged supply from A to B.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following reasons best explains the change in equilibrium position from A to B?

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Demand for good X is a downward-sloping straight line. When price rises from $40 to $50, quantity demanded falls from 25 to 20. When price rises further from $50 to $60, producers' total revenue ___________.

choices.text: may increase, decrease or remain unchanged

questions.explanation: Revenue is $1,000 at both $40 and $50, so the $50 point is unit elastic. At higher prices on a linear demand curve demand is elastic, therefore a further price rise reduces total revenue.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the subsidy
questions.stem:
Government provides a per-unit subsidy of $6 to producers of good X. Its price may __________ if elasticity of demand is __________ elasticity of supply.

(1) decrease by $2 ... higher than
(2) decrease by $4 ... higher than
(3) decrease by $4 ... lower than
(4) decrease by $3 ... equal to
questions.explanation: The less elastic side receives the larger subsidy share. Statements (1), (3) and (4) match the possible consumer and producer shares of a $6 subsidy.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the supply and demand curves of good X. The government imposes a price ceiling on good X at PC.
questions.explanation: After demand falls to D1, quantity demanded equals the fixed quantity supplied at the price ceiling, so excess demand disappears.

visuals.alt: Price-ceiling diagram with demand falling from D0 to D1.
visuals.caption: Demand fall under a price ceiling

movements: Demand shifts left from D0 to D1.
At Pc, D1 intersects supply at Q0.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Excess demand disappears, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the demand for good X decreases from D0 to D1. Which of the following statements about the market for good X is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply schedule of good X.

choices.text: A $10 price floor decreases quantity transacted by 10 units.
A quota of 25 units increases consumer expenditure by $70.
A $2 unit tax raises market price by $2.
A $2 unit subsidy raises total revenue including subsidy to $520.

questions.explanation: Initial equilibrium is $12 and 35 units. With a $2 subsidy, consumers pay $11 and buy 40 units while producers receive $13, so total revenue including subsidy is $13 x 40 = $520.

visuals.caption: Demand and supply schedule for good X

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the market of good X is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Give examples of monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly
questions.stem: Which statement about a perfectly competitive market is CORRECT?

choices.text: Different sellers sell similar but distinguishable products.
Sellers have perfect information while buyers do not.
A firm's marginal revenue equals market price.

questions.explanation: A price-taking firm faces the market price as its marginal revenue. Products are homogeneous, both buyers and sellers have perfect information, and market price can change.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in supply
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in supply
questions.stem: An increase in the supply of wool

choices.text: raises marginal benefit of the last unit of wool
can be caused by a rise in wool price
can be caused by a rise in demand for lamb

questions.explanation: Lamb and wool are jointly supplied, so stronger demand for lamb can raise supply of wool. A wool-price rise changes quantity supplied, not supply; efficiency and marginal benefit do not necessarily change.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the supply and demand curves of good X.
questions.explanation: At the ceiling, the quantity transacted is determined by the lower supply S1. At that quantity marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost, and deadweight loss is area abc.

visuals.alt: Supply-demand diagram with price ceiling P1 and supply shifting from S0 to S1.
visuals.caption: Price ceiling after supply fall

movements: Supply shifts left from S0 to S1.
Quantity transacted falls to the supply on S1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost and deadweight loss is abc, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose a price ceiling is set at P1. When the supply of good X decreases from S0 to S1, the marginal benefit will be ________ the marginal cost and the deadweight loss will be _________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: Jason plays piano at home. His neighbour Kelly enjoys it and wants more performances. Which statement is CORRECT?

choices.text: If Kelly pays Jason to play longer, economic efficiency can improve.
Jason has to compensate Kelly to reduce divergence between private and social costs.
If Kelly pays Jason, there will be no divergence between private and social benefits.
Government should ask Kelly to compensate Jason to achieve efficiency.

questions.explanation: Jason's playing generates an external benefit for Kelly. A voluntary payment can internalise part of the benefit and improve efficiency; it need not eliminate the divergence completely.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: The table below shows the Gini coefficient of Country A.

choices.text: Government reduced transfers to low-income groups.
Government tightened eligibility for subsidised housing.
Government raised progressivity of salaries tax.

questions.explanation: Greater progressivity makes high-income earners pay relatively more tax, narrowing post-tax income inequality and reducing the Gini coefficient.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following best explains the change in Country A from 2021 to 2022?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem:
Government distributes equal-value consumption vouchers to all residents aged 18 or above. Which statements are CORRECT?

(1) It reduces income inequality.
(2) It equalises opportunity.
(3) Aggregate output rises in the short run.
questions.explanation: The same transfer is a larger percentage of lower income and narrows income inequality. It raises consumption and short-run AD. It does not equalise opportunities merely by giving everyone the same voucher.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: The following diagram shows a production chain of automobiles in Country A.
questions.explanation: GDP at factor cost equals the local value added: X + $520 - $100 - $230 - $140 + $50 = $800. Therefore X is $170.

visuals.alt: Automobile production chain showing imported materials, local producers, manufacturers, retailers and exporters.
visuals.caption: Automobile production chain

labels: Raw materials imported from Country B
movements: Local manufacturers receive a $50 subsidy.
Only local value added contributes to GDP.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Solving the factor-cost GDP contribution gives X = $170, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the above production chain has included a subsidy of $50 that is given to the local manufacturers. If the contribution of the above production chain to Country A’s GDP at factor cost is $800, the value of X is ________.

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of nominal GDP and real GDP
questions.stem: Suppose a closed economy produces good X and good Y only. The output of 2021 and 2022 are as follows:
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP rises from $1,950 to $2,040. At either year's prices, the 2022 quantities have greater value, and the higher nominal-to-real GDP ratio means the GDP deflator rises.

visuals.caption: Output of goods X and Y

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the economy are CORRECT?

(1) Nominal GDP in 2022 is higher than that in 2021.
(2) Real GDP in 2022 is higher than that in 2021.
(3) The GDP deflator in 2022 is higher than that in 2021.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem:
An economy has GNI at market prices $475m, GDP at factor cost $515m, GDP at market prices $500m and GDP deflator 95. Which statements are CORRECT?

(1) Net factor income from abroad is positive.
(2) Subsidies exceed indirect taxes.
(3) Real GDP exceeds nominal GDP.
questions.explanation: Net factor income is GNI minus GDP, so it is negative. GDP at factor cost exceeds GDP at market prices, so subsidies exceed indirect taxes. A deflator below 100 means real GDP exceeds nominal GDP.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Many factories close because of a mass labour strike. Which will offset its effect on the economy's price level in the short run?

choices.text: Producers expect price level to increase.

questions.explanation: A strike lowers SRAS and raises price level. More desired saving lowers consumption and AD, putting downward pressure on price and offsetting the effect.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram.

choices.text: price level will be higher than P0
output will be higher than Y0
AD will shift left to attain equilibrium
LRAS will shift right to attain equilibrium

questions.explanation: Recovery abroad raises net exports and AD. The economy moves from a deflationary gap toward full employment; the new long-run price level is above the initial P0, while output returns to Y0.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with initial output Y1 below LRAS output Y0.
visuals.caption: Trading partners' recovery

movements: Initial economy is in a deflationary gap.
Trading-partner recovery raises AD and moves output toward full employment.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The new long-run price level is above P0, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: The initial output level of the economy is at Y1. Suppose the economy’s trading partners experience economic recovery. In the long run,

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem:
Hyperinflation occurs in Country A. People use Country B's stable currency for transactions. Which statements are CORRECT?

(1) Country A currency's store-of-value function weakens.
(2) Country B currency is money in Country A.
(3) Country B currency serves as medium of exchange.
questions.explanation: Hyperinflation weakens Country A currency as a store of value. Country B currency is generally accepted for transactions in A, so it functions as money and medium of exchange.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem:
Titus withdraws HK$800,000 from a time deposit with a deposit-taking company. He holds $200,000 in a safe deposit box, puts $500,000 in a restricted-licence bank and remits the rest overseas. What are the immediate effects?

(1) M1 increases by $200,000.
(2) M2 decreases by $600,000.
(3) M3 decreases by $100,000.
questions.explanation: Cash held by the public raises M1 by $200,000. The restricted-licence-bank deposit remains M3, while remitting $100,000 overseas lowers M3 by that amount; M2 does not fall by $600,000.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The following table shows the balance sheet of the banking system of a country. All banks do not hold excess reserves and the public hold $200 million cash.

choices.text: If public withdraw $100m as cash, maximum loans fall $400m.
If required reserve ratio rises to 30%, maximum deposits are $1,500m.
If required reserve ratio rises to 30%, reserves are $540m.

questions.explanation: The existing required reserve ratio is 25%. With $450m reserves and a 30% requirement, maximum deposits are $1,500m. Money supply includes public cash, and the other figures are incorrect.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the above banking system is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: People's confidence in electronic wallets weakens because of potential security risks. Which diagram best illustrates the money-market effect?
questions.explanation: Electronic wallets are used for transactions, so weaker confidence increases transaction demand for money. The correct visual is diagram B with Mt shifting right.

visuals.alt: Four money-market diagrams showing shifts in transaction or asset demand for money.
visuals.caption: Electronic-wallet confidence

movements: Weaker confidence in electronic wallets raises transaction demand for money.
