diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option B shows transaction demand shifting right and is correct.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: A bond's nominal interest rate is 5% and expected inflation is 3%. Which statement is CORRECT?

choices.text: If actual inflation is -1%, issuer gains.
If actual inflation is 4%, bondholders lose.
Expected real interest exceeds nominal interest.

questions.explanation: Expected real interest is 2%. If actual inflation is 4%, actual real return is 1%, below the expected return, so bondholders lose.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: Which statement about the classical quantity theory of money is CORRECT?

choices.text: A price-level rise causes money supply to rise by the same percentage.
If money-supply growth is constant, inflation rate is zero.
If money supply grows at a constant rate, real output grows at the same rate.
If money supply grows at a constant rate, nominal output grows at the same rate.

questions.explanation: With stable velocity, the quantity equation implies nominal output grows at the same rate as money supply. The other causal or growth-rate claims do not follow.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: Refer to the following unemployment data of Country A.

choices.text: More employed people went overseas to work under the Working Holiday Scheme.
Some unemployed workers gave up seeking jobs.
Government provided transport subsidy to employed people.

questions.explanation: The data show unemployed population rising while unemployment rate falls. A transport subsidy raises job-search incentive and labour force; unemployed population may rise by a smaller percentage, so the rate falls.

visuals.alt: Unemployment data for Country A from 2020 to 2022.
visuals.caption: Unemployment data

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following best explains the change in the unemployment data of Country A from 2020 to 2022?

questions.keyPoint: Taxation in
questions.stem: Anson lives and works in Hong Kong. His 2022 incomes are commission as salesperson, rental income from a car-park space, interest on licensed-bank time deposits and dividends from a listed Hong Kong company. Which are subject to taxation?
questions.explanation: Commission from employment is subject to salaries tax and rental income from property is subject to property tax. Interest on licensed-bank deposits and dividends are exempt from Hong Kong tax.

questions.keyPoint: Taxation in
questions.stem: Which policy will broaden Hong Kong's tax base?
questions.explanation: A general sales tax applies to a broad range of transactions and therefore broadens the tax base. Raising tax rates or progressivity changes burden, while abolition narrows the base.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem:
An economy plans to implement the following two policies:

Policy 1: to purchase government bonds from the public through the central bank
Policy 2: to increase spending on infrastructure construction

Which of the following AD-AS diagrams best illustrates the impact of the two policies above?
questions.explanation: Bond purchases raise money supply and shift AD right. Infrastructure spending shifts AD right in the short run and increases productive capacity, shifting LRAS right in the long run. Diagram C shows both.

visuals.alt: Four AS-AD diagrams for bond purchases and infrastructure investment.
visuals.caption: Expansionary monetary and infrastructure policies

movements: Bond purchases shift AD right.
Infrastructure investment shifts AD right and LRAS right.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Diagram C is correct.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: A country has a deflationary output gap. Which policy narrows both the deflationary gap and income gap?
questions.explanation: Higher transfer payments raise low-income households' disposable income, reduce income inequality and increase AD, narrowing the deflationary gap.

questions.keyPoint: Four basic principles of taxation
questions.stem: Budget proposal raises cigarette duty by 60 cents per stick to encourage smokers to cut down or quit. This is LEAST in line with which Adam Smith taxation principle?
questions.explanation: The duty is regressive because it takes a larger share of income from lower-income smokers, so it is least consistent with equity. The tax can still be convenient, economical and certain.

questions.keyPoint: Explain which country has a comparative advantage in the production of a good in a given case
questions.stem: The following table shows the output per unit of resources in Country A and Country B.
questions.explanation: A has absolute advantage and lower opportunity cost of apples (1.5 bread versus 1.8). A terms of trade of 1.6 bread lies between costs, and 20 apples cost A 30 bread but obtain 35, a gain of five.
questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose there is no transportation cost. According to the above table, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) Country A has both absolute advantage and comparative advantage in producing apples.
(2) A mutually beneficial terms of trade can be 1 unit of apples = 1.6 units of bread.
(3) If Country A exports 20 units of apples to Country B in exchange for 35 units of bread, Country A’s total gain from trade is 5 units of bread.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of a quota on domestic price, domestic consumption, domestic production and import quantity for a small open economy
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the market of good X in a small open economy. The economy imposes an import quota on good X.
questions.explanation: The economy is small so world price is unchanged. With a fixed quota, import volume remains unchanged; higher domestic price increases local production and clears the market.

visuals.alt: Small-open-economy diagram with a binding import quota.
visuals.caption: Demand rise under an import quota

movements: A demand rise raises domestic price under a binding quota.
Domestic supply increases while imports stay fixed.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Statements (2) and (3) are correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
If the demand for good X increases, which of the following are CORRECT?

(1) The world price of good X will increase.
(2) The domestic production of good X will increase.
(3) The import volume of good X will remain unchanged.
(4) There will be an excess demand for good X.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem:
The following diagram shows the change in the exchange rate between the British pound (GBP) and the Hong Kong Dollar (HKD).
(Source: Census and Statistics Department, HKSAR Government)

choices.text: fewer British tourists visiting Hong Kong
lower value of British exports to Hong Kong in GBP
lower value of Hong Kong exports to Britain in GBP

questions.explanation: HKD depreciates against GBP, raising British-goods prices in HKD. Demand for British exports to Hong Kong and their value in GBP fall; Hong Kong export value in GBP is uncertain.

visuals.alt: GBP-HKD exchange-rate chart from October to December 2022.
visuals.caption: GBP-HKD exchange rate

questions.postVisualStem: During the period of October to December 2022, the change in the exchange rate between GBP and HKD would lead to _____________.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: Study the following information about Country A.

choices.text: Value of garments imported from other countries increased.
Manufacturers replaced foreign imported raw materials with local raw materials.
More overseas residents bought life insurance from Country A insurance companies.
Residents of Country A spent more on visits to other countries.

questions.explanation: Higher garment imports increase imports of goods, explaining the deterioration in the visible trade balance shown in the source data.

visuals.alt: Information chart about Country A's changes from 2021 to 2022.
visuals.caption: Country A changes

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following best explains the above changes in the economy from 2021 to 2022?

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Carmen is a nursing graduate. After working as a full-time nurse in a public hospital for a year, she decides to quit her job and switch to teaching piano full-time. Which would be the LEAST important factor in deciding to change her occupation?

choices.text: Carmen spent a lot of time and money studying nursing.
The working hours for teaching piano full-time are shorter.
Working as a nurse in a public hospital has more opportunities for promotion.
Carmen earns a lot more income from teaching piano.

questions.explanation: The time and money spent studying nursing are sunk costs and cannot be recovered. The other options affect the current benefits or opportunity costs of changing occupation.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Miss Cheung is considering taking a bus or the MTR to Tsim Sha Tsui. If there is traffic congestion along the road the bus takes, her opportunity cost of taking a bus will __________ because __________.

choices.text: remain unchanged ... there is no change in the bus fare
remain unchanged ... the value of taking the MTR does not change
increase ... the bus journey will be lengthened due to traffic congestion
increase ... Miss Cheung will be dissatisfied with traffic congestion

questions.explanation: The full cost of taking the bus includes time cost. Traffic congestion lengthens the journey and therefore raises this cost.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
If a command economy turns into a market economy, which statement(s) is/are correct?

(1) people will become wealthier
(2) a greater proportion of resources will be privately owned
(3) the quantity of public goods will decrease
questions.explanation: A market economy has a greater proportion of private ownership. It does not necessarily make people wealthier or reduce the quantity of public goods.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
Mr. Wong is a small investor. He prefers debentures to shares. Which are possible reasons?

(1) If the company winds up, he can claim repayment prior to shareholders.
(2) The return of debentures is higher.
(3) He can still receive interest even if the company does not make a profit.
(4) He has voting rights in the company's decision-making.
questions.explanation: Debenture holders rank ahead of shareholders on winding up and receive fixed interest. Shares may earn a higher return, and debenture holders have no voting rights.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Which is a possible reason for turning a firm from a private limited company into a public limited company?

choices.text: Ownership and management of the firm can be separated.
The firm can become a legal entity.
The firm's accounting information can be kept confidential.
The firm will have wider sources of capital.

questions.explanation: A public limited company can issue shares or bonds to the public and therefore has wider sources of capital. Both company forms are legal entities and may separate ownership from management.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: The following shows the holiday decorations of a shopping mall in Hong Kong.
questions.explanation: The decorations help produce photo opportunities, so they are producer goods. Their use is non-rival and non-excludable in this setting, making them public goods; they remain economic rather than free goods.

visuals.alt: Holiday decorations at a Hong Kong shopping mall.
visuals.caption: Shopping mall holiday decorations

questions.postVisualStem:
Many people like to take photos in front of the decorations. To the shopping mall, the decorations are _________.

(1) producer goods
(2) consumer goods
(3) free goods
(4) public goods

questions.keyPoint: Types of division of labour
questions.stem:
A tutorial school changes its arrangements: instead of one tutor teaching several grade levels, each tutor teaches one grade level. Which would likely occur?

(1) The school can choose the most suitable tutor for each grade level.
(2) Tutors spend less time preparing lessons.
(3) The services become more standardised.
questions.explanation: Specialising tutors by grade lets the school match skills better, reduces repeated preparation, and makes services more standardised.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment

choices.text: The working environment of firm A is worse than that of firm B.
Firm A practices a lower degree of division of labour than firm B.
Firm A uses more producer goods than firm B.
Firm A uses time rate while firm B uses piece rate.

questions.explanation: Firm A has lower productivity but a higher proportion of output meeting the quality standard. Time-rate pay can favour quality over output volume, while piece-rate pay can encourage output at the expense of quality.

visuals.caption: Firm A and Firm B output data
rows: Number of working hours per worker per day
Percentage of output with quality up to standard

questions.postVisualStem: With reference to the above table, which of the following can best explain the difference in quality of the outputs between firm A and firm B?

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Which would raise both the occupational mobility of labour and average labour productivity of an economy?

choices.text: The government provides more vocational training courses.
The government increases the quota of its skilled immigration scheme.
The government sets up a website with information on job vacancies.
More professional groups tighten their licensing requirements.

questions.explanation: Vocational training raises workers' skills and their ability and willingness to change occupation. The other changes affect at most one of the two outcomes.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem:
Some insurance companies pay their agents a basic salary plus commission. From the agents' viewpoint, which is/are advantage(s) compared with commission only?

(1) Income is more stable.
(2) Monitoring the quality of their service costs less.
(3) Agents can increase income by improving performance.
questions.explanation: A basic salary stabilises agents' income. Lower monitoring cost benefits the firm, and agents can improve income under both pay arrangements.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The following table shows the production plan of a firm. The firm employs two inputs only, namely machinery and labour.
questions.explanation: With Q1 = 43 and Q2 = 60, marginal product rises from 13 to 15 to 17, so diminishing marginal returns is not illustrated.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the above data illustrates the law of diminishing marginal returns. Which of the following figures is NOT consistent with the law?

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of integration
questions.stem: A fitness-center group opens several branches and spends heavily promoting them, but few new members are attracted. The group may __________.
questions.explanation: The expansion may raise average cost: additional marketing expense is not covered by enough extra members. This is an internal diseconomy of scale.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: Mr. Cheung runs a second-hand handbag shop. Which would increase its profit-maximising output?

choices.text: The monthly rental payment of the store decreases.
Demand for second-hand designer handbags increases.
The wage rate of workers repairing designer handbags increases.
Acquiring second-hand designer handbags becomes more difficult.

questions.explanation: Higher demand raises market price and marginal revenue, increasing the profit-maximising output. Rent is fixed cost, while the other two changes raise marginal cost.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a price taker. The fixed cost of the firm is $2.

choices.text: the profit-maximising output will increase from 3 units to 5 units.
the maximum profit of the firm will be $6.
the minimum total cost of the firm will be $30.

questions.explanation: After the cost fall, marginal cost is $12 at output 3. Total revenue is $36 and total cost is $30, so maximum profit is $6.
questions.postVisualStem: If the average cost per unit of output falls by $2 and the market price is $12,

questions.keyPoint: Concepts of supply
questions.stem:
Which is/are assumed to be constant when constructing the market supply curve for chicken legs?

(1) market price of chicken wings
(2) market price of chicken legs
(3) per-unit government subsidy
questions.explanation: A market supply curve shows how quantity supplied changes with the good's own price, holding all other supply determinants constant, including the price of jointly supplied chicken wings and subsidies.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem:
McDonald's Hong Kong raises the prices of all products by $1. Which statements are correct?

(1) Total revenue from restaurant services will increase.
(2) Consumer surplus from its restaurant services will decrease.
(3) The proportion of higher-priced meals sold to lower-priced meals sold will increase.
questions.explanation: The price rise lowers quantity transacted and consumer surplus. Adding the same amount lowers the higher-priced meals' relative price, so they are bought in a greater proportion; total-revenue change is uncertain.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: When good X and good Y are in ______________, an increase in the price of good X will lead to a decrease in the ________________.

choices.text: joint supply ... quantity transacted of good Y
competitive supply ... total revenue from sale of good Y
joint demand ... producer surplus in the market of good Y
competitive demand ... producer surplus in the market of good Y

questions.explanation: Jointly demanded goods are complements. A price increase for X lowers demand, price and quantity for Y, thereby reducing Y producers' surplus.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem: Which situation is most likely to increase the supply of construction workers?

choices.text: There are more job opportunities in other industries.
The average wage rate for construction workers increases.
The government announces construction of more public housing.
The government abolishes restrictions on importing foreign workers.

questions.explanation: Removing restrictions lets more foreign workers enter the labour market, shifting the supply of construction workers right. A wage change moves along the supply curve; public-housing construction changes labour demand.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is a demand-supply diagram for cruise services. The original equilibrium point is E0.
questions.explanation: Higher income shifts demand right from D0 to D1 and higher maintenance cost shifts supply left from S0 to S2. Their intersection is E1.

visuals.alt: Cruise-services demand-supply diagram with D0, D1, D2, S0, S1, S2 and equilibria E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Cruise-services market

movements: Higher income shifts demand right from D0 to D1.
Higher maintenance cost shifts supply left from S0 to S2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The two shifts meet at E1, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose cruise services are normal goods. If people’s income increases and the maintenance cost of cruise ships increases sharply, the new equilibrium point will be _________.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: The table below shows the total expenditure of Miss Wong and Mr. Li on bread.

choices.text: 0 ... greater than 1 and smaller than infinity

questions.explanation: Miss Wong always buys four units, so demand is perfectly inelastic. Mr. Li's total expenditure falls as price rises, so demand is elastic.
questions.postVisualStem: Miss Wong’s elasticity of demand for bread is ____________ while Mr. Li’s elasticity of demand for bread is ____________ (without regard to the negative sign).

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: Demand for good X is derived demand for good Y. When demand for Y decreases, equilibrium price of X falls from $10 to $8 and quantity transacted changes by 30%. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: The derived demand for X falls, so price and quantity both fall. The 30% quantity change exceeds the 22.22% price change, showing elastic supply.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: The following shows the demand-supply diagram for good X.
questions.explanation: At Q2 the quota is ineffective: equilibrium quantity is Q3 and price is P3, so the market clears and marginal benefit falls. Statement (1) uses the wrong price and quantity after the change.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram with quota limits Q1 and Q2, prices P1 and P2, supply lines S1 and S2 and demand curve D.
visuals.caption: Quota limit increased

movements: At Q1 the quota is effective.
At Q2 the quota is ineffective and the market clears at the demand-supply intersection.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Statements (2) and (3) are correct, so option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
If the government increases the quota limit from Q1 to Q2, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The consumers’ total expenditure on good X will change from (P1 × Q1) to (P2 × Q2).
(2) The market of good X will be in equilibrium.
(3) The marginal benefit of the last unit of good X will decrease.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the tax burden
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply schedule for good X.
questions.explanation: After tax, 20 units are transacted, so tax revenue is $80. Consumer and producer tax burdens are both $2 per unit, which means the two elasticities are equal.
questions.postVisualStem: If the government imposes a $4 per-unit tax on the producers of good X, the total tax revenue received by the government will be _________ and the price elasticity of demand will be _________ the price elasticity of supply.

questions.keyPoint: Give examples of monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly
questions.stem: The figure below shows market shares in the magazine industry in an economy in 2023.

choices.text: monopolistic competition … different magazine publishers engage in non-price competition
monopolistic competition … there are many magazine consumers in the market
oligopoly … different magazine publishers publish magazines of different styles
oligopoly … the magazine market is dominated by a few major sellers

questions.explanation: The chart shows three major publishers account for almost all sales. Dominance by a few sellers identifies oligopoly.

visuals.alt: Magazine market-share chart: Beauty News 46.0%, Kids Monthly 31.8%, Fashion Press 20.0% and Others 2.2%.
visuals.caption: Magazine-market shares in 2023

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the information in the figure above, we can conclude that the market structure of the magazine industry in the economy in 2023 can be regarded as _________ because _________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Rationing function
questions.stem: At the Hong Kong Brands and Products Expo, exhibitors offer discounts and promotions to attract shoppers. This illustrates the ________ function of price because __________.

choices.text: rationing ... more buyers are willing to buy the products
rationing ... products are sold to the highest-valued buyers
allocative ... the arrangement guarantees products sell out
allocative ... buyers are allocated to preferred products

questions.explanation: The rationing function distributes goods to the buyers who place the highest value on them. A lower price raising quantity demanded is not the definition of this function.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: The following shows the demand-supply curves for good X.

choices.text: The consumer surplus is equal to area (V + W + X).
The total social surplus is equal to area (V + W + Y).
The producer surplus is equal to area Y.
The deadweight loss is equal to area X.

questions.explanation: At the binding ceiling, quantity transacted is the quantity supplied. Producer surplus is area Y; the other areas omit the resulting deadweight loss.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram with a price ceiling P1 below equilibrium price P0 and areas V, W, X and Y.
visuals.caption: Price ceiling and surplus

movements: The ceiling at P1 limits quantity transacted to the quantity supplied.
Producer surplus is area Y.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government sets a price ceiling on good X at P1. Which of the following is the result of setting the price ceiling?

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem:
Government imposes a tax on plastic tableware. Which statements are correct?

(1) Consumer surplus in the plastic-tableware market decreases.
(2) If demand is inelastic, consumers' total expenditure increases.
(3) Total social surplus in the wooden-tableware market decreases.
questions.explanation: The tax raises plastic-tableware price and lowers quantity, reducing consumer surplus. With inelastic demand, total expenditure rises. Wooden tableware is a substitute, so its demand and total social surplus increase rather than decrease.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem:
The Wai shopping mall atop Tai Wai Station, owned by MTR Corporation, opens in 2023. Which are private benefits to MTR?

(1) Shop rental at Tai Wai Station increases.
(2) Number of MTR passengers increases.
(3) Nearby private residential-property prices increase.
questions.explanation: Higher rent and more MTR passengers directly raise MTR's revenue, making them private benefits. Higher nearby property prices benefit owners who do not compensate MTR, so that is an external benefit.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Lorenz curve
questions.stem: Refer to the following post-tax post-social transfer Lorenz curves of Country A.

choices.text: The government reduced the transfer payments to the poor between 2020 and 2023.
Between 2020 and 2023, the tax system changed from regressive to progressive.
The government reduced the basic allowance of the salaries tax between 2020 and 2023.
Between 2020 and 2023, the income of low-income households decreased while the income of high-income households increased.

questions.explanation: The 2023 Lorenz curve is closer to perfect equality, indicating lower inequality. A more progressive tax system can cause that; the other policy changes worsen inequality or cannot be inferred from a Lorenz curve.

visuals.alt: Post-tax post-social-transfer Lorenz curves for Country A in 2020 and 2023.
visuals.caption: Country A Lorenz curves

labels: Cumulative percentage of post-tax post-social transfer income
movements: The 2023 Lorenz curve is closer to the line of perfect equality than the 2020 curve.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: A shift from regressive to progressive taxation can explain lower income inequality, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: With reference to the above information, which of the following can explain the change from 2020 to 2023?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising opportunities
questions.stem:
The Labour Department's Work Orientation and Placement Scheme gives employers an allowance to hire persons with disabilities and provide training, support and a mentor. Which statements are correct?

(1) It helps equalise opportunities.
(2) It helps reduce income inequality.
(3) It raises labour productivity.
questions.explanation: The scheme improves hiring opportunities for persons with disabilities, who are often low-income, and the training can raise productivity. All three statements are correct.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Tracy's preference order is e-sports athlete, government administrative officer, then a master's programme. Which factor would LEAST likely affect her cost-benefit analysis?

choices.text: Master's graduates have worse employment prospects.

questions.explanation: The third option's employment prospects do not change the benefit of the first option or cost of giving up the second. The other changes do.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: After paying $100,000 for a human-resources course, Mr Chan earns $25,000 monthly at Company A. Company B offers a $22,000 job. What is his opportunity cost of switching to Company B?

choices.text: Company A's salary and the $100,000 tuition fee.

questions.explanation: Switching means forgoing Company A's $25,000 monthly salary. The course fee is sunk cost.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: To cope with rising paper costs, government replaces paper leaflets and forms with e-Government services. This uses ______ to solve the problem of ______.
questions.explanation: The government makes the decision, and it changes resources and method of providing the service.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: A sole-proprietor dancing school becomes a private limited company. After the change: (1) it pays a higher profits-tax rate; (2) it has lasting continuity; (3) it can issue shares to the public.
questions.explanation: A private limited company has lasting continuity and faces the company tax rate, but only a public limited company may issue shares to the public.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Which statement about private goods is CORRECT?

choices.text: Extra cost of serving one more consumer is greater than zero.
They are goods provided by private enterprises.
Free television programmes by private stations are private goods.

questions.explanation: Private goods are rival; serving another consumer has positive extra cost. The other choices confuse provision, non-rival TV programmes, and consumer goods.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Who is least occupationally mobile in a secondary school?
questions.explanation: A principal has high specialist qualifications and salary, so the opportunity cost of changing occupation is greatest.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem: Country A encourages foreign professionals to work there and relaxes entry requirements. This will cause: (1) labour supply to increase; (2) Country A workers' geographical mobility to increase; (3) average labour productivity to increase.
questions.explanation: More foreign professionals raise labour supply and average productivity. Their migration does not make existing Country A workers more geographically mobile.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The table below shows the production plan of a firm. It employs only labour and machines.
questions.explanation: Total product is 12, 27, 48, 70 and 90; marginal product falls from 22 to 20 when the sixth unit is employed.
questions.postVisualStem: Diminishing marginal returns sets in when the ________ unit of labour is employed, and the corresponding marginal product of labour is ________ units.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm. The fixed cost of the firm is $1.
questions.explanation: Output falls from five to three because MC meets price at those quantities. Producer surplus falls from $20 to $6.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the market price decreases from $12 to $8 and the fixed cost of the firm increases by $2. As a result, the profit-maximising output of the firm will ________ while the producer surplus will __________.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand? (1) Cutting unemployment benefits increases unemployed people. (2) Cold spells raise heater quantity and price. (3) Raising swimming-pool admission fees lowers average time spent there.
questions.explanation: Cutting benefits raises the cost of unemployment, so unemployment falls. A uniform entry-fee rise lowers the relative price of a long visit, raising average time. Cold weather shifts heater demand, not a violation.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings of joint supply and competitive supply
questions.stem: When the price of ______ decreases, the supply of ______ will decrease.

choices.text: cross-harbour bus service ... cross-harbour rail service

questions.explanation: Wooden furniture and wood chips are jointly supplied. A lower furniture price reduces its supply and therefore the supply of wood chips.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is the demand-supply diagram of the private courier service market. E0 is the original equilibrium point.
questions.explanation: Online shopping raises demand for courier services and AI raises supply. The other events reduce the private-courier demand or supply.

visuals.alt: Private courier-service demand-supply diagram with E0 and E1.
visuals.caption: Private courier-service market

movements: Online shopping shifts demand right.
AI-assisted delivery shifts supply right.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Both shifts lead from E0 to E1, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following events occurring simultaneously may explain the change in the equilibrium point from E0 to E1?

(1) The government postal institution lowers its courier service charges.
(2) Many couriers switch to other industries due to an increase in average wage in other industries.
(3) People use online shopping services more often.
(4) Courier companies introduce artificial intelligence (AI) to assist in the distribution of mail.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: Belief in vitamin pills increases; price rises 10% and quantity transacted changes 50%. Which best explains the result?

choices.text: Nutrients can be obtained from food.
Taking vitamin pills is a habit.

questions.explanation: Demand rises, and the much larger quantity response indicates elastic supply. Spare production capacity makes supply elastic.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the subsidy
questions.stem: Government gives battery manufacturers a $6 unit subsidy. Original price is $30 and demand elasticity exceeds supply elasticity. New price can be: (1) $24; (2) $27; (3) $29; (4) $30.
questions.explanation: Consumers receive less than half the subsidy, so price cannot fall to $24 or $27. It can be $29, or $30 under perfectly elastic demand/perfectly inelastic supply.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: The following shows the supply and demand curves for good X. The government imposes a price floor on good X at PA.
questions.explanation: The market moves from floor-limited output to the new equilibrium. Expenditure and consumer surplus increase; it does not become a shortage.

visuals.alt: Price-floor diagram with demand rising from D0 to D1.
visuals.caption: Demand rise with price floor

movements: Demand shifts right from D0 to D1.
The previously effective floor becomes ineffective.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Statements (1) and (3) are correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the demand for good X increases from D0 to D1. Which of the following statements about the market for good X are CORRECT?

(1) Consumers’ total expenditure will increase.
(2) The market of good X will change from having a surplus to a shortage.
(3) Consumer surplus will increase.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the tax burden
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply schedule of good X.
questions.explanation: After tax, price is $13 and 30 units are sold. Producer net revenue falls to $330, and each side bears $30. Consumer expenditure falls, showing elastic rather than inelastic demand.
questions.postVisualStem:
If the government imposes a per-unit tax of $2 on good X,

(1) within the range of the original and new market prices, the demand for good X is inelastic.
(2) producers’ total revenue net of tax will decrease.
(3) consumers and producers bear the same tax burden.

questions.keyPoint: Give examples of monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly
questions.stem: Which explains why the Hong Kong cha chaan teng market is NOT perfectly competitive?

choices.text: They are free to leave the market.
There are many cha chaan tengs.

questions.explanation: Non-price competition is inconsistent with perfect competition. The other features can occur in a perfectly competitive market.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on consumer surplus
questions.stem: Suppose marginal benefit per unit of rice decreases. Which statements are correct? (1) Economic efficiency worsens. (2) Producer surplus decreases. (3) Marginal cost of the last unit decreases.
questions.explanation: Lower marginal benefit shifts demand left; equilibrium price and quantity fall, lowering producer surplus and the last unit's marginal cost. Efficiency remains because MB still equals MC at the new equilibrium.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the supply and demand curves for good X.
questions.explanation: The effective ceiling creates under-production, with MB above MC at output Q1. Producer surplus is PAba; the deadweight loss is the shaded triangle, not cfg.

visuals.alt: Price-ceiling diagram after supply shifts from S0 to S1.
visuals.caption: Price ceiling after supply fall

movements: Supply shifts left from S0 to S1.
A binding ceiling limits quantity below efficient output.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Statements (1) and (3) are correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the supply of good X changes from S0 to S1 and the government sets a price ceiling at PA. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The marginal benefit will be greater than the marginal cost.
(2) There is over-production for good X.
(3) The new producer surplus will be area PAba.
(4) The deadweight loss will be area cfg.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: Stores play advertisements loudly, disturbing nearby residents without compensation. Which statements are correct? (1) Private and social costs diverge and advertisements exceed efficient level. (2) Compensation reduces the divergence. (3) Fines eliminate the divergence.
questions.explanation: Noise is an external cost. Compensation or fines can reduce divergence, but a fine does not necessarily eliminate it.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: Which proposals reduce Country A's Gini coefficient based on household disposable income? (1) Increase transfers to low-income people. (2) Increase basic allowance for salaries tax. (3) Increase municipal solid-waste charging.
questions.explanation: Transfers and a higher tax allowance narrow the disposable-income gap. Waste charging is regressive and widens it.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem: Income inequality among insurance agents exceeds that among waiters. What is a possible reason?

choices.text: Agents have a larger difference in natural abilities.
Agents have a smaller difference in educational qualifications.

questions.explanation: A greater dispersion in natural ability can produce a greater dispersion in agents' incomes.

questions.keyPoint: Uses and limitations of national income statistics
questions.stem: Which is included in Hong Kong's current-year GDP?

choices.text: Estimated rental value of an owner-occupied unit.
Value of a new unit built last year and now purchased.

questions.explanation: Owner occupiers are imputed to provide rental services to themselves. The other items are not current production.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: The following diagram shows a production chain of chocolates in Country A.

visuals.alt: Chocolate production chain with local and imported inputs, manufacturers, supermarkets and consumers.
visuals.caption: Chocolate production chain

movements: Only domestic value added counts in GDP.
A subsidy is included when converting to market-price GDP.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The chain contributes $13,500, so option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose a $300 subsidy is provided to the local chocolate manufacturers by the government. The contribution of the above production chain to Country A’s GDP at market prices is ________.

questions.keyPoint: Growth rate of GDP
questions.stem: An economy has per-capita nominal GDP growth 0%, real GDP growth 1%, and population growth -3%. Compared with last year, general price level has ______ and per-capita real GDP has ______.
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP falls with population while real GDP rises, implying a lower general price level. Rising real GDP with fewer people raises per-capita real GDP.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: The following table shows the gross domestic product (GDP) data of an economy for a certain year.
questions.explanation: Capital consumption makes gross formation greater than net; positive net factor income makes GNI greater than GDP. Subsidies exceed indirect taxes, so GDP at market prices is lower than factor cost.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the economy are CORRECT?

(1) The gross domestic fixed capital formation is larger than the net domestic fixed capital formation.
(2) The gross national income (GNI) is larger than the GDP.
(3) The GDP at market prices is larger than the GDP at factor cost.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: People's desire to save increases. Which can offset the resulting short-run price-level effect?

choices.text: Producers expect price level to decrease.
Government raises the minimum wage rate.
Risk of holding interest-bearing assets increases.

questions.explanation: More saving lowers AD and price level. A higher minimum wage raises cost and reduces SRAS, putting upward pressure on prices.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Government gives publicly funded secondary schools up to $1m each for IT-related extracurricular activities. This increases: (1) AD; (2) SRAS; (3) potential output; (4) long-run price level.
questions.explanation: Government expenditure raises AD and improved productive capacity raises SRAS and potential output. Long-run price effect is uncertain.

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem: Which function is performed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority?
questions.explanation: The HKMA manages the Exchange Fund and official reserves. The other functions belong to the Financial Secretary, note-issuing banks, or commercial banks.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem: Mr Wong withdraws $500,000 from a restricted-licence bank, holds $100,000 cash, puts $200,000 in a licensed-bank time deposit and remits $200,000 overseas. Which immediate effects occur? (1) M1 rises $100,000. (2) M2 rises $200,000. (3) M3 falls $200,000.
questions.explanation: The final changes are M1 +$100,000, M2 +$300,000 and M3 -$200,000, so (1) and (3) are correct.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: The following table shows the balance sheet of the banking system of a country. All banks do not hold excess reserves and the public always hold $100 million cash.

choices.text: The monetary base will be $300 million.
The money supply will be $1,400 million.
The maximum possible amount of deposits will be $1,500 million.
The maximum possible amount of loans will be $900 million.

questions.explanation: The required reserve ratio is 25%. After the withdrawal, reserves are $300 million, so maximum deposits are $1,200 million and maximum loans are $900 million. Monetary base remains $400 million and money supply becomes $1,300 million.
questions.postVisualStem: If the public withdraw $100 million from the banking system and remit it overseas,

questions.keyPoint: Understand how central bank actions affect the monetary base
questions.stem: Which action will cause money supply to increase while the monetary base remains unchanged? (1) The central bank lowers the discount rate. (2) The central bank lowers the required reserve ratio. (3) The central bank purchases government bonds from the public.
questions.explanation: A lower required reserve ratio permits deposit creation and raises money supply without changing cash in circulation or bank reserves. Lowering the discount rate or buying bonds increases the monetary base.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money demand and money supply curves of an economy. The initial equilibrium point is at E0.

choices.text: will increase ... may increase or decrease
will decrease ... may increase or decrease

questions.explanation: E-wallet use lowers transaction demand for money, while bond sales lower money supply. Quantity of money falls, but the interest-rate effect depends on the relative size of the two shifts.

visuals.alt: Money demand and money supply diagram with initial equilibrium E.
visuals.caption: Money market

movements: E-wallet use shifts money demand left.
Central-bank bond sales shift money supply left.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Money quantity decreases; the nominal interest rate may rise or fall, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: If people are more used to make payments for daily expenses by e-wallets and at the same time the central bank sells government bonds to the public, the quantity of money __________ and the nominal interest rate __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Explain why debtors will gain (lose) and creditors will lose (gain) under unanticipated inflation (deflation)
questions.stem: Suppose actual inflation is -3% and the nominal interest rate is 4%. Which statement is CORRECT?

choices.text: The actual real interest rate is 1%.
The cost of holding money is 3%.
The nominal interest rate is lower than the expected real interest rate.
If expected inflation is -1%, bond issuers will lose.

questions.explanation: Actual real interest is 4% - (-3%) = 7%, and the cost of holding money is the 4% nominal interest rate. With unexpected deflation, the real value of the fixed interest paid by bond issuers rises, so they lose.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: The diagram shows a constant positive growth rate of money supply and a rising growth rate of the general price level.

choices.text: the growth rate of real output is decreasing.
the velocity of circulation of money is increasing.

questions.explanation: With MV = PY and constant velocity, money growth approximately equals inflation plus real-output growth. As price-level growth rises from below to above the constant money-growth rate, real-output growth decreases.

visuals.alt: Growth-rate diagram with a constant money-supply line and rising general-price-level line.
visuals.caption: Growth rates of money supply and price level

movements: Money-supply growth remains positive and constant.
General-price-level growth rises over time.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: With constant velocity, rising inflation relative to money growth means real-output growth is decreasing, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: According to the quantity theory of money,

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: In Country A, many civil servants retire. To reduce government expenditure, the government fills only part of the vacancies. The unemployment rate of Country A ______.
questions.explanation: The labour force and unemployed population both fall, but their percentage changes are not given. The unemployment rate may rise, fall or remain unchanged.

questions.keyPoint: Four basic principles of taxation
questions.stem: Every passenger aged 12 or above departing Hong Kong by air pays an Air Passenger Departure Tax of HK$120. Increasing this tax is LEAST consistent with Adam Smith's principle of taxation concerning ______.
questions.explanation: A fixed tax increase is a larger proportion of income for low-income passengers than for high-income passengers, so it is least consistent with the equity principle.

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the change in the income tax system in economy A.

choices.text: income distribution will become more uneven.
fewer people will fall into the tax net.
all workers will have a lower work incentive than under the old system.
the economy will result in a fiscal surplus.

questions.explanation: The old system is proportional, while the new system is regressive and removes the tax allowance. More low-income people enter the tax net while high-income taxpayers pay less, widening income inequality.

visuals.alt: Income-tax diagram comparing the old and new tax systems.
visuals.caption: Change in income-tax system

movements: The old system is proportional.
The new system is regressive and has no tax allowance.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The new system widens the income distribution, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Under the new tax system,

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Which policy would offset the effect of contractionary monetary policy on aggregate output?

choices.text: Selling government bonds to the public.

questions.explanation: Contractionary monetary policy lowers AD and output. Abolishing a general sales tax lowers production cost, raises SRAS and increases output, offsetting that effect.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem: Which may raise aggregate output and worsen equity in Hong Kong at the same time?

choices.text: A HK$20,000 cash allowance to parents for each newborn baby.
A reduction in the profits-tax rate.
Construction of a new railway spur line.
Electronic learning devices for students from low-income families.

questions.explanation: A lower profits-tax rate raises investment and AD, increasing output. As profits-tax payers are mostly high-income people, the tax cut widens the income gap.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem: Suppose the liquidity of interest-bearing assets decreases. Which policy can stabilise both short-run output and the interest rate?

choices.text: The central bank raises the discount rate.
The central bank lowers the required reserve ratio.
The government raises the salaries-tax rate.
The government changes civil servants' salary payments from bi-weekly to monthly.

questions.explanation: Lower asset liquidity raises money demand, raises interest rates and lowers AD and output. Lowering the required reserve ratio raises money supply, reducing the interest rate and restoring consumption, investment and output.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: Before trade, the output of Country A and Country B with all their resources evenly allocated between the production of computers and bread is shown below:
questions.explanation: Country A can produce 40 computers or 120 bread, while Country B can produce 80 computers or 110 bread. Country B specialises in computers and Country A in bread: totals rise from 60 to 80 computers and from 115 to 120 bread.
questions.postVisualStem: If Country A and Country B completely specialise their production and trade with each other, the total output of computers will increase by ____________ units and the total output of bread will increase by ____________ units.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the market of good X in a small open economy. The government imposes an import tariff on good X.
questions.explanation: Domestic price and consumption both rise, so consumer expenditure rises. Domestic production rises with the price. Import volume, and therefore tariff revenue, depends on the relative sizes of the world-price and demand increases.

visuals.alt: Small-open-economy import-tariff diagram with supply, demand, world price and tariff-inclusive price.
visuals.caption: Import tariff

movements: A higher world price raises domestic price.
Higher demand shifts demand right.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Consumer expenditure and domestic production increase; tariff revenue is uncertain, so all three statements are correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the world price of good X increases and the demand for good X increases at the same time. Which of the following are CORRECT?

(1) The total expenditure of local consumers on good X will increase.
(2) The government’s tariff revenue from good X may increase, decrease or remain unchanged.
(3) The domestic production of good X will increase.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Whether and how a given transaction affects the current account
questions.stem: Which transactions are included in Hong Kong's current account balance? (1) A Hong Kong resident rents a car while travelling in Japan. (2) A Hong Kong resident receives a remittance from a relative in Canada. (3) A Swedish investor sells shares in a Hong Kong listed company.
questions.explanation: Renting a car abroad is an import of services and a remittance received is a current transfer. Selling shares is recorded in the capital and financial account.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: The table below shows the change in the exchange rate between the US dollar (USD) and the Japanese yen (JPY).

choices.text: a decrease in the total value of goods imported from Japan to the United States (in terms of the US dollar)
an increase in the total value of goods exported from Hong Kong to Japan (in terms of the Hong Kong dollar)
a decrease in the number of Japanese tourists visiting Hong Kong
an appreciation of the Japanese yen against the Hong Kong dollar

questions.explanation: The US dollar, and under the linked system the Hong Kong dollar, appreciates against the Japanese yen. Hong Kong becomes more expensive in yen for Japanese tourists, reducing their visits. Effects on total import and export values are uncertain.
questions.postVisualStem: During the period from 1 June to 1 December 2023, the change in the exchange rate between USD and JPY will lead to _____________.

questions.keyPoint: Explain why past expenditure which is irrecoverable is not a cost
questions.stem: Anson is choosing between becoming a firefighter and studying economics abroad. Which factor is LEAST important in this choice?

choices.text: The expense of studying abroad is higher than expected.
The government raises the starting salary for new firefighters.
Anson has already spent three years studying economics.
More employers prefer to hire people who have studied abroad.

questions.explanation: The time already spent studying economics is irrecoverable past expenditure. It is not the opportunity cost of either current choice and does not affect the decision.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Mr Chan owns a residential unit and is deciding whether to sell it or renovate it before continuing to live there. He must rent another unit during renovation. In which situation will his cost of continuing to live in his unit increase?

choices.text: The market price of his unit decreases.
Market rent of other units decreases.
Renovation quality is better than expected.

questions.explanation: A delay makes Mr Chan rent another unit for longer, increasing the monetary cost. A lower sale price or rent lowers the cost, and better renovation quality raises the benefit rather than the opportunity cost.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem: If a good is scarce,

choices.text: there is a shortage of the good.
the good must have a market price.
its quantity is not sufficient to satisfy all people's wants.

questions.explanation: Scarcity means available quantity is insufficient for all wants. It does not require a shortage at the prevailing price, a market price, or a fixed quantity.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of interest
questions.stem: Which statement about interest is CORRECT?

choices.text: Interest still exists when there is no scarcity.
Interest will not exist in a command economy.
Interest can be in the form of goods or money.
Scarcity does not exist because interest does not exist.

questions.explanation: Interest is the cost of earlier availability of resources. It can be paid in goods or money and arises from scarcity rather than a particular economic system.

questions.keyPoint: Definition of free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: An online shopping platform provides free delivery to customers meeting a purchase threshold. The delivery services are ______ because ______.

choices.text: producer goods ... they directly satisfy customers' wants
free goods ... they are provided free of charge
public goods ... they are offered to all qualifying customers
economic goods ... they are produced from scarce resources

questions.explanation: Delivery uses scarce drivers, vehicles and fuel, so it is an economic good. Provision free of charge does not make a service a free good.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem: If a market economy turns into a command economy,

choices.text: more resources will be owned by the government.
income distribution will become more uneven.
the quantity of public goods will increase.

questions.explanation: A command economy has a larger role for public ownership and government allocation. The other effects do not necessarily follow.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: Under a school's One Tablet Per Student scheme, teachers install designated learning software and all Form 1 students are automatically included. Which basic economic problems are involved? (1) what to produce; (2) how to produce; (3) for whom to produce.
questions.explanation: Choosing learning software concerns resources and methods of providing education, so it is how to produce. Automatically including Form 1 students determines who receives the service.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Jonathan is choosing between a partnership and a private limited company for his swimming centre. Which are possible reasons to choose a private limited company? (1) A partnership is not a legal entity while a private limited company is. (2) Ownership of a private limited company can be freely transferred while that of a partnership cannot. (3) A private limited company has wider sources of capital.
questions.explanation: A private limited company is a legal entity and has wider sources of capital, including shares and bonds. Ownership in both forms requires other owners' consent to transfer.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Why might a public limited company issue shares rather than bonds?

choices.text: It has no obligation to redeem its shares.
Existing shareholders' control will not be diluted.
Issuing shares will not increase takeover risk.

questions.explanation: Ordinary shares do not require redemption, unlike bonds. Issuing shares can dilute control and increase takeover risk, while either method may raise capital.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Which is the closest example of a public good?

choices.text: Play equipment for children in a park
Free drinking water provided in a restaurant

questions.explanation: Street lighting is non-rival and non-excludable. The other examples are excludable, rival, or confined to a private setting.

questions.keyPoint: Describe the inter-relationship between the three types of production
questions.stem: Refer to the diagram showing primary, secondary and tertiary production.
questions.explanation: X is a service flowing from tertiary to primary production, while Y is producer goods flowing from secondary to primary production.

visuals.alt: Diagram linking primary, secondary and tertiary production with arrows X and Y.
visuals.caption: Links among types of production

movements: X flows from tertiary to primary production as services.
Y flows from secondary to primary production as producer goods.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: X is services and Y is producer goods, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: X and Y represent ______ and ______ respectively.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital
questions.stem: Which items are capital of a supermarket? (1) food samples for tasting; (2) cash registers; (3) cashiers; (4) shop premises.
questions.explanation: Food samples, cash registers and shop premises are man-made resources used in production. Cashiers are labour, not capital.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: The input-output relationship of two firms is as follows:
questions.explanation: Firm A supplies 400 man-hours against Firm B's 350. Its productivity is 4,000 / 400 = 10 units per man-hour, while Firm B's is 4,200 / 350 = 12.

visuals.caption: Input-output relationship of two firms
rows: Working hours per worker per day

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, _________ has a larger labour supply and _________ has higher average labour productivity.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: Firm A and Firm B produce the same mobile-phone accessories. They employ the same number of workers, but Firm A workers work longer hours and both firms have the same output. What may explain their different labour productivity?

choices.text: Firm A implements a higher degree of division of labour.
Firm A uses piece rate while Firm B uses time rate.
Firm B workers have lower skills.
Firm B uses more producer goods.

questions.explanation: Firm B produces the same output with fewer man-hours, so it has higher productivity. More producer goods used by Firm B can explain that; the other options would tend to raise Firm A productivity or lower Firm B productivity.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Occupational mobility of labour in Hong Kong will increase if

choices.text: firms adopt a higher degree of division of labour.
the monthly public-transport fare subsidy is raised.
the subsidy ceiling of the Continuing Education Fund is raised.

questions.explanation: A higher Continuing Education Fund ceiling helps workers gain skills for other occupations. Licensing and division of labour reduce occupational mobility, while transport subsidy mainly affects geographical mobility.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The following table shows the input-output relationship of a firm.
questions.explanation: Marginal product is 5, 7, 12, 8 and 3, so it begins to fall with the fourth unit. Machinery is fixed, showing the short run. Average product falls from 8 to 7 after three units.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the above firm are CORRECT?

(1) The marginal product of labour will start to dimmish when the fourth unit of labour is put to work.
(2) The above information shows a short run situation.
(3) The average product of labour keeps increasing.

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: After a firm doubles the quantity of all inputs, its total output and total cost change as follows.
questions.explanation: Average cost falls from $5 to $4 as scale increases, showing internal economies. Lower buying costs may cause this. Diminishing returns concerns the short run, and profit is uncertain without selling-price and sales information.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The firm enjoys internal economies of scale.
(2) The above data illustrate the law of diminishing marginal returns.
(3) It may be a result of lower buying costs.
(4) The firm has a higher profit.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: Mr Wong runs a taekwondo school. Which change will reduce its profit-maximising output?

choices.text: More primary schools emphasise sports performance in admissions.
There are more taekwondo schools in the market.
Rent for the school premises decreases.

questions.explanation: More competing schools increase market supply and lower market price and marginal revenue, reducing profit-maximising output. A lower instructor salary lowers marginal cost, higher demand raises output, and rent is fixed cost.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning and give examples of each type of integration
questions.stem: Which is vertical backward integration?

choices.text: A food wholesale company acquires a supermarket.
A hotel acquires a travel agency.
A bakery acquires a software-development company.
A dairy-products manufacturer acquires an overseas farm.

questions.explanation: The dairy manufacturer acquires a previous stage of production, an input supplier. The other examples are forward, lateral or conglomerate integration.

questions.keyPoint: Concepts of demand
questions.stem: When a market demand curve is derived, which are not assumed constant? (1) price of the good; (2) consumers' income; (3) quantity demanded; (4) price of a substitute.
questions.explanation: The demand curve studies the effect of a change in the good's price on quantity demanded, so neither its price nor quantity demanded is held constant. Income and substitute prices are held constant.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem: People queued for newly launched tour packages, but packages sold out although some were willing to pay the price. Which statements are CORRECT? (1) Price was below equilibrium. (2) There was a shortage. (3) Opportunity cost of obtaining a package exceeded its price.
questions.explanation: Unserved willing buyers mean quantity demanded exceeded quantity supplied, so price was below equilibrium and there was a shortage. Waiting time adds time cost, making the opportunity cost exceed the package price.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: A furniture store raises the lump-sum delivery fee for all furniture to cope with increasing costs. The table below shows the quantities of high-quality furniture and average-quality furniture sold.
questions.explanation: The fixed fee lowers high-quality furniture's relative price, so its share should increase. Cases (2) and (3) reduce its relative share; case (1) raises it.

visuals.caption: Furniture quantities before and after the delivery-fee rise
rows: Before the delivery fee is raised
After the delivery fee is raised

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following figures is/are inconsistent with the law of demand?

(1) Q1 = 11,500; Q2 = 7,500
(2) Q1 = 10,000; Q2 = 7,500
(3) Q1 = 10,000; Q2 = 7,000

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which is CONSISTENT with the law of demand?

choices.text: A 10% hotel service fee makes more people prefer deluxe rooms to standard rooms.
A higher fixed penalty for littering increases littering.
More low-quality fruits are sold near a farm than in a faraway market.
A per-unit import tariff on red wine worsens average imported-wine quality.

questions.explanation: A fixed transport cost raises the relative price of low-quality fruit in the faraway market, so relatively fewer low-quality fruit are bought there. The other changes contradict the law of demand applied to relative or full price.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: Which situation is most likely to increase demand for new electric cars?

choices.text: The price of gasoline cars increases.
Interest rate on car loans increases.
More research finds electric-car safety concerns.
Most sellers discount new electric cars.

questions.explanation: Gasoline and electric cars are substitutes. A higher gasoline-car price raises demand for electric cars; the other events lower demand or move along the demand curve.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is a supply-demand diagram for pet care services. The original equilibrium point is E0.
questions.explanation: More pet owners shift demand right from D0 to D1, while more trained workers shift supply right from S0 to S1. Their new intersection is E1.

visuals.alt: Pet-care-services demand-supply diagram with D0 to D2, S0 to S2 and equilibria E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Pet-care-services market

movements: Pet ownership shifts demand right from D0 to D1.
More trained workers shift supply right from S0 to S1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The new equilibrium is E1, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: As keeping pets becomes a trend, more people keep pets at home. At the same time, more young people take animal care courses and join the pet care industry. The new equilibrium point will be _________.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings of joint supply and competitive supply
questions.stem: When good X and good Y are in ______, an increase in demand for X will result in a decrease in the ______ good Y.
questions.explanation: Higher demand for X raises its price. If X and Y are jointly supplied, supply of Y rises, lowering Y's price and raising quantity demanded. Competitive supply would raise Y's price instead.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: Suppose many private residential properties have been completed in Country A in recent years. At the same time, more people hold a pessimistic view of future property prices. Which of the following diagrams could represent the above phenomena?
questions.explanation: Newly completed properties increase rental-housing supply. Pessimistic expected sale prices shift people from buying to renting, increasing rental-housing demand. Diagram B shows both rightward shifts.

visuals.alt: Four demand-supply diagram options for private residential rental and sales markets.
visuals.caption: Private residential housing-market options

movements: Completed properties increase rental supply.
Pessimistic sale-price expectations increase rental demand.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Diagram B shows a rental market with both supply and demand shifting right.
