questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: The table below shows the total expenditure of Miss Chan and Mr. Tong on fitness services.

choices.text: 0 ... greater than 1 and smaller than infinity

questions.explanation: As price rises, Miss Chan's expenditure rises while quantity falls, so demand is inelastic. Mr Tong always buys 20 units, so demand is perfectly inelastic.
questions.postVisualStem: Miss Chan’s elasticity of demand for fitness services is ____________ while Mr. Tong’s elasticity of demand for fitness services is ____________ (without regard to the negative sign).

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: The reproductive rate of cows in Country A rises significantly, causing a 40% change in local-beef price and a 55% change in quantity transacted. Which statements are CORRECT? (1) Demand for local beef increases. (2) Total expenditure on local beef increases. (3) Quantity transacted of imported beef decreases. (4) Total expenditure on imported beef may rise or fall depending on price elasticity of demand.
questions.explanation: More cows increase local-beef supply, lowering price and raising quantity. Quantity rises proportionately more, so total expenditure on local beef rises. Imported beef is a substitute, so its demand, price, quantity and total expenditure fall.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: Nutritional supplements are normal goods. General income rises, and their price and quantity transacted change by 15% and 20% respectively. What best explains the changes?

choices.text: There are no close substitutes for nutritional supplements.
Supplements account for a small share of income.

questions.explanation: Higher income shifts demand right. Quantity changes by more than price, showing elastic supply; spare capacity makes manufacturers able to expand output flexibly. The other options concern demand elasticity or make supply less elastic.

questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem:
A singer is going to hold a concert in Macau. Mr. Cheung spent $500 on a concert ticket a few months ago. Suppose he can resell the ticket to a friend for $400. Alternatively, he can spend $180 on taking a bus to Macau to watch the concert.

What is Mr. Cheung's opportunity cost of going to Macau to watch the concert?
questions.explanation: The $500 ticket payment is irrecoverable past expenditure. Going to Macau requires the $180 bus fare and gives up the $400 resale income, so the opportunity cost is $580.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
Which of the following cases are related to the problem of 'what to produce'?

(1) A smartphone manufacturer decides to develop a new foldable phone.
(2) A smartphone manufacturer plans to provide more colour options for existing phone models.
(3) A smartphone manufacturer considers moving its domestic production line overseas.
(4) A smartphone manufacturer plans to increase the selling price of its smartphones.
questions.explanation: Developing a product and choosing its colour range determine the kinds of goods to produce. Moving production overseas concerns how to produce, while a price change determines for whom the goods are produced.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about a private limited company and a public limited company in Hong Kong is CORRECT?

choices.text: A public limited company has more capital than a private limited company.
Compared with a private limited company, a public limited company has wider sources of capital.
A private limited company and a public limited company are required to disclose their financial information to the public.
There is no upper limit on the number of shareholders for both a private limited company and a public limited company.

questions.explanation: A public limited company can issue shares and bonds to the public, giving it wider sources of capital. It need not have more capital, private companies need not disclose accounts publicly, and a private company has a maximum of 50 shareholders.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem:
The following are facilities and services that can be found at Hong Kong International Airport.

(1) public restrooms
(2) flight information
(3) security services
(4) paid luggage storage service provided by the airport

Which of the above items are public goods?
questions.explanation: Flight information and security services are non-rival and non-excludable. Restroom use is rival, and paid luggage storage is excludable because non-paying users can be excluded.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital
questions.stem:
In Hong Kong, some organisations hold guided hiking tours on hiking trails managed by the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department, and participants can enjoy the natural scenery along the way.

In the above case, the hiking trails are _____________ because _____________.

choices.text: land ... they are a gift of nature
land ... they are made from natural resources
capital ... they require manpower to manage and maintain
capital ... they are man-made resources used in production

questions.explanation: Hiking trails are created by people and used to produce guided-tour services. They are therefore capital, not natural resources or land.

questions.keyPoint: External economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: As more technology enterprises in Silicon Valley in the United States invest in the development of artificial intelligence, more university graduates may go there to look for job opportunities. In this case, these technology enterprises will

choices.text: suffer from external diseconomies of scale.
suffer from internal diseconomies of scale.

questions.explanation: An expanding local industry attracts a larger pool of graduates, reducing firms' hiring cost. The fall in long-run average cost comes from industry expansion, so it is an external economy of scale.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: Miss Chan runs a garment factory. If the rent of the factory and the price of fabrics increase at the same time, the profit-maximising output of the factory will _____________ and the profit _____________.
questions.explanation: Rent is fixed cost, so it reduces profit but does not change profit-maximising output. Fabrics are a variable input, so their higher price raises marginal cost and reduces both output and profit.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem:
A beverage manufacturer launched a new drink, but at the current price, a large stock remains unsold.

From the information above, we can infer that the quantity transacted of the drink is _____________.

choices.text: equal to the quantity demanded and smaller than the quantity supplied
equal to the quantity demanded and larger than the quantity supplied
equal to the quantity supplied and smaller than the quantity demanded
equal to the quantity supplied and larger than the quantity demanded

questions.explanation: An unsold stock is excess supply, meaning the current price is above equilibrium. Quantity transacted equals quantity demanded and is smaller than quantity supplied.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem:
If the price of _____________ decreases, the equilibrium quantity of _____________ will decrease.

(1) butter ... margarine
(2) smartphones ... smartphone cases
(3) apple juice ... apple pies
(4) lamb ... wool
questions.explanation: Butter and margarine are substitutes, so cheaper butter reduces demand for margarine. Lamb and wool are jointly supplied, so a lower lamb price lowers the supply of wool. The other two changes raise the relevant equilibrium quantity.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Measuring price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the market supply curve of good X.
questions.explanation: Quantity supplied rises from 25 to 38 and price rises from $11 to $30. Using midpoint percentages, arc elasticity of supply is [(13 / 31.5) / (19 / 20.5)] = 0.45.

visuals.alt: Supply curve S with points A at quantity 25 and price 11, and B at quantity 38 and price 30.
visuals.caption: Arc elasticity of supply

movements: Movement from A to B raises quantity supplied from 25 to 38.
Price rises from $11 to $30.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Using midpoint percentages, arc price elasticity of supply is 0.45, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: The arc elasticity of supply between point A and point B is ____________.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X. Suppose the government has imposed a quota on good X, and the market price is $8.

choices.text: There will be a shortage in the market for good X.
The quantity transacted of good X will decrease by 1 unit.
The equilibrium price of the complements of good X will decrease.

questions.explanation: At $8 the effective quota is 5 units. A $2 fall brings price to the equilibrium $6, where 6 units are traded and the quota is ineffective. Producers' revenue falls from $40 to $36.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: After the government increases the quota on good X, the market price changes by $2. Which of the following statements about the situation after the increase in the quota is CORRECT?

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the tax burden
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X.

choices.text: The total tax revenue of the government will be $24.
The total revenue net of tax will be $72.
The ratio of consumers' tax burden to producers' tax burden will be 2:1.
Within the range of the original and the new equilibrium prices, the elasticity of demand of good X is smaller than one.

questions.explanation: The original equilibrium is $10 and 8 units. After tax, consumers pay $12 and 6 units trade; producers receive $9. Consumers bear $12 and producers bear $6, giving a 2:1 burden ratio.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government imposes a per-unit sales tax of $3 on good X. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the subsidy
questions.stem: Refer to the following market supply schedule for apples.

choices.text: The market price will decrease by $3.
The total subsidy granted by the government is $24.
The demand for apples is more elastic than the supply of them.
The producers' total revenue including the subsidy is $96.

questions.explanation: The subsidy raises quantity from 10 to 12 and lowers the consumer price to $5. Producers receive $8 per unit including the subsidy, so total revenue is $96. The subsidy is $36, and consumers receive the larger share.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the original equilibrium price is $7. If the government provides a per-unit subsidy of $3 to the producers of apples, the quantity transacted of apples will increase by 2 units. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Give examples of monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the market share of different banks in the mortgage loan market in Country A in recent years.

choices.text: monopolistic competition ... there are many banks in the market and each has a small market share
monopolistic competition ... there are many mortgage loan applicants in the market
oligopoly ... the banks are interdependent in their pricing strategies
oligopoly ... a few major banks dominant the mortgage loan market

questions.explanation: The chart shows Banks A to D hold substantial market shares while other banks collectively have only a small share. This supports oligopoly because a few major sellers dominate the market.

visuals.alt: Line chart of mortgage-loan market shares for Banks A to D and other banks between 2020 and 2024.
visuals.caption: Mortgage-loan market shares

movements: Four named banks each retain a substantial share.
Other banks account for only about one tenth of the market.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: A few major banks dominate the market, which supports oligopoly in option D.

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, we can conclude that the mortgage loan market in Country A can be regarded as ______________ because ______________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on consumer surplus
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram for good X.

choices.text: area (a + b + c) ... area (c + e + f)

questions.explanation: Consumer surplus rises from area a to a + b + c, an increase of b + c. Total social surplus rises from a + b + d to a + b + c + d + e, an increase of c + e.

visuals.alt: Demand curve D with supply shifting right from S0 to S1, price falling from P0 to P1 and quantity rising from Q0 to Q1.
visuals.caption: Consumer and total social surplus after a supply increase

movements: Supply shifts right from S0 to S1.
Equilibrium price falls from P0 to P1 and quantity increases from Q0 to Q1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Consumer surplus increases by b + c and total social surplus increases by c + e, so option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the supply of good X changes from S0 to S1. As a result, consumer surplus will increase by _________

and total social surplus will increase by _________.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram for good X.
questions.explanation: P0 becomes a binding floor after supply increases, creating excess supply. At Q0, marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost, so output is below the efficient level and deadweight loss occurs. The demand curve is unchanged, so the marginal benefit of the last unit does not decrease.

visuals.alt: Demand curve D, initial supply S0 and higher supply S1 with a price floor P0 at the original equilibrium E0.
visuals.caption: Price floor after a supply increase

movements: Supply shifts right from S0 to S1.
The former equilibrium price P0 becomes an effective price floor.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The floor creates excess supply and deadweight loss; the marginal benefit at Q0 is unchanged, so statements (1) and (2) are correct.

answerVisuals.alt: Suggested-solution diagram showing the binding price floor, excess supply and deadweight loss after supply shifts right.
answerVisuals.caption: Suggested answer diagram

movements: Supply shifts right while the binding price floor remains above equilibrium.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Award the answer that shows excess supply and the resulting deadweight loss.

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the government sets a price floor at P0. When the supply curve shifts from S0 to S1, which of the

following statements are CORRECT?

(1) There will be an excess supply in the market of good X.
(2) There will be a deadweight loss in the market of good X.
(3) The marginal benefit of the last unit of good X will decrease.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Allocative function
questions.stem:
Which of the following cases illustrate(s) the allocative function of price?

(1) A strong preference for electric cars prompts car manufacturers to switch from producing petrol cars to electric cars.
(2) An increasing number of tourists encourages developers to build more hotels.
(3) A person sells a sofa on a social media platform using the 'highest bidder wins' approach.
questions.explanation: The allocative function directs resources to goods with stronger demand, so manufacturers move to electric cars and developers build hotels. Highest bidder wins is the rationing function, allocating a fixed sofa to the highest-valued buyer.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: During the 2024 Summer Olympics, many shopping malls in Hong Kong provided live broadcasts, attracting many people to watch the events and bringing customers to stores near the shopping malls. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The government needs to subsidise these shopping malls to improve efficiency.
If the stores do not give any compensation to the shopping malls, the number of broadcasts of Olympic events will be lower than the efficient level.
There is a divergence between private and social costs.
If the stores give compensation to the shopping malls, the marginal social benefit will equal the marginal social cost.

questions.explanation: Stores receive an external benefit if they do not compensate the malls. Marginal social benefit then exceeds marginal social cost, so broadcasts are below the efficient level. The evidence does not prove a subsidy is needed or that compensation fully restores efficiency.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: The table below shows Singapore's Gini coefficient from 2021 to 2023.
questions.explanation: Both Gini coefficients fall, showing a more even income distribution. The post-tax, post-transfer coefficient is lower than the pre-tax, pre-transfer coefficient, showing taxation and transfers reduce inequality. The table does not show amounts of tax revenue or transfers.

visuals.caption: Singapore Gini coefficients
rows: Gini coefficient based on pre-tax pre-social transfer household income
Gini coefficient based on post-tax post-social transfer household income

questions.postVisualStem:
Based on the above information, we can conclude that, during this period,

(1) the income distribution in Singapore became more even.
(2) government tax revenue decreased while social transfers increased.
(3) taxation and social transfers reduced income inequality in Singapore.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem:
In July 2024, the government announced the launch of the 'Re-employment Allowance Pilot Scheme'. Any Hong Kong residents aged 40 or above who have not engaged in any paid work in Hong Kong for 3 consecutive months or more are eligible to join the scheme and receive an allowance of up to $10,000 after working continuously for 6 months, and an additional allowance of up to $10,000 after working continuously for 12 months.

Which of the following would likely occur after the implementation of the above scheme?

(1) The scheme will help equalise income.
(2) Hong Kong's labour supply will increase.
(3) The opportunity cost of finding a job for the unemployed aged 40 or above will decrease.
questions.explanation: The recipients are mainly low-income people, narrowing the income gap. The allowance raises the reward from finding work and therefore labour supply. It raises the value of finding work rather than lowering its opportunity cost.

questions.topicGroup: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.keyPoint: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.stem:
Which of the following would be included in the calculation of Hong Kong's gross domestic product (GDP) in the current year?

(1) wages paid by the Social Welfare Department to its staff
(2) rental income received by a private property owner from leasing office space to the Social Welfare Department
(3) the disability allowance provided by the Social Welfare Department
questions.explanation: Government wages are included in government consumption expenditure, and rent is factor income earned from providing property services. Disability allowance is a transfer payment and does not reflect current production.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: The following diagram shows a production chain of electric cars in Country A.
questions.explanation: Manufacturers' contribution is $800 + $300 - $500 - $400 + $200 = $400. Adding domestic value added at retailers gives total production-chain GDP at factor cost of $1,400.

visuals.alt: Production chain linking imported and domestic raw materials, domestic manufacturers and retailers, domestic consumers, foreign consumers and inventory.
visuals.caption: Electric-car production chain

movements: Imported inputs are excluded from domestic value added.
The $200 subsidy is added in calculating GDP at factor cost.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Domestic manufacturers contribute $400 and the whole chain contributes $1,400, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government provides a subsidy of $200 to the domestic electric car manufacturers. The contributions of the domestic electric car manufacturers and the above production chain to Country A's GDP at factor cost are ___________ and ____________ respectively.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: Consider the following gross domestic product (GDP) data about Country A in a certain year.
questions.explanation: GDP at factor cost equals private consumption + gross investment + government consumption + net exports - indirect taxes + subsidies. Substituting the data gives 750 = 250 + (200 + X) + 150 + 180 - 27 + 12, so X = -15.
questions.postVisualStem: The value of X is $ _____________ million.

questions.keyPoint: Meanings of nominal GDP and real GDP
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the GDP of Country A from 2000 to 2020.

choices.text: The general price level in Country A decreased continuously every year between 2000 and 2010.
The general price level in 2015 was lower than that in 2005.
Country A's nominal GDP and real GDP increased continuously every year between 2000 and 2020.
The GDP deflator in 2010 was the same as that in 2020.

questions.explanation: Nominal GDP equals real GDP in both 2010 and 2020, so the GDP deflator is 100 in both years. The remaining statements conflict with the nominal-real GDP relationship or the fall in nominal GDP after 2015.

visuals.alt: Line chart of Country A nominal GDP and real GDP from 2000 to 2020.
visuals.caption: Nominal and real GDP

movements: Nominal GDP equals real GDP in 2010.
Nominal GDP equals real GDP again in 2020.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The GDP deflator equals 100 in both 2010 and 2020, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above diagram, which of the following is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Growth rate of GDP
questions.stem:
Hong Kong's implicit price deflator of GDP increased by 2.8% in 2023, while its nominal GDP and population increased by 6.1% and 0.7% respectively.

Based on the information above, we can conclude that Hong Kong's per capita nominal GDP _____________ and its per capita real GDP _____________ in 2023.
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP grew faster than population, so per capita nominal GDP rose. Real GDP grew by about 3.2% after allowing for the 2.8% deflator increase, which also exceeds population growth, so per capita real GDP rose.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: To calculate Hong Kong's gross national income (GNI), which of the following should be added to Hong Kong's gross domestic product (GDP)?

choices.text: the dividends received by a Hong Kong resident from shares in South Korea's Samsung Group
the salary earned by a Hong Kong chef working at a hotel in Japan for two years
the salary earned by a Hong Kong resident working at the Hong Kong branch of a German company
the rent received by a Japanese resident from property held in Hong Kong

questions.explanation: GNI adds factor income earned by residents outside the economic territory and subtracts income earned locally by non-residents. Dividends received by a Hong Kong resident from South Korea meet that condition.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem:
Which of the following will result in a rightward shift of the aggregate demand curve of an economy?

(1) People increase their savings due to the desire for a better retired life.
(2) The economy relaxes visa requirements for foreign travellers.
(3) Electronic payments become more common.
questions.explanation: Relaxed visas raise tourism and net exports. More electronic payments lower transaction demand for money and interest rates, raising consumption or investment. More saving lowers consumption and aggregate demand.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.stem: Consider the following short run aggregate supply curve for Country A.
questions.explanation: The diagram shows a rightward SRAS shift. AI raises productivity, while an end to an oil embargo lowers input costs. Expected price rises shift SRAS left, and a trading partner's recovery shifts AD rather than SRAS.

visuals.alt: Short-run aggregate supply shifts right from SRAS0 to SRAS1.
visuals.caption: Increase in short-run aggregate supply

movements: SRAS shifts right from SRAS0 to SRAS1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Artificial-intelligence-assisted production and cheaper oil inputs both increase SRAS, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following would most likely result in the above shift of the short run aggregate supply curve?

(1) More firms expect the general price level to increase.
(2) A major trading partner experiences an economic recovery.
(3) More firms use artificial intelligence to assist with production.
(4) A major trading partner abolishes its embargo on exporting oil.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: A large natural gas field has been discovered in Country A. The government plans to extract natural gas on its own and supply it to domestic households and enterprises. Which of the following diagrams best describes the effect of the above events?
questions.explanation: The natural-gas discovery increases resource endowment and productive capacity, shifting LRAS right. Government extraction raises government consumption expenditure and shifts AD right. Only option C shows both changes.

visuals.alt: Four AS-AD option diagrams labelled A to D.
visuals.caption: Natural-gas discovery AS-AD options

movements: The discovery raises productive capacity, shifting LRAS right.
Government extraction raises government consumption, shifting AD right.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Only option C shows both a rightward LRAS shift and a rightward AD shift.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of the equilibrium level of output and price level using the AS-AD model
questions.keyPoint: Long run macroeconomic equilibrium
questions.stem: Refer to the following AS-AD diagram for Country A.
questions.explanation: The move from E to A follows a fall in aggregate demand. Imported-car preference lowers net exports and pessimism lowers investment. Cheaper raw materials raise SRAS instead.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with long-run equilibrium E on LRAS and point A below it at the same output Y1.
visuals.caption: Long-run equilibrium moving from E to A

movements: A decrease in aggregate demand moves the long-run equilibrium from E to A.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Imported-car preference and pessimistic firms reduce aggregate demand, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Country A's long run equilibrium point changes from E to A. Which of the following are possible reasons for the change?

(1) People prefer to use imported cars instead of locally produced cars.
(2) The price of imported raw materials decreases.
(3) Firms are pessimistic about business prospects.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Inflationary gap
questions.stem: Country A's inflationary (output) gap is narrowed while the general price level increases. Which of the following best explains the above changes?

choices.text: The transportation cost of raw materials increases.
The government provides subsidies to companies that invest in building factories.
The government reduces the living allowance for the elderly.

questions.explanation: Higher transport costs raise production costs and shift SRAS left. Output falls, narrowing the inflationary gap, while the general price level rises.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: The stock market in Country A has been booming recently, and therefore people are buying more locally produced goods. Which of the following would offset the effect of the above event on aggregate output in the short run?

choices.text: Many manufacturers suspend production due to severe flooding.
A billionaire funds the construction of a new university.
A large-scale strike in Country A comes to an end.
The government lowers the general sales tax rate.

questions.explanation: The boom raises consumption and AD, increasing short-run output. Flooding reduces SRAS and output, offsetting that effect. The other events would increase output further.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: Country A is an oil-importing country. The diagram below shows the aggregate demand (AD) curve, the short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve and the long run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve of Country A. The country initially operates at E0.
questions.explanation: Oil-pipeline damage raises imported oil prices and production costs, shifting SRAS left from SRAS0 to SRAS2. Short-run equilibrium is E2; wages and costs later adjust, returning SRAS to SRAS0 and long-run equilibrium to E0.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with AD0 to AD2, SRAS0 to SRAS2, LRAS and equilibrium points E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Oil-supply shock in an importing economy

movements: Oil-pipeline damage raises imported-input cost and shifts SRAS left from SRAS0 to SRAS2.
In the long run SRAS returns from SRAS2 to SRAS0.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The short-run equilibrium is E2 and the long-run equilibrium is E0, so option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: If the oil pipelines of a major oil-exporting country are damaged, Country A's short run equilibrium will be at _____________ and its long run equilibrium will be at _____________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising opportunities
questions.stem:
Which of the following can narrow the deflationary (output) gap and help equalise opportunities in an economy at the same time?

(1) distributing the same amount of cash to all households
(2) arranging for more civil servants to study abroad
(3) providing subsidies on medicine for patients with chronic diseases
questions.explanation: Medicine subsidies help financially constrained patients access treatment, improving future productivity and opportunity. They also raise recipients' disposable income and aggregate demand, narrowing the deflationary gap. The other policies fail one of the two conditions.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem:
Refer to the following pamphlet of a bank:

Preferential HKD Time Deposit

Exclusive time deposit offer for new customers. Deposit HK$100,000, and you will receive HK$6,000 in interest after one year.

Which of the following are the functions of money that are performed by the Hong Kong dollar in this case?

(1) unit of account
(2) store of value
(3) standard of deferred payment
questions.explanation: The Hong Kong dollar quotes the deposit and interest, stores purchasing power over the year, and specifies the future interest payment. It performs all three stated functions.

questions.topicGroup: Licensed banks, restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies in
questions.keyPoint: Features of the three types of deposit-taking institutions
questions.stem:
Alex sold a car for $300,000 in cash. He plans to deposit the money in a financial institution as a time deposit for three months. Which of the following financial institutions in Hong Kong can accept his deposit?

(1) licensed banks
(2) deposit-taking companies
(3) restricted licence banks
questions.explanation: Licensed banks can accept deposits of any amount and maturity. Deposit-taking companies can accept time deposits of at least $100,000 with at least three months' original maturity. Restricted licence banks cannot accept deposits below $500,000.

questions.keyPoint: Definitions of M1, M2 and M3 in
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the relationship between money supply M1 and M2 in Hong Kong.

choices.text: reserves with licensed banks ... all customers' deposits with licensed banks
customers' demand deposits with licensed banks ... customers' savings deposits with licensed banks
customers' demand deposits with licensed banks ... customers' savings and time deposits with licensed banks
all customers' deposits with licensed banks ... all customers' deposits with restricted licence banks

questions.explanation: M1 is currency held by the public plus customers' demand deposits with licensed banks. M2 adds negotiable certificates of deposit held outside the banking sector and customers' savings and time deposits with licensed banks.

visuals.alt: Nested M1 and M2 definitions showing currency held by the public, X, negotiable certificates of deposit and Y.
visuals.caption: Definitions of M1 and M2

labels: Negotiable certificates of deposit issued by licensed banks held outside the banking sector
movements: M1 is contained within M2.
M2 adds savings and time deposits to the M1 components.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: X is customers' demand deposits and Y is customers' savings and time deposits with licensed banks, so option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: In the above diagram, the components X and Y are _____________ and _____________ respectively.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual banking multipliers
questions.stem: Study the following information about the banking system of a country. The public always hold $100 million in cash.

choices.text: If the public withdraw $50 million from the banking system, the excess reserves will immediately drop by $50 million.
If the banks lend out all their excess reserves, the money supply will increase by $200 million.

questions.explanation: Bank reserves are $500 million and deposits are $1,000 million. The actual reserve ratio is 50%, so the actual banking multiplier is 2. Required reserves are $400 million, a withdrawal cuts excess reserves by $30 million, and lending all excess reserves raises money supply by $250 million.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Refer to the following balance sheet of a banking system. Suppose the public always hold $50 million in cash and the required reserve is $250 million.
questions.explanation: The original required reserve ratio is 25%; after the cut it is 20%. With reserves of $400 million, deposits rise to $2,000 million and loans to $1,600 million, so both loans and money supply increase by $1,000 million. Monetary base is unchanged.
questions.postVisualStem:
If the required reserve ratio is lowered by 5 percentage points and the banks are fully loaned up, which of the following statements about the banking system are CORRECT?

(1) Loans will increase by $1,000 million.
(2) The money supply will increase by $1,000 million.
(3) The monetary base will decrease by $200 million.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the money supply and money demand curves of an economy. The initial equilibrium point is at E.
questions.explanation: A lower required reserve ratio increases money supply, shifting Ms0 right to Ms2. Higher income increases transaction demand for money, shifting Md0 right to Md2. Their new intersection is B.

visuals.alt: Money market diagram with supply curves Ms1, Ms0 and Ms2, demand curves Md1, Md0 and Md2, and points A to E.
visuals.caption: Money demand and supply

movements: A lower required reserve ratio shifts money supply right from Ms0 to Ms2.
Higher income shifts money demand right from Md0 to Md2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The new equilibrium is point B, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the central bank lowers the required reserve ratio, and at the same time, the income of the public rises. The new equilibrium point will be at _____________.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Josie is considering renting an industrial building unit to set up a studio for producing short films for her personal social media channel. Otherwise, she will make short films at home. Which of the following will lower Josie's cost of renting an industrial building unit to make short films?

(1) The landlord lowers the rent of the unit.
(2) The tenant next to the unit often makes noise, which affects the quality of Josie's short films.
(3) Due to a lack of soundproofing equipment, Josie is often disturbed by noise when making short films at home.
questions.explanation: Lower rent reduces the monetary cost. Noise at home reduces the value of the forgone alternative, while noise next door reduces the chosen option's benefit rather than its cost.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about Hong Kong International Airport are positive statements?

(1) The passenger volume of Hong Kong International Airport increased by 52.8% in the first half of 2024 compared with the same period the year before.
(2) Hong Kong International Airport should further expand to cope with higher passenger demand in the future.
(3) Hong Kong International Airport was voted 'Asia's Leading Airport 2023' in the 30th World Travel Awards.
(4) Hong Kong International Airport is more beautiful than Narita International Airport in Japan.
questions.explanation: Statements (1) and (3) can be checked against facts and do not contain value judgements. Statements (2) and (4) express value judgements.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem: On 4 August 2024, the Leisure and Cultural Services Department held 'Sport For All Day 2024', on which most leisure facilities under LCSD were opened for free use. The sessions for free use of facilities were allocated by drawing lots. The case is related to the ______ question(s) in economics.

choices.text: 'how to produce' and 'for whom to produce'
'what to produce' and 'for whom to produce'

questions.explanation: The case concerns who can use scarce facilities and how sessions are allocated. It does not change the types or quantities of facilities provided.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of buying shares and bonds from small investors’ point of view
questions.stem: Miss Chan is a small investor. Which of the following is a possible reason for her deciding to purchase shares instead of bonds of a listed company?

choices.text: If the company winds up, she can get repayment prior to bondholders.
If the company suffers a loss, she can still receive dividends.
The market price of shares may increase while that of bonds is fixed.
She may get higher returns compared to holding bonds if the company makes great profits.

questions.explanation: Shareholders rank behind bondholders on winding up and dividends are not guaranteed. Both shares and bonds can change market price, but shareholders may receive higher returns when profits are strong.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem: Mr Li runs a restaurant and provides free soft drinks to customers during lunchtime. These soft drinks provided for free are ______ because they ______.

choices.text: consumer goods ... are goods used for final consumption
free goods ... are free for all customers
private goods ... are non-rival in consumption

questions.explanation: The drinks are used in final consumption. They remain economic goods because scarce resources produce them, and private goods are rival and excludable.

questions.keyPoint: Describe the inter-relationship between the three types of production
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram.
questions.explanation: Primary production supplies raw materials to households, while tertiary production supplies services to secondary production.

visuals.alt: Production-flow diagram joining primary, secondary and tertiary production with households; X and Y label two flows.
visuals.caption: Inter-relationship among types of production

movements: X flows from primary production to households.
Y is the flow between secondary and tertiary production.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: X is raw materials and Y is services, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: X and Y stand for ______ and ______ respectively.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: Refer to the following table.
questions.explanation: Firm A produces 8 units per man-hour while Firm B produces 10. Less training and time-rate payment at A versus piece-rate payment at B can explain the difference; more machines at A would not.

visuals.caption: Firm A and Firm B
rows: Number of working hours per worker per day
Percentage of output with quality up to standard

questions.postVisualStem:
Based on the above information, which of the following are possible reasons for the difference in average labour productivity between firm A and firm B?

(1) Firm A uses more machines in the production process.
(2) Firm A’s workers receive less training than firm B’s workers.
(3) Firm A pays its workers hourly wages while firm B pays by piece rate.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The table below shows the production plan of a firm. The only two inputs required for production are labour and machines.
questions.explanation: Total product is 6, 16 and 35, so marginal product is 10 then 19. The sixth machine's marginal product must be below 19, so total product is below 54 and average product X is below 9.
questions.postVisualStem: If the above data illustrates the law of diminishing marginal returns, the value of X ____________.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Give possible motives behind each type of internal expansion
questions.stem: Matsuya, a Japanese beef rice restaurant chain, opened its first branch in Hong Kong in August 2024. Which of the following is the LEAST likely advantage of the expansion?

choices.text: ensuring a market outlet for its products

questions.explanation: A new branch can raise market share, permit more efficient resource use and create economies of scale. Ensuring an outlet for its products is not the usual advantage of expanding a restaurant branch.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a competitive firm.
questions.explanation: At output 3, marginal cost and price are $7. Total revenue is $21, total variable cost is $15 and total cost is $18, giving producer surplus $6 and profit $3.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the profit-maximising output level is 3 units and the fixed cost at 3 units is $3. The producer surplus of the firm is __________ while the profit is __________.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem: The Hong Kong Housing Authority sells newly constructed flats under the Home Ownership Scheme. Some eligible citizens are willing to pay the selling price but are unsuccessful in the lottery. The quantity supplied is ______, while selling price is ______.

choices.text: smaller than quantity demanded ... lower than equilibrium price
smaller than quantity demanded ... higher than equilibrium price
larger than quantity demanded ... lower than equilibrium price
larger than quantity demanded ... higher than equilibrium price

questions.explanation: Unsuccessful buyers willing to pay show excess demand. Quantity supplied is below quantity demanded and price is below equilibrium.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is the demand-supply diagram of Country A’s catering service market. E is the original equilibrium point.
questions.explanation: More foreign workers lower production cost and shift supply from S0 to S2. More tourists shift demand from D0 to D2, placing the new equilibrium at E4.

visuals.alt: Catering-service market with demand curves D0-D2, supply curves S0-S2, and equilibrium points E to E4.
visuals.caption: Catering-service market

movements: More foreign catering workers shift supply right from S0 to S2.
More tourists shift demand right from D0 to D2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The new equilibrium is E4, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government of Country A increases the quota for imported foreign workers in the catering industry. At the same time, a newly completed theme park in Country A attracts many tourists to visit Country A. The new equilibrium point will be at ________.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem: The demand for ______ can be regarded as a derived demand for ______.
questions.explanation: Physical therapists are inputs in providing physical therapy. The other pairs reverse derived demand or describe joint supply or joint demand.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem:
Suppose Country A sets an effective price floor on instant noodles, which are inferior goods. If citizens' income increases, which statements are CORRECT?

(1) Marginal benefit from the last unit remains unchanged.
(2) Excess supply increases.
(3) Total expenditure on instant noodles increases.
questions.explanation: Income growth reduces demand for an inferior good. At an effective floor, price and last-unit marginal benefit stay at the floor, while quantity traded falls and excess supply widens; total expenditure falls.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: When the per-unit subsidy granted to producers of good X is halved, total subsidy is also halved. Which is a possible explanation?

choices.text: The elasticity of demand for good X is 0.
The elasticity of demand for good X is 1.
The elasticity of supply of good X is 1.
The elasticity of supply of good X is infinity.

questions.explanation: Since total subsidy equals the per-unit subsidy times quantity traded, quantity must be unchanged. Perfectly inelastic demand can produce that result.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram for good X.
questions.explanation: Q3 is an ineffective quota. At the binding quota Q1, supply equals demand, price rises to P3 and total expenditure falls; there is no excess supply.

visuals.alt: Supply-demand diagram with quota limits Q1 and Q3, original equilibrium Q2 and prices P1-P3.
visuals.caption: Lowering an import quota

movements: A quota at Q3 is ineffective.
Lowering the quota to Q1 reduces quantity from Q2 to Q1 and raises price from P2 to P3.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Statements (2) and (3) are correct, so option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
If the government lowers the quota limit from Q3 to Q1,

(1) there will be an excess supply of good X and the amount is (Q3 - Q1).
(2) the market price of good X will increase from P2 to P3.
(3) consumers’ total expenditure on good X will decrease.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following market demand schedule of good X. The equilibrium price is $20.
questions.explanation: The tax reduces supply while the cheaper substitute reduces demand. Quantity falls below 40, so tax revenue is below $160, and marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost at the new equilibrium, creating deadweight loss.

visuals.caption: Market demand schedule of good X

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the government imposes a per-unit sales tax of $4 on good X. At the same time, the price of a substitute for good X decreases. As a result, the price of good X remains unchanged. Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?

(1) The government’s tax revenue from good X will be $160.
(2) The quantity transacted of good X will decrease.
(3) Imposing the per-unit sales tax will not cause any deadweight loss.

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem:
The market of air transport in Hong Kong is an oligopoly. Which statements are CORRECT?

(1) Airlines engage in non-price competition.
(2) Different airlines provide homogeneous services.
(3) A few airlines have significantly larger market shares than others.
(4) Airlines are interdependent in pricing strategies.
questions.explanation: Oligopolists sell differentiated services, compete beyond price, have a few large firms and are interdependent in decisions.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram for good X.
questions.explanation: The ceiling changes from ineffective to effective. Price and quantity traded fall, so producer surplus, social surplus and total revenue fall while deadweight loss rises.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram with a price ceiling lowered from P1 above equilibrium to P2 below equilibrium.
visuals.caption: A newly effective price ceiling

movements: P1 is ineffective above the equilibrium price.
P2 is an effective ceiling below equilibrium.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Producer surplus, total social surplus and total sales revenue fall; option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
If the government lowers the price ceiling from P1 to P2, the __________ will decrease.

(1) producer surplus
(2) total social surplus
(3) deadweight loss
(4) total sales revenue

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram for good X. Initially, the market for good X is at equilibrium.
questions.explanation: A sales tax and effective price ceiling reduce quantity below the efficient level, causing deadweight loss and reducing producer surplus. A quota has an uncertain producer-surplus effect, while a demand fall preserves marginal benefit equal to marginal cost.

visuals.alt: Supply-demand diagram initially at equilibrium price P and quantity Q.
visuals.caption: Initial competitive-market equilibrium

movements: The market starts where marginal benefit equals marginal cost.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: A sales tax and an effective price ceiling both reduce producer surplus and create deadweight loss, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following situations will reduce producer surplus and create a deadweight loss in the market of good X at the same time?

(1) the imposition of a per-unit sales tax on good X
(2) the imposition of an effective quota on good X
(3) the imposition of an effective price ceiling on good X
(4) a decrease in the demand for good X

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem: A shopping mall plans outdoor rooftop concerts, but nearby residents oppose the noise pollution. Which statement is CORRECT?

choices.text: Compensation to affected residents can narrow the divergence between private and social costs.
There is no divergence if the mall has the right to hold concerts.
A fine for excessive noise reduces under-production of music.

questions.explanation: Compensation internalises part of the external cost and moves output closer to the social optimum. It need not eliminate noise, and negative externality creates over-production, not under-production.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem:
Which changes raise Hong Kong's Gini coefficient based on post-tax, post-social-transfer monthly household income?

(1) cancelling rates concession
(2) increasing rent for public rental housing
(3) decreasing marginal salaries-tax rates
questions.explanation: Higher public-housing rent hurts lower-income households, and lower marginal salaries-tax rates help higher-income households. Cancelling a rates concession mainly reduces higher-income households' disposable income, narrowing inequality.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Lorenz curve
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the Lorenz curves of Country A and Country B.

choices.text: Country A likely has a regressive tax system while Country B likely has a progressive tax system.
Country A's GDP is lower than Country B's.
Low-income households in Country A have a lower living standard.
Country A's Gini coefficient is higher than Country B's.

questions.explanation: Country A's curve is farther from equality, giving it a larger Gini coefficient. A Lorenz curve does not reveal tax systems, GDP or absolute living standards.

visuals.alt: Lorenz curves for Country A (solid) and Country B (dashed), with Country A farther from perfect equality.
visuals.caption: Lorenz curves of two countries

movements: Country A's curve lies farther from the line of perfect equality than Country B's.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Country A has the higher Gini coefficient; the curves do not reveal GDP, tax systems or absolute living standards.

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, which of the following statements about the two countries is CORRECT?

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: Consider the following gross domestic product (GDP) data for Country A.
questions.postVisualStem: If Country A’s GDP at factor cost is $1,400 million, the value of X is ____________.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of per capita GDP
questions.stem: The following table shows some data for an economy in a certain year.

choices.text: Real GDP decreased in year 1 and increased in year 2.
Per capita nominal GDP decreased in year 1 and increased in year 2.
Per capita real GDP decreased in year 2.
The inflation rate increased in year 1 and decreased in year 2.

questions.explanation: Nominal GDP grew more slowly than the price level in year 1, so real GDP fell. In year 2 the price level fell while nominal GDP rose, so real GDP rose. The other conclusions conflict with the population data or lack a comparison with prior inflation.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the economy is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: Which of the following should be deducted from Hong Kong's gross domestic product to calculate its gross national income?

choices.text: The salary earned by a professor from Australia invited to work as a consultant at a university in Hong Kong for three months
The fee paid by a Japanese fencing club to a Hong Kong fencing team for an exhibition match in Japan
The dividend paid by a listed company in the United States to a Hong Kong resident
The fee paid by a Korean student to take a psychology course offered by a college in Hong Kong

questions.explanation: The Australian professor is a non-resident earning factor income within Hong Kong, so that income is deducted from GDP. The income in B and C is earned by residents abroad, and D is resident production in Hong Kong.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.stem: The diagram shows the short-run aggregate supply curve shifting left. Which is a possible reason?

choices.text: The government abolishes tax incentives for firms.
Firms expect the general price level to increase.
The price of raw materials decreases sharply.

questions.explanation: Expected price-level increases lead firms to reduce present supply, shifting SRAS left. The first and third choices reduce AD, while cheaper raw materials shift SRAS right.

visuals.alt: Short-run aggregate supply shifts left from SRAS0 to SRAS1.
visuals.caption: Decrease in short-run aggregate supply

movements: SRAS shifts left from SRAS0 to SRAS1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Firms expecting a higher general price level reduce present supply, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following is a possible reason for the above movement of the short run aggregate supply curve?

questions.keyPoint: Direct tax and indirect tax
questions.stem: Hong Kong will re-impose hotel accommodation tax at 3% from 1 January 2025. Which statement about the measure is CORRECT?

choices.text: The hotel accommodation tax is a direct tax.
The measure will lead to a fiscal surplus.
The measure follows Adam Smith's equality principle of taxation.
The measure will lead to a decrease in Hong Kong's aggregate demand.

questions.explanation: The hotel accommodation tax is an indirect tax. It raises the cost of visiting Hong Kong, lowers tourism and exports of services, and therefore lowers aggregate demand; higher revenue alone does not ensure a fiscal surplus.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Inflationary gap
questions.stem: An economy initially has an inflationary output gap. Which would widen the gap?

choices.text: The central bank prints more money.
The government raises the business registration fee.
Transport cost of raw materials increases.
A major trading partner experiences recession.

questions.explanation: More money lowers interest rates and raises consumption and investment, shifting AD right. The other changes reduce AD or SRAS and narrow the inflationary gap.

questions.keyPoint: Qualities of good money
questions.stem:
Compared with salt, 9999 gold is a better form of money because it is more ______.

(1) divisible
(2) scarce
(3) durable
questions.explanation: Gold is scarcer and more durable than salt. Salt is readily divisible, so divisibility is not an advantage of gold in this comparison.

questions.keyPoint: Definitions of M1, M2 and M3 in
questions.stem: Which transaction increases Hong Kong's money supply M2?

choices.text: Miss Li withdraws HK$10,000 from a time deposit at a licensed bank and holds cash.
Miss Wong deposits HK$500,000 cash into a time deposit at a restricted licence bank.
Mr Cheung transfers HK$10,000 from savings to current account in the same licensed bank.
Mr Chan withdraws HK$10,000 from a time deposit at a restricted licence bank to buy a negotiable certificate of deposit issued by a licensed bank.

questions.explanation: M2 includes M1, savings and time deposits at licensed banks, and licensed-bank NCDs held outside the banking sector. Option D moves $10,000 into M2; the other changes leave it unchanged or lower it.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate excess reserves, required and actual reserve ratios
questions.stem: Refer to the following balance sheet of a banking system. The required reserve ratio of the banking system is 25% and the public always hold $50 in cash.
questions.explanation: Reserves remain $500. Required reserves are 25% of $1,500, or $375, so excess reserves are $125. Money supply is $1,550 and monetary base is $550.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose some banks lend out their excess reserves. After deposit creation, the amount of deposits in the banking system is $1,500. Which of the following statements about the banking system is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual banking multipliers
questions.stem: Study the following information.
questions.explanation: Reserves are $80 million. Deposits are $320 million using actual banking multiplier 4; required reserves are $64 million, leaving $16 million excess reserves and $240 million loans. Money supply is $390 million.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate
questions.stem: Suppose the nominal interest rate is 5% and actual deflation is 1%. Which statement is CORRECT?

choices.text: The nominal rate of return on holding money is 1%.
The actual real interest rate is 4%.
The nominal interest rate is higher than the expected real interest rate.
The real rate of return on holding money is higher than the nominal rate of return on holding money.

questions.explanation: The nominal return on money is 0%, so deflation of 1% gives a real return of 1%. Actual real interest rate is 6%, while expected real interest cannot be found without expected inflation.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: Suppose the central bank continues to sell government bonds to the public. According to the classical quantity theory of money,

choices.text: the velocity of circulation of money will decrease.

questions.explanation: With MV = PY and constant velocity and real output, bond sales reduce money supply and thus price level, causing deflation.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: The following table shows some data for an economy.
questions.explanation: Labour force is 7,500,000 plus 400,000, or 7,900,000. The unemployment rate is 400,000 / 7,900,000 = 5.06%; underemployed people are already included among employed people.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above data,

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the relationship between taxable income and tax payment in a tax system.
questions.explanation: The upward-convex schedule is progressive and can reduce inequality. Taxable income is calculated after allowances and deductions, so the graph cannot establish whether an allowance is provided.

visuals.alt: Convex upward tax-payment curve against taxable income.
visuals.caption: Progressive income-tax schedule

movements: Tax payment rises more than proportionately as taxable income rises.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The tax is progressive and can make income distribution more even; taxable income does not reveal whether an allowance is used.

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the above tax system is/are CORRECT?

(1) It is a regressive tax.
(2) It will result in a more even income distribution.
(3) A tax allowance may be provided for the tax.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: Cyberattacks lead many citizens to stop using electronic payment tools. Which can offset the effects on output level and interest rate at the same time in the short run?

choices.text: More enterprises change from monthly payments to weekly payments.
The government increases the allowance for salaries tax.
The government issues more government bonds to the public.
The risk of stock-market investment increases.

questions.explanation: Stopping electronic payments raises transaction demand for money, interest rates and reduces output. More frequent wage payments lower transaction demand, reduce interest rates and raise consumption, investment and output.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem: If the government raises the standard rate of salaries tax, output level ______, and government revenue from salaries tax ______.

choices.text: will decrease ... may increase or decrease
may increase or decrease ... may increase or decrease
may increase or decrease ... will decrease

questions.explanation: Higher salaries tax lowers disposable income and AD, reducing output. Tax revenue is uncertain because the higher rate can be offset by lower taxable income and reduced work incentive.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Balance of payments and balance of the BOP account
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of balance of payment surplus and deficit
questions.stem: Which measure may increase aggregate output and the balance of payments surplus at the same time?

choices.text: cancelling tax incentives for foreign investors
holding more international competitions to attract tourists
importing more foreign raw materials to replace local production

questions.explanation: More tourism raises service exports, aggregate demand and output, while improving invisible trade and the balance of payments. The other measures worsen one or both outcomes.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money demand and money supply curves of an economy. The original equilibrium point is at E.
questions.explanation: A higher discount rate shifts money supply left to Ms1. Higher liquidity of other assets reduces asset demand for money, shifting money demand left to Md1. Their intersection is D.

visuals.alt: Money market with Ms0-Ms2, Md0-Md2 and equilibrium points A-D and E.
visuals.caption: Money market after two shifts

movements: A higher discount rate shifts money supply left from Ms0 to Ms1.
More liquid interest-bearing assets shift money demand left from Md0 to Md1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The new equilibrium is D, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government increases the discount rate and the liquidity of other interest-bearing assets increases. The new equilibrium point will be at __________.

questions.keyPoint: Calculate the gains from trade
questions.stem: The following table shows the number of man-hours required to produce clothing and toys in Country A and Country B.
questions.explanation: Country A exports clothing because its opportunity cost is 2 toys versus 5 in Country B. Trade gives 2.5 toys per clothing unit, so gain is 2.5 - 2 - 0.1 = 0.4 toys per unit, or 1.6 for four units.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the clothing-exporting country exports 4 units of clothing in exchange for 10 units of toys. At the same time, the clothing-exporting country needs to pay 0.1 units of toys per unit of export as transportation cost. What is the total gain from trade for the clothing-exporting country?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of a quota on domestic price, domestic consumption, domestic production and import quantity for a small open economy
questions.stem: The diagram shows an import quota in a small open economy.
questions.postVisualStem: If the world price of the good decreases,

choices.text: domestic price will be lower than P1
import volume will be smaller than Q3 - Q2
revenue of domestic producers will remain unchanged
total import value will be P1 x (Q3 - Q2)

questions.explanation: The quota remains binding, fixing domestic price at P1 and imports at Q3 minus Q2. Domestic output and producers' revenue therefore remain unchanged, while lower world price lowers import value.

visuals.alt: Small-open-economy import quota diagram with world price Pw, domestic price P1 and quantities Q1-Q4.
visuals.caption: Binding import quota

movements: The quota fixes imports at Q3 minus Q2.
A lower world price does not change domestic price, domestic output or quota-limited import volume.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Domestic producers' revenue remains unchanged, so option C is correct.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Balance of payments and balance of the BOP account
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of balance of payment surplus and deficit
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about the balance of payments of an economy in a certain year.
questions.explanation: Current account is 230 + 170 + (40 - 20) + (20 - 25) = $415 million surplus. Reserve assets falling by $50 million shows a BOP deficit; positive net factor income means GNI exceeds GDP.
questions.postVisualStem:
Based on the above information, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The current account surplus is $415 million.
(2) The economy’s gross domestic product (GDP) is higher than its gross national income (GNI).
(3) The balance of payments deficit is $50 million.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: The following table shows the change in the exchange rate between the Hong Kong dollar (HKD) and the Japanese yen (JPY).

choices.text: a decrease in Hong Kong tourists to Japan
a decrease in total value of Japanese goods exported to Hong Kong in HKD
an increase in competitiveness of Hong Kong goods exported to Japan
a decrease in total value of Hong Kong goods exported to Japan in HKD

questions.explanation: HKD appreciates against JPY. Hong Kong exports become more expensive to Japanese buyers, reducing export quantity and total value in HKD. Japanese imports become cheaper in HKD, while their total value is elasticity-dependent.
questions.postVisualStem: Under the linked exchange rate system, the above change in the exchange rate will lead to

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Miss Wong owns a commercial property which is worth $20,000,000. She is considering selling the property and depositing the $20,000,000 in a bank at an annual interest rate of 4%. She can also rent out the property at $60,000 a month.

Under which of the following situations will Miss Wong's opportunity cost of renting out the property increase?

(1) The government announces plans to build a railway station near the property, making transportation in the area more convenient in the future.
(2) The annual interest rate on deposits is adjusted to 5%.
(3) The rental value of Miss Wong's commercial property increases.
questions.explanation: The opportunity cost is the value of selling the property. A future railway station raises its sale value, and a higher deposit rate raises the interest obtainable after sale. A higher rental value changes the benefit of renting, not its opportunity cost.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Zoe is thinking about her career plan. Her order of preference is: first, to work as an intern at a restaurant in Japan; second, to work at a local bank; and third, to work in Australia for one year through the Working Holiday Scheme.

Which of the following factors would affect Zoe's cost-benefit analysis for her choice?

(1) The restaurant provides free meals to Zoe.
(2) The bank increases the wage level of new employees.
(3) Finding a job in Australia is more difficult than expected.
questions.explanation: Zoe chooses the first option because its benefit exceeds the value of the next-best option. Free meals raise the first option's benefit and a higher bank wage raises its cost. A change to the third option affects neither.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem:
Which of the following situations imply the existence of scarcity?

(1) Interest exists.
(2) Goods have market prices.
(3) People compete to get what they want.
questions.explanation: Interest reflects scarce resources having alternative uses. Market prices and competition also arise because available economic goods are insufficient to satisfy all wants.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem: Compared with a market economy, in a planned economy,
questions.explanation: A planned economy relies more on public ownership and central allocation. The other statements do not necessarily follow from the type of economic system.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meaning of private property rights and its importance in a market economy
questions.stem:
When private property rights are not well defined,

(1) market transactions may not occur.
(2) non-price competition is more likely to arise than when private property rights are well defined.
(3) resources are more likely to be allocated to their highest-valued use than when private property rights are well defined.
questions.explanation: Without clear rights, exchange may be impossible and rationing by queues or other non-price means becomes more likely. Resources are less, not more, likely to move to their highest-valued use.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
Mr. Chan and Ms. Wong jointly own a firm. The firm cannot issue shares and bonds to the public.

Which of the following statements about the firm is CORRECT?

choices.text: The profits tax rate paid by the firm is lower than that of a limited company.
The upper limit on the number of owners of the firm is 50.
The firm cannot own assets under its name.
Mr. Chan cannot freely transfer his ownership of the firm.

questions.explanation: The firm may be a partnership or a private limited company, so transfer of ownership requires other owners' consent. The other statements are not true for both possible forms.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about two firms in Hong Kong.
questions.explanation: Firm A is public and Firm B is private, but both are limited companies. They face the same profits-tax rate, both can issue shares and bonds, and both have lasting continuity.

visuals.caption: Two Hong Kong firms
rows: Disclosure of accounting information to the public

questions.postVisualStem:
Based on the above information, which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?

(1) When the two firms have the same amount of profit, they are subject to the same profits tax rate.
(2) Firm A can issue shares and bonds while firm B cannot.
(3) Firm A has better continuity than firm B.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
