questions.stem: Some shopping malls provide people with free shuttle bus service between railway stations and the shopping mall. The free shuttle bus service is a __________ because __________.

choices.text: free good ... people do not need to pay for the service
capital good ... people prefer more of the service
private good ... concurrent consumption of a seat is not possible
consumer good ... it is used for final consumption

questions.explanation: The service is scarce even when riders do not pay. Seats cannot be consumed concurrently, so it is a private good. It is a capital good because it helps produce other services, not simply because people prefer it.

questions.keyPoint: Definition of free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about economic goods is CORRECT?

choices.text: An economic good may not have a market price.
The demand for an economic good is greater than its supply.
People prefer economic goods to free goods.
Economic goods are produced by people using scarce resources.

questions.explanation: An economic good can lack a market price. Scarcity does not mean demand always exceeds supply, and economic goods can include natural resources that are not produced by people.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem:
The Hong Kong SAR Government announced that it would expand the list of eligible universities under the Top Talent Pass Scheme and extend the validity period of the first visas from two years to three years to attract more talent to come to Hong Kong for development.

The above measure will lead to

(1) an increase in the geographical mobility of labour in Hong Kong.
(2) an increase in Hong Kong's average labour productivity.
(3) an increase in Hong Kong's labour supply.
questions.explanation: The scheme can add talent to Hong Kong, increasing labour supply and average productivity. It changes the mobility of people coming to Hong Kong, rather than the geographical mobility of Hong Kong workers.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: The following table shows the input-output relationship of firm A and firm B.

choices.text: Firm A practises a higher degree of division of labour.
Firm A adopts piece rate while firm B adopts time rate.
The management of firm B is better.
The working environment of firm B is worse than firm A.

questions.explanation: Firm A produces 10 units per man-hour while Firm B produces 15. Better management in Firm B can explain this. More division of labour or piece rate at A would tend to raise A's productivity, and a worse environment at B would lower B's.

visuals.caption: Input-output relationship
rows: Number of working hours per worker per day

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following is a possible reason for the difference in labour productivity between firm A and firm B?

questions.keyPoint: Variable costs and fixed costs
questions.stem:
Which of the following are variable costs involved in extending the opening hours of a fast food shop?

(1) business registration fee
(2) rates
(3) expenditure on ingredients
(4) electricity fee
questions.explanation: Extra opening hours require more ingredients and electricity. Business registration fees and rates do not vary with the additional hours, so they are fixed costs here.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The following table shows the relationship among input, output and cost for a firm.

choices.text: The law of diminishing marginal returns applies to the firm.
The firm enjoys economies of scale.
The optimal scale of production is 24 units.
When the quantity of labour is 2 units, the average output of labour is the highest.

questions.explanation: With machinery fixed at five units, marginal product falls from 10 to 9 when labour rises from two to three units. This shows diminishing marginal returns. The highest average product is 8 at three or four units, and economies of scale concern the long run.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the firm is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: Mr. Lee runs a travel agency that specialises in organising local tours. Which of the following will raise its profit-maximising output?

choices.text: The rental for the premises of the travel agency decreases.
The basic hourly wage of tour guides increases.
More tourists prefer to travel by themselves instead of joining local tours.
Some travel agencies that used to organise local tours close their businesses.

questions.explanation: When rival agencies close, market supply falls and the market price and marginal revenue rise, increasing profit-maximising output. Lower rent is a fixed-cost change, while the other two changes lower the firm's desired output.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning and give examples of each type of integration
questions.stem:
A Hong Kong chain fashion store acquired an Indonesian garment factory.

Which of the following is the LEAST likely motive for the above acquisition?

choices.text: to ensure a reliable supply of input
to develop sales channels for its products

questions.explanation: The chain store has expanded vertically backward into an earlier stage of production. That can secure inputs or offer scale benefits, but it does not develop downstream sales channels.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about shortage and scarcity is CORRECT?

choices.text: The existence of shortage implies the existence of scarcity.
The existence of scarcity implies the existence of shortage.
There may also be shortage for a free good.
Adjusting the market price can eliminate shortage and scarcity.

questions.explanation: A shortage can occur only for a scarce good. Scarcity is permanent while shortage depends on a price being below equilibrium, so a price adjustment can remove shortage but not scarcity.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem:
Country A is an importing country of electronic products. As the price of oil drops, the transportation cost for electronic products decreases. Which of the following is/are effect(s) of the above event?

(1) The sales volume of electronic products will increase.
(2) The average quality of electronic products sold in the market will decrease.
(3) The proportion of high-end electronic products sold in the market will increase.
questions.explanation: Lower transport cost lowers the full price of electronic products and raises sales. Because high-end products usually have a higher money price, their relative price rises against ordinary products, reducing their share and the market's average quality.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is a demand-supply diagram for the residential rental market. The original equilibrium point is E0.
questions.explanation: Reducing the deduction lowers demand from D0 to D2, while the completed properties raise supply from S0 to S1. The new equilibrium is E2.

visuals.alt: Residential-rental market with demand curves D0 to D2, supply curves S0 to S2, and equilibrium points E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Residential rental market

movements: Reducing the rental-expense tax deduction shifts demand from D0 to D2.
Completion of private homes shifts supply from S0 to S1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The new equilibrium is E2, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government reduces the tax deduction for domestic rental expenses. At the same time, many private residential properties have been completed. The new equilibrium point will be ________.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem: Suppose the government of Country A simplifies the procedures for foreign tourists to apply for tourist visas. At the same time, more graduates expect the average wage in the hotel industry to increase. Which of the following diagrams can best describe the effect of the above events?
questions.explanation: Simpler visa procedures raise demand for hotel services and therefore derived demand for hotel staff. Expected higher pay raises the supply of hotel staff. Only Diagram D shows both shifts.

visuals.alt: Four option diagrams for the hotel-services and hotel-staff markets in Country A.
visuals.caption: Hotel-market diagram options

movements: Simpler tourist visas increase demand for hotel services and derived demand for hotel staff.
Graduates expecting higher hotel wages increase the supply of hotel staff.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Only diagram D shows both the rightward demand shift for hotel staff and the rightward supply shift, so option D is correct.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem:
An increase in the price of ______________ will lead to an increase in the price of ______________.

(1) fitness centre membership ... home fitness equipment
(2) beef ... leather
(3) milk ... ice cream
questions.explanation: Fitness memberships and home equipment are substitutes, so a membership-price rise raises the demand and price of home equipment. Milk is an input for ice cream, so its higher price raises ice-cream cost and price. Beef and leather are jointly supplied, so dearer beef increases leather supply and lowers its price.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: As the supply of raw materials for producing sports shoes is suspended, the price of sports shoes has increased by 10% and the quantity transacted has changed by 20%. Which of the following best explains the above changes in the price and quantity transacted of sports shoes?

choices.text: Sports shoes are necessities for consumers.
Sports shoes manufacturers have spare production capacity.
Equipment for producing sports shoes is not readily available.

questions.explanation: The supply fall raises price and lowers quantity. Quantity changes by a larger percentage than price, so demand is elastic. Highly durable shoes let consumers postpone replacement, making their demand relatively elastic.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the tax burden
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X.
questions.explanation: The original equilibrium is $4 and 50 units. With tax, buyers pay $5 and 40 units are sold; sellers receive $2. Consumers bear $40 and producers $80, so demand is more elastic. Tax revenue is $120 and sellers' net revenue is $80.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the government imposes a per-unit sales tax of $3 on each unit of good X sold. Which of the following statements about good X are CORRECT?

(1) The demand for good X is more elastic than its supply.
(2) Sellers' revenue net of tax is $200.
(3) Total tax revenue is $120.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of a quota on domestic price, domestic consumption, domestic production and import quantity for a small open economy
questions.stem: The government of Country A imposes a quota limit on imported textiles to protect the local textile industry. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The total wage earnings of workers in the local textile industry will increase.
Country A's demand for imported textiles will decrease.
The supply of textiles in Country A will increase.
If the demand for imported textiles is inelastic, consumers' expenditure on imported textiles will decrease.

questions.explanation: Imported and local textiles are substitutes. The quota raises the imported textile price, raising demand for local textiles and derived demand for local textile workers. The quota changes quantity demanded, not demand, and inelastic demand could raise total expenditure.

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a common feature of monopolistic competition and oligopoly?

choices.text: The firms can adjust their prices to maximise profits.
The firms are interdependent in their pricing strategies.
The firms may engage in non-price competition.
Neither buyers nor sellers have perfect market information.

questions.explanation: Pricing interdependence distinguishes oligopoly; it is not a general feature of monopolistic competition. The other statements can apply to both market structures.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Allocative function
questions.stem:
As more people prefer fresh food, firms shut down canned food production lines and switched to producing fresh food.

The above case illustrates the __________ function of price because __________.

choices.text: allocative ... profits from producing fresh food are higher
allocative ... more resources are used to produce fresh food
rationing ... the supply of fresh food will increase as prices increase
rationing ... fresh food is distributed to the highest-valued users

questions.explanation: Higher demand and price for fresh food direct resources from canned food to fresh-food production. This is the allocative function of price.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram.
questions.explanation: The effective floor raises price and reduces quantity sold. Above the demand midpoint, demand is elastic, so the percentage fall in quantity exceeds the percentage rise in price and producers' total revenue falls. Consumer surplus also falls.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram with midpoint M on demand curve D at equilibrium price P0 and quantity Q0.
visuals.caption: Price floor above the demand midpoint

movements: An effective price floor is above P0.
Quantity transacted falls along the elastic portion of demand.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Producer total revenue and consumer surplus both decrease, so option C is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Point M is the mid-point of the demand curve. When the government imposes an effective price floor on the good, the total revenue of producers will __________ and consumer surplus will __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Effect of a change in price/demand/supply on consumer surplus
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the demand-supply diagram for good X. Initially, the market for good X is in equilibrium.
questions.explanation: A parallel rightward demand shift increases consumer surplus, producer surplus and equilibrium price. Since the marginal cost of the final unit equals its price, marginal cost rises too.

visuals.alt: Initial demand-supply equilibrium for good X at P0 and Q0.
visuals.caption: Initial market equilibrium

movements: Demand shifts right in parallel.
Equilibrium price, quantity, consumer surplus and producer surplus rise.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: All three statements are correct, so option D is correct.

answerVisuals.alt: Marking-scheme diagram with demand shifting right from D0 to D1 and areas a to e.
answerVisuals.caption: Demand increase: surplus changes

movements: Demand shifts right from D0 to D1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Use the official areas a to e to identify the stated surplus change.

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the demand for good X increases. Which of the following statements are CORRECT? (Assume the demand curve for good X shifts parallel.)

(1) The consumer surplus in the market of good X will increase.
(2) The producer surplus in the market of good X will increase.
(3) The marginal cost of producing the last unit of good X will increase.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: After the completion of a large private housing estate, the number of diners at restaurants in the nearby shopping malls has significantly increased. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The developer of the housing estate should charge these restaurants to improve efficiency.
The diners that the housing estate brings to these restaurants is an external benefit to the developer of the housing estate.
If these restaurants pay the developer of the housing estate, there will be no divergence between private and social benefits.
If these restaurants are owned by the developer of the housing estate, there will be no divergence between private and social benefits.

questions.explanation: More diners are an external benefit to independent restaurants, not the developer. If the developer owns the restaurants, that benefit becomes private and there is no divergence between private and social benefits.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Lorenz curve
questions.stem: The diagram below shows

choices.text: Between 2021 and 2023, the tax system changed from progressive to regressive.
The government raised the standard tax rate of the salaries tax between 2021 and 2023.
The government reduced the transfer payments to the poor between 2021 and 2023.
Between 2021 and 2023, the percentage increase in post-tax post-social transfer income of low-income households was lower than that of high-income households.

questions.explanation: The 2023 Lorenz curve is closer to perfect equality, so inequality improved. A higher standard salaries-tax rate can reduce high-income households' post-tax income while leaving low-income households' income unchanged. The other changes would worsen inequality.

visuals.alt: Lorenz curves for Country A in 2021 and 2023, both based on post-tax post-social-transfer household income.
visuals.caption: Lorenz curves after tax and transfers

labels: Cumulative percentage of post-tax post-social transfer household income
movements: The 2023 Lorenz curve is closer to the line of perfect equality than the 2021 curve.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: A higher standard salaries-tax rate can lower high-income households' post-tax income and explain the improvement, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem:
Lorenz curves for Country A, constructed based on post-tax post-social transfer household income.

Which of the following can best explain the above change in the Lorenz curve?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem:
Which of the following government policies are likely to make income distribution more even and at the same time increase the number of people being employed in the economy?

(1) subsiding employers to hire people with disabilities
(2) reducing the basic allowance for the salaries tax
(3) increasing the amount of unemployment benefits
(4) increasing the subsidies provided to citizens for public transportation expenses
questions.explanation: Hiring subsidies can raise employment and incomes of people with disabilities. Public-transport subsidies are a larger share of low income and can widen job access. A lower tax allowance and higher unemployment benefits can reduce incentives to work.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem: Irene planned to visit Tokyo in Japan for a week. Before departing, she was informed that a typhoon was likely to hit Tokyo during the planned trip. She considered cancelling the trip. The opportunity cost for Irene to continue going to Tokyo would _____________ because _____________.

choices.text: remain unchanged ... air ticket expenses could not be recovered
remain unchanged ... this would only decrease the value of her trip to Tokyo
decrease ... many tourist attractions in the city would close during the typhoon
increase ... there was a higher chance of her getting injured during the trip

questions.explanation: Going during the typhoon makes injury and possible medical expenses more likely. This raises the value of the best forgone alternative and therefore the opportunity cost of continuing the trip.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of interest
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about interest are CORRECT?

(1) Interest exists in a barter economy.
(2) If the price level remains unchanged, interest will not exist.
(3) When the interest rate increases, people will reduce their current consumption.
(4) Interest is the cost paid by the lender for deferring consumption.
questions.explanation: Interest can exist in a barter economy and a higher rate rewards postponing current consumption. It is unrelated to whether the price level changes, and it is compensation received by the lender, not a cost paid by the lender.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about a market economy is CORRECT?

choices.text: This economy mainly uses the price mechanism to tackle the three basic economic problems in economics.
Income is less evenly distributed than in a command economy.
People have private property rights over all resources.

questions.explanation: A market economy mainly allocates resources and goods through market prices. It does not guarantee a particular income distribution, it can have non-price competition, and private property rights do not cover every resource.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Mr. Cheung is an owner of a firm. All owners enjoy limited liability, but they cannot transfer their ownership without the consent of other owners. Which of the following statements about the firm is CORRECT?

choices.text: The firm can issue shares to the public to raise capital to expand its business.
The firm is required to disclose its financial information to the public.
There is no upper limit on the number of owners.
The firm can sue other firms in the name of the firm.

questions.explanation: The features describe a private limited company. It is a legal entity and can sue in its own name, but cannot issue shares to the public and has a limit on the number of owners.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about private goods is CORRECT?

choices.text: When someone consumes a private good, the amount available to others must be reduced.
The price of a private good must be greater than zero.
An apple is a private good because the cost of producing an additional unit of apples is greater than zero.
Private goods are goods provided by private enterprises.

questions.explanation: Private goods are rival in consumption, so one person's consumption reduces what is available to others. They can be free, are defined by rivalry and excludability rather than marginal cost, and can be supplied by the government or individuals.

the overall employment rate remained unchanged.
the relative importance of tertiary production in terms of employment decreased.
the contribution of tertiary production to gross domestic product (GDP) decreased.

questions.explanation: The tertiary share of employment fell from 79% to 75%. The table gives no information about total employment, the employment rate, or GDP contribution.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following people has the highest occupational mobility?
questions.explanation: A clerk generally requires the least specialised training or licensing among the choices, so changing occupation has the lowest cost and occupational mobility is highest.

questions.keyPoint: Supply of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following will reduce the labour supply in Country A?

choices.text: The number of public holidays is reduced.
The government has enacted legislation requiring companies to pay overtime to employees who work extra hours.
The government provides tuition subsidies for university graduates enrolled in full-time master's programmes.
Other countries tighten immigration applications for Country A's residents.

questions.explanation: Tuition subsidies encourage graduates to take full-time master's programmes instead of looking for full-time jobs, reducing labour supply. The other changes increase work incentives or reduce emigration.

questions.keyPoint: External economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem:
Refer to the following excerpt from a news report about 'The Chief Executive's 2024 Policy Address'.

In the 2024 Policy Address, the Chief Executive noted that Hong Kong ranks among the largest markets in the world for gold import and export by volume, attracting international demand for physical gold storage. To further support this development, the government plans to promote the establishment of world-class gold storage facilities, providing physical gold storage and delivery for users and investors while driving demand for related financial services such as collateral and borrowing.

Based on the above information, when the government builds gold storage facilities, gold traders in Hong Kong will

choices.text: suffer from internal diseconomies of scale.
suffer from external diseconomies of scale.

questions.explanation: The facilities develop related industries and services for gold traders. The resulting fall in traders' average production cost comes from industry development, so it is an external economy of scale.

questions.explanation: At $10, the firm produces 5 units. At $8, it produces 3; total revenue falls by $26 and variable cost falls by $19, so profit falls by $7. The first two marginal costs are unknown, and fixed cost does not affect producer surplus.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: Which of the following is INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

choices.text: When the government abolishes the airport departure tax charged to each passenger, the average flight distance for departing travellers decreases.
When the government imposes an ad valorem sales tax on each bottle of wine, the quantity of high-quality wine sold decreases.
When the transportation cost per kilogram of goods increases by 10% due to an increase in fuel price, the average quality of imported white rice people purchased decreases.
The price and quantity transacted of air conditioners increase during the summer.

questions.explanation: Equal per-kilogram transport-cost increases lower the relative price of high-quality rice, so buyers should buy relatively more high-quality rice and average quality should increase. The other observations can be explained consistently with the law of demand.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem:
Anson and Joey watched the same movie in different cinemas. Later, Anson found that Joey paid a lower ticket price. Which of the following are possible reasons for such a price difference?

(1) The location of the cinema Anson went to is more convenient.
(2) The cinema Anson visited has better sound equipment.
(3) Joey watched the movie in the morning, while Anson watched the movie in the evening.
questions.explanation: A more convenient location and better sound equipment add value to the cinema service, while peak-evening demand can justify a higher price. Each can explain the price difference.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: Which of the following would most likely cause an increase in total expenditure on air services?

choices.text: The government reduces the basic allowance for the salaries tax and air services are normal goods.
The fare for cross-border trains increases.

questions.explanation: Cross-border train services and air services are substitutes. A higher train fare increases air-service demand, raising both price and quantity transacted, so total expenditure increases.

questions.stem: In which of the following situations will the government imposing a per-unit tax on the producers of a good not affect the producers' total revenue net of tax?
questions.explanation: With perfectly inelastic demand, a per-unit tax raises the price paid by buyers by the tax amount while quantity and the price received by producers stay unchanged. Producers' total revenue net of tax is therefore unchanged.

questions.keyPoint: Give examples of monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about a perfectly competitive market are CORRECT?

(1) The market price will not change.
(2) The market price is equal to the firms' marginal revenue.
(3) There is no price competition in the market.
(4) There is no non-price competition in the market.
questions.explanation: A price-taking firm's marginal revenue equals market price, and homogeneous products with perfect information eliminate non-price competition. Market price can change with market demand or supply, and price remains the competitive criterion.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Negative externality and economic inefficiency; internalising external costs
questions.stem:
Refer to the following news excerpt.

A factory in Country A has been found discharging sewage into a river, causing the death of a large number of fish in the downstream area. This is not only destroying the local ecological environment but also seriously affecting the livelihood of fishermen.

Based on the above information, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) If the government imposes fines on the factory that discharges sewage, the divergence between private cost and social cost may decrease.
(2) If the government prohibits the factory from discharging any sewage into the river, the total social surplus will increase.
(3) If the factory provides compensation to the fishermen in the downstream area, deadweight loss may decrease.
questions.explanation: A fine raises marginal private cost and compensation can internalise part of the external cost, both reducing inefficiency. A complete ban can reduce total social surplus if the efficient amount of discharge is positive.

questions.explanation: Higher profits can let financial-services firms bid for more productive workers, unions can raise negotiated wages, and supervisory staff normally have more human capital. All three can explain the wage differences.

(2) Workers in the financial services sector are protected by labour unions, while those in the construction sector are not.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Gini coefficient
questions.stem: Which of the following will lower the Gini coefficient based on post-tax post-social transfer monthly household income in Hong Kong?

choices.text: increasing the per-unit tax levied on each cigarette
lowering the maximum income limit for receiving Comprehensive Social Security Assistance (CSSA)
raising the minimum age for receiving Old Age Living Allowance from 65 to 75 years old
increasing the amount of the personal disability allowance of the salaries tax

questions.explanation: People with disabilities generally have lower original income. A larger disability allowance lowers their tax payment and raises their post-tax income, making income distribution more even. The other measures can reduce support for lower-income groups or impose a regressive tax.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising opportunities
questions.stem: In November 2024, the Macao SAR Government announced that it would implement the Wealth Partaking Scheme again the next year and distribute MOP 10,000 to each Macao permanent resident. Which of the following statements about the above scheme is CORRECT?

choices.text: Since all Macao permanent residents receive the same amount of money, it will not help reduce income inequality.
It will not help equalise opportunity.
It will increase Macao residents' demand for all goods.
The amount distributed will be included in the calculation of government consumption expenditure of Macao.

questions.explanation: A uniform cash transfer does not give poorer people more resources to improve future productivity or earning ability, so it does not equalise opportunity. It can reduce income inequality, lowers demand for inferior goods, and is a transfer payment rather than government consumption.

questions.stem: The per capita nominal GDP of Country A is higher than that of Country B, but people's general living standard is lower than in Country B. Which of the following is a possible reason?

choices.text: Country A has a larger population than Country B.
The Gini coefficient of Country A is lower than that of Country B.
Country A has more unreported production activities than Country B.
Consumer goods constitute a smaller proportion of Country A's GDP compared to Country B.

questions.explanation: A smaller consumer-goods share means Country A's per capita GDP overstates the part of production that contributes directly to current living standards. Population is already accounted for, a lower Gini coefficient implies more even distribution, and more unreported activity would make measured GDP understate living standards.

questions.stem: Suppose a typhoon hits a country and disrupts the supply of raw materials. Which of the following can offset its effect on the purchasing power of the country's currency in the short run?

choices.text: Banks tend not to lend out excess reserves.
Firms expect the price level to increase.
More people go to work overseas.

questions.explanation: The typhoon lowers SRAS and raises the price level, lowering purchasing power. If banks do not lend excess reserves, money supply and AD fall, which puts downward pressure on the price level and offsets the effect.

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: Which of the following is/are the difference(s) between a progressive tax and a regressive tax?

choices.text: When taxable income increases, the tax payment will increase under a progressive tax, while the tax payment will decrease under a regressive tax.
A progressive tax is in line with the equity principle of taxation put forward by Adam Smith, while a regressive tax is not.
A progressive salaries tax system can make income distribution more even, while a regressive salaries tax system cannot.

questions.explanation: Progressive tax raises the average tax rate as income rises and can make distribution more even; regressive tax lowers the average tax rate and makes it more uneven. A regressive tax payment itself may increase, decrease, or stay unchanged, and Adam Smith's equity principle is satisfied by proportional tax.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem: Suppose a deflationary (output) gap exists in an economy. Which of the following is a fiscal policy that would help the economy restore to its long run equilibrium?

choices.text: exempting the first $5 million of an enterprise's profits from profits tax
having the central bank purchase government bonds from the public
increasing the standard rate of the salaries tax

questions.explanation: The profits-tax exemption encourages investment and shifts AD right, helping close a deflationary gap. Bond purchases are monetary policy, while the other taxes reduce AD or SRAS.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem:
Which of the following will reduce the effectiveness of an expansionary monetary policy on real output?

(1) The public's willingness to deposit cash obtained from loans into the banking system decreases.
(2) Companies tend to issue bonds rather than borrow from banks to raise capital.
(3) Commercial banks are more willing and able to lend out their excess reserves.
questions.explanation: Holding loan proceeds as cash and firms borrowing less from banks both reduce deposit creation, weakening the effect on real output. Banks being more willing and able to lend increases deposit creation instead.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels

questions.stem: In which of the following situations may the fiscal balance and the trade balance be improved at the same time?

choices.text: The government chooses to buy more locally produced goods rather than imported goods.
The central bank lowers the discount rate.
The government increases the business registration fee.
The government reduces the unemployment benefits.

questions.explanation: Lower unemployment benefits reduce government expenditure and improve the fiscal balance. They reduce unemployed people's disposable income and hence consumption of imports, improving the trade balance.

choices.text: the domestic price of wheat will remain unchanged.
the total revenue of domestic producers of wheat will increase.
the international price of wheat will increase.

questions.explanation: With a binding quota, higher demand raises domestic price and domestic production, increasing local producers' revenue. The small economy cannot affect world price and imports remain fixed at the quota.

visuals.alt: Small-open-economy wheat market with world price Pw and quota-limited imports Q2 minus Q1.
visuals.caption: Import quota in a small open economy

movements: Higher demand raises the domestic price while the quota fixes import volume.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Domestic output and producer revenue rise; world price and quota-limited imports do not change.

questions.postVisualStem:
Pw is the international price of wheat and the import quota imposed by the government is (Q2 - Q1) units. If the

demand for wheat increases,

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of current account surplus and deficit
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the percentage changes in the total value of exported goods and the total value of imported goods in an economy. The economy recorded a trade surplus in 2021.

choices.text: total value of goods exported decreased.

questions.explanation: Export values grow faster than import values in every year. Given the initial trade surplus, the surplus increases. The diagram does not provide the service, income, or transfer data needed for invisible-trade or current-account balances.

visuals.alt: Line chart showing year-on-year percentage changes in total values of exported and imported goods from 2021 to 2024.
visuals.caption: Export and import value changes

labels: Year-on-year percentage change in total value of exported goods
Year-on-year percentage change in total value of imported goods
movements: Export-value growth exceeds import-value growth in each year.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Given the initial trade surplus, the surplus increases.

questions.postVisualStem: According to the above diagram, from 2021 to 2024, the economy's

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on imports and exports
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in the exchange rate on import and export prices in terms of domestic and foreign currencies, import and export volumes, and values of imports and exports in terms of domestic and foreign currencies
questions.stem: The following table shows the change in the exchange rate between the Canadian dollar (CAD) and Hong Kong dollar (HKD).
questions.explanation: After the first 1% fee, he receives about CAD 17,491. After converting back at CAD 1 = HKD 5.58 and paying the second fee, he receives about HKD 96,624, a loss of about HKD 3,375.
questions.postVisualStem: On 31 October 2023, Mr. Cheung exchanged HKD 100,000 for Canadian dollars. Later, he exchanged the amount back to Hong Kong dollars on 31 October 2024. Suppose Mr. Cheung needs to pay 1% of the transaction amount as a handling fee for each transaction. From the above transactions, Mr. Cheung ______________.

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of scarcity
questions.stem:
The existence of scarcity implies that

(1) human desires are unlimited.
(2) there is price competition.
(3) some people's wants are not satisfied.
questions.explanation: Scarcity means available resources are insufficient to satisfy all wants, so some wants are not satisfied. It is possible for wants to be limited, and competition need not take the form of price competition.

questions.keyPoint: Explain why past expenditure which is irrecoverable is not a cost
questions.stem: Lyndon is considering what career to pursue after graduating from university. He is considering becoming a fencing coach or a civil servant. Which of the following would be the LEAST important factor for Lyndon in choosing whether to become a fencing coach or a civil servant?

choices.text: The government increases benefits for civil servants.
Many schools are establishing fencing teams and hiring fencing coaches.
The income of a fencing coach is lower than Lyndon expected.
Lyndon had already obtained the qualification of a fencing coach when he was in university.

questions.explanation: The resources spent obtaining the fencing-coach qualification are past, irrecoverable expenditure. They are sunk costs and do not affect Lyndon's current choice.

questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem: Mr. Wong plans to purchase an exercise bike from a second-hand trading website. Which of the following situations would increase his cost of purchasing the exercise bike?

choices.text: Mr. Wong needs to pay an additional transportation fee to have the exercise bike delivered to his home.
Mr. Wong finds that the usage experience of the exercise bike is not as good as expected after purchasing it.
Mr. Wong gets injured while using the exercise bike.
Mr. Wong finds that the exercise bike is damaged after purchasing it and needs to pay extra repair fees before he can use it.

questions.explanation: The extra delivery charge is a monetary cost of purchasing the bike. The other cases affect the value of, or cost of using, the bike after it has been purchased.

questions.keyPoint: Use of the circular flow model to explain why GDP can be measured by three different approaches
questions.stem: Refer to the circular flow diagram of an economy.

choices.text: consumption expenditure on final goods and services ... final goods and services
consumption expenditure on final goods and services ... factors of production
cost of production ... factors of production
cost of production ... final goods and services

questions.explanation: Flow X is households' consumption expenditure paid to firms for final goods and services. Flow Y is the real flow of factors of production supplied by households to firms.

visuals.alt: Circular-flow diagram between firms and households, showing money flow and real flow.
visuals.caption: Circular flow of money and real resources

movements: Flow X is a dotted money flow from households to firms and a solid real flow from firms to households.
Flow Y is a solid real flow from households to firms and a dotted money flow from firms to households.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Flow X is consumption expenditure on final goods and services; Flow Y is factors of production, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: In the diagram, flow X represents the __________________ and flow Y represents the __________________.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
In a public housing estate mall managed by the Hong Kong Housing Authority, a restaurant has decided to stop serving steak for dinner and instead to offer hot pot, as the latter is more popular among customers.

This is an example of using ____________________ to solve the problem of ____________________.

choices.text: the market mechanism ... 'for whom to produce'

questions.explanation: The restaurant changes the type of meal provided, so it addresses what to produce. It is a private firm's response to customers, so it uses the market mechanism.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: Ways of tackling the three basic economic problems by different societies
questions.stem: Compared with a market economy, in a planned economy,

choices.text: resource allocation relies less on price competition.
income will be more evenly distributed.
fewer resources will be owned by the government.

questions.explanation: A planned economy relies more on government decisions and less on price competition for resource allocation. The other outcomes do not necessarily follow.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem:
Many companies provide lockers for employees to use. Generally, only the employees themselves hold the keys to their lockers. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) Employees have the exclusive right to use their own lockers.
(2) To the company, the employees' lockers are capital goods.
(3) The lockers are private goods.
questions.explanation: Employees can decide how to use their lockers, giving them exclusive use. For the company, lockers help provide services and are capital goods. A locker is rival in consumption, so it is a private good.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Compared with a private limited company,

choices.text: a public limited company has wider sources of capital.
a sole proprietorship has better continuity.
the financial information of a partnership is more confidential.
a public limited company has more capital.

questions.explanation: Public limited companies can issue shares and bonds to the public, giving them wider sources of capital. A sole proprietorship has weaker continuity, partnership information can also be confidential, and public limited companies do not necessarily have more capital.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of buying shares and bonds from small investors’ point of view
questions.stem: From the viewpoint of a small investor, which of the following is a possible reason for choosing to buy shares instead of bonds?

choices.text: The rate of return from shares is more stable.
Shareholders may get a higher return from holding shares.
Shareholders can claim repayment prior to bondholders if the company winds up.
Shareholders can participate in the company's daily operations.

questions.explanation: Shareholders may receive a higher return, but that return is less certain. Bondholders have priority over shareholders on winding up, and ownership and management are normally separated.

questions.keyPoint: Definition of free goods and economic goods
questions.stem: A company provides a bike-sharing service. The public can rent bikes by paying through a mobile application.

choices.text: capital, because producing these bikes involves costs.
private goods, because these bikes directly satisfy human wants.
public goods, because these bikes are available for public use.
economic goods, because people are willing to pay and compete for the use of these bikes.

questions.explanation: The bikes are scarce: people are willing to pay and compete to use them, so they are economic goods. They are private goods, but direct satisfaction of wants is not the definition; public availability does not make them public goods.

visuals.alt: A dockless shared bicycle available for rental through a mobile application.
visuals.caption: Bike-sharing service

diagramDetails.answerFocus: The rental bicycles are economic goods because access is scarce, users are willing to pay and they compete to use them.

questions.postVisualStem: These bikes are

questions.keyPoint: Describe the inter-relationship between the three types of production
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram.

choices.text: secondary production ... primary production ... tertiary production
secondary production ... tertiary production ... primary production
primary production ... secondary production ... tertiary production
primary production ... tertiary production ... secondary production

questions.explanation: Primary production supplies raw materials to secondary production. Secondary production supplies producer goods to tertiary production, which supplies services to primary production.

visuals.alt: Production-flow diagram with raw materials moving from B to A, producer goods from A to C and services from C to B.
visuals.caption: Inter-relationship between types of production

movements: Raw materials move from primary to secondary production.
Producer goods move from secondary to tertiary production.
Services move from tertiary to primary production.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: A is secondary production, B is primary production and C is tertiary production, so option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: A, B and C represent __________, ___________ and _________ respectively.

questions.keyPoint: Natural resources: land
questions.stem:
Which of the following is/are considered as 'land' in economics?

(1) water in a natural lake
(2) rainwater collected in a reservoir
(3) water used for cooling machinery in a factory
questions.explanation: Water in a natural lake is a natural resource and therefore land. Rainwater stored in a reservoir and water used in a factory have undergone human processing, so they are capital.

questions.keyPoint: Man-made resources: capital
questions.stem:
Refer to the following conversation between a music studio owner and a music teacher.

Music studio owner: I purchased this place and opened this music studio. You can pay the rent to use this studio.

Music teacher: I will rent your music studio to launch music courses, and I will recruit students and teach violin by myself.

The income earned by the studio owner consists of ______________ while the income earned by the music teacher consists of ______________.

choices.text: interest and profit ... wage and profit

questions.explanation: The studio owner supplies capital and bears business risk, so receives interest and profit. The teacher supplies labour and bears the risk of running courses, so receives wage and profit.

questions.keyPoint: Productivity of labour
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about a factory in 20X4 and 20X5.

choices.text: The working environment of the factory in 20X4 was better than that in 20X5.
The production technology of the factory in 20X5 was more advanced than that in 20X4.
The labour supply of the factory increased in 20X5.
The average labour productivity of the factory in 20X5 was lower.

questions.explanation: Average labour productivity rises from 5 units per man-hour in 20X4 to 6 in 20X5. More advanced technology could explain the rise. Total working hours, the labour supply given here, are unchanged.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, which of the following statements is most likely to be CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem: Which of the following situations will lead to an increase in the geographical mobility of labour in Hong Kong?

choices.text: more trade unions of different industries getting dissolved
providing tax concessions to talents coming to Hong Kong from abroad
providing public transportation subsidies to low-income people

questions.explanation: Transport subsidies lower the cost of working in other districts, increasing geographical mobility of Hong Kong labour. The other options concern occupational mobility or foreign labour instead.

questions.keyPoint: Variable costs and fixed costs
questions.stem:
A Chinese restaurant has decided to change from closing on Mondays to operating every day. Which of the following are variable costs incurred due to the decision?

(1) expenditure on purchasing tea leaves
(2) salary of the human resources department staff
(3) electricity fee
(4) rent
questions.explanation: Buying tea leaves and paying for electricity increase with the extra day of operation. Human-resources salaries and rent stay fixed regardless of the number of operating days.

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: The table below shows the input-output relationship of a firm. Labour is the only input of the firm. The cost per unit of labour is $10.

choices.text: short run ... the law of diminishing marginal returns applies
short run ... the law of diminishing marginal returns does not apply.
long run ... diseconomies of scale exists when output increases from 24 units to 31 units
long run ... economies of scale exists when the output increases from 31 units to 35 units

questions.explanation: As labour is the only input, all inputs are variable and the firm is in the long run. Average cost rises from $1.25 at 24 units to about $1.29 at 31 units, showing diseconomies of scale.
questions.postVisualStem: The table above shows a __________ situation, where __________.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: Refer to the following table.
questions.explanation: Total output rises by 2, 4, 6 and 8 before the fifth unit of labour. With diminishing marginal returns beginning at the fifth worker, its marginal product must be below 8, so 5X is below 28 and X is below 5.6. X can therefore be 5.
questions.postVisualStem: If the law of diminishing marginal returns applies to the firm, the value of X __________.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The following table shows the cost-output relationship of a profit-maximising firm. Suppose the market price is $8.
questions.explanation: Initially, marginal cost equals $8 at 4 units. Adding $2 to average cost makes total costs $10, $18, $28, $40 and $54, so marginal cost equals $8 at 3 units. Profit is $8 x 3 minus $18, or $6.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the firm's average cost per unit of output increases by $2. The profit-maximising output of the firm will __________ and the profit will be _________.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: Karmen operates a baking studio. Under which of the following situations would Karmen reduce production to maximise profit?

choices.text: The monthly rent of the baking studio decreases.
The price of flour rises significantly.
A television drama related to baking has inspired more people to take an interest in baking.

questions.explanation: Flour is a variable cost. A higher flour price raises marginal cost and lowers the profit-maximising output. Changes in business registration fee or rent are fixed-cost changes; stronger demand raises output.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning and give examples of each type of integration
questions.stem: In March 2025, PepsiCo proposed acquiring the prebiotic soda brand Poppi. Poppi is marketed for its low-calorie formula, distinguishing it from traditional sugary sodas. Which of the following is the LEAST likely motive behind the acquisition?

choices.text: ensure a reliable supply of input

questions.explanation: The firms are both beverage producers at the same production stage, so the acquisition is horizontal integration. Reducing competition, economies of scale and more efficient resource use are possible motives, but it cannot ensure an input supply.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem:
To celebrate the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Establishment Day on 1 July, many restaurants launched discount promotions. As a result, the number of customers visiting these restaurants on 1 July increased significantly. Some customers, even though willing to pay the price set by the restaurants, were unable to reserve a table.

Based on the above information, which of the following statements about the situation on 1 July is/are CORRECT?

(1) The demand for restaurant services provided by the restaurants increased due to the discount promotions.
(2) There was a shortage in the market of restaurant services.
(3) The restaurants offering discounts did not maximise their profits.
questions.explanation: Customers who are willing to pay but cannot reserve show excess demand, so there is a shortage. The promotion changes quantity demanded, not demand, and it need not imply that restaurants failed to maximise profit.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram.
questions.explanation: At P1, quantity supplied is Q2 while quantity demanded is Q1, creating a surplus. The quantity actually transacted is the smaller quantity, Q1.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram with equilibrium P0, Q0, a price P1 above equilibrium and a price P2 below equilibrium.
visuals.caption: Market surplus diagram

movements: At P1, quantity supplied is Q2 and quantity demanded is Q1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: At P1, Q2 exceeds Q1, so quantity transacted is Q1 and there is a surplus. Option A is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: When the market price is __________, the quantity transacted will be __________. There is a surplus in the market.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: When the government increases the fixed airport departure tax charged to all travellers,

choices.text: there will be an excess supply of flight seats.
the average flight distance of outbound passengers will decrease.
government's revenue from the airport departure tax must increase.
the proportion of passengers choosing business class seats will increase relative to economy class seats.

questions.explanation: A larger fixed tax lowers the relative price of business class compared with economy class, so a greater proportion choose business class. The average flight distance rises, tax revenue is uncertain, and lower demand need not create excess supply if the initial market condition is unknown.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem:
The supply curve for good X is upward sloping, and its demand is perfectly inelastic.

If the production cost of good X decreases, and the price of the substitute for good X increases, the equilibrium price of good X __________ and its equilibrium quantity __________.

choices.text: may increase, decrease or remain unchanged ... will decrease
may increase, decrease or remain unchanged ... will increase

questions.explanation: Lower production cost raises supply: price falls while quantity is unchanged with perfectly inelastic demand. A higher substitute price raises demand: both price and quantity rise. Quantity must rise, while the price effect is ambiguous.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is the demand-supply diagram of instant noodles. E0 is the initial equilibrium point.
questions.explanation: Raw-material shortage shifts supply left from S0 to S2. Higher income reduces demand for an inferior good, shifting demand left from D0 to D2. The new equilibrium is E4.

visuals.alt: Instant-noodle market with demand curves D0 to D2, supply curves S0 to S2 and equilibria E0 to E4.
visuals.caption: Instant-noodle demand and supply shifts

movements: Raw-material shortage shifts supply left from S0 to S2.
Higher income for an inferior good shifts demand left from D0 to D2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The new equilibrium is E4, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose there is a shortage of raw materials for producing instant noodles. At the same time, people's income generally increases and instant noodles are regarded as inferior goods. The new equilibrium point will be at ____________.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Producer goods and consumer goods
questions.stem: Suppose the government of a country relaxes the licensing requirements for tutoring centres. At the same time, students generally pay more attention to academic performance. Which of the following diagrams can represent the above situation?
questions.explanation: Relaxing licensing requirements increases the supply of tutoring services. Greater student attention to academic performance raises demand for tutoring services and therefore the derived demand for tutors. Diagram C shows the rightward shift of demand for tutors.

visuals.alt: Four demand-supply diagrams for tutoring services and tutors, with labelled curves S0, S1, D0 and D1.
visuals.caption: Tutoring-service and tutor-market options

movements: Relaxing licensing requirements shifts the supply of tutoring services right.
Stronger academic focus increases demand for tutoring services and the derived demand for tutors.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Only option C shows a rightward shift of demand for tutors, so option C is correct.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Types of price elasticity of supply
questions.stem: Given that the price elasticity of supply of cakes is 0.5. When the price of cakes increases,

choices.text: the demand for cakes will decrease.
the quantity supplied of cakes will decrease.
the quantity supplied of cakes will change by the same percentage.
the quantity supplied of cakes will increase, while the percentage increase will be smaller than the percentage increase in price.

questions.explanation: A price elasticity of supply between 0 and 1 means supply is inelastic. Quantity supplied rises when price rises, but by a smaller percentage than price.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Which of the following will increase the price elasticity of demand for bus services?

choices.text: More minibus routes stop their services.
The wage rate of bus drivers increases.
More railway branch lines are completed.
The breakdown rate of buses decreases.

questions.explanation: More railway lines provide more substitutes for bus services. Consumers can more readily switch transport mode after a bus-fare change, making demand more price elastic.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in supply
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in supply
questions.stem:
With technological advancements, Country A's drug production technology has significantly improved. As a result, the price of locally produced drugs has changed by 40% and the quantity transacted has changed by 20%. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The total revenue of locally produced drugs will decrease.
(2) Both the demand for and supply of locally produced drugs will increase.
(3) The price and quantity transacted of imported drugs will decrease.
(4) The total expenditure on imported drugs may increase.
questions.explanation: Improved technology raises supply of locally produced drugs, lowering price by 40% and raising quantity by 20%; total revenue therefore falls. Local and imported drugs are substitutes, so lower local-drug prices reduce demand for imported drugs, lowering their price and quantity and their total expenditure.

questions.topicGroup: Interest as the cost of earlier availability of resources
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of interest
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about interest is CORRECT?

choices.text: Interest only exists in a monetary economy.
Interest only exists in a market economy.
When the interest rate decreases, people will reduce current consumption.
Without scarcity, interest will not exist.

questions.explanation: Interest is the price of earlier availability of resources. Without scarcity, no choice between present and future consumption is needed, so interest does not exist. It can exist without money or a market economy, and a lower interest rate encourages current consumption.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Miss Hui purchased a newly built private residential unit for $5,000,000 two years ago and has been living in it. Recently, Miss Hui plans to move abroad and is considering either renting out the unit for a monthly rent of $15,000 or selling it for $5,200,000 and depositing the amount into a time deposit account.

Which of the following will increase Miss Hui's opportunity cost of renting out the residential unit?

(1) a decrease in the commission required for renting out the unit
(2) an increase in the interest rate on the time deposit
(3) a decrease in the maximum amount that a buyer is willing to pay for the unit
questions.explanation: Renting out the unit forgoes the interest income from selling it and making a time deposit. A higher deposit rate raises that forgone income. Lower rental commission or a lower sale price reduces the opportunity cost.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
Which of the following are related to the question of 'how to produce'?

(1) A minibus company hired more foreign workers as minibus drivers.
(2) A manufacturer relocated its factory to reduce production costs.
(3) A toy manufacturer lowered the price of its products.
questions.explanation: Hiring different workers and relocating a factory change the resources used in production, so concern how to produce. Lowering price affects who receives the goods.

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of issuing shares and bonds to raise capital
questions.stem: A public limited company decides to issue bonds to raise capital for the expansion of its business. From the viewpoint of the existing shareholders, which of the following is an advantage of issuing bonds over shares?

choices.text: The interest paid to the bondholders is lower than the dividends paid to the shareholders.
The company does not need to disclose its accounting information to the public.
The risk of the company being taken over by others will not be increased.
The company can raise more capital.

questions.explanation: Bondholders are creditors, not owners. Issuing bonds therefore does not increase the risk of a takeover. Interest may exceed dividends, public disclosure remains required, and bonds need not raise more capital.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem: Baidu Baike is an online encyclopedia. The knowledge on Baidu Baike is _________________________.

choices.text: a private good because Baidu Baike is run by a private enterprise
a free good because people do not have to pay to obtain the knowledge
a capital in Economics because people are willing to pay for the knowledge
a public good because a person's consumption does not reduce the amount available to others

questions.explanation: The knowledge is non-excludable and non-rival, so it is a public good. No charge does not make it a free good: people want more knowledge than is available.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The following table shows the production information of a firm. The firm employs two inputs only, namely machines and labour.

choices.text: The firm enjoys economies of scale.
The law of diminishing marginal returns applies to the firm.
The total product is at the highest when the quantity of labour is 6 units.
The firm is at its optimal scale of production when the quantity of labour is 5 units.

questions.explanation: With machines fixed at two, the firm is in the short run. Marginal product falls from 37 when labour rises to five, to 19 with six workers, so diminishing marginal returns apply. Total product is highest at seven workers.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the above firm is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem:
After opening more branches, a restaurant finds that its average production cost has increased. Which of the following can be a possible reason?

(1) The restaurant is suffering from external diseconomies of scale due to increased labour costs.
(2) The restaurant is enjoying internal economies of scale due to decreased borrowing costs.
(3) The restaurant is suffering from internal diseconomies of scale due to increased marketing expenses.
questions.explanation: More branches can raise marketing expense. If sales do not rise enough to cover it, the restaurant suffers internal diseconomies of scale. The other two statements do not explain its higher average cost.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem:
A singer sold some clothes he had previously worn, and they were all sold out within a short period of time. Many people expressed that they were unable to buy them even though they were willing to pay the listed price.

From the information above, we can infer that at the prevailing price, the quantity transacted of the clothes is _____________.

choices.text: equal to the quantity demanded and smaller than the quantity supplied
equal to the quantity demanded and greater than the quantity supplied
equal to the quantity supplied and smaller than the quantity demanded
equal to the quantity supplied and greater than the quantity demanded

questions.explanation: The willing but unsuccessful buyers show price is below equilibrium and there is excess demand. Thus quantity transacted equals the smaller quantity supplied.

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem:
In which of the following situations will a decrease in the price of good X lead to a decrease in the quantity transacted of good Y?

(1) Good X and good Y are in joint demand.
(2) Good X and good Y are in competitive supply.
(3) Good X and good Y are in competitive demand.
questions.explanation: For competitive demand, a lower X price reduces demand for Y, so Y quantity falls. Joint demand raises Y demand, while competitive supply raises Y supply, both increasing Y quantity.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings of joint supply and competitive supply
questions.stem:
Good X and good Y are in joint supply. If consumers expect the price of good X to increase in the future,

(1) the marginal benefit of the last unit of good Y will increase.
(2) total revenue of good Y will increase.
(3) consumer surplus in the market for good Y will increase.
(4) the quantity transacted of good Y will increase.
questions.explanation: Expected dearer X raises demand and price of X. Joint supply then increases Y supply, reducing Y price and raising Y quantity and consumer surplus. Marginal benefit falls with price, while total revenue is uncertain.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Suppose the government implements effective rent control by setting a cap on the rent per square foot that landlords can charge tenants. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The landlords will be more willing to spend money on repairing the rental units.
The rental that the landlords can earn from renting out their units may increase, decrease or remain unchanged.
The number of vacant rental units available will increase.

questions.explanation: An effective rent ceiling creates excess demand, so landlords choose tenants using non-price criteria. Rent and quantity traded fall, reducing maintenance incentives and vacant units.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price floor on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand and supply schedules of good X.

choices.text: there will be a shortage in the market for good X.
the quantity transacted of good X will decrease by 40 units.
the equilibrium price of the substitutes of good X will decrease.

questions.explanation: The original equilibrium is $10 and 60 units. Raising the floor from ineffective $9 to effective $12 reduces quantity traded to 20, a fall of 40. At $12 there is a surplus, producer revenue falls, and substitute prices rise.

visuals.caption: Demand and supply schedules of good X

questions.postVisualStem: If the government raises the price floor of good X from $9 to $12,

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram of good X.

choices.text: The total expenditure on good X will decrease.
The quota will change from ineffective to effective.

questions.explanation: Q2 exceeds equilibrium quantity and is therefore ineffective. Raising the quota from effective Q1 to Q2 returns output to the efficient level and eliminates deadweight loss.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram for good X with quota quantities Q1 and Q2.
visuals.caption: Quota adjustment

movements: The quota increases from Q1, below equilibrium quantity, to Q2, above equilibrium quantity.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The quota changes from effective to ineffective, quantity reaches the efficient level and deadweight loss is eliminated.

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the government adjusts the quota of good X from Q1 to Q2. Which of the following statements is

CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Understand how price elasticities of demand and supply affect the share of the subsidy
questions.stem:
Which of the following combinations may result in the consumers' share of the subsidy being smaller than the producers' share of the subsidy when a per-unit subsidy is provided for a good?

(1) elastic demand; unitarily elastic supply
(2) elastic demand; perfectly inelastic supply
(3) inelastic demand; inelastic supply
(4) inelastic demand; perfectly elastic supply
questions.explanation: The more elastic side receives the smaller subsidy share. Demand is certainly more elastic in (1) and (2), may be more elastic in (3), and is certainly less elastic than perfectly elastic supply in (4).

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the market share of Country A’s medical insurance market in 2024.

choices.text: monopolistic competition ... insurance companies in the market had similar market shares
monopolistic competition ... there were many consumers of medical insurance in the market
oligopoly ... there was price and non-price competition among the insurance companies
oligopoly ... the market was dominated by a few insurance companies

questions.explanation: Four named firms account for 95% of the market, so a few firms dominate it. That is a defining feature of oligopoly.

visuals.alt: Pie chart of Country A medical-insurance market shares: Graceful 31%, Fulfilment 27%, Serenity 20%, Integrity 17% and others 5%.
visuals.caption: Medical-insurance market shares

diagramDetails.answerFocus: A few firms dominate the market, so it is oligopoly.

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, we can conclude that the market structure of the medical insurance market in Country A was ______________ because ____________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Calculate consumer surplus
questions.stem: The following table shows the marginal benefit schedule of a consumer for coconut water.

visuals.caption: Marginal benefit schedule for coconut water

questions.postVisualStem: If the price of coconut water increases from $22 to $23, consumer surplus will ____________.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand and supply schedules of good X.

choices.text: The ratio of consumers' tax burden to producers' tax burden is 1:2.
If the government raises the per-unit tax to $5, total social surplus will increase.
The imposition of a quota of 8 units instead of the per-unit tax would have an equivalent effect on the price.
The demand for good X is inelastic within the price range of the original and new equilibrium.
