questions.explanation: The tax gives price $12 and quantity 8. A quota of 8 also gives price $12. Consumer and producer tax burdens are $16 and $8 respectively, and the fall in total expenditure shows elastic demand over this interval.

visuals.caption: Demand and supply schedules of good X

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government imposes a per-unit tax of $3 on good X. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) price ceiling on (money) price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc.
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply-demand diagram for rice. P0 is the price ceiling set by the government.
questions.explanation: Recovery raises demand for normal rice. With the binding ceiling, quantity supplied remains fixed, so excess demand and the marginal-benefit/marginal-cost gap both grow. Marginal cost at the traded quantity is unchanged.

visuals.alt: Rice market under a binding price ceiling P0, with upward supply and downward demand curves.
visuals.caption: Rice price ceiling

movements: Economic recovery shifts demand for normal rice right while the price ceiling fixes quantity supplied.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Excess demand and the deadweight loss both increase, while the marginal cost of the last traded unit does not change.

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose rice is a normal good and the economy is experiencing an economic recovery. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The excess demand for rice will increase.
(2) Deadweight loss will increase.
(3) The marginal cost of the last unit of rice will decrease.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Lorenz curve
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the Lorenz curves of Country A and Country B.
questions.explanation: At the lowest 20%, Country A's curve is below Country B's. At 90%, A's curve is above B's, so A's highest 10% earn a smaller share. The number of high-income people cannot be inferred.

visuals.alt: Lorenz curves for Country A and Country B with cumulative household and income percentages.
visuals.caption: Lorenz curves

diagramDetails.answerFocus: At 20% Country A is below B; at 90% Country A is above B, so its top 10% income share is smaller. The graph does not show the number of high-income people.

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the total incomes in the two counties are equal. Based on the above information, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The total income of the bottom 20% of households in Country A is lower than the total income of the bottom 20% of households in Country B.
(2) The top 10% of households in Country A earn a smaller proportion of the country’s total income than that in Country B.
(3) Country A has more high-income people.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising opportunities
questions.stem:
The government of a country plans to increase the number of subsidised university degree programs and to waive tuition fees for students from families with an annual income below a certain amount. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The plan will help improve equity.
(2) The plan will reduce the labour supply of the country.
(3) The plan will cause the aggregate output to decrease in the short run.
questions.explanation: Fee waivers broaden education opportunities for lower-income students. More people remain in education rather than seek full-time work, reducing labour supply. Higher government spending raises AD while labour supply reduction lowers SRAS, so short-run output is uncertain.

questions.keyPoint: Production/value added approach
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the production chain for umbrellas in an economy.
questions.explanation: Value added is $250 for local raw materials, $650 + X for local manufacturers and $800 for retailers. GDP at factor cost is $1,700 + X minus $100 tax, so X is $1,400.

visuals.alt: Umbrella production chain from imported and local raw materials to local manufacturers, retailers, local consumers and foreign consumers.
visuals.caption: Umbrella production chain

movements: Local manufacturers sell to retailers and foreign consumers.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Using value added and subtracting the $100 tax, X equals $1,400.

questions.postVisualStem: The contribution of the above production chain to the economy's GDP at factor cost is $3,000. The value of X is ________.

questions.keyPoint: Expenditure approach
questions.stem: The following table shows the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data of an economy in a certain year.
questions.explanation: GDP is C + gross investment + G + net exports = 500 + (300 + 25 + 20) + 350 + (600 + 350 - 300) = $1,845 million.
questions.postVisualStem: The GDP at market prices is $_____________ million.

questions.topicGroup: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.keyPoint: Meanings of GDP and resident producing units; items included/excluded in calculating GDP
questions.stem:
Mr. Cheung received the Old Age Living Allowance in June 2025. He used part of it to dine at a fast food shop in Hong Kong. He also gave part of it to his grandson as pocket money.

Which of the following are NOT included in the calculation of Hong Kong's GDP in 2025?

(1) the amount of Old Age Living Allowance received by Mr. Cheung from the government
(2) the amount Mr. Cheung spent at the fast food shop using the Old Age Living Allowance
(3) the pocket money Mr. Cheung gave to his grandson from the Old Age Living Allowance
questions.explanation: The allowance and pocket money are transfers without production and are excluded. Restaurant spending is household consumption expenditure on final services and is included.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: Which of the following is the factor income earned by residents outside the economic territory of Hong Kong?

choices.text: interest received by a Hong Kong resident from investing in overseas bonds
rental income received by a Chinese accountant from renting out a property under his name in Hong Kong
salary earned by a Hong Kong resident working for the Hong Kong branch of a foreign company
salary earned by an American teacher working in a school in Hong Kong for two years

questions.explanation: A is income received abroad by a Hong Kong resident. The other incomes are earned inside Hong Kong, including the American teacher's income after two years because the teacher is a Hong Kong resident.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: The following table shows the data of an economy in a certain year.

choices.text: Nominal GDP is greater than real GDP.
Gross national income is smaller than gross domestic product.
GDP at factor cost is greater than GDP at market prices.
Total exports are greater than total imports.

questions.explanation: Negative net factor income from abroad means GNI is smaller than GDP. A GDP deflator of 98 means nominal GDP is below real GDP; indirect taxes exceed subsidies; and negative net exports mean imports exceed exports.
questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the economy is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Meaning of per capita GDP
questions.stem:
Country A's implicit price deflator of GDP rose by 8% in 2024, while its nominal GDP rose by 6% and its population fell by 1% during the same period.

Based on the above information, we can conclude that Country A's per capita nominal GDP in 2024 has _____________, while its per capita real GDP has _____________.
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP rises while population falls, so per-capita nominal GDP rises. Real GDP falls by about 1.85% because nominal GDP rises more slowly than the deflator; this exceeds the population fall, so per-capita real GDP falls.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting short run aggregate supply
questions.stem: Which of the following can explain why a short run aggregate supply curve is upward sloping?

choices.text: Everyone adjusts their behaviour according to economic conditions.
Input and output prices are not fully adjusted.
The productive capacity of an economy changes in the short run.

questions.explanation: In the short run, input prices adjust less fully than output prices. Higher output prices therefore make firms willing to supply more output.

questions.topicGroup: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting long run aggregate supply
questions.stem:
The HKSAR Government announced the arrangements for the admission of professionals of specified skilled trades to Hong Kong to address acute manpower shortage. Based on the above information, which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) Hong Kong's GDP will increase.
(2) Hong Kong's long run aggregate supply will increase.
(3) Hong Kong's aggregate demand will increase.
questions.explanation: More skilled professionals raise labour supply and LRAS. A larger population also raises consumption and AD, so GDP increases.

questions.keyPoint: Factors that cause a shift of an AD curve
questions.stem: Which of the following will cause the aggregate demand curve of an economy to shift to the right?

choices.text: The government provides cash subsidies to applicants waiting for public housing.
The government cuts production subsidies to firms.
A major trading partner experiences economic recession.
The implicit deflator of GDP has increased for several consecutive years.

questions.explanation: Cash subsidies raise low-income households' disposable income and private consumption, shifting AD right. The other options lower SRAS, reduce net exports, or move along AD.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem:
The government of an economy has the following policy proposals:

I. to introduce more capital to support production
II. to tighten the visa requirements for foreign visitors
III. to raise the salaries tax rate
IV. to provide transportation subsidies to housewives who re-enter the workplace

Which of the following combinations is most likely to increase the economy's aggregate output in the short run?
questions.explanation: More capital raises SRAS. Transport subsidies raise labour supply and disposable income, raising SRAS and AD. The visa restriction and higher salaries tax reduce AD.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Inflationary gap
questions.stem:
There is an inflationary (output) gap in economy A. Which of the following will narrow the inflationary (output) gap?

(1) an increase in the labour costs
(2) an increase in the progressivity of salaries tax
(3) an increase in production subsidies
questions.explanation: Higher labour costs lower SRAS and higher tax progressivity lowers AD, both reducing output and narrowing an inflationary gap. Production subsidies raise SRAS and widen it.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: Refer to the following long run aggregate supply curve of Country A. Country A's long run equilibrium point

choices.text: More firms use artificial intelligence to replace labour.
Firms become more optimistic about their business prospects.
Firms expect the general price level to decrease.
People prefer to consume imported goods instead of locally produced goods.

questions.explanation: More imported-goods consumption lowers net exports and AD, creating a deflationary gap. Lower input costs then shift SRAS right until output returns to Y1 at lower price level E2.

visuals.alt: Vertical LRAS at output Y1 with long-run equilibrium moving from E1 to E2 at a lower price level.
visuals.caption: Long-run equilibrium adjustment

movements: Aggregate demand falls and long-run adjustment lowers input prices and shifts SRAS right.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Preference for imports reduces net exports and AD, creating a deflationary gap before output returns to Y1 at E2.

questions.postVisualStem: changes from E1 to E2. Which of the following is a possible reason for this change?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem:
Which of the following would increase the aggregate output of an economy and enhance equity at the same time?

(1) to increase the living allowance provided to grassroots children
(2) to allocate more resources to improve the quality of education in public schools
(3) to abolish the general sales tax
questions.explanation: Each policy can raise output through higher AD or lower production costs. Allowances and public-school quality help lower-income children, while abolishing a regressive sales tax raises lower-income households' income proportionately more.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem: Gold is better than salt at performing the _____________ function of money because the former is more _____________.
questions.explanation: Gold is scarcer and therefore better retains value. Salt is more divisible; portability and homogeneity do not explain the named functions.

questions.keyPoint: How central bank functions are carried out in
questions.stem: Which of the following descriptions about how the functions of a central bank are carried out in Hong Kong is INCORRECT?

choices.text: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is the lender of last resort for Hong Kong's financial institutions.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority carries out monetary policies in Hong Kong.
The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited acts as the government's banker.
The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited acts as the clearing house.

questions.explanation: Hong Kong Interbank Clearing Limited, not HSBC, acts as the clearing house. The other descriptions are correct.

questions.topicGroup: Licensed banks, restricted licence banks and deposit-taking companies in
questions.keyPoint: Features of the three types of deposit-taking institutions
questions.stem:
Mr. Wong plans to deposit HK$500,000 to an authorised institution in Hong Kong as a time deposit for one month. Which of the following authorised institutions can accept his deposit?

(1) licensed banks
(2) restricted licence banks
(3) deposit-taking companies
questions.explanation: Licensed banks accept all deposits. Restricted licence banks accept time deposits of HK$500,000 or above. Deposit-taking companies cannot accept a time deposit below three months.

questions.keyPoint: Effects of asset transfers on money supply
questions.stem:
Mr. Tai withdrew HK$100,000 cash from a demand deposit with a licensed bank. He then deposited HK$50,000 of the amount into a time deposit with the same bank and remitted the remainder overseas.

What will be the immediate effect of the above actions on the money supply of Hong Kong?

choices.text: Money supply M1 will decrease by HK$100,000.
Both money supply M1 and money supply M2 will decrease by HK$50,000.
Money supply M3 will remain unchanged.
Money supply M1, money supply M2 and money supply M3 will decrease by HK$50,000.

questions.explanation: The withdrawal changes no money aggregate. The time deposit lowers M1 by $50,000 but leaves M2/M3 unchanged; remitting the other $50,000 lowers all three. Overall M1 falls $100,000, while M2 and M3 fall $50,000.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem:
Which of the following may lead to an increase in the money supply?

(1) The public deposits all their cash into commercial banks.
(2) Commercial banks hold fewer excess reserves.
(3) The government raises the required reserve ratio.
questions.explanation: Cash deposits allow deposit creation, and fewer excess reserves allow more lending and deposit creation. A higher required reserve ratio reduces lending and money supply.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Study the following information about an economy.

choices.text: the maximum possible amount of money supply will be $5,400 million.
the maximum possible amount of loans will be $3,900 million.
the maximum possible amount of deposits will be $4,900 million.
the monetary base of the economy will decrease by $100 million.

questions.explanation: Initially deposits are $4,800m, reserves $1,200m and loans $3,600m, so the required reserve ratio is 25%. The $100m cash deposit gives reserves $1,300m, deposits $5,200m and loans $3,900m. Monetary base remains $1,400m.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the banks do not hold excess reserves. If the public deposit $100 million in cash into the banking system,

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money demand and money supply curves of an economy. The original equilibrium point is at E.
questions.explanation: Printing money shifts supply right from Ms0 to Ms2. Expected lower bond prices increase asset demand for money, shifting money demand right from Md0 to Md2. Their intersection is D.

visuals.alt: Money-market diagram with money supply curves Ms0 to Ms2, money demand curves Md0 to Md2 and points A to E.
visuals.caption: Money-market shifts

movements: Printing money shifts supply right from Ms0 to Ms2.
Expected bond-price falls raise asset demand for money and shift demand right from Md0 to Md2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The new equilibrium is D.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the central bank prints more money and at the same time people expect the price of bonds to fall. The new equilibrium point will be at __________.

questions.keyPoint: Explain whether and how cost changes under different circumstances
questions.stem:
Macy is a university student who is planning how to spend her summer holiday. She has several options and her order of preference is shown below:

First option: to travel to Europe
Second option: to work as a private Economics tutor
Third option: to work part-time in a fast-food shop

Which of the following factors would LEAST likely affect Macy's cost-benefit analysis for her choice?

choices.text: A tourist attraction in Europe that Macy longs to visit is temporarily closed for maintenance.
Benefits for part-time workers at the fast-food shop are reduced.
The working hours for working part-time at the fast-food shop become more flexible.
The tutoring student gets along very well with Macy.

questions.explanation: Macy chooses Europe because its value exceeds the cost, the value of her next-best option. Reducing the value of her third choice does not affect that benefit or cost; the other changes can affect the value of Europe or her next-best alternative.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
Which of the following cases are related to the problem of 'how to produce'?

(1) A technology company locates its data centre in a country with lower electricity costs.
(2) A hospital hires more non-local doctors to provide medical services.
(3) An education center offers English phonics classes for children.
questions.explanation: Choosing a production location and deciding which workers to employ concern the resources and method of production. Choosing which classes to offer concerns what to produce.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about three firms in Hong Kong.

choices.text: Firm A has better continuity than firm B and firm C.
Firm C has the fewest owners among the three firms.
The profits tax rate paid by firm C is lower than that of firm A and firm B.
The owners of the three firms are required to obtain consent from the other owners when transferring their ownership.

questions.explanation: Firm A is a public limited company, Firm B a private limited company, and Firm C can be a sole proprietorship or partnership. A sole proprietorship or partnership has a lower profits-tax rate than either form of limited company.

visuals.caption: Information about three firms
rows: Disclosure of financial information to the public

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, which of the following statements about the firms is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem:
In 2024, a total of 16 listed companies announced privatisation and cancelled their listing status on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: These companies cannot own assets under their names after privatisation.
The size of these companies will decrease.
The risk of these companies being taken over will increase.
The liquidity of the shares of these companies will become lower.

questions.explanation: After privatisation, shares cannot be freely traded on the stock market, so their liquidity falls. The companies remain legal entities, their size need not change, and restrictions on transfer reduce takeover risk.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem:
A technology company provides 'artificial intelligence (AI) image generation service' for free. Users can upload photos to its platform, which will convert these photos into cartoon-style images. The service has been very popular since its launch, and some users have complained that they often have to wait for several minutes to receive their results due to the system being busy.

Based on the above information, the AI image generation service is __________ because __________.

choices.text: a free good ... people do not have to pay to use the service
an economic good ... people's demand for the service is greater than the supply
a private good ... the service is rival in consumption
a consumer good ... scarce resources are used in providing the service

questions.explanation: When one user's request makes the system unable to process another's promptly, access is rival in consumption. The service can therefore be a private good even though it is free of charge.

questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of division of labour
questions.stem:
In a newspaper company, different reporters specialise in covering different types of news. For example, some reporters cover sports news, while others cover financial news.

Compared to an arrangement in which each reporter covers all types of news, which of the following are the benefits of the above arrangement?

(1) The time required for reporters to write each article will be reduced since practice makes perfect.
(2) The time required to train junior reporters to master relevant knowledge will be reduced.
(3) The tools required for writing articles will be reduced, such as requiring fewer personal computers.
questions.explanation: Specialisation lets reporters gain experience and reduces the knowledge each needs to master. It does not reduce the number of computers required.

questions.keyPoint: Mobility of labour
questions.stem:
In 2025, the HKSAR Government implemented the 'Greater Bay Area (GBA) Youth Employment Scheme - Arrangements for Mainland Youth to Work in Hong Kong'. Enterprises that employ Hong Kong young persons to work in GBA Mainland cities may apply for the same number of Mainland young persons to work in Hong Kong.

Based on the above information, the above arrangement will most likely lead to

choices.text: an increase in Hong Kong's labour supply.
an increase in Hong Kong's labour productivity.
an increase in the geographical mobility of Mainland young persons.
an increase in the occupational mobility of Hong Kong young persons.

questions.explanation: The arrangement makes it easier for Mainland young persons to work in Hong Kong, increasing their geographical mobility. Effects on Hong Kong labour supply and productivity are not certain, and it does not concern occupational mobility.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem:
The contract of a professional football player with his team includes the following terms:

Basic salary: US$5 million
Appearance bonus: US$200,000 per match

From the viewpoint of the team, which of the following is most likely the reason for adopting the above wage payment method instead of a basic salary only?

choices.text: The cost of measuring player contribution will be lower.
This can transfer the risk of player injury to the player.
The player's income will be higher.
The cost of the team calculating the salary will be lower.

questions.explanation: If injury prevents the player from appearing, the total pay is lower. The appearance-based component transfers some injury risk from the team to the player.

questions.keyPoint: Internal economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem:
Mr. Cheung runs a restaurant in Mong Kok serving 'Rice with two sides'. He is considering whether to expand the kitchen of the existing restaurant to increase the number of meal boxes produced each day, or to open a new branch in another district.

Which of the following is a possible reason to expand the existing kitchen instead of opening a new branch?

choices.text: A greater degree of division of labour can be practised in the same kitchen to reduce the average cost of production.
Mr. Cheung will receive discounts for purchasing more ingredients.
The restaurant can spread transportation costs over a larger quantity of output and enjoy external economies of scale.

questions.explanation: A larger kitchen permits greater division of labour, an internal economy of scale. Bulk-purchase discounts may arise under either option, and neither expansion diversifies a single-product business.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The table below shows the cost-output relationship of a price-taking firm.
questions.explanation: The original marginal cost of the third unit is $7 and the price at the original profit-maximising output is $11. Marginal cost therefore rises by $4. Original profit is $55 - $35 = $20, and new profit is $33 - $27 = $6, a fall of $14.
questions.postVisualStem: After the increase in the marginal cost per unit of output, the profit-maximising output level decreases from 5 units to 3 units. The marginal cost per unit of output has increased by __________ and the profit will __________.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning and give examples of each type of integration
questions.stem: GreenLife is a company that produces organic food. Recently, it acquired two companies as illustrated in the following diagram:
questions.explanation: Full Organic Farm supplies GreenLife's ingredients, so X is vertical backward integration. A health-beverage business is related but not directly competing, so Y is lateral integration.

visuals.alt: GreenLife acquisition chart linking Full Organic Farm as X and Lively Beverage Company as Y.
visuals.caption: GreenLife integrations

movements: X links GreenLife to a supplier of organic ingredients.
Y links GreenLife to a related health-beverage producer.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: X is vertical backward integration and Y is lateral integration.

questions.postVisualStem: Full Organic Farm is a farm that provides organic ingredients while Lively Beverage Company is a health beverage company. To GreenLife, the types of integration shown by X and Y are __________ integration and __________ integration respectively.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem:
The underground railway in a city is often full during peak hours and passengers have to wait for multiple trains before they can board. Which of the following events would shorten the waiting time for passengers?

(1) The government increases bus fare concessions for the elderly.
(2) The underground railway company increases the train frequency.
(3) The underground railway company provides fare concessions during non-peak hours.
questions.explanation: All three changes reduce excess demand during peak hours: bus and MTR are substitutes, more trains increase supply, and non-peak and peak travel are substitutes.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem: The table below shows the quantities of high-quality and average-quality fruits sold before and after a decrease in the transportation cost.
questions.explanation: A lower transport cost raises the relative price of high-quality fruit, so the proportion of average-quality fruit should increase. The ratio stays 1:1.5 in (1) and falls to 1:1.4 in (3), so both are inconsistent.

visuals.caption: Fruit quantities before and after a transportation-cost decrease
rows: Before the decrease in the transportation cost
After the decrease in the transportation cost

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose people’s preference for fruits does not change. Which of the following figures is/are INCONSISTENT with the law of demand?

(1) Q1 = 50; Q2 = 75
(2) Q1 = 50; Q2 = 80
(3) Q1 = 60; Q2 = 84

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The demand curve for good X is downward-sloping and its supply is perfectly inelastic. In which of the following cases must the equilibrium quantity of good X increase and the equilibrium price decrease?

choices.text: The demand for good X decreases and at the same time its supply increases.
The demand for good X increases and at the same time its supply decreases.
The demand for and supply of good X increase at the same time.
The demand for and supply of good X decrease at the same time.

questions.explanation: With perfectly inelastic supply, a demand decrease lowers price without changing quantity. A supply increase then lowers price and raises quantity, so both stated outcomes must occur.

questions.keyPoint: Understand the meanings of joint supply and competitive supply
questions.stem:
Suppose the demand for good Y is inelastic. In which of the following cases will an increase in the price of good X lead to an increase in the total revenue of good Y?

(1) Good X and good Y are in joint demand.
(2) Good X and good Y are in competitive supply.
(3) Good X and good Y are in joint supply.
questions.explanation: With competitive supply, a higher X price diverts resources from Y, reducing Y supply. Its price rises and, with inelastic demand, Y's total revenue rises. Joint demand or joint supply reduces Y's total revenue.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between price elasticity of demand and total revenue
questions.stem:
In which of the following cases will consumers' total expenditure on good X increase?

(1) The price of raw materials used to produce good X increases and the demand for good X is inelastic.
(2) The government increases the effective quota for good X and the demand for good X is elastic.
(3) The government imposes a per-unit tax on a substitute of good X and the demand for good X is unitarily elastic.
questions.explanation: (1) reduces supply and raises price; with inelastic demand, expenditure rises. (2) lowers price and raises quantity; with elastic demand, expenditure rises. (3) raises a substitute's price, shifting X demand right and raising X expenditure.

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the provision of a unit subsidy on price, quantity transacted, total revenue etc., and show the share of the subsidy between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following market demand and supply schedules of good X.

choices.text: If the government imposes a per-unit tax of $2 on good X, the quantity transacted will decrease by 2 units.
If the government sets a price floor on good X at $14, there will be an excess demand.
If the government sets a price ceiling on good X at $14, consumers' total expenditure on good X will be $364.
If the government provides a per-unit subsidy of $2 for good X, producers' total revenue (including the subsidy) will be $432.

questions.explanation: Supply is perfectly inelastic at 24 units and equilibrium price is $16. A $2 subsidy gives producers $18 per unit, so total revenue is $18 x 24 = $432.

visuals.caption: Market demand and supply schedules of good X

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about good X is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: State the general features of different market structures
questions.stem: Hong Kong's banking industry is most likely an example of __________ because __________.

choices.text: monopolistic competition ... Hong Kong has more than 100 licensed banks
monopolistic competition ... banks provide heterogeneous services
oligopoly ... it is costly to open a bank
oligopoly ... a few banks have significantly higher revenue than the others

questions.explanation: Several banks have much higher revenue and market shares than others, showing that a few dominant sellers operate in the market.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram for good X. The initial equilibrium point is E.
questions.explanation: A unit tax reduces quantity transacted. Moving left along downward demand raises marginal benefit, while moving left along upward supply lowers marginal cost.

visuals.alt: Demand and supply diagram for good X, with initial equilibrium E.
visuals.caption: Per-unit tax on good X

movements: A per-unit tax shifts the supply curve upward/left and reduces quantity transacted.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: At the lower transacted quantity, marginal benefit rises and marginal cost falls, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the government imposes a per-unit tax on good X. The marginal benefit of the last unit of good X will __________, while the marginal cost of the last unit of good X will __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.topicGroup: With the aid of a demand-supply diagram, analyse the effects of market interventions on consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency
questions.keyPoint: Quota
questions.stem: Refer to the following demand-supply diagram for good X. Initially, the quota is set at Q1.

choices.text: There is no deadweight loss in the market for good X.
Consumer surplus increases by area bcP1.
Producer surplus increases by area cdef.
There is an excess supply of (Q2 - Q1) in the market for good X.

questions.explanation: Original producer surplus is P1cfg and new producer surplus is P1deg. The increase is area cdef; the new market clears at Q2 and still has deadweight loss because marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost there.

visuals.alt: Demand-supply diagram with demand increasing from D1 to D2 and quota rising from Q1 to Q2 while price stays P1.
visuals.caption: Quota and market surpluses

movements: Demand shifts right from D1 to D2.
The quota is raised from Q1 to Q2 and the market clears at P1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Producer surplus rises from P1cfg to P1deg, an increase of area cdef.

questions.postVisualStem: When the demand for good X increases from D1 to D2 and the quota changes from Q1 to Q2, the price remains at P1. Which of the following statements about the above situation is CORRECT?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (I)
questions.keyPoint: Positive externality and economic inefficiency; correcting externality
questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a divergence between private and social benefits?

choices.text: A coffee shop customer uses the free Wi-Fi in the shop to browse social media.
A resident was annoyed by pollution caused by feral pigeons. After the government strengthened the enforcement of the ban on feeding feral pigeons, the pollution issue improved.
A passerby enjoys a free street art performance in the West Kowloon Cultural District without making a donation.
A university student improves academic performance after reading books borrowed from the university library.

questions.explanation: The performers provide an external benefit to passers-by who enjoy the performance without compensating them. The other benefits are internalised, or the case concerns external cost.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Interpret the information delivered from the Lorenz curve
questions.stem: The following diagram shows the Lorenz curves of Country A and Country B.
questions.explanation: Country A's curve is closer to equality, so its Gini coefficient is lower. Its bottom 40% earn 20% of income, while Country B's bottom 60% earn under 20%. Country B's top 20% receive the larger share.

visuals.alt: Two Lorenz curves for Country A and Country B with cumulative household and income percentages.
visuals.caption: Country A and Country B Lorenz curves

diagramDetails.answerFocus: Country A's curve is closer to the equality line. Its Gini coefficient is lower, and its bottom 40% receive more than Country B's bottom 60%.

questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the total household incomes in the two countries are equal. Based on the above information, which of the following statements about the two countries are CORRECT?

(1) Country A has a lower Gini coefficient than Country B.
(2) The bottom 40% of households in Country A earn a higher income than the bottom 60% of households in Country B.
(3) The top 20% of households in Country A earn a higher proportion of the country’s total income than that of Country B.

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.topicGroup: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.keyPoint: Sources of income inequality including human capital, discrimination, unequal ownership of capital, etc.
questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why income inequality among freelance photographers in Hong Kong tends to be greater than that among bus drivers?

choices.text: The average working hours of freelance photographers are shorter.
There are greater differences in creativity and skill level among freelance photographers.
The supply of freelance photographers is more elastic.
The market demand for freelance photographers is smaller.

questions.explanation: Photographers vary greatly in creativity, skill and popularity, so top photographers can charge far higher fees. Bus-driver earnings are more closely tied to a fixed wage.

questions.keyPoint: Production/value added approach
questions.stem: The following diagram shows a production chain of agricultural products in Country A.

visuals.alt: Agricultural-products production chain with imported and local materials, local manufacturers, exporter, retailers, consumers and inventories.
visuals.caption: Agricultural-products production chain

movements: Local manufacturers sell to exporters, retailers and inventories.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Country A's GDP at factor cost is $830 after adding local value added and deducting the $80 sales tax.

questions.postVisualStem: The contribution of the above production chain to Country A’s GDP at factor cost is ________.

questions.keyPoint: Gross national income (Gross national product)
questions.stem: To calculate Hong Kong's gross national income (GNI), which of the following should be added to Hong Kong's gross domestic product (GDP)?

choices.text: the dividends received by a Japanese resident from a listed company in Hong Kong
the salary earned by an American working in a bank in Hong Kong for six months
the rent received by a Hong Kong resident from a property in the United Kingdom
the salary earned by a Hong Kong engineer working in a Korean company for three years

questions.explanation: GNI adds factor income earned by Hong Kong residents outside the territory. The rent is such income; the other options are income of non-residents in Hong Kong, or of an engineer who has ceased to be a Hong Kong resident.

questions.topicGroup: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.keyPoint: Relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices
questions.stem: The following table shows some data of an economy in a certain year.
questions.explanation: Subsidies exceed indirect taxes, so GDP at market prices is lower. Net exports are -$75m + $40m = -$35m. Negative net factor income from abroad means GNI is smaller than GDP.
questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the economy are CORRECT?

(1) GDP at market prices is smaller than GDP at factor cost.
(2) Net exports is positive.
(3) GNI is smaller than GDP.

questions.topicGroup: Deviations of short run equilibrium from long run equilibrium
questions.keyPoint: Inflationary gap
questions.stem: Which of the following would MOST likely help an economy narrow the inflationary (output) gap?

choices.text: The government provides production subsidies to firms, and the trading partner experiences an economic recovery.
Labour cost increases, and the government reduces spending on national defense.
Technology improves, and people have an increased preference for imported consumer goods.
Firms suspend production due to a typhoon, and firms buy more inventories.

questions.explanation: Higher labour cost lowers SRAS and lower government spending reduces AD. Both reduce output and narrow an inflationary gap; the other combinations widen the gap or have an uncertain effect.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: The mechanism of moving from a short run equilibrium to a long run equilibrium
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the AD curve, SRAS curve and LRAS curve for an economy. The economy initially operates at E.

choices.text: the output level will be higher than Y0 in the short run.
the price level will be higher than P0 in the short run.
the output level will be equal to Y0 in the long run.
the price level will be lower than P1 in the long run.

questions.explanation: Higher saving reduces consumption and shifts AD left. Output and price fall in the short run; in the long run SRAS shifts right until output returns to Y1, at a price below P1.

visuals.alt: AS-AD diagram with initial short-run equilibrium E at Y0, a vertical LRAS at Y1, and price levels P0 and P1.
visuals.caption: Saving and long-run adjustment

movements: A higher desire to save lowers consumption and shifts AD left.
In the long run, SRAS shifts right until output returns to LRAS at Y1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The long-run price level falls below P1, so option D is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: If people's desire to save increases,

questions.topicGroup: Changes in the equilibrium level of output and price level caused by change(s) in AD and/or AS
questions.keyPoint: Explain how a given event leads to changes in AD, SRAS and/or LRAS by specifying the component(s) of AD affected and/or factor(s) affecting SRAS and/or LRAS, leading to a shift of the AD curve, the SRAS curve and/or the LRAS curve
questions.stem: Suppose that the government increases its subsidies for research and development to firms. Which of the following diagrams best describes the effect of the above event?
questions.explanation: The subsidies raise investment and AD. In the long run, R&D raises productive capacity and shifts LRAS right. Diagram C shows both effects.

visuals.alt: Four AD-AS diagrams A to D for an increase in R&D subsidies to firms.
visuals.caption: R&D-subsidy diagram options

movements: R&D subsidies increase investment, shifting AD right.
Higher R&D increases productive capacity, shifting LRAS right.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Only option C combines a rightward AD shift with a rightward LRAS shift.

questions.keyPoint: Functions of money
questions.stem:
A major economic crisis in Country A has led to a significant depreciation of its currency. As a result, people have started bartering or trading using US dollars. Many people withdraw their bank deposits and convert them into US dollars. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The function of Country A's currency as a medium of exchange is weakened.
(2) The US dollar serves the function of money as a store of value.
(3) The US dollar is the legal tender of Country A.
questions.explanation: Barter and USD use show Country A's currency is less accepted as a medium of exchange. People hold USD to preserve purchasing power, but widespread use alone does not make it legal tender.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Suppose the public withdraw $100 million from the banking system and remit the amount overseas. After the deposit contraction process is completed, deposits in the banking system decrease by $400 million. We can conclude that

choices.text: the monetary base decreases by $400 million.
the money supply decreases by $500 million.

questions.explanation: Assets equal liabilities. Reserves fall by $100m and deposits by $400m, so loans must fall by $300m. Monetary base and money supply each fall by $100m and $400m respectively; the reserve ratio cannot be inferred when prior excess reserves are unknown.

questions.keyPoint: Understand and calculate maximum and actual changes in deposits, loans, money supply, etc. after deposit creation/contraction
questions.stem: Refer to the following balance sheet of the banking system of an economy. The required reserves of the banking system are $200.
questions.explanation: The original required reserve ratio is 200/800 = 25%, so the new ratio is 20%. With $300 reserves, maximum deposits are $300/(20%) = $1,500 and loans are $1,200.
questions.postVisualStem: Suppose the central bank lowers the required reserve ratio by 5 percentage points. If the banking system is fully loaned up and there is no cash leakage, which of the following shows its final balance sheet after the deposit creation/contraction process is completed?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse changes in money demand, money supply and nominal interest rate
questions.stem: The diagram below shows the money supply curve (Ms) and money demand curve (Md) of an economy. Suppose the initial equilibrium point is at E.

choices.text: may increase or decrease ... will increase
may increase or decrease ... will decrease

questions.explanation: Concern about defaults raises asset demand for money and tends to raise the rate. Bond purchases raise money supply and tend to lower the rate. The rate is therefore uncertain, but money quantity rises.

visuals.alt: Money-market diagram with vertical money supply Ms and downward money demand Md meeting at E.
visuals.caption: Money market

movements: Greater concern over bond default shifts money demand right.
Government bond purchases increase the money supply.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Money quantity increases, but the two interest-rate effects oppose each other, so the rate may rise or fall.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose people are more concerned about bond defaults and the government increases the amount of government bonds it buys from the public each month. In this case, the nominal interest rate __________, and the quantity of money __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Effects of inflation and deflation on different aspects
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about inflation is CORRECT?

choices.text: During inflation, the prices of all goods and services will increase.
If the government distributes cash to all citizens in a certain year, inflation will increase.
When people expect inflation to occur, they prefer to hold real assets rather than cash.
Inflation will redistribute wealth from debtors to lenders if it is unanticipated.

questions.explanation: Expected inflation reduces the purchasing power of cash, so people prefer real assets. Inflation concerns the general price level, a one-off cash payment need not cause inflation, and unanticipated inflation benefits debtors rather than lenders.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Relationship between nominal and real interest rates
questions.keyPoint: Understand the equation: nominal interest rate = real interest rate + expected inflation rate
questions.stem: Suppose the nominal interest rate of a one-year bond is 3% and the expected inflation rate is 1%. If the actual inflation rate turns out to be 4%, the actual real interest rate and the real rate of return on holding cash will be __________ and __________ respectively.
questions.explanation: Actual real interest rate is 3% - 4% = -1%. Cash has a nominal return of 0%, so its real return is 0% - 4% = -4%.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.topicGroup: Inflation and quantity theory of money
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of quantity theory of money
questions.stem: According to the quantity theory of money, if the money supply of an economy decreases by 5%,

choices.text: the price level will decrease by 5%.
the nominal output will decrease by 5%.
the real output will decrease by less than 5%.
the government's income tax revenue will decrease by 5%.

questions.explanation: Under MV = PY with velocity constant, a 5% fall in money supply gives a 5% fall in nominal output (PY). The division between prices and real output is not determined.

questions.chapterTitle: Business Cycle, Changes in the General Price Level and Unemployment
questions.keyPoint: Calculate the unemployment rate and identify the labour force
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram.

choices.text: More people quit their jobs and search for jobs in other regions. Some of their positions remain unfilled.
The government raises the statutory minimum wage level.
The government lowers requirements for companies to apply for the importation of foreign workers.
The government reduces assistance to the unemployed.

questions.explanation: The number unemployed falls while the unemployment rate rises. This is possible when the labour force falls by a greater percentage because workers leave the region while some jobs remain vacant.

visuals.alt: Column and line chart: unemployed population falls from 2023 to 2024 while the unemployment rate rises.
visuals.caption: Country A unemployment data

movements: The unemployed population falls but the unemployment rate rises.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: This can occur when labour force shrinks by a larger percentage because people quit and leave the region, while some vacancies remain unfilled.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following is MOST likely to cause the above change in the unemployment data of Country A?

questions.chapterTitle: Efficiency, Equity and the Role of Government (II)
questions.keyPoint: Equalising income
questions.stem: Which of the following may lead to a rise in the economy's price level and make income distribution more even at the same time?

choices.text: The government raises the standard tax rate of salaries tax.
The government imposes a tariff on all imported consumer goods.
The government tightens the requirements for receiving unemployment benefits.
The government distributes $10,000 in cash to all households.

questions.explanation: An equal cash payment is a larger percentage of income for lower-income households, making distribution more even. It also raises disposable income, consumption, AD and the price level.

questions.keyPoint: Progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax
questions.stem: Which of the following diagrams shows a progressive tax?
questions.explanation: A progressive tax has a rising average tax rate as income rises. Diagrams (2) and (3) show that; (1) is regressive and (4) proportional.

visuals.alt: Four tax-payment or tax-rate diagrams labelled (1) to (4) against taxable income.
visuals.caption: Progressive-tax diagrams

movements: Diagram (2) has tax payment rising at an increasing rate.
Diagram (3) has a tax rate rising with taxable income.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Both (2) and (3) show a progressive tax, so option C is correct.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of fiscal policy on price and output levels
questions.keyPoint: Effects of expansionary fiscal policy
questions.stem: If the government of a country increases taxes on households to fund its expenditure, and the increase in taxes equals the increase in government expenditure, the aggregate demand of the country _________.

choices.text: may increase, decrease or remain unchanged

questions.explanation: An equal increase in government expenditure has a larger expansionary effect than the contractionary effect of the equal tax increase, so aggregate demand rises.

questions.keyPoint: Expansionary and contractionary monetary policy, including changes in required reserve ratio and discount rate
questions.stem:
Which of the following is/are contractionary monetary policy/policies?

(1) The People's Bank of China raises the required reserve ratio.
(2) The Bank of China issues bonds denominated in Renminbi.
(3) The Ministry of Finance of the People's Republic of China provides cash subsidies to consumers to buy home appliances.
questions.explanation: A central-bank reserve-ratio increase reduces money supply and is contractionary monetary policy. The Bank of China is commercial, and cash subsidies are fiscal policy.

questions.topicGroup: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.keyPoint: Understand the condition(s) under which mutually beneficial trade is possible
questions.stem: The following table shows the labour requirement for the production of good X and good Y in Country A and Country B respectively.
questions.explanation: The opportunity cost of one Y is 1.5 X in A and 3 X in B. Including the shared 0.5 X transport cost, mutually beneficial terms satisfy 0.4Y < 1X < 0.5Y; only 0.45Y fits.
questions.postVisualStem:
Suppose the transportation cost for 1 unit of good Y is 1 unit of good X and it is borne equally by both countries.
Which of the following is a mutually beneficial terms of trade between Country A and Country B?

(1) 1 unit of good X = 0.4 units of good Y
(2) 1 unit of good X = 0.45 units of good Y
(3) 1 unit of good X = 2.25 units of good Y

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of free trade and a tariff on price, domestic output, import, consumption quantity and tariff revenue for a small open economy
questions.stem:
A small open economy has imposed a per-unit tariff on imported good X. Suppose the international price of good X decreases. Which of the following statements are CORRECT?

(1) The domestic production of good X will decrease.
(2) The government's tariff revenue will increase.
(3) The total value of imports of good X net of tax will increase.
questions.explanation: A lower international price lowers domestic price and domestic output. Import volume rises, so a constant per-unit tariff yields more tariff revenue. The import value net of tax is uncertain because price falls while quantity rises.

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Current account (main components: goods, services, income and current transfers)
questions.keyPoint: Meaning of current account surplus and deficit
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about the balance of payments of an economy in a certain year.

choices.text: there was a current account surplus in 2023 and a current account deficit in 2024.
exports of goods in 2024 were lower than those in 2023.
imports of goods in 2024 were higher than those in 2023.
exports of services were smaller than imports of services in both 2023 and 2024.

questions.explanation: The balance of trade in services is negative in both years, so service exports are smaller than service imports. The chart lacks enough information to infer current accounts or separate exports and imports of goods.

visuals.alt: Balance-of-trade bar chart for goods and services in 2023 and 2024.
visuals.caption: Balance of payments data

movements: The goods balance moves from surplus in 2023 to deficit in 2024.
The services balance is below zero in both years.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Both years have a deficit in the balance of trade in services, which means service exports are smaller than service imports.

questions.postVisualStem: According to the above information, we can conclude that

questions.chapterTitle: Balance of Payments Account and Exchange Rate
questions.topicGroup: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.keyPoint: Brief introduction to the linked exchange rate system in
questions.stem: Under the linked exchange rate system in Hong Kong, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

choices.text: The non-bank public can sell Hong Kong dollars to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in exchange for US dollars at the linked exchange rate.
The money supply M3 of Hong Kong is fully backed by the US dollar.
A trade deficit in the United States will lead to a trade deficit in Hong Kong.
When the US dollar depreciates against other currencies, the number of tourists from those currency zones visiting Hong Kong will increase.

questions.explanation: The Hong Kong dollar depreciates with the US dollar against other currencies, making Hong Kong goods and travel cheaper in those currencies and attracting more tourists. Only note-issuing banks may exchange with the HKMA at the linked rate, and only the monetary base is fully backed by US dollars.

questions.keyPoint: Identify and calculate the cost (explicit cost and implicit cost) involved in choosing an option
questions.stem:
Macy received a theatre ticket from her father with an original price of $280. A friend offered to buy the ticket for $200. At the same time, a fast-food restaurant offered to hire Macy for a part-time job for $300 during the time of the play. If Macy accepts the part-time job, she will sell the ticket to her friend.

According to the above information, Macy's opportunity cost of choosing to watch the play is __________.
questions.explanation: The ticket's original $280 price was not paid by Macy and is not her opportunity cost. Watching the play gives up both the $300 job income and the $200 resale income, for a total of $500.

questions.topicGroup: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.keyPoint: Distinction between positive statements and normative statements
questions.stem:
Refer to the following conversation.

Cody: The world produces over 400 million tonnes of plastic waste every year.
Yanny: Even if it increases business costs, we should fully ban single-use plastic products.

____________ statement is ____________ because ____________.

choices.text: Cody's ... positive ... it is consistent with real world data
Cody's ... normative ... not everyone agrees with it
Yanny's ... positive ... it can be rejected by facts
Yanny's ... normative ... value judgement is involved in the statement

questions.explanation: Yanny's use of 'should' expresses a value judgement, so it is normative. A positive statement is distinguished by whether it can be tested with facts, not by whether it matches data.

questions.chapterTitle: The Three Basic Economic Problems and Private Property Rights
questions.keyPoint: The meanings of the three basic economic problems and examples of the problems
questions.stem:
The organiser of a large concert makes these rules: (1) all tickets are sold online, starting at $280, while stocks last; (2) real-name registration is adopted and tickets are non-transferable.

Which statements about the ticket-sales arrangement are CORRECT?

(1) The rules are related to the problem of 'for whom to produce'.
(2) The right to transfer over the tickets would be weakened.
(3) Price competition would not be involved in allocation of the tickets.
questions.explanation: The rules govern who obtains tickets, so relate to for whom to produce. Real-name, non-transferable tickets restrict transfer rights. Buyers still pay at least $280, so price competition remains.

questions.keyPoint: Comparison of features, advantages and disadvantages of different forms of ownership
questions.stem: Refer to the following information about two firms in Hong Kong.

choices.text: Both Firm A and Firm B can possibly have 1,000 owners.
Firm B cannot keep its accounting information confidential while Firm A can.
Firm B has better continuity than Firm A.
When both firms have the same amount of profit, Firm B may enjoy a lower profits tax rate than Firm A.

questions.explanation: Firm A can be a sole proprietorship or partnership, while Firm B is a public limited company. A limited company has a higher profits-tax rate, not a lower rate; the other statements can be true.

visuals.caption: Information about two firms
rows: Owners bear all the liability of the firm
The liability of owners is confined to the amount of their investment

questions.postVisualStem: Based on the above information, which of the following statements about firm A and firm B is INCORRECT?

questions.topicGroup: Shares and bonds as sources of capital
questions.keyPoint: Advantages and disadvantages of issuing shares and bonds to raise capital
questions.stem: A listed company in Hong Kong is considering issuing shares or bonds to raise capital. For existing shareholders, which is an advantage of issuing shares instead of bonds?

choices.text: Since most small investors participate in the stock market rather than the bond market, issuing shares can raise more capital.
The company has no repayment obligation.
Existing shareholders' power of control over the company will not be diluted.
If the share price rises, shareholders can earn capital gains.

questions.explanation: A company has no obligation to redeem shares from shareholders. The amount raised is uncertain, new shares can dilute control, and capital gains are possible regardless of which instrument the company issues.

questions.topicGroup: Types of goods and services produced
questions.keyPoint: Private goods and public goods
questions.stem:
Which of the following are examples of public goods?

(1) an ancient poem
(2) public bus service
(3) free television broadcasts
(4) medicine provided by public hospitals
questions.explanation: An ancient poem and free television broadcasts are non-rival and non-excludable. Bus travel can exclude non-payers, and medicine is rival because one person's use leaves less for others.

questions.keyPoint: Describe the inter-relationship between the three types of production
questions.stem: Refer to the following diagram. Each box in the diagram represents a type of production.

choices.text: primary production ... tertiary production ... producer goods
tertiary production ... primary production ... producer goods

questions.explanation: Y is primary production because it sends raw materials to X; X is tertiary production, and services Z flow from secondary production to tertiary production.

visuals.alt: Production-flow chart joining boxes X, Y and Secondary production, with raw materials and Z labelled on directed arrows.
visuals.caption: Types of production

movements: Raw materials flow from Y to X.
Producer goods flow from Y to secondary production.
Z flows from secondary production to X.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: Y is primary production, X is tertiary production and Z is services.

questions.postVisualStem: X, Y and Z represent __________, ___________ and _________ respectively.

questions.keyPoint: Types of division of labour
questions.stem: Jason, Joyce and Karmen are organising a birthday party. Jason decorates, Joyce prepares dinner and Karmen buys gifts. This is an example of __________ division of labour because __________.

choices.text: simple ... each person is responsible for one task
complex ... each person is responsible for one aspect of the birthday party
simple ... each person is involved in different stages of production
complex ... each person prepares the birthday party according to their own expertise

questions.explanation: The party is divided into related aspects, each handled by a person, so it is complex division of labour.

questions.keyPoint: Natural resources: land
questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about land and capital in economics are CORRECT?

(1) The quantity of land cannot be increased by human effort, while the quantity of capital can.
(2) The return on land is rent, while the return on capital is profit.
(3) In wind-power generation, wind belongs to land while generators belong to capital.
questions.explanation: Land is a natural resource and capital is man-made. The returns are rent for land and interest for capital, so (2) is false.

questions.keyPoint: Different methods of wage payment
questions.stem: The table below shows data for two firms:

choices.text: Firm B uses piece rate while Firm A uses time rate.
Firm A has a better working environment than Firm B.
Firm A employs workers with higher skills.
Firm B does not provide appropriate training to employees.

questions.explanation: Firm B has higher output per man-hour but a larger percentage below standard. Piece rate encourages workers to increase output, potentially at the expense of quality; time rate does not create the same incentive.

visuals.caption: Two-firm labour data
rows: Percentage of output with quality below standard

questions.postVisualStem: Refer to the above table. Which of the following can best explain the difference in average labour productivity and quality of outputs between the two firms?

questions.keyPoint: Variable costs and fixed costs
questions.stem:
After a major sporting event, a bus company arranges additional services to transport spectators. Which of the following are fixed costs involved?

(1) fuel costs for buses
(2) insurance expenses of the bus company
(3) hourly wages of part-time bus drivers
(4) salaries of administrative staff
questions.explanation: Insurance expenses and administrative salaries do not change with the number of additional services. Fuel and hourly driver wages increase with output and are variable costs.

questions.topicGroup: Input-output relationship in the short run
questions.keyPoint: Law of diminishing marginal returns
questions.stem: The table below shows the input-output relationship of a firm. The only input required for production is labour. The fixed cost is $10 and the wage rate per unit of labour is $5.

choices.text: Since average cost per unit keeps falling, the firm enjoys economies of scale.
The optimal scale of production is 26 units.
When the 6th unit of labour is employed, marginal product starts to diminish, indicating diminishing marginal returns.
Since total output keeps rising, diminishing marginal returns do not apply.

questions.explanation: Marginal product is 5, 6, 7 and then 6 units as labour rises from three to six, so it first diminishes at the sixth worker. The firm has fixed factors and operates in the short run, so economies and optimal scale do not apply.
questions.postVisualStem: According to the above table, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: External economies/diseconomies of scale
questions.stem: The HKSAR Government approved the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology to establish a medical school to train more doctors and expand medical services. In this case, hospitals will
questions.explanation: A larger pool of trained doctors benefits firms in the medical-services industry from outside each individual hospital, so hospitals enjoy external economies of scale.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: The following table shows the cost-output relationship of a profit-maximising firm.
questions.explanation: Total cost at six units is $5 + (6 x $6) = $41. Marginal cost of the sixth unit is $11, so price is $11. Profit is $66 - $41 = $25.
questions.postVisualStem: Given the fixed cost is $5. If the profit-maximising output is 6 units, the market price will be ____________ and the profit will be ____________.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.topicGroup: The basic objective of firms: profit maximisation
questions.keyPoint: Profit-maximising choice of output for a competitive firm
questions.stem: A profit-maximising firm will increase its output if __________.

choices.text: average cost for each unit of output decreases by $10
demand for the good produced by the firm decreases
the marginal cost of production for the firm increases

questions.explanation: A $10 fall in average cost at every output means marginal cost falls by $10, so the profit-maximising output rises. Fixed cost does not affect marginal cost, while lower demand or higher marginal cost reduces output.

questions.chapterTitle: The Objectives and Expansion of Firms
questions.keyPoint: Understand the meaning and give examples of each type of integration
questions.stem:
An automobile manufacturer acquires an engine manufacturer. The engine manufacturer has several clients, and its engines can be used in cars of different brands. Which could be motives behind the acquisition?

(1) to enjoy economies of scale
(2) to diversify risk through business diversification
(3) to expand the market outlet for its products
questions.explanation: The acquisition can create economies of scale and diversify risk through a related business. It expands into an earlier production stage, so it does not expand the market outlet for the automobile manufacturer's products.

questions.topicGroup: Determination of equilibrium price and output
questions.keyPoint: Market disequilibrium: excess demand and excess supply
questions.stem: A large chain convenience store advertises shop-assistant jobs at $50 per hour but cannot hire enough assistants. The quantity transacted in the labour market is __________ the quantity demanded and __________ the quantity supplied.
questions.explanation: The wage is below equilibrium, producing excess demand for labour. Quantity transacted equals the smaller quantity supplied and is below quantity demanded.

questions.topicGroup: Money Price (Nominal Price) and Relative Price
questions.keyPoint: Explain phenomena by applying the law of demand (using relative price or full price)
questions.stem:
Two neighbouring fitness centres use different prices. Centre A charges $40 per entry. Centre B charges a fixed $200 monthly fee for unlimited entry. Suppose their services are similar. Which statements are CORRECT?

(1) Users of Centre A tend to spend a shorter time there on average.
(2) Members of Centre B tend to visit more frequently.
(3) The marginal benefit of the last unit of service for Centre B members tends to be lower.
questions.explanation: The average price per visit at Centre B falls as members visit more, so they tend to visit more often and consume until a lower marginal benefit. With Centre A's entry fee, the relative price of a long stay is lower, so users tend to stay longer, not shorter.

questions.topicGroup: Changes in both demand and supply
questions.keyPoint: Explain the effects of a change in demand and a change in supply on equilibrium price and quantity
questions.stem: The following is the demand-supply diagram for the canned coffee of brand A. E0 is the initial equilibrium point.
questions.explanation: More firms selling substitute canned coffee reduce demand for Brand A, while costlier coffee beans reduce its supply. The diagram's combined leftward demand and supply shift gives E4.

visuals.alt: Canned-coffee demand and supply diagram with D0-D2, S0-S2 and equilibrium points E0-E4.
visuals.caption: Canned-coffee market shifts

movements: More competing canned-coffee firms shift demand for Brand A left from D0 to D2.
Higher coffee-bean price shifts Brand A supply left from S0 to S2.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The combined change moves the equilibrium from E0 to E4.

questions.postVisualStem: Suppose more firms enter the canned coffee market. At the same time, the price of coffee beans rises. The new equilibrium point will be at __________.

questions.topicGroup: Effects of a change in supply
questions.keyPoint: Effects of a change in supply
questions.stem: The demand curve for smartphone repair services is D.

choices.text: The price of brand-new smartphones decreases.
The price of replacement parts for smartphones decreases.
The equilibrium wage of repair technicians for other electronic products increases.

questions.explanation: A lower price of replacement parts lowers the cost of repair services and increases supply, moving equilibrium down along demand from E1 to E2. The other events reduce supply or shift demand.

visuals.alt: Demand curve D for smartphone repair services with equilibrium moving from E1 to E2 along the same demand curve.
visuals.caption: Smartphone-repair market

movements: A lower price of replacement parts reduces repair providers' costs and shifts supply right.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: The move down along the demand curve to E2 is caused by an increase in supply, so option B is correct.

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following reasons best explains the change in the equilibrium point for smartphone repair services from E1 to E2?

questions.keyPoint: Explain how prices of related goods, income, price expectations, weather, number of consumers in the market, etc. affect individual demand and market demand
questions.stem: The table below shows the demand schedule for good Y before and after a decrease in the supply of good X.
questions.explanation: Less supply of X raises its price. Demand for Y rises at every given price, so consumers substitute Y for X.
questions.postVisualStem: Based on the table above, good X and good Y are most likely __________.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Factors affecting price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely to increase the price elasticity of demand for mobile data services?

choices.text: The government issues more licences for mobile data services.
Network providers raise the price of mobile data services.
The government sets up free Wi-Fi hotspots in more locations.
People become more used to using mobile data to watch videos.

questions.explanation: More free Wi-Fi hotspots increase the availability of substitutes for mobile data, making its demand more price elastic.

questions.chapterTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand and Supply
questions.keyPoint: Measuring price elasticity of demand
questions.stem: Good X and good Y are in joint supply. When demand for X increases, the price of Y changes by 25% and Y quantity transacted rises from 250 units to 300 units. Which statement is CORRECT?

choices.text: Demand for good Y is inelastic.
Demand for good Y is elastic.
Supply of good Y is inelastic.
Supply of good Y is elastic.

questions.explanation: More demand for X increases joint supply of Y, lowering Y's price. The midpoint percentage rise in Y quantity is 50/275 = 18.18%, below the 25% price change, so Y demand is inelastic.

questions.topicGroup: Tax on goods and services (Sales tax)
questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of a unit tax on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, etc., and show the share of the tax burden between producers and consumers
questions.stem: Refer to the following supply and demand schedules for good X.

choices.text: If the government imposes a price ceiling of $3, quantity transacted will be 12 units.
If the government imposes a price floor of $7, quantity transacted will remain unchanged.
If the government provides a per-unit subsidy of $2 to producers, equilibrium price will fall.
If the government imposes a per-unit sales tax of $2, producers' total revenue net of tax will be $30.

questions.explanation: Equilibrium is $5 and 10 units. With a $2 tax, buyers pay $5 and producers receive $3 at 10 units, so revenue net of tax is $30. At a $3 ceiling transacted quantity is supply of 10, a $7 floor reduces it to 8, and the subsidy leaves buyer price at $5.

visuals.caption: Supply and demand schedules for good X

questions.postVisualStem: Which of the following statements about the market of good X is CORRECT?

questions.keyPoint: Analyse the effects of the imposition of (effective) quota on price, quantity transacted, total revenue, product quality, etc.
questions.stem: The following is the demand-supply diagram for drones. The government imposes a quota of Q1 on drones.
questions.explanation: The quota is binding. Cheaper motors increase supply but keep quantity at Q1; greater demand raises price while quantity remains Q1, raising sales value. A larger quota lowers price.

visuals.alt: Drone-market demand and supply diagram with a binding quota Q1, original supply S0 and vertical quota supply S1.
visuals.caption: Drone quota

movements: Cheaper drone motors shift supply right but binding quota fixes quantity at Q1.
More popular drones shift demand right while quantity stays at Q1.
diagramDetails.answerFocus: With a binding quota, cheaper inputs leave quantity unchanged and greater demand raises price and total sales value; increasing quota lowers price.

questions.postVisualStem:
Which of the following statements about the drone market are CORRECT?

(1) If the price of drone motors falls, the quantity transacted will remain unchanged.
(2) If drones become more popular, the total sales value will increase.
(3) If the government increases the quota, the market price will increase.

questions.keyPoint: Give examples of monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly
